loc_03000806.summary: The mobile base crawler, also known as the Enclave Mobile Platform and the Adams AFB Mobile Platform, is a large command vehicle found at Adams Air Force Base.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An ancient, pre-War mobile satellite array/space shuttle launch platform carried by a crawler-transporter is the Enclave's backup command center on the East Coast. The massive vehicle was upgraded by the Enclave with newly developed technology, crafting it into a battle-station where the elite Enclave Squad Sigma trains, deathclaw experimentation continues, and access to Earth's remaining orbital payloads (like the Bradley-Hercules) are attempted. The amount of technology is so staggering that it would take even a technologically capable organization many years to sift through all of it.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The crawler can only be entered after the terminal to lower the ramp has been activated; the terminal becomes accessible during Who Dares Wins. The interior consists of four parts:

Base floor:
The first area is the base floor and is called the mobile base crawler. Stiggs, an Enclave engineer who will help the Lone Wanderer if he is allowed to live, can be found here. If the alarm sounds, Enclave Squad Sigma will appear. There is also a small room behind a pulse field which contains various materials and a workbench. Behind another repulsion field lies an armory that contains several weapons, ammunition, and armor.

The repulsion fields around the base can be turned off via nearby control panels. When these panels are activated, there will be four options:
• Do nothing: Nothing will happen.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Alien blaster - Launch platform base, in a Hard locked gun case in the armory which is guarded by the armory master. Along with it are a few alien power cells and three more Average locked boxes containing cells below the gun case.
• Precision Gatling laser - Carried by the armory master.
• Composite recon helmet - Worn by the armory master.
• Slo-burn flamer - Launch platform base, in the southeast end inside a stasis field behind the sign labeled "Sensitive Electronics".
• 13 combat knives in perfect condition can be found in the storage room, behind a large white crate.
• 17 lead pipes, all in perfect condition, can be found in the storage room, close to one of the middle deck access hatches to the entrance bay.
• 17 knives in perfect condition can be found in the kitchen, on the oven.

loc_03001490.summary: The Rockland car tunnel is a section of a collapsed road tunnel located in the southwest corner of the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: It served as an entrance to the Enclave satellite relay station. The Brotherhood of Steel has driven the Enclave out of the tunnel and now uses it as a staging area.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Since the main entrance is collapsed, the tunnel is entered through a door built into a wall on the side. There are several irradiated pools outside of the gate as well as an intact army truck loaded with Aqua Pura crates. The interior consists of a short stretch of an intact tunnel with the thrashed remains of the Enclave's former occupation scattered all throughout (barricades, turret, supply crates, etc). Now, the premises has been claimed by Brotherhood of Steel knights and scribes.

Seven sets of Enclave power armor can be found inside of the tunnel on piled bodies of deceased Enclave soldiers, in a bus stop on the east side of the main chamber, as well as lying among rocks along the west wall.

loc_0300739a.summary:
The Old Olney S. Wilson Building is a collapsing office building, which can be accessed via the Old Olney underground.

As part of the quest Shock Value, the Lone Wanderer passes through this area to reach Olney Powerworks. The area is inhabited by four Enclave soldiers who arrive via a Vertibird on the top level shortly before the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Points of interest
sections.text:
• Tucked away behind some filing cabinets in the northwestern corner at the same level as the door to the Olney Powerworks entrance, there is a setup of a teddy bear "playing cards" with an intact garden gnome that is using metro tickets as cards. The gnome is smoking and has a pair of eyeglasses, whiskey and a shot glass close at hand. Next to the teddy bear are tortiseshell glasses, a pre-War bonnet and it is holding sexy sleepwear. Both the hat and sleepwear are in 100% condition.
• It is possible to get to the upper levels, try climbing the rubble that is immediately to the left as you enter the open zone.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Two of the rare police hats can be found here. One is in an office near a cash register, and another is in the center of the room perched above the toilet on a piece of concrete jutting out from a supporting column. Standing on the empty deathclaw cage enables access to the latter one.
• Two mini nukes, sitting on a ledge inside of the fallen length of the radio tower in the center of the area. To retrieve them, you can either shoot them off the ledge and then gather them from the floor below, or make your way up to the east side of the highest level of the building and jump into the length of the tower's open end.
• One Nuka-grenade hidden underneath a desk. Go up the wall as high as the pile of debris will go, turn right and walk along the wall to find the desk.

loc_03003d63.summary: Memorial Sub-Basement is a interior location in Interior Location (Broken Steel).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Jefferson Memorial was constructed in Washington, D.C. to honor Thomas Jefferson, the principal author of the Declaration of Independence and third president of the United States. The monument was built on the bank of the Tidal Basin and became a major tourist attraction. Unlike many other monuments in the city that were damaged or destroyed in the Great War of 2077, the Jefferson Memorial survived relatively intact into the 23rd century.

Project Purity:
The memorial was selected by wasteland scientist James for Project Purity sometime prior to 2257, for which he partnered with Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel to gain their military support defending the memorial against attacks by super mutants.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
It has five interior sections that can be accessed. The exterior of the Jefferson Memorial has a variety of platforms as well as a few super mutant patrols. The entrance to the memorial is through the gift shop doors on either side of the platform.

Upon entering the memorial from the gift shop side entrance, one enters into a long hallway. At the other end of this hallway is a rubble-filled room with a sewer grate hatch that is accessible and is the main part during The Waters of Life quest. Taking a right down the hall leads to a lobby with the gift shop and a turret placed on the roof, Bigsley's office during Broken Steel to the left and ruined bathrooms to the right. Once past the second double doors, the player enters an area of ruined corridors and entrances to the rotunda and the memorial sub-basement.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Project Purity journals
• Better Days
• Project Purity personal journals
• Colonel Autumn's uniform - Worn by Colonel Autumn, can either be obtained from The Waters of Life or Take it Back!
• Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol - Used by Colonel Autumn during The Waters of Life, can be obtained if he falls close enough to the door when James activates the radiation.
• Colonel Autumn's laser pistol - Used by Colonel Autumn during Take it Back!
• Dad's wasteland outfit - Worn by James, can be obtained from The Waters of Life when he activates the radiation and falls close to the door.

loc_0300674d.summary: Hank's Electrical Supply is a fairly small building next to the Jury Street Metro station, occupied by raiders. There is only one interior section.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
The building is an old abandoned shop. On top of the roof there are two raiders and Aqua Pura barrels (although these will only be present if Broken Steel is installed).

Interior:
The inside contains two rooms, the larger of which (apparently the former shop area) is divided by a counter. A ladder on the back of the building provides access to the roof. Against the middle of the back wall is a workbench. The main feature of the smaller room is a safe with a terminal nearby which could be used to open it, were it not already unlocked. The area is home to three raiders.

loc_03000807.summary: The presidential metro is a network of pre-War metro tunnels. It connects various government buildings in the D.C. area, including the White House, the Capitol Building and Adams Air Force Base.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The presidential metro can be used by the Lone Wanderer to traverse from the presidential sub level beneath the White House with Adams Air Force Base and the Capitol Building's east wing. An automated defense system is headed by a computer system called Metro Authority Rapid Governmental Transit System. M.A.R.Go.T. controls the trains, robots, and other maintenance personnel.

The area is guarded by sentry bots and swarming with feral ghouls. At higher levels, multiple feral ghoul reavers will be present. The enemy groups may be fighting one another.

The metro can be activated by way of acquiring fuses from the destroyed presidential sentry bot or by killing the ghouls present. Once the ghouls are killed, the security breach will be considered cleared, and the presidential sentry bot will automatically replace the fuses.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Nuka-Cola Quantum in the equipment room, which connects the western and eastern lines.
• A police hat can be found near M.A.R.Go.T. in the room where first encountered, and another by a skeleton by a caved-in area to the right when finding the ghouls.
• A single mini nuke located in a half-buried train car at a tunnel dead-end.
• Upwards of 20 pieces of scrap metal on shelves, in containers, and by the side of train tracks throughout the metro.

sections.title: Related quests
sections.text: • The Sorrowful Suitor: A holotape titled "Sorry, my darling" can be found on a bench near the exit to the Capitol building. The holotape begins the quest.

loc_030011c3.summary: The mobile base crawler, also known as the Enclave Mobile Platform and the Adams AFB Mobile Platform, is a large command vehicle found at Adams Air Force Base.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An ancient, pre-War mobile satellite array/space shuttle launch platform carried by a crawler-transporter is the Enclave's backup command center on the East Coast. The massive vehicle was upgraded by the Enclave with newly developed technology, crafting it into a battle-station where the elite Enclave Squad Sigma trains, deathclaw experimentation continues, and access to Earth's remaining orbital payloads (like the Bradley-Hercules) are attempted. The amount of technology is so staggering that it would take even a technologically capable organization many years to sift through all of it.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The crawler can only be entered after the terminal to lower the ramp has been activated; the terminal becomes accessible during Who Dares Wins. The interior consists of four parts:

Base floor:
The first area is the base floor and is called the mobile base crawler. Stiggs, an Enclave engineer who will help the Lone Wanderer if he is allowed to live, can be found here. If the alarm sounds, Enclave Squad Sigma will appear. There is also a small room behind a pulse field which contains various materials and a workbench. Behind another repulsion field lies an armory that contains several weapons, ammunition, and armor.

The repulsion fields around the base can be turned off via nearby control panels. When these panels are activated, there will be four options:
• Do nothing: Nothing will happen.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Alien blaster - Launch platform base, in a Hard locked gun case in the armory which is guarded by the armory master. Along with it are a few alien power cells and three more Average locked boxes containing cells below the gun case.
• Precision Gatling laser - Carried by the armory master.
• Composite recon helmet - Worn by the armory master.
• Slo-burn flamer - Launch platform base, in the southeast end inside a stasis field behind the sign labeled "Sensitive Electronics".
• 13 combat knives in perfect condition can be found in the storage room, behind a large white crate.
• 17 lead pipes, all in perfect condition, can be found in the storage room, close to one of the middle deck access hatches to the entrance bay.
• 17 knives in perfect condition can be found in the kitchen, on the oven.

loc_030035a1.summary: The Olney Powerworks is an old power plant accessible through the Olney sewers. The player character is sent here in order to find a Tesla coil during the Shock Value quest.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The powerworks were owned by PPE before the Great War and may have been the site of Olney's main power supply as well as an experimental testing ground for unorthodox power sources as evidenced by the presence of a Tesla coil.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
After going through the Old Olney S. Wilson Building, head up the stairs. The left hallway has a door connected to a Very Hard-locked terminal which leads directly to the small lab that houses the Tesla coil. The right path leads into a generator room guarded by sentry bots and connects to a storage area with a workbench. Up another flight of stairs is a Hard-locked door that opens to a short hallway with six radiation emitters.

The hallway leads to a room filled with transformers of arcing electricity. Through another Hard-locked door is an orange-lit hallway with computer servers lining the walls. To the left is a blast door guarded by automated turrets and to the right is the door that leads to the main laboratory and the Tesla coil.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Tesla coil - Inside the central reactor.
• Alien power cells - Three sets of 12 can be found on the bottom floor in the area just before the Tesla coil. One on the stove, one on the table next to the stove and one on the table with the glowing plasma ball.
• Additionally, a variable amount of alien power cells (20, give or take without the Scrounger perk) can be found in two ammunition boxes in a small room at the end of the orange-lit computer server room. The ammo boxes are located in the nook above the two Mark IV turrets on either side.

loc_030095c3.summary: The Citadel, alternatively called the DC Bunker, is the heavily defended headquarters of the Capital Wasteland chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel in 2277. It is built into and beneath the ruins of the Pentagon, a key pre-War U.S. military installation in Washington, D.C.. It can be found on the west end of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, northeast of Arlington Library.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Before the Great War, the Pentagon was the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense, making it a key installation for the U.S. military, including the U.S. Army.

In the 2070s, the Pentagon was adapted as a primary site for another of the military's most confidential projects: a joint venture between the U.S. Army's Strategic Arms Division, General Atomics, RobCo, and Mass Fusion, aiming to create Liberty Prime, the ultimate American war machine. This robotic superweapon was intended to be deployed on the Alaskan frontline to turn the tides of the Sino-American War, and this was publicly hinted at by General Constantine Chase during a press conference held at the Pentagon in June 2072.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
The Citadel is a large fortress with walls of stone and steel. It retains the shape which gave it its name, the "Pentagon." The massive concrete building has five concentric rings, designated from the center out as "A" through "E" (with "F" and "G" in the basement), as well as five facades.

The Citadel only has a single entrance, a large metal gate usually guarded by multiple paladins, and one sentry bot. (With Broken Steel, these guards disappear after completing Take it Back!.) A small corridor leads from the main gate to a door which provides access to the inner bailey.

The inside is inaccessible until the quest The Waters of Life is completed. Entry is scripted as part of the completion of this quest. Before then, the gate guard Paladin Bael will gruffly deny entry.

sections.text: Notable items: Tin Can, Bent Tin Can, Small Ruined Book, Turpentine, Small Burned Book, Small Scorched Book. Interactive objects: Desk, Door, Armory Door, Armory 089A Terminal, Callahan's Terminal, Callahan's Safe.

loc_0400f05a.summary: Lighthouse is a interior location in Lighthouse (Point Lookout). Connects directly to Underground Lab.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The lighthouse, although thought to be owned and operated by the government of Maryland, was a tourist attraction hiding the Calvert family's underground research hospital.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text: The lighthouse is a moderately sized tower with some small, but notable stashes of loot. The interior of the lighthouse has a long spiral staircase leading up to a top platform area. The staircase is littered with the skeletons of what appear to be tourists to Point Lookout (the cameras surrounding some of the bodies suggest this) and a police officer (the police hat and.32 pistol suggest this). The platform at the top of the stairs has a door that leads to an exterior balcony. Once smugglers occupy the lighthouse, the staircase can become treacherous as they will shoot down the staircase if they spot the player character. The most notable location of the building is the basement which it is necessary to go into during the quest A Meeting of the Minds.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Three pre-War books in a room with an active computer terminal and lockers. Also in this room is an average locked safe.
• The microwave emitter in a room at the end of the quest.
• Holotape note at the top of the lighthouse, on a table.
• Stealth Boy at the top of the stairs, on a table during A Meeting of the Minds.

loc_0400c828.summary: People's Bank of Point Lookout is a small pre-War bank in Pilgrim's Landing in 2277. Its only current living inhabitants are a few radroaches.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Before the Great War, the bank was a subsidiary of Isla Negra Holdings, and recently had a new voice-operated safe unlock system put in place. This did nothing to prevent the bank from being robbed. There are many skeletons with blood splatter on the walls behind them, and a complete lack of cash in the vaults. Next to the door is the remains of a security guard, also with a pool of blood around it. Looking in the Homestead Motel room 1G reveals the most likely bank robbers' remains and their cash.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text: The bank is abandoned and infested with radroaches. On the wall to the left of the entrance is one of many wanted posters in Point Lookout for a woman named Wan Yang, a secret agent involved in The Velvet Curtain quest. There are two safes in the main hall, one has a Hard lock and the other is Average. A debris-filled staircase leads to a second floor, even though from the outside the bank is shown to have only one floor.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• To access the safe deposit boxes, one needs to find the corresponding holotapes and play them inside the room with the boxes. The holotapes are:
• Box 1191 - Password backup, found in the right desk from the main room. This safe contains buffout and pre-War money.
• Box 1207 - Spy's audio password, found in a locker on the boardwalk of Pilgrim's Landing. This is part of the quest The Velvet Curtain. The safe contains the espionage debriefing as well as some pre-War money.
• Box 1213 - Bern's voice, found in the Grower's shack.
• There is a police hat near a skeleton on the floor in the main room.
• During The Velvet Curtain, outside on the wall is a wanted poster for Wan Yang; reading it results in the Wanted Person: Yang, W. note being added to the player character's inventory.

loc_04008125.summary: The excavated muck holes are unmarked locations in the Fallout 3 add-on Point Lookout, found one block east and slightly north of the Lil' Tyke Playhouse. They are part of the An Antique Land side quest.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The excavated muck holes are the result of a Bysshe Company pre-War research team surveying bio-gas. The muck holes are heavily irradiated, abandoned, contain gas pockets, and contain the soil sample holotapes. If the player character uses flame-based weapons, merely stepping into a pocket of gas while equipped with the flamer, Shishkebab, or various other flame weapons with it drawn will cause the gas to ignite, setting them on fire. Likewise, drawing such a weapon while standing in gas will also cause it to ignite.

Sample site one:
This excavated muck hole is north of the trash heap. Inside there is a desk with a few items on it, such as:
• Soil survey tape #1
• Two bio-gas canisters
• One fission battery
• One advanced radiation suit
• Outside the muck hole there is a destroyed shack, a couple feral ghouls and a muck pool.

In the library is a staircase that ascends to the second floor which has some bedrooms, one with an Average locked safe. loc_0400811d.summary: Run-down Shack is a interior location in Gardener's Shack (Point Lookout).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
This area contains a small swampfolk farm that grows wild punga fruit, which is then sold to Tobar the Ferryman.

The rows of flickering lights that were installed at the location help keep bloatflies away.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
A small dock and outbuilding and two rickety bridges allow access to this growing operation. Right outside the shack, beneath strings of lights, is a large field of wild punga fruits.

Interior:
Inside Grower's shack, there is a usable queen-sized bed, as well as a sink and toilet. It also contains various furniture pieces that can be sat upon. There is a random swampfolk living inside.

• A mini nuke - Behind the holotape near the bed.

loc_0400977f.summary: The St. Aubin Medical Facility (called underground lab in-game) is a location in Point Lookout in 2277, found beneath the Point Lookout Lighthouse.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Before the Great War, this facility was used for research into improving the process of extracting and isolating human brains, pioneered by General Atomics for their Robobrains. It was discovered that by manipulating the mixture for the bio med gel, it was possible to achieve the effects previously thought impossible. Not only could the brain retain its full mental capacity under the right circumstances, but it could also project images and thoughts into other minds. This opened the door not only to applications in battlefield technologies but also, for example, interrogation methods. The only concern was whether being isolated in biogel for years might have undesirable psychological effects.

Senator Calvert had his brother, Professor Calvert, transferred to the project not much later.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The underground facility is a more-or-less straightforward path from the entrance one arrives at with Desmond until the central antechamber where the actual brain of Professor Calvert is contained. The path winds ever downward, with side rooms and laboratories branching off from the central corridor. These rooms usually contain useful materials, particularly crafting components, scrap metal, and energy weapon ammunition; energy cells in particular. Along the way, there are several locked doors that can be opened by keycards of increasing security clearance.

However, these keys are in possession of the primary opponents in the facility: namely, General Atomics' Robobrain automated security. In addition to the robots, several automated turrets activate at regular security checkpoints.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:

loc_0400c2b4.summary: The sub recovery site is a location and where the U.S. military was attempting to raise a covert Chinese submarine (SSN-37-1A) lodged in the shallow waters off the coast of Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The submarine was sent to patrol hostile waters along the East Coast of the United States of America. It was discovered by the U.S. shortly before the Great War, and the crew was captured before they could scuttle the submarine. The two-man crew then attempted to commit suicide with cyanide pills, but only the captain's pill worked, and the surviving crew member was transferred to Turtledove Detention Camp.

The submarine is still partially functional by 2277. While the player is unable to interact with much of the submarine's equipment, it still has functional electric generators on board.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
Above the waterline are a small stranded boat and a buoy. Below, is a medium-sized submarine with a hatch on top.

Interior:
The submarine, based on her external size, is extremely compact inside. There is only one accessible room, with just two beds available. The ladder leads straight into the roof and a pipe spraying water is also severed in another point but not leaking. There is a silver mainframe computer at the forward end of the chamber, and a generator leaking some kind of green goo to the aft. The sub has about a foot of irradiated water along the floor.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text: • Stealth Boy - Inside the submarine, on the operations terminal, next to a Chinese pistol.

loc_0400811e.summary: Haley's Hardware is a small building north of Pilgrim's Landing in 2277. Its only inhabitant is its sole proprietor, Haley. It has only one interior section.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Nothing is known about the shop before the bombs fell. Haley, the merchant who currently lives and works there, woke up with a case of amnesia not knowing who or where he was, but since people kept coming to buy things he decided to become a merchant, taking the shop's name and calling himself "Haley."

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
Like most houses in Point Lookout, Haley's Hardware is a small wooden shack with a pile of rubble next to it.

Interior:
Inside on the right there is a bedroom with a bed and chest at the foot of the bed, a kitchen with some empty cabinets, and a bathroom. The part of the house where Haley does business with the people of Point Lookout has a counter and a locker holding Haley's inventory and requires a key. There is also a workbench that can be used to the left of the bathroom. A bottlecap mine on the bench can be stolen, which results in negative Karma. There is also an Average locked safe containing various loot.

• Bottlecap mine - On the workbench.

loc_0400811f.summary: The trapper's shack is a shack with a basement in Point Lookout in 2277. It is inhabited by around half a dozen swampfolk.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The trapper's shack is the northernmost point in the middle of the "Trapper's Triangle," which stretches between here, the grower's shack in the west, and the Lil' Tyke Playhouse to the southeast. The shack itself is full of traps.

The trapper who lives here entertains himself by capturing mutated creatures in cages, and pitting them against one another in the basement. Two large cells have been set up, with an electronically-controlled door between them.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The main section of the shack has a similar layout to other shacks in Point Lookout, but highly cluttered. There are many traps laying out in the open. Many of the swampfolk's "bone-tree" and doll-based totems have been constructed inside, some of them in flowerpots. The bathtub is full of whiskey bottles and moonshine-related items.

The shack's cellar is accessible through a door on the back of the building. There are two connected cages here. One cell holds six swamp ghouls, and the other imprisons a swamplurk. They are hostile towards each other. An electric switch on the table will open the door between the cages. There is also a workbench off to the left.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Bottlecap mine on the workbench in the cellar.
• A miniature bottle of Nuka-Cola Quantum can be found in the swamplurk's cage in the cellar, on top of the two safes.
• The only strange meat pie outside of Andale is found in the cellar, buried under miscellaneous meats in the cooler off to the left.
• A Stealth Boy on a table in the bedroom.

loc_0400d971.summary: Recruitment Station is a interior location in Supply Depot (Point Lookout). Featured in quests: The Velvet Curtain.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A recruitment center located at 1811 St. Mary's Branch in Point Lookout, serving to enlist individuals in the United States Navy.

The center also served as a location from which Lieutenant Krumfolz of the Defense Intelligence Agency operated. Krumfolz had been monitoring Doctor Jiang, an agent posing as a defector from China and due to a public news release, local community informants of Point Lookout provided information to Krumfolz regarding Jiang's contact Wan Yang, resulting in her capture and subsequent imprisonment at Turtledove Detention Camp.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
A small building with a sign hanging above the door. Down the street to the west is the Homestead Motel, and the bank. It is adjacent to the broken bumper car ride.

There are two rooms inside with some radroaches in them. The second room has a terminal, safe, a skeleton holding a double-barrel shotgun, a mini nuke and several custom weapon parts.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text: Mini nuke - On the table next to the terminal in the second room.

It requires a special code (see The Velvet Curtain) and the cryptochromatic spectacles to get in through the secret door. Inside is a large number of stacked ammunition boxes and loot. loc_0400f28f.summary: Coastal grotto is a small cave in Point Lookout in 2277. It is where Plik lives and holds a "safari" of sorts with ghouls as the hunt. There are also two men, Jacob Humboldt and Rip Smithy, in the safari chamber, who will most likely die by the end of the safari. It only has one interior section.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
There is a buoy outside, just east of where the door to get inside is. The door itself is up the cliffside and the Lone Wanderer will need to climb up. With careful jumping, it is possible to reach the entrance from the top of the cliff (i.e. near the Ark & Dove resting grounds). Also, there are some swamplurks around the coastline.

Two buoys can be seen in front of the entrance. Beneath the northern buoy is a shipwreck with a first aid box and a Very Easy locked safe. Below the southern buoy is the skeleton of a Tyrannosaurus Rex or similar dinosaur, along with a human skeleton with a lever-action rifle. Nearby are two ammunition boxes and an Average locked safe.

Interior:
Inside, there is a long tunnel that leads to Plik.

sections.text: The Ark & Dove Cathedral is named after the English settling ships Ark and Dove, which landed in the region in 1634.

sections.text:

An old church surrounded by a brick wall with a gate at the entrance. Outside, there are many refined punga fruit and wild punga fruit and two double-barrel shotguns hidden under bushes and separately lying right next to the building. Jimson, Croatoa, and other tribals can be found tending to punga plants or walking around. To the northwest is a well that leads to the sea cave, as well as the Ark & Dove resting grounds.

Interior:
Inside, there are special breeding pots that are used to grow refined punga fruit. Woodrose and Nadine can be found at the back of the church. Other tribals wander around inside periodically, as well.

loc_04009b39.summary: Plik's Safari is a interior location in Interior Location (Point Lookout). Connects directly to Coastal Grotto. Featured in quests: Plik's Safari.

sections.title: Detailed walkthrough
sections.text:
When first entering the coastal grotto, there is a small room on the right which contains Plik's journal (on the desk), and some minor loot. Reading it awards the Ghoul Ecology perk, which gives a 5 point damage bonus when fighting ghouls. Plik is located further down the hallway, and offers a chance to join his small hunting club, but only if paid the entry fee of 1,000 caps. Pay the fee, and ask to join in the next safari.

Join the safari:
Enter the door behind Plik, and meet the other contestants for this hunting excursion, Jacob Humboldt and Rip Smithy. After preparations have been made to begin the hunt, flip the switch on the block in the center of the room.

Survive Plik's Safari:
Several waves of leveled feral ghouls, ranging from swamp ghouls to glowing ones will begin swarming the platform and immediate area.

sections.title: Reward
sections.text: The Dismemberer and 100 XP. After the last feral ghoul stops breathing, the safari is over. Walk out, and talk to Plik to receive the reward: The Dismemberer, a unique axe Plik pilfered from one of his club members who "won't be needing it anymore."

sections.title: Loot, Objects & Related Quests
sections.text: Standard wasteland containers and supplies. Interactive objects: Door, Cell Door, Switch. Related quests: Plik's Safari.

loc_04008122.summary: Miner's Rest is a interior location in Kenny's Cave (Point Lookout). Connects directly to Herzog Mine, Blackdamp Shaft. Featured in quests: Latchkey Kenny.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
To reach Kenny's cave the first time, one might go through Herzog Mine as it leads to Miner's Rest, where Kenny resides. The surface entrance might prove much harder to find.

Kenny may be grudgingly encouraged to allow the Lone Wanderer to share his hideout. This requires passing a Speech check, using Child at Heart or the retrieval of Kenny's bear which can be found in the nearby mirelurk and swamplurk infested "Blackdamp Shaft."

Once Kenny gives his approval:
• The cot will grant the player character the Well Rested effect.
• Kenny will be available to play both Hide and Go Seek and Tag.
• The ladder to Point Lookout will be accessible.
• All interactive loot items and storage will be free for the taking with no hostility or Karma penalty.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
During the Sino-American War, this location was used to detain and interrogate those suspected of being Chinese agents. Prisoners were kept in abysmal conditions, with outhouses being the only sanitary facilities available and bunk beds crammed into wooden houses serving as living quarters. Watchtowers with searchlights were erected at the perimeter while many security robots patrolled the base.

All dead bodies were stored in the morgue, beneath the administration building. The morgue also contained a small crematorium, where bodies were disposed of, as well as a drainage channel leading outside the camp. The camp administration had known that the morgue drainage could be used for an escape attempt, and hoped to catch any potential escapees in the act.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The detention camp is composed of six constructs including four wooden buildings (bunkhouse A and B, and two interrogation rooms), a concrete administration building and an underground morgue. There is a metal barrel south of Interrogation Room A with a skeleton inside of it. Inside the morgue, there is a waste tunnel that leads to the outside. The camp is fenced and several guard towers are located at the corners of the fence, as well as at the entrance.

Many hostile feral ghouls and sentry bots can be found in and around the camp. A group of three to four smugglers may spawn here as well. In addition, there are sentry bots as well as turrets mounted under the guard towers. The radioactive environment is the home of several ghouls. Even after the area is cleared out, new ghouls will continue to migrate to the camp.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Mini nuke - On the shelf in the administration's armory.
• Stealth Boy - In the bunkhouse A's locker in front of the player on the shelf.
• Submarine self-destruct codes - By opening the cadaver compartment that houses the remains of Wan Yang in the morgue underneath the Turtledove Detention Camp.
• Toy knife - Can be found directly south of Turtledove Detention Camp, close to the yellow entryway sign. Past the sign, one will see a long line of bushes to the west/northwest. Behind these bushes is the toy knife sitting next to a hockey mask on a crate.

loc_04008123.summary: Herzog Mine is a location in Point Lookout in 2277. Herzog Mine is set into the rock, to the south of the Ark & Dove resting grounds and southwest of the Coastal grotto.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Herzog mining site was named after its owner, Old Man Herzog, who put his miners through poor working conditions. According to Kenny, who lives in the mine, a group of miners sat down and refused to work any longer in the mine's poor conditions. In response, Herzog blew up the site with a "million million tons" of dynamite, killing the miners. As a result, no one else was willing to work in the mine, leaving it abandoned by all but Herzog. After he detonated his explosives, Kenny says that old man Herzog then hung himself.

The swampfolk believe the mine is haunted, and thus most of them avoid it. Kenny uses this to his advantage, noting that those who do enter the mine are easy to scare away with a few simple traps.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Exterior:
Herzog Mine is set into the rock cliffs south of the Ark & Dove resting grounds. It can be accessed by a path down the rocks from the top of the cliff, or by climbing up to it from the beach below. It consists of a small cave entrance with some rubbish around.

Interior:
The mine consists of a linear set of cavernous passages winding into the cliffside. Various branches of the mine have collapsed, due to explosives set off before the Great War. Kenny is the mine's only inhabitant, and has set up numerous traps to make the mine seem haunted, including bear traps. Eventually, winding through the passages will lead to Miner's Rest, or Kenny's cave.

Kenny's cave:
Kenny's cave is a section of Herzog Mine in which Kenny has taken up residence. From here, the mine can be exited via a ladder in Kenny's living space.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Kenny's cave contains one of the add-on's two Pint-Sized Slasher masks.
• After falling down the mine shaft in Blackdamp Shaft, Kenny-bear will be leaning against a pile of cinder blocks.

loc_04002881.summary: Calvert Mansion is a large Victorian mansion located in Point Lookout in 2277. It is inhabited by Desmond Lockheart, a 200-year-old ghoul from before the Great War.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The mansion is one of the largest buildings on the peninsula, the other being Blackhall Manor. The mansion itself, while being in excellent condition compared to buildings in the Capital Wasteland, is still in bad shape. A good amount of the wood is rotting, and parts of the floor will break if they are stepped on.

The mansion bears the name Calvert from its former inhabitants, the powerful Calvert family. The Calvert family were a major force in pre-War Maryland, spawning a political dynasty that saw family members elected to various offices at both the state and national levels.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Calvert Mansion is inhabited by a ghoul named Desmond Lockheart and his two dogs, Freki and Geri. He has been attacked numerous times by a group of tribals, whose aim is to raze the mansion to the ground. According to Tobar, the building holds hidden treasures.

The place is filled with ammunition and medical supplies set up by Desmond, which can be used to survive the tribal attack. In the numerous wardrobes/cupboards are pre-War outfits, hats, and bonnets.

Inside Desmond's corner is an assortment of weapons, ranging from a sledgehammer to a flamer, as well as a punga experiment that will illuminate a light bulb.

Panic room:
The panic room is a room under Calvert Mansion that was designed to be a shelter in the case of an attack. It can only be accessed after the quest Thought Control.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Several undersized drinking glasses and forks on and around the table in the dining room.
• One undersized Nuka-Cola Quantum in the panic room.
• Over 30 bottles of wine in the wine cellar, some of them cannot be taken.
• Desmond's eyeglasses - Worn by Desmond.

loc_04002edf.summary: The excavated muck holes are unmarked locations in the Fallout 3 add-on Point Lookout, found one block east and slightly north of the Lil' Tyke Playhouse. They are part of the An Antique Land side quest.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The excavated muck holes are the result of a Bysshe Company pre-War research team surveying bio-gas. The muck holes are heavily irradiated, abandoned, contain gas pockets, and contain the soil sample holotapes. If the player character uses flame-based weapons, merely stepping into a pocket of gas while equipped with the flamer, Shishkebab, or various other flame weapons with it drawn will cause the gas to ignite, setting them on fire. Likewise, drawing such a weapon while standing in gas will also cause it to ignite.

Sample site one:
This excavated muck hole is north of the trash heap. Inside there is a desk with a few items on it, such as:
• Soil survey tape #1
• Two bio-gas canisters
• One fission battery
• One advanced radiation suit
• Outside the muck hole there is a destroyed shack, a couple feral ghouls and a muck pool.

loc_05000f96.summary: Robot Assembly is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Engineering Core. Featured in quests: Among the Stars.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The robot assembly is where support and guardian drones are assembled. It is also the location of one of the generators that must be destroyed during the quest Among the Stars.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The robot assembly entrance is directly west of the engineering core. The area is U-shaped, with two floors. Most of the second floor will initially be inaccessible to the player character, but if the player character took Somah with them, she will tinker with the teleporter and will be teleported into the second floor.

Using some stairs and heading down to the first floor will trigger an alarm (the same one used in the holding cells) and six support drones and guardian drones with drone cannons will be teleported into the two rooms with the teleportation platforms in them. There are also three alien workers which pose no threat and will run around.

A section of the assembly line (A) must be destroyed to gain access to the generator, where one alien turret is seen on the ceiling.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• The drone control device can be looted from the first alien seen in the area beyond the assembly line that Somah says to blow up.
• 44 alien power cells can be found on/near a corner shelf in the first downstairs chamber, near a small container, opposite the robot escalator. 2 pieces of 12 rounds clip into the wall at the back of the shelf and are only obtainable with.
• 39 alien crystals (22 small, 17 large), the highest amount in a single section aboard the ship.

loc_05002fd1.summary: Space Walk is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Decompression Chamber. Featured in quests: Among the Stars.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The space walk cannot be entered without the spacesuit being worn. The player character cannot use the Pip-Boy or use any weapons on the map. There are no enemies, although the Lone Wanderer can see some aliens running fast with their weapons out around the corridors below the transparent parts of floor. The player character must locate three panels that stand out slightly from the ship's hull. They are emitting a yellow glow to make them obvious. Activate all three panels and the transporter to the next portion of the ship will become available. The transporter is located directly in the center of the circular hull the player character is traversing.

loc_05008ec7.summary: Research Lab is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Cargo Hold.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The research lab is an area of Mothership Zeta accessible via the cargo hold. It is unnecessary to visit the research lab to gain access to the bridge and further the main questline. However, the area becomes inaccessible after leaving the engineering core and all chance of retrieving captive recordings towards the Alien Archivist achievement/trophy will be permanently lost if not explored before taking the teleporter to the bridge. One should enter the research lab via the door in the southwest of the cargo hold (the door leading to the research lab next to where one first enters the cargo hold will be initially locked. It can be unlocked by pressing the button on the other side of the door - this requires accessing the research lab through the southwest door in the cargo hold).

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The research lab consists of two large main areas that are connected by a hallway. Upon entering, the player character finds themselves in the vehicular research area. This area contains a single large room with various vehicles and mechanical devices. The hallway leading to the Giddyup Buttercup research area is immediately south from the entrance to this room.

The Giddyup Buttercup research area has two levels and is comprised of a large room with three connected smaller rooms. The southernmost room in this area contains a teleportation matrix that the player character can activate in order to return to the cargo hold.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
In the first section (vehicular study):
• Alien captive recorded log 13 - Across from the warehouse door.
• 37 toy cars - In the entrance to the hallway that connects the vehicular study area to the Buttercup warehouse area.

In the second section (Buttercup warehouse):
• Alien captive recorded log 21 - Across from the healing archway.
• Buttercup toy - In the larger Buttercup warehouse, southwest corner (across from a work table on the second level of the storage shelf).

loc_05007397.summary: The maintenance level and the connected waste disposal are locations onboard Mothership Zeta in 2277.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Maintenance level:
If the Lone Wanderer uses the teleportation matrix, next to the door to robot assembly, to the maintenance level during Among the Stars, they will find Sally attempting to fix the control panel on a Zeta trash can. She explains that she is not really lost and they both might find 'something neat'. Before long though, it starts moving, and it's a long way down...

The trash can stops at several levels of the Zeta Mothership, a small hatch to the player character's right (when facing Sally) opening for them to look and shoot out:
• A level with a single alien shooting at the player character.
• A level containing brahmin. ("We're having burgers tonight!") and also ("Cows? We got cows!")... perhaps a reference to a line from "Twister."
• A level with a Corvega in pristine condition.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• In the vicinity of the first aliens encountered in waste disposal, in a high-ceiling room with a low metal catwalk, a military footlocker can be found on the floor to the right of the railing, against the east wall. It contains General Chase's overcoat along with a blank holotape labeled Anchorage quartermaster shipment.
• Alien captive recorded log #19 is in the room past the hallway of trash compactors, in the room where Sally says "ambush", just before the LAST room with the teleporter.
• At the end of waste disposal, in the room where Sally meets the player character and wants to race them to the teleporter - opposite the getting into that room, in a closet type area with lots of medical kits, on the shelf in front of the player character is the samurai's sword.

sections.title: Loot, Objects & Related Quests
sections.text: Notable items: Tin Can, Bent Tin Can, Empty Whisky Bottle, Milk Bottle, Empty Soda Bottle. Interactive objects: Door, Teleportation Matrix.

loc_05000ef8.summary: The living quarters are a location on board Mothership Zeta. The player must travel through this location as part of the quest This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough...

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The aliens themselves apparently use it as a place to sleep in small stasis chambers dotted around the central area, and have fortified the position with two pairs of force field generators and two alien turrets.

The living quarters are composed of three main rooms linked by hallways. The first room is a small atrium with side balconies blocked by force fields, so in order to go further the player must jump down from the balcony to the floor below. Alternatively, the player can destroy the force field generators with weapons, to facilitate a return the same way. In the atrium, the player must fight three aliens with two turrets.

There are very few points of interest; most of the rooms contain only empty stasis chambers. Going further, the player will enter a hallway crossing. The left (east) corridor leads to a room.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text: • Alien captive recorded log 23 - Holotape, in the cafeteria (the large western room), on the east wall, immediately to the right upon entering the diner.

sections.title: Loot, Objects & Related Quests
sections.text: Notable items: Small Alien Crystal, Large Alien Crystal. Interactive objects: Door, Teleportation Matrix.

loc_05002fd2.summary: Engineering Core is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Cryo Lab, Cargo Hold, Robot Assembly. Featured in quests: Not of This World, This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough..., Among the Stars.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The engineering core is the third area that the Lone Wanderer encounters aboard the mothership, and serves as a hub between numerous other locations aboard the ship, including the steamworks, hangar, cryo lab, robot assembly, cargo hold, maintenance level and engine room. Here, the player can also find several other captives who will assist them aboard the ship. As one progresses through the main quest, the engineering core changes. Defenses are put up and barricades are made by the other captives; eventually, a broken Nuka-Cola vending machine will show up; a teleporter to the Bridge appears near the steamworks entrance, down a corridor to the left of the Nuka-Cola machine; and a terrified alien will appear and plead for its life, only to be shot by Paulson.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Power core:
The central power for Mothership Zeta is at the center of the map. The lower level surrounding the core contains little of interest.

Lower observation deck:
The lower level is far smaller than the top level. It has a small room where Toshiro Kago sits most of the time with a large window that displays the reaches of space. There is a table opposite Kago and a footlocker near that. Across the window is a hallway that has some garbage in the middle of it. Through this hallway, one will reach the main part of the lower floor. This has a main energy pillar in the middle of it, surrounded by capacitors. Also, on this floor underneath the stairs is a bed for the player character to sleep on.

Upper observation deck:
In Kago's room is a staircase that leads up to the second level.

sections.title: Loot, Objects & Related Quests
sections.text: Notable items: Tin Can, Coffee Mug, Bent Tin Can, Empty Whisky Bottle, Wrench, Milk Bottle. Interactive objects: Toolbox, First Aid Box, Door, Teleportation Matrix, Work Bench, Stasis Controls. Related quests: Not of This World, This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough..., Among the Stars, Mothership Zeta: Steerage Rats.

loc_05004a12.summary: The experimentation lab is a location on board Mothership Zeta. It appears to be the origin of the ship's abominations.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Based on the name of this area, the captive recordings found, the odd machinery, and the abominations in holding cells at the end, it is probable that the aliens are creating the abominations here as part of some scientific experiment on human anatomy.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
This level is easily navigated and completed. For the most part, it runs northwest and west, eventually entering a room with a generator. The experimentation lab is located between the weapons lab and the biological research areas of Mothership Zeta. It mostly contains three alien workers who will simply run from the player character, and a single hostile weapon-using alien. A healing archway is located in a locked room to the left, just before entering the generator room.

The next room has the first appearance of the abominations, seen in five small chambers with white force field door. Four alien workers are seen walking around in the room, and two abominations are seen dead on lab tables, one with its leg cut off and with an alien worker standing nearby with a sliver alien tablet.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Alien captive recorded log 9 - Holotape, near the tables with the abominations being operated on.
• Alien captive recorded log 10 - Holotape, in the room with the core and the core coolant switches; look on the right wall of the room for the log.
• Alien captive recorded log 20 - Holotape, found by taking a right from the entrance and heading further right until one enters a room with the experimentation chairs. It is on the wall in front of those chairs.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text: The engine room is mostly circular with one inaccessible door, forcing the player character to explore the area in a clockwise fashion. The area inaccessible via the main room is linear, with straight hallways and corridors. Scattered throughout are aliens, support drones and guardian drones. There are also a few opportunities for one to sabotage turrets.

loc_0500098b.summary: Cargo Hold is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Engineering Core, Research Lab.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The cargo hold is accessible through a door on the east side of the engineering core just south of the door to the hangar. It is filled with human clutter neatly organized on metal shelves, the metal shelves have various items from teddy bears, and baby cribs, to missile launchers. The cache is guarded by aliens and their guardian drones and alien turrets.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The cargo hold is an area of the ship which the player character does not have to visit in order to complete the storyline of Mothership Zeta, but can be worthwhile due to the wide variety of items housed within. A unique and potent variant of the plasma pistol, the MPLX Novasurge, is obtained here.

The cargo hold consists of one upper and a few lower walkways, the lower area consists of a large conveyor belt, and a disposal area. To the left of the entrance from the Engineering core is a locked door (which is unlocked from the other side in the research lab) concealing a teleporter to the research lab. To the right of the entrance are three alien containers.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Two bottlecap mines - On a shelf to the right of the south research lab entrance.
• Reid Underwood's terminal - Unlocks Underwood's safe near the waste disposal hole. (A)
• A mini nuke - On the conveyor belt.
• MPLX Novasurge - Unique plasma pistol located in Underwood's safe. (B)

loc_05002fd3.summary: Steamworks is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Engineering Core.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The steamworks is a massive series of conduits and machinery designed to help propel Mothership Zeta through space. It is a sub-area to the engineering deck and the second level encountered.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The area starts out in a short corridor with a small room to the right containing nothing of interest. At the intersection is a dead end to the right and at the left end is another short "T" intersection that dead ends back to the left. To the right, the corridor curves westward. A door on the left leads to another corridor that runs parallel to the main one and has a healing archway near the end. At the conjunction of the two corridors, the main one curves around to the north and ends in an orange lit room.

This room houses a loot chest and three doors leading to other areas. The door on the left opens up to stairs and a catwalk that has doors on the left containing a chest and some alien epoxy.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text: • 48 alien power cells - Can be found on a shelf in the upper northwest room with a healing archway.

loc_0500481f.summary: The death ray control is a location on board Mothership Zeta. It is a single large room serving as the control center for Zetas death ray.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The death ray control room is a huge square shaped room with four power generators in the corners of the room, on the walls of this room are long rectangle shaped windows, where one can see outer space and the sun.

Looking down you will see the death ray, which have to be destroyed as a part of the quest This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough... The death ray itself is visible beneath the glass floor and gives a view of the post-war Earth. The room has two teleporters leading to the living quarters and the death ray hub.

The death ray can be fired from this room by using the buttons on the two consoles. The two buttons on the right aim the death ray at one of two pre-targeted locations.

loc_05004a13.summary: The biological research is a location on board Mothership Zeta. It contains two medium-sized chambers and is inhabited by both aliens and abominations.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: There are two dead aliens lying around, which were probably killed by the escaped abominations. Their corpses can be looted for alien atomizers, disintegrators and other items.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The biological research is located between the experimentation lab and the bridge. The area contains two (sometimes three) abominations in the first chamber, an alien worker in the second room, and two regular hostile aliens.

In the second chamber are three transport matrices, one leading to the observation deck, one to the bridge and one to the death ray hub. The observation deck transporter must be activated in order to allow the other survivors through. The teleporter to the bridge is shut down and the player character must go to the death ray hub to continue the quest.

sections.title: Notable loot

• Alien captive recorded log 18.
• 109 alien power cells located on a shelf in the downstairs section of the entrance to the bridge.

loc_05001616.summary: Cryo Lab is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Engineering Core, Cryo Storage.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This location is used by the Zetan aliens to store abductees tagged for collection or for temporary storage when they are not being experimented on. As of late 2277, it houses frozen feral ghouls, raiders, and four super mutants.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Cryo lab:
On the lower level by the entrance, there is a small room containing a healing archway, three containers and various loot. The teleporter to the far right is across a catwalk and is used as an exit after the destruction of the generator. Going back up the stairs leads to a hallway with a metal rack on the wall holding one tray of alien worm food.

The next part of the map is a large, rectangular silver room with three visible blue transparent cryopods holding three frozen naked raiders. Aliens and a single turret are seen in this area. The player character can defrost all of these at once by pushing the button on the console below the window facing the area. This results in four more cryopods raising from the ground and a battle starting between the three feral ghouls, five weaponless raiders, and the aliens and their turret.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• Two suits of winterized medic armor and two winterized medic helmets, worn by Daniels and Beckett.
• A Chinese commando hat. Look for a room with the option to "rig the controller to explode" on the panel outside.
• A rare police hat can be found in the lower level of the large room that has several cryo-pods that contains raiders and feral ghouls along with a turret.

Alien captive recordings:
There are a total of six alien captive recorded logs to be collected in these zones; four in the cryo lab (2, 4, 11 and 17) and two in the cryo storage (16 and 25). See the recorded logs' page for details.

loc_05004820.summary: Death Ray Hub is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Biological Research, Death Ray Control. Featured in quests: This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough....

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
From the teleport point, follow the corridor to the left to reach a small room and use the terminal next to the door to open it. Within this room is a container and a support drone. The drone can be rewired and activated so that it targets enemies of the player.

To the right from the teleporter leads to a room symmetrical to the other small one, also containing a support drone. This drone may also be rewired and activated to provide useful support to the player. Several aliens will be coming from the only door left coming from this room. Follow this path to come into a large room. There is a healing archway, and to the right is a turret terminal that can be used to disable the nearby turret.

Continue following the fairly linear path. There are not many alien enemies, but lots of alien workers.

loc_05004a14.summary: The weapons lab is a location on board Mothership Zeta. The player must travel via this location as a part of This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough... quest.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This facility is located on the upper level of Mothership Zeta through a door leading from the observation deck. As the name indicates, the lab is the place where alien weapons are being created and tested, thus, many standard weapons as well as several unique versions of these weapons can be found here, They may also be studying human energy weapons here, as evidenced by a few energy weapons on a table.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Passing through the door near the teleporter that has been deactivated leads to a large room. Almost immediately, there will be a confrontation with two ceiling mounted alien turrets. Additionally, a couple of aliens and a guardian drone inhabit this room. Heading southwest, there is a small room on the right (open it via the control panel just next to it with a Science check of 75) that holds the atomic pulverizer, which is a unique and slightly upgraded version of the alien atomizer.

Continuing through this passageway will lead to a three-way intersection. Left is a blocked passageway, right goes to a flight of stairs. Go up the stairs and then take the first left to wind up on the platform from which the aliens first encountered in this room were.

sections.title: Notable loot
sections.text:
• 87 alien power cells on a counter, usable with the alien blaster, in the room with other human and alien technology consisting of several ordinary alien weapons and a Gatling laser (south in local map).
• Destabilizer (unique version of alien disintegrator) on a shelf in the training area, next to exit (B on the map).
• Atomic pulverizer (unique version of alien atomizer), as well as a Buttercup toy, in the room containing a drone pod behind an unlockable door in one of the corridors (D on the map), plus even more alien power cells on the same shelf.
• Two drone cannon Ex-Bs (unique drone cannon), obtainable by killing the experimental weapons drones (C on the map).
• Alien captive recorded log 24 in the same room as the alien power cells.

loc_05002fce.summary: The bridge is an open, two-tiered deck on Mothership Zeta in 2277. four aliens reside here along with the alien captain.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The bridge serves as the ship's main control room, upon entering the room you will see the captain calmly sitting in his chair simply looking at the two aliens in front of him. The captain himself is fairly weak and simply acts as another regular alien, but he does carry a powerful weapon, the Captain's Sidearm, which fires multiple shots at once.

Once he is dead, a large orange holographic alien head will speak to the player character, but as always, it is impossible to understand. Once he has finished talking, another mothership, identical to Zeta passes by, and attacks the Zeta with its death ray, presumably trying to stop you from taking over Zeta.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Mothership Zetas bridge consists of several distinct areas or compartments.
• An entry compartment contains
• a workbench to the extreme rear
• a transporter to the Capital Wasteland (only functions after the quest is completed)
• a stasis unit (alien "bed") on the left (port) side of the compartment
• a door connecting this compartment with the rest of the bridge.
• A "captain's compartment", immediately forward of the entry compartment, contains
• a transporter to the engineering section on the left (port) side
• a healing archway on the right (starboard) side
• doors on the fore and aft sides of the compartment.

loc_0500428e.summary: Decompression Chamber is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Engineering Core, Space Walk. Featured in quests: Among the Stars.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This is the area used by the player character to get to the upper section of the spacecraft, following the destruction of the three generators. The entrance to it is next to the work bench of the engineering core and will be locked until all three generators have been blown up. There is a large button in the middle of the room that starts decompression. Note that the astronaut's spacesuit must be worn before depressurization to avoid explosive-decompression and the death of the player character. Dead alien bodies may be found scattered around after leaving the first chamber (presumably killed by the depressurisation process).

loc_05000f94.summary: Hangar is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Part of the Mothership Zeta dataset (EditorID: DLC05testJesse).

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
The hangar is the part of the ship where smaller spacecraft may enter and exit Mothership Zeta. It has room for a single smaller craft to be "docked," suspended in midair using energy fields. Upon entering, one will notice a large open hole on the ground, with outer space visible below, and recon craft Theta will be suspended above it in energy fields from eight pylons around the hole.

The hangar holds one of the generators that must be destroyed as part of Among the Stars. If the player character has requested his help, Paulson will follow them into this area. Once reaching the upper control center and activating a button, an alarm will go off, alerting the aliens to the player character's presence. This begins a battle using the gravity beams that hold up recon craft Theta.

loc_05002fcf.summary: Observation Deck is a interior location in Interior Location (Mothership Zeta). Connects directly to Engineering Core, Weapons Lab, Biological Research. Featured in quests: This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough..., Among the Stars.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The observation deck is a room with a large glass floor through which the player character and any surviving companions witness the aliens firing the death ray towards Earth. Initially, it is accessed from the space walk. Later, one can teleport to/from the observation deck and the engineering core.

Below the observation deck's glass floor, in the center of the room, which is facing Earth; one can see what appears to be the East Coast and Central America extending down below Florida and upwards north of Canada. Including this, one can make out the Great Lakes and Michigan.

chr_0007e952.behavior: Very Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_0007e952.summary: Talon Company mercs are members of the Talon Company, a mercenary company operating in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only rank 1 mercs can be enslaved

Other interactions:
• Talon Company mercs are almost always hostile to the Lone Wanderer wherever they are encountered. In some areas, like Takoma Industrial and the Capitol Building, they will be found in combat with other groups such as super mutants, but will still be hostile to the player character.
• Talon Company mercs are involved in various random encounters across the Capital Wasteland, as well as in scripted encounters in certain locations, both in the base game and in Broken Steel.

Talon Company hit squads:
If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

chr_0007086e.summary: William Brandice was an Enclave deserter and former resident of the Brandice's house in Grayditch, whose corpse can be found in Marigold station in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
William was the husband of Sheila and the father of Will Brandice. Originally stationed at Camp Navarro, Brandice eventually deserted from the Enclave. He journeyed across the continent with his family, hopping from settlement to settlement to avoid capture by the Enclave. In October 2276, they finally settled down at Grayditch in the Capital Wasteland, with William setting up as a doctor. The settlement was appealing to William not just because of the distance, but also because his son Will got along well with Bryan Wilks, the child who lived across the road from them.

The peace did not last long. On October 30, 2276, William discovered a radio broadcasting Enclave Radio, with the old patriotic music and the speeches of President John Henry Eden. He immediately grew paranoid, fearing that the Enclave could be coming for him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Those!: Brandice is found dead in the ant tunnels.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Marigold Station. Notable equipment & inventory: William Brandice's Key, Ant Nectar, itm_0003c345, Biker Goggles, itm_000340ff.

chr_0006c69b.summary: Scientist is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 25 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Scientists are found wearing bright yellow radiation suits or lab coats. Some carry skill books that can be taken from their remains. Their bodies are sometimes surrounded by chems and weapons, among the detritus.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One scientist is located in a truck on a highway south of Raven Rock. When one approaches, an explosion goes off inside the truck and the body of a scientist flies out the back, off the bridge. He is carrying a Big Book of Science.
• Another scientist can be found outside Vault 87 in a highly irradiated area. Her body is found in a pile of miscellaneous objects and bones.
• Yet another scientist is found dead in a wastelander camp along a lake. A drowned raider can be found near the bloody corpses of the scientist and a wastelander nearby.
• The final scientist is found dead near a dumptruck in the Greener Pastures disposal site. She is found lying near a pile of radioactive barrels and a Big Book of Science is found next to her remains.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Sensor Module, Radiation Suit, Surgical Tubing.

chr_0006c5c9.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: follow, patrol, sandbox
chr_0006c5c9.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC06a (Vernon Square — North). Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. chr_0006c583.summary: Jim Wilkins is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101 Entrance.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The Lone Wanderer remembers Jim from their days playing "Grognak the Barbarian" in the Vault cafeteria. Son of Officer Wilkins, he was always game for a laugh. He and his sister Janice are found dead upon the Lone Wanderer's return to Vault 101.

chr_0006c582.summary: Chip Taylor is a dead Vault 101 resident found near the entrance to the Vault's upper level during Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Born a year or two after the Lone Wanderer, Chip's ambition was to be a Vault technician like Stanley Armstrong. His plans were cut short by the chaos that took over Vault 101 after James' escape: Chip was killed in the factional struggle, near the upper levels.

chr_0006c581.summary: Steve Armstrong is a resident of Vault 101. He is found dead at the vault's entrance during Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Steve was adopted by Stanley Armstrong and his unmarried daughter, Beatrice. He was given his foster parents' surname and spent most of his youth sick, and the Lone Wanderer knew him mostly by conversations with Stanley. Steve survived into adulthood, just in time to see James and the Wanderer flee Vault 101. Caught up in the upheaval that followed their departure, Steve apparently tried to sneak out on his own, using a pilfered Stealth Boy, but ran into a radroach on his way out, ending his life prematurely.

sections.text:
Quests:
Trouble on the Homefront: Steve is found dead shortly after re-entering the Vault.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Entrance. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, Stealth Boy, itm_000236d8.

chr_0006c57f.summary: Janice Wilkins is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101 Lower Level.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Lone Wanderer remembers Janice's wavy red hair from their youth. Daughter of Officer Wilkins, she was always quiet. After the Wanderer's escape from Vault 101, she's found dead in the diner area upon their return.

Her brother, Jim Wilkins, is also found dead during Trouble on the Homefront. If their father, Officer Wilkins, encounters/is encountered by the Lone Wanderer, he will attack in vengeance for the Wanderer's involvement in their deaths.
