chr_0006bc15.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: puzzled. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox
chr_0006bc15.summary: Officer Wilkins is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Sub-Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Related to Janice and Jim Wilkins, Officer Wilkins is much less forgiving than Officer Taylor and he blames the Lone Wanderer directly for the chaos currently affecting Vault 101. He is liable to attack as soon as he gives the Lone Wanderer a tongue-lashing.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Trouble on the Homefront: Wilkins is one of the security guards encountered in the vault and one of the few guards that are hostile. He is in possession of one of the passwords unlocking the terminal in the jail section of Vault 101.

Effects of player's actions:
When the Lone Wanderer returns to the vault in Trouble on the Homefront, Wilkins angrily talks about how much he despises them and their father, blaming the two for the dire situation Vault 101 is in after they escaped, saying, "You never should have left, kid. And now we'll make sure that nobody ever leaves again!" This is most likely due to the deaths of his two children during the vault riot.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Sub-Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Security Helmet, Pip-Boy Glove, Police Baton, Vault 101 Security Armor, Jail Cell Password, itm_000236d8.

chr_000655e7.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_000655e7.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_0005c341.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Weapons, Armor, Supplies / Barter)
chr_0005c341.summary: Chief Gustavo is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Metro Access & Generator.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Prior to becoming security chief of Tenpenny Tower, Gustavo worked his way up to become leader of a mercenary band of professional fighters. Mister Burke was rescued by Gustavo and his band, and quickly hired him and his men to form the security force at the Tower. His personality is gruff, but also good natured in a "Don't give me grief, I'm just doing my job, ma'am" sort of manner. However, he soon becomes a loud no-nonsense hard-ass when his team or his charges are in immediate danger. He is particularly hostile to ghouls. "The only good ghoul is a dead ghoul," is a fond saying of his, particularly if ghouls are nearby. He expressed that "it's only a matter of time before they go zombie" and people shouldn't take the risk. He even goes as far to say that you would be doing them a favor by putting a bullet between their eyes.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: After the Lone Wanderer's first encounter with Gustavo, he is found sitting in the lobby of the hotel or sleeping outside during the night, most of the time he will stand guard at the entrance.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: Gustavo will task the Wanderer with getting rid of the ghoul menace if asked.

chr_0005c340.summary: Allistair Tenpenny is the founder and owner of Tenpenny Tower, appearing. He is one of only nine named characters in the base game to have "Very Evil" Karma. He is also a Legendary dweller, coming with a unique rifle and suit.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Entrepreneur:
Born around, He does not like talking about himself or his past, preferring his achievements to speak for themselves.

As such, little is known about him before the founding of Tenpenny Tower. What is known is that with his fake aristocratic accent,

Shortly after this botched job, Tenpenny met a man who changed his life: Mister Burke. Burke made the restoration of the future Tenpenny Tower (then just a husk of a derelict resort, jutting up from the horizon in southwestern Capital Wasteland) a plausible endeavor, establishing himself as Tenpenny's right-hand man, capable of doing "what needs to get done." A lot of work went into restoring the tower to a fraction of its former glory, and then securing the right kind of tenants to enjoy its security and luxuries.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Tenpenny rarely leaves his penthouse suite, but for the rare occasion he does, he has a seat reserved in Margaret Primrose's cafe. Generally, he has his meals delivered to the penthouse, always ordering an "iguana bit sandwich, no salt, with a peeled pear on the side" for lunch.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom: If the player agrees with Burke's pitch and installs the fusion pulse charge, they will join Tenpenny and Burke to witness the destruction of Megaton in a nuclear explosion. The player will be rewarded with a suite in the tower in return for their services.
• The quest can still be completed even if Roy Phillips had his way with Tenpenny.
• Tenpenny Tower: The Lone Wanderer can convince Tenpenny to give his permission for the ghouls to move in. After the ghouls are allowed to move in, Roy Phillips and Tenpenny will have a "disagreement" and Tenpenny will have an "accident," which results in Tenpenny's body being stuffed in a storage closet.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Mister Crowley wants someone to kill Tenpenny.

chr_0005c336.summary: A Tenpenny resident, or Tenpenny Tower resident is one of the many unnamed inhabitants who reside in the Tenpenny Tower in 2277.

sections.text: They have enough means to stay in the affluent tower, and may disappear and be replaced by ghoul counterparts, depending on the Lone Wanderer's decisions.

sections.text:
Quests:
• Tenpenny Tower: If the Lone Wanderer lets the ghouls into the tower, the feral ghouls will kill every human Tenpenny resident in the building. They are then replaced with ghoul counterparts.

sections.text: Known locations: Metro Access & Generator. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0005c32b.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Alcohol, Food, Supplies / Barter, Apparel & Goods)
chr_0005c32b.summary: Margaret Primrose is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 35 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Metro Access & Generator.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Margaret owns and operates the Café Beau Monde. Because the cafe only serves the residents of Tenpenny Tower, her clientele is limited, allowing Margaret to prepare and serve all the meals. The restaurant is open from 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM, and Margaret is the service provider the entire time. When the restaurant closes, she generally spends her time in her room.

Margaret says she picked up cooking from her late mother. She explains that her mother wasn't always the best, though she showed her love for her family through cooking. Since Allistair Tenpenny refuses to come down from his suite, Margaret has to prepare all his meals and take them up to him herself.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tenpenny Tower: She can be asked to support the ghouls admission to the tower.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Metro Access & Generator. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Alcohol, Food, Supplies / Barter, Apparel & Goods.

chr_0005c32a.summary: Herbert "Daring" Dashwood is a self-proclaimed wasteland adventurer. Long since retired as of 2277, he now resides in Tenpenny Tower in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
According to the 70-year-old Herbert, in his younger days, he was a prolific traveler and adventurer, performing feats that allowed him to amass a big enough fortune to purchase a residency under Allistair Tenpenny for a comfortable retirement. In these adventures, he was accompanied often by a 200-year-old ghoul named Argyle whom he first met in 2241 when Dashwood seduced and stole his girlfriend.

Daring Dashwood's Deeds:
The duo visited many places during their exploration of the wasteland. Dashwood can recall one instance where, in the summer of 2248, they were given permission to take shelter inside Rockopolis by the ruling King Crag. But when Dashwood had an "incident" with Crag's daughter, the two were exiled from the underground city.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Herbert will typically walk around Tenpenny Tower and occasionally play a joke on Cheng by messing with his terminal. He also occasionally visits the Federalist Lounge on the first floor and can otherwise be found in his room where he sits beside his radio.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• A Manhandled Manservant: If Argyle's body has been found, Dashwood can be informed of his fate to receive a key to his safe, which contains bottlecap mine schematics.
• The Replicated Man: Dashwood is in possession of a Replicated Man holotape.
• Tenpenny Tower: While looking for the key to the generator room, he implies the Lone Wanderer should steal it from him as a game. If the player character is caught stealing it, he will turn hostile in the usual way. Asking him to give up the key will provoke a response stating the Lone Wanderer is "no fun."

chr_0005c323.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Chems & Medicine, Supplies / Barter)
chr_0005c323.summary: Doctor Banfield is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 20 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Metro Access & Generator.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The physician for Tenpenny Tower, Banfield runs the wellness center, and is responsible for the health of the Tower's residents. He achieves this primarily by providing them with various prescription drugs and his own concoctions based on pre-War medicines. While Banfield is not terribly fond of the Tower's landlord, he is wary of crossing him. It's not terribly difficult, as Tenpenny rarely comes down and Banfield only had to treat him once, for "bed sores".

It's not clear where Banfield comes from, but he does make mention of some of his scientific colleagues publishing papers. Much of Banfield's knowledge of ghouls, for example, comes from papers published by his colleagues, although he never actually verified their findings (and, unsurprisingly, has never been published).

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tenpenny Tower: Banfield has always wanted to experiment on ghouls so he can learn more about them but hasn't had the opportunity. As a result, Banfield is willing to allow ghouls to move into the tower so he can perform some tests on them. If the Lone Wanderer asks him about it, he will tell them that he has found, through research, that all ghouls will eventually become feral (though he also spouts this theory before the ghouls are let in).

Other interactions:
• Banfield keeps to a regular schedule, working at the wellness center, with a break at noon to eat lunch at the Café Beau Monde or the Federalist Lounge On Tuesdays and Thursdays, he's locked up in a penthouse with Susan Lancaster.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Metro Access & Generator. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Chems & Medicine, Supplies / Barter.

chr_0005c320.summary: Tiffany Cheng is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 35 HP). Affiliated with Cheng Family, Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Metro Access & Generator.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Tiffany Cheng spends most of her days avoiding her husband, drinking in the Federalist Lounge, or shopping down on the first level. She eats at the Café Beau Monde and then returns to the Cheng suite and spends some time in her room before going to sleep.

chr_0005c31b.role: Tenpenny Tower Residents, Cheng Family — Caucasian Elderly
chr_0005c31b.summary: Irving Cheng is an inhabitant of Tenpenny Tower in 2277, who is married to Tiffany Cheng.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Irving, a wealthy elderly man with a secret identity, believes himself to be the direct descendant of Chairman Cheng, the leader of the People's Republic of China before the War. Prideful of his assumed lineage, he insists on addressing himself and all others as "comrade," and is embarrassed by his own given name, as it fails to reflect his imagined heritage.

In his computer terminal, he writes that his father was one of the leading officers in the Chinese Army. He also writes about his "plans" for creating a communist society in Tenpenny Tower, which he terms the "Tenpenny Commune." Cheng heavily implies he is prejudiced against ghouls, as with many of the other Tenpenny residents.

chr_0005c31a.summary: Michael Hawthorne is a frequent patron at Tenpenny Tower's Federalist Lounge and is known to be the local drunk.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Michael Hawthorne is one of Tenpenny Tower's residents and a primary visitor to its Federalist Lounge. His drinking habits have taken over his life and his life savings, to the point where he may as well have a reserved seat at the lounge due to how frequent his visits are. Although little is known about Michael's background, during his conversations with Herbert Dashwood he jokes that he has been drinking since he was a toddler. When Dashwood warns him to be careful with his remaining brain cells, he replies "Nah, drown the buggers!" and shows little concern for his own wellbeing.

Despite his constant drunken stupor, he has formed friendships with some of the other residents.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Michael Hawthorne wanders Tenpenny Tower but always returns to the Federalist Lounge for a drink. On Wednesday nights, he can be seen in bed with the local courtesan of the tower, Susan Lancaster.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
Upon first meeting him, he will jovially ask the Lone Wanderer to share a drink with him, in which he will then begin discussing the ghoul business around the tower.

chr_00057508.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: fearful. AI packages: flee, travel
chr_00057508.summary: Tom Holden is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Atrium. Directly connected to quests: Escape!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
In the chaos of the Lone Wanderer's escape from Vault 101, Tom Holden wishes to flee the Vault alongside his wife Mary, although she would prefer that they simply return to their quarters. However, he doesn't listen to her, and subsequently attempts to approach Officer O'Brian and Officer Richards, who gun him down. His wife attempts to run to his body, but is also shot and killed just after him.

However, if the Lone Wanderer manages to reach the guards before Tom does, neither Tom nor Mary will be killed, and instead will flee together into a separate hallway. Even if they do survive, they disappear from the game, and do not appear in Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: Tom Holden is talking about escaping with his wife, Mary Holden, in the atrium. But when they try to make a run for it, they are shot on sight and killed by Officer O'Brian and Officer Richards unless the player character assaults the guards before the Holdens attempt to make a break for it.

Effects of the player's actions:
• If the guards are killed before the couple run into the hallway, the pair will survive and proceed to run through an inaccessible doorway.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Atrium. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Jumpsuit, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_00057507.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: fearful. AI packages: flee, travel, dialogue

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
During the chaos of the Lone Wanderer's escape from Vault 101, Mary's husband Tom wishes to flee the Vault with her, but she would prefer that they simply return to their quarters. However, Tom doesn't listen to her, and subsequently attempts to approach Officer O'Brian and Officer Richards, who gun him down. Mary then attempts to run to his body, but is also shot and killed just after him.

However, if the Lone Wanderer manages to reach the guards before Tom does, neither Tom nor Mary will be killed, and instead will flee together into a separate inaccessible hallway. Even if they do survive, they disappear from the game, and do not appear in Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: Mary and her husband, Tom, can be heard talking about escaping the vault in the main atrium. Following their brief chat, she and her husband run, trying to escape, but to no avail.

Effects of player's actions:
• Waiting to watch Tom get shot will also cause Mary to run towards the guards shortly after, getting killed as well.
• If the guards are killed before the couple run into the hallway, the pair will survive and proceed to run through an inaccessible doorway.

chr_000569b1.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: puzzled. AI packages: travel
chr_000569b1.summary: Allen Mack is a resident of Vault 101, a fervent isolationist, and its potential overseer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The head of the Mack household, Allen is a powerful presence in the Vault, and believes that it's a good life, sealed forever underground. Anyone who goes out of their way to mess it up is a sworn enemy of his. He is extremely protective of his family, When James entered Vault 101 and became its resident physician, Allen was deeply against taking him or his child in, believing that the Vault should remain shut. If it wasn't for the calming influence of his wife, Gloria, he would likely be even more aggressive. He certainly resolved to replace Alphonse Almodovar, should anything happen to him. while addicted to unspecified "pills" that James simply refused to give him at one point.

His redeeming feature is his love for his family.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: While never interacted with directly, Allen is briefly met on the way out, in an inaccessible common room, pounding on and shouting through the glass to alert others to the Lone Wanderer's presence. Gloria Mack is in the background.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If the player chooses to kill the overseer during their escape, Allen Mack rises to the position, as he was involved in saving numerous people. However, instead of opening the Vault, as expected, he decided to seal it permanently, leading to the uprising. Mack cannot be peacefully convinced to open the Vault, and the only options are either killing him or breaking the back of the rebellion for him. Mack will reward the player with the modified utility jumpsuit, then kick them out of the Vault.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only during Trouble on the Homefront if he becomes the overseer.

chr_00054433.role: Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian Elderly
chr_00054433.summary: Floyd Lewis is a Vault 101 engineer in 2277. He is seen dead in a control room when the Lone Wanderer is trying to escape near several radroaches.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Floyd Lewis was a talented engineer and technician, but was unskilled in the use of firearms. He was kind to the Lone Wanderer growing up, but was killed during their escape by a group of radroaches that he didn't see coming.

sections.title: Background & Story Role

chr_00054397.role: Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security — Asian Elderly
chr_00054397.summary: Grandma Taylor is a asian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security. Found primarily around Vault 101.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Agnes was part of a survey team who went to Megaton in 2241. She remained outside the vault to serve as a scout from Vault 101, acting as an ambassador of sorts to Megaton, and was continually collecting information about the wasteland. She returned to Vault 101 sometime before 2258. Her husband Taylor was worried about her recent problems with her heart. She died due to stress that her heart could not handle. Her final resting place is the diner encountered during Escape!

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
When the Lone Wanderer is trying to escape the vault, the player character can see Grandma Taylor dead on the floor of the Vault 101 cafeteria surrounded by radroaches. During Trouble on the Homefront, Officer Taylor tells the Lone Wanderer that he "lost [his] poor wife Agnes" because "her old ticker just couldn't take it anymore."

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_00035da9.role: Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian Elderly
chr_00035da9.summary: Officer Wolfe is a Vault 101 security guard. Together with Officer Park, he is the last obstacle between the Lone Wanderer and the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: One of Allen Mack's friends, Officer Wolfe was posted to the Vault blast door together with Officer Park to watch for any additional escape attempts. He does not want to breathe the irradiated air outside, preferring the recycled atmosphere of the Vault.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: Officers Wolfe and Park are the last security guards that try to prevent the Lone Wanderer from escaping. They can be easily avoided by running out the Vault door. Neither he nor Park will actually follow the player beyond the door's threshold, exclaiming "I'm not crazy enough to go out there!"
• Neither of them appear during Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Entrance. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00035da8.role: Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian Elderly
chr_00035da8.summary: Officer Park is a Vault 101 security officer. Together with Officer Wolfe, he is the last obstacle between the Lone Wanderer and the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Posted by Overseer Almodovar to the Vault blast door to ensure that the Lone Wanderer does not open the door again and flee into the wasteland in pursuit of their father, Park is confident about his ability to stop a jumped-up young adult from opening the door and contaminating his Vault.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: Park and Officer Wolfe are the last security officers the player fights on the way outside. If they are not killed, they will not cross the threshold of the Vault and remain inside, exclaiming "I'm not crazy enough to go out there!"
• Neither of them appear during Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Entrance. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00035b13.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_00035b13.summary:
The dead branchtender is a member of the Treeminders, found dead in the Oasis caverns.

The fastest way of finding him is opening the south gate to the caverns (Very Hard lock), then soon after a bend to the left his corpse is lying near a ground lantern. The alternative is going through the damp cave, sunken chambers and then entering the caverns.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This branchtender was one of the Oasis' armed guards alongside the other branchtenders. At some point, he traveled into the caverns underneath the Oasis, where he was killed by mirelurks.

chr_000cc26c.summary: Scientist is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 25 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Scientists are found wearing bright yellow radiation suits or lab coats. Some carry skill books that can be taken from their remains. Their bodies are sometimes surrounded by chems and weapons, among the detritus.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One scientist is located in a truck on a highway south of Raven Rock. When one approaches, an explosion goes off inside the truck and the body of a scientist flies out the back, off the bridge. He is carrying a Big Book of Science.
• Another scientist can be found outside Vault 87 in a highly irradiated area. Her body is found in a pile of miscellaneous objects and bones.
• Yet another scientist is found dead in a wastelander camp along a lake. A drowned raider can be found near the bloody corpses of the scientist and a wastelander nearby.
• The final scientist is found dead near a dumptruck in the Greener Pastures disposal site. She is found lying near a pile of radioactive barrels and a Big Book of Science is found next to her remains.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Conductor, Sensor Module, Bottle Cap, Big Book of Science, itm_000340d9.

chr_000cc228.summary: The dead Regulator is a member of the Regulators who can be found lying on the front steps leading out of the Arlington Wasteland Metro into the Arlington Cemetery North.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The dead Regulator will only appear if the Lone Wanderer has taken the Lawbringer perk. This member of the Regulators had met his fate while searching for Junders Plunkett to claim his bounty, as evident from the holotape on his body.

chr_000cbcfb.summary: The Overseer is a hispanic elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 145 HP). Found primarily around Vault 106 Living Quarters.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The overseers were often aware of their vault's purpose as an experiment and helped coordinate it. Overseers were chosen in a variety of ways, with initial leaders chosen before the war, and subsequent overseers afterward. In Vault 11, elections were held each year to choose a new overseer, who in turn would be killed as that year's "sacrifice."

The overseer's role and extent of their authority varied from vault to vault; in one vault an overseer might serve in a purely advisory capacity, Dr. Stanislaus Braun distributed sealed orders to each vault's overseer in the weeks before the Great War. According to a letter addressed by Dr. Braun to the original overseer of Vault 101, disclosing the contents of those sealed orders to the vault's residents or deviating from the experiment were grounds for termination of employment from Vault-Tec.

chr_000cafa7.summary: Junders Plunkett is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 65 HP). Affiliated with Raiders. Found primarily around Arlington House. Directly connected to quests: Lawbringer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Plunkett committed theft and murder in the town of Canterbury Commons, prompting the Regulators under Sonora Cruz to place a one-thousand cap bounty on his head. As the bounty has prompted the Regulators to harass his fellow raiders for information on his whereabouts, he has sought solace in a house in the Arlington Cemetery and has taken to building a shrine to an ancient figure named Lincoln. A member of the Regulators managed to track him to the Arlington Cemetery, but was killed before he managed to reach the house. In the bounty notice, Junders is described as being of fair complexion, average height, and missing an eye. He is also noted for his uncommon ability with a pair of small, concealable blades that are known as Plunkett's Valid Points.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
Junders only appears in the game if the player character has the Lawbringer perk, and he will attack on sight. If killed, Junders Plunkett will have a unique finger on him which can be turned in for the bounty to Sonora Cruz, with 1000 caps paid as a reward. One does not need to kill Plunkett personally to get credit. Plunkett can die from any means, and the finger will be on his corpse.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Arlington House. Notable equipment & inventory: Plunkett's Valid Points.

chr_000cadc5.summary: Winger Gervais is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 65 HP). Affiliated with Sudden-Death Overtime. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC21a (Red Racer Factory — Bailey's Crossroads).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Gervais, together with Centre Dubois and Winger Mercier, is part of the icegang led by Goalie Ledoux. They are obsessed with a sport played by Ledoux's ancestors. He is ambitious and wants to become Centre soon. His behavior and taunts are sadistic, yet he shows some regret over Winger Mercier's death.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Just for the Taste of It: Gervais will appear with Goalie Ledoux and Centre Dubois in front of the Red Racer factory once the Lone Wanderer has retrieved the Nuka-Cola Clear formula. Should Gervais be met there for the first time, he may be encoutered again upon entering the Nuka-Cola factory.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC21a (Red Racer Factory — Bailey's Crossroads). Notable equipment & inventory: Hockey Mask, Merc Troublemaker Outfit.

chr_000cadc4.summary: Winger Mercier was a member of the gang Sudden-Death Overtime. He is found dead in the Nuka-Cola plant in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mercier was a member of a gang called Sudden-Death Overtime, obsessed with an ancient ice sport that Goalie Ledoux's ancestors played. Winger Mercier was sent to procure a secret formula for a new type of Nuka-Cola while Ledoux made contact with the buyer. Mercier has been gone an awfully long time, because of his sudden death in the factory.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Just for the Taste of It: Mercier is found dead on the middle level of the Nuka-Cola plant offices during the quest The Nuka-Cola Challenge. He carries the note Finding the formula which points the player character towards the quest's objective.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Offices. Notable equipment & inventory: Hockey Mask, Merc Troublemaker Outfit, Finding the Formula.

chr_000cadc3.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: angry. AI packages: travel
chr_000cadc3.summary: Centre Dubois is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 60 HP). Affiliated with Sudden-Death Overtime. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC21a (Red Racer Factory — Bailey's Crossroads).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Part of the ice hockey themed gang formed by Goalie Ledoux (an icegang, as they call it), Dubois is the group's centre, a forward player who would normally be found in the middle of the ice, with wingers to the side (Gervais and Mercier), and the goalkeeper, or goalie, in the back. Dubois seems to like them most because they let her play with "their pucks".

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Just for the Taste of It: The Sudden Death Overtime gang spawns at the entrance to the Red Racer factory once the player collects Nuka-Cola Clear formula from the body of Winger Mercier in the Nuka-Cola plant. They will not spawn if the player already completed The Nuka-Cola Challenge without picking the Clear formula.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC21a (Red Racer Factory — Bailey's Crossroads). Notable equipment & inventory: Hockey Mask, Merc Troublemaker Outfit.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Ledoux is the leader of the Sudden-Death Overtime gang and is obsessed with the ancient ice sport, hockey that his own ancestors played. Winger Mercier was sent to procure a secret formula for a new type of Nuka-Cola while Ledoux made contact with the buyer.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment

chr_000ca994.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_000ca994.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_000ca98e.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

Once under the Brotherhood of Steel's protection, the MDPL mass relay station is now home to a small raider scavenger team under Torcher's leadership.

They carry a flamer and wear a unique raider arclight helmet called "Torcher's mask" and a set of raider badlands armor. They have nothing else in their inventory unless the Lone Wanderer has the Lawbringer perk, then Torcher will also carry a finger.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Barrett serves as Murphy’s bodyguard and assistant as the ghoul scientist attempts to synthesize and sell Ultrajet, a potent chem. He is not very vocal, and not even Murphy knows about his past, which Barrett is more than content with.

chr_000c9cef.summary: Murphy is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 80 HP). Found primarily around Northwest Seneca Station.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Murphy has set up a small laboratory inside the station, from which he and his assistant Barrett are attempting to synthesize and sell the potent chem Ultrajet, as regular Jet has a limited effect on ghouls. However, although he has an abundance of two of the three ingredients required to make Ultrajet, he is missing the third, Sugar Bombs, and is more than willing to employ the Lone Wanderer in an attempt to acquire sums of it - despite initially being paranoid that they have come to steal his Ultrajet formula.

His assistant acts primarily as a bodyguard, but can also be seen assisting Murphy with other tasks.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Murphy's Bombing Run: Talking to Murphy will start the quest.

Other interactions:
• If the Lone Wanderer berates Murphy in dialogue, he will end the conversation. If one then starts another conversation with him and asks about the Sugar Bombs, he and Barrett will turn hostile once the conversation ends.
• Provided that the Lone Wanderer participates in his quest and supplies him with Sugar Bombs, he will begin to synthesize Ultrajet and will sell it to them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Northwest Seneca Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Eyeglasses, itm_000340ff. Provides services: Chems & Medicine.

chr_000c9ae1.behavior: Unaggressive, cautious; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_000c9ae1.summary: Isabella Proud is a dead scientist found at the hidden irradiated pool within Takoma Park. The corpses of her and her colleague Jason are found behind the buildings on the other side of the canal through the factory.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A scientist conducting research into feral ghouls, Isabella and Jason embarked on a months-long research effort to better understand the ghoulified former humans. On the 45th day, thanks to Jason locating a suitable terminal, she decided to move their workstation closer to their research area, inching ever closer to Takoma Park. Proud was a keen observer and on the day of moving, she observed that feral ghouls were not afraid of the daylight, but preferred indoor habitats.

She performed a number of experiments to obtain hard data on feral ghoul behavior. One of these occurred on day 51, when she filled heavy basins with water and irradiated them to varying degrees.

chr_000c9ae0.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_000c9ae0.summary: Jason was a scientist researching feral ghouls and a colleague of Isabella Proud. His body is found next to Isabella's at the hidden irradiated pool.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jason and Isabella set up a camp near the factory in Takoma Park, with a terminal describing their work.

Before his demise, Isabella wrote about their progress, mentioning Jason's frequent scavenging in the ruins and his ability to find and set up the terminal in which she wrote her entries. A little over a week later, he recovered and repaired a generator, which allowed them to move the terminal and some of their equipment out to a better position for observation of the feral ghouls they were studying.

Throughout the time spent in the camp, Jason expressed continued concern regarding Isabella's increasing proximity to the feral ghouls, insisting she carried a pistol.

chr_000c942c.summary: The Drifter is a hostile wastelander who can be found in the Dickerson Tabernacle Chapel in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Drifter was once a member of the Treeminders in Oasis, but was exiled long ago for unknown reasons. Scorned and alone in the unforgiving wilderness, the apostate was only able to survive by hunting wildlife and stealing from other wastelanders.

Circa 2277, the Drifter has currently taken up residence in the dilapidated husk of the old Dickerson Tabernacle Chapel.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: The Drifter spends his days standing guard on the chapel's top floor attacking anything that gets close.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
The Drifter is located on the top floor of the chapel and will attack the player character once they reach the building.

chr_000c8e0e.summary: Grady is a deceased wastelander, found inside a ticket booth in Marigold station in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Grady was hired by Ronald Laren to steal a package of naughty nightwear from Lug-Nut and Lag-Bolt and stash it in the sewers of Grayditch to later deliver to Ronald in Girdershade for 200 caps. Grady was tracked down by Lug-Nut, Lag-Bolt, and another raider leading him to commit suicide with a.32 pistol before they found him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Grady's Package: Near his skeleton is a recording of his last words, asking anyone who finds his corpse to finish the job of delivering the package to Ronald Laren in Girdershade.

chr_000c825b.summary: The wanderer (called a wanderer in-game) is a lone raider living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The wanderer is accompanied by three guard dogs. They are found at their makeshift camp on top of an elevated platform made of floorboards, located east of Roosevelt Academy.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: South of Roosevelt Academy is an elevated railway track. Follow alongside it heading east until one sees an explosive chain of cars ending in a bus. Hop down into the valley where the highway breaks off and a red train car has collapsed. Go down the valley a short distance northwest, and one will see a raised wooden platform on the left, which is their camp. The wanderer will be patrolling around this area, accompanied by three raider guard dogs.

sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000151a3, Wanderer's Leather Armor.

chr_000c7faf.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: find, dialogue, sandbox
chr_000c7faf.summary: Victoria Watts is a resident of Rivet City and a field agent of the Railroad in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
This mysterious woman is allied with a clandestine group of ex-slaves, Abolitionists, working together with them and her like-minded colleagues up north to form a new type of underground railroad. She is forceful and bright and doesn't tolerate foolishness.

The Railroad works to protect escaped synths, who according to them, are akin to slaves. In January 2276, she volunteered to track a courser, who attempt to reclaim escaped synths, that was traveling south, for Railroad leader Pinky Thompson.

A year later, she lives in the Capital Wasteland, registered as a resident of Rivet City. She stays to serve as a bodyguard for Harkness, helping to safeguard his true identity after the arrival of the head of the Synth Retention Bureau, Dr. Zimmer, and his synth bodyguard Armitage, searching for their missing "property."

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Prior to the beginning of the quest The Replicated Man, Victoria Watts lives in the Rivet City market, staying in the eastern area around the pool table. She will interact with other residents, eat, and use furniture objects, but will not sleep at any time.

After delivering her quest-related message, Victoria will remain in the general vicinity where she first encountered the Lone Wanderer. She may attempt to travel to Rivet City, but she is incapable of fast-traveling and only moves position if the Lone Wanderer is in the same active map cell as her. As a result, she is almost certain to be killed in the wasteland if encountered far away from Rivet City.

If Victoria Watts reaches Rivet City, she will return to her regular schedule in the Rivet City market. She can be spoken to again but has no additional dialogue.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: After the Lone Wanderer is asked by Dr. Zimmer to track down Harkness' location for the Institute, Watts will request that they feign his death using an android component. If she is assisted in saving Harkness, she will later ask the Lone Wanderer to not speak to her again, for the safety of the Railroad.

Other interactions:
• Victoria searches out anyone looking to identify the android hiding out within Rivet City. Once The Replicated Man quest has started, Watts will begin actively tracking down the sleuth outside her home within Rivet City. She can potentially be met anywhere, including rather incongruous locations and situations, such as inside of the Arlington Library or even underwater.

chr_000c77f0.behavior: Very Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_000c77f0.summary: Prime is a wasteland hacker found dead at Dot's Diner near the Jury Street Metro station in 2277. On his corpse, one can find the unique Xuanlong assault rifle.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: After completing an unknown job with his partner Jiggs, Prime made a difficult journey to the Museum of Technology to stash Jiggs’ share of the loot for him to find. After easily hacking into several of the museum’s ancient terminals, Prime left behind a set of riddles on them that only Jiggs would be able to solve. Prime then hid Jiggs’ share of the loot in a safe inside the museum that could only be accessed after the riddles were completed. Had Jiggs managed to acquire his share of the loot, Prime planned for them to meet up at Dot's Diner near the Jury Street Metro station. However, Jiggs was killed before he could solve the riddles, and Prime met a grisly end at the diner while waiting for his partner.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Jiggs' Loot: Prime has left notes in certain terminals in the Museum of Technology in order to help his partner Jiggs find "his share of the loot."

Effects of player's actions:
• Prime's corpse will only appear after completing the Jiggs' Loot quest.

chr_000c6e97.summary: Willy is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 21 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Driven half-mad by lack of sustenance, and half-blind with hatred over his treatment by the snooty inhabitants of Tenpenny Tower, Willy still remains close to the structure, in the vain hope that a water caravan or kindly stranger will cross his path.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Water Beggars: Granting Willy's request for water yields a small amount of good Karma.

Effects of player's actions:
Willy will accept purified water and Aqua Pura. If the Lone Wanderer tells him to get his own water, he will have died by the time he is found.

Other interactions:
Regardless of how much water given, Willy will continue to ask for more. He will not accept dirty water, as he can't handle irradiated water any longer. If he is given Aqua Pura, he will die despite it being clean.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_000c6e95.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_000c6e95.summary: Carlos is a homeless water beggar sitting across the bridge from Rivet City. He is one of three beggars, the others being Micky outside Megaton and Willy outside Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Carlos is a survivor of a super mutant abduction, who narrowly escaped winding up on a mutant bonfire. He made his way to Rivet City, but has been unable to enter the vessel and resigned himself to begging at the entry station. He was drinking the irradiated water from the Anacostia, but lately his body revolted against the radiation and he just throws dirty water right back up.

As a result, he is increasingly dehydrated, with all the effects to cognition and thinking that entails. His only hope is that a kindly stranger or water caravan passes by to Rivet City and takes pity on him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Water Beggars: He is asking for purified water. Giving him purified water results in +50 positive Karma. If the Lone Wanderer refuses to give Carlos any water, he will die after they leave.
• Due to an oversight, giving him Aqua Pura will kill him, regardless of whether the player infected Project Purity at Eden's request or not.
• Carlos may also be killed by nearby threats, regardless of whether the player gave him water or not.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia). Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_000c6e90.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_000c6e90.summary: Micky is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 21 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom, Holy Water.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Driven slightly demented by lack of sustenance, and fearful of his life after a narrow escape from the raider gang holed up in the Springvale school, Micky made it to the entrance of Megaton by late 2277 and began begging for water, However, Megaton only gives water to its residents, or those that can pay for it.

Micky remains hopeful that someone will be kind enough to give him water. Truthfully, that is his only hope, as he is out of caps and so could not possibly buy water. Even the Brotherhood of Steel's water caravans would not simply hand out Aqua Pura to wasteland beggars. Though he is jaded by his experiences, he will be very grateful for any help given.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Water Beggars: The Lone Wanderer may give Micky purified water (and Aqua Pura, during Broken Steel) for a small amount of good Karma.
• Holy Water: During the quest, Micky will be replaced by a character named as a generic water beggar (who has the same appearance, inventory, and stats), regardless of whether Micky is already dead or not. Approaching Megaton's entrance from outside will cause a scene to play in which Rosa, a well-meaning wastelander, gives him water that she did not realize had been irradiated by the Apostles of the Eternal Light, killing him.
• Micky's death scene can be avoided entirely if the player fast travels straight into Megaton and progresses the quest by collecting a holy water pamphlet, or if they head directly to the Holy Light Monastery and speak to Brother Gerard.

sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_000c4f40.summary: Willow is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 20, 160 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Underworld's forward observer, Willow is young and satirical, calling visitors to the Mall "tourists" and inquiring if they have a death wish as they have entered a combat zone. If asked where she came from, she remarks that the Lone Wanderer is oblivious for a sightseer; if the Lone Wanderer protests being labeled as one, she sarcastically affirms that they are "taking in the sights" and "visiting the monuments," continuing with her tourist comparison.

She claims that she is not harassed by super mutants, who she calls "knuckle draggers," chalking it up to them seeing ghouls as family. Instead, she has issues with humans, particularly with the Brotherhood of Steel and Talon Company; she refers to the former as humans with "testosterone and guns" and the latter simply as "psycho," making no attempt to conceal her disdain for them.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She can usually be found on the Mall, wandering around just outside the entrance to the Museum of History.

chr_000c191a.summary: Enclave soldiers are the fighting force of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Enclave officer:
Enclave officers wear standard Enclave officer uniforms and hats. They are armed with plasma pistols, and carry plasma grenades as backup.

Enclave trainee (Rank 0):
Enclave trainees can be found at certain Enclave outposts after The Waters of Life, doing push-ups under the supervision of an Enclave officer. Trainees are equipped only with laser pistols; they do not wear helmets, and their power armor is in poor condition.

Enclave soldier (Ranks 1 and 2):
Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

chr_000c1120.summary: Paul Hannon is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around Vault 106 Science Labs.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is the only child of Paul Hannon Sr. and Vikki Hannon. Butch DeLoria, Freddie Gomez, and Wally Mack are his friends and fellow gang members.

The other Tunnel Snakes sometimes tease him because of his father being the chief of security in Vault 101, but this also gives him a certain cachet among his friends, though.

2260s:
On July 13, 2268, Paul attends the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party. In a conversation with the Lone Wanderer, Paul expresses his disappointment that he did not have a Pip-Boy 3000 yet. and they will start teasing him about "having a crush" on you (if the player character is a female), or about him being your "friend" (if the player character is male), which will then cause him to call you a "dorkface" so he could keep up his appeal with the other boys.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

Quests:
• Growing Up Fast
• Future Imperfect

chr_000c111f.summary: Butch DeLoria is a resident of Vault 101 and the leader and co-founder of the Tunnel Snakes gang in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born and raised in Vault 101 all his life and being under the care of his mother Ellen, a notorious alcoholic who neglected to oversee her son's negative maturing, Butch has been forced to put on a mask as a boorish, overbearing bully to cover up his deep-seated feelings of inadequacy due to not knowing his father despite living in a Vault with a close-knit community.

On July 13, 2268, when he was ten years old, During the party, Butch held a small meeting with his only two friends, Wally Mack and Paul Hannon Jr., to toss around ideas for a name for their gang, which later would be decided to be the "Tunnel Snakes" while rejecting other names such as "Vault Dwellers." He also attempted to strongarm the Wanderer into giving up the sweetroll they got from Lucy Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Butch becomes non-essential during Escape! and he can optionally be killed before leaving Vault 101, preventing him from appearing during Trouble on the Homefront and becoming a companion later.
• If Trouble on the Homefront was completed by either opening or destroying Vault 101, and Butch was left alive, he can be found residing in the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. He can be recruited as a companion only while the player character has Neutral Karma.

Companion:
• Butch can give the Lone Wanderer a haircut during Trouble on the Homefront, and if recruited as a companion, also at any time during their travels.
• If separated from the player character, Butch will return to the Muddy Rudder.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Items will be replaced by a non-player switchblade and 10mm pistol, if no replacement weapons are left in Butch's inventory while he is a companion.

chr_000c111e.behavior: Very Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: puzzled. AI packages: guard
chr_000c111e.summary: Wally Mack is a resident of Vault 101 in 2277 and is a member of a greaser gang called the Tunnel Snakes.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wally is the son of Allen and Gloria Mack. Wally's siblings are Stevie and Susie.

Wally is the brains of the Tunnel Snakes. Butch DeLoria and Paul Hannon Jr. are Wally's friends and fellow gang members. During their formative years, the Tunnel Snakes harassed other students in Vault 101, even being bold enough to taunt the overseer's daughter, Amata Almodovar. Butch presumes to be the leader of the Tunnel Snakes, but Wally might disagree if challenged.

He does not talk as much as the others, but they listen to what he has to say when he does say something. He is one of the Lone Wanderer's peers in Vault 101 and is encountered throughout the Lone Wanderer's youth inside Vault 101.

By 2287, Mack had traveled to the Commonwealth, where he reestablished the Tunnel Snakes under his rule.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tunnel Snakes Rule!: Wally Mack (as a glowing one) must be eliminated in Fens Way station.

chr_000c0cae.summary: Rivet City Security is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Bridge Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Bridge Tower. Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform, Hangar Key.

chr_000c09d6.summary: Officer Taylor is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Atrium/Upper Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Officer Taylor is a senior member of the Vault 101 security team. After his beloved wife's death, he blames the reckless escapees for the stress it caused her.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Officer Taylor was married to Agnes Taylor.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Trouble on the Homefront: Taylor is the second security guard the Lone Wander encounters when reentering the vault. Although he blames the Lone Wanderer and James for the problems in Vault 101, he is not hostile.

Effects of player's actions:
• His wife Agnes died due to a heart attack from the tension of the fighting leading up to the events of Trouble on the Homefront.
• Upon the Lone Wanderer's entry into the Vault 101 atrium during Trouble on the Homefront, he will be seen arguing with Freddie Gomez, who is attempting to leave the vault and has a knife. He will fire at Freddie but miss, resulting in Freddie's retreat.
• Despite him having neutral Karma, killing him results in Karma loss.

chr_000c09d5.behavior: Aggressive, cautious; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, patrol, sleep, sandbox
chr_000c09d5.role: Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents — African American
chr_000c09d5.summary: Officer Armstrong is a security officer in Vault 101. He greets the Lone Wanderer after they re-enter the vault during Trouble on the Homefront if the player chose to kill Officer Gomez on their way out.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
One of the rank and file members of the Vault's security team, Armstrong and the others have been trying to maintain order inside the bunker ever since its doctor absconded, unleashing a crisis that claimed far too many lives within the Vault. He is somewhat resentful towards James over the crisis, and is completely unaware of the fact that Overseer Almodovar's actions greatly exacerbated the conflict. He does know that the whole situation resulted in a revolution brewing in the Vault, as his emergence led others to question whether staying behind the Vault door is the right idea.

Regardless, he considers James a good friend, and the news of his passing is quite upsetting. He has known the Lone Wanderer since birth, and is one of the dwellers who genuinely likes them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Trouble on the Homefront: If Officer Gomez is dead, Officer Armstrong will be the first security member encountered upon entering the vault. He can escort the player character to the overseer, Amata, or let the player character go in alone. He also offers the alternative option for the Lone Wanderer to leave forever.
• Armstrong has the same dialogue as Gomez. His physical appearance is duplicated from Officer Richards.

sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Entrance. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Security Helmet, Vault 101 Security Armor, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_000bd693.summary: Doctor Stanislaus Braun is a scientist, a former member of the Vault-Tec Corporation, and the overseer of Vault 112 in 2277. He appears as a young girl named Betty when in the Tranquility Lane simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Working for Vault-Tec:
Hailing from the town of Kronach in Bavaria, Germany, Dr. Stanislaus Braun was a talented scientist who developed a long, varied career before the Great War. Braun served as the director of Vault-Tec's Societal Preservation Program, as well as the department head of Future-Tec. Braun had a large role in organizing and developing the Vaults' true purpose as sinister scientific experiments conducted on their resident populations, for which he was admired by some such as Valery Barstow, overseer of the unfinished Vault 88 in Massachusetts. As one of the persons responsible for designing the Vaults' social experiments, Braun was in direct contact with the overseers of some Vaults, tasking them with the successful completion of their experiments.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text:
A psychopath and narcissist at heart, Braun is arrogant and has a tremendous ego coupled with an inflated sense of his own intelligence. Coupled with severe anger issues, he lashes out over perceived slights, believes that he is always right and answers even simple questions with lengthy condescending digressions.

He also has a sadistic side, lacking any empathy for the inhabitants of Vault 112 that he's kept trapped in a simulated world where they are routinely killed, resurrected, mind-wiped and killed again, and does not have any mercy as he views them all as mere playthings for his own amusement. Braun views death in the simulation as a minor deterrence as he can normally resurrect his victims at any time he desires.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tranquility Lane: Braun (as Betty) is the man pulling the strings when the Lone Wanderer enters the Tranquility Lane lounger trying to rescue James. To escape, Braun asks them to complete several instructions that involve harming the trapped Vault inhabitants in different ways:

• Complying with all of Braun's instructions nets significant bad Karma.
• Activating the failsafe inside the abandoned house gives good Karma for ending the torment of the residents in Vault 112. A side effect of the failsafe is severing all control Braun had over the simulator, leaving him trapped forever, powerless and alone.
• Completing all of Betty's tasks except the "kill everyone" task and then activating the failsafe instead will result in neutral Karma. Braun reacts to the failsafe the same way as if none of his tasks were completed.

chr_000b07a8.summary: Argyle was the "stalwart ghoul manservant" of the reputed adventurer Herbert "Daring" Dashwood who journeyed together around the Capital Wasteland until his death at Rockopolis where his remains can be found by the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Originally born before the Great War, at some point in his 200+ years living as a ghoul, Argyle resided in the town of Shady Sands, developing his pickpocketing skills. He first met his future companion Herbert Dashwood in 2241 when the adventurer seduced and stole his girlfriend. However, despite the initial misunderstanding, they became good friends. At some point during their adventures together, Argyle elected to become Dashwood's manservant.

Daring Dashwood's Deeds:
The duo visited many places during their exploration of the wasteland. According to Dashwood, in the summer of 2248, they were given permission to take shelter inside Rockopolis by the ruling King Crag. But when Dashwood had an "incident" with Crag's daughter, the two were exiled from the underground city.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text: From his representation in the radio plays, Argyle appears to have been a very irritable individual, constantly exasperated by his master's recklessness and how easily he fell for the charms of women. Nevertheless, Argyle was very loyal to Dashwood, refusing to abandon him and always saving him even in the worst of situations, no matter how much effort, time and skill was required.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• A Manhandled Manservant: Argyle's corpse can be found in Rockopolis. This information can then be given to Dashwood for a reward, much to the ex-adventurer's sorrow.

chr_000b05e7.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_000b05e7.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. chr_000a7883.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: surprised. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_000a7883.summary: Amata Almodovar is a resident of Vault 101, the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar, and a major character. Along with Owyn Lyons and Sarah Lyons, she is one of only three characters in the game to have "Very Good" Karma.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only daughter of the overseer, Amata is around the Lone Wanderer's age and the two grew up together ever since James arrived in the Vault with his child in tow. They bonded over many things, from Grognak the Barbarian to being raised by single fathers after their mothers passed away at a young age: Amata lost her mother at two, leaving her father, the overseer, to raise her on his own. The burden of leading the Vault and enforcing his isolationist policy slowly drove Amata and Alphonse apart, despite her deep love for her father and an innate sense of loyalty.

The bond between Amata and the Lone Wanderer developed into a deep friendship over the years, with the two becoming inseparable, best friends. Another was that he simply didn't like the Lone Wanderer, in part due to their father's stubborn, insubordinate personality.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Amata organizes the Lone Wanderer's birthday party on July 13, 2268, gifting them an intact copy of the 14th issue of Grognak the Barbarian, and demonstrating some of the reactivity of the game.
• Future Imperfect: Amata takes the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, together with the Lone Wanderer. Before entering the class room, she is harassed by the Tunnel Snakes, allowing the player to experiment with various approaches to resolving quests and introducing them to the Karma system.
• Escape!: Amata awakens the Lone Wanderer with news of James' escape from the vault. She offers a gun and outlines a plan for the Lone Wanderer's own escape. Toward the end of the quest, it turns out that she was captured and is interrogated by her father and Officer Mack.

sections.text: • Only if she was told to keep the pistol during "Escape!"

chr_00095b48.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, flee, patrol
chr_00095b48.summary: William "Bill" Foster is one of the inhabitants of Vault 112 trapped within the Tranquility Lane virtual reality simulation. He does not have a home at the Lane, apparently the only adult without one.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Resident 906 of Vault 112, William Foster has been given the role of the local kindly elder engineer, working down at the RobCo Industries plant. He has been given a chipper personality, manifesting as whistling, humming patriotic songs, and an infinite amount of kindness towards kids, disguising quiet desperation within.

Foster is on good terms with everyone at the Lane, keeping his nose out of other people's business and giving a helpful hand to everyone in need. Mabel Henderson, the local gossip, tops this list, as she's very fond of her gadgets and her Mister Handy robot is very maintenance intensive. Foster blames it on her reluctance to order replacement parts. Like virtually everyone else, he thinks the Neusbaums dote on Timmy too much, and as a result, he's a real "momma's boy", as they said in his youth.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tranquility Lane: Bill Foster is one of the residents that has to be killed to complete Betty's tasks. Beyond that, he has no real role, aside from directing the player to talk to Betty upon their arrival.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: RobCo Jumpsuit, Reading Glasses, Pre-War Baseball Cap.

chr_0007542a.summary: Beatrice Armstrong (simply Beatrice in the game) is a resident of Vault 101 and a minor character. She is encountered during Growing Up Fast and later found dead during Trouble on the Homefront, in James' former office in the clinic.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An eccentric, airheaded dweller of Vault 101, Beatrice is one of the daughters of Stanley Armstrong, and the only one among them not to have a husband (although she is interested in Edwin Brotch, the Vault's resident teacher). Unlike her sisters, Mary Kendall and Gloria Mack, she has ample free time away from her family, which she spends snooping into the lives of other residents and gossiping to her sisters and her best friend, Pepper Gomez. She also dabbles in tarot readings and poetry as hobbies, often writing commemorative poems for special events such as Founder's Day and resident birthdays. Despite her friendly demeanor, many of her neighbors find her attitude insufferable and condescending, particularly the Vault's children.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Beatrice is one of the guests at the Lone Wanderer's birthday party. She will give the Lone Wanderer a poem for their tenth birthday party.
• If the player does not interact with Beatrice, she will continue to follow the Lone Wanderer throughout the Vault, even onto the reactor level.

Other interactions:
• Beatrice is found dead during Trouble on the Homefront. Despite complaining of a sprained toe, Andy amputated her right leg (incorrectly stating that he took off the left one).

chr_0003e644.summary: Ant Researcher is a asian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 20 HP). Found primarily around Shalebridge Tunnels.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The researcher evidently had a deep interest in ants, leading him to explore the Shalebridge ant colonies. He seems to have underestimated them; while the smaller forager ants ignored him, the aggressive, enemy colony did not and he suffered the lethal consequences, winding up dead in a small, stagnant pool inside the colony's egg chamber.

The researcher carries a Big Book of Science.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• The ant researcher respawns every 72 in-game hours with a new copy of Big Book of Science, providing an unlimited source of Science skill points to a patient player.
• While initially encountered dead, he will be hostile to the player once he respawns. Killing him does not result in a loss of Karma.

chr_0003d09c.summary: Brotherhood of Steel Scribe is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 60 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel, Brotherhood of Steel (Scribes), Citadel Residents. Found primarily around Citadel - Laboratory.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
There are three major scribe orders; each order is headed by a high scribe (proctor), designated by the head scribe.

• is responsible for weapons research and development. Guns, ammunition anything of an offensive nature. Once the Enclave exposes themselves to the Capital Wasteland by capturing Project Purity, the scribes come to realize just how technologically advanced the Enclave is compared to the Brotherhood as a whole. They are both excited at the prospect of analyzing new technology, particularly the Vertibirds, and frustrated at their lack of technological development. If interrupted, they will direct the Lone Wanderer to Scribe Jameson, or Elder Lyons when their situation develops. When the Brotherhood is ready to take the fight to the Enclave, they will express patriotic fervor for their victory.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Take it Back!: These scribes will be enthusiastic about the upcoming fighting for Project Purity.
• The American Dream: These scribes will direct the Lone Wanderer to Elder Lyons in the main laboratory.
