chr_0003923f.summary: Chinese remnant soldiers are ghoulified Chinese survivors of pre-War PLA operations on US soil, appearing.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The surviving remnants of Chinese military operations on United States soil are ancient ghouls, who were once spies, intelligence agents, and special operations soldiers left to fend for themselves after the Great War ended the Sino-American War. Two hundred years later, a handful of these ghoulified, stranded soldiers remain at Mama Dolce's, their former cover operations, maintaining a stronghold against any and all intruders. Dead, mummified soldiers may be found out in the wasteland as well, still manning listening posts eg. at Taft Tunnel or Broadcast tower KT8.

Despite two centuries of isolation, the remnants are still committed to communism and fight with the name of the likely long-dead Chairman Cheng on their chapped lips, with hatred of Americans still burning in their hearts.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• The remnant soldiers are encountered at Mama Dolce's, numbering about a dozen, split between regular soldiers, sergeants, and officers. Five are found in the Processed Foods section, another six in Food Distribution, along with the unique Chinese remnant captain.
• Unlike most other ghouls from the Capital Wasteland, and similar to the ghoulified version of Moira Brown, the voices of the Chinese aren't raspy and they sound the same as they do in the Battle of Anchorage.
• Two dead Chinese remnant spies are located in an underground sewer near broadcast tower KT8. Another spy cell is found in Taft Tunnel, during the flight from Project Purity.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: Note: Due to the way the spawns are structured, the following loadouts are default ones, and the actual weapon depends on which marker spawns the soldier. There's a special Chinese sniper spawn in Arlington, on the outside of Mama Dolce's, who carries a sniper rifle instead of the regular weapon, and two more in the courtyard of Mama Dolce's, which carry a sniper rifle and a missile launcher respectively.

chr_0002aeff.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sleep, sandbox, eat, use item
chr_0002aeff.summary: Sapling Yew is a african american child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Treeminders of Oasis. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Oasis.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: She is the only child of the Oasis village leaders, Tree Father Birch and Leaf Mother Laurel. She does gardening with her mother and enjoys playing in the grove, climbing on and around the god-spirit, and touching her bear charm. She is the closest thing to a friend Harold has among the Treeminders, by virtue of being the only one who actually listens to him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Oasis: If one passes a Speech check with her before fulfilling Harold's death wish, she will give them Yew's bear charm when the Lone Wanderer next speaks with her after the resolution of the quest. Speaking to her with a high enough Speech skill or the Child at Heart perk will also allow one to learn that Harold is afraid of fire.
• If the player character becomes hostile with the inhabitants of Oasis (by attacking them or Harold), Sapling Yew will vanish from the game.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Patients are residents who have become ill or injured and now reside in the clinic so the doctor may observe and later treat them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Attempting to talk to them will result in a "patient is unconscious" message.
• The patients in Megaton will drop an ear, while the one in Rivet City will drop a finger when killed.

chr_0002a27f.summary: Branchtender Maple is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 70 HP). Affiliated with Treeminders of Oasis. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Oasis.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The newest member of the Treeminders, Maple does not divulge many details about her past, but does note that she was drawn to Oasis by the calls of the Great One, and that in order to become a Treeminder, she had to accept the teachings of Tree Father Birch and cast aside her dependence on technology. Since her arrival and induction into the group, she has served as a branchtender, one of Oasis' armed defenders, where she is the primary guard for the gate, only being relieved by her fellow branchtender Linden in order to eat and sleep. She also helped to create the garbs that all of the Treeminders wear. However, she agrees with the ideals of Birch over those of Laurel, believing that Oasis should be protected and hidden from the wasteland rather than shared with it.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Oasis: She is with Tree Father Birch in that she believes that Oasis's growth should be stopped. After you have completed the quest and added Birch's sap to Harold's heart, she will give you Maple's garb.

Other interactions:
• You can try to convince her that Oasis is too secluded to be discovered with a Speech check.

chr_0002a27a.summary: Branchtender Linden is a member of the Treeminders and one of Oasis' armed defenders.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Prior to his arrival in Oasis, Linden was a member of the Brotherhood Outcasts, and, by extension, was once a member of the Brotherhood of Steel. During a mission to scavenge technology, Linden's squad was set upon and attacked by deathclaws, leaving the rest of the squad dead and Linden badly wounded. He was found by a trader caravan and taken to Oasis, where Bloomseer Poplar of the Treeminders saved his life and nursed him back to health. After he awoke, he felt that he owed a great debt to the group that had saved his life and decided to remain with them, leaving the Outcasts behind and becoming one of the settlement's guardians. He is somewhat hesitant to discuss his past as some people might not appreciate the fact that he was once a Brotherhood Outcast, but he can still be convinced to tell his story.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Oasis: If the player character gives Harold the enhancer that makes him grow, Linden will give them his unique Outcast power armor.

chr_0002a279.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sleep, eat, use item, travel
chr_0002a279.summary: Branchtender Cypress is a member of the Treeminders and one of Oasis' armed defenders.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Before he arrived in Oasis, Cypress was a wasteland adventurer for many years, where he made use of a missile launcher for at least some time. During his time as an adventurer, he witnessed many horrors, which had a profound impact on him and turned his disposition against the wasteland. When he arrived in Oasis and discovered its serene beauty, he believed that he had found a holy place. Tree Father Birch of the Treeminders allowed him to stay, and he eventually undertook the purification ceremony and met with the Great One in order to become a branchtender, one of Oasis' armed defenders. Birch then taught him everything he would need to know about Oasis and told him why it had to remain a secret.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can be normally found hanging out around the gate to the caves.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Oasis: He gives the Lone Wanderer the key to enter the caves below Oasis. If the player character chooses to add Birch's sap to Harold's heart, Cypress gives the player character a missile launcher and two missiles.

chr_0002a278.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sleep, eat, use item, sandbox
chr_0002a278.summary: Bloomseer Poplar is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 40 HP). Affiliated with Treeminders of Oasis. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Oasis.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born around, Bloomseer Poplar is the daughter of a healer. She took up her father's trade after studying his many books on trees, plants, and their medicinal properties. When she was 35, she heard rumors about Oasis and spent the next decade looking for it. When she finally discovered the site in, she decided to join Tree Father Birch and Leaf Mother Laurel, taking the name "Poplar" and becoming the third member of the nascent Treeminders.

While Birch was wary of letting her stay, Laurel convinced her husband otherwise, and Poplar began studying the ways of the Treeminders.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Oasis: Bloomseer Poplar provides context for the situation at the Oasis, and explicitly supports Leaf Mother Laurel's approach. If the player completes the quest as suggested by Leaf Mother Laurel, Poplar rewards them with Poplar's hood.

Other interactions:
• The player can ask Bloomseer Poplar to tell their future, and she will give them information about any of the game's named quests that they haven't found yet. The player character has to wait a couple of days after asking her to see the future before this option is available again. When there are no more quests left, this dialogue option will not exist.

chr_0002a276.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, travel, sleep, eat, sandbox
chr_0002a276.summary: Leaf Mother Laurel is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 45 HP). Affiliated with Treeminders of Oasis. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Oasis.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The wife of Tree Father Birch and fellow leader of the people of Oasis, Leaf Mother Laurel spends much of her day wandering around Oasis, tending the plants and flowers, and speaking with the people of the village with her daughter Sapling Yew usually at her side or playing nearby. She believes it is her responsibility to tend to the spiritual and mental well-being of her fellow villagers.

Not much else is known about Leaf Mother Laurel, other than her passion to let the whole Capital Wasteland experience Harold's "gift," contrary to her husband's belief.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Tree Father Birch is her husband and Sapling Yew is her daughter.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Leaf Mother Laurel is always in Oasis. She can be found at the outdoor hut in the mornings, sitting on the middle log. She also wanders around in Oasis and maintains the vegetation. She spends her evenings usually sitting on a stump with her husband and sleeps in a secluded spot with both her husband and child.

chr_0002a275.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, travel, eat, sleep, dialogue
chr_0002a275.summary: Tree Father Birch is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 80 HP). Affiliated with Treeminders of Oasis. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Oasis.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Birch founded the Treeminders. While the village is ostensibly a democratic commune, Birch acts as the group's spiritual and temporal leader. He is the Tree Father, a role similar to a high priest, and guides the cult in their communion with the "god-spirit" Harold.

Birch spends most of his time in the Pavilion, sitting on his throne, occasionally eating, and sleeping for a few hours at night. He also walks around Oasis, overseeing the village more directly.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Oasis: He greets the Lone Wanderer upon nearing the entrance. After leading them to the center of the grove, Birch will enter a conversation, which will begin the Oasis quest.

Effects of player's actions:
• The Animal Friend and Life Giver perks offer special dialogue options.

chr_00000a9c.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

chr_000b875b.summary: Paladin Bael is a Brotherhood of Steel paladin in charge of guarding the entrance to the Citadel.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Bael is an experienced fighter, but his conversational skills leave something to be desired. However, his commanding presence ensures that unwanted visitors stay well away from the Citadel's entrance.

Although he is initially dismissive and hostile towards the Lone Wanderer and their abilities, as he would be towards any other wastelander, he changes his tune upon their surprising return from the depths of Vault 87 and the Enclave-controlled Raven Rock. After the Battle of Project Purity, he ceases to guard the gate.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Bael guards the Citadel's gate until Take it Back! is completed.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Waters of Life: Bael guards the entrance to the Citadel and denies entrance until this quest is completed.

chr_000b69be.summary: Enclave soldiers are the fighting force of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Enclave officer:
Enclave officers wear standard Enclave officer uniforms and hats. They are armed with plasma pistols, and carry plasma grenades as backup.

Enclave trainee (Rank 0):
Enclave trainees can be found at certain Enclave outposts after The Waters of Life, doing push-ups under the supervision of an Enclave officer. Trainees are equipped only with laser pistols; they do not wear helmets, and their power armor is in poor condition.

Enclave soldier (Ranks 1 and 2):
Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

chr_000b25b5.summary: Commander Jabsco is the leader of the Talon Company, and the only member of the organization not to wear its trademark armor. Instead, he wears metal armor and a Talon Company combat helmet, a unique piece of armor, and uses the Occam's Razor unique weapon in close combat, on top of being the boss character of the Fort Bannister dungeon.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Jabsco is the brains of Talon Company, planning mercenary operations from the safety of his bunker within Fort Bannister. Although he claims to be a combat veteran who proved his ability many times over, his subordinates have yet to see proof of his claims. In fact, he is called Jetting Jabsco behind his back, as he apparently tends to flee combat rather than face anything other than favorable odds.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Commander Jabsco is a hostile non-player character who can only be fought. He has a substantial amount of health (more than a deathclaw or companions), good armor (metal armor and a Talon Company combat helmet), and uses a missile launcher, Chinese pistol and Occam's Razor in combat, making him the boss character of Fort Bannister.
• Furthermore, Jabsco is supported by two to three Talon mercenaries who spawn when he reaches 75% health (they are scaled down to be extremely short, almost child-sized), and the commander will also activate a Mister Gutsy to assist him using a nearby terminal (though according to the script, it will enter combat once Jabsco is at 25% health).

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Commanding Officer's Quarters. Notable equipment & inventory: Jabsco's Key, Metal Armor, Talon Combat Helmet.

chr_000b22c9.summary: Enclave scientists are members of the Enclave's Research and Development Division in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Enclave scientists perform research and development into new and improved weaponry solely for the Enclave. Wearing a white, airtight environmental suit with an orange Plexiglas visor, they are easily identified among the Enclave's personnel. Although they are armed with AEP7 laser pistols and have had moderate combat training, they very rarely make actual use of this; with few exceptions, virtually every Enclave scientist will flee rather than fight. They are, without a doubt, the brains to match Enclave soldiers' brawn.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Enclave scientists can be found working on their projects at several Enclave bases, such as Raven Rock and the mobile base crawler.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Raven Rock - Level 2, Satellite Facility. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_0001b5bd.

chr_000b22c7.summary: The Adams Air Force Base scientist is an Enclave scientist working in one of the hangars at the Adams Air Force Base in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This scientist requested that her older brother hide away a stash of flamer fuel and an incinerator for her. Her brother was able to successfully stash the fuel for her; however, he was unable to get his hands on an incinerator and added in a note to her if she wanted one, she would have to get it herself.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She works all day in one of the hangers, occasionally pausing to study the various consoles and control panels near her.

chr_000b22c6.behavior: Very Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_000b22c6.summary: Enclave scientists are members of the Enclave's Research and Development Division in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Enclave scientists perform research and development into new and improved weaponry solely for the Enclave. Wearing a white, airtight environmental suit with an orange Plexiglas visor, they are easily identified among the Enclave's personnel. Although they are armed with AEP7 laser pistols and have had moderate combat training, they very rarely make actual use of this; with few exceptions, virtually every Enclave scientist will flee rather than fight. They are, without a doubt, the brains to match Enclave soldiers' brawn.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Enclave scientists can be found working on their projects at several Enclave bases, such as Raven Rock and the mobile base crawler.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment

chr_000ae66d.summary: Dead slaves can be found in five static locations throughout the Capital Wasteland. They hold the slave map on them. Additionally, slaves appearing as part of random encounters may be found dead due to nearby hostiles and also have the slave map on their corpse.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The RobCo facility parking lot, south of the building near the road.
• Directly northeast of Big Town, on the side of the road.
• In northern area of Metro Central. Walking from the Dupont Circle station entrance, once you reach the tracks take the first left through an opening between the tracks. The body is located to the right of the crashed train just through the opening.
• West of the Robot repair center, down the cliffs.
• South of Paradise Falls, near a ruined house.

chr_000ae072.summary: Enclave officers are encountered leading squads of Enclave soldiers through the Capital Wasteland in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Enclave officers are often found commanding a group of Enclave soldiers at the many outposts established throughout the Capital Wasteland. They are highly skilled combatants, but their lack of proper armor leaves them far more vulnerable to damage than their rank-and-file subordinates.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The American Dream: The Lone Wanderer is stopped and questioned by an Enclave officer named Williams in this quest. They can bluff their way past him with a Charisma, Strength or Speech check, or can offer a 500 cap bribe. Otherwise, he will alert Raven Rock's security early.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC10b (Jefferson Memorial). Notable equipment & inventory: Enclave Officer Hat, itm_000340de.

chr_000ac3d8.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, guard
chr_000ac3d8.summary: Chinese remnant soldiers are ghoulified Chinese survivors of pre-War PLA operations on US soil, appearing.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The surviving remnants of Chinese military operations on United States soil are ancient ghouls, who were once spies, intelligence agents, and special operations soldiers left to fend for themselves after the Great War ended the Sino-American War. Two hundred years later, a handful of these ghoulified, stranded soldiers remain at Mama Dolce's, their former cover operations, maintaining a stronghold against any and all intruders. Dead, mummified soldiers may be found out in the wasteland as well, still manning listening posts eg. at Taft Tunnel or Broadcast tower KT8.

Despite two centuries of isolation, the remnants are still committed to communism and fight with the name of the likely long-dead Chairman Cheng on their chapped lips, with hatred of Americans still burning in their hearts.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• The remnant soldiers are encountered at Mama Dolce's, numbering about a dozen, split between regular soldiers, sergeants, and officers. Five are found in the Processed Foods section, another six in Food Distribution, along with the unique Chinese remnant captain.
• Unlike most other ghouls from the Capital Wasteland, and similar to the ghoulified version of Moira Brown, the voices of the Chinese aren't raspy and they sound the same as they do in the Battle of Anchorage.
• Two dead Chinese remnant spies are located in an underground sewer near broadcast tower KT8. Another spy cell is found in Taft Tunnel, during the flight from Project Purity.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: Note: Due to the way the spawns are structured, the following loadouts are default ones, and the actual weapon depends on which marker spawns the soldier. There's a special Chinese sniper spawn in Arlington, on the outside of Mama Dolce's, who carries a sniper rifle instead of the regular weapon, and two more in the courtyard of Mama Dolce's, which carry a sniper rifle and a missile launcher respectively.

chr_000abd05.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_000abd05.summary: Ryan Brigg is a wasteland scientist masquerading as a raider in the Jury Street Metro station in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ryan Brigg is a wasteland inventor conducting research on the widely-available mole rat meat in an attempt to improve its taste. As a result, he has come up with wonder meat that he plans to sell in order to fund further experimentation to refine his creation. To secure his innovation and investments, he poses as a raider captain in order to recruit the manpower he needs. He plans to set up shop in one of the Capital Wasteland's towns, hoping to finally be away from the raiders on his payroll, viewing them as "destitute," "filthy" and his "bane."

According to the computer in his small hideout, he has been running experiments to eliminate the bitter taste of mole rat meat.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Ryan Brigg's Wonder Meat: The wonder meat maker he created produces a piece of mole rat wonder meat for every mole rat meat and wonder glue used.

Other interactions:
• Ryan is automatically hostile and will attack the Lone Wanderer on sight. He is set to respawn if killed.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Jury St. Tunnels. Notable equipment & inventory: Tinted Reading Glasses, Ryan Brigg's Safe Key, itm_00073d57, itm_000340ff.

chr_000aa846.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_000aa846.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_000a873e.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_000a873e.summary: Ted is a deceased wastelander whose corpse can be found in the Anchorage Memorial facility in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Ted was once a part-time hunter, and full-time butcher, carving up mirelurk corpses to sell to merchants and settlements across the wasteland. Growing increasingly paranoid of "sabotage," Ted inserted a few failsafes to keep his frozen hatchling meat safe. He met his end via unknown hands.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

chr_000a6efe.summary: Enclave soldiers are the fighting force of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Enclave officer:
Enclave officers wear standard Enclave officer uniforms and hats. They are armed with plasma pistols, and carry plasma grenades as backup.

Enclave trainee (Rank 0):
Enclave trainees can be found at certain Enclave outposts after The Waters of Life, doing push-ups under the supervision of an Enclave officer. Trainees are equipped only with laser pistols; they do not wear helmets, and their power armor is in poor condition.

Enclave soldier (Ranks 1 and 2):
Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

chr_000a6d67.summary: Sid is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 125 HP). Affiliated with Centaurs. Found primarily around Test Labs. Directly connected to quests: Finding the Garden of Eden.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Sid and a group of his friends were captured by super mutants in Vault 87. His friends were mutated into extremely deformed creatures, and he was told that he would soon meet the same fate. Upon the Lone Wanderer's arrival in Vault 87, Sid, having lost almost all rational thought as a result of his situation, is openly hostile towards them and all others.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Finding the Garden of Eden: Depending on the method one chooses to release Fawkes, Sid will attack the Lone Wanderer. If one frees Fawkes by activating the lab's emergency fire systems, this will open all the other isolation rooms, freeing both Sid and two centaurs. Although both are hostile towards the player character, they will also attack each other if either of them spots the other first. Sid most commonly dies in this scenario. Unlocking the door via terminal will result in Sid being hostile towards the player character as well. Picking the lock to the door does not turn Sid hostile, and he will keep acting as if he was still locked in the cell. If the fire alarm is activated, Sid will attack even if his cell was already open.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Test Labs. Notable equipment & inventory: Lead Pipe, Merc Grunt Outfit.

chr_000a1212.summary: Professor Malleus is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Professor John Malleus was in charge of implementing the experiment conducted by Vault Tec on the residents of Vault 92 which were intended to subject some of the world's greatest musicians to white noise containing subliminal messages. The hope was that this project could be used to create "super soldiers" who fought harder and with greater endurance for the United States military.

Malleus was initially intrigued and optimistic about the results of the test, until those residents subjected to the white noise began to go violently insane.

chr_000a0c20.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_000a0c20.summary: Wasteland captives are imprisoned humans captured by super mutants. They are found at super mutant encampments throughout the Capital Wasteland during 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The captives are wastelanders held prisoner by super mutants. During the quest Big Trouble in Big Town, humans from Big Town are captured by super mutants and held in the Germantown Police HQ. These humans have been captured to be used as food. While in the building, a super mutant can be overheard conversing with Shorty, a captive who is about to be killed. The human asks why he is to be killed when there are plenty of human remains available surrounding them. The super mutant jailer reveals that they prefer their food to be from a fresh kill.

Uncle Leo, a friendly super mutant, suggests that captives could be used to create more super mutants. Other super mutants remark that they need more new recruits to transform into super mutants using "green stuff."

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Releasing captives results in a Karma boost. If one frees a captive, they will express gratitude and offer some food, Rad-X, or ammunition. If one accepts these supplies, they will receive 50 Karma points and the supplies. Telling them to keep it will result in 75 Karma. There is no Karma penalty for leaving the captive to their fate. Karma is not lost for killing a captive. If surrounding enemies are not cleared out before freeing a captive, they could be killed while escaping.
• If one ignores a captive or chooses to leave them to their fate, a new captive will respawn along with new super mutant guards if revisiting the location. However, if one frees the captive, or if the captive is killed, no new captives will appear in that location.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• A captive is located north of the Anchorage Memorial, in a tent behind the trucks, guarded by a leveled super mutant and two centaurs. If escorting the captive after freeing them, they will run to the northwest of the map near Fort Constantine and will keep running beyond the northern map limit, remaining at a rock formation.
• There are two captives at clifftop shacks which is north of Minefield and west of Vault 92. This area is also the site of a 'Type B' random encounter, which may lead to a battle between the spawned encounter and the super mutants, potentially resulting in harm to the captives.
• A captive located at the eastern highway entering the city, accessible by progressing from Friendship Heights to Farragut West Metro station, enclosed in the city walls. The captive is guarded by a super mutant and centaur.

The captives are wastelanders held prisoner by super mutants. During the quest Big Trouble in Big Town, humans from Big Town are captured by super mutants and held in the Germantown Police HQ. These humans have been captured to be used as food. While in the building, a super mutant can be overheard conversing with Shorty, a captive who is about to be killed. The human asks why he is to be killed when there are plenty of human remains available surrounding them. The super mutant jailer reveals that they prefer their food to be from a fresh kill.

Uncle Leo, a friendly super mutant, suggests that captives could be used to create more super mutants. Other super mutants remark that they need more new recruits to transform into super mutants using "green stuff."

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Releasing captives results in a Karma boost. If one frees a captive, they will express gratitude and offer some food, Rad-X, or ammunition. If one accepts these supplies, they will receive 50 Karma points and the supplies. Telling them to keep it will result in 75 Karma. There is no Karma penalty for leaving the captive to their fate. Karma is not lost for killing a captive. If surrounding enemies are not cleared out before freeing a captive, they could be killed while escaping.
• If one ignores a captive or chooses to leave them to their fate, a new captive will respawn along with new super mutant guards if revisiting the location. However, if one frees the captive, or if the captive is killed, no new captives will appear in that location.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• A captive is located north of the Anchorage Memorial, in a tent behind the trucks, guarded by a leveled super mutant and two centaurs. If escorting the captive after freeing them, they will run to the northwest of the map near Fort Constantine and will keep running beyond the northern map limit, remaining at a rock formation.
• There are two captives at clifftop shacks which is north of Minefield and west of Vault 92. This area is also the site of a 'Type B' random encounter, which may lead to a battle between the spawned encounter and the super mutants, potentially resulting in harm to the captives.
• A captive located at the eastern highway entering the city, accessible by progressing from Friendship Heights to Farragut West Metro station, enclosed in the city walls. The captive is guarded by a super mutant and centaur.

chr_000a0bd4.behavior: Very Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox
chr_000a0bd4.summary: Enclave soldiers are the fighting force of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Enclave officer:
Enclave officers wear standard Enclave officer uniforms and hats. They are armed with plasma pistols, and carry plasma grenades as backup.

Enclave trainee (Rank 0):
Enclave trainees can be found at certain Enclave outposts after The Waters of Life, doing push-ups under the supervision of an Enclave officer. Trainees are equipped only with laser pistols; they do not wear helmets, and their power armor is in poor condition.

Enclave soldier (Ranks 1 and 2):
Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

sections.text: In game files (EditorID: MQ11EnclaveTeslaArmor), Enclave Soldier is defined as a Caucasian in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Faction memberships: Enclave. Appears in or relates to quests: Take it Back!. Linked story events: Liberty Prime March & Project Purity Activation.

chr_000a0a4c.summary: The dead Chinese commando is a deceased Chinese soldier who may be randomly encountered.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This man was a ghoulified Chinese commando and pilot who apparently became stranded in the United States of America after his aircraft crashed. He recorded a radio beacon to try to signal other friendly forces, but eventually died somewhere in the Capital Wasteland, with the beacon still active.

sections.title: Interactions
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Downed Chinese Pilot: The commando's corpse can be randomly encountered in the wasteland. The Chinese radio beacon will become available when in the vicinity of the commando, and will become louder as one gets closer to the body.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Med-X, Stimpak, Chinese Officer's Sword, Dirty Chinese Jumpsuit, Chinese Pistol.

chr_0007d313.role: Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian Elderly
chr_0007d313.summary: Officer O'Brian is a member of Vault 101 security. He is guarding the locked atrium door to the Vault 101 entrance together with Officer Richards.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A vicious sadist under the command of Vault 101 overseer Alphonse Almodovar, O'Brian basks in the ability to inflict pain on other Vault dwellers. The confusion and chaos accompanying James' escape is a boon to him, as it makes it easy for him to indulge his violent side with impunity.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: O'Brian and Richards will immediately open fire on the player when they notice them. They will also kill Tom and Mary Holden, who try to make a run for it - unless the player character is spotted first, causing both officers to attack them instead of the Holdens.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Atrium. Notable equipment & inventory: 10mm Round, 10mm Pistol.

chr_000456a3.summary: Emaline is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 120 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Emaline is a very close and very loyal friend of Sydney. Experienced with heavy weapons, she will track down and seek retribution from anyone—especially men—who attempts to cross her girlfriend.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Encounter:
• Bragging Rights: Emaline appears in a random encounter together with Sydney if the Lone Wanderer cheats the latter out of the reward for finding the Declaration of Independence. Emaline has no unique lines.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00037f43.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_00037f43.summary: Jaime Dexter Palabras is a crazed ghoul in the Dunwich Building in 2277. He can be found worshiping a strange obelisk in the virulent underchambers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Jaime is of Hispanic ancestry, and was born to a man who was a member of an unspecified group of Rangers his father brought back a mysterious old tome from an expedition, which he believed to be valuable. They then travelled to the Capital Wasteland, hoping to sell it to the scribes of the Brotherhood of Steel chapter who had recently settled there. Failing to sell the book to the Brotherhood, Jaime's father instead vowed to return it "to its source" and set off, leaving his son in an old hospital without a flashlight. Jaime eventually fell in with another group of travelers, who turned out to be raiders. It was not long until they killed a family for a "sack of rotten vegetables," upon which he secretly resolved to get away from this dangerous group as soon as possible.

chr_000230df.role: DeLoria Family, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian Elderly
chr_000230df.summary: Ellen DeLoria is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 325 HP). Affiliated with DeLoria Family, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront, Escape!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ellen likes to get drunk often, but this causes her not to pay attention to what her son Butch is up to. Ellen and Butch live together in one of the smallest family apartments. Butch's father is a mystery to the other residents of Vault 101.

In 2268, Ellen encouraged her son Butch to attend the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party in the cafeteria.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: Ellen will come under attack by radroaches, leading Butch to appeal to the Lone Wanderer to save her.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If she was saved in Escape!, she is revealed to be a loyalist to the overseer, and despite the Lone Wanderer saving her life, she blames the entire incident on James.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should she be saved from the radroaches, Butch will declare that the Lone Wanderer is his best friend and he will give them his Tunnel Snake outfit, while Ellen asks if they would like a drink. This also gives the Lone Wanderer some good Karma.
• If the Lone Wanderer simply allows Ellen to be mauled by the radroaches, Butch will despise them and attempt to lead Vault 101 security in the right direction to capturing them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Vodka, Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_000230dd.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sandbox
chr_000230dd.summary: Amata Almodovar is a resident of Vault 101, the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar, and a major character. Along with Owyn Lyons and Sarah Lyons, she is one of only three characters in the game to have "Very Good" Karma.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only daughter of the overseer, Amata is around the Lone Wanderer's age and the two grew up together ever since James arrived in the Vault with his child in tow. They bonded over many things, from Grognak the Barbarian to being raised by single fathers after their mothers passed away at a young age: Amata lost her mother at two, leaving her father, the overseer, to raise her on his own. The burden of leading the Vault and enforcing his isolationist policy slowly drove Amata and Alphonse apart, despite her deep love for her father and an innate sense of loyalty.

The bond between Amata and the Lone Wanderer developed into a deep friendship over the years, with the two becoming inseparable, best friends. Another was that he simply didn't like the Lone Wanderer, in part due to their father's stubborn, insubordinate personality.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Amata organizes the Lone Wanderer's birthday party on July 13, 2268, gifting them an intact copy of the 14th issue of Grognak the Barbarian, and demonstrating some of the reactivity of the game.
• Future Imperfect: Amata takes the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, together with the Lone Wanderer. Before entering the class room, she is harassed by the Tunnel Snakes, allowing the player to experiment with various approaches to resolving quests and introducing them to the Karma system.
• Escape!: Amata awakens the Lone Wanderer with news of James' escape from the vault. She offers a gun and outlines a plan for the Lone Wanderer's own escape. Toward the end of the quest, it turns out that she was captured and is interrogated by her father and Officer Mack.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only if she was told to keep the pistol during "Escape!"

chr_000230dc.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, flee, travel, sandbox
chr_000230dc.role: DeLoria Family, Tunnel Snakes, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian
chr_000230dc.summary: Butch DeLoria is a resident of Vault 101 and the leader and co-founder of the Tunnel Snakes gang in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born and raised in Vault 101 all his life and being under the care of his mother Ellen, a notorious alcoholic who neglected to oversee her son's negative maturing, Butch has been forced to put on a mask as a boorish, overbearing bully to cover up his deep-seated feelings of inadequacy due to not knowing his father despite living in a Vault with a close-knit community.

On July 13, 2268, when he was ten years old, During the party, Butch held a small meeting with his only two friends, Wally Mack and Paul Hannon Jr., to toss around ideas for a name for their gang, which later would be decided to be the "Tunnel Snakes" while rejecting other names such as "Vault Dwellers." He also attempted to strongarm the Wanderer into giving up the sweetroll they got from Lucy Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Butch becomes non-essential during Escape! and he can optionally be killed before leaving Vault 101, preventing him from appearing during Trouble on the Homefront and becoming a companion later.
• If Trouble on the Homefront was completed by either opening or destroying Vault 101, and Butch was left alive, he can be found residing in the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. He can be recruited as a companion only while the player character has Neutral Karma.

Companion:
• Butch can give the Lone Wanderer a haircut during Trouble on the Homefront, and if recruited as a companion, also at any time during their travels.
• If separated from the player character, Butch will return to the Muddy Rudder.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Items will be replaced by a non-player switchblade and 10mm pistol, if no replacement weapons are left in Butch's inventory while he is a companion.

chr_000230da.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_000230da.role: Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents — Hispanic Elderly
chr_000230da.summary: The unnamed Vault 101 overseer before Alphonse Almodovar was in charge of Vault 101 up until the 2250s.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Vault 101 overseer before Almodovar was a proponent of outside contact, well respected among many for their leadership and transparency. Under their tenure, the Vault opened in early 2241, with the first survey team, led by Anne Palmer, reporting that the outside was not an uninhabitable hellscape, but merely a dangerous, irradiated wasteland. The Vault began trade relations, establishing ambassadors at Megaton, and dwellers were permitted to travel freely between the Vault and the outside world. The Vault's large population at the time was sustained by this policy.

However, this policy did not sit well with a young Alphonse Almodovar. Inheriting his parents' belief that the Vault should remain sealed away from the outside world, Almodovar waited for a chance to correct the lapses in security.

chr_0009b171.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, travel, patrol
chr_0009b171.summary: Officer Kendall is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 230 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
John Kendall is the husband of Mary Kendall and the father of Christine and Monica. John is friendly, yet tough and no-nonsense. While he is not actively sinister, he will follow orders without putting much thought into it. Introspection is not a trait he commonly displays. He loves being a cop and whether what he is doing is right does not worry him; he is the law.

During the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party on July 13, 2268, Officer Kendall can be overheard talking with the overseer in the stairway to the upper level. Officer Kendall is assigned by the overseer to give the party just a few more minutes and then make sure everyone gets back to work. He may idley wish the Wanderer a happy birthday if near him, and gleefully remark the party sounds like fun.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• He will only drop a finger prior to Trouble on the Homefront

Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: The Lone Wanderer encounters Kendall at the entrance to the Vault 101 atrium, near the reactor level.
• Escape!: The Lone Wanderer encounters Kendall just outside their room, whereupon Kendall will be attacked by several radroaches. The Lone Wanderer can sneak past him through the restrooms, attempt to save him from the radroaches, or kill him. He is the first person that can be killed in the game. He will become hostile after the radroaches are dead.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Officer Kendall will be present if he did not die during Escape! When interacted with, he blames the Lone Wanderer and James for the vault's problems.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only during Trouble on the Homefront

chr_00099343.summary: Jonas is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 20 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Atrium.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Good-humored, smart, and kind, Jonas has been James' assistant as well as his and the Lone Wanderer's friend for as long as the Lone Wanderer can remember. He can appear stern and strict if he wants to, but even there, his sense of humor asserts itself.

In the late 2260s, Jonas was appointed to be James' assistant by the overseer, who hoped he would be a voice of reason. Jonas and James forged a friendship very quickly and together, they worked at examining and treating patients, as well as conducting routine experiments, testing the health of the vault. For an unknown length of time, James deliberately kept his assistant in the dark about covert experiments aimed at reviving Project Purity.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Jonas is first encountered during the Lone Wanderer's 10th birthday when James takes the Lone Wanderer down to the generator room to give them a present (a BB gun). Jonas later takes a picture of the two.
• Future Imperfect: Jonas is encountered upon opening the office door, telling the Lone Wanderer good morning and good luck on the G.O.A.T.

chr_00097f39.summary: Manny Koch was the leader of a search party that set out from Canterbury Commons to look for Cheryl in 2277. He is found dead.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The leader of the Canterbury Commons search party that attempted to locate the whereabouts of his sister, "Cheryl," Manny Koch is the only visible remains of the group; the rest are either buried, chopped into manageable pieces and stored on gore bags, or gone. Manny is dead when the Lone Wanderer approaches him. After inspecting the body, one should prepare for a super mutant behemoth.

Manny Koch had searched for Cheryl and their dog Myles from the Citadel to Calverton with the search party he organized: Henry, Emmet, and Kaya.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

• Searching for Cheryl: Manny is found dead at the end of the player character's search for Cheryl, near Jury Street Metro station.

chr_0009550a.summary: Susie Mack is a caucasian child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Susie is the daughter of Allen and Gloria Mack, and the younger sister of both Stevie and Wally. Growing up, Susie despises the Tunnel Snakes, of which her brother Wally is a member. However, Wally does not give Susie a hard time, as she has something of a mean streak in her teenage years. When taking the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, Susie has no respect for the Lone Wanderer, and aggressively shuns any attempt from them to even speak with her. Prior to the test, she engages in small talk with Freddie Gomez, on whom she secretly has a crush. After the test, Mr. Brotch informs Susie that she is headed for a teaching career, sarcastically surmising this must be due to her "gift" for communication. Susie is unsurprised by and somewhat apathetic of the results.

By 2277, Susie has become more mature and thoughtful.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Susie Mack is one of the Lone Wanderer's classmates taking the G.O.A.T. at the same time.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Susie Mack sides with Amata's rebels during the crisis.

Effects of player's actions:
Out of the Vault: If the Lone Wanderer resolves Trouble on the Homefront in the rebels' favor, Susie can be randomly encountered alive in the wasteland, during which she will explain that some order has been restored to Vault 101.

chr_00095501.summary: Christine Kendall is a asian child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Christine and her younger sister Monica are the daughters of John and Mary Kendall. During her adolescence, Christine became introverted due to living under a household with a strict Vault 101 security officer for a father. She was often the subject of verbal harangues from her father, even when she tried to appease him. This led her to become rather unhappy with life underground and more curious about the outside world. During her childhood, she was given the pejorative nickname "Mean Christine" by her peers, presumably for arrogant behavior on her part.

On August 3, 2274, Christine takes the G.O.A.T. exam, during which she displays an aversion to the Lone Wanderer, unsure of why they are speaking to her before class, as an extension of her teenage belief in superiority over them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Christine appears in Mr. Brotch's class as one of the students taking the G.O.A.T. exam alongside the Lone Wanderer.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Christine has sided with Amata's "rebels" during the crisis in Vault 101.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Child's Jumpsuit, Kid's Party Hat.

chr_000942c8.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_000942c8.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

chr_0008d10d.summary: Gary was one of the original inhabitants of Vault 108, and clones of him are the only people left in the Vault by 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Part of a grand cloning experiment with a fatal end, 54 clones of "Gary" were created. Each had varying levels of violent and psychotic traits and behaviors, leading to the scientists' deaths and Garys running freely throughout the Vault. They use inflections of voice tone, speaking only their name, to communicate and are hostile towards any outsiders.

A holotape labeled cloning log can be found in the Vault 108 cloning lab, which explains that Gary was cloned at least 54 times. All clones exhibited hostility towards non-clones, with each successive clone being more and more violent. When the Vault scientists started running out of room to store the clones, they planned to destroy some of them to make room for additional test subjects. Sometime afterward, the clones violently took control of the Vault.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Part of a grand cloning experiment with a fatal end, 54 clones of "Gary" were created. Each had varying levels of violent and psychotic traits and behaviors, leading to the scientists' deaths and Garys running freely throughout the Vault. They use inflections of voice tone, speaking only their name, to communicate and are hostile towards any outsiders.

A holotape labeled cloning log can be found in the Vault 108 cloning lab, which explains that Gary was cloned at least 54 times. All clones exhibited hostility towards non-clones, with each successive clone being more and more violent. When the Vault scientists started running out of room to store the clones, they planned to destroy some of them to make room for additional test subjects. Sometime afterward, the clones violently took control of the Vault.

chr_000892c7.summary: James, also known as Dad, is the father of the Lone Wanderer and Vault 101's physician.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Project Purity:
James was always an inquisitive, meticulous and determined man; this personality led him to form or join a group of like-minded scientists, who were set on changing the wasteland for the better. Before the Lone Wanderer was born, James led an ambitious scientific endeavor known as Project Purity. He and his group of scientists, including wife Catherine and Dr. Madison Li, aimed to build an advanced water purifier within the ruins of the Jefferson Memorial, which would serve to purify the water of the Potomac. The project began to lose momentum, lacking concrete results while having to compensate for lost time due to super mutant attacks. The number of mutants was steadily increasing, and protecting the project was becoming increasingly difficult for the Brotherhood.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Related quests:
• Baby Steps: James puts the one-year-old Lone Wanderer in a playpen in their room which contains the You're S.P.E.C.I.A.L.! book. After a brief absence, James returns and shows the child their mother's favorite Bible quotation, and takes his child to see Amata.
• Growing Up Fast: James has a small conversation with the Lone Wanderer at the beginning of their tenth birthday party, and later in the party gives them a BB gun as a birthday gift, and tasks them with killing a radroach.
• Future Imperfect: James has a brief conversation with his now 16-year-old before their G.O.A.T. exam.
• Escape!: James' unexpected absence from Vault 101 prompts a security crisis and propels the Lone Wanderer out into the wastes.
• Following in His Footsteps: The Lone Wanderer searches for their dad.

sections.text:

2 On his way back to Rivet City.

chr_000824ab.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Weapons, Armor, Supplies / Barter)
chr_000824ab.summary: Smiling Jack is a non-hostile raider merchant who runs his general shop in the Evergreen Mills bazaar in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jack is a master trader and barterer, having set up his business in the bazaar of the raider-controlled Evergreen Mills. He mends the raiders' equipment for them, which keeps him busy and unable to continue modifying and upgrading his pride and joy: The Terrible Shotgun.

Despite being a raider, Smiling Jack holds no animosity towards the Lone Wanderer and is not aggressive unless he is provoked. As a trader, he does not care who buys or sells from his store, so long as the caps are there. He holds no loyalty to the raiders he lives with, as he does not turn aggressive even if the Lone Wanderer kills them in his sight. Still, he urges them not to let the raiders see him trading with an outsider, likely fearing that the group would turn on him if he was caught doing so.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He stays at Evergreen Mills bazaar running a general shop.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Evergreen Mills Bazaar. Notable equipment & inventory: The Terrible Shotgun, Roving Trader Outfit. Provides services: Weapons, Armor, Supplies / Barter.

chr_0007f4ff.summary: Talon Company mercs are members of the Talon Company, a mercenary company operating in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only rank 1 mercs can be enslaved

Other interactions:
• Talon Company mercs are almost always hostile to the Lone Wanderer wherever they are encountered. In some areas, like Takoma Industrial and the Capitol Building, they will be found in combat with other groups such as super mutants, but will still be hostile to the player character.
• Talon Company mercs are involved in various random encounters across the Capital Wasteland, as well as in scripted encounters in certain locations, both in the base game and in Broken Steel.

Talon Company hit squads:
If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

chr_0006f92b.behavior: Very Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: ambush
chr_0006f92b.summary: Hitman is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Depending on the Lone Wanderer's actions, Talon Company mercenaries or Abolitionist hitmen will hunt down and attack them.

Burke's hitmen:
These hitmen are Talon Company mercs hired by Mister Burke. They will greet the target with a threat before immediately attacking. They carry a contract for extermination signed by Burke with the threat of the outcome of not satisfying Tennpenny's expectations.

Abolitionist hitmen:
These hitmen are average wastelanders who take contracts on killing prominent slavers. They will track down their slaver target and attack with the intent of killing them. They carry the contract killing note demanding "wasteland justice" by their employer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Hitmen will spawn in the game world depending on certain choices made in specific quests:
• Burke's hitmen will only appear during the Watch Your Back random encounter if The Power of the Atom was completed by helping Lucas Simms and disarming the bomb found in Megaton. They carry a contract for extermination signed by Burke, even if they were previously killed or has never spoke to by the Lone Wanderer.
• Abolitionist hitmen will only appear during the Kill the Slaver random encounter if Strictly Business was completed by helping Grouse and capturing his four VIP slaves or if the player character used the Mesmetron to enslave named or generic NPCs and send them to Paradise Falls up to a certain unknown threshold.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

chr_0006f833.summary: Hitman is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Depending on the Lone Wanderer's actions, Talon Company mercenaries or Abolitionist hitmen will hunt down and attack them.

Burke's hitmen:
These hitmen are Talon Company mercs hired by Mister Burke. They will greet the target with a threat before immediately attacking. They carry a contract for extermination signed by Burke with the threat of the outcome of not satisfying Tennpenny's expectations.

Abolitionist hitmen:
These hitmen are average wastelanders who take contracts on killing prominent slavers. They will track down their slaver target and attack with the intent of killing them. They carry the contract killing note demanding "wasteland justice" by their employer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Hitmen will spawn in the game world depending on certain choices made in specific quests:
• Burke's hitmen will only appear during the Watch Your Back random encounter if The Power of the Atom was completed by helping Lucas Simms and disarming the bomb found in Megaton. They carry a contract for extermination signed by Burke, even if they were previously killed or has never spoke to by the Lone Wanderer.
• Abolitionist hitmen will only appear during the Kill the Slaver random encounter if Strictly Business was completed by helping Grouse and capturing his four VIP slaves or if the player character used the Mesmetron to enslave named or generic NPCs and send them to Paradise Falls up to a certain unknown threshold.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sweet, always worried and not very bright, Stanley is the father of Beatrice, Mary and Gloria. Stanley and Andy are responsible for keeping the vault running, tending to all the machinery and acting as its janitors.

2260s:
On July 12, 2268, Stanley repairs the water purifier. This repair is a point of discussion between himself and Amata Almodovar when they engage in small talk the next day.

On that same day, Stanley performs routine maintenance on the pipes in the corridor outside the cafeteria. Midway through his work, he attends the birthday party of the Lone Wanderer. Though the Overseer presents the Pip-Boy 3000A to the Lone Wanderer, it is Stanley who selects the model. Though he admits that some might find the 3000A basic, Stanley believes the series is very reliable.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Stanley is the father of Beatrice Armstrong, Gloria, and Mary. Stanley's constant companion is Andy, a Mister Handy robot, that aids his human friend in cleaning and maintaining the vault. Stanley is friendly with the vault physician James and his child. In fact, during Escape!, he allows the Lone Wanderer to get past him without denouncing them to the vault's security, out of appreciation. However, he still says "Good riddance, get out" when the Lone Wanderer is exiled out of the vault after Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: He asks the Lone Wanderer about what they think about their new Pip-Boy 3000 which he fixed, and also gives a child's baseball cap.
• Future Imperfect: Stanley can be interacted with while he suffers from an illness.
• Trouble on the Homefront: He holds the password to the terminal used to sabotage Vault 101. It can either be pickpocketed from him, or it can be looted from him if he is to be killed.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer chooses to sabotage the Vault during Trouble on the Homefront, he may be killed by the explosion.

Other interactions:
• During the Lone Wanderer's escape at age 19, Stanley is encountered struggling against radroaches outside of the infirmary, but he is most likely saved by the arrival of Officer Gomez and Andy.

chr_0006f211.summary: Sonora Cruz is the leader of the Regulators in the Capital Wasteland in 2277, directing their operators and paying bounty rewards at the group's headquarters north of the Washington, D.C. ruins.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sonora serves as the leader of the Regulators, an organization that seeks to dispense justice and maintain peace where possible. The organization has only appeared within the past ten years prior to 2277, but it is unknown if she has served as the leader for the entire duration of the organization's existence. In any case, she did not set up the Regulators herself, as they were instead started by a group of unknown individuals who fund the organization.

Sonora operates out of the Regulators' headquarters at a small farmhouse near Canterbury Commons. She is assisted there by a few other members, although the majority of the Regulators are operating in secret elsewhere around the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• When the player character obtains the Lawbringer perk, they can gain Karma and caps by completing bounties, and bringing fingers to her from evil human or ghoul characters they have killed. If the Lone Wanderer's Karma is "Very Good," they will get a bonus from her, and her dialogue when turning in favors will offer greater praise and enthusiasm.
• Sonora will pay a special bounty reward of 1000 caps for Junders Plunkett's finger, commenting that "it's about time" that someone killed "that bastard" Plunkett.

sections.text: Known locations: Regulator Headquarters. Notable equipment & inventory: Regulator Duster, 10mm Round, itm_0006f210, itm_0002dd80.

chr_0006f1f2.summary: Daniel Littlehorn is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Scrapyard Office. Directly connected to quests: Lawbringer, Contract Killer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Having run his enigmatic organization for as long as any of his secretaries can remember, Daniel Littlehorn is now in his late seventies. His clandestine organization commits such malevolent acts as murdering innocents, tainting water supplies, and seeing to it that altruistic individuals falter in their objectives, all while maintaining the organization’s secrecy. He and a small group of secretaries operate out of a small office in the Scrapyard. While his secretaries handle the task of creating and filing records of the organization’s activities across the east coast, Daniel is responsible for paying the organization’s operatives for their work and accepting the evidence of that work, that evidence being the ears of altruistic individuals that he and the organization want dead.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
If the player character has the Contract Killer perk any good character they kill will have an ear on their corpse. This ear can then be sold to Daniel Littlehorn, located in the scrapyard office, for 15 caps and some XP per ear.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Scrapyard Office. Notable equipment & inventory: Grimy Pre-War Businesswear.

chr_0006c48d.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_0006c48d.summary: The Surgeon is a reclusive mad scientist conducting experiments inside the Red Racer factory in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Only known as "the Surgeon," a lunatic with a knack for the hard sciences, they have been conducting experiments into mind-control technology along with the study of ghoul and super mutant brain patterns, with the hope of selling their findings to the highest bidder. Their work has taken the form of a miniature high-tech chip that can be implanted into the body of the subject, turning them into an obedient slave. However, wary of the possibility their test subjects turn on them, the Surgeon also implemented a failsafe: small amounts of volatile material from an explosives cache they recovered are embedded in every chip and tuned to a specific frequency that, when broadcast throughout the factory, triggers a reaction that detonates the chip and instantly kills the subject; they consider this a last resort option they hope never to use.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
The Surgeon is hostile towards the player character unless they appear wearing the ghoul mask obtained by completing the quest Tenpenny Tower. If the mask is equipped, the Surgeon becomes friendly to them and can even be spoken to, though they only repeat the line "I'm not in the mood for you, asshole."

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: CEO Offices. Notable equipment & inventory: Tinted Reading Glasses, The Surgeon's Key, itm_000c71e1.

sections.title: Family
sections.text:
Allen Mack's wife, Gloria is a stoic person who exercises - or at least tries to exercise - a calming influence on her hard-headed husband and her three children: Wally, Steve, and Susie. She comes from the Armstrong family of Vault 101, and is the daughter of Stanley Armstrong, and the sister of Mary Kendall and Beatrice Armstrong. However, rather than technical affairs, she has readied herself for the position of a security officer if Vault 101 was ever compromised.

When James escaped the Vault, leading to a disaster within its walls, she was visiting her sister, Beatrice. The attack traumatized her, leaving her barely coherent, with the disgruntled Officer Stevie escorting her home to his father. Gloria turned out to be unsuited for security duties, as the event left her completely shattered, trying to pull herself together.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: She can be seen sitting at the table behind Allen Mack through the window he taunts the Lone Wanderer through. She later passes away off-screen and is never seen again.

sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Atrium. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Jumpsuit, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_00064d47.summary: Gallo is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 95 HP). Found primarily around County Sewer Mainline.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Gallo has made a home out of a small service room in the county sewer mainline. A mixture of the mainline's solitude, sewer gas contamination, and his long lifespan have had a significant impact on his mental state, making him quite mad and hostile towards all outsiders. He recently celebrated his birthday, having invited his two favorite gnomes and carving up feral ghoul corpses for consumption to mark the occasion.

Gallo has a small Nuka-Cola collection - including two trucks, five bottles, four Nuka-Cola bar stools, a neon Nuka-Cola sign, a Nuka-Cola clock above his bed, a Nuka-Cola lamp on his table, and a Nuka-Cola Quantum in his safe. He also has a Radiation King television in pristine condition on his shelf and keeps a pen of small radroaches as pets.
