sections.text: A little more stable than his sadistic partner, Richards is nonetheless perfectly willing to open fire on hapless dwellers, as per his standing orders. The posting at the atrium door, separating the entrance from the rest of the Vault, is a perfect spot for this.

They will also kill Tom and Mary Holden, who try to make a run for it - unless the player character is spotted first, causing both officers to attack them instead of the Holdens, who will flee to safety. If Richards isn't killed, he'll later appear again at the Vault door and immediately attack.

chr_00064911.summary: Officer Gomez is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 45 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront, Escape!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
An archetypal "good cop," Herman Gomez has more of a conscience than many of his fellow Vault 101 security officers. He is the husband of Pepper Gomez and the father of Freddie Gomez, whom he attempts to keep away from the Tunnel Snakes' influence. However, he knows that this is difficult because there are few other children Freddie's age in the Vault. More generally, Gomez is interested in youth outreach and preventing bullying in the Vault. He believes that responsibility lies with a parent to raise a child right, though if all else fails, the influence of Vault security can also have an impact.

As a friend of James, the Vault physician, Officer Gomez extends faith that he must have had his reasons for leaving the Vault in 2277, even if this view is not shared by most of his peers.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only drops a finger during Growing Up Fast and Escape!.

Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: If a scuffle occurs between the Lone Wanderer and Butch DeLoria over the sweetroll, Officer Gomez will intervene.
• Escape!: Gomez will be helping Stanley and Andy fight radroaches. Provided he is not attacked, he warns the Lone Wanderer that security is on the lookout for them. Gomez believes that James is innocent and suggests leaving the vault to search for him.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If he lives, Gomez will be the first vault resident the Lone Wanderer runs into. Staying civilized with him will have him escort the Lone Wanderer to either Amata or the current overseer. If Allen Mack attacks while any guards are around, the guards will immediately come to his side to protect him. This includes Officer Gomez.

sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is Susie and Wally Mack's brother, and Allen Mack and Gloria Mack's son. Stevie is 25 years old as of the events of Escape! He is a sadistic and gung-ho member of the Vault's security force, and willing to do anything to gain favor with his boss, including being particularly overzealous during emergencies.

He is responsible for the killing of Jonas Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• He will only drop a finger during Escape!

Quests:
• Escape!: Officer Mack is found in the security office interrogating Amata. If the Lone Wanderer took the overseer's gun from Amata, they have no choice but to fight Mack, due to the fact that he attacks them on sight. If one insisted Amata keeps her father's gun to protect herself, she will shoot Mack in self-defense, killing him. If you interrupt before Amata fires on him, she will escape and the player character will again be responsible for killing Mack.

chr_0006490f.summary: Officer Kendall is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 45 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront, Escape!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
John Kendall is the husband of Mary Kendall and the father of Christine and Monica. John is friendly, yet tough and no-nonsense. While he is not actively sinister, he will follow orders without putting much thought into it. Introspection is not a trait he commonly displays. He loves being a cop and whether what he is doing is right does not worry him; he is the law.

During the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party on July 13, 2268, Officer Kendall can be overheard talking with the overseer in the stairway to the upper level. Officer Kendall is assigned by the overseer to give the party just a few more minutes and then make sure everyone gets back to work. He may idley wish the Wanderer a happy birthday if near him, and gleefully remark the party sounds like fun.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

• He will only drop a finger prior to Trouble on the Homefront

• Escape!: The Lone Wanderer encounters Kendall just outside their room, whereupon Kendall will be attacked by several radroaches. The Lone Wanderer can sneak past him through the restrooms, attempt to save him from the radroaches, or kill him. He is the first person that can be killed in the game. He will become hostile after the radroaches are dead.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Officer Kendall will be present if he did not die during Escape! When interacted with, he blames the Lone Wanderer and James for the vault's problems.

sections.text:
He is the father of Paul Hannon Jr. and husband of Vikki Hannon.

He is extremely aggressive and by-the-book, and he wishes his vault security force was a real military with a war to win. He is not nearly as smart as he thinks he is, and his men are not nearly the crack security force he thinks they are. Spit and polish are everything to him; following orders is his highest calling.

chr_00063bfa.summary: Crazy Wolfgang is an eccentric caravan merchant, specializing in the sale of junk, in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wolfgang is an eccentric salesman, playing up a "crazy" persona to make sales for his wide inventory of mostly random junk and general supplies. He has a wide variety of over-the-top, alliterative names for his business, including the "Depot of Detritus," the "Shop of Slop" and the "Caravan of Crap." He can be traded with for a wide variety of wasteland finds, which he believes anyone can find value in, embodying the principle of one man's trash being another's treasure.

According to Uncle Roe, Wolfgang is just "like that," referring to how his sales methods and madman persona draw in customers. In particular, Wolfgang considers his use of the words junk, garbage, and other such terms to describe his wares to be a very successful marketing ploy, especially when he uses "junk"-related sexual innuendo to capture customers' attention.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Like all caravan merchants in the Capital Wasteland, Crazy Wolfgang's route takes him to Canterbury Commons, the Temple of the Union, Agatha's house, Paradise Falls, Arefu, Evergreen Mills, Megaton, and Rivet City.

This allows him to repair to 85% condition. After the second investment, he rewards the Lone Wanderer with between five and seven Stealth Boys, depending on level.

chr_00063bf9.summary: Lucky Harith is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 140 HP). Affiliated with Caravan Merchants. Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Harith is an easily excitable, eccentric salesman who believes that the way to bring about peace in a dangerous wasteland is to stock up on weapons, so that everyone is equally armed and has the capability to be dangerous themselves. Putting this belief into practice, Harith set up a caravan business with the help of Uncle Roe from Canterbury Commons, with Harith traveling the Capital Wasteland to sell weapons to prospective customers.

Harith considers himself a "student on the path of the wasteland," providing safety to wanderers through his trading of weaponry.

Note however that his actual skill is 5% lower, since he is wearing a Red Racer jumpsuit. After the second investment, he will reward the Lone Wanderer with what he calls a "micro-nuke" as a gift of gratitude.

He is rumored to have come from Oasis, although he does not make this information known to others. If asked to repair an item, he may reply that he will only do so if the item wishes to be repaired, and similarly when revealing his inventory will ask the Lone Wanderer to see if anything "calls out" to them.

chr_00063bf7.summary: Doc Hoff is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 140 HP). Affiliated with Caravan Merchants. Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Doc Hoff likes to call himself "the good doctor," although he does not directly heal people like a physician would; he is instead a chem dealer who offers "the finest of chemical assistance" to his customers. He also sells food, drinks and may repair one's gear. Doc Hoff is convinced that, through his sale of medicine and chems, he is helping to ease humanity's suffering in its dying years, for a price. As a traveling merchant, he does not have a definitive home office, although he is part of the caravan network associated with Ernest Roe in Canterbury Commons. Doc Hoff has a fairly elevated style of speaking, though his musings occasionally become somewhat macabre as he reflects on his place as a merchant of medicine in a violent wasteland.

chr_00062ab2.summary: Child slaver is a slaver appearing during the unmarked quest The Kid-Kidnapper outside Little Lamplight, to kidnap Bumble.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
One of the most capable slavers in Eulogy Jones' employ, she specializes in manipulating and abducting children - a particularly horrific character, even among the slavers of Paradise Falls. Evidently, she specializes in the enslavement of children and is shown to be adept at exploiting their naivety. When attempting to secure victims, she uses a facade consisting of a soft tone of voice and friendly behavior. For example, when talking to Bumble, she tells her that she is going on the "adventure express."

Where other slavers rule and dominate through violence and fear, she feigns friendship and interest to gain the child's trust, and manipulates them accordingly. In six-year-old Bumble's case, it means complimenting and convincing her that she is going on an adventure with her, rather than to a life of slavery.

chr_00061794.summary: Biwwy is a african american child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Little Lamplighters. Found primarily around The Great Chamber.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Biwwy is a nine-year-old inhabitant of Little Lamplight, recently kicked off the scavenging team due to his speech impediment annoying the other children to a point where they no longer wished to listen to him. He struggles with pronouncing the "L" and "R" sounds, and seems oblivious to his own speech impediment, as the Lone Wanderer may ask him to stop talking the way he does and is met by confusion on Biwwy's end. Similarly, if asked about "Biwwy" being his nickname, he is unaware that he possesses one at all. He is generally ostracized and avoided by the other children, and has subsequently resigned himself to solitude in the Great Chamber.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Biwwy doesn't seem to have any friends, as everyone finds him annoying, possibly because of his speech impediment and apparent hyperactive nature.

chr_000606cd.summary: Talon Company mercs are members of the Talon Company, a mercenary company operating in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

* Only rank 1 mercs can be enslaved

Other interactions:
• Talon Company mercs are almost always hostile to the Lone Wanderer wherever they are encountered. In some areas, like Takoma Industrial and the Capitol Building, they will be found in combat with other groups such as super mutants, but will still be hostile to the player character.
• Talon Company mercs are involved in various random encounters across the Capital Wasteland, as well as in scripted encounters in certain locations, both in the base game and in Broken Steel.

Talon Company hit squads:
If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

chr_0005f9ce.summary: The Mysterious Stranger is an enigmatic character that has made multiple appearances in the Fallout series, typically only when one has the Mysterious Stranger perk and uses V.A.T.S..

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Mysterious Stranger has been spotted throughout the wasteland in the aftermath of the Great War, always wearing his trademark trench coat and fedora. He appears suddenly to certain people during combat and assists them with his signature.44 Magnum before vanishing as abruptly as he appeared. Chronologically, the Stranger has been seen assisting members of the Vault 76 reclamation effort, the Vault Dweller, the Chosen One, the Lone Wanderer, the Courier, and the Sole Survivor. He has also been spotted within certain active Vaults.

Similar figures to the Stranger have also been seen in post-War America, such as the Mysterious Savior, a different man wearing identical clothing who provides life-saving healing, and Miss Fortune, a non-lethal female counterpart who wears a veil and a revealing armored showgirl outfit.

chr_0005eddf.summary: Catherine was a scientist and the wife of James, working together on Project Purity, an attempt to produce purified water in mass quantities, overcoming the critical shortage of this essential good in the Capital Wasteland. Despite intense efforts, the Project was cut short when Catherine died after giving birth to the Lone Wanderer in 2258.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Little is known about Catherine's background or origins. She was a dedicated scientist, familiar with the Bible and Christianity, with her favorite passage being Revelation 21:6: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely." This passage inspired her life's work on Project Purity: Together with James, they attempted to bring the waters of life to the Capital Wasteland and restore it. Catherine was originally one of several scientists working on the project, eventually falling in love with James and marrying him. She brought with herself not just knowledge, but also beauty within and without, and a spectacular passion for life and love.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Baby Steps: Catherine dies in the prologue of the game. She appears during a cutscene that shows the Lone Wanderer's birth, but only her legs and her voice can be perceived. A holotape recording of James flirting with her called "Better Days" can be located in the Jefferson Memorial's lower levels. Her favorite quote from the Bible is Revelation 21:6, and reflects one of the core themes of the game.
• In Point Lookout, while intoxicated on the Mother Punga, the Lone Wanderer will find one of the many giant bobbleheads on a medical examination table with a skeleton marked "Mom," balloons, and a party hat. The bobblehead will say "Blech. If my kid looked like that, I'd abandon it too." The skeleton is Catherine, reflecting the lack of maternal presence in the Lone Wanderer's life.

chr_0005cfe8.summary: Enclave soldiers are the fighting force of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Enclave officer:
Enclave officers wear standard Enclave officer uniforms and hats. They are armed with plasma pistols, and carry plasma grenades as backup.

Enclave trainee (Rank 0):
Enclave trainees can be found at certain Enclave outposts after The Waters of Life, doing push-ups under the supervision of an Enclave officer. Trainees are equipped only with laser pistols; they do not wear helmets, and their power armor is in poor condition.

Enclave soldier (Ranks 1 and 2):
Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

chr_00058059.summary: Mel is a wannabe mugger the Lone Wanderer may come across during the Locked and Unloaded random encounter. He wants the player character to give him all of their caps. He will appear as friendly on the radar, and his clearly unassertive and stammering speaking voice makes his demands indeed pathetic.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mel used to live at a mercenary settlement, but after being forced out, he has taken up the role of a highwayman in the Capital Wasteland. He possesses an unloaded sawed-off shotgun and will threaten the Lone Wanderer with it should they encounter him. However, he poses very little threat owing to his nervousness, ineptitude, and lack of ammunition.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
There may be several conversation options, depending on skills:
• (Speech) Back off or I'll make you regret threatening me.
• (Speech) How about I give you 5 caps and you leave me alone?
• (Intelligence) Bullshit, a mugger in the Wasteland? A real raider would've shot me already.
• (Perception) That gun doesn't look loaded.
• All right. I haven't killed anyone all day. Let's go.
• I can't give you all my stuff, sorry.

If a skill-based topic is used, Mel will end the conversation without turning hostile and will cower as if fleeing. If one refuses to be give anything, he may turn hostile. Mel will also fight any roving hostiles that travel near him (i.e. raiders or critters). But, since his shotgun is unloaded, he is limited to fighting unarmed.

chr_0002e032.summary: Paladin Northup is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: DC Ruins Exploration.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Northup and his team were sent from the Citadel to find a storage box of mini nukes in Chesterbrook, following a lead uncovered by a scribe. He and his team managed to find the box and also its key, but were ambushed by super mutants soon after. They were fighting a losing battle, constantly attacked by mutants every several hours, resulting in them going without sleep for days. As they lacked a radio, they had no way to call for help, so many of Northup's subordinates began to lose hope of survival; however, they still continue to hold out.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Paladin Northup and his team would have appeared somewhere in Chesterbrook, the entire location of which was cut from Fallout 3. However, Northup's dialogue evidences some possible interactions he would have had.

If the Lone Wanderer showed up, Northup would have warned them about the situation and advised them to leave the area while the mutants were still focused on him and his team. If spoken to again, he would repeat his warning, shouting at the Lone Wanderer for not heeding his advice.

If the Lone Wanderer offered their help, he would have requested for them to exterminate any super mutants they stumbled across in the nearby area. However, he would explain that he had no reward he could offer them except him and his team's sincere thanks.

chr_000290a6.summary: James, also known as Dad, is the father of the Lone Wanderer and Vault 101's physician.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Project Purity:
James was always an inquisitive, meticulous and determined man; this personality led him to form or join a group of like-minded scientists, who were set on changing the wasteland for the better. Before the Lone Wanderer was born, James led an ambitious scientific endeavor known as Project Purity. He and his group of scientists, including wife Catherine and Dr. Madison Li, aimed to build an advanced water purifier within the ruins of the Jefferson Memorial, which would serve to purify the water of the Potomac. The project began to lose momentum, lacking concrete results while having to compensate for lost time due to super mutant attacks. The number of mutants was steadily increasing, and protecting the project was becoming increasingly difficult for the Brotherhood.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Related quests:
• Baby Steps: James puts the one-year-old Lone Wanderer in a playpen in their room which contains the You're S.P.E.C.I.A.L.! book. After a brief absence, James returns and shows the child their mother's favorite Bible quotation, and takes his child to see Amata.
• Growing Up Fast: James has a small conversation with the Lone Wanderer at the beginning of their tenth birthday party, and later in the party gives them a BB gun as a birthday gift, and tasks them with killing a radroach.
• Future Imperfect: James has a brief conversation with his now 16-year-old before their G.O.A.T. exam.
• Escape!: James' unexpected absence from Vault 101 prompts a security crisis and propels the Lone Wanderer out into the wastes.
• Following in His Footsteps: The Lone Wanderer searches for their dad.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Early life:
Madison was born around the year 2229. Her admiration for James later developed into romantic feelings over the course of their work, but she kept them hidden out of respect for James' marriage to Catherine. Though it strained her personal relationship with them, her professional relationship never changed.

The progress of the project faced numerous complications, not the least of which were frequent super mutant attacks, but the martial support of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel allowed them to continue in relative safety, though Madison personally did not trust the organization's motives for lending their aid.

chr_0005215f.summary: Grandma Sparkle is a trader and cook residing at Wilhelm's Wharf in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Despite recent super mutant and raider incursions into the surrounding area in 2277, Sparkle has refused to leave her encampment at the wharf and protects her claim through her skill with a hunting rifle and the support of her family, who frequently go out searching for mirelurk meat. She claims to have tasted many types of meat (up to and including yao guai) and says that mirelurk is the most delicious.

Due to her relative isolation, Sparkle does not involve herself in the greater politics of the Capital Wasteland, and so does not recognize the threat some groups present to herself or others. However, she is happy to receive visitors and is welcoming towards any and all, even bandits using the wharf as a hideout to plan their activities.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
If the Lone Wanderer asks Grandma Sparkle about any local happenings, she will mention being visited by "some fellas" looking for a "dogooder" from a Vault, referring to the Talon Company mercs who hunt the player character if they have good Karma.
• If the Lone Wanderer has bad Karma, Grandma Sparkle would mention being visited by people looking for a "troublemaker" from a Vault, referring to the Regulators who hunt the player character if they have bad Karma.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC15a (Grayditch — Anchorage Memorial). Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Weapons, Armor, Alcohol, Books & Schematics.

chr_0005213f.summary: The Preacher (appearing as a simple wastelander in-game) is a crazed inhabitant of Seward Square in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Preacher is standing on the second floor of a building in an alleyway west of the Ranger compound entrance in Seward Square. From there, he preaches madness to anyone that can hear him, with intermittent complaints about severe headaches. He suffers from frightening revelations.

The topics of his rants vary. He rants about the apocalypse, the sun and the sun in a jar, trees to the north and an evil worm that he plans to blow up with the explosives he gathered. The alley he overlooks has been rigged with five frag mines and five mini nukes that he detonates if anyone tries to get close to him.

There is a hostage (another wastelander) at the east end of the alley the Lone Wanderer can talk to about the booby-trapped alley and the Preacher.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• If the player approaches the Preacher, he will set off the charges (they go off even if the player disarmed all the mines and mini-nukes), moments after waving at the player character. The ledge he occupies is not accessible through normal means and contains nothing of value.
• Dogmeat does not trigger the scripted explosion and can retrieve all of the mini nukes should the Lone Wanderer keep their distance.
• The Lone Wanderer can talk to the hostage and, with a Charisma 1 check, convince him to confront the Preacher for negative Karma. This will result in him running towards the Preacher but being blown up by the mini nukes and killing the Preacher in the process.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Seward Sq. Southeast. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0005157a.summary: Christine Kendall is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Rebels. Found primarily around Vault 101 Lower Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Christine and her younger sister Monica are the daughters of John and Mary Kendall. During her adolescence, Christine became introverted due to living under a household with a strict Vault 101 security officer for a father. She was often the subject of verbal harangues from her father, even when she tried to appease him. This led her to become rather unhappy with life underground and more curious about the outside world. During her childhood, she was given the pejorative nickname "Mean Christine" by her peers, presumably for arrogant behavior on her part.

On August 3, 2274, Christine takes the G.O.A.T. exam, during which she displays an aversion to the Lone Wanderer, unsure of why they are speaking to her before class, as an extension of her teenage belief in superiority over them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Christine appears in Mr. Brotch's class as one of the students taking the G.O.A.T. exam alongside the Lone Wanderer.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Christine has sided with Amata's "rebels" during the crisis in Vault 101.

sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Lower Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Jumpsuit, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_0004e896.summary: Freddie Gomez is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Rebels. Found primarily around Vault 101 Atrium/Upper Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The son of Herman and Pepper Gomez, Freddie was the result of an unplanned pregnancy. At just nine years old, Freddie was diagnosed with Vault depressive syndrome, which was considered highly unusual for someone of his age. Freddie's condition was known to some residents of the Vault by 2268;

As Freddie grew older, Vault 101's physician, James, noted that his depressive condition was worsening. Freddie showed signs of lethargy, anxiety, and low self-esteem. On many days, Freddie was unable to get out of bed in the morning; meanwhile, on days he was able to function, Freddie would mask his issues by acting out as a bully. Vault-Tec protocols dictated that James prescribe chlorpromazine for Freddie, but James worried that Freddie might become permanently dependent on the medication.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Freddie Gomez is one of the Lone Wanderer's classmates taking the G.O.A.T. at the same time. At the end of the G.O.A.T. exam, Freddie is the only person who has not submitted his exam to Mr. Brotch. He can be heard struggling on the last question, even though the only choice is "overseer."
• Trouble on the Homefront: Freddie is part of the Tunnel Snakes in this quest, and is one of the more hesitant members of the Vault rebels. If one chooses to sabotage the vault, Freddie and the other residents will flee into the wasteland.

Effects of player's actions:
Should the Lone Wanderer choose to destroy Vault 101 in Trouble on the Homefront, a random encounter is enabled in which the player finds the corpses of the Gomez family, with a different individual each time the encounter triggers.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Atrium/Upper Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Tunnel Snake Outfit, itm_000236d8.

chr_0004e895.summary: Susie Mack is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Rebels, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Lower Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Susie is the daughter of Allen and Gloria Mack, and the younger sister of both Stevie and Wally. Growing up, Susie despises the Tunnel Snakes, of which her brother Wally is a member. However, Wally does not give Susie a hard time, as she has something of a mean streak in her teenage years. When taking the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, Susie has no respect for the Lone Wanderer, and aggressively shuns any attempt from them to even speak with her. Prior to the test, she engages in small talk with Freddie Gomez, on whom she secretly has a crush. After the test, Mr. Brotch informs Susie that she is headed for a teaching career, sarcastically surmising this must be due to her "gift" for communication. Susie is unsurprised by and somewhat apathetic of the results.

By 2277, Susie has become more mature and thoughtful.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Susie Mack is one of the Lone Wanderer's classmates taking the G.O.A.T. at the same time.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Susie Mack sides with Amata's rebels during the crisis.

Effects of player's actions:
Out of the Vault: If the Lone Wanderer resolves Trouble on the Homefront in the rebels' favor, Susie can be randomly encountered alive in the wasteland, during which she will explain that some order has been restored to Vault 101.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Lower Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_0004e894.summary: Wally Mack is a resident of Vault 101 in 2277 and is a member of a greaser gang called the Tunnel Snakes.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wally is the son of Allen and Gloria Mack. Wally's siblings are Stevie and Susie.

Wally is the brains of the Tunnel Snakes. Butch DeLoria and Paul Hannon Jr. are Wally's friends and fellow gang members. During their formative years, the Tunnel Snakes harassed other students in Vault 101, even being bold enough to taunt the overseer's daughter, Amata Almodovar. Butch presumes to be the leader of the Tunnel Snakes, but Wally might disagree if challenged.

He does not talk as much as the others, but they listen to what he has to say when he does say something. He is one of the Lone Wanderer's peers in Vault 101 and is encountered throughout the Lone Wanderer's youth inside Vault 101.

By 2287, Mack had traveled to the Commonwealth, where he reestablished the Tunnel Snakes under his rule.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tunnel Snakes Rule!: Wally Mack (as a glowing one) must be eliminated in Fens Way station.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Lower Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Jumpsuit, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_0004cfc7.summary: Tara is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 20 HP). Found primarily around Bomb Storage.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: In 2257, Tara and four other mercenaries - Dave, Jeff Strayer, Dukov, and Mister Crowley - were hired by independent financier Allistair Tenpenny to break into Fort Constantine supposedly to retrieve a rare weapon; as discovered by Crowley later, it was actually a pristine set of T-51b power armor, contained in its experimental chamber. Dukov confidently claims that he and Tara had a physical relationship while working for Tenpenny, though his blowhard personality makes this questionable. Tara actually managed to survive and got as far as the fort's basement level, just outside the experimental chamber. However, she was stopped there upon realizing she lacked the special keys possessed by the others needed to open the chamber.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: The Lone Wanderer can obtain the warhead storage key from Tara's body to unlock the fort's warhead storage room and bypass the Very Hard-locked door.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Bomb Storage. Notable equipment & inventory: Raider Painspike Armor, Warhead Storage Key, 10mm Round.

chr_0004bf63.summary: Talon Company mercs are members of the Talon Company, a mercenary company operating in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only rank 1 mercs can be enslaved

Other interactions:
• Talon Company mercs are almost always hostile to the Lone Wanderer wherever they are encountered. In some areas, like Takoma Industrial and the Capitol Building, they will be found in combat with other groups such as super mutants, but will still be hostile to the player character.
• Talon Company mercs are involved in various random encounters across the Capital Wasteland, as well as in scripted encounters in certain locations, both in the base game and in Broken Steel.

Talon Company hit squads:
If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

chr_00048127.summary: Slaver is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 80 HP). Found primarily around Mall Southwest. Directly connected to quests: Head of State.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Slavery is a significant part of the Capital Wasteland's economy. Paradise Falls is a slaver compound, and several quests feature slavery as either major or minor elements, such as Head of State and its association with slavery and Abraham Lincoln's role as the "Great Emancipator."

Additionally, the Lone Wanderer can capture people to sell them to slavers. The Lone Wanderer can even buy a slave, Clover, who will then serve as a bodyguard. The Lone Wanderer does not have the option of activating or defusing Clover's explosive collar.

The number of slaves present compared to the number of slavers is remarkably low, meaning that the slaves are being shipped off somewhere. It is revealed by Wernher that many of these slaves are being shipped off to work in the Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State
• Strictly Business
• Those!
• Strictly Profitable
• The Kid-Kidnapper

Effects of player's actions:
Slavers are generally not hostile to the Lone Wanderer as long as they are not provoked with hostile dialogue responses, but attacking them can make the Paradise Falls slavers permanently enemies with the player character. If slavers are hostile first and killed, Paradise Falls slavers will not be initially hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Mall Southwest. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00048122.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox
chr_00048122.summary: Ronald Laren is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Found primarily around Factory Floor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
After his wife died, he wandered the wasteland before settling in Girdershade. Living close to Sierra Petrovita has increased his negative feelings regarding his loneliness, as he misses the physical intimacy he once shared with his wife. As a result, he has made several advances at Sierra, but she is oblivious to his motivations due to her pursuit of Nuka-Cola. Ronald is angered by her rejection, and although he does not want to physically force himself on her, he still wishes to spite her in other ways.

According to Sierra, Ronald is a skilled fighter. She recalls one occasion where he killed two raiders at Girdershade and punched their leader, Lug-Nut, in the face.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Nuka-Cola Challenge: Should one accept Sierra's mission to obtain Nuka-Cola Quantum for her, Ronald will attempt to convince the Lone Wanderer to give all the Quantums to him.
• Grady's Package: Ronald is the recipient of Grady's package, which is the naughty nightwear found in Marigold station. Depending on one's Speech and/or Barter skills, they can get him to pay up to 300 caps for it.

Effects of player's actions:
• A female player character with the Black Widow perk can convince him to retrieve the Nuka-Cola Quantums for her, with the promise of a threesome with her and Sierra. Excited, Ronald will run off to the distant Nuka-Cola plant and die. If the Lone Wanderer then asks Sierra if he's been bothering her, she'll say she hasn't seen him in a while, but she's sure he'll come back.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Factory Floor. Notable equipment & inventory: Leather Armor, The Kneecapper.

chr_000464f7.summary: Slaver is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 80 HP). Found primarily around Mall Southwest. Directly connected to quests: Head of State.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Slavery is a significant part of the Capital Wasteland's economy. Paradise Falls is a slaver compound, and several quests feature slavery as either major or minor elements, such as Head of State and its association with slavery and Abraham Lincoln's role as the "Great Emancipator."

Additionally, the Lone Wanderer can capture people to sell them to slavers. The Lone Wanderer can even buy a slave, Clover, who will then serve as a bodyguard. The Lone Wanderer does not have the option of activating or defusing Clover's explosive collar.

The number of slaves present compared to the number of slavers is remarkably low, meaning that the slaves are being shipped off somewhere. It is revealed by Wernher that many of these slaves are being shipped off to work in the Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State
• Strictly Business
• Those!
• Strictly Profitable
• The Kid-Kidnapper

Effects of player's actions:
Slavers are generally not hostile to the Lone Wanderer as long as they are not provoked with hostile dialogue responses, but attacking them can make the Paradise Falls slavers permanently enemies with the player character. If slavers are hostile first and killed, Paradise Falls slavers will not be initially hostile.

chr_000458be.summary: Sam Warrick (also called Ken Rollins in certain localized versions) is a raider roaming the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sam developed a friendly rivalry with Laszlo Radford, who considers him a friend. Sam also has a fondness for the pre-War sport of baseball, carrying a few keepsakes with him wherever he goes, and imbibes Jet on the side.

At some point, Sam became affiliated with the raider gang occupying Evergreen Mills. Armed with his sniper rifle, he started venturing out into the wasteland, hunting down weaker creatures and mutants alike. The raider's ultimate goal is finding a high-value target to sight in his scope and collect the caps bounty on them in order to pay for "special services" from Madame and her working girls at the Mills' bazaar.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
Sam Warrick spawns randomly at Type B locations, seen chasing and hunting a wastelander. If he kills the wastelander, he will attack the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Sunglasses, Baseball, Baseball Glove, Leather Armor, Jet.

chr_000444ab.summary: Talon Company mercs are members of the Talon Company, a mercenary company operating in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only rank 1 mercs can be enslaved

Other interactions:
• Talon Company mercs are almost always hostile to the Lone Wanderer wherever they are encountered. In some areas, like Takoma Industrial and the Capitol Building, they will be found in combat with other groups such as super mutants, but will still be hostile to the player character.
• Talon Company mercs are involved in various random encounters across the Capital Wasteland, as well as in scripted encounters in certain locations, both in the base game and in Broken Steel.

Talon Company hit squads:
If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

chr_00043dec.summary: Defender Rococo Rockfowl is a soldier and heavy-weapons specialist of the Brotherhood of Steel Outcasts, stationed at Fort Independence in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Rococo Rockfowl is the Outcasts' heavy-weapons specialist at Fort Independence, primarily tasked with guarding the bridge from the Fairfax ruins due to regular raider incursions. Apart from perimeter defense, he is often paired with Defender Morgan for special operations, including reconnaissance missions in Fairfax to determine the extent of raider encroachment in the area. On one occasion, the pair had been placing explosives in the utility tunnels underneath Fairfax in order to disturb raider operations when they were interrupted by one of the raider patrols; both Rockfowl and Morgan, diligently operating according to mission parameters, opted not to engage and returned back to Fort Independence.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Defender Rockfowl patrols the highway overpass next to the entrance to Fort Independence.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
Rockfowl will attack if the Lone Wanderer decides to start a fight with the Outcasts.

chr_00043deb.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: happy. AI packages: dialogue, eat, sleep, sandbox, patrol
chr_00043deb.summary: Defender Anne Marie Morgan is a soldier of the Brotherhood of Steel Outcasts, stationed at Fort Independence.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Posted on the perimeter of Fort Independence alongside Rococo Rockfowl, Defender Morgan is a tough soldier who does not take her duties lightly. She is a close friend of Protector Henry Casdin, the leader of the Outcasts, and is fiercely loyal to their cause.

Most wastelanders approaching the Outcasts' base will quickly learn to respect her laser rifle and no-nonsense attitude. Anyone approaching with hostile intentions will learn even quicker that the rifle is not just for show, as Morgan takes their head off. Any wastelander who catches her reference earns her grudging respect, or disdain, if they do not. Morgan also enjoys black humor and wit, but not overconfidence, considering it borderline suicidal.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Outcast Collection Agent: Morgan says to speak with Protector Casdin about a job to turn in loot for supplies.

Other interactions:
• When the Lone Wanderer first encounters Morgan, a battle is triggered between her and two raiders who suddenly attack from the southern road. After the raiders are dead, she will speak with the Lone Wanderer and tell them to talk to Protector Casdin.
• She and the other Outcasts will turn hostile if told to "shut up and get that fucking gun out of my face" when spoken to for the first time.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Fort Independence Access.

chr_00041712.summary: Megaton settlers are the unnamed wastelanders who have settled, but do not officially reside, in the city of Megaton, in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Megaton's unusual immigration laws seem to have created a condition where a substantial portion of the population of the town is in this situation. Essentially, new visitors to the town seem to be approved individually by the sheriff/mayor, Lucas Simms. Meeting this approval allows one to remain inside the town's protective walls, but does not constitute citizenship. Non-citizens of the town are not permitted to own housing, and instead must either rent lodging at Moriarty's Saloon, or for the less transient settlers, space in the common house is shared communally.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the player character's Karma is at the "very good" level, once per day while in town, a Megaton settler will come and give them some gift, such as bottle caps (sometimes even only 1 cap), food, a stimpak, or ammunition. The settler can usually be found around the entrance of Megaton and can vary in clothing, as well as change equipment throughout the game.
• If the player character decides to destroy Megaton with the bomb located in the town's center, any surviving settlers (known as Megaton refugees) that the player character encounters will immediately become hostile towards them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Brass Lantern. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0004168a.summary: Gary was one of the original inhabitants of Vault 108, and clones of him are the only people left in the Vault by 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Part of a grand cloning experiment with a fatal end, 54 clones of "Gary" were created. Each had varying levels of violent and psychotic traits and behaviors, leading to the scientists' deaths and Garys running freely throughout the Vault. They use inflections of voice tone, speaking only their name, to communicate and are hostile towards any outsiders.

A holotape labeled cloning log can be found in the Vault 108 cloning lab, which explains that Gary was cloned at least 54 times. All clones exhibited hostility towards non-clones, with each successive clone being more and more violent. When the Vault scientists started running out of room to store the clones, they planned to destroy some of them to make room for additional test subjects. Sometime afterward, the clones violently took control of the Vault.

chr_00040c39.summary: Protector Henry Casdin is the leader of the Brotherhood of Steel Outcasts in the Capital Wasteland. He is also a special dweller.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Level-headed and professional, Protector Casdin was once one of the most accomplished soldiers of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel and traveled with Owyn Lyons during the expedition. He fought with the Elder side-by-side during the Scourge of the Pitt. However, he broke ties with the Elder during the Schism. It was a result of dissatisfaction with Lyons' focus on protecting the wastes by killing super mutants. A part of Lyons' contingent perceived it as an ineffectual waste of men and resources that would ultimately destroy the Brotherhood. The situation deteriorated, finally tipping when Elder Lyons ignored their repeated requests to recover tech from Fort Independence, a pre-War scientific military base.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Protector Casdin can be found standing at the entrance to Fort Independence, the headquarters of the Brotherhood Outcasts. He holds one of several keys to Fort Independence.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Outcast Collection Agent: One can trade pieces of power armor, energy weapons, sensor modules, scrap metal and alien power cells to Casdin in return for various loot and, eventually, entrance to Fort Independence. Items turned in are added directly to his inventory, causing him to automatically equip any item given to him if it is better than his current equipment; this applies to armor as well as weapons.

Other interactions:
• If one possesses Outcast power armor when encountering Protector Casdin for the first time, he will confiscate it, even if they are wearing it. One can safely wear Linden's Outcast power armor around him, though.
• He will no longer confiscate the Outcast power armor once the Lone Wanderer becomes a friend of the Outcasts by doing his repeatable quest.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escaped Slaves: These slaves appear in a random encounter, and they can give the player the location of the Temple of the Union.
• Water, Water, Nowhere: Another encounter has two wastelanders and two escaped slaves fighting over a fridge filled with purified water. After the fight is over, the surviving side will become hostile to the player character if they get too close to the water.

chr_0002f7a0.summary: Slaver is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Slavery is a significant part of the Capital Wasteland's economy. Paradise Falls is a slaver compound, and several quests feature slavery as either major or minor elements, such as Head of State and its association with slavery and Abraham Lincoln's role as the "Great Emancipator."

Additionally, the Lone Wanderer can capture people to sell them to slavers. The Lone Wanderer can even buy a slave, Clover, who will then serve as a bodyguard. The Lone Wanderer does not have the option of activating or defusing Clover's explosive collar.

The number of slaves present compared to the number of slavers is remarkably low, meaning that the slaves are being shipped off somewhere. It is revealed by Wernher that many of these slaves are being shipped off to work in the Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State
• Strictly Business
• Those!
• Strictly Profitable
• The Kid-Kidnapper

Effects of player's actions:
Slavers are generally not hostile to the Lone Wanderer as long as they are not provoked with hostile dialogue responses, but attacking them can make the Paradise Falls slavers permanently enemies with the player character. If slavers are hostile first and killed, Paradise Falls slavers will not be initially hostile.

chr_0002e2a2.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_00026362.summary: Enclave soldiers are the fighting force of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Enclave officer:
Enclave officers wear standard Enclave officer uniforms and hats. They are armed with plasma pistols, and carry plasma grenades as backup.

Enclave trainee (Rank 0):
Enclave trainees can be found at certain Enclave outposts after The Waters of Life, doing push-ups under the supervision of an Enclave officer. Trainees are equipped only with laser pistols; they do not wear helmets, and their power armor is in poor condition.

Enclave soldier (Ranks 1 and 2):
Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: MQ08EnclaveGuard02), Enclave Soldier is defined as a African American in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Appears in or relates to quests: Finding the Garden of Eden. Linked story events: Vault 87 G.E.C.K. & Enclave Ambush.

Regular Enclave soldiers wear Enclave power armor, and are usually armed with laser rifles and laser pistols. On rare occasions, they can also be equipped with flamers or rippers and sometimes can carry a plasma rifle. They also carry a random chem, like Psycho or Buffout.

chr_0003d34a.summary: Agatha is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 35 HP). Found primarily around Agatha's House. Directly connected to quests: Agatha's Song.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Agatha is a 76-year-old violinist and the descendant of a long line of talented, classical musicians, including her great-great grandmother Hilda Egglebrecht. Hilda was also a violinist, and among the world's best musicians, leading her to be invited to Vault 92 when the War broke out. Agatha knows of her familial ties to the musician through a paper trail of letters Hilda sent to her daughter, Mary, before the vault was sealed; as such, Hilda’s "diaries" are deemed the final contact that the Egglebrecht family had with her, and the letters were subsequently passed down from Mary, all the way to Agatha.

Though Agatha is unaware of the Vault-Tec experiment that led her to her great-great grandmother's demise in the vault, she knows that Hilda was in possession of the Soil Stradivarius, a priceless, one-of-a-kind violin.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quest:
Agatha's Song: Agatha asks the Lone Wanderer to recover the Soil Stradivarius and music sheets. It is possible to be locked out of this quest if the Lone Wanderer chooses to respond in a mean and disrespectful way.

Other interactions:
With a high Charisma, Lady Killer perk or Speech, the player character can obtain her ammunition box key.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mister Brotch inherited the position of a schoolteacher from his father and grandfather. Since the day the Vault 101 residents entered the vault, there has been a Brotch as a schoolteacher. Mr. Brotch is concerned about carrying on that tradition, but with no children of his own, he is beginning to worry that he will be the last in line. He is the man responsible for administering the G.O.A.T. exams. He once modified a utility jumpsuit to improve his odds of survival in the wastes, in case that he would ever have to leave the vault.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: In the Lone Wanderer's youth, Edwin can be found in the classroom. During the Trouble on the Homefront quest, he can be found in the Vault 101 jail cell. If he is released, he will join the rebels in the vault's clinic.

• Trouble on the Homefront: Brotch has been imprisoned due to his loyalty to Amata Almodovar during the rebellion.

chr_0003d346.summary: Allen Mack is a resident of Vault 101, a fervent isolationist, and its potential overseer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The head of the Mack household, Allen is a powerful presence in the Vault, and believes that it's a good life, sealed forever underground. Anyone who goes out of their way to mess it up is a sworn enemy of his. He is extremely protective of his family, When James entered Vault 101 and became its resident physician, Allen was deeply against taking him or his child in, believing that the Vault should remain shut. If it wasn't for the calming influence of his wife, Gloria, he would likely be even more aggressive. He certainly resolved to replace Alphonse Almodovar, should anything happen to him. while addicted to unspecified "pills" that James simply refused to give him at one point.

His redeeming feature is his love for his family.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: While never interacted with directly, Allen is briefly met on the way out, in an inaccessible common room, pounding on and shouting through the glass to alert others to the Lone Wanderer's presence. Gloria Mack is in the background.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If the player chooses to kill the overseer during their escape, Allen Mack rises to the position, as he was involved in saving numerous people. However, instead of opening the Vault, as expected, he decided to seal it permanently, leading to the uprising. Mack cannot be peacefully convinced to open the Vault, and the only options are either killing him or breaking the back of the rebellion for him. Mack will reward the player with the modified utility jumpsuit, then kick them out of the Vault.

sections.text: • Only during Trouble on the Homefront if he becomes the overseer.

chr_00038df5.summary: Anna Holt is a botanist and member of the scientist staff that works under Doctor Madison Li together with Janice Kaplinski on portable fusion power and hydroponics experiments.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Holt is responsible for the gestation of naturally occurring foodstuffs during her tenure in the Rivet City science lab, where she works under the esteemed Doctor Madison Li. and dealing with Li's occasional forgetfulness.

Furthermore, the distractions from her work by visitors is certainly not helping her less than cheery disposition, especially in the case of Doctor Zimmer's constant pestering about his android.

She gladly uprooted and took her research to the Jefferson Memorial with the rest of the laboratory staff when James returned from Vault 112 with the knowledge of how to successfully complete Project Purity. After the team restarted the project with little trouble, she was held hostage with the other scientists by the invading Enclave.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

chr_000388e3.summary: Lug-Nut is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 60 HP). Affiliated with Raiders. Found primarily around Marigold Station.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
An adversary of Ronald Laren, Lug-Nut is a raider who suffers from episodes of depression and mania due to his chem addiction. He recently had two pairs of nightwear made by a man known as The Tailor, a post-War master of apparel. Lug-Nut sent one set of the nightwear to his brother Lag-Bolt. He has hidden one pair of nightwear in an old caretaker's locker, as the deceased Grady will not be needing it any more.

Lug-Nut is mentioned by Sierra Petrovita when asked more about Ronald Laren. She will start talking about how tough Ronald is and will mention Lug-Nut and two other raiders. The two unknown raiders were killed by Ronald, who then punched Lug-Nut in the face.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Grady's Package: Lug-Nut appears and confronts the Lone Wanderer as soon as they loot the naughty nightwear. At this point, the Lone Wanderer can give him the naughty nightwear, kill him or pass a Speech check resulting in Lug-Nut backing off.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment

chr_000388e1.summary: Ronald Laren is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 9, 110 HP). Affiliated with Girdershade Residents. Found primarily around Ronald Laren's Home. Directly connected to quests: The Nuka-Cola Challenge.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
After his wife died, he wandered the wasteland before settling in Girdershade. Living close to Sierra Petrovita has increased his negative feelings regarding his loneliness, as he misses the physical intimacy he once shared with his wife. As a result, he has made several advances at Sierra, but she is oblivious to his motivations due to her pursuit of Nuka-Cola. Ronald is angered by her rejection, and although he does not want to physically force himself on her, he still wishes to spite her in other ways.

According to Sierra, Ronald is a skilled fighter. She recalls one occasion where he killed two raiders at Girdershade and punched their leader, Lug-Nut, in the face.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Nuka-Cola Challenge: Should one accept Sierra's mission to obtain Nuka-Cola Quantum for her, Ronald will attempt to convince the Lone Wanderer to give all the Quantums to him.
• Grady's Package: Ronald is the recipient of Grady's package, which is the naughty nightwear found in Marigold station. Depending on one's Speech and/or Barter skills, they can get him to pay up to 300 caps for it.

Effects of player's actions:
• A female player character with the Black Widow perk can convince him to retrieve the Nuka-Cola Quantums for her, with the promise of a threesome with her and Sierra. Excited, Ronald will run off to the distant Nuka-Cola plant and die. If the Lone Wanderer then asks Sierra if he's been bothering her, she'll say she hasn't seen him in a while, but she's sure he'll come back.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Ronald Laren's Home. Notable equipment & inventory: Leather Armor, The Kneecapper.

chr_000388df.summary:
Sierra Petrovita is a Nuka-Cola fanatic and collector residing in the small settlement of Girdershade in the Capital Wasteland with her neighbor and protector Ronald Laren in 2277.

By 2287, the older Sierra has taken a trip to the Nuka-World amusement park near the Commonwealth, looking to complete an ancient scavenger hunt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
One of only two residents of the overpass-hidden settlement named Girdershade, Sierra Petrovita is known for her hyperfixation on Nuka-Cola Corporation products, which began when her lips first touched a bottle of Nuka-Cola. She has dedicated much of her life since in pursuit of knowledge related to Nuka-Cola, reading what she could and collecting many flavors of Nuka-Cola products, whether it be the popular soft drinks they produced, the branded vending machines they were dispensed in, or the promotional merchandise created to advertise the drinks.

Orphaned at some point in her youth, Sierra settled underneath the wrecked overpass that came to be known as Girdershade at the age of 16, becoming the de-facto founder of the small settlement.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: In Fallout 3, Sierra stays in her house, drinking Nuka-Cola. In the Fallout 4 add-on Nuka-World, she can be found near Bradberton's office in Nuka-Town USA.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Cappy in a Haystack: Sierra asks the Sole Survivor to find 10 hidden Cappy images in the park.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ymir and his son Jotun work as slavers for Eulogy Jones in Paradise Falls. He is described as a jovial madman armed with a super sledge who loves drinking and fighting.

Ymir does not like the slave bartender Frank and will make this clear by murdering him upon the Lone Wanderer's entry into Paradise Falls, alleging that Frank intentionally watered down his vodka in an attempt to make more money off him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• When the Lone Wanderer has gained access to Paradise Falls without fighting their way in, Ymir can be found when entering the "food section" inside Paradise Falls. The first time going there, he will probably be seen arguing with the bartender, which results in the bartender getting himself killed. Talking to Ymir while he is in the argument can result in Ymir just walking away after finishing the conversation. This keeps the bartender alive. There are no assets or drawbacks to either option. If the Lone Wanderer asks Ymir for his reasoning, he claims the bartender had been watering down drinks so as to encourage patrons to pay for more.
• Killing Ymir will immediately turn all slavers in Paradise Falls hostile.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jotun takes on the task of keeping his father Ymir safe, which he describes simply as a "big job." He has difficulty forming basic sentences and speaks very infrequently, being described alongside his father as "Paradise Falls's pair of knuckleheads."

He seems to be very awkward and unsocial, responding vaguely and briefly to the Lone Wanderer and only responds to fellow slavers with grunts. His father has always been very proud of him and constantly praises him, bragging to the other slavers about him, which Jotun seems to find quite embarrassing.

chr_000384d4.summary: Carolina Red is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Slaver Barracks.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Carolina Red grew up experiencing regular abuse and torture by her father. However, by her adulthood, the psychopathic Carolina has come to consider these fond childhood memories; one of her favorites to recount is an incident where her father cut off a man's legs purely for personal enjoyment, laughing as the victim tried to crawl away before crushing his skull with a rock.

In 2277, she operates as a slaver under Eulogy Jones in the Capital Wasteland and is considered one of the least pleasant individuals found at Paradise Falls, even by the other slavers. and happily laughs along in the face of violence within their stronghold. Despite this, she seemingly has a small crush on Jotun, to the point that she can carry a friendly conversation with him, as well as his father Ymir exclusively on that topic.

chr_00036f86.summary: Tinker Joe is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 85 HP). Affiliated with Caravan Merchants. Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Companion Recruitment: Sergeant RL-3.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Tinker Joe is a traveling merchant who wanders the wastes with robotic companions, including an old Mister Gutsy army unit named Sergeant RL-3. He sells miscellaneous items, ranging from junk to equipment and weaponry. He considers his specialty to be the sale of robots and their parts, alongside servicing them. In addition to his trade with wastelanders, he has sold to towns such as Megaton, supplying them with Deputies Steel and Weld, a purchase which Sheriff Simms takes pride in.

He is keen to sell Sergeant RL-3, to a point where he may sell him at a discount of 500 caps to the Lone Wanderer as he is tired of waking up to the Mister Gutsy playing "revelry" at him.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Tinker Joe moves between the following locations:
• Northwest of the RobCo facility.
• The parking area south of the RobCo facility (around 8 a.m.).
• The crossroad east of Tenpenny Tower, south of the RobCo facility.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

Joe sells Sergeant RL-3, a robot companion, for the price of 1,000 bottle caps (500 with a Barter skill of 70) if the player character has neutral Karma. If he is dead, Sergeant RL-3 will no longer be available for recruitment as a companion.

chr_00036c1c.summary: Tanya Christoff, currently known as the AntAgonizer, is a supervillain residing in an underground lair near the town of Canterbury Commons. She has been terrorizing the town with a horde of giant ants and has recently begun to fight the Mechanist and his robots.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Tanya is the daughter of caravan drivers who perished in a giant ant attack that both spared her and left her orphaned. In an attempt to come to terms with her grief and rationalize why the ants had done this, Tanya turned to Hubris Comics, specifically Grognak the Barbarian, where she attached herself to the villain AntAgonizer. She found solace in their similarities; both were orphaned girls who would befriend and live among ants and would later develop a hatred for humankind.

In particular, she blamed Canterbury Commons, a trading hub which her parents helped make popular as a result of their trade route, that she now interpreted as a "blight" upon the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
The Superhuman Gambit: After witnessing the latest battle between the AntAgonizer and Mechanist, the Lone Wanderer is offered payment by Uncle Roe to put an end to the struggle between the "supers."

Effects of player's actions:
• Wrath of the AntAgonizer: If the Lone Wanderer sides with the AntAgonizer during "The Superhuman Gambit," there is a random encounter later on in which they find the AntAgonizer and a group of her ants attacking a group of wastelanders. The AntAgonizer is neutral towards the Lone Wanderer but will turn hostile if they attack her ants.
• The Lone Wanderer can convince her to stop harassing the town without passing the Speech challenge.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Born around 2237, Scott Wollinski grew up as the son of simple bean farmers. However, at 15 years old, Scott's father made a desperate choice, trading his son to a caravan merchant in exchange for more supplies of beans for their farm; this was not done out of malice but pragmatism and true love, as Scott's father believed that the traders would give young Scott a better life. The peculiar nature of the trade, a young man's being for mere beans, stuck with Scott and led to his steady nickname of "Bean." From there, Wollinski plied his time working as an indentured servant for the caravans for some years. Eventually, he accrued enough caps to buy his own freedom from the caravan he served in, finally giving him the chance to decide his own future.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Superhuman Gambit: After witnessing the latest battle between the AntAgonizer and Mechanist, the Lone Wanderer is offered payment by Uncle Roe to put an end to the struggle between the "supers."

Effects of player's actions:
• He will attack the Lone Wanderer if he finds out that they work for the AntAgonizer (or if he suspects that they are working for her). Wearing the AntAgonizer's costume or not giving him the AntAgonizer's costume will also cause him to attack, the latter option as a dialogue outcome.
• If one convinces him they are not a secret agent of the AntAgonizer, they can work with him. Alternately, he can be convinced to give up his life as the Mechanist; the default option is a Speech check.

sections.text: * Only if convinced to stop being a superhero.

chr_00034202.summary: Christine Kendall is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Future Imperfect.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Christine and her younger sister Monica are the daughters of John and Mary Kendall. During her adolescence, Christine became introverted due to living under a household with a strict Vault 101 security officer for a father. She was often the subject of verbal harangues from her father, even when she tried to appease him. This led her to become rather unhappy with life underground and more curious about the outside world. During her childhood, she was given the pejorative nickname "Mean Christine" by her peers, presumably for arrogant behavior on her part.

On August 3, 2274, Christine takes the G.O.A.T. exam, during which she displays an aversion to the Lone Wanderer, unsure of why they are speaking to her before class, as an extension of her teenage belief in superiority over them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Christine appears in Mr. Brotch's class as one of the students taking the G.O.A.T. exam alongside the Lone Wanderer.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Christine has sided with Amata's "rebels" during the crisis in Vault 101.
