chr_00032f74.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0003210b.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_00031eca.summary: Joe Porter is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 65 HP). Affiliated with Canterbury Commons Residents. Found primarily around Ernest "Uncle" Roe's House. Directly connected to quests: The Superhuman Gambit.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Joe Porter, or "Porter Joe" as the name he prefers to go by, was once a loader-for-hire at a caravan. However, when he first arrived at Canterbury Commons, the idea of having a permanent base of operations and a steady community was very appealing to him. He settled down there with his dog, Ol' Mule, in about 2271 and has been working as an unloader, a basic cook, and a basic repairman since then. Since the death of his dog, he has been minding the town diner, the center of chatter in this settlement.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Superhuman Gambit: Porter can reveal the AntAgonizer's real name, which is used to peacefully convince the AntAgonizer to give up her ways and cease attacking the town.

Other interactions:
• The player character can obtain a bottle of dirty water when talking to him for the first time.
• If the Point Lookout add-on is installed, he may have punga fruit available for sale.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Ernest "Uncle" Roe's House. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit. Provides services: Alcohol, Food, Supplies / Barter.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Raised as part of trade caravan, by the time Ernest was twelve he possessed the ability to turn five caps into fifty with a series of trades. At the age of twenty he set out with his sister Daisy Roe and used the money acquired through his mercantile skills to finance the creation of the trading post of Canterbury Commons which caravans of the Capital Wasteland are known to stop at regularly.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

• Merchant Empire - Talking to Roe about the caravans will start this quest.

chr_00031ec8.summary: Machete is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 50 HP). Affiliated with Canterbury Commons Residents. Found primarily around Ernest "Uncle" Roe's House. Directly connected to quests: The Superhuman Gambit.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
She used to fiercely defend Little Lamplight. At the age of 7, she slaughtered a mole rat in the caves with a machete, thus earning her nickname. She has been a bona fide celebrity ever since.

At the age of 16, she was supposed to head to Big Town, but she became lost due to a dust storm and arrived at Canterbury Commons instead. Because of her pride, she refuses to admit she went to the wrong place. Dominic D'Ellsadro felt she had the potential to work as a guard, and after a year of his guidance, she has earned some respect among the residents. She works alongside Dominic as his junior law enforcer. They both keep Canterbury Commons safe from raiders, unwanted creatures, and danger in general.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Machete patrols Canterbury Commons from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., eats until 1:00 p.m., patrols until 6:00 p.m., eats until 7:00 p.m., then patrols again until 2:00 a.m., after which she goes to bed and wakes up at 8:00 a.m.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Ernest "Uncle" Roe's House. Notable equipment & inventory: Dominic's House Key.

chr_00031ec7.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, sleep, eat
chr_00031ec7.summary: Derek Pacion is a young boy and resident of Canterbury Commons in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
By 2277, the 15-year-old Derek has lived in Canterbury Commons all his life. He was originally raised by his parents, Louis Pacion and Daisy Roe, a pair of traders who met and settled down. When they were killed in separate raider attacks (Daisy six years ago and Louis three years ago), Derek was left to the care of his "Uncle Roe," the town mayor.

Since then, Derek has become introverted and reserved as he works around the trade town as a general assistant, but does not really say much unless it is necessary. He harbors a secret crush on Machete but has never worked up the courage to approach her. He devotes much of his free time to reading intact pre-War Hubris Comics material and drawing posters of the town's local "hero," the Mechanist who "protects" Canterbury Commons from the ant armies of the AntAgonizer.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
After the deaths of both his parents prior to 2277, Derek is looked after by his foster uncle, Canterbury mayor Ernest Roe. Derek often travels to the Republic of Dave to see his friend Ralph, Dave's son.

Derek also knew Scott Wollinski before he became the Mechanist. An optional conversation topic reveals that Derek convinced Scott to become a superhero and fight the AntAgonizer after she destroyed a robot, escalating the conflict between the two in Canterbury Commons to dangerous levels.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Superhuman Gambit: Asking him about the Mechanist and AntAgonizer reveals that Joe Porter knows the AntAgonizer's real name. This information can be used in a Speech check to get the AntAgonizer to peacefully surrender. If the player character finishes the quest, he will complain about how boring it is in Canterbury Commons. If all of Canterbury Commons characters are murdered, the reward for the quest is given by Derek who, like all children in Fallout 3, cannot die.

chr_00031ec6.summary: Dominic D'Ellsadro is a hispanic elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 70 HP). Affiliated with Canterbury Commons Residents. Found primarily around Ernest "Uncle" Roe's House. Directly connected to quests: The Superhuman Gambit.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: He used to lead a small group of mercenaries, although he would encounter a lot of near-death experiences. He retired from it with some scavenged supplies to give him a little wealth. He has been in the town for about a decade, and his leadership qualities has earned him respect. Dominic treats the teenage young woman Machete like both a daughter and soldier, and he is teaching her how to be efficient security.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: During the day, he can be found patrolling the streets of Canterbury Commons or eating at the town diner. At night, he sleeps at Dominic and Machete's house which is at the end of the main street.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Superhuman Gambit: The Lone Wanderer can talk to Dominic about the duo bothering the inhabitants of the town.

chr_00031e28.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, eat, find, travel
chr_00031e28.summary: Ben Canning is a water beggar found at random locations in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Unlike other water beggars in the Capital Wasteland, Ben does not sit outside of a settlement. Rather, he is a friendly wasteland traveler who has ventured out sorely unprepared, leaving him dehydrated after running out of water. He does not expect help from other wasteland travelers, and if someone were to donate him some water, he would be pleasantly surprised.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
Ben Canning appears in a random encounter. Upon meeting, the Lone Wanderer may choose to give him water or let him die. Unlike the water beggars found outside Megaton, Tenpenny Tower, and Rivet City who will only accept purified water, Ben will also accept dirty water. However, he will not accept Aqua Pura, Aqua Cura, or holy water.

If one has both purified and dirty water in their inventory, the game will prioritize the latter over the former. If given water, he proceeds to drink it repeatedly; when activated, he apologetically tells the character that he's not up to traveling yet. Standing after a minute or two, he simply says "Good to see you again, friend!" If one refuses to give him water, he will ask them to shoot him in the head, because he is out of ammunition, or else he would do it himself.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Roving Trader Outfit, itm_00074334.

chr_0003197a.summary: Fred Wilks is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Wilks' House. Directly connected to quests: Those!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Father to Bryan Wilks, he died defending his home from the fire ants that invaded Grayditch. He was a provider and protector for his family, and instilled a strong sense of purpose and respect for family in his son.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Those!: Bryan Wilks asks the Lone Wanderer to help find his father.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wilks' House. Notable equipment & inventory: Shack Key, Wasteland Wanderer Outfit.

chr_00031648.summary: Stanley is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sweet, always worried and not very bright, Stanley is the father of Beatrice, Mary and Gloria. Stanley and Andy are responsible for keeping the vault running, tending to all the machinery and acting as its janitors.

2260s:
On July 12, 2268, Stanley repairs the water purifier. This repair is a point of discussion between himself and Amata Almodovar when they engage in small talk the next day.

On that same day, Stanley performs routine maintenance on the pipes in the corridor outside the cafeteria. Midway through his work, he attends the birthday party of the Lone Wanderer. Though the Overseer presents the Pip-Boy 3000A to the Lone Wanderer, it is Stanley who selects the model. Though he admits that some might find the 3000A basic, Stanley believes the series is very reliable.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Stanley is the father of Beatrice Armstrong, Gloria, and Mary. Stanley's constant companion is Andy, a Mister Handy robot, that aids his human friend in cleaning and maintaining the vault. Stanley is friendly with the vault physician James and his child. In fact, during Escape!, he allows the Lone Wanderer to get past him without denouncing them to the vault's security, out of appreciation. However, he still says "Good riddance, get out" when the Lone Wanderer is exiled out of the vault after Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: He asks the Lone Wanderer about what they think about their new Pip-Boy 3000 which he fixed, and also gives a child's baseball cap.
• Future Imperfect: Stanley can be interacted with while he suffers from an illness.
• Trouble on the Homefront: He holds the password to the terminal used to sabotage Vault 101. It can either be pickpocketed from him, or it can be looted from him if he is to be killed.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer chooses to sabotage the Vault during Trouble on the Homefront, he may be killed by the explosion.

Other interactions:
• During the Lone Wanderer's escape at age 19, Stanley is encountered struggling against radroaches outside of the infirmary, but he is most likely saved by the arrival of Officer Gomez and Andy.

chr_00030d82.summary: Carter is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Rescue from Paradise.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Desperate to reclaim his freedom and with his mental state deteriorating, Carter is in the middle of an unlikely escape attempt from Paradise Falls just as the Lone Wanderer arrives there. He yells for his fellow captive Sammy to run with him and claims that they can make it out, but Sammy doesn't follow him. Though the slaver Forty screams for Carter to stop, he continues to run.

Despite his certainty that Forty lacks the means to detonate his slave collar, Carter is nonetheless killed instantly when the collar detonates during his escape. Forty remarks that Carter should've known better than to run away while still wearing a collar, and tells Sammy to return inside, criticizing their attempt at escape.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
When the Lone Wanderer is first allowed entry into Paradise Falls and approaches the entrance, Carter will come running towards them. Moments later, his collar explodes, killing him.

chr_000309b0.summary: Stevie Mack is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 60 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is Susie and Wally Mack's brother, and Allen Mack and Gloria Mack's son. Stevie is 25 years old as of the events of Escape! He is a sadistic and gung-ho member of the Vault's security force, and willing to do anything to gain favor with his boss, including being particularly overzealous during emergencies.

He is responsible for the killing of Jonas Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• He will only drop a finger during Escape!

Quests:
• Escape!: Officer Mack is found in the security office interrogating Amata. If the Lone Wanderer took the overseer's gun from Amata, they have no choice but to fight Mack, due to the fact that he attacks them on sight. If one insisted Amata keeps her father's gun to protect herself, she will shoot Mack in self-defense, killing him. If you interrupt before Amata fires on him, she will escape and the player character will again be responsible for killing Mack.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If not killed in Escape!, Mack is found in the vault upon returning. He is not hostile.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • He will only wear the helmet during Trouble on the Homefront.

chr_000309ae.summary: Officer Gomez is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
An archetypal "good cop," Herman Gomez has more of a conscience than many of his fellow Vault 101 security officers. He is the husband of Pepper Gomez and the father of Freddie Gomez, whom he attempts to keep away from the Tunnel Snakes' influence. However, he knows that this is difficult because there are few other children Freddie's age in the Vault. More generally, Gomez is interested in youth outreach and preventing bullying in the Vault. He believes that responsibility lies with a parent to raise a child right, though if all else fails, the influence of Vault security can also have an impact.

As a friend of James, the Vault physician, Officer Gomez extends faith that he must have had his reasons for leaving the Vault in 2277, even if this view is not shared by most of his peers.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only drops a finger during Growing Up Fast and Escape!.

Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: If a scuffle occurs between the Lone Wanderer and Butch DeLoria over the sweetroll, Officer Gomez will intervene.
• Escape!: Gomez will be helping Stanley and Andy fight radroaches. Provided he is not attacked, he warns the Lone Wanderer that security is on the lookout for them. Gomez believes that James is innocent and suggests leaving the vault to search for him.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If he lives, Gomez will be the first vault resident the Lone Wanderer runs into. Staying civilized with him will have him escort the Lone Wanderer to either Amata or the current overseer. If Allen Mack attacks while any guards are around, the guards will immediately come to his side to protect him. This includes Officer Gomez.

chr_000309ac.summary: Beatrice Armstrong (simply Beatrice in the game) is a resident of Vault 101 and a minor character. She is encountered during Growing Up Fast and later found dead during Trouble on the Homefront, in James' former office in the clinic.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An eccentric, airheaded dweller of Vault 101, Beatrice is one of the daughters of Stanley Armstrong, and the only one among them not to have a husband (although she is interested in Edwin Brotch, the Vault's resident teacher). Unlike her sisters, Mary Kendall and Gloria Mack, she has ample free time away from her family, which she spends snooping into the lives of other residents and gossiping to her sisters and her best friend, Pepper Gomez. She also dabbles in tarot readings and poetry as hobbies, often writing commemorative poems for special events such as Founder's Day and resident birthdays. Despite her friendly demeanor, many of her neighbors find her attitude insufferable and condescending, particularly the Vault's children.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Beatrice is one of the guests at the Lone Wanderer's birthday party. She will give the Lone Wanderer a poem for their tenth birthday party.
• If the player does not interact with Beatrice, she will continue to follow the Lone Wanderer throughout the Vault, even onto the reactor level.

Other interactions:
• Beatrice is found dead during Trouble on the Homefront. Despite complaining of a sprained toe, Andy amputated her right leg (incorrectly stating that he took off the left one).

sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_000309a7.summary: Old Lady Palmer is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jonas' grandmother lives alone in her apartment where nothing has changed for decades. She is kind and proud of her grandson, and she bakes the most delicious sticky sweetrolls.

During the escape from Vault 101, one can find a file on the overseer's computer which states that Anne Palmer, her daughter, was the team leader of a scouting party that left the vault to explore the outside world in February 2241.

Palmer is old enough to have retired from work duty in the vault, and therefore no longer has a Pip-Boy.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: On July 13, 2268, Old Lady Palmer celebrates the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party. She gives them a sweetroll as a birthday present.
• Trouble on the Homefront: She will be holed up in the classroom with Amata's rebel faction. She explains that during the player's escape from the vault, her grandson Jonas died in suspicious circumstances, which she attributes to the overseer.

chr_000307c8.summary: Dr. Weston Lesko is a scientist living in Grayditch, found inside Marigold station in 2277. He is indirectly responsible for causing the destruction of Grayditch.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The brilliant but aloof Doctor Lesko is determined to achieve one goal: save the wasteland from the mutated wildlife (specifically, giant ants) ravaging it. He seeks to revert the giant ants back to their original pre-War size by genetically manipulating their egg broods, and thus prove to the people of the wastes that they are merely misunderstood creatures. He understands the risks and the "rhetoric" of tampering with nature, but he is convinced that his cause is just and his results will speak for themselves.

Dr. Lesko's experiments did not kick off until after his arrival in Grayditch in November 2276, when he moved into a laboratory shack built with the help of Fred and Bryan Wilks.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Those!: Doctor Lesko requires the Lone Wanderer's help to regain control of his experiment. If the player has a high enough Science skill and Intelligence, an additional dialogue option appears when asking Lesko about his experiments. When the Science option is chosen (60 Science needed), Lesko reveals that he has been using FEV in his experiments. An additional dialogue option will also appear if the player has chosen the perk Entomologist, which upsets the doctor slightly.
• If this quest is completed and Lesko stays alive, he will move back to his shack in Grayditch.
• Nectar Collecting for Fun and Profit: After completion of "Those!", Lesko will pay for samples of fire ant nectar.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Marigold Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Reading Glasses, 10mm Pistol, 10mm Round, itm_000340d7.

chr_000307c7.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: disgusted. AI packages: sandbox, travel, eat, sleep, follow
chr_000307c7.summary: Bryan Wilks is an eight-year-old survivor of Grayditch. Talking to him automatically begins the quest Those!

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only son of Fred Wilks, Bryan came to Grayditch with his dad in 2276. The town was a stopover in their travels further, but the bricked houses and a small community provided welcome respite and delayed their plans to move on, away from the dangerous ruins of Washington, D.C. During their stay, his father made supply runs for the entire settlement, becoming an important part of the small community while trying to raise an eight-year-old son on his own, as Bryan's mother passed away when he was younger.

Though young, Bryan was raised to survive in the wasteland and Fred trusted his son with a supply key for emergencies, trusting his judgement. He instructed his son to stay away from dangerous parts of Grayditch, such as Marigold station and the old Pulowski Preservation shelter near the old diner.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Those!: Bryan automatically approaches the player when they near Grayditch, asking for help finding his father and figuring out what happened to him. Afterwards, he takes shelter in a closed Pulowski Preservation shelter next to the diner near his home, waiting for the player to find his dad and then Doctor Lesko.
• During the initial meeting, the player can use Child at Heart or pass a Speech challenge to obtain a key to Bryan's father's emergency supplies (he will otherwise lie about them). The dumpster has a Very Hard lock on the dumpster, and can spawn a sidearm (.32 pistol, Chinese pistol, 10mm pistol, laser pistol, or scoped.44 Magnum), and several frag grenades and/or pulse grenades.
• Once the quest concludes, Bryan stays alone in Grayditch.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC15a (Grayditch — Anchorage Memorial). Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000340f8.

chr_00030104.summary: Mad Johnny Wes is a heavily armed, hostile wastelander and the only human occupant of Hubris Comics.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Johnny was trapped inside Hubris Comics due to the nearby presence of a super mutant group in the Mason District. He was almost killed by an onslaught of feral ghouls inside the building but has managed to defend himself by utilizing a minigun as well as automated turrets and improvised traps, coordinating the effort from a fortified foreman's office that he has nicknamed "the Alamo." However, the difficult situation has put a strain on Johnny and caused him to lose his mind, turning him hostile towards any wastelanders who approach his position.

chr_000300f0.summary: The unnamed Vault 101 overseer before Alphonse Almodovar was in charge of Vault 101 up until the 2250s.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Vault 101 overseer before Almodovar was a proponent of outside contact, well respected among many for their leadership and transparency. Under their tenure, the Vault opened in early 2241, with the first survey team, led by Anne Palmer, reporting that the outside was not an uninhabitable hellscape, but merely a dangerous, irradiated wasteland. The Vault began trade relations, establishing ambassadors at Megaton, and dwellers were permitted to travel freely between the Vault and the outside world. The Vault's large population at the time was sustained by this policy.

However, this policy did not sit well with a young Alphonse Almodovar. Inheriting his parents' belief that the Vault should remain sealed away from the outside world, Almodovar waited for a chance to correct the lapses in security.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: CG02Overseer), The Overseer is defined as a Hispanic Elderly in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Marked as essential (cannot be killed during normal gameplay until plot flags allow). Appears in or relates to quests: Growing Up Fast. Linked story events: Vault 101 Escape.

chr_000300ec.summary: Wally Mack is a resident of Vault 101 in 2277 and is a member of a greaser gang called the Tunnel Snakes.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wally is the son of Allen and Gloria Mack. Wally's siblings are Stevie and Susie.

Wally is the brains of the Tunnel Snakes. Butch DeLoria and Paul Hannon Jr. are Wally's friends and fellow gang members. During their formative years, the Tunnel Snakes harassed other students in Vault 101, even being bold enough to taunt the overseer's daughter, Amata Almodovar. Butch presumes to be the leader of the Tunnel Snakes, but Wally might disagree if challenged.

He does not talk as much as the others, but they listen to what he has to say when he does say something. He is one of the Lone Wanderer's peers in Vault 101 and is encountered throughout the Lone Wanderer's youth inside Vault 101.

By 2287, Mack had traveled to the Commonwealth, where he reestablished the Tunnel Snakes under his rule.

sections.text:
Quests:
• Tunnel Snakes Rule!: Wally Mack (as a glowing one) must be eliminated in Fens Way station.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is the only child of Paul Hannon Sr. and Vikki Hannon. Butch DeLoria, Freddie Gomez, and Wally Mack are his friends and fellow gang members.

The other Tunnel Snakes sometimes tease him because of his father being the chief of security in Vault 101, but this also gives him a certain cachet among his friends, though.

In a conversation with the Lone Wanderer, Paul expresses his disappointment that he did not have a Pip-Boy 3000 yet. and they will start teasing him about "having a crush" on you (if the player character is a female), or about him being your "friend" (if the player character is male), which will then cause him to call you a "dorkface" so he could keep up his appeal with the other boys.

chr_000300ea.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: angry. AI packages: dialogue, travel
chr_000300ea.summary: Butch DeLoria is a resident of Vault 101 and the leader and co-founder of the Tunnel Snakes gang in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born and raised in Vault 101 all his life and being under the care of his mother Ellen, a notorious alcoholic who neglected to oversee her son's negative maturing, Butch has been forced to put on a mask as a boorish, overbearing bully to cover up his deep-seated feelings of inadequacy due to not knowing his father despite living in a Vault with a close-knit community.

On July 13, 2268, when he was ten years old, During the party, Butch held a small meeting with his only two friends, Wally Mack and Paul Hannon Jr., to toss around ideas for a name for their gang, which later would be decided to be the "Tunnel Snakes" while rejecting other names such as "Vault Dwellers." He also attempted to strongarm the Wanderer into giving up the sweetroll they got from Lucy Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Butch becomes non-essential during Escape! and he can optionally be killed before leaving Vault 101, preventing him from appearing during Trouble on the Homefront and becoming a companion later.
• If Trouble on the Homefront was completed by either opening or destroying Vault 101, and Butch was left alive, he can be found residing in the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. He can be recruited as a companion only while the player character has Neutral Karma.

Companion:
• Butch can give the Lone Wanderer a haircut during Trouble on the Homefront, and if recruited as a companion, also at any time during their travels.
• If separated from the player character, Butch will return to the Muddy Rudder.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Items will be replaced by a non-player switchblade and 10mm pistol, if no replacement weapons are left in Butch's inventory while he is a companion.

chr_000300e9.summary: Amata Almodovar is a resident of Vault 101, the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar, and a major character. Along with Owyn Lyons and Sarah Lyons, she is one of only three characters in the game to have "Very Good" Karma.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only daughter of the overseer, Amata is around the Lone Wanderer's age and the two grew up together ever since James arrived in the Vault with his child in tow. They bonded over many things, from Grognak the Barbarian to being raised by single fathers after their mothers passed away at a young age: Amata lost her mother at two, leaving her father, the overseer, to raise her on his own. The burden of leading the Vault and enforcing his isolationist policy slowly drove Amata and Alphonse apart, despite her deep love for her father and an innate sense of loyalty.

The bond between Amata and the Lone Wanderer developed into a deep friendship over the years, with the two becoming inseparable, best friends. Another was that he simply didn't like the Lone Wanderer, in part due to their father's stubborn, insubordinate personality.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Amata organizes the Lone Wanderer's birthday party on July 13, 2268, gifting them an intact copy of the 14th issue of Grognak the Barbarian, and demonstrating some of the reactivity of the game.
• Future Imperfect: Amata takes the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, together with the Lone Wanderer. Before entering the class room, she is harassed by the Tunnel Snakes, allowing the player to experiment with various approaches to resolving quests and introducing them to the Karma system.
• Escape!: Amata awakens the Lone Wanderer with news of James' escape from the vault. She offers a gun and outlines a plan for the Lone Wanderer's own escape. Toward the end of the quest, it turns out that she was captured and is interrogated by her father and Officer Mack.

sections.text: • Only if she was told to keep the pistol during "Escape!"

chr_000300e7.summary: Jonas is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 120 HP). Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Good-humored, smart, and kind, Jonas has been James' assistant as well as his and the Lone Wanderer's friend for as long as the Lone Wanderer can remember. He can appear stern and strict if he wants to, but even there, his sense of humor asserts itself.

In the late 2260s, Jonas was appointed to be James' assistant by the overseer, who hoped he would be a voice of reason. Jonas and James forged a friendship very quickly and together, they worked at examining and treating patients, as well as conducting routine experiments, testing the health of the vault. For an unknown length of time, James deliberately kept his assistant in the dark about covert experiments aimed at reviving Project Purity.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Jonas is first encountered during the Lone Wanderer's 10th birthday when James takes the Lone Wanderer down to the generator room to give them a present (a BB gun). Jonas later takes a picture of the two.
• Future Imperfect: Jonas is encountered upon opening the office door, telling the Lone Wanderer good morning and good luck on the G.O.A.T.
• Escape!: The Note from dad holotape can be taken from Jonas' body, containing a message pertaining to James' escape.

sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Eyeglasses, itm_000236d8, itm_0001cbdc.

chr_000300a3.summary: Meat is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Meat is one of two glowing one test subjects Doctor Barrows keeps at the ghoul clinic, the other being Ethyl. They are former residents of Underworld, who were exposed to intense amounts of radiation. It caused them to turn feral, then into glowing ones, making them excellent subjects of Barrows' research, who wants to understand the ghoul condition on a scientific level. He works with them whenever he is not tending to sick and injured ghouls of the community.

chr_0002fdcf.summary: James, also known as Dad, is the father of the Lone Wanderer and Vault 101's physician.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Project Purity:
James was always an inquisitive, meticulous and determined man; this personality led him to form or join a group of like-minded scientists, who were set on changing the wasteland for the better. Before the Lone Wanderer was born, James led an ambitious scientific endeavor known as Project Purity. He and his group of scientists, including wife Catherine and Dr. Madison Li, aimed to build an advanced water purifier within the ruins of the Jefferson Memorial, which would serve to purify the water of the Potomac. The project began to lose momentum, lacking concrete results while having to compensate for lost time due to super mutant attacks. The number of mutants was steadily increasing, and protecting the project was becoming increasingly difficult for the Brotherhood.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Related quests:
• Baby Steps: James puts the one-year-old Lone Wanderer in a playpen in their room which contains the You're S.P.E.C.I.A.L.! book. After a brief absence, James returns and shows the child their mother's favorite Bible quotation, and takes his child to see Amata.
• Growing Up Fast: James has a small conversation with the Lone Wanderer at the beginning of their tenth birthday party, and later in the party gives them a BB gun as a birthday gift, and tasks them with killing a radroach.
• Future Imperfect: James has a brief conversation with his now 16-year-old before their G.O.A.T. exam.
• Escape!: James' unexpected absence from Vault 101 prompts a security crisis and propels the Lone Wanderer out into the wastes.
• Following in His Footsteps: The Lone Wanderer searches for their dad.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
1 Only while in Vault 101.
2 On his way back to Rivet City.

chr_0002dc08.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_0002db1a.summary: Paladins are a rank of the Brotherhood of Steel, reserved for the organization's elite members who have proven themselves as seasoned warriors and battlefield commanders.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Paladins are the protectors of the Brotherhood, considered to be their elite fighting force. Achieving the rank of paladin typically means the bearer is a highly trained combat veteran with extensive battlefield experience, marking them as a capable leader that completes the missions given to them and their subordinates dutifully. Due to the great responsibility that comes with their rank, paladins are often afforded the best equipment at the Brotherhood's disposal, such as power armor and advanced weaponry. They are trusted with maintaining the security of the Brotherhood's operations in their territory, being the first line of defense against enemies both inside and outside the organization.

sections.title: Ranks
sections.text:
Head paladin:
The head paladin is the overall commander of the paladins, responsible for implementing the elder's combat plans, enforcing Brotherhood laws and discipline on top of overseeing the overall training regime. They are a veteran soldier and are required to periodically convene with other caste heads and the elders.

Notable members:
• John Maxson, Lost Hills (promoted to elder by 2161)
• Head Paladin Rhombus, Lost Hills, 2161
• Head Paladin Lindquist (succeeded Kenneth Jones as elder)
• Head Paladin Edgar Hardin, Mojave, 2281

Star paladin:
Star paladins are only answerable to their elder and are given a wide authority to do what they see fit to accomplish their objectives.

The Midwest chapter renamed the position to paladin lord, but kept it identical in practice (being one step below the general/elder).

chr_0002d3c0.summary: Moira Brown is the proprietor of the general store Craterside Supply in Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. She is an independent researcher studying post-nuclear survival methods for a guidebook to help others in the wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Past:
Moira is from the trading community of Canterbury Commons, where she grew up with an "uncommon curiosity about the world." and among the locals for her tinkering skills. Other residents of Megaton are generally annoyed with her eccentric behavior and "research," but cannot help but respect her effectiveness as a saleswoman.

Sometime between 2265 to 2267, a woman from Vault 101 came to Megaton and visited her shop; Moira took pity on the young woman's ignorance of wasteland life and offered to make some defensive modifications to her Vault jumpsuit. Though she eventually completed the armored jumpsuit, the client never returned for it, leading Moira to conclude she had died.

In her daily life, Moira takes every opportunity to learn as much as she can, largely by reading almost every book that comes through the town.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text:
Living most of her life in the relative safety of Megaton has left Moira oblivious as to how the wasteland functions. That said, she is a renowned optimist and always displays a chipper personality. Her drive to try to improve the lives of her fellow wastelanders inspired her to create the Wasteland Survival Guide. Though her research for the guide involves sending the Lone Wanderer into dangerous situations, Moira's naivete makes her fail to realize the full weight of her requests, which also leads to the ironic situation of keeping her new assistant away from the printing presses she uses, since she considers them to be more dangerous.

All that said, Moira is not completely detached from reality, as, in 2277, she recently hired a mercenary to serve as security for her shop.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: As the owner of Craterside Supply, she spends the day sweeping and trading as well as conducting odd experiments. She opens the store at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 8:00 p.m. Craterside Supply is also her home; Moira sleeps upstairs, and if the Lone Wanderer is caught trespassing after hours, she will become increasingly upset. The only time she will leave her shop is if Megaton is destroyed during The Power of the Atom. If Wasteland Survival Guide is completed before Megaton is destroyed, she will instead stay near the entrance to the ruins and only has the option to repair equipment, lacking an option to buy or sell items.

chr_0002d043.summary: The unnamed Vault 101 overseer before Alphonse Almodovar was in charge of Vault 101 up until the 2250s.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Vault 101 overseer before Almodovar was a proponent of outside contact, well respected among many for their leadership and transparency. Under their tenure, the Vault opened in early 2241, with the first survey team, led by Anne Palmer, reporting that the outside was not an uninhabitable hellscape, but merely a dangerous, irradiated wasteland. The Vault began trade relations, establishing ambassadors at Megaton, and dwellers were permitted to travel freely between the Vault and the outside world. The Vault's large population at the time was sustained by this policy.

However, this policy did not sit well with a young Alphonse Almodovar. Inheriting his parents' belief that the Vault should remain sealed away from the outside world, Almodovar waited for a chance to correct the lapses in security.

chr_0002c884.summary: Shawna is a citizen of the Republic of Dave in 2277. She also runs the Museum of Dave and is in charge of the schooling.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: At the age of 17, she is Dave's eldest daughter. She has been raised to be a fighter and knows how to survive if the need ever arises for her to leave the Republic. She is supportive of her father.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Election Day: Shawna is one of the citizens that Dave asks the Lone Wanderer to get to vote.

Other interactions:
Shawna, as curator for the Museum of Dave, handles the museum budget. By passing a Speech check, she can be convinced to buy any item for its base value to her. The budget of the museum is 700 caps. Items sold to her will not actually be displayed in the museum.

Effects of player's actions:
Shawna will be very distressed if anyone besides Dave wins the election, but she nonetheless remains in the Republic.

Museum Tour Speech:
So, I'll just get started on the tour of the museum then. To my far right is the baby carriage that our great leader slept in as a newborn baby. Unlike most babies, he never cried and his poop didn't stink. Dave had 8 siblings and made his own baseball team.

chr_0002bd23.summary: Arkansas is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 45 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Strictly Business.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The last remaining member of a tribe made up of military survivors who resided in the town of Ridgefield, Arkansas was a small boy when slavers from Paradise Falls came to the town and captured nearly everyone else.

Swearing revenge on the slavers, Arkansas began spreading rumors that the town had been repopulated in hopes of luring the slavers that took his tribe back, this time into a trap set by him. The trap succeeded, and when the slavers returned to the town, they found themselves under attack from Arkansas, who used a combination of sniper fire and landmines to defend the town, wiping out the slaver group. Following this encounter, slaving raids on the town ceased entirely, and Ridgefield from then on became known as Minefield.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Aside from targeting inanimate objects nearby, from his perch in a three-story building at the north end of town, Arkansas will fire upon the vehicles scattered about the area, causing them to explode, when the player character approaches.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Strictly Business: Grouse has a list of VIP targets marked for enslavement, Arkansas among them.
• The Wasteland Survival Guide: To prepare her survival guide, Moira Brown wants to study the design of a land mine and points the Lone Wanderer toward the aptly-named Minefield with the warning about "a ghost" living in the town that attacks anyone who goes there.

chr_0002b8ec.summary: Chinese commandos are simulated People's Liberation Army soldiers, a part of the Tranquility Lane simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The Iron Army PLA commandos were originally designed for a virtual reality combat exercise, designated Military Training Program 923-B: Chinese Invasion. The program simulated a Chinese attack on American soil, and the commandos were programmed accordingly. However, as the simulation was designed for military, not civilian hardware, and the version obtained by Braun from General Chase came with all the failsafes removed, the commandos were not so much part of an exercise, but an elaborate suicide tool to be used if Braun grew bored of the simulation and life.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tranquility Lane: Activating the training program is one of the ways to resolve the quest. Once the failsafe is activated, a squad of commandos spawns in Tranquility Lane and sweeps through the area, killing everyone in their path except for the Lone Wanderer, Betty and Doc.
• Commandos are marked as essential and cannot be killed. If knocked unconscious, they will get up in short order and continue the killing.

chr_0002b898.summary: Bob is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 50 HP). Affiliated with Republic of Dave. Found primarily around Republic of Dave Men's Quarters.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2258, Bob is young, hotheaded and bossy, and has been given the title of "Second-Commander of the Army of Dave." He is nineteen years old, thinks of himself as Vice Dave, insisting that he knows best and that all citizens of the republic should listen to him. From his speech, before him becoming an emperor, he appears to possess dictatorship tendencies.

Although Dave will not talk badly to Bob in public, it is widely known that he really lets Bob have it when the two are alone. Bob often butts heads with his father behind closed doors and is looking forward to establishing the Empire of Bob. Although Bob is Asian, both his father Dave and biological mother Rosie are Caucasian.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Bob can be found at the Republic of Dave grounds during the day. At night Bob sleeps in the men's quarters.

Bob will wander between the Republic of Dave buildings, approaching their outer walls and repairing them with a wrench in his hand. This results in no actual change. He can, on occasion, be found practicing at the shooting range.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Election Day: The Lone Wanderer can convince Bob to run for the presidential election.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Bob wins the presidential election, he becomes "President Bob." Other residents of the location will comment that after his victory, Bob has been "more of a jerk than usual."

chr_0002b896.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, patrol
chr_0002b896.summary: Jessica is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 45 HP). Affiliated with Republic of Dave. Found primarily around Republic of Dave Capitol Building.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: She is Dave's new younger wife and lives in the Republic of Dave. Her husband is a survivalist and has made sure his wife and older children know how to fight. Jessica is 24 and has never left the Republic; she fences but is extremely naive, conceited, and catty, especially when dealing with the first wife, Rosie.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Election Day: Jessica is one of the people who can be convinced to vote in the election. She cannot be convinced to run for president in the election.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Republic of Dave Capitol Building. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Veteran Outfit.

sections.title: History
sections.text:
In 2254, the Brotherhood's ruling council, based in the Lost Hills bunker in Southern California, decided to send a contingent to the East Coast, with one primary objective: recover any and all advanced technology from East Coast cities and bases. As secondary objectives, they were also told to seek out a previous expeditionary force near Chicago that had since gone rogue, as well as to investigate rumors of super mutant activity on the East Coast. However, technology retrieval remained their chief priority.

The contingent was placed under the command of Star Paladin Owyn Lyons, accompanied by technological adviser Scribe Reginald Rothchild, who was privately Owyn's friend, as well as several veteran members of the Brotherhood, including the paladins Henry Casdin, Ishmael Ashur and Tristan.

sections.title: Expedition to the Commonwealth
sections.text:
Starting in 2280, while still operating under the Lyons doctrine, the Capital Wasteland chapter of the Brotherhood would begin investigating the Commonwealth. The Brotherhood would send a total of three reconnaissance missions into the Boston region. In 2280, an unnamed recon squad volunteered to go into the Commonwealth. The first recon team was hugely successful, bringing back crates full of pre-War technology and historical documents and proving that further exploration would be fruitful.

The Capital Wasteland chapter, reinstated and now under the command of Elder Arthur Maxson dispatched a second team, Recon Squad Artemis to the Commonwealth in 2284. Artemis had problems beginning at their drop-off point in Malden, ambushed by a unknown party following just a few communications sent back to command.

sections.title: Divisions
sections.text:
• Lyons' Pride
• 2nd Monument Defense Detachment
• Water Distribution Network
• First Recon Team
• Recon Squad Gladius
• Recon Squad Artemis
• Alpha Squad

chr_0002ae21.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sleep, patrol, follow, find, eat
chr_0002ae21.summary: Cherry is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Dukov's Place Residents. Found primarily around Dukov's Place. Directly connected to quests: The Waters of Life, Trouble on the Homefront, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The 27-year-old Cherry lives in Dukov's riverside apartment close to the Anchorage Memorial on the east shore of the Potomac River. There, she and Fantasia act as his "playmates"; Dukov takes offense to calling them "whores," claiming their relationship is one of mutual care rather than simply him paying them for service. However, he does still give them caps, but in the form of small allowances. Their only jobs are to look sexy, pour drinks on command, and sleep with Dukov whenever he wants. While Cherry does not love Dukov, she initially liked his attention, his money, and the fact that he manages to keep both of them safe and well-fed, a rarity in the Capital Wasteland, even if it means having to spend long hours of the day wearing skimpy sleeping attire, sometimes outside in the cold on his terrace.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Cherry will steal Dukov's special key if the Lone Wanderer agrees to take her to Rivet City.
• Cherry's Freedom: If her offer is accepted, getting Cherry to Rivet City in exchange for the special key will gain Karma and Cherry will become a permanent resident of Rivet City.

Effects of player's actions:
• If she is escorted to Rivet City, after 73 in-game hours, Cherry will swap out of her sexy sleepwear for a wasteland settler outfit.
• Cherry may be found wandering the wasteland outside Rivet City after escorting her there. In this instance, it is highly likely she will be killed if she is not found dead in the first place.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
1 Requires completing her request to move to Rivet City.
2 Only after starting combat.

chr_0002ae20.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: find, follow, eat, sandbox, sleep
chr_0002ae20.summary: Fantasia is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Dukov's Place Residents. Found primarily around Dukov's Place. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Similar to Cherry, Fantasia stays with Dukov for his protection. She says "Dukey" is alright, can be a nice guy, is good in bed, and he gives her caps. Fantasia says she would rather be a "whore" than dead, and she and Cherry frequently party with him. Fantasia is also into Jet to some degree.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
If Dukov is killed and Cherry goes to Rivet City, Fantasia will remain in Dukov's place, wandering around and drinking. If one speaks to her, she may respond as if one had just told her of Dukov's death (even if the Lone Wanderer killed him in front of her earlier). She will explain briefly what used to go on there and why she is so scantily dressed, and express regret that Dukov is gone and the good times are over.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Dukov's Place. Notable equipment & inventory: Sexy Sleepwear.

chr_0002ae1e.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_0002ae1e.summary: Dukov is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 60 HP). Found primarily around Dukov's Place. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Dukov's life mainly consists of partying and having sex with women, a reflection of his carefree yet sleazy nature. Although he is profane, boisterous, and has an obnoxiously loud and distinctive laugh, Dukov is nevertheless charismatic. He is concerned only with his material possessions, his lavish home (or "pad" as he calls it), and women.

He is one of the three surviving mercenaries hired by Allistair Tenpenny for an expedition into Fort Constantine. He is now retired, and lives in his estate (Dukov's Place) along the east bank of the Potomac River in the D.C ruins.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He spends his time drinking lots of alcohol and taking Jet with Cherry and Fantasia. Though one will never see it, he talks often about his "parties" with the two girls.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Dukov possesses one of the keys Crowley desires. There is a variety of ways to obtain it.

chr_000288bc.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, guard, eat, sleep
chr_000288bc.summary: Dusty is the watchman in Big Town in the year 2277, who can, for the most part, be found sitting on the chair overlooking the bridge - the only way into Big Town.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Pappy has given Dusty the responsibility of guarding the only entrance to Big Town - the rope bridge at the settlement's north end. He isn't very eager and usually sits dozing on his chair, perhaps one of the reasons why the super mutants seem to just walk in, take their "food," and leave. Dusty is jittery and desperate and lacks the know-how to properly prepare the town's defenses for another attack.

He is the sole sentry against the endless onslaught of super mutants from the German Town PD and the slavers from Paradise Falls. He often laments at the fact that if the mutants don't kill everyone, the slavers will enslave them. He, like all the other Big Towners, originates from Little Lamplight. He seems shocked by the position that he and the other residents are currently in.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: When first encountering the Lone Wanderer, he will ask them who they are and tell the player character about the constant attacks by super mutants and slavers.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Leather Armor, Rivet City Security Helmet.

chr_0002805a.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: sleep, travel, combat, guard, follow
chr_0002805a.summary: Timebomb is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 26 HP). Affiliated with Big Town Residents. Found primarily around Big Town, Red's Clinic. Directly connected to quests: Big Trouble in Big Town.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Timebomb, like every other inhabitant of Big Town, came from Little Lamplight. He is known as Timebomb due to his mood swings; he has prolonged periods of calm before eventually "blowing up." Usually, Timebomb is innocent and excitable, but will occasionally burst with anger, seemingly out of nowhere. He is also somewhat socially awkward, occasionally stumbling over his words and failing to read social cues.

Currently laid out in a coma in the operating room of Red's clinic, Timebomb was severely wounded during the last super mutant attack, when Red and Shorty were kidnapped. He has very few memories of his injury, but actually took on seven bullet wounds and broke both of his clavicles from super mutant gunfire. If the Lone Wanderer uses their skill in Medicine to heal Timebomb, he will be grateful for their help in Red's absence.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• With a Medicine skill of 40, it is possible to either revive or kill Timebomb.
• With a Medicine skill lower than 40, the only options presented are to "leave him alone" or "put him out of his misery."
• If healed, after the Big Trouble in Big Town quest is completed and the super mutant attack repelled, Timebomb will give the Lucky 8 ball as a reward upon speaking to him.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Big Town, Red's Clinic. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_0002796c.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, combat, guard, follow, sandbox
chr_0002796c.summary: Pappy is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 35 HP). Affiliated with Big Town Residents. Found primarily around Big Town, Common House. Directly connected to quests: Big Trouble in Big Town.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Pappy claims to have come from Little Lamplight with his girlfriend Bittercup and the others hoping to find Big Town, a nice town with plenty of food and protection. Bittercup broke up with him when they found Big Town to be a shoddy bunch of houses and junk organized into a fortress, that was constantly under attack by slavers and super mutants. Now in his mid-twenties, Pappy is the old-timer of Big Town, trying to hold the settlement together, but is becoming increasingly pessimistic.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: Like all inhabitants of Big Town, Pappy participates in the defense of the town against the super mutant attack.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Big Town, Common House. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_0002796b.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, combat, guard, follow, sandbox
chr_0002796b.summary: Flash is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 35 HP). Affiliated with Big Town Residents. Found primarily around Big Town, Clubhouse. Directly connected to quests: Big Trouble in Big Town.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Growing up together in Little Lamplight, Flash, Pappy, Bittercup, Red and Kimba were close, and often played together. They also traveled as a group to Big Town. Flash was told by the other children of Lamplight that Big Town would be safe, and have plenty to eat. However, this is plainly not the case, with Flash joking that he is shot at more times than he has a good meal.

On the surface, Flash exudes bravado and overconfidence, and has a penchant for making big, childish claims that he cannot really back up. For example, he is exceptionally proud of his "kick-ass" gun (in reality, a simple, weak.32 pistol) and boasts his desire to defend the town and kill super mutants with it. He also claims that he must have killed a hundred raiders on one patrol, despite only having ten bullets.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Flash handles the patrolling of the town during daylight hours. At nighttime, he switches out with Bittercup and rests.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: Flash asks the Lone Wanderer to go alleviate the hostage crisis, which sends them to the Germantown Police HQ.

Other interactions:
• When the Lone Wanderer first talks to Flash, there is a dialogue option to declare their intent on killing him. If this option is chosen, the whole town will become hostile towards the player character.
• Flash continually boasts about his "kick-ass gun," although it is not unique, and is just a standard.32 pistol. This is probably because there is a lack of firearms in Big Town, with the only other gun being Dusty's hunting rifle.

chr_0002796a.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, combat, guard, follow, sandbox
chr_0002796a.summary: Bittercup is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 35 HP). Affiliated with Big Town Residents. Found primarily around Big Town, Common House. Directly connected to quests: Big Trouble in Big Town.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Apathetic, self-involved, and rebellious, Bittercup is one of the troubled young characters that live in Big Town. She spends time worrying about what dark clothing to wear and applying homemade makeup often at the expense of better guarding the town against threats. Many of the other Big Town residents are tired of her, but they don't do much about it as the threat of super mutant and raider attacks takes higher priority.

Through dialogue, it is revealed that Bittercup has been romantically involved with most of the males in Big Town at one point or another, but it is remarkable that she does not seem to take any of their interests in a physical way. She had a romantic interest in Pappy, whom she left after arriving in Big Town, believing that he was a liar.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
• 12 noon - 8 p.m.: Sleeping in the common room
• 8 p.m. - 10 p.m.: Eating in the town hall
• 10 p.m. - 10 a.m.: Patrolling the town
• 10 a.m. - 12 noon: Eating in the town hall

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: When the Lone Wanderer first meets Bittercup, she will tell them that Red and Shorty have been captured by super mutants and taken to the Germantown Police HQ.
• Bittercup Runneth Over: Through dialogue options, the Lone Wanderer can endear themselves to Bittercup, who will become their girlfriend. Once every 24 hours, she will give a random present for a lengthy, albeit limited time.

chr_0002ab95.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: puzzled. AI packages: travel, follow, guard, dialogue, combat
chr_0002ab95.summary: Shorty is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 85 HP). Affiliated with Big Town Residents. Found primarily around Big Town, Clubhouse. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom, The Waters of Life, Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Despite being of short stature, Shorty's nickname actually originates from his bad temper, with his neighbors in Big Town calling him "Short-T." He has a generally negative attitude and a large ego. Even as a child in Little Lamplight, he did not believe the fantastical stories about Big Town, but did not want everyone he knew to go there without him. His current feelings on Big Town are summed up by his sarcastic answer when asked about Big Town's origins, stating that a super mutant likely sat down in a ditch and "shat" it out. The Lone Wanderer first encounters Shorty in the basement kitchen of the Germantown Police HQ, where he is being held captive, soon to become a super mutant meal.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: As an optional objective, the Lone Wanderer has to save Shorty in addition to Red.

Other interactions:
• If Shorty is undiscovered during Big Trouble in Big Town and encountered after completing this quest, he will act as if the player character had saved him.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only if the Small Guns path is taken in Big Trouble in Big Town.

chr_0002ab94.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, combat, guard, follow, sandbox
chr_0002ab94.summary: Kimba is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 35 HP). Affiliated with Big Town Residents. Found primarily around Big Town, Common House. Directly connected to quests: Big Trouble in Big Town.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Hoping against hope for some outside help, Kimba goes along with the rest of the inhabitants' wishes most of the time, even if they contradict her logical thoughts. Despite the terrible current situation, Kimba remains stable and soft-spoken, and she is always ready to pitch in, learn a new skill and fight for her friends.

As with all the inhabitants of Big Town, she used to live in Little Lamplight.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: Like all inhabitants of Big Town, she is involved in the defense against the super mutant attack.

Other interactions:
• If inquired by the player, she tells about how she, Red, Pappy, and Flash used to play together when they were younger.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Big Town, Common House. Notable equipment & inventory: Leather Armor, BB, BB Gun.

chr_0002a9ff.behavior: Unaggressive, cautious; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, find
chr_0002a9ff.summary: Nurse Graves is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Found primarily around The Chop Shop. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head, Reilly's Rangers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Young by ghoul standards, Doctor Barrows' assistant Nurse Graves is knowledgeable and keen. She helps in Barrows' experiments to diagnose and treat the various brand-new ailments that ghouls are always complaining about. Happy with her lot in life, she spends her time cutting up corpses, inspecting brain tissue samples, and poking feral ghouls with a variety of (mainly sharp) implements.

Unlike other ghouls in the Fallout universe, she sympathizes with humans as much as ghouls (stating they were all the same once) while most other ghouls and humans are on non-friendly terms. She will mention that Doctor Barrows performed experiments on Reilly while she was in her coma and that he believes that if they can study the human body, then they may be able to stop or even reverse the effect of human to ghoul transformations.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Reilly's Rangers: She will talk to the Lone Wanderer about Reilly and explain how they found her and brought her to Underworld.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Chop Shop. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000340ff.

chr_0002a7f4.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: angry. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_0002a7f4.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00029aa9.summary: Old Man Harris is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 85 HP). Found primarily around Old Man Harris' House.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Old Man Harris lives alone in a small shack on the perimeter of the town. His wife Gladys passed away, leaving him an unenthusiastic version of his former self. He spends his time inside his home, sustained by the effort of other residents of the community, though due to his regrets, he barely eats. Old Man Harris will share information about his past, including growing up in Andale and marrying Gladys. He will relay details of his family who currently live with him in town, including his daughter Linda who has grown up to marry Jack. He implores the player character to escape, stating that although it looks normal and everyone is nice, it is only a trick. He encourages the Lone Wanderer to look into it if they need to be convinced, pointing them to the nearby basement and shed.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Our Little Secret: Old Man Harris will warn the Lone Wanderer to get away from Andale, telling them that the town is not what it seems to be.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer kills the town's residents, Old Man Harris will become the guardian of the children and speak more openly about his past.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Old Man Harris' House. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Casualwear, Tortiseshell Glasses.

chr_00029aa8.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00029aa8.summary: Karen Johnson is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: It appears that Karen Johnson was abandoned sometime during development prior to the Andale-based unmarked quest Our Little Secret being completed. There is another cut character with a similar name in the game's files, Tuck Johnson, presumably her husband. Karen Johnson and her husband were most likely one of the other "families" living in Andale. This is because it is said that four families survived the great war in Andale but in-game there are only two "families."

chr_00029aa7.summary: Tuck Johnson is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Tuck Johnson was abandoned sometime during development prior to the Andale-based unmarked quest Our Little Secret being completed. Little remains implemented with regards to the non-player character, but remaining AI packages and code snippets lend clues as to his intended role within Andale. The character was to be based primarily out of his house (location not specified) and would proceed about a normal routine. It is not clear if any special conversations were to be available between him and the Lone Wanderer, but remaining dialogue and conversations in the associated packages for Andale residents have him responding to the Lone Wanderer in a friendly, welcoming manner.

There is another cut character with a similar name in the game's files, Karen Johnson, presumably his wife.
