chr_00029aa6.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_00029aa6.summary: Jenny Wilson is a caucasian child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Found primarily around The Wilson's House.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Jenny is a young girl who has a crush on her cousin Junior Smith, much to her parents' delight and Junior's dismay. She plans on one day marrying Junior, saying she thinks that they would be especially good "married people," as her and Junior's fathers are brothers.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Our Little Secret: If the Lone Wanderer decides to cooperate with the families and keep their secret, Jenny stays with her family. If the Wanderer decides to free the town of its residents (excluding Old Man Harris), Jenny and Junior Smith will go to live with Old Man Harris, who expresses sadness about the situation to the player character.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Wilson's House. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000340c4.

chr_00029aa5.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00029aa5.summary: Martha Wilson is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 70 HP). Found primarily around The Wilson's House.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Martha is the rather quiet wife of Bill Wilson. If asked her opinion on Andale or other matters, she will be fairly perplexed that someone cared enough to ask.

As part of a family that carries on a tradition of cannibalism as the main way of life in Andale, Martha helps keep the house clean and cooks meals while her husband Bill goes to work with Jack Smith in the aforementioned "family business."

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Our Little Secret: Martha is one of Andale's cannibals. Should the Lone Wanderer uncover this secret, upon leaving the shed behind the Smiths' house, the inhabitants of Andale will confront them.

Effects of player's actions:
If she is asked about Old Man Harris (after talking to him) she will disclose the fact that he is her father, then states that she "...probably shouldn't have said that."

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Wilson's House. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Businesswear, Tortiseshell Glasses.

chr_00029aa4.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00029aa4.summary: Willy "Bill" Wilson is one of seven residents living in Andale, along with his wife Martha and daughter Jenny in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Bill and his family are the next-door neighbors of the Smiths. Bill, alongside his wife, is pleased that his daughter seems to have feelings for the Smiths' son, Junior. Bill spends most of his time in the shed or Smith house basement working with his brother, Jack, on Andale's "family business" - cannibalism. This practice was adopted over two centuries ago by Bill's ancestors and is how he and his modern relatives survive in the wasteland, seeing the practice as honoring tradition and a point of pride.

Like the other residents of the town, Bill is quite pleased to raise his family there.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Along with the two Andale children, Bill is the only Andale resident who leaves his house, spending much of his time in front of the shed behind the Wilson house.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Our Little Secret: Like all residents of Andale, Bill Wilson is a cannibal. Should the Lone Wanderer uncover their secret, they can choose to let them continue their slaughter of wasteland inhabitants or kill them all.

chr_00029aa3.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_00029aa3.summary: Jack "Junior" Smith is the son of Jack Smith and Linda Smith and resides in Andale in 2277.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Junior is the son of Jack and Linda Smith, and one of two children in Andale, the other one being Jenny Wilson, with whom he seems to get along well. He is supposed to marry her when he grows up, just as every Andale boy marries the girl closest to his age.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Our Little Secret: If the Lone Wanderer decides to cooperate with the families and keep their secret, Junior stays with his family living day to day on strange meat pies. If the Wanderer decides instead to eliminate the town's residents (excluding Old Man Harris), Junior and Jenny will go to live with Old Man Harris. He will express some confusion as to what happened, saying that Harris told him and Jenny that their parents went away and won't be coming back.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Smith's House. Notable equipment & inventory: Kid's Baseball Cap, itm_000340c4.

chr_00029aa2.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00029aa2.summary: Linda Smith is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 70 HP). Found primarily around The Smith's House.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
House-proud and vehemently opposed to outside influences, the Smiths are a strange but reasonably friendly bunch. Jack seems to be Andale's patriarch and he knows the best little town in America is here, where Linda bakes a delicious meat pie!

Linda is part of a family of inbred cannibals that lives in Andale. She is married to Jack Smith and together they have a son, Junior Smith. Linda is the child of Old Man Harris.

She, as a housewife, performs household chores and cooks meals while her husband goes to work with her neighbor and brother Bill in the "family business," capturing and killing wastelanders in order to dine on their flesh. All of this cannibalistic activity is conducted in the Smiths' garden shed and the Wilson family basement.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Linda Smith is the wife of Jack Smith and the mother of Junior Smith. Her father is Old Man Harris, and her mother was Gladys Smith.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Our Little Secret: Once the Lone Wanderer learns about the town's cannibalism and incest, they can choose to either put an end to the state of affairs or support the status quo.

chr_00029aa1.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00029aa1.summary: Jack Smith is part of a family of cannibals living in Andale, along with his wife Linda and their son Junior in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jack Smith appears to be Andale's patriarch, priding himself on the town being the best that Virginia has to offer, with a heavy emphasis on rejecting the outside influence that the Capital Wasteland presents. The Smiths appear exceedingly friendly, to a point where it is strange, and the Lone Wanderer may then find out it is due to their unusual diet.

Presenting himself as a loyal U.S. citizen and father, Jack and his wife (and sister) Linda have a son Junior Smith. While his wife cooks and cleans the house, he goes to work with his neighbor (and brother) Bill Wilson in the "family business." In this enterprise, they preserve and maintain a centuries-long local tradition: cannibalism. Wastelanders passing through are allowed by the local families to stay in town and become accustomed to the warm attitude and reception of them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Our Little Secret: Like all residents of Andale, Jack Smith is a cannibal. Uncover their secret and choose to let them continue their slaughter of wasteland inhabitants, or kill them all.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Smith's House. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Spring Outfit, Andale Basement Key.

chr_00029a98.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, sandbox, sleep, eat
chr_00029a98.summary: Dave is the self-proclaimed president of the Republic of Dave, a small farmstead on the far northeast edge of the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
After being exiled from the family farmstead (then known as the Kingdom of Tom under the leadership of his father, Tom), Dave made a living operating as a mercenary in and around the Capital Wasteland, and took part in an ill-fated expedition to Fort Constantine along with a handful of other mercenaries on behalf of Allistair Tenpenny. He eventually returned to the Kingdom of Tom and made a coup d'état, renaming it the "Republic of Dave" and giving the citizens the "freedom of democracy" in the form of an annual election, in contrast to the dictatorship of Tom.

Dave decided the marital standards needed changing after inheriting the Republic from his father, allowing polygamous relationships and resulting in his marriage to his second wife, Jessica.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Dave's activities consist of staying in his office and never going outside of the main building in the Republic of Dave.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Dave is in possession of one of the keys Mister Crowley desires.
• Election Day: Dave asks the Lone Wanderer to gather the republic's citizens for the upcoming election for a small reward. One can vote for Dave (after paying the 250 caps immigration fee), or encourage his first wife Rosie and/or his son Bob to run against him. One can also tamper with the ballot box to make it possible for someone other than Dave to win.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Dave loses the election, he will leave the Republic forever and retreat to Old Olney, which he will declare the New Republic of Dave. Thereafter, he will be found sitting in the gore-strewn alleyway just a few feet from the fast-travel arrival location. Speaking to him repeatedly afterward will result in him turning hostile.

chr_00029690.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: angry. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_00029690.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

chr_000295eb.summary: Sticky is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom, The Waters of Life, Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He was known to his Lamplighter friends as "Sticky Hands," though he calls himself Jack now that he is older. If questioned what his nickname meant, he only replies, "use your imagination." He is a chatterbox who can be annoying and self-centered. Despite being 16, he acts younger than that, although this is due to having a lack of adult role models.

Sticky states that his age is 18, while everybody else says he is 16. In 2277, he is forced to leave Little Lamplight as all children must eventually do once they reach the age of 16.

He is first encountered after gaining entry into Little Lamplight, where the other Lamplighters will be telling him he needs to leave, while Sticky displays his unhappiness at leaving.

Sticky is friends with Red in Big Town. He refers to her as his "girlfriend."

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Before the unmarked quest Happy Birthday to You, he can be found in Little Lamplight. Upon successful completion of the quest, he will reside in Big Town spending his days in the town hall, and nights sleeping in the common house.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Happy Birthday to You: Sticky needs to get to Big Town, but needs an escort to get him there safely.
• Big Trouble in Big Town: If one escorts Sticky to Big Town before solving Big Town's super mutant problem, he will help fend off the super mutant raid.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer fires Sticky, or refuses to take him to Big Town, Sticky will remain in the area he was fired from until the next time the Lone Wanderer enters that map cell, at which point he dies.
• If one kills him while he is saying goodbye in Lamplight caverns, the other kids will comment that they thought he was annoying.
• If the player character refuses to escort Sticky when first meeting him by saying that they "want to visit Little Lamplight first," Sticky will stand on the other side of the gate indefinitely.

chr_00029579.summary: Theo is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 30 HP). Found primarily around Statesman Hotel Mid Level.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Although Reilly regarded the recently recruited Theo as "green" and viewed him as an insufficient replacement for the recently deceased members Dallas and Kira, she hoped that he would grow with experience. Theo served as the mercenary company's quartermaster, helping maintain the equipment while also carrying extra ammunition on missions.

As Theo was itching to participate in one of the company's mapping trips into the downtown ruins, the entire group made an excursion to Vernon Square, where they were ambushed and pursued by a large army of super mutants. The group was forced to take shelter in Our Lady of Hope Hospital before crossing over an impromptu bridge into the Statesman Hotel.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Theo's corpse can be found in a stairwell in the Statesman Hotel. His ammunition box can be looted (during the quest) if Reilly gives the player character the code (Reilly9090). Inside are 200 5mm rounds, 100 5.56mm rounds, 100 10mm rounds, and 4 frag grenades. If the ammunition is taken from the cache, they can either keep it or share it with the other members of Reilly's Rangers on the roof of the Statesman Hotel.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Statesman Hotel Mid Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Charmer Outfit.

chr_00029578.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sleep, sandbox, guard
chr_00029578.summary: Butcher (real name Carl) is the Reilly's Rangers medic. He can be found with the rest of the team on the roof of the Statesman Hotel, waiting for Reilly to return. After completing the Reilly's Rangers quest, he and the other rangers can be found at the Ranger compound.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born around as Carl,

The next mission would put that to the test. Reilly opted to scout Vernon Square, both to gather salvage and to train Theo, a new ranger on a probationary contract. Butcher hoped to pick through the ruins of Our Lady of Hope Hospital to find more medical materials and supplies. However, nobody among the Rangers enjoyed mapping missions into that sector of downtown, with the sole exception of Brick: the sheer number of super mutants was overwhelming to most people, but to her, it was merely a target-rich environment. Butcher believed that there was something in the area that attracted super mutants or something they were looking for. However, he lacked the resources and time to investigate on his own.

Soon, he would discover that he had very little time for anything but survival.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Reilly's Rangers: Butcher is among the members of Reilly's Rangers who need to be rescued from the top of the Statesman Hotel. If the Lone Wanderer manages to save Butcher, he will become a free doctor.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: * Only if one does not give him any ammunition.

chr_00029577.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, sleep, sandbox, guard
chr_00029577.summary: Donovan is the Reilly's Rangers engineer first seen on the rooftop of the Statesman Hotel.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Donovan is the technical expert of the Rangers, with a proficiency in hacking, repairing weapons and armor, and working on electronics. According to Reilly, he is an "absolute wizard" when it comes to maintaining weapons and armor in particular, but she wishes he possessed more knowledge on electrical systems or hydraulics, for instance, to help with safely navigating the downtown ruins. If handed the battery, Donovan himself comments that fixing the elevator would only take him a few minutes. It has taken Donovan one year to develop the geomapper which he has successfully produced a limited supply of that Reilly can source to the Lone Wanderer if they agree to assist with mapping for the Rangers. If he is successfully rescued, he may be found having utilized his creation to locate the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Reilly's Rangers: Donovan holds Donovan's wrench, a quest item used for repairing the elevator in the Statesman Hotel, allowing the Lone Wanderer to finish the repairs if Donovan dies. Otherwise, he can fix the elevator himself using a fission battery. If he survives at the end of the quest, he will return to the Ranger compound where he can repair the player character's gear for less than what other merchants charge.

Effects of player's actions:
• After completing the Reilly's Rangers quest, one may encounter Donovan while traveling through the Capital Wasteland. Soon after, he appears to be engaging in a firefight against three super mutants.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Ranger Battle Armor, Ranger Battle Helmet, Chinese Assault Rifle.

chr_00029576.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: puzzled. AI packages: sleep, sandbox, travel, guard
chr_00029576.summary: Brick is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 10, 110 HP). Affiliated with Reilly's Rangers. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Reilly's Rangers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born around, the 24 year old Brick was hired by Reilly as a heavy weapons specialist. Together with her minigun, Eugene, the muscle-bound gunner is considered an outstanding asset for the Rangers, combining a zeal for destruction with reliability and calmness under fire. She lacks patience for mission planning and debriefings, but remains fiercely loyal to the group, and Reilly considers her to be the go-to person in case of problems. Brick's contract specifies 50 caps per mission, and her service record resulted in five merits and one demerit by the time of the ill-fated Vernon Square deployment.

Brick gets along fine with most of the Rangers. She sees them as eggheads, with more skill in sciences and such, than combat, which is fine by her. She just points, shoots, and makes anything that gets in the Rangers' way die.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Reilly's Rangers: Brick is one of Reilly's Rangers stuck on top of the Statesman Hotel.
• One of the Eugenes is a quest reward, with the alternative being the Ranger battle armor. If the player chooses the armor, they can pickpocket Brick's own minigun or kill Brick for it. Of course, if she dies during the retreat from the hotel, her body can be looted for Eugene as well.
• After the quest, she will offer to assist the player in combat whenever "they are in the neighborhood," but the Rangers do not leave the compound. She does mention that once the Lone Wanderer joins, Reilly is back to her old self and they are running ops again.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: * If she is not provided with ammo during the quest.

chr_00027fb1.summary: Slaver is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 80 HP). Found primarily around Mall Southwest. Directly connected to quests: Head of State.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Slavery is a significant part of the Capital Wasteland's economy. Paradise Falls is a slaver compound, and several quests feature slavery as either major or minor elements, such as Head of State and its association with slavery and Abraham Lincoln's role as the "Great Emancipator."

Additionally, the Lone Wanderer can capture people to sell them to slavers. The Lone Wanderer can even buy a slave, Clover, who will then serve as a bodyguard. The Lone Wanderer does not have the option of activating or defusing Clover's explosive collar.

The number of slaves present compared to the number of slavers is remarkably low, meaning that the slaves are being shipped off somewhere. It is revealed by Wernher that many of these slaves are being shipped off to work in the Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State
• Strictly Business
• Those!
• Strictly Profitable
• The Kid-Kidnapper

Effects of player's actions:
Slavers are generally not hostile to the Lone Wanderer as long as they are not provoked with hostile dialogue responses, but attacking them can make the Paradise Falls slavers permanently enemies with the player character. If slavers are hostile first and killed, Paradise Falls slavers will not be initially hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Mall Southwest. Notable equipment & inventory: Frag Grenade.

chr_00027f65.role: Tunnel Snakes, DeLoria Family, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian
chr_00027f65.summary: Butch DeLoria is a resident of Vault 101 and the leader and co-founder of the Tunnel Snakes gang in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born and raised in Vault 101 all his life and being under the care of his mother Ellen, a notorious alcoholic who neglected to oversee her son's negative maturing, Butch has been forced to put on a mask as a boorish, overbearing bully to cover up his deep-seated feelings of inadequacy due to not knowing his father despite living in a Vault with a close-knit community.

On July 13, 2268, when he was ten years old, During the party, Butch held a small meeting with his only two friends, Wally Mack and Paul Hannon Jr., to toss around ideas for a name for their gang, which later would be decided to be the "Tunnel Snakes" while rejecting other names such as "Vault Dwellers." He also attempted to strongarm the Wanderer into giving up the sweetroll they got from Lucy Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Butch becomes non-essential during Escape! and he can optionally be killed before leaving Vault 101, preventing him from appearing during Trouble on the Homefront and becoming a companion later.
• If Trouble on the Homefront was completed by either opening or destroying Vault 101, and Butch was left alive, he can be found residing in the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. He can be recruited as a companion only while the player character has Neutral Karma.

Companion:
• Butch can give the Lone Wanderer a haircut during Trouble on the Homefront, and if recruited as a companion, also at any time during their travels.
• If separated from the player character, Butch will return to the Muddy Rudder.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Items will be replaced by a non-player switchblade and 10mm pistol, if no replacement weapons are left in Butch's inventory while he is a companion.

chr_000273cb.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: sad. AI packages: sandbox, eat
chr_000273cb.role: Vault 101 Security, DeLoria Family, Vault 101 Residents — Caucasian Elderly
chr_000273cb.summary: Ellen DeLoria is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 125 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Security, DeLoria Family, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Lower Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ellen likes to get drunk often, but this causes her not to pay attention to what her son Butch is up to. Ellen and Butch live together in one of the smallest family apartments. Butch's father is a mystery to the other residents of Vault 101.

In 2268, Ellen encouraged her son Butch to attend the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party in the cafeteria.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Escape!: Ellen will come under attack by radroaches, leading Butch to appeal to the Lone Wanderer to save her.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If she was saved in Escape!, she is revealed to be a loyalist to the overseer, and despite the Lone Wanderer saving her life, she blames the entire incident on James.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should she be saved from the radroaches, Butch will declare that the Lone Wanderer is his best friend and he will give them his Tunnel Snake outfit, while Ellen asks if they would like a drink. This also gives the Lone Wanderer some good Karma.
• If the Lone Wanderer simply allows Ellen to be mauled by the radroaches, Butch will despise them and attempt to lead Vault 101 security in the right direction to capturing them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Lower Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_00027057.behavior: Aggressive, cautious; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, patrol, sleep, sandbox
chr_00027057.summary: Officer Gomez is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 60 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Security, Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101 Entrance. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
An archetypal "good cop," Herman Gomez has more of a conscience than many of his fellow Vault 101 security officers. He is the husband of Pepper Gomez and the father of Freddie Gomez, whom he attempts to keep away from the Tunnel Snakes' influence. However, he knows that this is difficult because there are few other children Freddie's age in the Vault. More generally, Gomez is interested in youth outreach and preventing bullying in the Vault. He believes that responsibility lies with a parent to raise a child right, though if all else fails, the influence of Vault security can also have an impact.

As a friend of James, the Vault physician, Officer Gomez extends faith that he must have had his reasons for leaving the Vault in 2277, even if this view is not shared by most of his peers.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only drops a finger during Growing Up Fast and Escape!.

Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: If a scuffle occurs between the Lone Wanderer and Butch DeLoria over the sweetroll, Officer Gomez will intervene.
• Escape!: Gomez will be helping Stanley and Andy fight radroaches. Provided he is not attacked, he warns the Lone Wanderer that security is on the lookout for them. Gomez believes that James is innocent and suggests leaving the vault to search for him.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If he lives, Gomez will be the first vault resident the Lone Wanderer runs into. Staying civilized with him will have him escort the Lone Wanderer to either Amata or the current overseer. If Allen Mack attacks while any guards are around, the guards will immediately come to his side to protect him. This includes Officer Gomez.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is Susie and Wally Mack's brother, and Allen Mack and Gloria Mack's son. Stevie is 25 years old as of the events of Escape! He is a sadistic and gung-ho member of the Vault's security force, and willing to do anything to gain favor with his boss, including being particularly overzealous during emergencies.

He is responsible for the killing of Jonas Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• He will only drop a finger during Escape!

Quests:
• Escape!: Officer Mack is found in the security office interrogating Amata. If the Lone Wanderer took the overseer's gun from Amata, they have no choice but to fight Mack, due to the fact that he attacks them on sight. If one insisted Amata keeps her father's gun to protect herself, she will shoot Mack in self-defense, killing him. If you interrupt before Amata fires on him, she will escape and the player character will again be responsible for killing Mack.
• Trouble on the Homefront: If not killed in Escape!, Mack is found in the vault upon returning. He is not hostile.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
John Kendall is the husband of Mary Kendall and the father of Christine and Monica. John is friendly, yet tough and no-nonsense. While he is not actively sinister, he will follow orders without putting much thought into it. Introspection is not a trait he commonly displays. He loves being a cop and whether what he is doing is right does not worry him; he is the law.

During the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party on July 13, 2268, Officer Kendall can be overheard talking with the overseer in the stairway to the upper level. Officer Kendall is assigned by the overseer to give the party just a few more minutes and then make sure everyone gets back to work. He may idley wish the Wanderer a happy birthday if near him, and gleefully remark the party sounds like fun.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• He will only drop a finger prior to Trouble on the Homefront

Quests:

• Escape!: The Lone Wanderer encounters Kendall just outside their room, whereupon Kendall will be attacked by several radroaches. The Lone Wanderer can sneak past him through the restrooms, attempt to save him from the radroaches, or kill him. He is the first person that can be killed in the game. He will become hostile after the radroaches are dead.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Officer Kendall will be present if he did not die during Escape! When interacted with, he blames the Lone Wanderer and James for the vault's problems.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is the father of Paul Hannon Jr. and husband of Vikki Hannon.

He is extremely aggressive and by-the-book, and he wishes his vault security force was a real military with a war to win. He is not nearly as smart as he thinks he is, and his men are not nearly the crack security force he thinks they are. Spit and polish are everything to him; following orders is his highest calling.

• Trouble on the Homefront: He will be present in the vault upon returning during the quest if he lived during Lone Wanderer's escape. He will have a younger, completely different model.

Effects of player's actions:
• It is likely that Hannon will attack the Lone Wanderer during Escape!, though his attacks do not cause significant damage and he can largely be ignored as one progresses through the quest.
• If he lives during Escape!, he will be present during Trouble on the Homefront. He can usually be found patrolling near the overseer's office.

chr_00026c57.summary: Paladin Gunny is a Brotherhood of Steel paladin stationed at the Citadel in 2277, and is tasked as the drill instructor for new initiates.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Paladin Gunny was involved in Elder Lyons' original expedition to the Capital Wasteland. Although he disagrees with Elder Lyons’ policy of recruiting wastelanders into the Brotherhood, he still works to train them to the best of his abilities before they are pressed into service, whether that be against the super mutants or the renewed threat of the Enclave. As the Enclave’s presence means that many of his initiates are likely to be sent into battle before they’ve taken the Brotherhood’s oath, his work has been cut out for him. He has particularly strong feelings on the Enclave, viewing them as cowards for shooting unarmed civilians. He fully believes that the Brotherhood will defeat them, and that the experience and equipment gained by doing so will improve the Brotherhood’s abilities.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can be found in the A ring just outside the lab in the council room, outside in the courtyard training recruits during the daytime, or inside a dormitory in B ring.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• If permission is granted by Elder Lyons, Gunny can train the Lone Wanderer to properly use and wear power armor. However, Gunny does not like it as he clearly states, "Yeah, I can train you. But don't ask me to like it. My initiates sweat blood, and you just get a free pass?"
• He has a low opinion of the Enclave and their tactics, and will readily voice these opinions if inquired about them.
• Once Gunny has provided the Lone Wanderer with power armor training, he will lose his essential status.

chr_00025fd0.summary: Scribe Elizabeth Jameson is the head librarian and proctor for the Order of the Quill in the East Coast Brotherhood of Steel.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Due to her roles within Elder Lyons' chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel, Scribe Jameson is tasked with overseeing the archives and library of the Citadel, alongside ensuring the upkeep of the chapter's scrolls. Her order is dedicated to conserving both pre-War and Brotherhood history, which includes the procurement of pre-war books and holotapes, as well as the recovery of Brotherhood holotags. While Scribe Yearling is the order's only field associate tasked with obtaining books from Arlington Library, Jameson lacks the necessary manpower to send messengers and detachments to recover holotags; However, the situation has been made worse by the shortage of communication equipment, necessary for contacting the Brotherhood operatives scattered around the DC ruins, making Jameson unaware of the locations of possible casualties.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Scribe Jameson can be found working in the archives area of the A ring in the Citadel when she is not sleeping.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Wilks acts as the leader of the security detail assigned to protect the GNR plaza. In exchange for Three Dog's permission to use the plaza as a base for the Brotherhood's operations in downtown D.C., Wilks and the rest of his team defend the building from the super mutants. chr_0002549e.summary: Amata Almodovar is a resident of Vault 101, the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar, and a major character. Along with Owyn Lyons and Sarah Lyons, she is one of only three characters in the game to have "Very Good" Karma.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only daughter of the overseer, Amata is around the Lone Wanderer's age and the two grew up together ever since James arrived in the Vault with his child in tow. They bonded over many things, from Grognak the Barbarian to being raised by single fathers after their mothers passed away at a young age: Amata lost her mother at two, leaving her father, the overseer, to raise her on his own. The burden of leading the Vault and enforcing his isolationist policy slowly drove Amata and Alphonse apart, despite her deep love for her father and an innate sense of loyalty.

The bond between Amata and the Lone Wanderer developed into a deep friendship over the years, with the two becoming inseparable, best friends. Another was that he simply didn't like the Lone Wanderer, in part due to their father's stubborn, insubordinate personality.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Amata organizes the Lone Wanderer's birthday party on July 13, 2268, gifting them an intact copy of the 14th issue of Grognak the Barbarian, and demonstrating some of the reactivity of the game.
• Future Imperfect: Amata takes the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, together with the Lone Wanderer. Before entering the class room, she is harassed by the Tunnel Snakes, allowing the player to experiment with various approaches to resolving quests and introducing them to the Karma system.
• Escape!: Amata awakens the Lone Wanderer with news of James' escape from the vault. She offers a gun and outlines a plan for the Lone Wanderer's own escape. Toward the end of the quest, it turns out that she was captured and is interrogated by her father and Officer Mack.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Intelligent, slightly sarcastic, and motherly, Red is Big Town's doctor in residence. She previously taught Lucy her medical knowledge so Little Lamplight would be safer, and the two had a sisterly relationship.

Red is on an enforced leave thanks to the current kidnapping sweeps by super mutants in the local area. Her nickname stems from the blood she is always splattered in and her affinity for the color. She runs the clinic in Big Town, and she is the unofficial mayor and an old girlfriend of an older boy named Sticky Hands, an ex-resident of Little Lamplight.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Big Trouble in Big Town: Red is being held captive in the Germantown police station, where the Lone Wanderer is asked to go to rescue her.
• Strictly Business: Red is one of the targets for enslavement identified by Eulogy Jones. Grouse refers to her as that "hot doctor chick" from Big Town.

Effects of player's actions:
• Once freed from the super mutants, Red will resume selling medical supplies in Big Town.
• If the Lone Wanderer heals Timebomb, Red will say she is impressed with their medical skills and that they're clearly a better doctor than she is. She will then heal the Lone Wanderer for free from then on.
• If the Lone Wanderer frees Red and returns her to Big Town, she may still die during the super mutant raid that happens soon after.

chr_00025093.summary: Timmy Neusbaum is one of the residents of Vault 112, trapped within the Tranquility Lane simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Timmy is the son of George and Pat Neusbaum, well-behaved and quiet, though somewhat of a "momma's boy" according to Bill Foster. Betty considers him a "big crybaby" and tasks the Lone Wanderer with making him cry, even though she constantly upsets him herself. Mabel Henderson has been attempting to convince his mother to send him to military school, even giving her a military school brochure as she claims Timmy is too attached to his parents; Pat dismisses her suggestion and asserts that Mabel has never been fond of Timmy.

He has set up a lemonade stand in Tranquility Lane per his mother's advice of "if life gives you lemons, make lemonade," in an effort to save up money to purchase a Red Racer tricycle like the one Betty owns.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tranquility Lane: The first task Betty gives out is to make Timmy cry. When the player has made Timmy cry successfully and reports back to Betty, Timmy is turned into a garden gnome by the Neusbaum's front door (called Timmy the Gnome).
• If the failsafe is used without upsetting Timmy, he simply disappears.

chr_000244a3.summary: Mabel Henderson is one of the inhabitants of Vault 112 trapped in the Tranquility Lane virtual reality simulation, met.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A resident of Vault 112 for over 200 years, Stanislaus Braun has given Mabel the role of the local gossip and baking contest winner. Mabel won the Tranquility Lane Finest Meat Pie award for the last three years in a row, and is incredibly proud of her achievement. She loves to share the results of her baking with other residents, which also gives her the chance to chat, eavesdrop, and gossip. She tends to brag about her oven when coming along for a visit, which some residents find a bit grating, like George Neusbaum.

However, they also recognize her as a prime source of news on what's going on in Tranquility Lane. This earns Mabel the scorn of some: Pat Neusbaum distrusts and dislikes Mabel both for being a busybody, and for insisting on sending her son to a military school, to cure him of his attachment to parents.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Tranquility Lane: Mabel is one of the residents one will have to kill if they choose to do all of Betty's tasks. One of the assignments includes killing her in a creative fashion, leveraging her love of baking, for example, after which Braun will simply respawn it.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Old Lady Dithers is a inhabitant of Vault 112 and, like the other Vault Dwellers, is trapped in the Tranquility Lane simulation and subject to Stanislaus Braun's whims. Unlike the others, she is aware of what Braun is doing and tries to alert the others, who are dismissive of her. The terminal attached to her Tranquility lounger in Vault 112 notes that several readouts show anomalous readings as follows:

Lounger Monitor:
DISPLAY RESIDENT STATUS
• Pulse: 80 bpm
• BP: ERROR
• Temp: 00.0 F
• Respiratory Rate: 5/min
• WARNING: ANOMALY DETECTED

DISPLAY RESIDENT STRESS LEVEL
• Stress Level: Extreme
• WARNING: RESIDENT REQUIRES MEDICAL ATTENTION

chr_000244a1.summary: Martha Simpson is one of the inhabitants of Vault 112 trapped inside the Tranquility Lane virtual reality simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Resident 227 of Vault 112, Martha has been trapped with her fellow dwellers by Stanislaus Braun for over 200 years. Tormented to death an uncountable number of times, including the slow death by scurvy at the Toucan Lagoon, her latest role is that of a sexually frustrated housewife, pining for another woman's husband. The object of her desire is Roger Rockwell, married to Janet Rockwell. Martha is despised by Janet, who would kill her if she could find proof of her husband's infidelity.

The irony is that while there was some chemistry between Roger and Martha, Rockwell pushed her away and denied it, much to Martha's frustration. He wanted to keep his marriage intact. Janet noticed that chemistry too, but after a bitter fight in front of an open window earlier in the year, she finally believed Roger's word.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tranquility Lane: Martha Simpson is one of the residents one may have to kill if they choose to do all of Betty's tasks. She is also involved in one of Braun's tasks to creatively torment his prisoners: The player can choose to murder Martha with Janet's rolling pin, then pin the slaying on Janet, to break up their marriage.

chr_000244a0.summary: Roger Rockwell is one of the inhabitants of Vault 112 trapped within the Tranquility Lane virtual reality simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Resident 226 of Vault 112, Rockwell has been one of several people tortured by Stanislaus Braun for two centuries. His latest torment is less physical and more mental: Braun has placed him in the role of a husband married to a jealous wife, Janet Rockwell, suspecting him of infidelity and sleeping with Martha Simpson, their common neighbor. The irony is that while Martha did try flirting with Roger, and there was chemistry between them, Roger pushed her away. This did not stop his wife from tearing into him in a most vicious way, in front of an open window that made their frayed marriage public knowledge.

While Roger eventually managed to convince Janet that nothing was going on between them, few aside from Janet believe it. While they worked it out, or so they say, relations between the Rockwells remain strained.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tranquility Lane: Roger Rockwell is one of the residents one will have to kill if they choose to do all of Betty's tasks. During the task Betty gives the Lone Wanderer to break destroy the Rockwells' marriage, the player can convince Janet into thinking Roger is having an affair with Martha Simpson. Alternatively, one can take Janet's rolling pin and kill Martha with it then convince Roger that Janet killed Martha.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Janet is one of Vault 112's inhabitants, trapped in Tranquility Lane alongside her husband, Roger. She has an affinity for baking and gardening, as well as caring for her appearance with occasional trips to the salon. Janet has a vague memory of moving to the simulation's neighborhood, apart from commenting that it was Roger's choice though she cannot recall when the decision was made.

She has a dislike for Mabel Henderson, stemming from her being "a little too nosey" and questioning if the Lone Wanderer has been asked to pry into her marriage per Mabel's request; if Mabel is asked about the Rockwells' marriage, she states that an argument broke out a year prior where Janet accused her husband of cheating on her with Martha Simpson. As a result, she has been plotting various ways to kill her husband's alleged mistress.

chr_0002449e.summary: Pat Neusbaum is one of the inhabitants of Vault 112 and part of the Tranquility Lane virtual reality simulation, found.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The proud all-American wife of George Neusbaum and mother of Timmy, Pat is resident 375 of Vault 112, hooked up at lounger 37 for over 200 years. After numerous other simulations, she was finally placed by Stanislaus Braun, her tormentor, in the role of a shy housewife, fretting over her son, though unable to offer more than platitudes.

Old Lady Dithers tops her list of worries, as she considers her to be crazy and a potential bad influence on Timmy. However, rather than confront her directly, she wants her husband to break up any potential contact between the two. She also dislikes Mabel Henderson, the local gossip, particularly the way she sticks her nose in other people's business. George enjoys teasing her over it, in fact.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Resident ID 374 in lounger 37,

Here, George was brainwashed to be the head of the Neusbaum household, proud husband of Pat and father of Timmy, with an honorable discharge from the American military. Braun ensured some friction within the family: Timmy was set to be a weakling, easily tormented by Betty (Braun's form within the simulation), which led Neusbaum to consider sending his son to a military academy, where he'd be toughened up - enough to face the real world that would never come. The only thing that comes is torment at the hands of Braun, preying on Neusbaum's love and close relationship with his family, especially Timmy. In fact, the very mention of Betty is enough to shake him to the core, with George struggling to maintain his happy, carefree persona.

chr_000239d2.summary: Bill Seward is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 55 HP). Affiliated with Temple of the Union. Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Head of State, Lincoln Artifacts.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Bill had been a slave his entire life before running away from his master after having accidentally killed their daughter. Had the accident not occurred, he would never have attempted an escape. In the hours after the incident, Bill was found by Hannibal Hamlin, saving him from a fate of recapture or succumbing to a wasteland danger. Although he can be heard insulting the former, he has a particular affinity for the latter, praising Four Score for his unconditional love towards him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State: Bill Seward is one of the slaves the player can either help relocate to Lincoln Memorial or lead back into slavery.

sections.title: Inventory

chr_000239d1.summary: Alejandra Torres is a freedwoman working with Hannibal Hamlin as a teacher at the Temple of the Union.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Alejandra is a quiet woman of great intelligence. She was captured by slavers at 17 and sold into slavery. Her enslaver forced her to have sex, and seemed to like her well enough to provide her with an education, including the ability to read and write, history, mathematics and basic science. After he married, his new wife demanded that Alejandra be sold. After four years in captivity, Alejandra was sold again, this time to Hannibal Hamlin, who promptly returned her freedom.

A free person again at 21, Alejandra joined Hannibal, becoming the group's teacher, historian, and tinkerer. She helps educate the group, starting with basic literacy. Caleb Smith is one of her students, and would like nothing more than becoming someone more significant, but Alejandra maintains a professional distance.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State: Alejandra is the teacher at the Temple, and the player can choose to aid her in relocating to the Lincoln Memorial or enslave her again for Paradise Falls.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Simone was part of a mercenary crew before slavers took her. She was a slave for only seven months, feigning obedience and escaping as soon as the opportunity presented itself. As a former mercenary, she is very comfortable with weapons and fighting, and possesses the highest combat skill out of all of Hannibal's followers. She is a rough and tough person, with a total lack of respect for almost anyone except Hannibal.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

• Head of State: Before being allowed access to the Temple of the Union, the Lone Wanderer will have to get past the front gate. Simone will let them in.

chr_000239cf.summary: Caleb Smith is a runaway slave and member of the Abolitionists residing at the Temple of the Union in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born to enslaved parents in the Capital Wasteland around 2245,

Within the Abolitionists, Caleb was the first to become a follower of Hannibal and cemented his loyalty by offering his masonry skills to restore any stone structure his leader asked of him; once the Abolitionists began to idolize the "Great Emancipator" Abraham Lincoln, Caleb had the dream to one day put his tools to work restoring the statue of Lincoln situated within the Lincoln Memorial, most importantly by reattaching the decapitated head being kept in the Temple.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Caleb can always be found at the Temple of the Union, working on a stone slab containing an old, faded inscription from the Lincoln Memorial that he's trying to restore.

If the Lone Wanderer completes Head of State by helping the Abolitionists clear out the Lincoln Memorial so they can move in, he will relocate there and reside at his tent for the rest of the game.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State: Caleb needs a picture of the Lincoln Memorial to further his efforts of reconstructing the statue. In addition, he can provide information about the Temple of the Union, himself, or the Lincoln Memorial once the proper stage of the quest has been reached.

chr_000239ce.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, dialogue, find, guard, travel
chr_000239ce.summary: Leroy Walker is a slaver from Paradise Falls residing in the Lincoln Memorial in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A firm believer in the rule of the strong over the weak, Leroy is unique among other slavers in that he does not concern himself with the profits made from conducting slavery. Instead, he believes that the transaction of human beings is simply natural law being put into practice, and takes pride in his role as a slave catcher, chasing down runaways in the wasteland.

During his attempts to recover runaways and return them to Paradise Falls, Leroy became interested in the activities of Hannibal Hamlin and the Abolitionists, and discovered their base at the Temple of the Union. In his eyes, were the Abolitionists to succeed in their mission to reclaim the Lincoln Memorial and make it into a bastion for all runaway slaves in the Capital Wasteland, Paradise Falls and the slavers will be severely hurt.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Leroy can usually be found in the operations office on the first floor of the Memorial, through the door to the left of the front steps.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State: Leroy and the slavers have laid claim to the Lincoln Memorial and won't leave easily. If notified of the slaver threat, Hannibal will ask the player character to deal with them however they see fit. Alternately, they can side with Leroy against the Abolitionists.
• Lincoln's Profit Margins: Leroy offers the player character the opportunity to locate various items related to Abraham Lincoln in the Museum of History and will pay caps for any item returned to him.

chr_000239cd.role: Temple of the Union — African American
chr_000239cd.summary: Hannibal Hamlin is the founder and leader of the Abolitionists, a militant anti-slavery organization residing in the Temple of the Union in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. A former slave himself, he is committed to freeing all slaves and defeating the institution of slavery at Paradise Falls.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: When he was around 14 years old, Hannibal Hamlin's life changed forever when he was enslaved and ended up as a servant to an unnamed man. Sometime around 2271, however, Hannibal managed to escape from his master, who has been hunting him for recapture ever since. As an escaped slave, Hamlin knew that he would continually be plagued by slavers looking to put him back in shackles. By coincidence, sometime in 2274, he found shelter in a crumbling ruin that he discovered contained the severed stone head of Abraham Lincoln's statue from the Lincoln Memorial, as well as a block with part of its inscription. After learning more about Lincoln's history, including his role in giving the Emancipation Proclamation to free all slaves, Hannibal took this finding as a sign that he was destined to oppose the institution of post-War slavery.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State: The Lone Wanderer can meet Hannibal and his Abolitionists at the Temple of the Union, where the escaped slave leader asks them to help his group relocate to the Lincoln Memorial by clearing it of hostiles.
• Lincoln's Profit Margins: Hannibal is one of the three available options to sell Lincoln-related artifacts obtained from the Museum of History, the other two being Leroy Walker and Abraham Washington.

Other interactions:
• With the Contract Killer perk, one will be able to obtain an ear upon killing him that can be turned in to Littlehorn & Associates.

Speeches:
Abraham Lincoln biography

The Gettysburg Address

chr_00019938.summary: Initiate Pek is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Office Building. Directly connected to quests: DC Ruins Exploration.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Initiate Pek is young, inexperienced, and very headstrong. He recently took part in a long-range recon mission to Falls Church alongside Paladin Hoss, Knight Church, and an unnamed paladin, which was also meant to double as a training exercise for the young initiate to gain experience. Although the group believed that the district would be clear, as long-range recon is typically performed in areas that have already been secured, they were instead set upon and attacked by a group of super mutants.

By the time the Lone Wanderer arrives in Falls Church, Hoss and the other paladin are continuing to fight the super mutants outside, while Pek is still trapped in the office building.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Pek has a strong relationship with Paladin Hoss, as he was confident that Hoss would not leave him behind after they were separated. Pek is also very much in love with Sentinel Sarah Lyons, but, although she secretly finds him amusing, she is annoyed by his behavior on a professional level and requested that he be sent to operate in a different area of the city.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Lost Initiate: The Lone Wanderer must free Pek from the office building where he is trapped.

Effects of player's actions:
• Hoss and Pek will follow the Lone Wanderer around Falls Church (and even to other places) if one does not accept caps as a reward. If Hoss is killed, Pek will spawn dead in the closet, with the door locked (Very Hard).

chr_0001558e.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: follow, travel, patrol
chr_0001558e.summary: Paladins are a rank of the Brotherhood of Steel, reserved for the organization's elite members who have proven themselves as seasoned warriors and battlefield commanders.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Paladins are the protectors of the Brotherhood, considered to be their elite fighting force. Achieving the rank of paladin typically means the bearer is a highly trained combat veteran with extensive battlefield experience, marking them as a capable leader that completes the missions given to them and their subordinates dutifully. Due to the great responsibility that comes with their rank, paladins are often afforded the best equipment at the Brotherhood's disposal, such as power armor and advanced weaponry. They are trusted with maintaining the security of the Brotherhood's operations in their territory, being the first line of defense against enemies both inside and outside the organization.

sections.title: Ranks
sections.text:
Head paladin:
The head paladin is the overall commander of the paladins, responsible for implementing the elder's combat plans, enforcing Brotherhood laws and discipline on top of overseeing the overall training regime. They are a veteran soldier and are required to periodically convene with other caste heads and the elders.

Notable members:
• John Maxson, Lost Hills (promoted to elder by 2161)
• Head Paladin Rhombus, Lost Hills, 2161
• Head Paladin Lindquist (succeeded Kenneth Jones as elder)
• Head Paladin Edgar Hardin, Mojave, 2281

Star paladin:
Star paladins are only answerable to their elder and are given a wide authority to do what they see fit to accomplish their objectives.

The Midwest chapter renamed the position to paladin lord, but kept it identical in practice (being one step below the general/elder).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Paladin Hoss has taken on the job of conducting training exercises in the field with some of the Brotherhood's initiates, something that he hates almost as much as cleaning the latrines at the Citadel. He recently took part in a long-range recon mission to Falls Church alongside Initiate Pek, Knight Church, and an unnamed paladin, which was also meant to double as a training exercise for the initiate. Although the group believed that the district would be clear, as long-range recon is typically performed in areas that have already been secured, they were instead set upon and attacked by a group of super mutants. Since that initial strike, Hoss and the other paladin have been continuing to fight the super mutants in the neighborhood by themselves.

Knight Church has been killed in the initial attack and Initiate Pek is trapped in an office building, while Paladin Hoss and the other paladin are fighting nearby.

chr_0002248b.summary: Three Dog is the radio host, DJ, and news anchor for Galaxy News Radio, operating from the old GNR station within the ruins of Washington, D.C. in 2277. With the protection of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel, Three Dog keeps his listeners up to date on current events in the Capital Wasteland with his color commentary and entertained with music tracks.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Three Dog's parents were members of a traveling theater group. He grew up on the sounds of pre-War rock music and his parents teaching him about "the haters" and their propaganda, resulting in a mistrust for those making big promises with nothing to back them up, and deep-seated resentment for the government that he holds responsible for the Great War despite being born well after the lifetime of the United States. Contrasting his hatred, Three Dog fully believes in the personal right to free speech and the tenets of communal law.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Three Dog remains inside the GNR building throughout the entire game, wandering from room to room.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: The Lone Wanderer finds their way to the surrounding area of the GNR building trying to find their father and has to ask Three Dog for information. Passing a Speech challenge will give immediate information about the Lone Wanderer's father.
• Should Three Dog die before completing Galaxy News Radio and learning about Rivet City, this will trigger the unmarked quest The Search Continues.
• Galaxy News Radio: Failing or ignoring the Speech check during the above quest results in Three Dog demanding a favor in exchange for his information and sends them to get new equipment for his radio station.

chr_000210ed.summary: Brotherhood of Steel Scribe is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 60 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel (Scribes), Citadel Residents, Brotherhood of Steel. Found primarily around Citadel - B Ring.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
There are three major scribe orders; each order is headed by a high scribe (proctor), designated by the head scribe.

• is responsible for weapons research and development. Guns, ammunition anything of an offensive nature. Once the Enclave exposes themselves to the Capital Wasteland by capturing Project Purity, the scribes come to realize just how technologically advanced the Enclave is compared to the Brotherhood as a whole. They are both excited at the prospect of analyzing new technology, particularly the Vertibirds, and frustrated at their lack of technological development. If interrupted, they will direct the Lone Wanderer to Scribe Jameson, or Elder Lyons when their situation develops. When the Brotherhood is ready to take the fight to the Enclave, they will express patriotic fervor for their victory.

• Take it Back!: These scribes will be enthusiastic about the upcoming fighting for Project Purity.
• The American Dream: These scribes will direct the Lone Wanderer to Elder Lyons in the main laboratory.

chr_0001f355.summary: Initiate Jennings is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Chevy Chase East.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Jennings, a Brotherhood of Steel initiate, was under the mentorship of Paladin Vargas, a member of the elite squad Lyons' Pride. Sometime after August 17, 2277, Jennings accompanied Lyons' Pride to back up the garrison at the GNR building plaza against a super mutant assault force. Despite the gravity of this situation, Paladin Vargas was supposed to ensure that Jennings could receive combat training while staying away from dangerous heavy combat areas in the ensuing Battle of GNR Plaza. However, in an oversight, Vargas failed to protect Jennings from a super mutant attack on his position. While he survived the initial onslaught, he later died from his wounds. Jennings' death would be confirmed by Paladin Vargas and the leader of Lyons' Pride, Sentinel Sarah Lyons.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: If the player character follows the quest objectives to find Galaxy News Radio, they will emerge from the Chevy Chase North metro station and soon encounter Lyons' Pride. Following Lyons' Pride will lead to an alley where Knight Captain Colvin is firing on some super mutants and Initiate Jennings is dead nearby. Jennings' inventory still contains his weapon and power armor, but his power armor helmet is removed and lying nearby, along with some energy cells.
• Jennings' corpse is disabled by the game once Following in His Footsteps is completed. This means that he will never appear if Scientific Pursuits was started before ever going to GNR, for example. Jennings' helmet will also be disabled if not collected.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
There are three major scribe orders; each order is headed by a high scribe (proctor), designated by the head scribe.

• is responsible for weapons research and development. Guns, ammunition anything of an offensive nature. Once the Enclave exposes themselves to the Capital Wasteland by capturing Project Purity, the scribes come to realize just how technologically advanced the Enclave is compared to the Brotherhood as a whole. They are both excited at the prospect of analyzing new technology, particularly the Vertibirds, and frustrated at their lack of technological development. If interrupted, they will direct the Lone Wanderer to Scribe Jameson, or Elder Lyons when their situation develops. When the Brotherhood is ready to take the fight to the Enclave, they will express patriotic fervor for their victory.

chr_0001e71a.summary: Knight Captain Durga is the Brotherhood of Steel quartermaster based out of the Citadel in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The Citadel's quartermaster, Knight Captain Durga is not entirely pleased with her position in the Brotherhood of Steel, and makes no attempt to hide it in her interactions. She is quick and curt with her responses, rushing the Lone Wanderer if they ask to peruse her wares, or responding with a bored "yeah, I suppose" to their request. Frustrated with both her role and the secluded location of the armory, she will sarcastically reply with "what else would I be doing back here?" if one asks to purchase gear from her. Instead, her preferences lie outside the Citadel, where she would rather be engaged in field operations and using the armory's weapons, not polishing and cataloging them as she does now.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She is located in the backroom of the armory in the Citadel laboratory. She never sleeps at any point of the day, even though a bed can clearly be seen behind her.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
One needs the permission of Elder Lyons to trade with her. After completing Take it Back!, this permission is no longer needed.

chr_00003a22.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: happy. AI packages: dialogue, ambush, sandbox, travel, guard
chr_00003a22.summary: Sydney is a mercenary who specializes in relic hunting in the year 2277, and a temporary companion.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sydney is a self-taught survivor, who braved the wasteland all on her own since the age of fourteen; her mother was raped and killed by raiders, While she believes she was abandoned, in reality, he was killed in a deal gone bad at the Statesman Hotel.

The skills he taught her, especially gunsmithing and reloading, served her well over the years. She learned to always be ready for a fight, to the point of sleeping with a gun under her pillow all the time, and perfected her combat skills, becoming a consummate freelance mercenary who specializes in hunting down pre-War treasures and relics. She enjoys high profile, dangerous jobs in particular, taking calculated risks to reach her goal.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• If she finishes the quest alive and makes it to Underworld.

Quests:
• Stealing Independence: Sydney is encountered in the Rotunda of the National Archives. She can become a temporary companion until the quest is completed.
• Bragging Rights: If the Lone Wanderer refuses to team up with Sydney or double-crosses her in the National Archives, she and her girlfriend Emaline will attack in a random encounter. Killing them will result in bad Karma.
• If Sydney remains alive at the end of the quest, she will travel from Rivet City to the Ninth Circle in Underworld and set up shop as a vendor, stating that she likes to hang out at Underworld because the ghouls do not constantly hit on her.

chr_000208f6.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, sleep
chr_000208f6.summary: Megaton settlers are the unnamed wastelanders who have settled, but do not officially reside, in the city of Megaton, in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Megaton's unusual immigration laws seem to have created a condition where a substantial portion of the population of the town is in this situation. Essentially, new visitors to the town seem to be approved individually by the sheriff/mayor, Lucas Simms. Meeting this approval allows one to remain inside the town's protective walls, but does not constitute citizenship. Non-citizens of the town are not permitted to own housing, and instead must either rent lodging at Moriarty's Saloon, or for the less transient settlers, space in the common house is shared communally.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the player character's Karma is at the "very good" level, once per day while in town, a Megaton settler will come and give them some gift, such as bottle caps (sometimes even only 1 cap), food, a stimpak, or ammunition. The settler can usually be found around the entrance of Megaton and can vary in clothing, as well as change equipment throughout the game.
• If the player character decides to destroy Megaton with the bomb located in the town's center, any surviving settlers (known as Megaton refugees) that the player character encounters will immediately become hostile towards them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Common House. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0002044f.role: Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents — African American
chr_0002044f.summary: Rivet City Security is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Bridge Tower. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Bridge Tower. Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform, Hangar Key.
