chr_0002029b.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, dialogue, guard, travel
chr_0002029b.summary: Paladins are a rank of the Brotherhood of Steel, reserved for the organization's elite members who have proven themselves as seasoned warriors and battlefield commanders.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Paladins are the protectors of the Brotherhood, considered to be their elite fighting force. Achieving the rank of paladin typically means the bearer is a highly trained combat veteran with extensive battlefield experience, marking them as a capable leader that completes the missions given to them and their subordinates dutifully. Due to the great responsibility that comes with their rank, paladins are often afforded the best equipment at the Brotherhood's disposal, such as power armor and advanced weaponry. They are trusted with maintaining the security of the Brotherhood's operations in their territory, being the first line of defense against enemies both inside and outside the organization.

sections.title: Ranks
sections.text:
Head paladin:
The head paladin is the overall commander of the paladins, responsible for implementing the elder's combat plans, enforcing Brotherhood laws and discipline on top of overseeing the overall training regime. They are a veteran soldier and are required to periodically convene with other caste heads and the elders.

Notable members:
• John Maxson, Lost Hills (promoted to elder by 2161)
• Head Paladin Rhombus, Lost Hills, 2161
• Head Paladin Lindquist (succeeded Kenneth Jones as elder)
• Head Paladin Edgar Hardin, Mojave, 2281

Star paladin:
Star paladins are only answerable to their elder and are given a wide authority to do what they see fit to accomplish their objectives.

The Midwest chapter renamed the position to paladin lord, but kept it identical in practice (being one step below the general/elder).

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Chevy Chase East. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_000200cd.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_000200cd.summary: Robert is a member of the Family as well as its sentry and doorman, protecting the entrance to the service tunnel connected to the Meresti Metro station where they reside in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2243, By 2277, Robert acts as their guardian against interlopers from the surface, hedging his talent with firearms to elect himself as their combat instructor, though only for the protection of the Family.

Due to his duties as the doorman, Robert spends much time separated from the cultish elements of the Family infused by Vance and does not profess them as much, even remarking negatively on having to memorize and orally recite the gang's guiding rules at will. This also means he is vulnerable to being bought for the right price in caps, even over the Family. Despite his concerns, Robert still supports Vance's mission to create a place where recovering cannibals can gather and be with people who share their struggles.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Robert stands behind a wall of sandbags within the Meresti Metro station, occasionally wandering the small area between the sandbags and the Family's headquarters.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: Robert guards the entrance to the Family's lair, and will either attack those trying to get through, or let them pass to see Vance. If Blood Ties was not started beforehand, Robert will not allow passage under any circumstances.

chr_000200c9.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_000200c9.summary: Justin is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 100 HP). Affiliated with The Family. Found primarily around Meresti Metro Station. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Since the age of fourteen, Justin has been a member of the Family, and is a great admirer of Vance, who saved him from an Enclave patrol of the wasteland. Justin is a strong believer in Vance's vampire stories and helps preach these stories to his fellow Family members. He is eager, headstrong, and very friendly to those he does not perceive as a threat. Justin feels a close bond with Ian West, a recent member of The Family, and it almost borders on love. He is often found spending time with Ian.

Justin mentions that if it were not for Vance, the guards at Rivet City would still be beating him.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: TheFamilyJustin), Justin is defined as a Caucasian in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Faction memberships: The Family. Appears in or relates to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 6, 100 HP. S.P.E.C.I.A.L. profile: STR 6, PER 7, END 5, CHA 3, INT 3, AGI 6, LCK 5. Behavioral traits: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, sandbox.

chr_000200c4.summary: Karl is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 95 HP). Affiliated with The Family. Found primarily around Meresti Metro Station. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Karl was married to a woman named Skyler and they lived together in Meresti before her death. They used to be shop owners in Megaton, and Vance encountered them while getting supplies. Vance felt a kinship with them and invited them to join him. Karl is gruff and has a short temper; he prefers others leave him alone. He is cynical, suspicious of others and thinks the worst of them.

Karl does not believe in Vance's vampiric teachings but plays the part in order to keep his store in the Meresti Metro Station.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: Investigate the people behind the murdering of Lucy West's family and the brahmin herd in Arefu.

sections.title: Store
sections.text:
• His store is open from 3 p.m. to 8 p.m. (unlike other stores, open from approximately 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.). He sometimes sells blood packs at the regular "junk item" price (base value 5), which can then be sold nearby to Vance for 15 caps (not subject to Barter). This is only possible if one has brokered a deal with Vance and Evan King of Arefu.
• Karl also has one of the biggest merchant inventories in Capital Wasteland. His inventory is located in a freezer near his desk.
• He stocks around twenty pieces of scrap metal at the start of the game.
• Unlike anyone else, Karl never runs out of stimpaks to sell.

chr_000200be.summary: Alan is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 100 HP). Affiliated with The Family. Found primarily around Meresti Metro Station. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A newer member of the Family, Alan was rescued by Vance after the former escaped from Paradise Falls and was wounded in the process. Alan does not partake in the dietary habits of the Family, but is being taught by Vance of The Family's ways.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Blood Ties: If the Lone Wanderer asks Vance to protect Arefu in exchange for blood packs, Alan is sent there as a guard. He stays in the abandoned residence at the entrance to Arefu next to the brahmin pen, which was originally blocked off.

chr_000200bb.summary: Brianna is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 100 HP). Affiliated with The Family. Found primarily around Meresti Metro Station. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
At 19 years of age, she is the youngest member of the Family. Originally a prostitute, her cannibalism caused her much torment in Washington, D.C. She set out into the wasteland and crossed paths with "vampires" in Meresti Metro station. Sensing her traits, Vance quickly took her in and as a result, Brianna's cannibalism was turned into hematophagy. Since then, she has been living in Meresti.

She gives the male members of the Family a little company at night. She can be heard flirting suggestively with Karl and Justin, much to Vance's embarrassment. He will often ask her to tone down her "morale" boosting and keep it to "one at a time."

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• During the quest Blood Ties, one can use the Lady Killer perk to seduce Brianna into giving them Ian's location and the password for the terminal that unlocks the door.

chr_0001ff12.summary: Mercenary is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 10, 120 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Craterside Supply. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mercenaries are guns for hire in the Capital Wasteland. Most are not known to be affiliated with any known mercenary group, but a few are known to be associated with Talon Company.

Only one character named as a mercenary is found alive, a mercenary hired as Moira Brown's guard inside Craterside Supply in Megaton. All other mercenaries are found dead, their bodies scattered throughout the wasteland in places such as Old Olney, Rock Creek caverns, and the deathclaw sanctuary.

Each mercenary found dead is typically equipped with leather armor in poor condition. Unlike many other NPCs, they can also be carrying a bobby pin.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:

• One south of MDPL-16 power station, at an Enclave post (After The Waters of Life).
• One in mirelurk nesting hole's main area in the south.

chr_0001f1cb.role: Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents — Caucasian
chr_0001f1cb.summary: Rivet City Security is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Bridge Tower. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Bridge Tower. Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform, Hangar Key.

chr_0001e7ae.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, follow, eat, find
chr_0001e7ae.summary: Armitage is a third generation synth bodyguard protecting Dr. Zimmer of the Synth Retention Bureau (who insists on calling him an android), during his mission to Rivet City in 2277. He appears.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Constructed in, the physically imposing Armitage is quiet, reserved, and utterly deadly to anyone who threatens his charge, and can blend in with normal human populations with ease. Although he is technically of the same class or generation as A3-21, the synth Zimmer is pursuing, A3-21 is a cutting-edge humanoid and the most advanced creation of the Institute - and Zimmer - at the time. Armitage is an older model and easily replaced, though perfectly capable of protecting Zimmer in the field. Together, they are slowly searching the massive derelict, deck by deck, in search of the escaped synth.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Armitage shares his schedule with Zimmer, shadowing him everywhere across the derelict after the player meets Zimmer in the Rivet City science lab and watches the cutscene. They will move from deck to deck, sweeping the area for A3-21, and retire to eat or drink in the evening. Once The Replicated Man is completed, Armitage disappears, one way or the other.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: As a bodyguard, Armitage will turn hostile if the Lone Wanderer decides to attack Dr. Zimmer.
• He can be killed with no loss of Karma, and killing him with Harkness' permission will not cause Rivet City's security to turn hostile toward the player character.
• If he is killed, one of only four android components in the game can be found on his body (of the other three, one is on Zimmer, one is given to the Lone Wanderer by Victoria Watts and one is on Pinkerton).
• Killing Zimmer before he tries to leave with Harkness in The Replicated Man quest will result in Armitage staying in the Rivet City market.

chr_0001e759.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sleep, follow, eat, sandbox
chr_0001e759.summary: Mister Lopez is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Midship Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mister Lopez is a quiet, lonely and severely depressed 65-year-old man. Raiders took the lives of his wife and child, and he came to Rivet City alone and lost. For the past decade, he has been living in the common room of Rivet City. He consumes his meals in the common room and often sleeps for long periods out of sheer depression. He has a daily habit of climbing to the top of the bridge tower and contemplating whether to end his life by jumping.

He regularly visits Saint Monica's Church and spends much of his time reading or praying there. Lopez also attends the weekly church service and receives frequent counseling from Father Clifford, the church priest.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: This character informs the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

• Suicide Watch: Lopez considers committing suicide due to the fact that no one remembers him or even cares about him (also learned by talking to him on the flight deck that he couldn't save his family), but he doesn't have the courage to do it himself. One can find him on the observation deck at the top of bridge tower every day from 8:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m., during this time he will simply tell the Lone Wanderer to "Just leave me alone." He will also go to the observation deck every day from 3:00 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. During this time, one can:
• Help him to commit suicide by pushing him off the deck (negative Karma).
• Talk him into committing suicide by saying he's pathetic (negative Karma).

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Midship Deck. Notable equipment & inventory: Pack of Cigarettes, Mister Lopez's Key, Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_0001e745.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sandbox, sleep
chr_0001e745.summary: Sister is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Upper Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, The Replicated Man.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
One of the least personable denizens of the City, the 29-year-old Sister is a beast of a man with an incredibly short fuse. Nobody knows where he got the nickname from, and even fewer manage to walk away if they make the mistake of asking him about it. Despite numerous altercations with other citizens, he managed to avoid getting thrown off by Harkness and Lana Danvers.

Sister is well-known among the citizens of Rivet City as a murderous sociopath and most steer clear of him. The mystery of his stay at the Weatherly Hotel drives Mei Wong to anxiety, as she recognized him as a Paradise Falls slaver and is afraid that he might be coming for her. However, Sister is after a much greater prize. He was sent to Rivet City by Eulogy Jones to be the slavers' eyes and ears inside the city, to find and secure a runaway synth, A3-21.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Sister's room contains a recording of the android. He can also be interrogated about his mission in Rivet City, which may require passing a Speech check, or Evil or Very Evil Karma.
• Slave Hunt: The player can learn that Mei Wong is a freedwoman who took shelter at Rivet City and is deathly afraid of Sister, correctly identifying him as a slaver. It is up to the player to decide how to handle her case. They can report her to Sister or remove the slaver.

Other interactions:
• Sister has little to say outside the quests. Asking about his name will not cause him to attack, but it can potentially lock out the Slave Hunt resolution if his attitude towards the player character drops too low.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Upper Deck. Notable equipment & inventory: Sister's Key, Brahmin-Skin Outfit.

chr_0001e379.summary: Chief Gustavo is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 12, 90 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Prior to becoming security chief of Tenpenny Tower, Gustavo worked his way up to become leader of a mercenary band of professional fighters. Mister Burke was rescued by Gustavo and his band, and quickly hired him and his men to form the security force at the Tower. His personality is gruff, but also good natured in a "Don't give me grief, I'm just doing my job, ma'am" sort of manner. However, he soon becomes a loud no-nonsense hard-ass when his team or his charges are in immediate danger. He is particularly hostile to ghouls. "The only good ghoul is a dead ghoul," is a fond saying of his, particularly if ghouls are nearby. He expressed that "it's only a matter of time before they go zombie" and people shouldn't take the risk. He even goes as far to say that you would be doing them a favor by putting a bullet between their eyes.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: After the Lone Wanderer's first encounter with Gustavo, he is found sitting in the lobby of the hotel or sleeping outside during the night, most of the time he will stand guard at the entrance.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: Gustavo will task the Wanderer with getting rid of the ghoul menace if asked.

chr_0001dc19.summary: Michael Masters is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 60 HP). Affiliated with Warrington Station Ghouls. Found primarily around Warrington Station. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Prior to the bombs dropping, Michael was a renowned and highly intelligent electronic and biological engineer who had a focus in human mutation experiments. After being inspired by the works of German, Russian, and Chinese doctors, he began breeding super-warriors in an attempt to keep America at the forefront of such scientific advancements. He acknowledges that individuals were hurt as a result of the experimentation but also points out progress was being made. Despite remarking how the experiments were yielding great results, he views his ghoulification as a "karmic curse" for them and remains bitter at his transformation, albeit appreciates the added longevity.

He also mentions that he used to vacation in Tenpenny Tower prior to the war, and finds irony in now having to fight his way in.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: Upon first meeting Michael, he will try to make the Lone Wanderer go back the way they came, eventually leading them to Roy Phillips if they insist.

Effects of player's actions:
• If one completes the Tenpenny Tower quest by convincing the other residents to let the ghouls in, Michael will have a shop and will sell random guns, ammunition, and other items with a nice discount.
• If one chooses to kill Roy Phillips after the ghouls move into Tenpenny Tower, even if done silently with no observers, Michael Masters will turn hostile and further trading with him becomes impossible.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Warrington Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Motorcycle Helmet, Wasteland Settler Outfit. Provides services: Weapons, Armor, Books & Schematics, Chems & Medicine.

chr_0001dc18.summary: Bessie Lynn is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents, Warrington Station Ghouls. Found primarily around Warrington Station. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Bessie is a timid and nervous woman who consistently defers to her boyfriend Roy Phillips in all matters, stemming from her self-consciousness at having become a ghoul. Although she has accepted her new physical state, she mentions how she once was pretty and adored by many, and how her ghoulification has put an end to such things. If she is allowed into Tenpenny Tower, she appears to be unaware of what Roy Phillips did to the previous inhabitants and subsequently, the Lone Wanderer may inform her of their fates. If the Lone Wanderer has not yet completed the Tenpenny Tower quest, Bessie can be found in the living quarters of Warrington station.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Bessie Lynn is in a relationship with Roy Phillips and lives together with him and Michael Masters deep inside of Warrington station.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• Only if the Tenpenny Tower quest is completed by allowing the ghouls to live in the tower.

Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: If it is chosen to kill all of the ghouls, Bessie Lynn is one of the targets that needs to be eliminated.

Effects of player's actions:
If the Lone Wanderer has completed the Tenpenny Tower quest by letting the ghouls in, she will take over the New Urban Apparel store, and can be found there from then on out.

chr_0001d7b0.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, patrol, sandbox, eat
chr_0001d7b0.summary: Roy Phillips is a ghoul revolutionary leading a small group of other ghoul dissidents from an old subway station in the Warrington tunnels in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
One of the oldest ghouls in the wasteland, Roy Phillips is originally from the pre-War era, where he served as a police officer. Even then, he was notorious for his bad temper, no-nonsense demeanor, and solidly black-and-white worldview; none of this has diminished since starting his new life as a ghoul. While he has long accepted his mutated status, Roy conversely has zero patience to spare when dealing with the hatred and bigotry of smoothskin humans, firmly demanding his kind be treated with respect, though he does not extend his courtesy to the crazed feral ghouls.

At some point, Roy met and interacted with Sanders.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: Speaking to Roy in the Warrington tunnels is one of two options for starting the quest.

Effects of player's actions:
• Roy's fate and place of residence are dependent on the player character's choices during the quest Tenpenny Tower:
• If one sides with the ghouls and unleashes the feral ghoul horde into the tower, it is possible for Tenpenny's security to kill Roy in combat.
• If one chooses the negotiation route and convinces the tower residents to allow the ghouls inside, after a few in-game days, the ghouls will massacre nearly all of the human residents, including Allistair Tenpenny, Herbert Dashwood, and the security personnel (but excluding Mister Burke and Shakes), then take up permanent residence there. This will occur off-screen.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Warrington Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Brahmin-Skin Outfit, Leather Armor.

chr_0001d036.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, follow, travel, eat, sleep
chr_0001d036.role: Rivet City Residents, Dr. Li's Research Team — Hispanic
chr_0001d036.summary: Garza is a citizen of Rivet City and general laborer for Doctor Madison Li's science team in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born around 2247, Garza is a physically imposing and very reserved man. His past is a mystery to others in Rivet City, and he refuses to talk about it with anyone. In fact, he would prefer not to talk at all, and tends to limit his speech to as few words as necessary. Since then, he has been working for Doctor Li as a general laborer in the Rivet City science lab, moving heavy equipment for her, helping maintain the hydroponic gardens for Janice Kaplinski, storing newly-received shipments, and providing general assistance to Henry Young. Rivet City's working people often ask him about the doctor's work, though he has little to say about it, true to character.

Garza spends his free time working out on the Rivet City flight deck.

sections.title: Schedule
sections.text:
The following is Garza's intended daily schedule in Rivet City. His home room is on the ground floor of the Rivet City science lab, and he will try to stay there at any time that he does not have other activities in his schedule.
• 5 to 7 a.m.: Garza wakes up and idles in his room.
• 7 to 9 a.m.: Garza eats in his room.
• 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.: Garza sandboxes around the science lab, interacting with the other NPCs.
• 5 to 7 p.m.: Garza goes out to the flight deck and wanders around.
• 7 to 9 p.m.: Garza goes back to his room to eat.
• 9 to 11 p.m.: Garza goes back outside to the flight deck.
• 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.: Garza goes back to his room and goes to sleep.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Waters of Life: Provided Garza is alive when this quest begins, he will join the Project Purity team and head to the Jefferson Memorial to help Doctor Li restart the project. He does not necessarily believe in the project, but he believes Dr. Li will make it work and wishes to help her in any way possible. He is somewhat unnerved by the super mutants infesting the memorial, cautioning that they previously overwhelmed the Brotherhood of Steel garrison there, but is thankful to the Lone Wanderer for helping to ensure their safety. After the memorial is cleared, Garza will work inside it until the Enclave attacks, and will flee with Doctor Li, Alex Dargon, and Daniel Agincourt through the Taft Tunnel. He can be asked to help fight against the Enclave soldiers, but he will be unable to, saying that he is not feeling well.

chr_0001d02a.behavior: Unaggressive, cautious; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, eat
chr_0001d02a.summary: Pepper Gomez is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security. Found primarily around Vault 101 Lower Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Pepper is the wife of Herman Gomez and the mother of Freddie Gomez. Freddie was the result of an unplanned pregnancy, and Pepper expressed panic upon learning she was pregnant. Pepper is best friends with Beatrice Armstrong, and is also cordial with Stanley Armstrong.

While her husband works with Vault 101 security, Pepper has raised Freddie largely on her own for much of his life. Although she has tried her best to raise him well, she has felt hopeless due to his behavioral issues. Freddie has suffered from Vault depressive syndrome since early childhood, and he has coped with his issues by acting out as a bully. This has earned him the validation of the Tunnel Snakes gang under the leadership of Butch DeLoria, and they have more influence over Freddie than Pepper does.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Trouble on the Homefront: She is encountered in the living quarters during the Lone Wanderer's visit.

Effects of player's actions:
Should the Lone Wanderer choose to destroy Vault 101 in Trouble on the Homefront, a random encounter is enabled in which the player finds the corpses of the Gomez family, with a different individual each time the encounter triggers. In order, the bodies of Freddie, Pepper, and Herman appear in this encounter (provided they survived to the point of the Vault's evacuation), potentially near a random wasteland creature. Once all possible corpses have been discovered, the encounter does not trigger again.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Lower Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Vault 101 Jumpsuit, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_0001d019.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: find, dialogue, travel
chr_0001d019.summary: Freddie Gomez is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Future Imperfect.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The son of Herman and Pepper Gomez, Freddie was the result of an unplanned pregnancy. At just nine years old, Freddie was diagnosed with Vault depressive syndrome, which was considered highly unusual for someone of his age. Freddie's condition was known to some residents of the Vault by 2268;

As Freddie grew older, Vault 101's physician, James, noted that his depressive condition was worsening. Freddie showed signs of lethargy, anxiety, and low self-esteem. On many days, Freddie was unable to get out of bed in the morning; meanwhile, on days he was able to function, Freddie would mask his issues by acting out as a bully. Vault-Tec protocols dictated that James prescribe chlorpromazine for Freddie, but James worried that Freddie might become permanently dependent on the medication.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Freddie Gomez is one of the Lone Wanderer's classmates taking the G.O.A.T. at the same time. At the end of the G.O.A.T. exam, Freddie is the only person who has not submitted his exam to Mr. Brotch. He can be heard struggling on the last question, even though the only choice is "overseer."
• Trouble on the Homefront: Freddie is part of the Tunnel Snakes in this quest, and is one of the more hesitant members of the Vault rebels. If one chooses to sabotage the vault, Freddie and the other residents will flee into the wasteland.

Effects of player's actions:
Should the Lone Wanderer choose to destroy Vault 101 in Trouble on the Homefront, a random encounter is enabled in which the player finds the corpses of the Gomez family, with a different individual each time the encounter triggers.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8, itm_000425ba.

chr_0001cfdd.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, find
chr_0001cfdd.summary: Susie Mack is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Future Imperfect.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Susie is the daughter of Allen and Gloria Mack, and the younger sister of both Stevie and Wally. Growing up, Susie despises the Tunnel Snakes, of which her brother Wally is a member. However, Wally does not give Susie a hard time, as she has something of a mean streak in her teenage years. When taking the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, Susie has no respect for the Lone Wanderer, and aggressively shuns any attempt from them to even speak with her. Prior to the test, she engages in small talk with Freddie Gomez, on whom she secretly has a crush. After the test, Mr. Brotch informs Susie that she is headed for a teaching career, sarcastically surmising this must be due to her "gift" for communication. Susie is unsurprised by and somewhat apathetic of the results.

By 2277, Susie has become more mature and thoughtful.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Susie Mack is one of the Lone Wanderer's classmates taking the G.O.A.T. at the same time.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Susie Mack sides with Amata's rebels during the crisis.

Effects of player's actions:
Out of the Vault: If the Lone Wanderer resolves Trouble on the Homefront in the rebels' favor, Susie can be randomly encountered alive in the wasteland, during which she will explain that some order has been restored to Vault 101.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_0001cfd8.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: eat, sandbox
chr_0001cfd8.role: Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security — Caucasian Elderly
chr_0001cfd8.summary: Stanley is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security. Found primarily around Vault 101 Lower Level. Directly connected to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sweet, always worried and not very bright, Stanley is the father of Beatrice, Mary and Gloria. Stanley and Andy are responsible for keeping the vault running, tending to all the machinery and acting as its janitors.

2260s:
On July 12, 2268, Stanley repairs the water purifier. This repair is a point of discussion between himself and Amata Almodovar when they engage in small talk the next day.

On that same day, Stanley performs routine maintenance on the pipes in the corridor outside the cafeteria. Midway through his work, he attends the birthday party of the Lone Wanderer. Though the Overseer presents the Pip-Boy 3000A to the Lone Wanderer, it is Stanley who selects the model. Though he admits that some might find the 3000A basic, Stanley believes the series is very reliable.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Stanley is the father of Beatrice Armstrong, Gloria, and Mary. Stanley's constant companion is Andy, a Mister Handy robot, that aids his human friend in cleaning and maintaining the vault. Stanley is friendly with the vault physician James and his child. In fact, during Escape!, he allows the Lone Wanderer to get past him without denouncing them to the vault's security, out of appreciation. However, he still says "Good riddance, get out" when the Lone Wanderer is exiled out of the vault after Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: He asks the Lone Wanderer about what they think about their new Pip-Boy 3000 which he fixed, and also gives a child's baseball cap.
• Future Imperfect: Stanley can be interacted with while he suffers from an illness.
• Trouble on the Homefront: He holds the password to the terminal used to sabotage Vault 101. It can either be pickpocketed from him, or it can be looted from him if he is to be killed.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer chooses to sabotage the Vault during Trouble on the Homefront, he may be killed by the explosion.

Other interactions:
• During the Lone Wanderer's escape at age 19, Stanley is encountered struggling against radroaches outside of the infirmary, but he is most likely saved by the arrival of Officer Gomez and Andy.

chr_0001cfbf.role: Vault 101 Residents, Vault 101 Security — Asian Elderly
chr_0001cfbf.summary: Beatrice Armstrong (simply Beatrice in the game) is a resident of Vault 101 and a minor character. She is encountered during Growing Up Fast and later found dead during Trouble on the Homefront, in James' former office in the clinic.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An eccentric, airheaded dweller of Vault 101, Beatrice is one of the daughters of Stanley Armstrong, and the only one among them not to have a husband (although she is interested in Edwin Brotch, the Vault's resident teacher). Unlike her sisters, Mary Kendall and Gloria Mack, she has ample free time away from her family, which she spends snooping into the lives of other residents and gossiping to her sisters and her best friend, Pepper Gomez. She also dabbles in tarot readings and poetry as hobbies, often writing commemorative poems for special events such as Founder's Day and resident birthdays. Despite her friendly demeanor, many of her neighbors find her attitude insufferable and condescending, particularly the Vault's children.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Beatrice is one of the guests at the Lone Wanderer's birthday party. She will give the Lone Wanderer a poem for their tenth birthday party.
• If the player does not interact with Beatrice, she will continue to follow the Lone Wanderer throughout the Vault, even onto the reactor level.

Other interactions:
• Beatrice is found dead during Trouble on the Homefront. Despite complaining of a sprained toe, Andy amputated her right leg (incorrectly stating that he took off the left one).

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101 Lower Level. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Vault 101 Jumpsuit, itm_000236d8.

chr_0001cfbc.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sandbox
chr_0001cfbc.summary: Jonas is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Future Imperfect.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Good-humored, smart, and kind, Jonas has been James' assistant as well as his and the Lone Wanderer's friend for as long as the Lone Wanderer can remember. He can appear stern and strict if he wants to, but even there, his sense of humor asserts itself.

In the late 2260s, Jonas was appointed to be James' assistant by the overseer, who hoped he would be a voice of reason. Jonas and James forged a friendship very quickly and together, they worked at examining and treating patients, as well as conducting routine experiments, testing the health of the vault. For an unknown length of time, James deliberately kept his assistant in the dark about covert experiments aimed at reviving Project Purity.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Jonas is first encountered during the Lone Wanderer's 10th birthday when James takes the Lone Wanderer down to the generator room to give them a present (a BB gun). Jonas later takes a picture of the two.
• Future Imperfect: Jonas is encountered upon opening the office door, telling the Lone Wanderer good morning and good luck on the G.O.A.T.
• Escape!: The Note from dad holotape can be taken from Jonas' body, containing a message pertaining to James' escape.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Eyeglasses, itm_000236d8, itm_0001cbdc.

chr_0001cfb7.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue
chr_0001cfb7.summary: Mr. Brotch is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Future Imperfect.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mister Brotch inherited the position of a schoolteacher from his father and grandfather. Since the day the Vault 101 residents entered the vault, there has been a Brotch as a schoolteacher. Mr. Brotch is concerned about carrying on that tradition, but with no children of his own, he is beginning to worry that he will be the last in line. He is the man responsible for administering the G.O.A.T. exams. He once modified a utility jumpsuit to improve his odds of survival in the wastes, in case that he would ever have to leave the vault.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: In the Lone Wanderer's youth, Edwin can be found in the classroom. During the Trouble on the Homefront quest, he can be found in the Vault 101 jail cell. If he is released, he will join the rebels in the vault's clinic.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Future Imperfect: Brotch administers the G.O.A.T.
• Trouble on the Homefront: Brotch has been imprisoned due to his loyalty to Amata Almodovar during the rebellion.

chr_0001ce38.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, travel, use item
chr_0001ce38.summary: James, also known as Dad, is the father of the Lone Wanderer and Vault 101's physician.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Project Purity:
James was always an inquisitive, meticulous and determined man; this personality led him to form or join a group of like-minded scientists, who were set on changing the wasteland for the better. Before the Lone Wanderer was born, James led an ambitious scientific endeavor known as Project Purity. He and his group of scientists, including wife Catherine and Dr. Madison Li, aimed to build an advanced water purifier within the ruins of the Jefferson Memorial, which would serve to purify the water of the Potomac. The project began to lose momentum, lacking concrete results while having to compensate for lost time due to super mutant attacks. The number of mutants was steadily increasing, and protecting the project was becoming increasingly difficult for the Brotherhood.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Related quests:
• Baby Steps: James puts the one-year-old Lone Wanderer in a playpen in their room which contains the You're S.P.E.C.I.A.L.! book. After a brief absence, James returns and shows the child their mother's favorite Bible quotation, and takes his child to see Amata.
• Growing Up Fast: James has a small conversation with the Lone Wanderer at the beginning of their tenth birthday party, and later in the party gives them a BB gun as a birthday gift, and tasks them with killing a radroach.
• Future Imperfect: James has a brief conversation with his now 16-year-old before their G.O.A.T. exam.
• Escape!: James' unexpected absence from Vault 101 prompts a security crisis and propels the Lone Wanderer out into the wastes.
• Following in His Footsteps: The Lone Wanderer searches for their dad.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
1 Only while in Vault 101.
2 On his way back to Rivet City.

chr_0001ce2a.summary: Wally Mack is a resident of Vault 101 in 2277 and is a member of a greaser gang called the Tunnel Snakes.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wally is the son of Allen and Gloria Mack. Wally's siblings are Stevie and Susie.

Wally is the brains of the Tunnel Snakes. Butch DeLoria and Paul Hannon Jr. are Wally's friends and fellow gang members. During their formative years, the Tunnel Snakes harassed other students in Vault 101, even being bold enough to taunt the overseer's daughter, Amata Almodovar. Butch presumes to be the leader of the Tunnel Snakes, but Wally might disagree if challenged.

He does not talk as much as the others, but they listen to what he has to say when he does say something. He is one of the Lone Wanderer's peers in Vault 101 and is encountered throughout the Lone Wanderer's youth inside Vault 101.

By 2287, Mack had traveled to the Commonwealth, where he reestablished the Tunnel Snakes under his rule.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tunnel Snakes Rule!: Wally Mack (as a glowing one) must be eliminated in Fens Way station.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Pip-Boy Glove, Tunnel Snake Outfit, itm_000236d8.

chr_0001ce28.summary: Paul Hannon is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Vault 101 Residents. Found primarily around Vault 101. Directly connected to quests: Future Imperfect.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is the only child of Paul Hannon Sr. and Vikki Hannon. Butch DeLoria, Freddie Gomez, and Wally Mack are his friends and fellow gang members.

The other Tunnel Snakes sometimes tease him because of his father being the chief of security in Vault 101, but this also gives him a certain cachet among his friends, though.

2260s:
On July 13, 2268, Paul attends the Lone Wanderer's tenth birthday party. In a conversation with the Lone Wanderer, Paul expresses his disappointment that he did not have a Pip-Boy 3000 yet. and they will start teasing him about "having a crush" on you (if the player character is a female), or about him being your "friend" (if the player character is male), which will then cause him to call you a "dorkface" so he could keep up his appeal with the other boys.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast
• Future Imperfect

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vault 101. Notable equipment & inventory: Tunnel Snake Outfit, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_000236d8.

chr_0001ce26.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, find
chr_0001ce26.summary: Butch DeLoria is a resident of Vault 101 and the leader and co-founder of the Tunnel Snakes gang in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born and raised in Vault 101 all his life and being under the care of his mother Ellen, a notorious alcoholic who neglected to oversee her son's negative maturing, Butch has been forced to put on a mask as a boorish, overbearing bully to cover up his deep-seated feelings of inadequacy due to not knowing his father despite living in a Vault with a close-knit community.

On July 13, 2268, when he was ten years old, During the party, Butch held a small meeting with his only two friends, Wally Mack and Paul Hannon Jr., to toss around ideas for a name for their gang, which later would be decided to be the "Tunnel Snakes" while rejecting other names such as "Vault Dwellers." He also attempted to strongarm the Wanderer into giving up the sweetroll they got from Lucy Palmer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Butch becomes non-essential during Escape! and he can optionally be killed before leaving Vault 101, preventing him from appearing during Trouble on the Homefront and becoming a companion later.
• If Trouble on the Homefront was completed by either opening or destroying Vault 101, and Butch was left alive, he can be found residing in the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. He can be recruited as a companion only while the player character has Neutral Karma.

Companion:
• Butch can give the Lone Wanderer a haircut during Trouble on the Homefront, and if recruited as a companion, also at any time during their travels.
• If separated from the player character, Butch will return to the Muddy Rudder.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Items will be replaced by a non-player switchblade and 10mm pistol, if no replacement weapons are left in Butch's inventory while he is a companion.

chr_0001ce24.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, dialogue, find, travel
chr_0001ce24.summary: Amata Almodovar is a resident of Vault 101, the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar, and a major character. Along with Owyn Lyons and Sarah Lyons, she is one of only three characters in the game to have "Very Good" Karma.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only daughter of the overseer, Amata is around the Lone Wanderer's age and the two grew up together ever since James arrived in the Vault with his child in tow. They bonded over many things, from Grognak the Barbarian to being raised by single fathers after their mothers passed away at a young age: Amata lost her mother at two, leaving her father, the overseer, to raise her on his own. The burden of leading the Vault and enforcing his isolationist policy slowly drove Amata and Alphonse apart, despite her deep love for her father and an innate sense of loyalty.

The bond between Amata and the Lone Wanderer developed into a deep friendship over the years, with the two becoming inseparable, best friends. Another was that he simply didn't like the Lone Wanderer, in part due to their father's stubborn, insubordinate personality.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Amata organizes the Lone Wanderer's birthday party on July 13, 2268, gifting them an intact copy of the 14th issue of Grognak the Barbarian, and demonstrating some of the reactivity of the game.
• Future Imperfect: Amata takes the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, together with the Lone Wanderer. Before entering the class room, she is harassed by the Tunnel Snakes, allowing the player to experiment with various approaches to resolving quests and introducing them to the Karma system.
• Escape!: Amata awakens the Lone Wanderer with news of James' escape from the vault. She offers a gun and outlines a plan for the Lone Wanderer's own escape. Toward the end of the quest, it turns out that she was captured and is interrogated by her father and Officer Mack.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only if she was told to keep the pistol during "Escape!"

chr_0001cca3.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, travel, follow
chr_0001cca3.summary: Alex Dargon is a botanist, and member of Doctor Madison Li's science team. He is found at Project Purity after it's restored, then at The Citadel after The Waters of Life, and back at the purifier.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Alex grew up in Rivet City and was always interested in what the scientists were doing there. Doctor Madison Li took him under her tutelage, and taught him everything he knows. Alex is the team's botanist whose specialty is in growing naturally occurring foodstuffs. Friendly and well-liked, if overzealous, he was entrusted with overseeing elements of Project Purity, and is in awe of his mentor, Doctor Li.

After James returns to his former colleagues, almost twenty years after abandoning it and fleeing to Vault 101, Alex and Daniel Agincourt get the call to return from the field. He cheerfully follows Doctor Li's return to the project and is confident that they will have it up and running soon.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Waters of Life: A part of the Project Purity team Alex is one of the characters the player must escort to safety.

Effects of player's actions:
• If he survives, Alex will appear in Broken Steel at the Jefferson Memorial, continuing his work alongside Daniel Agincourt.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Jefferson Museum and Gift Shop. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000340d7.

chr_0001cca1.behavior: Unaggressive, cautious; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, travel, follow
chr_0001cca1.summary: Daniel Agincourt is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Dr. Li's Research Team. Found primarily around Jefferson Museum and Gift Shop. Directly connected to quests: Death From Above, The Waters of Life.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Daniel is rather rude, prideful and standoffish. At the same time, he is also an extremely loyal and competent engineer, preferring to focus most of his energy on his work rather than the fanciful plans and adventures of others. When Project Purity was abandoned, he was the last one to leave the premises. Afterward, he followed Doctor Madison Li to Rivet City and continued to work with her for years. Since the abandonment of the project, he has held disdain for both James and the Lone Wanderer, who he views as the cause for the project's indefinite hiatus. He and Alex Dargon were out in the field when they got the call to return. Almost twenty years later, after James returns to his former colleagues, Daniel follows Dr. Li back to the project.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Waters of Life: A part of the Project Purity team Daniel is one of the characters the player must escort to safety. During the quest he can become a temporary companion, should the player provide him with a handgun. If the player does there are unique responses:
•.32 pistol -
• 10mm pistol -
• Silenced 10mm pistol -
• Chinese pistol -
• Scoped.44 Magnum -

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer kills Daniel, Garza will often become hostile to them, even if the Lone Wanderer is hidden when he is killed or if Garza is a long distance away from the Lone Wanderer.
• If he survives, Daniel will appear in Broken Steel at the Jefferson Memorial, continuing his work alongside Alex Dargon.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Jefferson Museum and Gift Shop. Notable equipment & inventory: RobCo Jumpsuit.

chr_00019a1f.summary: Colonel Augustus Autumn is the commanding officer of the Department of the Army for John Henry Eden's division of the Enclave occupying the Capital Wasteland in 2277. He serves as one of the two primary antagonists of alongside John Henry Eden.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Early life:
Born and raised on Control Station ENCLAVE off the coast of New California, Augustus was the son of a high-ranking scientist during President Dick Richardson's final term. Both were later posted to the mainland sometime prior to 2241, allowing them to avoid dying to nuclear fire when the Chosen One infiltrated the rig in the fall of 2242, killed President Richardson, and destroyed the Enclave's HQ by causing a meltdown. With the loss of their executive leadership, the Enclave's mainland bases were left to fend for themselves. Sometime later, a select group was contacted by John Henry Eden from his stronghold of Raven Rock in the mountains of Pennsylvania on the East Coast, claiming to be their new commander-in-chief.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Waters of Life: Colonel Autumn is first encountered by the Lone Wanderer during the quest, The Waters of Life, locked in the Project Purity control room at the Jefferson Memorial with James and Janice Kaplinski. He declares the Enclave's intention to confiscate the project, and, in a show of his deadly seriousness, kills Janice in order to force James' cooperation. James, instead of shutting down the project, floods the area with radiation from the purifier, in an attempt to kill Autumn and his men. James and the Enclave soldiers fall to the radiation and die, while Autumn seemingly injects himself with advanced RadAway or Rad-X.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Raven Rock - Level 2, Jefferson Memorial Rotunda. Notable equipment & inventory: 10mm Round, Col. Autumn's 10mm Pistol, itm_0005157e.

chr_00019a1c.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_00019a1c.summary: President John Henry Eden is an advanced ZAX AI unit installed in the Raven Rock military complex northwest of Washington, D.C.. Using a crafted presidential persona, it proclaimed itself to be the next president of the Enclave after the fall of Control Station ENCLAVE circa 2241, becoming the organization's public face to the inhabitants of the Capital Wasteland by 2277. It serves as one of the two primary antagonists alongside Augustus Autumn.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Origins:
President John Henry Eden is not a human being, but an artificial intelligence, reigning from within a pre-War ZAX supercomputer. The ZAX at Raven Rock was loaded with data about American history, and Eden's personality is thusly based on an implausible amalgamation of the personalities and cultural legends of all previous presidents. For instance, he states he "grew up in rural Kentucky," a trait borrowed from the life of Abraham Lincoln. He further claims to have roamed the countryside with his dog Honey, "from Knob Creek to Hodgenville," areas close to Lincoln's birthplace.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
The American Dream: When the Lone Wanderer finally meets Eden in person, he wants them to poison the water supply with a modified form of FEV. The Lone Wanderer can accept his offer, or talk him into self-destructing. In either case, the room cannot be exited before picking up the FEV canister.

Effects of player's actions:
• The Lone Wanderer can convince him to destroy Raven Rock and himself through three different dialogue paths. Two of the paths require special conditions to be met: One requires knowledge of the Raven Rock destruction sequence, the other requires a high Science skill to open a dialogue option. The last path is an average difficulty Speech check.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00019420.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: surprised. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00019420.summary: Holly is the wife of Vance and a member of the Family in 2277. She has several reservations about her husband's beliefs but supports him completely.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Holly is the oldest female member of the group and was the first to join Vance when he decided to exile himself to Meresti. Over the years, she has grown fond of Vance, and they have enjoyed a healthy relationship. She is often found following Vance around wherever he goes, and they share the same bed. Since she is a veteran member of the Family, the rest of them accept her relationship with Vance and do not feel she is trying to get anything out of him or use him to get what she wants. She is strong-willed and intelligent.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: She can be persuaded to reveal the password to Ian's meditation room with sufficiently high Charisma or the Scoundrel perk.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Meresti Metro Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Adventurer Outfit.

chr_00019020.summary: Security Guard is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 70 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head, Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They are hired by Allistair Tenpenny to ensure the security of Tenpenny Tower and its residents. Their main concern is to make sure unwelcome visitors don't get in, like Roy Phillips and his group of ghouls. Gustavo is the leader of these guards. The guards will react and attempt to subdue the Lone Wanderer should they start any trouble.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: They can be found outside the tower at the guard post and in areas around the building as well as inside on the different levels. Several guards stand near the main gate. There is also an area to the right once you enter the Tower that has several cots and tables. This is where the guards sleep at night or rest during the day.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Notable equipment & inventory: Tenpenny Security Uniform, Allistair Tenpenny's Suite Key.

chr_000179ec.summary: Margaret Primrose is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Margaret owns and operates the Café Beau Monde. Because the cafe only serves the residents of Tenpenny Tower, her clientele is limited, allowing Margaret to prepare and serve all the meals. The restaurant is open from 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM, and Margaret is the service provider the entire time. When the restaurant closes, she generally spends her time in her room.

Margaret says she picked up cooking from her late mother. She explains that her mother wasn't always the best, though she showed her love for her family through cooking. Since Allistair Tenpenny refuses to come down from his suite, Margaret has to prepare all his meals and take them up to him herself.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tenpenny Tower: She can be asked to support the ghouls admission to the tower.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Notable equipment & inventory: Tenpenny Resident's Key, Dirty Pre-War Relaxedwear. Provides services: Alcohol, Food, Supplies / Barter, Apparel & Goods.

chr_000179d6.summary: Zip is a asian child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 35 HP). Affiliated with Little Lamplighters. Found primarily around Lamplight Caverns. Directly connected to quests: Picking Up the Trail.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Hyperactive and quickly-spoken, Zip's energy is put to use as one of Little Lamplight's scouts and scavengers, a role he utilizes to further fuel his Nuka-Cola addiction by claiming any Nuka-Cola he finds for himself. His speediness assists with scavenging efforts, but it also worries him as one time he ran so fast he thought his legs would fly off, before calming down as he remembered "legs don't have wings." Apart from searching for Nuka-Cola, he uses scavenging as an opportunity to trade the items he has found in exchange for the beverage, an offer he can present to the Lone Wanderer from first approach.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Zip's Nuka Fix: He will trade the player character random items for Nuka-Cola.

chr_0001d714.summary: Karen Schenzy is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 50 HP). Affiliated with Arefu Residents. Found primarily around Schenzy Residence. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The recent conflict with The Family has put the extroverted Karen heavily at odds with the town's leader, Evan King, and his impromptu security measures meant to defend against The Family's incursions. Although she appreciates some of his attempts to help, she otherwise views him as a "spineless wimp" who is either unable or unwilling to take meaningful action to deal with the threat that The Family poses. Believing that living in constant fear is not the answer, she has taken to defiant actions such as wandering around outside of her house, even at night, in spite of The Family's incursions into the town. She would much rather take direct action against The Family, especially if she is informed about the deaths of Davis and Matilda West, but feels that King does not have her back.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She stays in her home all day, unless the Lone Wanderer has finished the Blood Ties quest and has selected the option for Vance to provide the town with security. Then, she will be seen wandering around Arefu more often.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: Karen Schenzy is one of the people Evan King wants the player character to check on.
• If she is asked for assistance after the Blood Ties quest is completed, she will mark the Dickerson Tabernacle Chapel, Five Axles Rest Stop, Fort Bannister, Rockbreaker's Last Gas and Shalebridge for the Lone Wanderer on the world map.

chr_0001d711.summary: Brailee Ewers is a resident of Arefu suffering from a severe case of delusional disorder in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The 36-year-old The recent troubles at Arefu caused by the Family had a profoundly negative effect on Brailee, as combined with a poor diet of pre-packaged "food" and long isolation at home with her overly protective husband resulted in her developing a severe delusional disorder. where the children play safely in the grassy knolls outside, or fishing at the lake. Brailee owns a garden with begonias near the front gate of her yard, and is a member of a homeowner's association, bringing "muffins" to each meeting, together with Matilda West. Inside this fantasy world, Brailee also makes preserves, chocolate chip cookies, and bakes pies (which, in reality, is just random junk she gives to others as presents).

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: Brailee Ewers is one of the Arefu residents who need to be checked on. After completing the quest, she rewards the player character by baking them "cookies," as she calls them, which are nothing more than tin cans.

chr_0001d710.summary: Ken Ewers is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 50 HP). Affiliated with Arefu Residents, Ewers Family. Found primarily around Ewer Residence. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ken is terrified of the current attacks that have been plaguing Arefu. He masks this by being incredibly short and gruff with strangers and will only impart the smallest tidbits of useless information to them. He is fiercely overprotective of his wife Brailee and will interpose himself if anyone even tries speaking with her. He is paranoid and lacks physical fighting skills. At the moment all he cares about is his and his wife's lives, and his wife's delusional mental state.

His wife's mentality was brought about by the combination of all the trouble around Arefu, living off a poor diet of prepackaged "food" and being confined to their home with Ken for long periods of time. In her delusion, she has compensated by creating a utopian world inside her mind.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Ken stays in his home all day. Upon completion of Blood Ties, he will come outside and roam around along with the other residents.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only after completing Blood Ties

Quests:
• Blood Ties: Ken Ewers is one of the people who the Lone Wanderer will have to check on to see if he's okay. He is rather aggressive in his dialogue and will insult the player upon entering his house. After the completion of the quest, he offers to repair any equipment (up to 49%).

chr_0001d5f7.summary: Vance is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 210 HP). Affiliated with The Family. Found primarily around Meresti Metro Station. Directly connected to quests: Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Leader of vampires:
When he was younger, Vance was a resident of Rivet City. Over time, he became dissatisfied with his life and decided to strike out on his own in the Capital Wasteland. Sometime soon after leaving the city, he supposedly manifested a supernatural ability to detect those who carry a craving for human flesh, which he also had himself. During this time, Vance befriended a man named Robert when the two worked together to defend themselves against an attack by slavers (who Vance personally detests).

Eventually, Vance made it his mission to create a home for others with cannibalistic urges like him, leading to the creation of the Family as he gathered others of his "kind" from across the wastes using his claimed ability to detect them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: The Lone Wanderer has to face Vance and the members of his family after discovering they had supposedly kidnapped Ian West from his home of Arefu.
• I Want to Drink Your Blood: If Blood Ties was completed by arranging an alliance between Arefu and the Family that involves the trade of blood packs to the latter, the Lone Wanderer has the option of donating supplies of their own to Vance in exchange for caps

Effects of player's actions:
• The fates of Vance and his Family are entirely determined by the player character's choices during the quest Blood Ties:
• Regardless of whether Ian West remains with the Family or is convinced to return to Arefu, the player character can speak with Vance and get him to agree to stop the Family's attacks on the shantytown.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Meresti Metro Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Vance's Sword Cabinet Key, Shishkebab, Vance's Longcoat Outfit.

chr_0001d5f6.summary: Evan King is a resident of the town of Arefu and is the lone defender of the town in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Evan King has lived in Arefu his entire life. Over the years, he has seen the settlement shrink from its high of thirty residents down to its current low of five, four if one does not count the missing Ian West. Despite the settlement's decline, he is still responsible for defending its residents and maintaining the town's security, going so far as to demolish the northern half of the settlement's bridge to prevent an attack from that direction. He has a wealth of combat experience, having previously defended the town from raiders, slavers, and various wasteland creatures.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: When the Lone Wanderer arrives in Arefu to deliver Lucy West's letter, he will throw a scripted grenade at the player. However, it does not hurt the player and he calls them over to him. After conversing, he will ask the Wanderer to check on the residents' welfare. Upon returning to him with news of the West's violent deaths, he will send them to search for Ian West, who was taken away by the Family. Upon returning Ian to Arefu and making a deal with the Family to protect the town, Evan will allow the Wanderer to make use of the weapons he has stored.
• If Megaton has been destroyed before completing the Blood Ties quest, King will give the quest to the Wanderer instead of Lucy West, although the speech options with Ian are identical to as if Lucy was still alive.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Evan King's House. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Troublemaker Outfit, itm_00078648.

chr_0001d5f5.summary: Ian West is a former resident of Arefu, presently living as a member of the Family at the Meresti Metro station in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Early life:
Ian West lived with his parents Davis and Matilda and older sister Lucy in the remote settlement of Arefu. For many years, he grappled with a strange condition that he says caused him to hunger for human flesh. He claims that this condition may have been caused by an incident during his childhood: according to Ian, one day when he and his sister Lucy were playing under the overpass and skipping rocks on the water, they saw a wastelander harassing the brahmin in the pen outside of Arefu. When the 10-year-old Ian went to warn him to stop, the wastelander laughed and shoved him aside, which Ian claims caused him to hit his head and black out. When he regained awareness, he found Lucy trying to pull him off the dead body of the scavenger.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: After finding the dead bodies of the West parents in their Arefu residence, the Lone Wanderer is asked by Evan King to find Ian, who was taken by the Family.

Effects of player's actions:
• Ian's fate depends on the player character's intervention during the quest Blood Ties:
• If one passes a high Speech skill check, or provides Lucy's sealed envelope to Ian in his holding cell, he will have an epiphany and decide to abandon the Family to return to his family home in Arefu. Conversely, if neither of these actions are available, he will confirm his loyalty to Vance and the Family and refuse to leave. Either choice can be relayed back to Evan King, earning good Karma regardless of Ian's ultimate decision.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Meresti Metro Station. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_0001d44e.summary: Paladin Vargas is a Brotherhood of Steel soldier and sergeant of the elite Lyons' Pride squad. He is initially encountered patrolling the lobby of the Galaxy News Radio building. After completing the Following in His Footsteps quest, he can be seen patrolling the Citadel. When traveling across the bridge during the quest Take it Back!, Vargas could be killed. If he does survive, he will disappear from the game.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Paladin Vargas is a professional soldier with little capacity for nonsense. Although he is four years older than Sentinel Lyons, he is a sergeant of the Lyons' Pride, responsible for managing the squad and carrying out her orders. He is her right hand, providing her with his experience, advice, and mentoring the Sentinel when needed. The two have a very close friendship, though they both maintain professionalism at all times.

In particular, Vargas is responsible for evaluating Pride candidates, such as Initiate Reddin. He keeps them on a tight leash, shutting down any signs of a gung-ho attitude, believing that they will get their fill of death soon enough. Even as a coping mechanism, he finds it unacceptable. Once that is taken care of, he can be a very patient teacher, especially with those who show promise as a Brotherhood soldier.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
• Only until the end of Following in His Footsteps.

Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: Vargas is encountered together with the Lyons' Pride.
• If the Galaxy News Radio part of the main quest is skipped and the Lone Wanderer proceeds directly to Rivet City to talk to Dr. Li, and subsequently continues the rest of the main quest, Paladin Vargas will be marked essential during Take it Back!

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Chevy Chase East. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0001d432.summary: Knight Captain Colvin is a Brotherhood of Steel marksman, serving in Sentinel Sarah Lyons' elite Lyons' Pride.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Knight Captain Colvin is a man of deep faith who treats warfare with reverence. He sees every battle he participates in as worship and his laser rifle as a holy item, dispensing his god's wrath on whoever is unfortunate enough to find themselves on the other end of the barrel. He bears no ill will towards the people he slays, even super mutants, and is known to pray for the soul of each one he dispatches, believing that he releases them from their torment. He is equally capable as a pointman and backup securing streets for the rest of the Pride.

Friendly rivalry with Dusk aside, Colvin is warm and friendly to everyone, treating them with uncommon kindness, even if they are just a random wastelander caught in between super mutants in downtown DC.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: Colvin is part of the Lyons' Pride when encountered at the GNR building plaza. He returns to the Citadel upon completion of the quest. He does not play a role in any subsequent quest, even those that involve the Lyons' Pride.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Chevy Chase East. Notable equipment & inventory: Power Helmet.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2251, at Lost Hills in New California, the three year old Sarah lost her mother in infancy, and accompanied her father on the transcontinental expedition to Washington, D.C. in 2254, under the elders' council mandate to recover technology from eastern cities and bases.

Over the next twenty-two years, Sarah accumulated training, experience, and leadership skills. As she rose to become one of the finest fighters at the D.C. Bunker, her father (promoted to elder from star paladin, for the discovery of Liberty Prime) gradually switched the chapter's mission from recovery to super mutant containment. He lied to the elder council about following the original mission, and eventually disobeyed direct orders, leading to Lost Hills breaking ties with him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Companion:
Lyons is available as a temporary companion at Chevy Chase during Following in His Footsteps and while attacking the Memorial during Take it Back!. Her stats are normally on par with a normal Brotherhood of Steel paladin. However, while fighting the Enclave on the way to the memorial, her health is increased to 505, giving her extremely high durability on par with Star Paladin Cross. The increase is largely a convenience, as Lyons is marked as essential unless the player chooses to destroy the Citadel.

Furthermore, Sarah Lyons is coded as a non-player character companion, and therefore uses up ammunition for her weapons, unlike most non-player characters. She has more than 100 microfusion cells in her inventory, giving her a substantial amount of ammunition before she switches to her melee weapon.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Chevy Chase East. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.
