chr_0001d42f.summary: Initiate Reddin is an initiate within the elite Lyons' Pride of the Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A wastelander who was only recently conscripted into the Brotherhood, Initiate Reddin is an overly curious and excitable recruit on her first combat assignment. Vargas does what he can to restrain her and teach her the ways of the Brotherhood. Reddin was added to Sarah's unit against his advice, but although Vargas may act angry and annoyed at Reddin, it is entirely because he is trying to keep her alive.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: Reddin gallantly fights alongside the Lone Wanderer in their journey to the Galaxy News Radio building in the pursuit for more information on the whereabouts of their father. During the quest, the explosion of the barrier of vehicles that heralds the arrival of the super mutant behemoth kills her instantly. After the behemoth battle, Sarah Lyons tells Vargas that she will tell the Brotherhood of Reddin's courage and that she will be remembered as Paladin Reddin.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer proceeds to Rivet City and speaks to Doctor Li without going to GNR first, and then later goes to GNR, the Lyons' Pride will not be encountered at all, alongside Initiate Reddin and the two dead Brotherhood of Steel initiates.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment

chr_000156f8.summary: Tulip is a ghoul resident of Underworld in the Capital Wasteland and an ally of the Railroad in 2277. She is the proprietor of the settlement's general goods store, Underworld Outfitters.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Tulip operates her shop in the old Museum of History with a reputation for being a shrewd businesswoman, with a "unique ability to obtain unique items," while simultaneously having one of the largest merchant inventories in the Capital Wasteland. When she's not behind the counter of her shop, she takes a seat over at Carol's Place, fully trusting Quinn to look after the merchandise. Quinn has also been the primary contributor to Tulip's large inventory through his wasteland travels. She is aware of Underworld's full history of habitation going all the way back to its first post-War settlers, such as Carol.

When he was still living at Underworld, Dunbar had a silent crush on Tulip and would spend hours sitting and pining for her.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Tulip possesses one of the holotapes containing information about an android from the Commonwealth.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: The Lone Wanderer can optionally speak to her about Mister Crowley and learn about his true intentions.

Effects of player's actions:
If asked about the origins of Underworld, Tulip can optionally give a copy of Paradise Lost. Reading this book increases the player character's Speech by the same number of skill points as a copy of Lying, Congressional Style.

Other interactions:
• In her merchant inventory, Tulip sells a schematic for the railway rifle.
• With the Contract Killer perk, one will be able to obtain an ear upon killing her that can be turned in to Littlehorn & Associates.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Underworld Concourse. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Adventurer Outfit. Provides services: Weapons, Armor, Books & Schematics, Supplies / Barter.

chr_000156f7.summary: Ahzrukhal is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Found primarily around The Ninth Circle. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head, Agatha's Song, Companion Recruitment: Charon.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The shrewd and fashionably dressed Ahzrukhal operates the Ninth Circle, Underworld's primary watering hole, where he milks people for all they are worth. He sees life as a simple equation: the more misery his customers suffer, the more money he makes when they come to drown their sorrows. Coupled with the fact that Underworld is the only ghoul refuge in the Capital Wasteland, he makes a killing on his customers. His friendly Uncle Ahzrukhal persona is crafted specifically to convince patrons to buy alcohol (and other stimulants) to get drunk, forget about their miserable existence for a while, then come back for more.

While he enables his customers' drinking, he keeps his drugs reserved for a more discerning clientele. While alcohol abuse is accepted at Underworld, abusing harder drugs and especially dealing in them is not.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Vendor:
• As a bartender, Ahzrukhal initially only offers alcohol, but through dialogue options (no Speech check), it is possible to convince him to offer drugs like Buffout, Jet and Psycho.
• The player can also purchase Charon's contract from him for 1,000 caps or a favor. Obtaining Charon will result in Ahzrukal being gunned down by his former slave, eliminating the chems and alcohol vendor permanently.

Quests:
• Agatha's Song: The player can sell the Soil Stradivarius to Ahzrukhal instead of returning it to Agatha. He does not appreciate the artifact as anything more than a bar ornament that might attract more clientele, and offers 200 caps or 300 caps with a Speech check.
• Hired Help: Ahzrukhal offers an alternative method of acquiring Charon by eliminating his competition.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Ninth Circle. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Businesswear. Provides services: Alcohol, Chems & Medicine, Supplies / Barter.

chr_000156f6.summary: Charon is a ghoul residing in Underworld in the Capital Wasteland, working as the bouncer for the Ninth Circle bar run by Ahzrukhal in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Very little of Charon's past before becoming the bouncer of the Ninth Circle in Underworld is revealed. Ahzrukhal will tell the Lone Wanderer that Charon was raised by an unspecified group who brainwashed him into being completely loyal and obedient to whoever has his contract. Despite the logical unfairness of their arrangement, Ahzrukhal will firmly state that Charon is not a slave, even implying that Charon did something in the past to deserve his "employment" with Ahzrukhal. While the exact terms of the contract are never shown, if Charon is an active companion when looking for the G.E.C.K. in Vault 87, and one asks him to enter the irradiated chamber to retrieve it, he says that his contract only obligates him to provide combat services and that he is "nobody's errand boy."

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: As the Ninth Circle's bouncer, Charon stands in the corner until needed. If recruited as a companion, then later dismissed by the Lone Wanderer, he will return there and sit in a nearby chair.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Hired Help: After asking about gaining Charon's services, Ahzrukhal offers to give his contract for free if the Lone Wanderer kills Greta, or by paying a large amount of caps. Either way the contract is obtained, after talking to him to confirm his allegiance, Charon will approach Ahzrukhal and murder him in cold blood as revenge for all the dirty work he made him do.
• Take it Back!: With Broken Steel installed, if Charon is an active companion when entering the Jefferson Memorial, he will agree to activate Project Purity if asked to, preventing the Lone Wanderer or Sarah Lyons from doing so.

Effects of player's actions:
• The player character can obtain Charon's contract by paying Ahzrukhal 2,000 caps, or 1,000 with 50 Barter, or by agreeing to kill Greta. Acquiring Charon's contract makes him a potential companion.

chr_000156f5.summary: Mister Crowley is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 10, 140 HP). Found primarily around Carol's Place. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Little is known about Mister Crowley's past other than that, over 20 years prior to 2277, he was involved in an incident that resulted in him being exposed to an extreme amount of radiation, bordering on fatal, leading to his current condition as a ghoul.

In 2257, Crowley and four other mercenaries - Dave, Jeff Strayer, Dukov, and Tara Fields - were hired by independent financier Allistair Tenpenny to break into Fort Constantine supposedly to retrieve a rare weapon; the hiring of Crowley in particular was surprising due to Tenpenny's well-known bigotry towards ghouls. However, after Tara was killed while they were exploring, Dukov saw an opportunity to take the others' shares of the payout for himself, and locked Crowley inside a room full of feral ghouls.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: In Underworld, Mister Crowley can typically be found in either his bed at Carol's Place, where he usually sleeps until 12 PM, or in the Ninth Circle wandering between empty seats.

sections.title: Interactions with the player
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: The Lone Wanderer is asked by Mister Crowley to hunt down a list of four targets that hate ghouls, with the special request to shoot them in the head and collect specific trophies of the kills to bring back to him.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer retrieves the keys from Crowley's targets, but does not return them, they can go to Fort Constantine and take the T-51b power armor contained inside. When next speaking with him, Mister Crowley will not be happy, however, and will only respond with "You stole what was rightfully mine! Get lost." There is also not an option to give the suit to him. He will give this dialogue as well if the Lone Wanderer pickpockets the keys from him after handing them over.

chr_000156f4.summary: Quinn is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 60 HP). Found primarily around Carol's Place. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A veteran of countless battles across the wastes, Quinn is a wandering ghoul trader who roams the blasted expanse of the former United States. in his travels, he covered the entire East Coast, from The Pitt and the Commonwealth, through the Capital Wasteland, all the way down south to Crater Banks. His home is the Underworld, and Quinn is, in fact, its primary lifeline, moving goods and caps the ghouls possess out of the Underworld and bringing back whatever he can find. He primarily delivers goods for Tulip, and Greta at Carol's Place (whisky distilled by a northern brewer is a perennial favorite),
as well as sourcing various foodstuffs, like mutfruit. Any ghoul can provide him with caps for trade, and he is, in fact, the third biggest recipient of caps after the Ninth Circle and Carol's Place.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:

chr_000156f3.summary: Greta is a ghoul cook, Carol's life partner, and co-host of the Carol's Place in Underworld. The two are the first same-sex couple to be portrayed in a Fallout game.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Greta is a ghoul from outside Underworld who immigrated there around 2217. Upon meeting Carol, the two fell in love, and opened a bed and breakfast together, realizing Carol's lifelong dream. Carol became the housekeeper and administrator, while Greta took up the responsibilities of a cook, tailoring the food to the peculiar ghoul physiology. After six decades of being together, their relationship is still going strong, although Greta constantly worries about Carol, who has begun to show signs of depression.

Greta's key advantage is her deadpan, sarcastic sense of humor, typically leveraging the fact that she's a ghoul cooking for ghouls. She's an expert at turning barely edible scraps into something approximating a dish, and jokingly refers to it as the finest food in DC (just don't ask what it's made of).

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: The Lone Wanderer can ask Greta about Mister Crowley and his "scheme" and she will reveal a few obvious things, and a few non-obvious with a Speech check.
• Hired Help: The Lone Wanderer may choose to kill Greta in exchange for Charon's contract.

Merchant:
• Greta is a consumables merchant, offering a selection of food, drinks, and chems, using a generic leveled list like most other such merchants.

Other interactions:
• If the Lone Wanderer is female, Greta will warn her to stay away from Carol upon first interaction.
• Telling Carol about Gob's death, should it happen, will cause Greta to berate the player character, but has no lasting consequences.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Carol's Place. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Spring Outfit. Provides services: Alcohol, Food, Supplies / Barter, Apparel & Goods.

chr_000156f2.summary:
Carol is a female ghoul denizen of Underworld. She is the owner and proprietor of Carol's Place, keeping it running together with her partner Greta.

The two are the first same-sex couple to be portrayed in a Fallout game.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Born in 2051, Carol was 26 years old when the Great War struck, but only remembers herself as a "little girl." As her family could not afford a space in the Vaults, they had to use a public fallout shelter in D.C. They made it inside just as the nuclear weapons started to detonate. Carol's father stopped to help a family get inside the shelter, as Carol called for him. That same moment, the first detonation engulfed D.C., with her father disappearing in a bright flash of light. Carol lost consciousness, waking up a few hours later, only to discover her father's shadow "burned" into the concrete wall. Fellow refugees arrived in the museum to seek shelter and eventually, the situation calmed down. A small community formed within, trying to make ends meet. However, the exposure to radiation during the Great War caused ghoulification.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Carol has two packages assigned which govern her schedule:
• She will stay at Carol's Place throughout the day, with a sandbox package active (meaning she will talk to customers and Greta and move through the area).
• At 2 AM, she will leave and go to sleep in her bed with Greta for six hours, waking up at 8 AM and returning to run Carol's Place.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Carol can be asked about Mister Crowley, noting his idle boasts about his plan, suggesting that dealing with ghoul bigotry is not the real reason for his plans.

Other interactions:
• Although Carol is hesitant to talk about her experiences during and since the War, she will tell her story if encouraged.
• When talking to Carol, she can be asked about Gob.
• If Megaton was blown up during The Power of the Atom and the Lone Wanderer tells Carol that they were responsible, everyone in Underworld (except Doctor Barrows, his assistant, and sometimes Tulip and Willow) becomes hostile (including Charon, even if he is currently a companion).
• If Megaton was not blown up but the Lone Wanderer killed Gob, only Carol will become hostile. Killing her in self-defense will not result in any Karma loss.

chr_000156f1.summary: Reilly is a member as well as the leader and founder of the mercenary band known as Reilly's Rangers encountered in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The young Reilly grew up without her parents in the ruins of the former American capital Washington, D.C., instead being raised by an unnamed man with a military background who brought her up to be self-sufficient. Her adoptive parent died around 12 years later, with Reilly carrying his body to Arlington Cemetery for a proper military burial. Four years prior to 2277, at the age of 26, she founded a group dedicated to eradicating the threat of super mutants and geomapping the Capital Wasteland, naming them Reilly's Rangers. By 2277, Reilly has been working with the members of Reilly's Rangers for years, and trusts all of them with her life.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Reilly's Rangers: After being revived, Reilly knows something has gone wrong and urges the Lone Wanderer to investigate the whereabouts of her mercs, somewhere in the Vernon Square area.
• Geomapping with Reilly: After rescuing her mercs from the Statesman Hotel, the Lone Wanderer will be asked to take a geomapper module and help her map out the DC area.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the harsh Speech options are chosen when first talking to her, Reilly gets mad and will never talk to the Lone Wanderer again.
• Depending on how she is woken up, Reilly's legs are crippled and can be seen limping if the Medicine skill is used to wake her up. However, she will look like normal if Doctor Barrows' Speech check is used to wake her up.

chr_000156f0.summary: Doctor Barrows is a ghoul and the resident doctor in the Chop Shop in Underworld in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Doctor Barrows is the informal mayor of the Underworld and proprietor of the Chop Shop, as well as one of the few doctors in the wasteland trying to gain a scientific understanding of ghoulification. He claims to be the foremost authority on the ghoul condition and has managed to contain a pair of live glowing ones named Meat and Ethyl in an observation cell. He and his assistant, Nurse Graves, are busily (but discreetly) studying a way to slow the advancement of the ghoul condition and maybe someday, reverse it. Whenever he is not tending to his patients, he runs experiments on samples gathered from human volunteers (skin, hair, and occasionally organs) to determine what ghoulification is and whether it can be rectified. He enjoys dark humor greatly, one of the few ways to maintain composure in a taxing line of work.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: At night, he leaves to eat dinner at Carol's Place for a few hours, and then returns to the clinic. He sleeps for a couple of hours on site.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Reilly's Rangers: He can start the quest, and also wake Reilly up. If Barrows is killed by the player character, it is not necessary to wake Reilly up. If one goes to the Statesman Hotel and helps the Rangers, Reilly will automatically appear in the Ranger compound.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Passing a Speech check or bribing him can reveal information about Mister Crowley.

chr_000156ef.summary: Patchwork is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Found primarily around Underworld Concourse. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Patchwork is the resident drunk of Underworld, drinking to a point where he consistently slurs his words and has a tendency to forget what is being said to him mid-conversation. Not many of the other ghouls acknowledge his presence, save for Ahzrukhal who keeps him intoxicated, and Winthrop who is attempting to put an end to his drinking problem to no avail. As such, Patchwork is surprised if the Lone Wanderer engages him in conversation, claiming that they must be new to the city or they would not be speaking to him.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Patchwork randomly wanders around the promenade inside the center area of Underworld. He may enter The Ninth Circle to obtain more alcohol. He and Quinn appear to be good friends, as in a non-player character to non-player character conversation Patchwork asks Quinn if he "brought anything back" for him.

chr_000156ee.summary: Winthrop is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 5, 50 HP). Found primarily around Underworld Concourse. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Winthrop is Underworld's technician. He checks on the electricity, makes sure any plumbing is in working order, and generally takes care of everything maintenance-wise. He restored and reprogrammed the robot Cerberus, and is responsible for its maintenance. Winthrop sleeps for a few hours in his little workshop off the concourse and is occasionally joined by his friend Greta.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• This Old House: Due to a steadily declining supply of resources, Winthrop will trade the Lone Wanderer one stimpak, RadAway, or Rad-X in exchange for every five pieces of scrap metal. With a high enough Strength, he can be threatened into handing over ten stimpaks for free. After this, he will refuse to speak with the Lone Wanderer again.

chr_000156ed.summary: Scribe Peabody is the proctor of the Order of the Sword, in charge of the armory for the chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel in the Citadel in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: As proctor of the Order of the Sword, Peabody is head of the armory, in charge of maintaining, researching and developing all of the chapter's various weapons and their systems. A weapons expert extraordinaire, he is already modifying the current armaments of the Brotherhood to counter the new threat of the "black devil power armor" that the Enclave members are wielding, and has previously used his expertise in helping repair Liberty Prime's weapon systems.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He is in the armory in the Citadel laboratory most of the day.

chr_000156ec.summary: Scribe Bowditch is the proctor of the Order of the Shield and head of the Brotherhood of Steel's smithy in the Citadel.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Scribe Bowditch is the proctor of the Order of the Shield, responsible for maintaining the defenses of the chapter. He was the mastermind behind the establishment of the Citadel out of the ruins of the Pentagon, complete with its crane-operated outer gate. Although he is responsible for many innovations over the past few years, his specialty is power armor which he has extensive knowledge and expertise on, spending most of his time obsessively modifying it. He is impressed by the Enclave's advanced Mark II power armor but believes improvements to the Brotherhood's armor will put them on par with one another.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: During the day, Scribe Bowditch can be found at the smithy in the Citadel laboratory. At night, he sleeps in the barracks that are located on the other side of the laboratory.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Bowditch is in possession of a Replicated Man holotape.

Other interactions:
• Bowditch can provide background information about the Brotherhood and the Brotherhood Outcasts.
• He will repair items, but only to 51%.

chr_000156eb.summary: Senior Scribe Yearling is a member of the East Coast Brotherhood of Steel, assigned to the Order of the Quill. She is in charge of the Brotherhood garrison and forward operations center at Arlington Library.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Yearling is the Order of the Quill's field operative tasked with collecting pre-War books from the Capital Wasteland. The purpose of her mission is to further expand the Citadel archives, with the gathering of written works a core responsibility of her order. As such, she and her team have set up for this project at Arlington Library, searching for records and utilizing the library's computer system to track the books collected. The Brotherhood, in spite of the personnel and resources shortage, has also managed to divert some manpower into sending the books back to the Citadel under escort, whereby they are transcribed into the archives.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She can be found in the front desk area of the Arlington Library, collecting valuable pre-War books for the Brotherhood of Steel.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Yearning for Learning: She offers caps for pre-War books at a rate of one hundred per book.

Effects of player's actions:
• She will completely ignore the Lone Wanderer if they insult the Brotherhood, and will order them to leave the library.
• Yearling will direct the Lone Wanderer to the restoration ink located on the higher floors of the library.

chr_000156ea.summary: Scribe Rothchild is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Citadel Residents. Found primarily around Citadel - Laboratory. Directly connected to quests: Death From Above, Take it Back!, Who Dares Wins.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Scribe Rothchild is in charge of the scribes of the Brotherhood of Steel in the Capital Wasteland, and greatly respects men of science and knowledge. and cybernetics, allowing him to save Star Paladin Cross' life after what seemed to be a mortal injury.

Despite that, Rothchild was a part of Star Paladin Owyn Lyons' expedition to Washington, D.C. in 2255. With the discovery of Liberty Prime, Rothchild was tasked with bringing the massive weapon of war online. Although he led his own team of talented scribes, he also interacted with a number of scientific minds from across the wasteland, including James of Project Purity. He developed a healthy respect for him and his independent team, even if the project fizzled out without producing any results. After all, James was a visionary and these were in short supply.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can usually be found in the Citadel laboratory.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Picking Up the Trail, Finding the Garden of Eden: Rothchild helps the Lone Wanderer locate a G.E.C.K. by first pointing them to an old Vault-Tec terminal in the Citadel's A-ring and then telling them about the location of Vault 87. This quest must be started before one can gain access to Vault 87.
• Death From Above: With the add-on Broken Steel, after waking up after two weeks of having been unconscious, Elder Lyons directs the Lone Wanderer to Rothchild, so he can fill them in on what has happened in the past two weeks.
• Getting Ready for Prime Time: After completing Who Dares Wins, Scribe Rothchild, when asked how the Lone Wanderer can help the Brotherhood further, asks that they bring him sensor modules and old cameras to help fix Liberty Prime.

chr_000156e9.summary: Paladin Glade is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel, Citadel Residents. Found primarily around Citadel - A Ring. Directly connected to quests: Take it Back!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Like the rest of the members of Lyons' Pride, Glade was handpicked by Sarah Lyons to be part of the elite unit. He is the group's oldest member, and serves as their technician and smith. However, beyond his technical capabilities, he is also heavily experienced in combat, serving as the most well-rounded member of the unit. His particular combat speciality is in heavy weapons, such as miniguns, missile launchers, and the Gatling laser that he is currently wielding.

Upon first meeting the Lone Wanderer, Glade is friendly and welcoming towards them, expressing relief that they and Madison Li were able to escape from the Jefferson Memorial after the arrival of the Enclave.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Take it Back!: Glade accompanies the Lone Wanderer during the reclamation of Jefferson Memorial, wiping out Enclave troops with his Gatling laser.
• Gallows Humor: Glade runs the betting pool regarding Knight Captain Gallows' real name.

chr_000156e8.summary: Knight Captain Gallows is an elite member of Lyons' Pride of the Brotherhood of Steel, found at the Citadel. His real name is Irving.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: One of the most enigmatic members of the Lyons' Pride, Knight Captain Gallows is a quiet, reserved man who specializes in reconnaissance and stealth assignments, with an official combat specialization of "special operations." He gives the other members of the Pride a wide berth and keeps to himself, often disappearing for days at a time, which only adds to the air of mystery that surrounds him. Whenever he returns, he does not share a word with his peers, answering only to Sarah Lyons. While most of the Pride members consider it almost funny, some, like Knight Captain Dusk, treat it as evidence of Gallows' untrustworthiness.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Take it Back!: Gallows assists the player and Liberty Prime in the battle towards Project Purity.
• Gallows Humor: The player can collect the betting pool by figuring out Gallows' real name through a Speech check. This will be impossible if the player has not yet asked the rest of the Pride about Gallows' name.

Other interactions:
• Gallows is a very curt person. The player can improve his disposition and earn a positive modifier for the Speech check that allows them to figure out his real name by staying silent during their first meeting.

chr_000156e7.summary: Knight Captain Dusk is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel, Citadel Residents. Found primarily around Citadel - A Ring. Directly connected to quests: Take it Back!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Self-confident and a skilled sharpshooter, Dusk is one of two Lyons' Pride snipers, claiming to be the best shot in not only the group, but the entire Brotherhood of Steel chapter. She is dedicated to honing her craft through live fire drills in the bailey, and does not take kindly to being interrupted by people, though she will converse with them nonetheless. She can be heard talking to Paladin Glade during these sessions, expressing disappointment in one of her shots dropping by a few inches and calling her own work "sloppy." She is positive she can penetrate Enclave helmets from 100 yards away, claims she can blow heads off from over 200 meters downrange, and asserts that any "mutie bastard" within a mile of her rifle will singlehandedly end the super mutant conflict.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Dusk is a member of the Lyons' Pride. She has a fairly friendly rivalry with Knight Captain Colvin, who is the Pride's other sniper, competing over kill counts and who the better shot is. She and Paladin Glade converse during live fire drills, where he compliments her shooting abilities, but she has a distrust for Knight Captain Gallows due to his secretive persona.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Take it Back!: She can be seen at the Citadel entrance, picking off Enclave soldiers with her sniper rifle.
• Gallows Humor: She can be asked about Knight Captain Gallows, starting the unmarked quest.

Other interactions:
• It is possible to taunt her into threatening the player character. However, when the player character meets her at the area she told them to, "in the den after lights out," nothing happens.
• Although the player character can taunt her about being a better shot, during the quest Take it Back!, she can be seen shooting across the entire span of the Potomac River, an extremely difficult feat for the player character to accomplish.

|age =~30 is a member of the elite Lyons' Pride within the Capital Wasteland chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born around 2247 in the Pitt, Paladin Kodiak is the single largest and strongest of the Brotherhood's fighters. He is the unit's "jack of all trades," capable enough to perform any thing the sentinel needs, from recon, through demolition, to tactical assaults. His size and strength mean he's a particular menace in close quarters, especially when he's using his powered sledgehammer, making him as gruff and vicious as an actual bear.

His attitude developed in spite of his traumatic childhood. It was spent in the violent Pitt, surrounded by trogs, raiders, and hellish pollution. Kodiak never knew his parents and remembers his childhood as mostly surviving on the streets and fighting rats for food: Not an environment for a child to grow up in, much less live.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can be found around the great hall in the A ring area of the Citadel.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Take it Back!: Kodiak deploys as part of the Pride during the attack on Project Purity.
• Gallows Humor: Kodiak is one of the characters mentioning the betting pool to figure out Knight Captain Gallows' real name.

Other interactions:
• While Kodiak provides a lot of information about The Pitt, The Pitt add-on does not add any extra dialogue for him, even though the player confronts and kills both of his brothers.

chr_000156e5.summary: Star Paladin Cross is an officer of the Capital Wasteland chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel residing in the Citadel in 2277. She is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
It is well known among the Brotherhood's members that Cross is actually a cyborg; she no longer has a need to eat or sleep. This was the result of Scribe Reginald Rothchild performing an operation in order to save her life after she was gravely wounded while protecting Elder Owyn Lyons in the past.

Sometime after the Brotherhood arrived in the Capital Wasteland, they were approached to provide protection for the scientists of Project Purity; Cross in particular helped to guard the endeavor from when it was in its infancy in 2257. However, following the death of a lead scientist, Catherine, in childbirth, the progress ground to a halt. With super mutant attacks increasing, Catherine's widower James took their newborn and left for Vault 101, with Cross serving as an escort for the pair as far as Megaton.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text:
Being the second highest-ranked soldier in the Brotherhood (behind Sentinel Sarah Lyons), Cross answers only to the elder, who has given her leave to pursue Project Purity's restoration as she sees fit. Naturally, this means crushing the Enclave and fulfilling James' mission of purifying the wasteland's water and making it safe to drink.

In traveling with the Lone Wanderer, Cross can express how she knew James well; As a member of the order, her reputation is very important to her. She is a "man of her word," and will swear to accompany and protect the Lone Wanderer in their travels. However, she is not their servant, She will also not travel with anyone not trusted by the Brotherhood.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Companion:
• Star Paladin Cross can be recruited as a companion after reaching the Citadel during The Waters of Life and only if the player character has Good Karma.
• Cross has the same response to trying to hire her with Neutral or Evil Karma.
• Her utility as a companion is to act as a "tank," drawing enemy attention and using her power armor to reduce incoming damage.

Other interactions:
• Cross is one of only two characters in Fallout 3 who will recite excerpts from the Codex; the other is Arthur Maxson.
• Like many other denizens of the Citadel, Star Paladin Cross will only spout lines such as "For Elder Lyons!" and "Good luck!" when Take it Back! is started.

Effects of player's actions:
• Cross will be immediately hostile towards any nearby Brotherhood Outcasts if she is dismissed in their presence.

chr_000156e4.summary: Elder Lyons is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 25, 155 HP). Affiliated with Citadel Residents, Brotherhood of Steel. Found primarily around Citadel - B Ring. Directly connected to quests: Death From Above, The Waters of Life, The American Dream.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Beginnings:
Lyons was born in the early 23rd century, and was originally a star paladin stationed at the Brotherhood's Lost Hills bunker in Southern California. and the other was to reestablish contact with the "Eastern Brotherhood" and return them under Lost Hills' command (this detachment had fallen off the grid near Chicago and was believed to have gone rogue). Thus, the contingent led by Star Paladin Lyons (and including Lyons' three-year-old daughter Sarah and his friend and technological advisor Scribe Reginald Rothchild, as well as Star Paladin Cross, Paladin Henry Casdin, Initiate Ishmael Ashur, Paladin Tristan, Knight Colvin and Paladin Gunny) set out from Lost Hills and began the long journey east to the Washington, D.C. ruins.

Going east:
Contact with the "Eastern Brotherhood" evidently turned out to be unsuccessful.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: His daughter, Sarah Lyons, is a member of the Brotherhood with the unique rank of sentinel. Reginald Rothchild is an old friend of Elder Lyons.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: As the leader of the Brotherhood of Steel, Lyons spends most of his day in the Citadel laboratory, A-ring or B-ring. He regularly converses with Scribe Rothchild, Bowditch, and Peabody on their various projects. In addition, he checks up on the progress on the Brotherhood's major project, rebuilding Liberty Prime, and supervises the armory as well as the smithy. When he is not working in the Citadel lab, he is usually eating in the A-ring's great hall, studying in his room in B-ring or sleeping.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Early life (2267-2277):
Born in 2267 to Jonathan and Jessica Maxson, Arthur is a descendant of Roger Maxson, founder of the Brotherhood of Steel. His father, a high-ranking paladin serving just outside the New California Republic, was soon killed in battle during the NCR-Brotherhood War, and his mother, Lady Maxson, sent the boy east to be raised under the tutelage of the then respected Elder Owyn Lyons. Part of the reason were internal conflicts in the Brotherhood out west, which created an unsafe environment for Arthur.

Studies:
Ever since arriving at the Citadel, Arthur was an attentive student, with a good knowledge of the Brotherhood's triumphs and history. He has also proven himself to be a keen observer, making accurate observations of the local super mutant threat and even observing a behemoth from the Citadel walls once.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tour of Duty: After Paladin Danse brings the Sole Survivor to the Prydwen after its arrival in the Commonwealth, Maxson promotes them to the rank of knight and asks them to tour the Prydwen and get to know her crew.
• Show No Mercy: Maxson orders the Sole Survivor to clear Fort Strong, a cache of Fat Man ammunition, from its super mutant occupiers.
• Outside the Wire: Maxson (rather than Proctor Ingram) will start this quest if the network scanner holotape was obtained from a faction other than the Brotherhood.
• From Within: Maxson orders the Sole Survivor to find Doctor Madison Li in the Institute and convince her to work for the Brotherhood of Steel.
• Blind Betrayal: Maxson orders the Sole Survivor to execute Danse, who turns out to be a synth.
• Ad Victoriam: Maxson appears as Liberty Prime reaches the C.I.T.

chr_000156e0.summary: Allistair Tenpenny is the founder and owner of Tenpenny Tower, appearing. He is one of only nine named characters in the base game to have "Very Evil" Karma. He is also a Legendary dweller, coming with a unique rifle and suit.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Entrepreneur:
Born around, He does not like talking about himself or his past, preferring his achievements to speak for themselves.

As such, little is known about him before the founding of Tenpenny Tower. What is known is that with his fake aristocratic accent,

Shortly after this botched job, Tenpenny met a man who changed his life: Mister Burke. Burke made the restoration of the future Tenpenny Tower (then just a husk of a derelict resort, jutting up from the horizon in southwestern Capital Wasteland) a plausible endeavor, establishing himself as Tenpenny's right-hand man, capable of doing "what needs to get done." A lot of work went into restoring the tower to a fraction of its former glory, and then securing the right kind of tenants to enjoy its security and luxuries.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Tenpenny rarely leaves his penthouse suite, but for the rare occasion he does, he has a seat reserved in Margaret Primrose's cafe. Generally, he has his meals delivered to the penthouse, always ordering an "iguana bit sandwich, no salt, with a peeled pear on the side" for lunch.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom: If the player agrees with Burke's pitch and installs the fusion pulse charge, they will join Tenpenny and Burke to witness the destruction of Megaton in a nuclear explosion. The player will be rewarded with a suite in the tower in return for their services.
• The quest can still be completed even if Roy Phillips had his way with Tenpenny.
• Tenpenny Tower: The Lone Wanderer can convince Tenpenny to give his permission for the ghouls to move in. After the ghouls are allowed to move in, Roy Phillips and Tenpenny will have a "disagreement" and Tenpenny will have an "accident," which results in Tenpenny's body being stuffed in a storage closet.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Mister Crowley wants someone to kill Tenpenny.

chr_000156df.summary: Herbert "Daring" Dashwood is a self-proclaimed wasteland adventurer. Long since retired as of 2277, he now resides in Tenpenny Tower in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
According to the 70-year-old Herbert, in his younger days, he was a prolific traveler and adventurer, performing feats that allowed him to amass a big enough fortune to purchase a residency under Allistair Tenpenny for a comfortable retirement. In these adventures, he was accompanied often by a 200-year-old ghoul named Argyle whom he first met in 2241 when Dashwood seduced and stole his girlfriend.

Daring Dashwood's Deeds:
The duo visited many places during their exploration of the wasteland. Dashwood can recall one instance where, in the summer of 2248, they were given permission to take shelter inside Rockopolis by the ruling King Crag. But when Dashwood had an "incident" with Crag's daughter, the two were exiled from the underground city.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Herbert will typically walk around Tenpenny Tower and occasionally play a joke on Cheng by messing with his terminal. He also occasionally visits the Federalist Lounge on the first floor and can otherwise be found in his room where he sits beside his radio.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• A Manhandled Manservant: If Argyle's body has been found, Dashwood can be informed of his fate to receive a key to his safe, which contains bottlecap mine schematics.
• The Replicated Man: Dashwood is in possession of a Replicated Man holotape.
• Tenpenny Tower: While looking for the key to the generator room, he implies the Lone Wanderer should steal it from him as a game. If the player character is caught stealing it, he will turn hostile in the usual way. Asking him to give up the key will provoke a response stating the Lone Wanderer is "no fun."

chr_000156de.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, patrol, travel, eat, sleep
chr_000156de.summary: Susan Lancaster is a former slaver from Paradise Falls who now lives in Tenpenny Tower as its resident "courtesan" in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
For some time, Susan was a member of the Paradise Falls slavers. For reasons unknown, she left the organization on bad terms, slitting the throat of one of their members before her departure. By 2277, she had gained residence at Tenpenny Tower, where she made a living as a high-class prostitute, or "escort" as the Tower's residents prefer.

Susan regularly services many of the tower's male residents, including Doctor Banfield, Herbert Dashwood, and Allistair Tenpenny himself. She maintains a rivalry with local gossip Millicent Wellington, who disapproves of her promiscuity, and is secretly carrying out an affair with her husband Edgar. When not with her customers, she spends her free time shopping or drinking at the Federalist Lounge, taking her meals at the Café Beau Monde.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Susan can be found in a different bed every night of the week between 10 p.m. and midnight, always wearing sexy sleepwear. On Monday, she's in Wellington's bed, she is with Banfield both Tuesday and Thursday night, Hawthorne on Wednesday, Mr. Cheng on Friday, while Sunday nights are spent with Dashwood. Even after moving in with Mister Burke, she continues her weekly rounds and never gets around to sharing a bed with him. She has sexual relations with every man in Tenpenny Tower, except Anthony Ling, who is implied to be homosexual, thus having no use for her "services."

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Strictly Business: Susan is one of the VIPs Grouse wants the Lone Wanderer to bring in. Completing the Tenpenny Tower quest in the ghouls' favor will mean Susan is counted as dead when the Strictly Business quest is acquired.
• Tenpenny Tower: Susan is one of the residents one has to convince to allow the ghouls to live in the tower.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Allistair Tenpenny is convinced into allowing Roy Phillips to move into the tower, Susan will move into Mr. Burke's quarters, but will not leave the tower.
• A love letter in her room reveals that she is having an affair with Edgar Wellington II. Showing this letter to Millicent Wellington will cause her to murder both Edgar and Susan for their treachery.

chr_000156dd.summary: Tiffany Cheng is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents, Cheng Family. Found primarily around Penthouse Suites. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Tiffany Cheng spends most of her days avoiding her husband, drinking in the Federalist Lounge, or shopping down on the first level. She eats at the Café Beau Monde and then returns to the Cheng suite and spends some time in her room before going to sleep.

chr_000156dc.summary: Irving Cheng is an inhabitant of Tenpenny Tower in 2277, who is married to Tiffany Cheng.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Irving, a wealthy elderly man with a secret identity, believes himself to be the direct descendant of Chairman Cheng, the leader of the People's Republic of China before the War. Prideful of his assumed lineage, he insists on addressing himself and all others as "comrade," and is embarrassed by his own given name, as it fails to reflect his imagined heritage.

In his computer terminal, he writes that his father was one of the leading officers in the Chinese Army. He also writes about his "plans" for creating a communist society in Tenpenny Tower, which he terms the "Tenpenny Commune." Cheng heavily implies he is prejudiced against ghouls, as with many of the other Tenpenny residents.

chr_000156db.summary: Anthony Ling is the owner of Tenpenny Tower's sole clothing store, New Urban Apparel, and one of the tower's residents. He is one of several openly gay characters in the game.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The proprietor of Tenpenny Tower's finest (and only) clothing store, Ling carries a selection of pre-War apparel salvaged throughout the years. Ling advertises his business to visitors of the tower, suggesting that they "upgrade to fabulous" at the New Urban Apparel; he firmly believes that every resident of Tenpenny Tower deserves to live in luxury, due to their smarts, beauty, and/or wealth. To him, it is simply survival of the fittest, and he is one of the winners. As such, he is firmly opposed to letting Roy Phillips and his ghouls inside the tower. He considers them to be less than human, labeling them as monsters who devour their own children, and refuses to even consider living alongside them.

As a whole, he fits in with the snobbish, privileged residents of the tower.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: Anthony Ling is one of the residents who needs to be convinced to allow ghouls to live in the tower.

Effects of player's actions:
• Anthony Ling can vanish from Tenpenny Tower if he has been robbed before trying to convince him to live with ghouls, but after talking to Allistair Tenpenny, he will be noted as convinced and payment can be received.
• If forced out of Tenpenny Tower through dialogue, he may be found loitering around Megaton's entrance.

Other interactions:
• He will comment negatively on the Lone Wanderer's clothing, regardless of what they are wearing.
• Robbing his safe results in Ling informing the Lone Wanderer that he is frustrated that Tenpenny Tower is not as safe as he thought and leaves.

chr_000156da.summary: Lydia Montenegro is a hispanic elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Lydia runs the Boutique Le Chic, which serves as the general store. She speaks as though she's running a high-end shop and not peddling salvage to wasteland dwellers, such is the elitist illusion she lives under. Lydia spends her days in the shop, then relaxes at the Federalist Lounge with her friend Michael Hawthorne.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: She is one of several bigoted residents that the Lone Wanderer must convince to change her views if they choose to advocate for Roy Phillips and the rest of the ghouls' admission into Tenpenny Tower.

Effects of player's actions:
She will leave the tower if her safe in Boutique le Chic is looted, claiming it's not safe despite all the guards. If her safe is looted before she is spoken to, which triggers her to leave and wander aimlessly around the wasteland, she will only come back if Roy and his gang are killed.

If she is convinced to leave, or simply killed, house upgrades will no longer be available to buy. If this happens, the only other option is to let the ghouls invade the tower. After the invasion, Michael Masters will take over the shop, and his shop will sell the house upgrades.

chr_000156d9.summary: Doctor Banfield is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man, Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The physician for Tenpenny Tower, Banfield runs the wellness center, and is responsible for the health of the Tower's residents. He achieves this primarily by providing them with various prescription drugs and his own concoctions based on pre-War medicines. While Banfield is not terribly fond of the Tower's landlord, he is wary of crossing him. It's not terribly difficult, as Tenpenny rarely comes down and Banfield only had to treat him once, for "bed sores".

It's not clear where Banfield comes from, but he does make mention of some of his scientific colleagues publishing papers. Much of Banfield's knowledge of ghouls, for example, comes from papers published by his colleagues, although he never actually verified their findings (and, unsurprisingly, has never been published).

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tenpenny Tower: Banfield has always wanted to experiment on ghouls so he can learn more about them but hasn't had the opportunity. As a result, Banfield is willing to allow ghouls to move into the tower so he can perform some tests on them. If the Lone Wanderer asks him about it, he will tell them that he has found, through research, that all ghouls will eventually become feral (though he also spouts this theory before the ghouls are let in).

Other interactions:
• Banfield keeps to a regular schedule, working at the wellness center, with a break at noon to eat lunch at the Café Beau Monde or the Federalist Lounge On Tuesdays and Thursdays, he's locked up in a penthouse with Susan Lancaster.

chr_000156d8.summary: Millicent Wellington is a resident of Tenpenny Tower in 2277, who can often be found arguing with her husband, Edgar Wellington II, or demanding his attention.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Millicent is one of the few souls who live in security in the Capital Wasteland, behind the stone walls of Tenpenny Tower. She lives in the tower with her husband, Edgar and, like her husband, comes off as rude and snobbish. She is the Tower's resident gossip and is infamous among its inhabitants for her busybody nature, to the point where her husband can be heard calling her a "social hermit" for her inability to form friendships with the female residents of the tower. She rejects being asked to socialize with them, chalking up her meager social circle as being a product of their jealousy towards her, rather than acknowledge the role her gossiping has had in influencing her relationships with her fellow residents.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Tenpenny Tower: She is one of several residents the Lone Wanderer must try to convince to change her mind if they are attempting to help move Roy Phillips' ghouls into Tenpenny Tower.

Effects of player's actions:
If the Lone Wanderer takes the love letter off Susan Lancaster's desk and takes it to Millicent, she will threaten to kill both her husband and his mistress, and will immediately run off to find her husband. She will proceed to kill him with her 10mm pistol, and go after Susan herself (the guards seem not to mind). After both murders are committed, she will abandon Tenpenny Tower and head for the Warrington trainyard, where she will head into the tunnels to meet her death at the hands of the ghouls.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only if one shows her the love letter.

chr_000156d7.role: Tenpenny Tower Residents, Wellington Family — Caucasian
chr_000156d7.summary: Edgar Wellington II is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 85 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents, Wellington Family. Found primarily around Tenpenny Suites. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Edgar Wellington spends most of his time in his suite with his wife, Millicent, who he despises; but like her, he only leaves to eat a couple of times a day. He sleeps with her in their bed a few hours every night (and sneaks out to sleep with Susan Lancaster on Mondays).

He is very proud of his luxurious lifestyle at Tenpenny Tower and believes himself to be above the common wastelander. Like most of the residents of Tenpenny Tower, he is a ghoul-hater due to Roy Phillips' persistent efforts to get inside.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Wellington is married to Millicent Wellington, but also has an affair with Susan Lancaster, an ex-slaver and the resident prostitute.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Wellington spends the day walking around Tenpenny Tower together with Millicent Wellington. She attempts to talk to him, but he shows little interest and doesn't listen to her, which in turn makes her angry. On Monday nights Edgar sneaks out of his room and spends the night with his mistress, Susan Lancaster.

chr_000156d6.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: eat, travel, sleep, sandbox
chr_000156d6.summary: Michael Hawthorne is a frequent patron at Tenpenny Tower's Federalist Lounge and is known to be the local drunk.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Michael Hawthorne is one of Tenpenny Tower's residents and a primary visitor to its Federalist Lounge. His drinking habits have taken over his life and his life savings, to the point where he may as well have a reserved seat at the lounge due to how frequent his visits are. Although little is known about Michael's background, during his conversations with Herbert Dashwood he jokes that he has been drinking since he was a toddler. When Dashwood warns him to be careful with his remaining brain cells, he replies "Nah, drown the buggers!" and shows little concern for his own wellbeing.

Despite his constant drunken stupor, he has formed friendships with some of the other residents.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Michael Hawthorne wanders Tenpenny Tower but always returns to the Federalist Lounge for a drink. On Wednesday nights, he can be seen in bed with the local courtesan of the tower, Susan Lancaster.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
Upon first meeting him, he will jovially ask the Lone Wanderer to share a drink with him, in which he will then begin discussing the ghoul business around the tower.

chr_000156d5.summary: Security Guard is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 70 HP). Affiliated with Tenpenny Tower Residents. Found primarily around Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Directly connected to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They are hired by Allistair Tenpenny to ensure the security of Tenpenny Tower and its residents. Their main concern is to make sure unwelcome visitors don't get in, like Roy Phillips and his group of ghouls. Gustavo is the leader of these guards. The guards will react and attempt to subdue the Lone Wanderer should they start any trouble.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: They can be found outside the tower at the guard post and in areas around the building as well as inside on the different levels. Several guards stand near the main gate. There is also an area to the right once you enter the Tower that has several cots and tables. This is where the guards sleep at night or rest during the day.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2227, Dr. Preston is a kind old man who is well-loved by Rivet City's denizens. Much of this has to do with the fact that he genuinely loves helping the injured and the sick. He takes his job in the Rivet City clinic seriously and treats his patients to the best of his ability. As part of this duty, he gives weekly checkups to Doctor Li because of how important her health is to the city, though Doctor Li herself views this as a waste of time. Furthermore, although Doctor Preston does not go to church (and has a low tolerance for faith-based practices), he allows Father Clifford and Diego to pray with his patients so long as they are not too much of a disturbance.

The doctor is a creature of habit in his personal life.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Doctor Preston wakes up at 6 a.m. and eats at the Weatherly Hotel until 8 a.m. He will spend the next 13 hours in the Rivet City clinic, only coming out once at 4 p.m. to eat dinner at the Weatherly Hotel until 6 p.m. before returning. At 10 p.m., he will leave the clinic and go to sleep in his room. On Thursdays, Doctor Preston will additionally visit Doctor Li in the Rivet City science lab from 8 to 10 p.m. for her weekly checkup; this will stop happening after she leaves the city.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Doctor Preston offers some information on the android, but dismisses the whole affair as a hoax.
• The doctor can be convinced to give over the holotape We got the tech, now we need the doc., through an Average Speech challenge (Speech 55), or a bribe of 100 caps.
• Similarly, a Speech 70 challenge, a Medicine 70 challenge, or another bribe of 100 caps can be used to persuade Doctor Preston to reveal Pinkerton as Rivet City's only facial surgeon.
• Wasteland Survival Guide: Doctor Preston can offer an avenue to peruse finding the true history of Rivet City.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: This character informs the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

chr_000156cf.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, sleep
chr_000156cf.summary: Abraham Washington is the owner and curator of the Capitol Preservation Society in Rivet City in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The 45 year old Abraham continues his parents' work at the Capitol Preservation Society, focusing on preserving the history of the United States, or at least an approximation thereof. Washington believes that his collection will eventually allow others to explore the American heritage, learn about the sacrifices made by those who came before, and at minimum preserve centuries of history almost lost in the fires of the Great War. He considers every wastelander to still be the children of the country, and in order to respect it, everyone should learn its history.

His greatest fear is that uneducated people and their casual disdain for history will cause America to fade from memory, and the once great nation will only be a blasted wasteland to future generations.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Abraham will wake up in his room at 10 a.m., stay there for an hour, then head to the Capitol Preservation Society, where he will stay for the next 14 hours. At 12 a.m., he will return to his room, and at 2 a.m., he will retire to his bed.

Abraham has two unused AI packages, and, which indicate that he would also be intended to have lunch and dinner at the Weatherly Hotel from 2 to 4 p.m. and 10 p.m. to 12 a.m. There is fully implemented dialogue that is unable to play because Abraham does not use these packages.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Stealing Independence: Washington tasks the Lone Wanderer with retrieving the Declaration of Independence from the National Archives.
• In addition, he buys the Bill of Rights and the Magna Carta for 100 and 75 caps respectively; alternatively, he will purchase them for 125 and 100 caps respectively, if one has a minimum Barter skill of 70.
• Agatha's Song: The Soil Stradivarius, a pre-War violin, can be sold to Washington for 200 caps (300 by passing a Speech check).
• Lincoln's Profit Margins: Washington is one of the potential buyers of the various Lincoln artifacts found in the Museum of History.

Other interactions:
When asked about the history of the Declaration of Independence, Washington will state the following:

It is a prime example of Abraham's casual approach to historical knowledge.

chr_000156ce.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_000156ce.summary: Diego is the acolyte of Saint Monica's Church and seminarian to Father Clifford in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Diego, now 18, was abandoned by his father in Rivet City a few years prior to 2277. Father Clifford took Diego in, and the pair have become like father and son. As a result, Diego has become the acolyte of Saint Monica's Church and next in line for the priesthood, currently studying the life of Saint Monica to prepare for this succession. Most of Father Clifford's sermons are centered around this saint; he delivers one daily even though he only has an audience on Sundays. Diego is mildly concerned by this, though Clifford believes that God and Saint Monica are in his audience as well. Although popular, these repetitive sermons easily bore the audience to sleep. Though he tries to be neutral when others complain about this, secretly even Diego himself falls victim to this.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• A Nice Day for a Right Wedding: There are rumors of his involvement with Angela Staley. Depending on player actions, his relationship with Angela or with the church may suffer:
• If one threatens to tell Father Clifford of Diego and Angela's actions, Diego will resolve not to see Angela again, even as a friend. This will break her heart, and they will no longer interact with each other.
• If one lies Father Clifford that Diego has broken his vow of chastity, Clifford will excommunicate Diego, kicking him out of the priesthood. He would then ask Angela to marry him, to which she would say yes. However, this will then allow Diego and Angela to marry, by which point Father Clifford will also have calmed down.
• If one helps Angela seduce Diego using ant queen pheromones, the lovers will be caught in the act by Father Clifford.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Father Clifford is the head of the Catholic derived Saint Monica's Church in Rivet City. He is the spiritual guide for the inhabitants of Rivet City, and spends his time tending to his flock. However, he does not spend all of his time in the church. Every day, he leaves for a few hours to engage the community and encourage more people to attend mass, especially those he sees as living immorally or unproductively, such as Brock, Flak, and Trinnie.

Father Clifford also concerns himself with the community as a whole. He and Diego occasionally visit the Rivet City clinic to pray for the patients. As he puts it, "the Holy Spirit can be a balm to the soul." Doctor Preston doesn't mind so long as they don't disturb the patients' rest or try to convince them of faith healing.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Reception towards Father Clifford is widely varied, though everyone seems to agree his sermons are boring. His regular audience is very appreciative of his services, which help them find comfort through faith. Vera Weatherly particularly appreciates him, giving both Clifford and his acolyte free meals as a sign of her devotion. His counseling helps assuage Mei Wong's fears about those who seek to harm her, On the other end, he is poorly received by the staff and patrons of The Muddy Rudder, who consider him an unwanted, moralizing intrusion into their way of life. This has even led to Belle Bonny throwing him out before. Among others, Ted Strayer also refuses his guidance, as Ted does not believe faith has ever provided for him.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Father Clifford is normally seen in and around Saint Monica's Church but will roam around the inside of Rivet City talking to other residents. On occasion, Father Clifford can be found in the Muddy Rudder, lecturing anyone present about sin. Every Sunday, he holds a mass which many of Rivet City's inhabitants attend.

Father Clifford wakes up at 6 a.m. every day and eats at the Weatherly Hotel. At 8 a.m., he returns to Saint Monica's Church to deliver his sermon until 10 a.m., and roams around the church for another hour. If the day is Sunday, he spends that hour interacting with his audience. Afterwards, the father's schedule depends on the day of the week. On Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, he will wait until 2 p.m., then go visit the Rivet City clinic with Diego until 4 p.m., then return.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Early life:
Madison was born around the year 2229. Her admiration for James later developed into romantic feelings over the course of their work, but she kept them hidden out of respect for James' marriage to Catherine. Though it strained her personal relationship with them, her professional relationship never changed.

The progress of the project faced numerous complications, not the least of which were frequent super mutant attacks, but the martial support of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel allowed them to continue in relative safety, though Madison personally did not trust the organization's motives for lending their aid.

chr_000156cb.summary: Janice Kaplinski is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 40 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents, Dr. Li's Research Team. Found primarily around Science Lab. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, The Waters of Life, The Replicated Man.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born around 2247 to 2248, Janice has been a part of the Rivet City science team for the last decade of her life. Looking for a career, she joined Doctor Madison Li at the Rivet City science lab when the latter needed an assistant; regarding the decision, Janice remarks that "it was either [that] or wind up dead in a ditch someplace."

In her time under Dr. Li's tutelage, Janice has come into her own as an accomplished botanist. She is every bit the equal to Doctor Li and James in technical knowledge, though she lacks their genius or ambition. managing hydroponics and directing the lab technicians, or her own independent work in developing new hydroponic crops, such as a new strain of lima beans and, in the near future, broccoli.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
Janice interacts primarily with the members of the Rivet City science team, but even then only in a professional sense for the most part: she may be observed briefly talking to Henry Young or Garza regarding maintenance of the hydroponics, while she only engages in generic small talk with Anna Holt.

Janice has a deeper bond with Doctor Li; her admiration for Doctor Li is a "classic case of hero worship," and Janice has complete faith in Doctor Li and their work together. Meanwhile, she is also close friends with Doctor Preston, who treats her like the daughter he never had, often trying to motivate Janice to lighten up and interact with others more.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Janice spends most of her day in the Rivet City science lab conducting experiments and talking with other lab personnel. At 7:00 a.m., she leaves the lab for the Weatherly Hotel to eat for around two hours before returning to the lab. She spends the entire day in the lab until leaving again for the Weatherly Hotel at night, with the exact time dependent on the day of the week:
• Monday, Wednesday, Friday: From 4 to 6 p.m.
• Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday: From 7 to 9 p.m.

At 10 p.m., Janice goes to sleep in the science team's quarters inside the lab.

chr_000156ca.summary: Doctor Horace Pinkerton is a reclusive scientist and ex-member of the Rivet City Council, presently residing in the broken-off bow of the pre-War aircraft carrier housing Rivet City in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City founder:
Born around 2217, Around 2237, they abandoned their former holdings and struck out into the wasteland to set up a new research facility elsewhere. The search eventually brought them to an abandoned U.S. Navy aircraft carrier resting on the shores of the Potomac River. After clearing out a nesting population of mirelurks, Pinkerton and his team moved into the carrier, which still had an intact science lab for them to use.

Over the next two years, seeing other wastelanders flock to their new home and a community beginning to form, Pinkerton spearheaded the formation of a governing body for the newly-minted Rivet City, creating the original incarnation of the Rivet City Council, with himself representing the science lab, Annette Holmes for the civilian populace, and Brad Danvers for the security force.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Wasteland Survival Guide: The Lone Wanderer can potentially track down the reclusive Pinkerton to fulfill an optional objective to learn the true history of Rivet City.
• The Replicated Man: The Lone Wanderer can optionally ask Pinkerton about his involvement with surgically altering a missing android from the Commonwealth.

Other interactions:
During and after completing The Replicated Man, the player character can receive facial reconstruction surgery from Pinkerton free of charge.

chr_000156c8.summary: Christie Young is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents, Young Family. Found primarily around Upper Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Christie and her family (husband Henry and daughter C.J.) live what could be considered "normal," middle-class lives in Rivet City. While her husband works as a handyman and mechanic for devices around the ship, she cleans the halls and keeps the ship's public areas tidy -- both thankless but necessary jobs. Christie's marriage is peaceful, and she enjoys chatting with Henry about his work, or going on walks with him on the flight deck. They also strive to raise their daughter well, reading her bedtime stories and allowing her ample play time (provided she does her chores, of course). If C.J. ever goes missing, she and Henry would both be worried sick to the point of refusing to speak about anything else.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: In the morning and early evening she can be found in the Rivet City market, usually to get something to eat at Gary's Galley. In the late mornings and afternoon, she can be found on the upper deck, sweeping the floors. At night she sleeps in her family's quarters on the upper deck.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: This character informs the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.
• The Runaways: If James Hargrave is convinced to run away from Rivet City, C.J. Young will follow him. Unlike James' mother Tammy, Christie and Henry will immediately notice the children's disappearance and inform security about it. If she or Henry are talked to during this, they will only say they are worried about C.J. and refuse to talk any further. This will also add the note C.J. Young is missing if it hadn't been obtained before. They will only engage in conversation again after C.J. returns to Rivet City, and they will be very grateful to the Lone Wanderer for bringing her back.

sections.text:
Henry's responsibility is general handiwork in Rivet City. Because of the frequency of repairs and the size of the settlement, he rarely has time to see his daughter C.J. Henry frequently laments the lack of people in his line of work and is privately frustrated with how few residents seem to pull their weight. Despite his attempts to keep his frustrations private he cannot help but to show some disdain and pity for hangar deck residents, barring Seagrave Holmes. As he is about the only other person more familiar with the city than he is. Such as the case with Tammy Hargrave, and emotionally abusive drunk who tried to keep their children apart due to her vanity,

Although his daughter's friendship with James Hargrave is generally looked at with concern by other Rivet City residents, his wife Christie instead hopes that C.J.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A trusting and honest young girl, C.J. is one of the happiest kids found in the Capital Wasteland. She's been raised by two loving parents and lives a great life in Rivet City. She spends her time hanging out on the flight deck or exploring the aircraft carrier with her best friend, James Hargrave. A year younger than C.J., James picks on her mercilessly. Nevertheless, she continues to forgive him for his teasing and the two remain best friends.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: C.J. is the daughter of Christie and Henry Young. She is the best (and only) friend of James Hargrave.

chr_000156c5.summary: Tammy Hargrave is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 85 HP). Affiliated with Hargrave Family, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Midship Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Tammy is a sour, middle-aged alcoholic, who married her husband, James' father, out of sheer desperation. Tammy believes that he just ran off one day and blames James for his disappearance. She assumes that he died at the hands of raiders and was left to take care of his son James alone. Due to this belief, she emotionally abuses James, who in turn has developed a reputation as a troublemaker. Her abuse isn't an act, her bitterness has coalesced into a lingering hatred and she would be fine selling him to the first buyer if the people of Rivet City would let her.

Tammy considers herself better than most of Rivet City's citizens, while ironically spending her time, unemployed and drunk in the Muddy Rudder surrounded by riffraff. Often not returning home for days at a time, leaving James to fend for himself.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Tammy is the mother of James Hargrave, and an emotionally abusive alcoholic who wouldn't mind selling him into slavery. Her husband, who she married because she was desperate, died in the wasteland. She uses this as an excuse to treat her son horribly, often emotionally abusing him. Due to her actions she has a poor reputation among the citizenry of Rivet City.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She can be found in the common bedroom area on the midship deck, in The Muddy Rudder, or occasionally the marketplace.
