chr_000156c4.summary: James Hargrave is a hispanic child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Hargrave Family, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Midship Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
James Hargrave is one of Rivet City's few children. His father is deceased, having died while in the wasteland, specifically Andale. His alcoholic mother, Tammy Hargrave, believes that he just ran off one day and blames James for his disappearance. Due to this belief, she emotionally abuses James, who in turn has developed a reputation as a troublemaker. Her abuse isn't an act, her bitterness has coalesced into a lingering hatred, and she would be fine selling him to the first buyer, if the people of Rivet City would let her. She tends to spend her time drunk in The Muddy Rudder and doesn't return home for days at a time, leaving James to fend for himself.

James is alternately sullen and wild and will do just about anything on a dare. He is capable of holding a grudge for months. He is loyal to his only friend C.J.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: James is the son of Tammy Hargrave, an emotionally abusive alcoholic who wouldn't mind selling him into slavery, and a father who died in the wasteland. His only friend, as there are no other children in the city, is C.J. Young. He and C.J. spend their time playing in the storage room or hanging around on the flight deck. He has developed a reputation similar to his mother, and a similar resentment towards her. Even keeping the drug addict Paulie Cantelli at bay, as to not give James a bad role model.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Wasteland Survival Guide: If asked about the history of the city, James will remark sarcastically about his father building it and that his mother is the "mirelurk queen." His remarks has an alternate should she be deceased or enslaved. If pressed about knowing anything about the city whatsoever, he will comment that it's a big boat.
• The Runaways: Should James Hargrave have been convinced to run away from home he will take C.J. Young with him. or from anyone else, security will look for them.
• If the player brings up the issue about his alcoholic mother, he gets angry. This leads to a Speech option that goads James into running away from home. If successful, he runs away with C.J. Young and the Lone Wanderer gains negative Karma. They can later be found at Anacostia Crossing Station.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Trinnie was, until recently, a resident of Little Lamplight. She has since become completely wasted on alcohol and chems 24/7. She spends her days in the Muddy Rudder and then takes a break to go to A Quick Fix and "borrow" some chems. She then goes off to hide and enjoy the high for a bit before returning to the Muddy Rudder. Belle and Brock feel bad for Trinnie and let her sleep in their quarters. She has been known to turn tricks to get money, but she is not forced to by Belle or Brock.

Trinnie's medical information may be accessed from Doctor Preston's terminal in the Rivet City clinic and it reads as follows:
Surprisingly healthy, apart from the alcoholism and other chronic dangers of her line of work. Guess they grow them strong in Lamplight.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She spends most of her time at the Muddy Rudder drinking and interacting with other non-player characters.

• Giving her 25 caps for drinks will result in getting her drunk and opening a Speech check. If successful, she will tell where Belle from the Muddy Rudder keeps a stash of caps: in a box under her bed.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Brock works for Belle Bonny as a bouncer at the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. He intervenes at the slightest sign of trouble, and many people have been sent to Doctor Preston's clinic by him as a result. When Belle Bonny is sleeping, Brock runs the bar.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: During the day, Brock can be found in the Rivet City market, usually in the morning. He will eat at Gary's Galley and wander about the flight deck in the afternoon for a while. After that, he works at the Muddy Rudder and goes to sleep in the side room of the establishment.

chr_000156c1.summary: Belle Bonny is the owner of the Muddy Rudder in Rivet City. Bonny rarely leaves her bar and keeps it open longer than most places, including the Weatherly Hotel.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Born around Birthdates, Belle Bonny is one of the oldest citizens of Rivet City. She arrived around, setting up the Muddy Rudder, a place of no tabs and fixed prices since it opened. The Rudder became the local working man's watering hole (or dive bar, as some would prefer), and Bonny has been running it with her unique kind of charm for years: acerbic, direct, and absolutely no-nonsense. Any new customers quickly learn not to cross her: they are fresh meat and starting anything will result in Brock promptly kicking them out. She does not have any doubts as to what her place is and what people come for. In fact, she knows full well the alcohol she serves might not be completely safe to drink, and anyone asking will be flatly told the truth, before Bonny asks what kind of poison they favor.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Bonny can provide some breadcrumbs on the trail of holotapes, but is unable to provide more concrete information.
• Wasteland Survival Guide: Bonny can point the player in the direction of Horace Pinkerton, but only if the player mentions Bannon claiming to be the founder of Rivet City. The incensed Belle will explain where to find Pinkerton.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Bonny can provide some information about where to find Ted Strayer.

chr_000156bf.summary: Mei Wong is a asian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Midship Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mei is a reserved woman who does not like to talk. She was previously a slave, once held at Paradise Falls, and was owned by Allistair Tenpenny, but she managed to escape and went into hiding. Her past is known by Harkness and he has promised that she is safe in town. She is knowledgeable about the slavers and suspects that Sister could be a slaver but she is unable to prove her hunch and she is scared of him. Luckily, he does not recognize her.

She lives in the common room of Rivet City and can usually be found there or in the Rivet City market. Mei can sometimes be found outside, wandering the flight deck, near James Hargrave and C.J. Young's baseball field.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: This character informs the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.
• Slave Hunt: Speaking with her starts the unmarked quest.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer offers to help her protect herself, they will give her 25 caps to buy a gun from Flak 'N Shrapnel's, resulting in a gain of Karma.
• If the Lone Wanderer informs Sister that she is an escaped slave, she will commit suicide resulting in a loss of Karma.
• If Sister has been killed, she will say, "I heard that Sister is dead, thank God."

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • The gun will appear only if you choose to provide her with 25 caps to buy a weapon from Flak 'N Shrapnel's.

chr_000156be.summary: Ted Strayer is a wasteland vagabond who decided to become a Rivet City resident in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ted has spend most of his life wandering the wasteland. Since his father's passing, leaving him with money to rely on, as he has three square meals a day, and a safe place to stay. One that can be described as overly relaxed, as he uses his caps to feed his drug addiction and has no plans for any future. It is easy to pique his interest, but it's difficult to hold it.

His father Jeff Strayer was a mercenary, who before passing was a part of a five-person expedition to Fort Constantine. The expedition was successful and it allowed him to accumulate a small fortune. However events of this expedition led him to become a target by another former member, Mister Crowley.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can be found in the Capitol Preservation Society in the afternoon. Furthermore, he frequents The Muddy Rudder bar and the common room between 4 and 6 a.m., along with wandering around the flight deck from noon to 2 p.m.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Ted is one of Crowley's targets and has one of the three special keys. It can be purchased from him for 25 caps, he could be convinced to part with it with a Speech check, or threatened to hand it over with either Strength 6+ or the Toughness perk.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Mr. Lopez is convinced not to kill himself, Ted will start learning how to read under his stead.

chr_000156bd.summary: Angela Staley is the daughter of Gary Staley, running a family restaurant, Gary's Galley, in Rivet City.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The sixteen-year-old Angela is a polite teenager inching towards adulthood. After a rough childhood that she survived with her dad, the two settled in Rivet City and set up a restaurant. Now, Angela alternates between working long hours assisting her overworked father at their galley and pining for love in her life, like her mother, actually, though Gary is skeptical of such a model: their relationship was very rocky. He loves his daughter immensely, though he tends to spend more time with her working at the restaurant than bonding in the rare moment of leisure. He cannot even give her money to compensate: while the galley has a lot of customers, it never makes enough caps to allow Angela to indulge herself and buy Bannon's fashions. Even water used in cooking has to come from the river.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Angela wakes up at 8 a.m. and eats breakfast at her father's restaurant, Gary's Galley, until 10 a.m. Afterwards, she will work at the restaurant serving customers until 6 p.m., when the shift ends. After that, she will move around the hangar, browsing stalls and chatting with other residents until 8 p.m., then return home for an hour. At 9 p.m., she will meet Diego on the flight deck and stay with him until 12 a.m., at which time she will go home and go to sleep. This is the same every day except Sunday, on which she wakes up at 7 a.m. for Sunday service in Saint Monica's Church, then stays there until 11 a.m. before returning to her normal schedule.

If Gary dies, Angela's schedule will shift; she will provide services at the restaurant for much longer hours, from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., after which her schedule will continue as normal.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• A Nice Day for a Right Wedding: The player can help Angela resolve the stalemate and help her seduce Diego. Doing so requires procuring ant queen pheromones. If the player character decides to help, Angela and Diego will marry and the player character may attend the wedding ceremony. Doing this results in positive Karma. Alternatively, the player can also persuade Diego to break things off with her, breaking her heart.

Other interactions:
• The Lone Wanderer can proposition her. Angela will spurn the advances.
• If Gary Staley dies for any reason, Angela will take over management of the galley and both her dialogue and interactions with other Rivet City denizens will change (see Rivet City conversations for examples).

chr_000156bc.summary: Gary Staley is a trader who lives in Rivet City and runs the Gary's Galley restaurant in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Gary is the owner and cook of Gary's Galley. He views himself as a gourmet chef, although he serves nothing more but canned food and an assortment of fruits and vegetables. He does occasionally sell high-quality produce, albeit at exorbitant prices. He is also the father of Angela Staley, and while they share a close relationship, he often neglects her in favor of maintaining his restaurant.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: GaryStaley), Gary Staley is defined as a Caucasian Elderly in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Faction memberships: Staley Family, Rivet City Residents. Appears in or relates to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

chr_000156bb.summary: Seagrave Holmes (b. circa 2247) is the proprietor of Rivet City Supply in Rivet City in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A genius tinkerer, Seagrave fixes anything he can get his hands on, but doesn't lord his abilities over others. He gets along well with common folk, fitting into their social world without even thinking about it. and this has made him intimately familiar with the inner workings of the ship. However, his years of repair work for the city have also left him with a chronic case of red-lung. Even still, Seagrave truly loves the city, spending countless hours tinkering, and often loses track of time when talking about it.

Despite his work for the city, Seagrave professes not to know much about its history or politics (due to his focus on keeping it afloat).

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
• Seagrave is generally to be found in his shop or (often on the flight deck), trying and failing to woo Vera Weatherly. He can also be found leaving his room, (mid-deck next to marketplace entry) around 2-4 a.m. The Lone Wanderer can overhear that she does not want to be with him as he reeks of sewage.
• Seagrave's store is restocked on Monday and Thursday.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Seagrave is in possession of a technical oriented Replicated Man holotape. He can be convinced to share the information with a Speech check, bribed for 100 caps, and a Science check. Further pressing him for information with a second Speech check another 100 cap bribe or a Science check will direct the player to Horace Pinkerton.
• The Wasteland Survival Guide: Should the player ask him, Seagrave has the second most information about the history of Rivet City, barring only Dr. Horace Pinkerton.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Seagrave can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.
• Council Seat: Bannon mentions that "his" Bannon will price gouge the Lone Wanderer on his wares in retribution.

chr_000156b9.summary: Dr. Zimmer is the director of the Institute's Synth Retention Bureau from the Commonwealth and a temporary resident of Rivet City in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
SRB director:
Born in 2219, sometime prior to or around 2277, Dr. Zimmer achieved the directorship of the the Institute's Synth Retention Bureau. That same year, the doctor personally ordered for tests on a strain of the Forced Evolutionary Virus to be carried out by the Institute's FEV lab lead scientist C. Syverson.

Hunting the android:
Later that same year, Zimmer left the Institute and journeyed south to the Capital Wasteland to conduct a personal search for a missing android. Accompanied by his android bodyguard, Armitage, he made his way to Rivet City in the hopes that their renowned science lab and its staff, especially fellow scientist Dr. Madison Li, could assist in the search for his missing property.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
The Replicated Man: Zimmer wants the Lone Wanderer to hunt down a rogue android.

Other interactions:
• If Zimmer is convinced the android is dead, he will leave Rivet City and disappear from the game.
• If killed, an android component is found on his body. However, Zimmer is identified in the game files as human.

chr_000156b8.summary: Vera Weatherly is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Weatherly Hotel, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Upper Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, Those!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
While Vera projects a quiet and demure attitude, this conceals a spirit of unshakeable determination. Vera is very proud of all she has achieved, including founding and even helping build her namesake hotel, which she named after a real location she read about in a book. Vera describes life in Rivet City as "noisy, dark, and smelly," but also understands that it is the safest settlement in the Capital Wasteland. Furthermore, she has faith in Doctor Li and her projects which could even provide more clean water for the settlement.

Although running the Weatherly Hotel is a full-time job for Vera, she actually has a relatively light schedule. This is thanks to her Mister Handy assistant, Mister Buckingham, who is more than capable of watching the hotel in her place for hours on end.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Vera is a prolific gossiper, constantly sharing grievances, advice, and banter with Cindy Cantelli (proprietor of A Quick Fix) and Angela Staley (server at Gary's Galley). Vera encourages Cindy to divorce her deadbeat chem addict husband Paulie, but also to give up her pursuit of Bannon, who barely even acknowledges her existence. (If Paulie winds up dead, Vera will also console Cindy over her loss). Meanwhile, Vera compliments Angela on how quickly she has grown up and gently urges her not to pursue her love interest Diego (since he, as acolyte of Saint Monica's Church, adheres to a vow of celibacy). Even so, if Angela and Diego manage to proceed with their wedding, Vera will be very happy for her and will attend their wedding.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Vera's regular daily schedule starts at 8 a.m., when she wakes up in her room in the Weatherly Hotel and then has breakfast in the hotel lobby until 10 a.m, when she begins working in the hotel until 6 p.m. At 6, she has dinner in her hotel, after which her specific schedule depends on the day, but ends with her heading back to her room at 8 p.m. and going to bed at 12 a.m. Her merchant services are generally available from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Vera's day-specific activities are as follows:
• On weekdays, Vera leaves the hotel and browses the Rivet City market from 12 to 2 p.m. before resuming her merchant services.
• On Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, Vera visits Saint Monica's Church from 8 to 10 p.m. before heading home.

chr_000156b7.summary: Cindy Cantelli is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 45 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents, Cantelli Family. Found primarily around Midship Deck. Directly connected to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide, You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Cindy and her husband Paulie own A Quick Fix, the drug dispensary in the Rivet City market. The shop has a reputation for having a good stock. However, it would be doing better if she could trust Paulie enough to be left unattended, let alone close the shop by himself. She's had to get Seagrave Holmes to make a secure storage unit for her, but Paulie stole the key and she has to get a new one. This is because Paulie is a chem addict who constantly steals from the shop to fuel his own addictions. Cindy has basically come to run the shop herself. At this point their marriage is almost nonexistent; they barely talk and have little in common. She, and others, have tried to talk some sense into him, but it hasn't worked, and the strain of his constant chem use and neglect has caused her to give up on him.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Cindy can be found at A Quick Fix during the market's business hours. She eats her lunch in the market and when she isn't doing this she can be found sleeping in her bed.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Wasteland Survival Guide: Cindy will tell the player to ask another character, Bannon, about the history of Rivet City.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should Cindy be deceased for whatever reason, Paulie Cantelli will run A Quick Fix.
• Should Paulie Cantelli be deceased for whatever reason, Cindy will find relief in his loss.

chr_000156b5.summary: Bannon is the owner of Potomac Attire, a clothing store in the Rivet City marketplace, and a member of the Rivet City Council representing civilian interests.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Bannon is Rivet City's fashionista and most ruthless merchant. After immigrating to the city in, at the young age of 18, his trade in clothes of all kinds led to a meteoric rise in the power structure of the city and its marketplace. By the age of thirty, he is the civilian representative on the Rivet City Council, and convinced himself that the City's position as the strongest settlement in the wasteland is entirely due to his leadership and sponsoring its development. In fact, he claims that he organized and heads the city council, and considers the "equality" of citizens in Rivet City as a smokescreen to conceal its oligarch, Bannon of the Potomac Attire.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Wasteland Survival Guide: Bannon tells the player his (fake) version of Rivet City's history.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: This character informs the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.
• Council Seat: Bannon mentions that his council seat is being contested by Seagrave Holmes. He wants you to look for incriminating evidence against his opponent.
• Reporting Seagrave Holmes to Commander Danvers will cause Bannon to give the player a discount at his store, they will also receive schematics for the deathclaw gauntlet.
• Reporting Bannon to Danvers for trying to blackmail Seagrave Holmes will cause Bannon to dislike the Lone Wanderer. He will still trade with them but will charge more.

Merchant:
• Bannon has two shop inventories.

sections.text: Known locations: Upper Deck. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Casualwear, Pencil, Bannon's Room Key. Provides services: Armor, Supplies / Barter, Apparel & Goods.

chr_000156b4.summary: Shrapnel is a merchant who runs the weapons store Flak 'N Shrapnel's in the marketplace of Rivet City together with Flak in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Shrapnel is a former raider whose edge never dulled. He is a grizzled veteran of the wasteland and quite coarse in his interactions. Ever since settling in Rivet City with Flak, he has focused on selling weapons and ammunition. He gets along well with Flak thanks to their shared interest in guns, to the point of being almost polite, but he has a hard time toning down his attitude towards other denizens of the ship. He is making an effort to be more polite, at Flak's request. He mostly succeeds, primarily with long-time Rivet City residents, though he is still direct and no-nonsense. He dislikes being called Mister, preferring to go just by Shrapnel, including with people far younger than him.

Shrapnel is an alcoholic.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Shrapnel has a complex daily schedule, with some overlapping AI packages:
• He wakes up at 10:00 and works at the gun shop between 10:00 and 23:00, with a two hour break at 11:00 for lunch and at 21:00 for dinner.
• After closing up shop, he goes to drink at the Muddy Rudder for two hours at 0:00.
• On Tuesday and Thursday, he drinks for an hour, starting at 23:00.
• He goes back to sleep with Flak at 3:00, for eight hours (interrupted by the morning package).
• On Saturday, he goes to sleep at 23:00 and sleeps a full eight hours.

Things change if Flak is dead:
• Shrapnel wakes up at 7:00 and eats breakfast at Gary's Galley until 9:00.
• Shrapnel runs the whole shop for 16 hours straight, starting at 7:00.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Strictly Business: Should one enslave Flak for Grouse at Paradise Falls, Shrapnel will likely be close enough to notice the action and subsequently turn hostile.
• Sometimes, when Flak is enslaved, Shrapnel will leave Rivet City and travel to Paradise Falls, into the slave pens where Flak is being detained. He will still buy or sell if approached in the wasteland or Paradise Falls. He can be asked to see his inventory wherever he is. This is primarily due to a bug; see below.

Other interactions:
• With Flak, he sells ordnance and repairs weapons in Rivet City. Flak and Shrapnel share their store's inventory, so buying or selling from either one of them will update both of their stocks. This means that if Flak is enslaved by the player character for Paradise Falls, Flak 'N Shrapnel's in the marketplace will still be open.

chr_000156b3.summary:
Flak is a former slaver from Paradise Falls who runs the weapons store Flak 'N Shrapnel's in the marketplace of Rivet City together with Shrapnel in 2277.

His portrayal is part of the game's LGBT representation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Born around 2227, Flak was a member of the Paradise Falls slavers in his younger years. After years of that life, Flak chose to make a clean break and start over at Rivet City. focusing on running the gun shop with his partner, Shrapnel, an ex-raider. His homosexuality was known to the slavers of Paradise Falls, who regarded him as impressively tough; now in Rivet City, Flak's experiences and settling down as a businessman have tempered his attitude, making him almost polite, at least for a former slaver. (he's a big believer in superior firepower). As Flak and Shrapnel specialize in a broad range of weapons, including big guns, it's not difficult to find a more powerful weapon. Flak is practical, though: He keeps the worst condition weapons as display pieces, and the ones actually intended for sale are locked up.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Strictly Business: Flak is one of four VIP targets that Grouse of Paradise Falls wants enslaved. In Flak's case, it is to capture and punish him for divulging slaver secrets to Rivet City.
• If Flak is enslaved by the player character for Paradise Falls, Flak 'N Shrapnel's in the marketplace will still be open under Shrapnel.
• Wasteland Survival Guide: Flak provides a very minor clue, pointing towards Bannon as a source of history about the city.

Merchant:
• As gun merchants, Flak and Shrapnel consistently have a larger amount of caps than the other shops in Rivet City. Their shop can spawn every weapon in the game, and uses a separate spawn list for mini nukes, making them one of the only sources of the explosive devices.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: * The key is not actually obtainable. The game sets as a condition for obtaining it that Shrapnel be dead and Flak be dead or enslaved. Since Shrapnel is set as essential, he cannot die.

chr_000156b2.summary: Rivet City Security is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around Bridge Tower. Directly connected to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Bridge Tower. Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform, Hangar Key.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Born around 2247, Lana was married until 2275 when her husband, also a Rivet City security officer, died from a disease. She is an extremely busy woman, and she makes that clear to anyone who speaks to her; Accordingly, Danvers cares little about the city's history, as she is more concerned about the problems of the present. As second-in-command, Danvers is slated to take over as security chief if Harkness can no longer fill the role for any reason. This also makes her next in line for the position of security representative on the Rivet City Council. However, even without being on the council, she has some sway over it. If it becomes clear that anyone on or trying to be on the council has engaged in unsavory activities, she will make sure their political aspirations come to an end.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Danvers can be found patrolling the Rivet City market every night from 7 p.m. to 3 a.m. During this time, the market is closed, and if the Lone Wanderer is present, she and other characters may tell them to leave. If they continue to stay for too long, they may turn hostile. Otherwise, Danvers spends the rest of her day sleeping in the bridge tower, only waking up at 5 p.m. to eat until starting her night patrol.

Danvers has several additional AI routines that fail to start because her sleeping package is incorrectly implemented: it is intended to only last for eight hours (DanversSleep9x8, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.), but the schedule is not implemented, so she will sleep whenever she can. Her intended routine is to return from patrol and eat in the bridge tower at 7 a.m., then sleep from 9 a.m.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Wasteland Survival Guide: Commander Danvers can be asked about Rivet City's history but will have no information about it.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: Commander Danvers can tell the player about the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.
• Council Seat: The player must speak with her to turn in evidence ruining either Bannon's or Seagrave's council campaigns. The quest cannot be completed if she is killed.
• The Runaways: Should James Hargrave have been convinced to run away from home he will take C.J. Young with him. Commander Danvers can be asked about C.J's disappearance and will note having heard of it directly from Christie Young or from somewhere else if Christie is dead, saying security will look for the missing children.

chr_000156ac.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, eat, patrol, sleep
chr_000156ac.summary:
Robert Joseph "RJ" MacCready is the adolescent mayor of the child-exclusive settlement of Little Lamplight in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

By 2287, the grown-up MacCready is working as a mercenary in the Commonwealth, selling his services from the backroom of the Third Rail in Goodneighbor. He is a possible companion of the Sole Survivor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mayor of Little Lamplight:
Born in the Capital Wasteland to parents he never knew, MacCready became the head of the child-only colony of Little Lamplight in 2274. MacCready's impromptu coup resulted in him becoming mayor by popular vote (and Angela gaining the unwanted nickname of "Princess").

As mayor, it became MacCready's duty to ensure the town's defense against both the super mutants lurking in Murder Pass and all prospective human visitors -- a responsibility helped by his marksmanship skills and his distrusting, aggressive personality. According to MacCready, his marksmanship skills were self-taught, and engaging targets at long range was a strategic choice he made to avoid facing danger in the Capital Wasteland, especially given his young age and small stature.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text:
Though notoriously foul-mouthed and belligerent in his younger years, the adult MacCready is far more reserved and polite. Years of hard living turned him into a hardened fighter, coping with adversity through liberal use of sarcasm and humor. However, he is not totally immune to shock, as some atrocities of pre-War society can inspire his anger. While MacCready isn't averse to violence, he doesn't revel in it either. If possible, he will bluff his way through to minimize danger to himself and others.

On a more personal side, MacCready misses many features of life in the Capital Wasteland, including listening to DJ Three Dog's broadcasts on Galaxy News Radio and the monuments of downtown D.C.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: * Unlike the other Little Lamplight characters, there's no interaction possible with his inventory when trying to pickpocket him.

chr_000156ab.summary: Stacey is a african american child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 50 HP). Affiliated with Little Lamplighters. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Picking Up the Trail.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: She and another girl named Caps guarded Little Lamplight's front gate together. Caps took care of Stacey and enjoyed her company guarding, as well as the jokes she often made. Stacey used to search for hats to give to Caps to add to her collection, leading to her name. One day, Stacey was away from the gate while she was on duty, and Caps was killed when raiders suddenly attacked.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: Stacey), Stacey is defined as a African American Child in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Marked as essential (cannot be killed during normal gameplay until plot flags allow). Faction memberships: Little Lamplighters. Appears in or relates to quests: Picking Up the Trail.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 4, 50 HP. S.P.E.C.I.A.L. profile: STR 6, PER 7, END 5, CHA 3, INT 3, AGI 6, LCK 5. Behavioral traits: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: disgusted. AI packages: sleep, sandbox.

chr_000156aa.summary: Harkness (designation A3-21) is a third generation synth serving as the chief and council representative of the security force of Rivet City in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The synth-hunter:
Presently unknown to the man himself, Harkness was "born" A3-21, a synthetic humanoid ("synth" for short) created by the Institute, considered to be a cutting-edge prototype of the Generation 3 model as of 2277. After his creation circa 2242,

The official opinion of Institute members such as Dr. Zimmer was that synth escape attempts were merely malfunctions, a result of their complex artificial intelligence causing them to mimic human beliefs that they were not supposed to have. these doubts led him to desert his post and make an escape himself.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text: In his capacity as Rivet City's security chief, Harkness has cultivated a reputation as a hard-nosed leader with a rough but fair demeanor. This extends even to Rivet City's Hangar Deck citizens, who are considered a separate social class from its Upper Deck citizens, which makes him popular with the former group. However, he has no patience for troublemakers causing chaos on the ship, along with additional disdain for chem addicts like Paulie Cantelli (in Paulie's case, Harkness tries to encourage him to drop his habit).

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text:
Harkness is initially encountered at the bridge to Rivet City, during which he will vet the player character to decide whether or not to grant them access to the city, though he will always allow them to enter. Afterwards, in most outcomes, Harkness will return to his regular routine; on the other hand, if the player character tells him they are going to leave, he'll be stuck at the entrance for the rest of the game. However, in this case, the player character can still walk past him without incident.

For his regular routine, during the day, Harkness will stand outside the weapons store Flak 'N Shrapnel's in the Rivet City marketplace. He can also found on the top floor of the bridge tower from midnight to 6 a.m.

chr_000156a4.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sleep, sandbox
chr_000156a4.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Weapons, Armor, Books & Schematics, Supplies / Barter)
chr_000156a4.summary: Pronto is the owner of the Lock and Load weapons store working for the slavers at Paradise Falls in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rumored to be the son of old slaver, Pronto is the sole proprietor of the Lock and Load weapons store at Paradise Falls, taking over after the untimely death of the previous owner due to an apparent weapons mishap, or so claims Forty. Pronto receives very little respect from his slaver compatriots. As a result, he lacks a proper stock of quality armaments.

A poor selection of weapons to sell, coupled with the danger of being enslaved or hung from the sign at the entrance to Paradise Falls if he tries to protest or take the better loot by force, has driven Pronto to seek outside assistance to improve his store's stock. Apart from weapons obtained from slave runs, Pronto has created some of his merchandise himself, while also dabbling in designing his own custom weapons.

sections.title: Gameplay
sections.text:
During the unmarked quest Economics of Violence, Pronto will ask the player to obtain twenty Chinese assault rifles to improve his weapon stock. Up to nine rifles are able to be traded at any given time. Once all of the rifles are traded, it will take a full in-game day for Pronto's inventory to update to his new selection. Eulogy Jones will travel to Lock and Load anytime between the hours of 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. to collect profits from Pronto.

Bartering:
Pronto sells weapons, armor and clothing, consumables and ammunition, and has the ability to repair items. Upon completion of Economics of Violence, Pronto states that he will provide a 20% discount to the player; however, no such discount exists.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Economics of Violence: One can expand Pronto's shop by giving him 20 Chinese assault rifles. In addition, he will gain a few more caps (around 400 instead of 150).

chr_000156a3.summary: Cutter is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Cutter's Clinic. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Cutter was born into slavery in the pens at Paradise Falls. As a youth, she learned about wasteland medicine from her mother. After her mother died, Cutter took over the responsibility of taking care of the slaves. However, she became increasingly annoyed with their inability to fight back against their slavers. After almost a decade of being paid for her services, Cutter earned the caps needed to buy her freedom. However, she stayed at Paradise Falls and continues to practice medicine there as a free woman, because the slavers needed a talented medic.

Cutter also stays in Paradise Falls because she enjoys draining wealthy slavers of their caps, a form of retribution for her life as a slave. She enjoys getting paid by injured slavers who have more caps than common sense.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Cutter has actually two different stores with separate caps and wares.

Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Cutter is one of many wasteland doctors who can be spoken to about the android during this quest. She may express some familiarity with Horace Pinkerton in Rivet City.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Cutter's Clinic. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Doctor Fatigues. Provides services: Chems & Medicine, Supplies / Barter.

chr_000156a2.summary: Clover is a slave residing with her owner Eulogy Jones at the slaver stronghold of Paradise Falls in 2277. She is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Originally captured a few months prior to the Lone Wanderer leaving Vault 101 in 2277, Clover and her fellow slave Crimson were systematically broken mentally by the torture and abuse perpetrated by the slavers of Paradise Falls until they became obedient to their captors. Eulogy Jones himself claimed both as his personal slaves, using them for sex, personal protection, and as stress relief while continuing to abuse them to no end. Unlike Crimson, who managed to retain some of her will despite the slavers' torture, Clover succumbed to her conditioning, and as a result, her original personality was replaced by one of blind devotion and love to Eulogy (or whoever happens to own her). She willfully kills for, sleeps with, and does everything else she's ordered to do by her owner.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Companion:
• Clover can be recruited as a companion by talking to Eulogy Jones in his pad at Paradise Falls and paying 1,000 caps (500 with 50 Barter), and only while the player character has Evil Karma.
• If dismissed, Clover returns to Eulogy's pad at Paradise Falls (even if Eulogy Jones and everyone in Paradise Falls is dead). She can be re-hired at any time free of charge and regardless of Karma rating.

Other interactions:
• While serving as an active companion, she will occasionally lament about not being near her "daddy," Eulogy.
• If all the slavers in Paradise Falls are dead while she is present and not yet a companion, she will turn hostile and become permanently unobtainable as a companion.
• She will turn hostile against the player character if she catches them stealing too many times while in Paradise Falls.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Eulogy's Pad. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar, itm_0006415d, itm_00066c71, itm_000ae8ae, itm_0004c5f9.

chr_000156a1.summary: Crimson is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Eulogy's Pad. Directly connected to quests: Rescue from Paradise.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Crimson is a prostitute, one of two caught and pressed into slavery by Eulogy Jones a few months before meeting the Lone Wanderer. She along with Clover are abused by their master, and attempt to stay out of his way. They will not talk to strangers. When Eulogy is not present, they will speak with one another, usually to bicker. At times, Crimson will speak back to Eulogy when he insults her.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Crimson can be found following Eulogy Jones around in Paradise Falls. The best chance to meet her is in Eulogy's pad, located near the slave pens.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Rescue from Paradise: If the player character cannot convince Forty to leave the pen, they can convince Crimson to seduce him.

chr_000156a0.summary: Forty is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 10, 145 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Eulogy's Pad. Directly connected to quests: Rescue from Paradise.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Forty is Eulogy's second in command and earned his nickname from the fact that, throughout his life, he has killed 40 men. However, killing slaves is something Forty considers "sport" and does not count toward his total.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Rescue from Paradise: Forty guards the slave pens, and as such, he needs to be distracted (or killed) for the kids from Little Lamplight to be able to escape.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Eulogy's Pad. Notable equipment & inventory: Combat Armor, Paradise Falls Box Key, Chinese Assault Rifle.

chr_0001569f.role: Paradise Falls Slavers — African American Elderly
chr_0001569f.summary: Eulogy Jones is a african american elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 10, 145 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Eulogy's Pad. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man, Those!, Rescue from Paradise.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Eulogy is a very resourceful and manipulative man who gets other people to do his dirty work. He does not wish for anyone to interfere with his slaving operation and will not hesitate to get rid of anyone who tries. Although he may say he reached his position through hard work, he did it through careful tactics and from the efforts of other people such as his slaves, and he also murdered the former leader Harmon Jurley and took over the role. He rules through intimidation and fear so no one messes with him. He has two personal slaves, Crimson and Clover.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Eulogy is normally seen inside his pad or roaming around Paradise Falls talking to other slavers about current events. Occasionally he can be found in Cutter's Clinic talking to Cutter. He also makes a daily trip to the slave pens, to 'check the livestock' (Eulogy will always react the same way when he inspects the pens, even if the slaves are not present).

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Kid-Kidnapper: Jones asks the Lone Wanderer to kidnap a kid from Little Lamplight, Bumble. If completed, they will get the Boogeyman's hood as a reward.
• Rescue from Paradise: Save the kids by buying them from Eulogy for 2000 caps (1200 with a Speech/Barter check) or free them by obtaining the slave pen key (either by stealing it from Eulogy's pad or by taking it off the corpse of Eulogy or Forty).
• Those!: When finding Bryan Wilks a place to stay, he can be sold to Eulogy for 100 caps (300, with a successful Speech check). This will result in significant negative Karma.

Other interactions:
With enough negative Karma and 1000 caps (500 with 50 in Barter), Eulogy can sell the Lone Wanderer his bodyguard Clover, as a companion.

chr_0001569e.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, follow, sandbox
chr_0001569e.summary: Rory Maclaren is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Directly connected to quests: Rescue from Paradise.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Instead of waiting until someone wants to purchase him, he is highly motivated to escape and is constantly thinking of escape methods. He dislikes being pushed around and has attacked his captors many times. He is forced to be in the Box permanently where unruly slaves go.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Rescue from Paradise: As a condition of leaving Paradise Falls, Penny will ask the Lone Wanderer to escort Rory to the entrance.

Effects of player's actions:
Once freed, he will travel to Moriarty's Saloon. Provided he survives, he will stand in the room to the right where Mr. Burke is found. When attempting dialogue, he will only say "Hey. Talk fast, they hate it when I talk to customers."

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar, Wasteland Wanderer Outfit.

chr_0001569d.summary: Bleak is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Bleak is a slave that continuously plans her escape from Paradise Falls, spending her days memorizing the slavers' patrols and routine in hopes of using it to her advantage. She can be heard asking both Bronson and Breadbox for help in carrying out her plans but encounters issues with both each time. The former is too drunk to remember the equipment she asks for, repeatedly bringing her wrong items and failing to listen to her instructions, yet this does not stop her from giving him more chances to help and escape with her. The latter on the other hand does not wish to escape, and rejects her help, refusing to even listen to her proposals nor assist in any form, though she still offers him her aid should he change his mind.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Bleak can be found at the Paradise Falls slave house for the entire day.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar.

chr_0001569c.summary: Miss Jeanette is a ghoul character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jeanette lives in the Paradise Falls' adult pen with other enslaved individuals, including Breadbox, Bleak, and Bronson. Although she has little hope for an escape, when the Lone Wanderer approaches, she will plead for help in fleeing, as she has been enslaved a significant amount of time, with the market for ghoul slaves being less than optimal. Jeanette does not talk with the other slaves, even with Bleak who is planning to break out, as she keeps to herself and is in a disoriented state, the cause of which is unknown.

If one speaks with her further, she will comment on how abysmal the place is, how much she misses her brother, and requests that if they reach Underworld, they share with others the fact that she is okay.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the slave's pen door is unlocked, one can tell her to run for it, in which case she will be shot at, unless the slavers have been cleared out first. If she survives she may act as though she's "making a run for it" but she may stay in the pen, occasionally muttering "they told me not to go too far." If she makes it to the gate, she will disappear upon exit.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar.

chr_0001569b.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox
chr_0001569b.summary: Bronson is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Bronson is both a slave and a drunk, drinking as a coping mechanism as he spends his days making a mockery of himself for the slavers' amusement. He offers to sing and dance, or do something amusing, in exchange for alcohol. His reliance on the substance is to a point where he claims it is the only thing keeping him going or he would have ended his life as a result of being a slave; at the same time, he would rather drink himself to death than meet his end by slavers.

Bleak has been tasking Bronson with finding equipment, including slave collar detonators, to help them escape; this is to no avail as he consistently returns with the wrong items, hindered by his constant drunkenness as he fails to remember and recognize what Bleak is asking for.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Bronson is locked up in the Paradise Falls slave pen, spending his entire life there until he is killed or has escaped.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
When first interacting with him, he offers to show the Lone Wanderer something funny, or asks if they wish to hear a song or see a dance, but only in exchange for booze. However, the player cannot give any alcohol and therefore cannot exchange booze for anything.

chr_0001569a.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: disgusted. AI packages: sandbox
chr_0001569a.summary: Breadbox is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Breadbox is the oldest slave in the camp, having been enslaved for over 30 years. Young slaves are valuable as far as buying and selling goes, but at his advanced age, being deaf and suffering from dementia, he would not fetch any price and so the slavers leave him be.

He lives in the adult pen with other enslaved individuals, including Jeanette, Bleak, and Bronson. When the other slaves encourage him to join them in their escape, he opposes and refuses to participate, not even wanting to listen to Bleak's plans; he mentions that although the life of a slave is difficult, one is able to acclimate to it and is better than the alternative of death.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Breadbox is a slave locked up in the Paradise Falls slave pen, and can be found there the entire day. If one is able to open the gate and free the other slaves, Breadbox is the only one that will not flee, making him the only slave that can only be found at the pens unless killed.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar.

chr_00015699.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: follow, travel, sandbox, dialogue, sleep

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Bumble is the youngest and most naive inhabitant of Little Lamplight, eager to prove herself as a "big girl" and go on adventures. Despite being taught to hide if she sees a raider, slaver, or super mutant, out of curiosity, she may opt to question the Lone Wanderer if they are any of these rather than immediately fleeing. With the Child at Heart perk, Bumble is trusting enough to tell the Lone Wanderer her real name is Betty and gullibly believes them to be the "biggest kid" in Little Lamplight. However, she does not buy into the Lone Wanderer being a slaver, claiming that the player character is trying to scare her and assures herself that "Mayor-Mac" would not allow slavers in.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Bumble spends most of her time in the office building either with Joseph, or with Lucy in the clinic. She calls Joseph "Uncle Joseph," which annoys Penny into telling Bumble he's not her uncle. She looks up to Lucy as an older sister, wanting to be "big and tough" like her, and avoids going outside alone per her instructions.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Bumble is likely to be found at the office building. If she is not there, she sometimes is in the main cave or the Great Chamber.

chr_00015698.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, guard, travel, sandbox
chr_00015698.summary: Grouse is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man, Blood Ties, Strictly Business.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Grouse was born in 2247 and has been with the slavers since he was a teenager. His father was the former leader of the slavers before Eulogy Jones usurped him and rose to power. Because of this, Grouse believes that he has a legacy to live up to. A self-serving sociopath, using the position to project power where he has it. Grouse acts as a guard of the settlement. When the Lone Wanderer approaches he will demand to know why they are there. only slavers and the enslaved, and depending on if the Lone Wanderer is wearing a Vault jumpsuit he will comment on how lucky they are for not having been immediately enslaved. Which he threatens to do if they waste his time.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Strictly Business: Grouse mentions that Eulogy Jones wants to acquire some VIP targets. If one accepts his proposal to capture some slaves, he will give the Lone Wanderer a list of four targets. He will allow entry into Paradise Falls after the first capture.
• Strictly Profitable is an unmarked quest that can be pursued simultaneously to the Strictly Business quest as well as after that quest's completion. The Lone Wanderer can enslave certain people (with a Karma hit) and Grouse will pay them 250 caps per slave and give out a new collar for the next victim.

Other interactions:
• He sells Mesmetron power cells when asked, at a rate of 10 cells for 200 bottle caps.
• Should the player question him on what Paradise Falls is changes depending on whether they are wearing a Vault jumpsuit.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Troublemaker Outfit. Provides services: Apparel & Goods.

chr_00015697.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: guard, sandbox
chr_00015697.summary: Slaver is a african american character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Paradise Falls Slavers. Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man, Strictly Business.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Slavery is a significant part of the Capital Wasteland's economy. Paradise Falls is a slaver compound, and several quests feature slavery as either major or minor elements, such as Head of State and its association with slavery and Abraham Lincoln's role as the "Great Emancipator."

Additionally, the Lone Wanderer can capture people to sell them to slavers. The Lone Wanderer can even buy a slave, Clover, who will then serve as a bodyguard. The Lone Wanderer does not have the option of activating or defusing Clover's explosive collar.

The number of slaves present compared to the number of slavers is remarkably low, meaning that the slaves are being shipped off somewhere. It is revealed by Wernher that many of these slaves are being shipped off to work in the Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Head of State
• Strictly Business
• Those!
• Strictly Profitable
• The Kid-Kidnapper

Effects of player's actions:
Slavers are generally not hostile to the Lone Wanderer as long as they are not provoked with hostile dialogue responses, but attacking them can make the Paradise Falls slavers permanently enemies with the player character. If slavers are hostile first and killed, Paradise Falls slavers will not be initially hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Food, Apparel & Goods.

chr_00015696.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_00015696.summary: Lucy is a hispanic child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Little Lamplighters. Found primarily around Little Lamplight Office Building. Directly connected to quests: The Replicated Man, Picking Up the Trail.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Lucy was born in Little Lamplight eleven years ago. She has learned practical medicine from Red, and she considers her to be like an older sister. By the age of seven, she was incredibly talented in healing. After a cave-in, she used her skills to save Mayor MacCready's life. Since then, she has cared a little more about him than everyone else and has become his companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Fungus Deal: She reveals information about the curative effects of the mushrooms present within Little Lamplight, namely, their anti-radiation effects. If Mayor MacCready allows it, she will trade Buffout for cave fungus.
• The Replicated Man: If bribed or if the Lone Wanderer can pass a Medicine or Speech check, she will say that Pinkerton is the one who pulled off the android's surgery.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Little Lamplight Office Building. Notable equipment & inventory: Stimpak, itm_000340fa.

chr_00015693.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: surprised. AI packages: travel, patrol, follow, eat, sleep
chr_00015693.summary:

|race =Human
|gender =Female
|age =14 is a girl in Little Lamplight in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Knock Knock and her twin brother Knick Knack were born 14 years ago. She is in charge of morale and keeping the peace around town, and telling jokes.

One of her sources for her jokes was a book that was once retrieved from the nearby Vault 87, but has since been destroyed, which given the bad quality of its contents is not considered a loss by her. Knock Knock is also eager to hear new stories, as she is limited to events that happen within the community, since their scavenger teams usually stay hidden.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Knock Knock wanders around Little Lamplight all day until she goes to sleep.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• If the Lone Wanderer asks her for a joke and either laughs at it, or pretends that it is funny, she asks them for tales from the wasteland.
• They can then tell her a total of three tales; the first one being about exiting the vault, the second one about James's sacrifice during The Waters of Life, and the third one about their own escape from the Enclave during The American Dream.
• Regardless of the Lone Wanderer's Karma, they can tell her three versions of their story: good, neutral and evil. Whichever versions are chosen, she will proceed to share the tales with every other Lamplighter she comes across.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Knick Knack and his twin sister, Knock Knock, are 14 years old and the two are dedicated to the town. While Knock Knock collects awful jokes, Knick Knack collects odds and ends, hence his nickname. Because of his fondness for collecting things, he organizes the settlement's store of goods.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He is in his store behind the counter until night when he is in his bed.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
Knick Knack will give Lone Wanderer a discount if they have the Child at Heart perk.

chr_00015691.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox, follow, eat, dialogue
chr_00015691.summary: Penelope, more commonly referred to as Penny, is one of several Little Lamplight children who have been captured by slavers at Paradise Falls in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
She spends much time alone in a corner of the slave house and laments that Rory Maclaren is in danger of dying due to being isolated in the Box for a long period. She has become fond of the man.

Outside of her role as a child slave, Penny is a scavenger adept at foraging food and understanding wasteland animals. At Lamplight, she admires her brother Joseph and she aspires to be like him due to his resourcefulness and wisdom.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Penny refuses to leave without her good friend Rory. It is optional for the player character to either help Rory or convince Penny to leave without him by passing a speech check. Rescuing Penny from Paradise Falls will make her brother Joseph more inclined to help the Lone Wanderer get into Vault 87, through the method that only he can unlock. After saving Penny from Paradise Falls and talking to her in Little Lamplight, there is an amusing dialogue path that reveals that her real name is Penelope.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar, itm_000340f8.

chr_0001568d.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: surprised. AI packages: travel, sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_0001568d.summary: Joseph is a african american child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Little Lamplighters. Found primarily around Lamplight Caverns. Directly connected to quests: Picking Up the Trail.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is fifteen and is close to having to leave Little Lamplight soon as a result. He has a younger sister named Penny who looks up to him as a role model because of his wisdom.

For now, he has taken a teacher-like role to the younger residents and teaches them what he feels they should know about the wasteland, as well as other things that pique their curiosity. He also does computer work and reads old textbooks scavenged from Vault 87.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: In the mornings he teaches kids in the classroom, and afterward, he can be found down by the water in the Great Chamber.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Picking Up the Trail: If you speak to Mayor MacCready about another way into Vault 87, you can seek out Joseph and ask him about an old access door controlled by a "broken" computer. Joseph will turn on a hackable computer terminal that can open the door.

Other interactions:
• Joseph is the town barber and can give the player character a change of hairstyle.
• The Lone Wanderer can sit in on Joseph's class by visiting the Little Lamplight schoolhouse in the mornings. If pressed during the conversation, Joseph explains that he and his predecessors began by teaching survival skills to younger children. They were able to recover some holodisks from Vault 87's classroom at some point, but this provided them limited teaching materials.

chr_00015686.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, follow, eat, sleep, sandbox
chr_00015686.summary: Squirrel (real name Peter) is a 13-year-old boy from Little Lamplight who needs to be saved from Paradise Falls in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
He is talented with computers and electronics; as a result, he is a valued member of the scavenging team because he is the only one able to tell which hardware is worth taking. He enjoys reading and playing with gadgets. He is also rather ill, often seeing Lucy for medication.

He was recently sold into slavery by Rip Smithy, but he is devising a plan to escape.

He says his nickname came from his inquisitive nature, but other Lamplighters say it's because he's "nuts". His best friend is Sammy.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Rescue from Paradise: Squirrel is the brains behind the escape from Paradise Falls. He will task the player with everything they need to do to get them out.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar, itm_00031948, itm_000340fb.

chr_00015685.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: angry. AI packages: travel, eat, dialogue, sandbox
chr_00015685.summary: Princess (real name Angela) is a girl in Little Lamplight in 2277. She guards the back gate.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: She gained her nickname when she appointed herself mayor of Lamplight and insisted that everyone call her "Princess.” However, after only five minutes, MacCready punched her in the nose and took over as the new mayor. Ever since then, she has had a crush on him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Bully the Bully: If one rescued Sammy from Paradise Falls, he will join Princess in guarding the back gate and relay to the Lone Wanderer information that one may confront Princess with, to "take her down a peg."

Effects of player's actions:
• Bringing up the origin of her nickname will make her cry and run off, resulting in negative Karma.
• Choosing the Charisma option of remarking that MacCready spends more time with Lucy will cause the Wanderer to lose Karma (only 1 point), and she will no longer talk to them. One can get her to talk to the player character again by asking Sammy about her nickname, and then asking if she still holds her grudge.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Lamplight Caverns. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000340c4.

chr_00015684.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, follow, patrol, sandbox
chr_00015684.summary: Sammy is a boy from Little Lamplight who was kidnapped and put into one of Paradise Falls' slave pens in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Sammy is the best friend of Squirrel and the youngest member of Little Lamplight's scavenging team. He has the duty of watching Little Lamplight's back door, where Princess pokes fun at him for having a somewhat feminine face. He is highly talented aiming with rifles, but his aim did not help when slavers captured him and his friends. Him and Squirrel were captured on a trading run for Little Lamplight and sold to Eulogy Jones by Rip Smithy. The two have been held captive for around a month. Sammy is irritated by Squirrel's escape attempts because he has not been involved.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Rescue from Paradise: Sammy asks the Lone Wanderer to break him and his friends out of Paradise Falls.
• Bully the Bully: He can provide embarrassing information, which the Lone Wanderer can use to bully Princess.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Slave Collar, itm_000340fa.

chr_00015682.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox
chr_00015682.summary: Eclair is a caucasian child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 8, 65 HP). Affiliated with Little Lamplighters. Found primarily around Lamplight Caverns.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Previously a casual member of the scavenging team, Eclair is now Little Lamplight's resident chef, cooking and serving cave fungus to the other children. He managed to locate a few pages from a cookbook during his time scavenging, but after being shot in the foot, he became incapacitated for several months and has now resolved to overseeing the town's food supplies. He is mostly concerned with attempting to take the "stink" off the cave fungus and skimming it in water as preparation, though admits it still tastes terrible, hesitating to even qualify it as "food." If the Lone Wanderer tells him that cave fungus sounds delicious, he is horrified by the remark, commenting that they must be either a freak or a liar to say so.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Eclair spends most of his time behind a counter in his restaurant, "Spelunkers" in Little Lamplight. He can also sometimes be seen around the restaurant when there are no other non-player characters in the area.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Fungus Deal: He will trade cave fungus in exchange for strange meat, provided Mayor MacCready allows it. The player character can also trade at least one cave fungus with him if they have the Child at Heart perk.

chr_00014f14.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: sleep, eat, sandbox
chr_00014f14.summary: Megaton settlers are the unnamed wastelanders who have settled, but do not officially reside, in the city of Megaton, in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Megaton's unusual immigration laws seem to have created a condition where a substantial portion of the population of the town is in this situation. Essentially, new visitors to the town seem to be approved individually by the sheriff/mayor, Lucas Simms. Meeting this approval allows one to remain inside the town's protective walls, but does not constitute citizenship. Non-citizens of the town are not permitted to own housing, and instead must either rent lodging at Moriarty's Saloon, or for the less transient settlers, space in the common house is shared communally.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the player character's Karma is at the "very good" level, once per day while in town, a Megaton settler will come and give them some gift, such as bottle caps (sometimes even only 1 cap), food, a stimpak, or ammunition. The settler can usually be found around the entrance of Megaton and can vary in clothing, as well as change equipment throughout the game.
• If the player character decides to destroy Megaton with the bomb located in the town's center, any surviving settlers (known as Megaton refugees) that the player character encounters will immediately become hostile towards them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Common House. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.
