chr_00003b1c.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, eat, sleep, patrol
chr_00003b1c.summary: Stockholm is a hispanic character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Wasteland, Megaton. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Stockholm serves as Megaton's gate guard, manning the sniper platform above the settlement's main entrance.

A successful hack of Colin Moriarty's terminal reveals that Stockholm owes Moriarty's Saloon eight caps.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
Speaking to Stockholm on his platform prompts him to complain that talking to the Lone Wanderer distracts him from watching for raiders, before asking how they managed to reach him.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland, Megaton. Notable equipment & inventory: Combat Armor, Head Wrap, Biker Goggles.

chr_00000a73.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, eat, follow, patrol
chr_00000a73.summary: Harden Simms is a african american child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Lucas Simms' House. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Harden was born in 2267. He is Lucas Simms' 10-year-old son. His father has instructed him not to talk to strangers in Megaton, and he reluctantly obeys. He goes to sleep early and rises early, which gives him enough time to meet up with Maggie and play.

By 2297, Harden is the sheriff of Megaton. When drunk, he often speaks about his father's death, and blames it on the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He is a good friend of Maggie and is usually seen near her in the mid-morning to late afternoon. It is implied by his father, Lucas Simms, that Harden also polishes Deputy Steel on a regular basis, but this is idle chatter as the child is not scripted to enter the Megaton armory.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom: If Lucas Simms is dead when the Lone Wanderer disarms the bomb, Harden will reward them with a home in Megaton and any caps they requested at the beginning of the quest. He exhibits little emotion despite his father's death.

Other interactions:
• The Child at Heart perk has no effect on this character.
• Sometimes, it may be impossible to engage Harden in regular dialogue, as he will say something like "I'm not supposed to talk with strangers" and continue walking or standing.
• If Lucas Simms dies, Harden will claim to be the new self-appointed sheriff.

chr_00000a71.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: angry. AI packages: dialogue, travel, guard, follow, eat
chr_00000a71.summary: Jericho is a former raider, currently retired and residing in Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. He is a possible companion of the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2212, little is known about Jericho's history other than, for a large portion of his early adulthood, he was a merciless and bloodthirsty raider, having the run of the wasteland where he killed, stole, and looted for the slightest of reasons and smallest of caps amounts.

After many years of bloodshed and mayhem among highwaymen gangs, helping him to become a crack shot with a rifle, Jericho saw fit to retire. Around 2252, he drifted into, and eventually permanently settled down in the shantytown of Megaton to enjoy his twilight years. While he may occasionally lend his weapon hand in defense of the settlement from various threats including his former raider ilk, Jericho mostly prefers the company of the bottle at Colin Moriarty's saloon, trying to keep all clues of his bloody past buried.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Companion:
• Jericho can be recruited as a companion inside Moriarty's Saloon in Megaton by paying him a sum of 1000 caps. This option is available only while the player character has Evil Karma.
• He has the same response to trying to hire him, as well as rehiring him, with Good or Neutral Karma.
• Jericho's default loadout being leather armor and a Chinese assault rifle means that he is an effective counter to most early-game threats including raiders, super mutants, Talon Company mercs, and small packs of yao guai. However, as the stronger variants start to appear, his damage output will fall behind significantly and necessitate an upgrade in armor and weapons.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Jericho's House. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_00078cc4, itm_00040840, itm_00066c72, itm_00063fdc.

chr_00000a70.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, travel, eat, sleep
chr_00000a70.summary: Mother Maya is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 4, 85 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Children of Atom. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mother Maya is Confessor Cromwell's wife, but they do not announce this to others, as they are both occupied with spreading the ideals of church.

Mother Maya is kind, and treats ghouls like Gob with respect and an air of reverence because of their spiritual beliefs.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: MotherMaya), Mother Maya is defined as a Caucasian Elderly in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Faction memberships: Megaton Residents. Appears in or relates to quests: The Power of the Atom. Linked story events: Fate of Megaton Atomic Bomb.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 4, 85 HP. S.P.E.C.I.A.L. profile: STR 5, PER 4, END 4, CHA 7, INT 5, AGI 4, LCK 4. Behavioral traits: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, travel, eat, sleep.

chr_00000a6f.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sleep, travel
chr_00000a6f.summary: Confessor Cromwell is a member of the Church of the Children of Atom residing in Megaton in the Capital Wasteland, where he leads the Children in the worship of the undetonated atomic bomb that gave Megaton its name.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Cromwell arrived in Megaton in his early 20s, where he first encountered the Children of Atom. In his personal quarters in Megaton, he keeps a personal journal on a terminal.

Considered the "father of the undying Glow," He fully believes in the faith, and will advise others to bask in Atom's Glow to understand that the greatest wealth that a person has is their own. He also believes that each person is lost in their own way on their own path. As the leader of his faith, he takes no effort to become involved in the lay matters around him. Confessor Cromwell and Mother Maya treat Gob with respect and an air of reverence because of their spiritual beliefs.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Cromwell can be seen standing in the center of town, next to the bomb, praying to it in ankle-deep irradiated water. He even beseeches Atom to "shape his fragile form." He is heard preaching to his audience about the teachings of the Children of Atom, mainly on the subject of "birthing a thousand stars," relating to his (and the Children of Atom's) belief that inside every atom is an entire universe.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Church Donations: Donating to the church through the appropriate dialogue choice incurs Karma gain. The amount of Karma gained is proportional to the amount of caps given.
• The Power of the Atom: Cromwell will discourage the Lone Wanderer from disarming the bomb. However, he will not notice if they decide to do so.

chr_00000a6e.behavior: Aggressive, cautious; mood: angry. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sandbox, eat, sleep
chr_00000a6e.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Chems & Medicine, Supplies / Barter)
chr_00000a6e.summary: Doc Church is a african american elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Megaton Clinic. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom, The Replicated Man, Following in His Footsteps.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Doc Church used to stay alive by trading his services to raiders and slavers before he moved to Megaton. At that point, the town had been without a doctor for years. It may be a "rat infested hellhole" as he calls it, but he also says that it is the least hellish place in which he has lived. He is always professional even if he is overworked, under-appreciated, and quite bitter because of it. Part of his professionalism is his adherence to doctor-patient confidentiality, although he will share patient information with other doctors if he thinks they can do some good.

As Megaton's only doctor, he has got a lot on his plate and does not appreciate people bothering him without good cause.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Doc Church can be found at the Megaton clinic at any given time during the day.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Doc Church is in possession of a Replicated Man holotape.
• Leo's Drug Habit: The player character can use Speech to convince him of their trustworthiness, or Medicine to convince him that they can help, to find out about Leo Stahl's addiction.

chr_00000a6d.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sleep, sandbox, patrol, travel
chr_00000a6d.summary: Jenny Stahl is a citizen of Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277, serving cooked meals for customers at the Brass Lantern.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jenny was born in Megaton in 2253, when the shantytown did not yet have a protective fence. She is the middle child of the Stahl siblings, and often has to serve as the mediator between the clashing personalities of her brothers Leo and Andy. At some point after Jenny and her siblings were born, their parents chose to leave Megaton and move their family somewhere to the east to raise their children. However, after their parents later died, Leo took over the raising of his siblings.

Sometime prior to 2277, the Stahls returned to their hometown, where they were able to work their way up to running their own bar and restaurant, the Brass Lantern. Jenny serves as the cook of the bar's attached restaurant, and often gets Megaton's residents as customers coming across her counter.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Jenny will spend all day standing outside the Brass Lantern, serving meals to Megaton settlers. At night, she relaxes and will advise prospective customers to instead head inside the bar and talk to her brother Leo.

chr_00000a6c.summary: Andy Stahl is the business manager of the Brass Lantern in Megaton. He's the brother of Jenny Stahl and Leo Stahl, who mean the world to him.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The oldest of the Stahl siblings running Moriarty's competition, Andy is the most quiet and reserved of the trio. He is clever and adept at manipulating other people, and is among the only people in Megaton aware that Mister Burke is planning to detonate the bomb in its heart - and has been slowly figuring out where to move the restaurant to a better location where the Stahls can generate more income. The Stahls aren't native to Megaton: They immigrated to the city from further out east in recent time, challenging Moriarty's control of the booze market in Megaton. Moriarty has not yet figured out how to undercut the Stahls, relying on Nova's prostitution for the time being.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Leo's Drug Habit: Andy can be asked about his brother's addiction and will react positively to the player helping Leo kick the habit. However, he does not get a new set of lines and will remain brusque in interactions.

Other interactions:
• Talking to him while wearing the sheriff's duster will cause Andy to address the player as sheriff.

chr_00000a6b.summary: Leo Stahl is a citizen of Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277, serving drinks as the bartender of the Brass Lantern.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Leo was born in Megaton in 2252, when the shantytown did not yet have a protective fence. However, after their parents later died, Leo took over the raising of his siblings.

Sometime prior to 2277, the Stahls returned to their hometown, where they were able to work their way up to running their own bar and restaurant, the Brass Lantern. However, their business has been strained by one key issue: Leo secretly has a Jet addiction -- a byproduct from time he spent in his teenage years traveling with caravans and seeing other corners of the wasteland. Leo is ashamed of his behavior but cannot bring himself to stop due to his craving.

Although he has managed to keep it a secret from his siblings, and Doc Church deduced it after catching Leo more than once trying to steal medical supplies from his clinic to feed his addiction.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Leo's Drug Habit: After discovering Leo's drug habit, the Lone Wanderer can choose to either help him kick his habit, or convince him to sell them chems so they stay quiet about it. If the Lone Wanderer chooses to help him, he will give them a key to his desk in the water processing plant and ask that they get rid of all of his drugs.

Effects of player's actions:
• His initial greeting when first speaking to him changes depending on if the player character is wearing the Vault 101 jumpsuit or a different outfit.
• Wearing jumpsuit: "Well goddamn. You're new, right? I've got to admit, the outfit's a little weird, but that's okay, that's okay. Name's Leo Stahl. It's a pleasure!"
• Not wearing jumpsuit: "Well goddamn. You're new, right? Name's Leo Stahl.

chr_00000a6a.summary: Mister Burke is an associate of Allistair Tenpenny operating in Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Little to nothing is known about Burke's past before 2277 save for that he and Tenpenny first met sometime around when Allistair first began accepting tenants and building a security force for Tenpenny Tower. The elderly Tenpenny comments that over time, Burke did so well at catering to his needs, he hardly ever had to do anything himself.

It was originally an off-hand suggestion by Allistair, complaining about how the sight of Megaton ruined his view from his penthouse balcony (though he also suggested for the town to be vacated beforehand) that led to Burke coming to the shantytown and trying to learn more about its people and especially the bomb residing at its center. Colin Moriarty considers him a "class A weirdo" but has not presently done any further digging into the man, seeing him as just another paying customer at his bar.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Mister Burke can typically be found sitting in a chair in Moriarty's Saloon prior to starting The Power of the Atom. After one accepts the fusion pulse charge and arms the bomb in Megaton, he will return to Tenpenny Tower and wait for the Lone Wanderer to rendezvous with him on the balcony. If Megaton is successfully destroyed, he will then spend all of his time in or on the same floor as his suite. However, in any outcome where the bomb does not go off and he is not killed, Burke will simply be disabled the next time the player leaves his current location cell, disappearing from the game.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom: Talking to Mister Burke at Moriarty's Saloon will begin the destruction path of arming and detonating the Megaton bomb to destroy the town.

Effects of player's actions:
• If a female Lone Wanderer has the Black Widow perk, they unlock a unique interaction where Burke can be seduced. Afterward he will refer to the player character as his "lover" and will plan accordingly to go to Tenpenny Tower and convince Tenpenny to not blow up Megaton. Burke will actually disappear from the game altogether but will send a total of four love letters to Colin Moriarty to give to the Lone Wanderer as if he were at Tenpenny Tower, with the last one declaring they are breaking up.
• If one refuses Burke's offer or disarms the bomb without speaking to him, hitmen will show up at random encounters to attack them.

chr_00000a69.summary: Lucy West is a caucasian character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 80 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Lucy West's House. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom, Blood Ties.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Lucy West grew up with her parents Davis and Matilda and younger brother Ian in the remote settlement of Arefu. Despite the ten-year age gap between them, Ever since that day, Lucy had always been Ian's closest confidant, lending an ear whenever Ian needed to talk about his feelings and manage his supposed condition; she always helped him to contain the cannibalistic cravings it caused until they went away.

Sometime prior to 2277, the adult Lucy decided that she needed to strike out on her own; her departure seemingly occurred after the initial invasions by the Family out of Meresti Metro station, as she recognizes their name upon mention. Even though it severely hurt Ian emotionally, what little caps she does earn mostly go toward feeding herself.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Blood Ties: The Lone Wanderer is asked to take a message back to Lucy's family in Arefu, leading to the discovery of their fates and the involvement of the Family.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Evan King is killed at Arefu, Lucy will refuse to speak to the player character. A similar outcome happens after completing Blood Ties by saving Ian but then killing any resident of Arefu or member of the Family in Meresti Metro station.
• If one speaks to her after visiting Arefu but before finding her brother, they can inform her what happened to her parents, and she will ask the player character to find Ian for her. Completing Blood Ties removes the option to inform her about what happened to her family.

chr_00000a68.summary: Manya Vargas is a former caravaneer, an elderly resident of Megaton, and the wife of Nathan Vargas.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in Megaton, Manya has lived to the ripe old age of 64, despite a lifetime spent on the caravan trail together with her husband, Nathaniel Vargas. After saving up caps on the caravan trail, they retired at Megaton. While Manya witnessed every misery in the wasteland in her long life, it has not destroyed her optimism and gentle nature. As a result, she is a font of wisdom and knowledge, happily sharing her accumulated experience with other denizens of the town, making her very popular and successful.

Manya is descended from one of the founders of Megaton, and one of the people most knowledgeable about the town's history.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: Manya is a member of the Railroad. The player can learn this fact after collecting the holotape in her home, which is one of the ways to learn where the synth changed their face and memories, eluding the Institute's pursuit.

Other interactions:
• Manya is one of the oldest residents of Megaton and thus knows much about the history of the town. If one asks her about Megaton and how it was built, she will explain how the town was founded. She will explain that the town was built up using old airplanes, salvaged by her father from an air station, if the player asks about the number of airplane parts around Megaton. While both the prompt and Manya claim that multiple airplanes were used, there are only enough parts around Megaton for one cargo plane, the rest is corrugated metal and assorted scrap.

chr_00000a66.summary: Maggie is a asian child character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 30 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Billy Creel's House. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
When Maggie was three years old, Billy Creel adopted her and brought her to Megaton. She has no memories of her life before Megaton. Billy was given a man's house ever since the man was shot in a raider attack; a few townspeople claim that Billy was the one behind that bullet that bought him his place in the town. Billy told Maggie the combination to his lost safe.

Her real parents died during a raider attack in 2275. Maggie is a friendly girl running around the town. She appears to be interested in Harden Simms and discusses with Billy the prospect of her kissing the boy, to which Billy tells her to slow down, as she has plenty of time to do that later. She also asks Billy about "the talk," stating that Harden has already had the talk.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
With the Child at Heart perk, one can convince Maggie to tell them the combination to Billy Creel's safe.

chr_00000a65.summary: Billy Creel is a former scavenger, adoptive father of Maggie and resident of Megaton. He peppers his sentences with slang terms from the 1950s/60s, such as "daddy-o" or referring to people as "cats."

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Growing up as a forager, Billy Creel eventually became a gun for hire, protecting wasteland caravans for money, then a scavenger. He was completely focused on survival, until a chance encounter in 2275 awoke his paternal instinct; Creel stopped at a small settlement up north to trade salvage in, only to realize that it was wiped out by a raider attack. He found Maggie there, hiding under a bed in the same room that her parents were killed in, and promptly took her in.

As a newly minted father, Creel journeyed south and settled in Megaton, becoming a permanent resident after he helped repulse a raider attack. One of the residents was killed in the attack, and he was promptly rewarded with their house for his contribution to the defense.

chr_00000a64.summary: Walter is a resident of Megaton, helping operate and maintain the town's water purifier in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An elderly handyman at 61 years of age, making him one of Megaton's oldest residents, By 2277, however, a combination of failing infrastructure and his advanced age has left Walter with more and more trouble maintaining the aging machine supporting an entire population. Consequently, he spends most of his time in the plant with the primary machinery, leaving him unable to fix the various small leaks that have sprung up in the pipe system outside; the only time he is able to leave is when he shuts off the system every night. This leaves him more than willing to employ anyone capable of fixing the leaks and scrounging additional supplies to make his job of maintaining the plant less burdensome.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: During the daytime, Walter can be found in the water processing plant for most of the day, though sometimes he will step outside for some air. During the night hours, he can be seen drinking in Moriarty's Saloon.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Treatment: Walter will ask the Lone Wanderer to fix all the leaking water pipes around Megaton. When finished, he will give 200 caps and 100 XP.
• Walter's Scrap Metal: Upon fixing all the leaking pipes, Walter will ask the Lone Wanderer to bring any scrap metal they find, and as a reward Walter will give them 10 caps and 5 XP per scrap metal. If scrap metal is given to Walter without charging him, they will gain Karma and earn extra XP.

chr_00000a63.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sleep, eat, dialogue
chr_00000a63.summary: Nova is one of the residents of Megaton, serving as the self-described whore at Moriarty's Saloon in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Nova spends most of her time hanging around the bar talking to Gob, Moriarty, Jericho, and other customers. Every now and then, she goes up to her room with a client. Her standards are not exactly high, but she explicitly states that she does not serve ghouls. Another part of her job is to sweet-talk the male patrons and get them to spend caps on booze, company, or just a bed for the night. She has a day off, on which she goes shopping.

She has lived in Megaton since around 2272, but has grown unenthusiastic during her stay. This is in no small part due to how Colin Moriarty treats her. Moriarty does not even trust her with her earnings, taking them and locking them up for himself. Nova also has a chem habit, as Moriarty is displeased of her consuming Jet.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Nova works at Moriarty's Saloon as a sex worker and can be found hanging out on the saloon's first floor talking to the locals and the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: After inquiring about Moriarty and completing a successful Speech check, she will give the Lone Wanderer the password for Colin's terminal, which contains valuable information about their father. A male player with the Lady Killer perk has a special dialogue option with her to acquire the password.

Effects of player's actions:
• When inquiring about hiring Nova's services, she advises the Lone Wanderer to rent a room. After paying her, she directs them to the room with the "big bed," and straight after finishing the conversation, walks up the stairs to the room, lies down on the bed, and appears to fall asleep. Attempting to speak with her at this point will result in the usual dialogue choices. However, there is access to the bed for a period of time after this.

chr_00000a62.behavior: Aggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, patrol, sleep, sandbox
chr_00000a62.summary: Gob, full name Gobtholemew, is an abused ghoul bartender who works at Moriarty's Saloon in Megaton in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Treated as a freakish, second-class citizen by many people in Megaton (particularly Colin Moriarty), Gob is skittish and nervous, always looking over his shoulder. He does his best to maintain a sense of humor and to be friendly with customers, but this is mostly out of his desire not to be beaten. Confessor Cromwell and Mother Maya treat Gob with respect and an air of reverence because of their spiritual beliefs.

Gob used to live in Underworld with his adoptive mother, Carol, in Carol's Place. He set out into the wasteland to find fortune and was caught by a group of slavers. Colin Moriarty then purchased him as his slave. He works for Colin Moriarty to repay the debt presumably incurred when Moriarty purchased Gob from the slavers. Gob has been working to repay his debt for 15 years, since Moriarty also charges Gob for rent and food.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Gob spends most of his time serving drinks and talking with the patrons in Moriarty's saloon. At night, he'll eventually go to sleep in the rentable room, sometimes resting for a few hours and then starting up the saloon in the early morning hours. During his working hours, he'll be cleaning glasses, communicating with people ("What, you never seen a ghoul before?"), tidying up the place with a dirty broom and checking the shelves behind the counter to see what's currently in stock. The first time the Lone Wanderer enters the saloon, Gob will be hitting the radio, trying to fix it. Nova tries to explain to him it doesn't work, and Jericho (if he is present) will curse at him to stop banging on it.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: If one passes a Speech check with Gob, he will tell them about Moriarty's terminal. He will also reveal that Nova has the password.

Effects of player's actions:
• If you kill Moriarty, Gob will eventually take over the saloon and place his name over Moriarty's on the front sign. However, he gets no new speech options and in no other way acknowledges Moriarty's absence. Nova will begin running the hotel and quit prostituting once Gob is in charge.

Other interactions:
• When first meeting Gob, treating him kindly will provide a 10% discount at the saloon (and only from Gob, Moriarty will charge full price), gain the player some good Karma, and reveal some more of his personal past. The discount is especially useful as Gob remains a cheap source of stimpaks for the entire game.

chr_00000a61.summary: Colin Moriarty is a caucasian elderly character in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 6, 55 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around Moriarty's Saloon. Directly connected to quests: The Power of the Atom, Following in His Footsteps.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Colin Moriarty, who is 50 years old in 2277, has lived in Megaton almost his entire life. According to Herbert Dashwood, he came to the former United States from Ireland as a child, alongside at least his father; Colin himself further claims that his grandfather was among the original founders of Megaton in the early post-War era, though the truth of this is uncertain. Either way, after coming to the U.S., Colin's father amassed wealth using nearby trade routes, and helped secure Megaton as a trading hub in the area. Colin's father died during a raider attack circa 2241 and his son inherited his wealth, including the saloon.

He is a very proactive businessman and a staunch supporter of the "just business" approach; if someone wants something from him, it had better be worth his while.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He spends most of his time in the saloon, but occasionally goes outside to smoke, leaning on the rail out in front of the bar.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Following in His Footsteps: He tells the Lone Wanderer where their father, James, is and recalls the time he saw them as a child, also mentioning their father's "Brotherhood of Steel friend" (Star Paladin Cross). If the Lone Wanderer tells Moriarty they lack 100 caps to buy information on James, he will ask them to find a woman called Silver and get his money back.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Moriarty dies, Gob takes over the saloon and changes the name on the sign to Gob's. Nova will also no longer be available for hire.

Other interactions:
• Jericho can be paid 20 caps to get information regarding Moriarty's key, specifically that it is around his neck, which unlocks Gob and Nova's pay stash in a locker by Moriarty's bed; however, this key (Form ID ) was cut from the game.

chr_00000a60.summary: Lucas Simms is the sheriff and de facto mayor of Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A native of Megaton, Lucas Simms grew up in the town and gained a deep understanding of what it takes to survive in the wasteland. Despite the harsh standard of living in the Capital Wastes, Lucas never surrendered his childhood cowboy fantasy, eventually acting on it to appoint himself the sheriff of Megaton in his adulthood; by 2277, few if any of the residents dispute his self-made position.

Along with his capacity as sheriff, Lucas also takes care of any public duty necessary for the people of his town - mayor, judge, etc. - and deals with most troublemakers by unceremoniously throwing them out of the town. More serious offenders, such as raiders trying to prey on the town, are shot dead on the spot, either by Simms, or by the town's militia and reprogrammed robots under his command.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom

Other interactions:
If Lucas, Moriarty, or both are killed, Manya Vargas, Leo Stahl, and Harden will have unique dialogue when next talked to.

chr_0100ccf7.summary: American soldiers are allies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation who replicate the pre-War United States Army servicemembers that fought in the Battle of Anchorage in the Sino-American War.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle, including recreations of the American defenders, with himself as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
American soldier:
American soldiers are standard US Army infantry who wear winterized combat armor and are armed with assault rifles. They have superior health and armor compared to their Chinese counterparts, but inferior weapons and are vulnerable to Crimson Dragoons and snipers.

The basic American soldier has about twice as much health as a basic Chinese soldier and is about on par with a Chinese special weapons unit (and also roughly on par with an Enclave soldier) in terms of skill and durability.

American sniper:
Trained in long-range engagement, American snipers wear winterized combat armor and utilize a sniper rifle. They are effective against Chinese infantry. They have lower Charisma than other soldiers, having the points reallocated to their Perception.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Winterized T-51b Power Helmet, Winterized T-51b Power Armor, Gauss Rifle, Microfusion Cell.

chr_0100c3c8.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

chr_0100c188.summary: The American war correspondent is a reporter found in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A grizzled war correspondent for the Capital Post, Washington's most prominent daily newspaper. He was dispatched to the frontlines of the Reclamation to cover the final stages of the Reclamation.

The simulated correspondent is an ardent patriot, informing soldiers that everyone on the home front is rooting for them, thanks to his coverage. He focuses on taking photos of soldiers in heroic poses for propaganda purposes, and the simulation shows the moment he took a picture that was later used as the basis for the Anchorage Memorial.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• The correspondent appears outside the U.S. Army field headquarters command tent, taking a photograph of three soldiers in a scripted scene, and rather bluntly pointing out that it is the basis for the memorial statue. He has no other interactions and will thank the player character for the work they do if interacted with.
• If he is killed or attacked, all non-player characters will become hostile.

chr_0100c0e4.summary: American soldiers are allies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation who replicate the pre-War United States Army servicemembers that fought in the Battle of Anchorage in the Sino-American War.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle, including recreations of the American defenders, with himself as their battlefield commander.

chr_0100b56e.summary: Doctor Adrienn Adami is an United States Army physician found at Gen. Chase's field headquarters in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The simulated head of General Chase's medical staff posted to the Anchorage forward bay, Doctor Adami is an experienced physician dealing with an overwhelming amount of work. She's glad to see soldiers return for treatment, as long as they do it on their own power, rather than in a body bag.

It's unknown whether the real Adrienn Adami was as compliant as her simulated persona: The simulation has discrepancies, and her records implicated Chase in the Psycho drugging scandal.

chr_0100a088.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, patrol, ambush
chr_0100a088.summary: Crimson Dragoons are elite members of the People's Liberation Army who appear in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Crimson Dragoons are an elite commando unit of the Chinese army, posted to the most sensitive locations. In the simulation depicting the Battle of Anchorage, they come equipped with Chinese stealth armor, rendering them invisible thanks to the Chinese mastery of stealth technology, and fight using Chinese officer's swords and various firearms. According to American intelligence, Crimson Dragoons are trained from birth.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Enemies:
• Crimson Dragoons level with the Lone Wanderer and are generally on par with a Brotherhood of Steel knight or paladin in terms of skill and durability. Their cloaking-field generating stealth armor allows them to pose a unique threat. With a few exceptions, most Crimson Dragoons will idle in sneak mode until the player character passes them, making them very difficult to detect at a glance. Once one's back is turned, they will attack.
Local variations
• Crimson Dragoons armed with Chinese officer swords at the artillery base have enhanced speed and move twice as fast as regular humanoid non-player characters. They also have additional special behavior provided by script (DLC02ArtilleryBaseDragoonSCRIPT), which provides a number of unique features: If hit in combat, the Dragoon will reactivate stealth mode after 1.5 seconds.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* When their bodies are searched via the console, Crimson Dragoons yield Brotherhood of Steel holotags.
** While Crimson Dragoons sometimes do carry Chinese pistols, they will never use them in combat.

• Crimson Dragoons level with the Lone Wanderer and are generally on par with a Brotherhood of Steel knight or paladin in terms of skill and durability. Their cloaking-field generating stealth armor allows them to pose a unique threat. With a few exceptions, most Crimson Dragoons will idle in sneak mode until the player character passes them, making them very difficult to detect at a glance. Once one's back is turned, they will attack.
Local variations
• Crimson Dragoons armed with Chinese officer swords at the artillery base have enhanced speed and move twice as fast as regular humanoid non-player characters. They also have additional special behavior provided by script (DLC02ArtilleryBaseDragoonSCRIPT), which provides a number of unique features: If hit in combat, the Dragoon will reactivate stealth mode after 1.5 seconds.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* When their bodies are searched via the console, Crimson Dragoons yield Brotherhood of Steel holotags.
** While Crimson Dragoons sometimes do carry Chinese pistols, they will never use them in combat.

Infobox character
|name =Benjamin Montgomery
|subtitle =Benji was a pre-War member of the United States Marine Corps who fought in the Battle of Anchorage. A digital avatar made in his likeness appears in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Gunnery Sergeant Benjamin Montgomery served during the Sino-American War in the late 21st century, during which he was deployed to the Anchorage frontline on multiple tours against the Chinese forces under General Jingwei occupying Alaska. While he acts as a model soldier and initially addresses others in military fashion, once he became friendly with someone, they were given an informal nickname by him as he proved to be a loyal confidante to his comrades.

Based on his depiction in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation, Montgomery participated in frontline operations directly leading to the liberation of Anchorage.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Guns of Anchorage: Montgomery will help the Lone Wanderer as they wake up when first entering the simulation. He will then hand them their equipment and begin climbing the cliffs, leaving the Lone Wanderer to take the long way to the cave outpost. At arrival, both he and the player will proceed with destroying the artillery guns.
• Paving the Way: Montgomery is a recruitable strike team leader and assists with the securing of the listening post, along with helping in the destruction of the fuel tanks and the Chimera armor depot.
• Operation: Anchorage!: Montgomery alone accompanies the Lone Wanderer through the pulse field and into the Chinese occupied refinery.

Effects of player's actions:
• Killing the quartermaster will cause Sgt. Montgomery to turn hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Winterized Combat Armor, Silenced 10mm Pistol, 10mm Round.

sections.text: Crimson Dragoons are an elite commando unit of the Chinese army, posted to the most sensitive locations. In the simulation depicting the Battle of Anchorage, they come equipped with Chinese stealth armor, rendering them invisible thanks to the Chinese mastery of stealth technology, and fight using Chinese officer's swords and various firearms. According to American intelligence, Crimson Dragoons are trained from birth.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle for training purposes. The simulation included recreations of the American defenders, with Chase as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
During the Operation: Anchorage quest Paving the Way, the player character receives a field promotion from General Chase and gains the ability to command an interactive strike team. The team is initially selected via Patterson's terminal in the U.S. Army field headquarters command tent, by spending recruitment markers given by Lieutenant Morgan; Morgan gives a total of five markers, and up to three units can be selected.

On the terminal, different compositions of the strike team can be selected with respect to the three unit slots and five markers available. Once selected, the team composition is final and cannot be changed again via the terminal. However, units can be dismissed by simply speaking to them, and they can also die during combat.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Strike team infantryman:
A rifleman clad in winterized combat armor with matching helmet who is armed with an R91 assault rifle. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team grenadier:
This soldier wears winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and is armed with a 10mm SMG and five frag grenades. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team missile unit:
Strike team missile units are protected by winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and carry a N99 10mm pistol as well as a missile launcher. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

Inventory

Strike team sniper:
Like the other human team members, snipers wear winterized combat armor with a matching helmet. Their armament consists of a trench knife and a sniper rifle. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle for training purposes. The simulation included recreations of the American defenders, with Chase as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
During the Operation: Anchorage quest Paving the Way, the player character receives a field promotion from General Chase and gains the ability to command an interactive strike team. The team is initially selected via Patterson's terminal in the U.S. Army field headquarters command tent, by spending recruitment markers given by Lieutenant Morgan; Morgan gives a total of five markers, and up to three units can be selected.

On the terminal, different compositions of the strike team can be selected with respect to the three unit slots and five markers available. Once selected, the team composition is final and cannot be changed again via the terminal. However, units can be dismissed by simply speaking to them, and they can also die during combat.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Strike team infantryman:
A rifleman clad in winterized combat armor with matching helmet who is armed with an R91 assault rifle. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team grenadier:
This soldier wears winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and is armed with a 10mm SMG and five frag grenades. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team missile unit:
Strike team missile units are protected by winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and carry a N99 10mm pistol as well as a missile launcher. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

Inventory

Strike team sniper:
Like the other human team members, snipers wear winterized combat armor with a matching helmet. Their armament consists of a trench knife and a sniper rifle. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle for training purposes. The simulation included recreations of the American defenders, with Chase as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
During the Operation: Anchorage quest Paving the Way, the player character receives a field promotion from General Chase and gains the ability to command an interactive strike team. The team is initially selected via Patterson's terminal in the U.S. Army field headquarters command tent, by spending recruitment markers given by Lieutenant Morgan; Morgan gives a total of five markers, and up to three units can be selected.

On the terminal, different compositions of the strike team can be selected with respect to the three unit slots and five markers available. Once selected, the team composition is final and cannot be changed again via the terminal. However, units can be dismissed by simply speaking to them, and they can also die during combat.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Strike team infantryman:
A rifleman clad in winterized combat armor with matching helmet who is armed with an R91 assault rifle. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team grenadier:
This soldier wears winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and is armed with a 10mm SMG and five frag grenades. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team missile unit:
Strike team missile units are protected by winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and carry a N99 10mm pistol as well as a missile launcher. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

Inventory

Strike team sniper:
Like the other human team members, snipers wear winterized combat armor with a matching helmet. Their armament consists of a trench knife and a sniper rifle. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle for training purposes. The simulation included recreations of the American defenders, with Chase as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
During the Operation: Anchorage quest Paving the Way, the player character receives a field promotion from General Chase and gains the ability to command an interactive strike team. The team is initially selected via Patterson's terminal in the U.S. Army field headquarters command tent, by spending recruitment markers given by Lieutenant Morgan; Morgan gives a total of five markers, and up to three units can be selected.

On the terminal, different compositions of the strike team can be selected with respect to the three unit slots and five markers available. Once selected, the team composition is final and cannot be changed again via the terminal. However, units can be dismissed by simply speaking to them, and they can also die during combat.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Strike team infantryman:
A rifleman clad in winterized combat armor with matching helmet who is armed with an R91 assault rifle. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team grenadier:
This soldier wears winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and is armed with a 10mm SMG and five frag grenades. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team missile unit:
Strike team missile units are protected by winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and carry a N99 10mm pistol as well as a missile launcher. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

Inventory

Strike team sniper:
Like the other human team members, snipers wear winterized combat armor with a matching helmet. Their armament consists of a trench knife and a sniper rifle. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

chr_0100845d.summary: Chinese soldiers are the primary enemies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation, and replicate the pre-War People's Liberation Army that fought in the Battle of Anchorage.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Led by Chairman Cheng, the People's Liberation Army played a pivotal role in the Resource Wars. They fought the United States and its armed forces during the Sino-American War, from the initial invasion and occupation of Alaska in 2066 to a defensive war in mainland China in the wake of the 2074 American invasion.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned the creation of a digital simulation based on the events of the battle using Virtual Strategic Solutions, including recreations of the Chinese forces and their leader, General Jingwei.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Chinese soldier:
Standard PLA infantry, they are usually armed with Chinese assault rifles, and wear winterized Chinese jumpsuits. Like every other character in the simulation, they are impossible to loot as they disappear upon death.

They are the most common enemy inside the simulation, typically appearing in squads of four or five. They are weaker than their American counterparts, especially soldiers clad in power armor, but have greater numbers. Chinese soldiers are roughly on par with raiders or (at higher levels) Talon Company mercs in terms of durability and skill. They have roughly about half as much health as the American strike team soldiers, but are on a similar level in terms of combat skill.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_01008453.summary: Chinese soldiers are the primary enemies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation, and replicate the pre-War People's Liberation Army that fought in the Battle of Anchorage.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Led by Chairman Cheng, the People's Liberation Army played a pivotal role in the Resource Wars. They fought the United States and its armed forces during the Sino-American War, from the initial invasion and occupation of Alaska in 2066 to a defensive war in mainland China in the wake of the 2074 American invasion.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned the creation of a digital simulation based on the events of the battle using Virtual Strategic Solutions, including recreations of the Chinese forces and their leader, General Jingwei.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Chinese soldier:
Standard PLA infantry, they are usually armed with Chinese assault rifles, and wear winterized Chinese jumpsuits. Like every other character in the simulation, they are impossible to loot as they disappear upon death.

They are the most common enemy inside the simulation, typically appearing in squads of four or five. They are weaker than their American counterparts, especially soldiers clad in power armor, but have greater numbers. Chinese soldiers are roughly on par with raiders or (at higher levels) Talon Company mercs in terms of durability and skill. They have roughly about half as much health as the American strike team soldiers, but are on a similar level in terms of combat skill.

chr_01008451.summary: American soldiers are allies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation who replicate the pre-War United States Army servicemembers that fought in the Battle of Anchorage in the Sino-American War.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle, including recreations of the American defenders, with himself as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
American soldier:
American soldiers are standard US Army infantry who wear winterized combat armor and are armed with assault rifles. They have superior health and armor compared to their Chinese counterparts, but inferior weapons and are vulnerable to Crimson Dragoons and snipers.

The basic American soldier has about twice as much health as a basic Chinese soldier and is about on par with a Chinese special weapons unit (and also roughly on par with an Enclave soldier) in terms of skill and durability.

American sniper:
Trained in long-range engagement, American snipers wear winterized combat armor and utilize a sniper rifle. They are effective against Chinese infantry. They have lower Charisma than other soldiers, having the points reallocated to their Perception.

chr_01004de6.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). chr_01004de5.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

chr_01004dd3.summary: Chinese soldiers are the primary enemies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation, and replicate the pre-War People's Liberation Army that fought in the Battle of Anchorage.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Led by Chairman Cheng, the People's Liberation Army played a pivotal role in the Resource Wars. They fought the United States and its armed forces during the Sino-American War, from the initial invasion and occupation of Alaska in 2066 to a defensive war in mainland China in the wake of the 2074 American invasion.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned the creation of a digital simulation based on the events of the battle using Virtual Strategic Solutions, including recreations of the Chinese forces and their leader, General Jingwei.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Chinese soldier:
Standard PLA infantry, they are usually armed with Chinese assault rifles, and wear winterized Chinese jumpsuits. Like every other character in the simulation, they are impossible to loot as they disappear upon death.

They are the most common enemy inside the simulation, typically appearing in squads of four or five. They are weaker than their American counterparts, especially soldiers clad in power armor, but have greater numbers. Chinese soldiers are roughly on par with raiders or (at higher levels) Talon Company mercs in terms of durability and skill. They have roughly about half as much health as the American strike team soldiers, but are on a similar level in terms of combat skill.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_01004ab4.summary: American soldiers are allies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation who replicate the pre-War United States Army servicemembers that fought in the Battle of Anchorage in the Sino-American War.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle, including recreations of the American defenders, with himself as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
American soldier:
American soldiers are standard US Army infantry who wear winterized combat armor and are armed with assault rifles. They have superior health and armor compared to their Chinese counterparts, but inferior weapons and are vulnerable to Crimson Dragoons and snipers.

The basic American soldier has about twice as much health as a basic Chinese soldier and is about on par with a Chinese special weapons unit (and also roughly on par with an Enclave soldier) in terms of skill and durability.

American sniper:
Trained in long-range engagement, American snipers wear winterized combat armor and utilize a sniper rifle. They are effective against Chinese infantry. They have lower Charisma than other soldiers, having the points reallocated to their Perception.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: 5mm Round, Minigun, Microfusion Cell, Fat Man, Winterized T-51b Power Armor, Winterized T-51b Power Helmet.

American grease-monkeys are U.S. Army mechanics found at the U.S. Army field headquarters in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

chr_01002d22.summary: The quartermaster is a "vendor" found at the U.S. Army field headquarters during the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The simulated soldier in charge of weapon stocks at headquarters, the quartermaster is logical and a stickler for correct procedure: Without the right requisition holotape, he won't hand out anything. It's necessary when managing weapons and ammunition on the front lines at Anchorage, as the Army has a limited amount of supplies this far out in the Alaskan tundra, and soldiers are expected to scavenge further supplies from the field. If anyone in the theater has a complaint, the quartermaster will have none of it, unless it's lodged in writing on the standard 10-78BGHCF form.

There's one exception: Those who went beyond the call of duty in service to their brothers in arms and knows how to speak to him can count on a little bit of extra gear, requisition limits or not. And if anyone asks, "it fell off a truck".

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Paving the Way, Operation: Anchorage!: He provides the Lone Wanderer with equipment after they provide a requisition holo, with a selection of specialized kits.
• The quartermaster can provide a scoped Gauss rifle in addition to the equipment already chosen if one passes his Speech challenge.
• He is the only person that can be killed in the simulation that won't immediately dissolve and disappear, allowing the player to search him.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Assault Rifle, Winterized Combat Armor, 5.56mm Round.

chr_010029cd.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_010029cd.summary: Gary was one of the original inhabitants of Vault 108, and clones of him are the only people left in the Vault by 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Part of a grand cloning experiment with a fatal end, 54 clones of "Gary" were created. Each had varying levels of violent and psychotic traits and behaviors, leading to the scientists' deaths and Garys running freely throughout the Vault. They use inflections of voice tone, speaking only their name, to communicate and are hostile towards any outsiders.

A holotape labeled cloning log can be found in the Vault 108 cloning lab, which explains that Gary was cloned at least 54 times. All clones exhibited hostility towards non-clones, with each successive clone being more and more violent. When the Vault scientists started running out of room to store the clones, they planned to destroy some of them to make room for additional test subjects. Sometime afterward, the clones violently took control of the Vault.

chr_01002944.summary: Chinese technicians are Chinese personnel encountered in the listening post in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Technicians found at the listening post are regular ground troops of the Chinese Army, responsible for operating and maintaining the equipment at the listening post. Apart from providing combat intelligence and relaying battle information, they also act as air traffic control, coordinating Chinese bombers constantly hammering American positions with high explosives.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Paving the Way: Two technicians are encountered in the listening post, and they are not immediately hostile or otherwise aggressive, continuing their work while nervously glancing at the player. Attacking them can either cause them to fight back or to flee.
• If the player character approaches the ham radio in the room, there will be Chinese reinforcements waiting for them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Listening Post. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0100293b.summary: Crimson Dragoons are elite members of the People's Liberation Army who appear in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Crimson Dragoons are an elite commando unit of the Chinese army, posted to the most sensitive locations. In the simulation depicting the Battle of Anchorage, they come equipped with Chinese stealth armor, rendering them invisible thanks to the Chinese mastery of stealth technology, and fight using Chinese officer's swords and various firearms. According to American intelligence, Crimson Dragoons are trained from birth.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Enemies:
• Crimson Dragoons level with the Lone Wanderer and are generally on par with a Brotherhood of Steel knight or paladin in terms of skill and durability. Their cloaking-field generating stealth armor allows them to pose a unique threat. With a few exceptions, most Crimson Dragoons will idle in sneak mode until the player character passes them, making them very difficult to detect at a glance. Once one's back is turned, they will attack.
Local variations
• Crimson Dragoons armed with Chinese officer swords at the artillery base have enhanced speed and move twice as fast as regular humanoid non-player characters. They also have additional special behavior provided by script (DLC02ArtilleryBaseDragoonSCRIPT), which provides a number of unique features: If hit in combat, the Dragoon will reactivate stealth mode after 1.5 seconds.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* When their bodies are searched via the console, Crimson Dragoons yield Brotherhood of Steel holotags.
** While Crimson Dragoons sometimes do carry Chinese pistols, they will never use them in combat.

Spawn notes

chr_010018d2.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: use item, dialogue, travel
chr_010018d2.summary: General Jingwei was a pre-War member of the People's Liberation Army, serving as the field commander during the Chinese occupation of Anchorage, Alaska. A digital avatar made in his likeness appears in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Nothing is known of Jingwei's career, such as how he attained the rank of general before he led the PLA forces to invade the North American continent. The initial invasion under his command was sweeping across the state, up until the Americans retaliated and the Battle of Anchorage ended with the expulsion of communist forces in 2077. His men knew him to be a cruel, but effective commander that demanded absolute loyalty, while his foes saw him as a ruthless and highly efficient tactician with a menacing tendency to bouts of savagery, yet always fighting with a certain sense of honor, no matter how twisted his actions were.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Operation: Anchorage!: When the Lone Wanderer first sees him, he is calmly executing an American soldier with his shocksword in the midst of the battle between American T-51b units and Chinese soldiers, after which the Lone Wanderer may deal with him either through a Speech check or through combat.
• He can be convinced to kill himself with his own sword to avoid capture via Speech. A Charisma of 4 and Speech of 90 will allow a 100% chance of success.
• He can be killed in combat. General Jingwei is a "boss" character with an extremely high durability. His uniform and hat have a combined Damage Resistance of 31 at 100% condition. Because of this armor and the general's large amount of health (more than 1,000 HP at higher levels), he is almost as durable as a super mutant behemoth.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Chinese Jumpsuit, Chinese General Hat, Jingwei's Shocksword.

chr_01000e26.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, guard, combat
chr_01000e26.summary: Defender Morrill is a member of the Brotherhood Outcasts located at Bailey's Crossroads. He stays outside the facility with the Outcasts to defend against periodic attacks from the super mutants.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Morrill is a veteran soldier who has fought in more battles than he would like, operating under the command of Protector McGraw. His latest assignment is at the VSS facility at Bailey's Crossroads, where he coordinates surface defenses against hordes of super mutants determined to wipe the Outcasts out. He also performs special operations for McGraw, such as a daring raid on Vault 108 and the abduction of Gary 23, in an attempt to acquire a Pip-Boy necessary to crack the VSS vault.

However, the attempt failed: Gary 23 died under interrogation, Specialist Olin is back at square one, and Morrill is stuck trying to keep the super mutants at bay. Due to a recent surge in their activity, Morrill decided to send out an urgent radio broadcast for help, requesting any available Outcasts to come to their aid at sector 7-B - Bailey's Crossroads.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Aiding the Outcasts: Morrill is the one responsible for sending out the emergency radio broadcast that brings the Lone Wanderer to the Outcast outpost. He meets the player at the exit from the Bailey's Crossroads Metro and requests their aid in clearing a path to the outpost. Upon arrival at the outpost, Morrill sends them down to speak to Protector McGraw.
• Morrill will have a different attitude if the player is wearing Outcast power armor, taking them for reinforcements. The player can either keep him in the dark, and fight alongside the Outcasts like one of them, with Morrill later either deciding they are a disgrace to the armor (if they have not pulled their weight) or commending them for their efforts, but asking about the rest of their detachment.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Outcast Power Armor, Outcast Power Helmet.
