chr_01000e24.summary: Defender Sibley is a african american character in Operation: Anchorage (Level 7, 100 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood Outcasts. Found primarily around Outcast Outpost. Directly connected to quests: Aiding the Outcasts, Operation: Anchorage!.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A grim and hostile individual, Defender Sibley is a Brotherhood hardliner, who firmly believes in the mission of the Brotherhood Outcasts, namely recovering technology and keeping it out of the hands of wastelanders by any means necessary. Anyone outside the Outcasts is a potential threat as far as Sibley is concerned, which is a key issue between him and Protector McGraw; The protector's willingness to negotiate and cooperate with wastelanders is seen by Defender Sibley as evidence of weak will and a danger to Outcast operations.

This attitude makes him a natural leader to fellow hardliners, particularly those operating under McGraw. While he understands and shares their sentiments, Sibley firmly believes in the chain of command. He follows McGraw's orders, even if he finds them disagreeable, and keeps any whispers of mutiny contained.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Aiding the Outcasts: Sibley is the first Outcast met underground and takes the Lone Wanderer to Olin and the VR pod when he is told to do so by Protector McGraw.
• If the player character is wearing Outcast power armor, Sibley will be grudgingly deferential, mistaking them for a fellow Outcast (as will other Outcasts).
• If the player character is female and has the Black Widow perk, a unique dialogue option will be available upon speaking to Sibley ("Listen, sweetie. I'm kind of lost. Can I talk to whomever's in charge?"), which results in Sibley being blown completely off-track and politely taking the player to McGraw. This does not affect the mutiny, however.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Outcast Outpost. Notable equipment & inventory: Outcast Power Armor.

chr_01000e23.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, escort, dialogue
chr_01000e23.summary: Protector McGraw is a high-ranking member of the Brotherhood Outcasts, and the commanding officer of the Outcast outpost at Bailey's Crossroads.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
One of the more personable Outcasts, McGraw can be direct, but polite in his dealing with wastelanders, rather than rude and condescending, which is a noted departure from the leadership style demonstrated by other Outcasts. McGraw leads an independent patrol focusing on recovering technology from a recently uncovered compound belonging to Virtual Strategic Solutions. Located in Bailey's Crossroads, the facility is located deep within super mutant country and the patrol could be wiped out at any minute. However, McGraw is willing to risk his life to uncover its secrets, and the lives of his men.

Their mission has not been going well. The Outcasts have suffered significant casualties due to constant mutant attacks, to the point that a single concentrated assault could wipe them all out.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Aiding the Outcasts: McGraw is running the operation and asks the Lone Wanderer to perform the Anchorage Reclamation simulation, so the Outcasts can open the VSS vault.
• The player gain access to a number of unique dialogue options, depending on what they did beforehand. If they completed Following in His Footsteps before talking to him. The player character will refer to "psychotic little girls," though McGraw will only react with confusion. Meeting Henry Casdin and working with him will also allow the player to mention Fort Independence and working with the Outcasts previously, which McGraw appreciates.
• After completing the simulation, McGraw and the other Outcasts get in an argument, escalating to a violent dispute. If McGraw survives, he will thank the Lone Wanderer and welcome them to come back anytime.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: Note: 30 MFC are guaranteed to spawn, with a 75% chance for 15 more. Laser rifle's condition is randomly leveled, and has 65% max.

chr_01000e22.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox
chr_01000e22.summary: Specialist Olin is a member of the Brotherhood Outcasts at their outpost at Bailey's Crossroads in the Capital Wasteland housing the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Like all of the Outcasts, Olin once swore loyalty to the Capital Wasteland chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel led by Elder Owyn Lyons. She was one of those who disagreed with "old man Lyons" over his disobedience to the West Coast elders, and she ultimately joined Henry Casdin and other hardliners in their schism, splintering off into the Outcasts.

Sometime prior to 2277, the now-Specialist Olin joined the group led by Protector McGraw in taking over the pre-War Virtual Strategic Solutions facility within the ruins of Washington D.C. Olin's technical expertise earned her the role of maintaining and running the facility's technology suite, including a fully virtual simulation recreating the events of the Battle of Anchorage.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Aiding the Outcasts: Olin gives the Lone Wanderer the neural interface suit needed to enter the Anchorage Reclamation simulation and directs them to enter the simulation pod.
• Operation: Anchorage!: After exiting the simulation and opening the armory, Defender Sibley and his supporters will revolt against McGraw. Olin is one of the Outcasts on McGraw's side, so she will help fight against Sibley's group.
• If Olin survives Sibley's revolt, she will thank the Lone Wanderer for their help against Sibley and offer her services as a repair vendor. She is able to repair items up to 50% of their condition.
• Olin will still mention Sibley revolting even if it did not happen (i.e. if Sibley died for any reason before his revolt would have occurred).

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Outcast Outpost. Notable equipment & inventory: Outcast Scribe Robe.

chr_010009c3.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox
chr_010009c3.summary: Lieutenant Thomas Morgan is an intelligence and logistics officer providing American soldiers with intel and clearing requisitions at the U.S. Army field headquarters in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Thomas Morgan is a young officer of the Intelligence Corps, working in Intelligence and Logistics (I&L). His role includes identifying targets and providing soldiers with intelligence and assets necessary to take them out - he points, they shoot. He carries out his duties with a wry sense of humor, which is his method of coping with being posted to Alaska, fighting one of the best militaries in the world, in freezing temperatures.

As part of his duties, Morgan processes intel, combining reconnaissance reports, radar monitoring and other data, to provide soldiers and their commander, General Chase, with an accurate picture of the battlefield and the changing situation, as well as identify targets that can weaken the Chinese army and shift the odds in favor of the United States.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Paving the Way and Operation: Anchorage!: Morgan provides the player with requisition holotapes and instructs on their use, as well as providing additional intel on objectives, such as the expected enemy composition and the way to achieve objectives.

Other interactions:
He refers to the strike team as "Patterson's suicide team." If asked about why he calls it that, he simply states that his humor is the only way he can cope with the cold.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: 1 He carries a 10mm pistol skinned with the wasteland version graphics, instead of the pre-War version typical in the simulation. He cannot be induced to draw the weapon, nor can it be pickpocketed from him.

chr_010009c2.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: happy. AI packages: follow, dialogue, travel, sandbox, use item
chr_010009c2.summary:
Infobox character
|name =Benjamin Montgomery
|subtitle =Benji was a pre-War member of the United States Marine Corps who fought in the Battle of Anchorage. A digital avatar made in his likeness appears in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Gunnery Sergeant Benjamin Montgomery served during the Sino-American War in the late 21st century, during which he was deployed to the Anchorage frontline on multiple tours against the Chinese forces under General Jingwei occupying Alaska. While he acts as a model soldier and initially addresses others in military fashion, once he became friendly with someone, they were given an informal nickname by him as he proved to be a loyal confidante to his comrades.

Based on his depiction in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation, Montgomery participated in frontline operations directly leading to the liberation of Anchorage.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Guns of Anchorage: Montgomery will help the Lone Wanderer as they wake up when first entering the simulation. He will then hand them their equipment and begin climbing the cliffs, leaving the Lone Wanderer to take the long way to the cave outpost. At arrival, both he and the player will proceed with destroying the artillery guns.
• Paving the Way: Montgomery is a recruitable strike team leader and assists with the securing of the listening post, along with helping in the destruction of the fuel tanks and the Chimera armor depot.
• Operation: Anchorage!: Montgomery alone accompanies the Lone Wanderer through the pulse field and into the Chinese occupied refinery.

Effects of player's actions:
• Killing the quartermaster will cause Sgt. Montgomery to turn hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: 10mm Round, Silenced 10mm Pistol, Winterized Combat Armor.

chr_010009c1.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, use item, sandbox, travel
chr_010009c1.summary: General Constantine Chase was a pre-War United States Army general, commanding officer of the Anchorage Reclamation, a military operation that repelled Chinese forces from Alaska in January 2077. The Lone Wanderer encounters and receives orders from a computer-generated reconstruction of Chase during their run through the Anchorage Reclamation simulation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Holding the highest general officer rank, Constantine Chase was one of the most prominent pre-War military officers, as the commander for the Battle of Anchorage responsible for driving the People's Liberation Army from Alaska. He was a competent officer, noted for his gruff personality and staunch anti-communism, bordering on paranoia, as well as a certain flair for the dramatic: Instead of relying on conventional military assets, Chase launched a development program to create a superweapon capable of liberating Anchorage Alaska, in the form of a "walking, talking, nuke-tossing hero who [would] remind the world what it means to be a super power" and shock the Chinese into submission, like the nuclear bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Paving the Way: General Chase is met after destroying the artillery guns bombarding the field headquarters, and grants the player character a field promotion to commander of the strike team formerly led by the late Colonel Patterson. He then assigns the objectives for Operation Anchorage: The destruction of the Chimera armor depot, the listening post, and the pulse field.
• Operation: Anchorage!: After all three objectives are completed and the player defeats General Jingwei, Chase will appear and debrief the player, commenting on their attitude and, if all intel was recovered, noting that fact.

Other interactions:
• Chase cannot be pickpocketed nor harmed in any way, even through console commands.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Command Tent. Notable equipment & inventory: General Chase's Overcoat.

chr_0200b65d.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: puzzled. AI packages: sandbox
chr_0200b65d.summary: Pitt Slave is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 9, 140 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Slaves. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Continuously watched by the Pitt raiders, they are forced to run the Pitt's steel industry. In addition, the slaves are also plagued by the troglodyte degeneration contagion, the disease which renders all of the Pitt's inhabitants infertile and turns some of them into wildmen and trogs over time.

Most of them are located in Downtown and The Mill, although a couple of dead slaves can be found in the Pitt steelyard, apparently recruits of Everett who died during their efforts to retrieve steel ingots, and a few are encountered on the Bridge trying to escape.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Free Labor: Determine the fate of the Pitt's slaves.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should the player character side with Wernher, the Pitt slaves are freed.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt slave:
Most of the Pitt slaves are found working in The Mill or in Downtown, working on various tasks to keep the Pitt's industry going. In the Mill, conversations between slaves regarding an uprising can be overheard.

Clad in varied slave outfits, they are not allowed to have better weaponry than the steel saws they need for work, although Marco works on providing them with better armament like auto axes for the revolt.

Slave fighter:
Three slave fighters are encountered in the first battle in The Pitt, said to be the fiercest fighters the slave force has to offer.

chr_0200a7c0.summary: Pitt Raider is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 9, 95 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Found primarily around Haven. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor.

sections.title: Interactions with player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Before entering the Hole, Pitt raiders and guards will show the Lone Wanderer little respect and often call them "scab" and "slave". Following the player character's success in the Hole, their demeanor will change and begin to respect them more and more.
• If one chooses to free the slaves by killing Lord Ashur and his followers during the main questline, then no more Pitt raiders will respawn afterward, making the special Pitt raider armors they wear limited in quantity.

Other interactions:
• If one's Intelligence is high enough, they may refer to the player character as "professor"; likewise, they comment on one's Strength if it is high enough. After completing the fights in The Hole, they may refer to the player character as "newbie".

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider:
The first time Pitt raiders of the generic variant are encountered is in the Capital Wasteland when answering Wernher's radio signal. In the Pitt itself, they are guarding every area except for the steelyard. Generic Pitt raiders are marginally stronger than standard raiders; they also have slightly superior armor and equipment.

The three Pitt raiders sent to pursue Wernher into the Capital Wasteland may be equipped with metal armor, making them somewhat tougher than average.

Guard:
Guards are found in the Pitt's Downtown and the Mill, watching the slaves. They are armed with 10mm SMGs and tire irons and wear one of the Pitt's raider armor variants.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Haven. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0200a688.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, travel
chr_0200a688.summary: Everett, also referred to as the foreman or Mill Foreman Everett, is a Pitt raider, usually found in The Mill.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Everett coordinates the effort to recover steel ingots from the Pitt steelyard. He enjoys sending slaves to their likely demise but is not without some sympathy for their struggle. He feels that sending the under-equipped slaves out to the steelyard to die is something of a waste, and believes that the Pitt raiders should also chip in for the ingot collection effort even though some believe that they're "too good for it." As a collector of unique items, he offers a variety of unique pieces of equipment to those slaves and Pitt raiders who manage to successfully acquire ingots from the steelyard.

He is originally dismissive of the Lone Wanderer and their abilities when they are first sent to him as the newest member of the ingot collection team, believing that they wouldn’t last long against the various dangers of the steelyard.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Unsafe Working Conditions: Everett is the person that the player's character reports to for steelyard duty. He also rewards the player for turning in steel ingots; 10 are required for this quest.
• Mill Worker: The player can choose to continue collecting ingots beyond the minimum required for "Unsafe Working Conditions". With every 10 ingots gathered, he will reward them with a piece of equipment. Note that he is the source of several unique weapons and armor, including The Mauler, the Perforator, tribal power armor, and the Metal Blaster.

Effects of player's actions:
• Regardless of who you side with, Everett will remain friendly. If you choose to free the slaves, Wernher will tell you that Everett is still alive and accepting ingots.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Mill. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_02009f4b.summary: Milly is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 30 HP). Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Find Wild Bill.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Milly and Wild Bill were extremely close friends, having worked the mill together for a long time. A week prior to the Lone Wanderer’s arrival, the slaves were forced to choose someone to gather ingots from the steelyard, for which Wild Bill volunteered, not wanting anyone else to die in his place. He never returned, prompting Milly to look for someone who could find him, not believing that he could be dead. Upon acquiring The Lone Wanderer’s assistance in finding Wild Bill, she asks them to be careful, insisting that Wild Bill would never forgive himself if someone else got hurt looking for him. Upon being informed of his death, Milly is very distraught, to the point of fainting if the details of Wild Bill’s death are brutally exaggerated.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Milly never actually grinds metal, she simply walks around the Downtown area, waiting for news from Wild Bill.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Wild Bill's Last Stand: Wild Bill has not been seen since volunteering to collect steel ingots from the steelyard, and Milly is offering a reward to anyone who can find him.

chr_02009f4a.summary: Wild Bill is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Wasteland Slaves. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Wild Bill and Milly were extremely close friends, having worked together in the mill for some time. About a week before the Lone Wanderer’s arrival, the slaves were forced to choose someone to send to the steelyard to collect steel ingots. Although he managed to collect several ingots and warded off or eliminated several trogs with his handgun, the gunfire attracted the attention of wildmen operating in the area, who ultimately killed him before he was able to return to the mill. He managed to leave a note to Milly before the wildmen found him, apologizing to her and the others for not managing to complete the task.

sections.title: Relationship
sections.text: Wild Bill developed a keen relationship with a fellow slave Milly, as their time in the mill together was a sort of bonding experience.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Wild Bill's Last Stand: Milly is extremely worried about Bill's disappearance and asks the player character for any information they may have regarding his whereabouts.

chr_02009b54.role: Capital Wastelander, The Pitt Slaves — Asian
chr_02009b54.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

chr_02009b53.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_02009acb.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, sandbox
chr_02009acb.summary: Pitt Slave is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Continuously watched by the Pitt raiders, they are forced to run the Pitt's steel industry. In addition, the slaves are also plagued by the troglodyte degeneration contagion, the disease which renders all of the Pitt's inhabitants infertile and turns some of them into wildmen and trogs over time.

Most of them are located in Downtown and The Mill, although a couple of dead slaves can be found in the Pitt steelyard, apparently recruits of Everett who died during their efforts to retrieve steel ingots, and a few are encountered on the Bridge trying to escape.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Free Labor: Determine the fate of the Pitt's slaves.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should the player character side with Wernher, the Pitt slaves are freed.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt slave:
Most of the Pitt slaves are found working in The Mill or in Downtown, working on various tasks to keep the Pitt's industry going. In the Mill, conversations between slaves regarding an uprising can be overheard.

Clad in varied slave outfits, they are not allowed to have better weaponry than the steel saws they need for work, although Marco works on providing them with better armament like auto axes for the revolt.

Slave fighter:
Three slave fighters are encountered in the first battle in The Pitt, said to be the fiercest fighters the slave force has to offer.

chr_02009385.summary: Pitt Raider is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Wasteland Slaves. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Before entering the Hole, Pitt raiders and guards will show the Lone Wanderer little respect and often call them "scab" and "slave". Following the player character's success in the Hole, their demeanor will change and begin to respect them more and more.
• If one chooses to free the slaves by killing Lord Ashur and his followers during the main questline, then no more Pitt raiders will respawn afterward, making the special Pitt raider armors they wear limited in quantity.

Other interactions:
• If one's Intelligence is high enough, they may refer to the player character as "professor"; likewise, they comment on one's Strength if it is high enough. After completing the fights in The Hole, they may refer to the player character as "newbie".

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider:
The first time Pitt raiders of the generic variant are encountered is in the Capital Wasteland when answering Wernher's radio signal. In the Pitt itself, they are guarding every area except for the steelyard. Generic Pitt raiders are marginally stronger than standard raiders; they also have slightly superior armor and equipment.

The three Pitt raiders sent to pursue Wernher into the Capital Wasteland may be equipped with metal armor, making them somewhat tougher than average.

Guard:
Guards are found in the Pitt's Downtown and the Mill, watching the slaves. They are armed with 10mm SMGs and tire irons and wear one of the Pitt's raider armor variants.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across The Pitt encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Frag Grenade, Gamma Shield Armor.

Most of them are located in Downtown and The Mill, although a couple of dead slaves can be found in the Pitt steelyard, apparently recruits of Everett who died during their efforts to retrieve steel ingots, and a few are encountered on the Bridge trying to escape.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Free Labor: Determine the fate of the Pitt's slaves.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should the player character side with Wernher, the Pitt slaves are freed.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt slave:
Most of the Pitt slaves are found working in The Mill or in Downtown, working on various tasks to keep the Pitt's industry going. In the Mill, conversations between slaves regarding an uprising can be overheard.

Clad in varied slave outfits, they are not allowed to have better weaponry than the steel saws they need for work, although Marco works on providing them with better armament like auto axes for the revolt.

Slave fighter:
Three slave fighters are encountered in the first battle in The Pitt, said to be the fiercest fighters the slave force has to offer.

chr_02007f95.summary: Pitt Raider is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 9, 90 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Before entering the Hole, Pitt raiders and guards will show the Lone Wanderer little respect and often call them "scab" and "slave". Following the player character's success in the Hole, their demeanor will change and begin to respect them more and more.
• If one chooses to free the slaves by killing Lord Ashur and his followers during the main questline, then no more Pitt raiders will respawn afterward, making the special Pitt raider armors they wear limited in quantity.

Other interactions:
• If one's Intelligence is high enough, they may refer to the player character as "professor"; likewise, they comment on one's Strength if it is high enough. After completing the fights in The Hole, they may refer to the player character as "newbie".

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider:
The first time Pitt raiders of the generic variant are encountered is in the Capital Wasteland when answering Wernher's radio signal. In the Pitt itself, they are guarding every area except for the steelyard. Generic Pitt raiders are marginally stronger than standard raiders; they also have slightly superior armor and equipment.

The three Pitt raiders sent to pursue Wernher into the Capital Wasteland may be equipped with metal armor, making them somewhat tougher than average.

Guard:
Guards are found in the Pitt's Downtown and the Mill, watching the slaves. They are armed with 10mm SMGs and tire irons and wear one of the Pitt's raider armor variants.

sections.title: Interactions with player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Before entering the Hole, Pitt raiders and guards will show the Lone Wanderer little respect and often call them "scab" and "slave". Following the player character's success in the Hole, their demeanor will change and begin to respect them more and more.
• If one chooses to free the slaves by killing Lord Ashur and his followers during the main questline, then no more Pitt raiders will respawn afterward, making the special Pitt raider armors they wear limited in quantity.

Other interactions:
• If one's Intelligence is high enough, they may refer to the player character as "professor"; likewise, they comment on one's Strength if it is high enough. After completing the fights in The Hole, they may refer to the player character as "newbie".

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider:
The first time Pitt raiders of the generic variant are encountered is in the Capital Wasteland when answering Wernher's radio signal. In the Pitt itself, they are guarding every area except for the steelyard. Generic Pitt raiders are marginally stronger than standard raiders; they also have slightly superior armor and equipment.

The three Pitt raiders sent to pursue Wernher into the Capital Wasteland may be equipped with metal armor, making them somewhat tougher than average.

Guard:
Guards are found in the Pitt's Downtown and the Mill, watching the slaves. They are armed with 10mm SMGs and tire irons and wear one of the Pitt's raider armor variants.

chr_02006c18.summary: Pitt Slave is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 1, 25 HP). Affiliated with Wasteland Slaves. Found primarily around Pitt Underground.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Continuously watched by the Pitt raiders, they are forced to run the Pitt's steel industry. In addition, the slaves are also plagued by the troglodyte degeneration contagion, the disease which renders all of the Pitt's inhabitants infertile and turns some of them into wildmen and trogs over time.

Most of them are located in Downtown and The Mill, although a couple of dead slaves can be found in the Pitt steelyard, apparently recruits of Everett who died during their efforts to retrieve steel ingots, and a few are encountered on the Bridge trying to escape.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Free Labor: Determine the fate of the Pitt's slaves.

Effects of player's actions:
• Should the player character side with Wernher, the Pitt slaves are freed.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt slave:
Most of the Pitt slaves are found working in The Mill or in Downtown, working on various tasks to keep the Pitt's industry going. In the Mill, conversations between slaves regarding an uprising can be overheard.

Clad in varied slave outfits, they are not allowed to have better weaponry than the steel saws they need for work, although Marco works on providing them with better armament like auto axes for the revolt.

Slave fighter:
Three slave fighters are encountered in the first battle in The Pitt, said to be the fiercest fighters the slave force has to offer.

chr_02006166.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: guard, travel
chr_02006166.summary: Mex is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor, Into The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mex once served as a general guard in The Pitt’s Downtown region, but his excessive cruelty and punishment towards the slaves led Ashur to instead have him guard the gates to the city. He now guards the gates against outside threats and disposes of escaped slaves who attempt to cross the bridge, going so far as to lay down mines and shoot escapees with his rifle.

Upon the Lone Wanderer's arrival, their interaction with Mex depends on the attire they are wearing. Should they be wearing the previously acquired slave outfit, he will assume them to be an escaped slave who was unable to cross the bridge, saying that they are lucky he doesn’t kill them right then and there, instead confiscating their equipment and sending them into Downtown. If they are not wearing the slave outfit, their options are more expansive.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Mex and three of his men keep their guns trained on the road into town all day, ready to blow away any pests or vermin trying to get in.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Into The Pitt - Mex is the Pitt's gate guard and needs to be passed to enter the city.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer tells him they are a returning escaped slave, he will strip the Lone Wanderer of their inventory (except the "hidden weapon" possibly received from Wernher), give a slave outfit that is automatically equipped (whether the Lone Wanderer is wearing one already or not), and then tell them to enter Downtown.
• If the Lone Wanderer tells him they came looking for work, he will sarcastically invite them to enter through the door to Downtown and fill out a "fucking application", whereupon the same happens as noted above; an ambush with items stripped (except the "hidden weapon"), and the slave outfit.

• Before entering the Hole, Pitt raiders and guards will show the Lone Wanderer little respect and often call them "scab" and "slave". Following the player character's success in the Hole, their demeanor will change and begin to respect them more and more.
• If one chooses to free the slaves by killing Lord Ashur and his followers during the main questline, then no more Pitt raiders will respawn afterward, making the special Pitt raider armors they wear limited in quantity.

Other interactions:
• If one's Intelligence is high enough, they may refer to the player character as "professor"; likewise, they comment on one's Strength if it is high enough. After completing the fights in The Hole, they may refer to the player character as "newbie".

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider:
The first time Pitt raiders of the generic variant are encountered is in the Capital Wasteland when answering Wernher's radio signal. In the Pitt itself, they are guarding every area except for the steelyard. Generic Pitt raiders are marginally stronger than standard raiders; they also have slightly superior armor and equipment.

The three Pitt raiders sent to pursue Wernher into the Capital Wasteland may be equipped with metal armor, making them somewhat tougher than average.

Guard:
Guards are found in the Pitt's Downtown and the Mill, watching the slaves. They are armed with 10mm SMGs and tire irons and wear one of the Pitt's raider armor variants.

chr_0200413e.summary: Reddup is a african american character in The Pitt (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor, Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Reddup is a former slave who fought his way up through the arena. He is one of only three known individuals to have achieved this; the others being Gruber and Squill. He is staunchly loyal to Ashur, but his rage causes him to be overzealous when dealing with those Pitt slaves who have supposedly committed crimes or misdemeanors while going about their duties. He does not think twice about killing them, and especially doesn’t think twice about killing trogs, who he snipes at with glee whenever they try to make an incursion into areas controlled by the Pitt raiders.

The Lone Wanderer’s interaction with Mex upon first arriving in The Pitt shapes their interactions with Reddup as well.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Into The Pitt: If the Lone Wanderer has chosen not to don a slave disguise nor to claim to be a slave when confronted, Reddup will lead their "welcoming committee" by beating the player character into unconsciousness. This applies whether one is "applying for a job" or they have killed the guards outside.

Other interactions:
• After one wins their freedom, the player character can challenge Reddup to a one-on-one rematch; this will cause him to become hostile and attack. Killing him during the "rematch" will not cause others in the area to become hostile.

chr_0200413d.summary: O-Dog is a member of the Pitt raiders who is commonly seen walking around the courtyard of Haven in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
O-Dog has a unique view of the world, considering all individuals to be differing grades of "meat." He believes that everyone will be eaten sooner or later and that they just have to be the best and eat what they can before they are next on the menu. He views the Lone Wanderer’s success in the arena as them simply having "moved up to a higher grade of sausage."

Being another competent user of precision firearms, O-Dog is infatuated with Vikia and competes with Duke to get her attention, though he is rarely successful.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: O-Dog spends a lot of time shooting at beer bottles on an opposite building with his.32 hunting rifle. He can also be found walking around Uptown.

chr_0200413c.summary: Duke is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Duke is vying for Krenshaw's position as Ashur's second-in-command, and has the rifle prowess to back up some of his plans to gain additional power within the faction. He is very knowledgeable of the history of The Pitt and some of its inhabitants, and will share some of these details with the Lone Wanderer upon their ascent from the fighting pit.

Duke is also known to compete with O-Dog for Vikia's attention.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can be seen either warming his hands at the fire next to where Phantom, Mona, or Squill are practicing their melee strikes, or shooting at the beer bottles at the same place where O-Dog and Vikia practice.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
He will congratulate the Lone Wanderer for fighting their way out of the Hole, and he will tell them that many of the Pitt raiders were once slaves who also fought their way out of the Hole, although the only confirmed members of this category are Gruber, Reddup, and Squill.

chr_0200413b.summary: Phantom is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Phantom is considerably more amicable towards the Lone Wanderer than most of the other Pitt raiders and will enthusiastically welcome them to the group. He acts as an improvised medic for the faction, working to treat radiation poisoning amongst the raiders with his supply of RadAway, which he will readily share with the Lone Wanderer if they need it.

He has strong opinions about the amount of work that both the raiders and the slaves do, believing that the slaves have it easy compared to the raiders, who risk their lives while raiding caravans to acquire food for the city’s residents.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Once a day, the player can ask Phantom for radiation treatment, resulting in Phantom giving the player a dose of RadAway.
• He will get defensive if one asks him "You think you work harder than the slaves?". He will reply "Fuck yes we do," and will back himself up by mentioning how raiders have to go through so much just to get supplies and food for the slaves.

chr_0200413a.summary: Squill is a african american character in The Pitt (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Unlike many of the other Pitt raiders, Squill is a good-natured and enthusiastic soldier. She is a former slave who fought her way through the arena, being one of only three slaves to accomplish this alongside Gruber and Reddup. As such, she has considerable respect for the Lone Wanderer’s own accomplishments in the arena and will lightheartedly joke with them about the situation.

Squill happily mentions that she often fires into the arena from the spectator area if the fight is not exciting enough. She also mentions that when this was done to her when she was a gladiator slave, she shot back, and hopes the Lone Wanderer would do the same as she did if she had shot down at them during their own fights.

chr_02004139.summary: Vikia is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A skilled sniper, Vikia is extremely condescending towards all others, especially current or former Pitt slaves. Unlike many of the other Pitt raiders, Vikia is strictly unimpressed with the Lone Wanderer’s accomplishments fighting in the arena. She approves of being called a "bitch," believing that being so is part of the cost of perfection of her craft. She firmly believes herself to be above others, and, should she be sexually propositioned by a male Lone Wanderer, will be disgusted by their attempts, believing a “beast of burden” to not be worthy of her.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Vikia can generally be found on the roof of the raider barracks, engaging in target practice with her sniper rifle on several rows of bottles in the building window across from her location.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Even if the player earns a position as a raider by fighting in the arena, she still considers them a former slave and therefore beneath her.
• If one has the Lady Killer perk, she tells the Lone Wanderer that she won't sleep with them, no matter how mighty they are.

chr_02004138.summary: Lulu is a asian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 70 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Lulu roams Uptown's walkways, praising Lord Ashur and feeding noodles to Uptown's raider population. An insane but fiercely loyal follower of Ashur, Lulu refers to everyone as "pets" belonging to Ashur, because Ashur chose all of them, including herself, to be in his company. She makes a distinction between "good" and "bad" pets: those who contribute and earn their keep are "good," while the "bad" ones are drowned in the Monongahela River. Lulu also constantly refers to herself in the third person. Her devotion to Ashur borders on the religious, and she is excited to see how Ashur judges the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Once a day, she will give the Lone Wanderer three bowls of noodles, if asked.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Trouble Man is a member of the Pitt raiders who is usually found guarding the catwalks in the Pitt Downtown. Due to the waking nightmares he experiences, he likes to keep to himself, rarely conversing with others. Trouble Man often consumes both beer and Jet to quell these nightmares, but this leaves him able to only say a few words, Even so, he is still a helper to Friday, who operates a repair shop in Downtown.

Trouble Man tells the Lone Wanderer that they don't want to know how he got his name, warning that he is trouble and that they should be careful.

Together with Trouble Man, Friday operates her own repair shop and merchant stand where she sells a variety of equipment and repairs broken weaponry. Although she is mild-mannered, she is a ruthless businesswoman.

As business is usually slow, she is ready for the Lone Wanderer to spend their money at her store after their ascent from fighting in the area.

The Lone Wanderer cannot engage with any meaningful conversation with Bingo, as he only says his name over and over again. Bingo is actually old enough remember the time of the Scourge, but would rather indulge in his alcoholism, building up his own beer collection in his apartment.

sections.title: Daily schedule

chr_02003e49.summary: Nola is a african american character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Slaves. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Nola has taken on the role of being an improvised medic for the other Pitt slaves, having some amount of rudimentary medical training. She attempts to tend to the sick, crippled, and wounded of those slaves working in Downtown and The Mill, but she is one of the least skilled practitioners that can be encountered by the Lone Wanderer.

If the Lone Wanderer is injured upon meeting Nola, she will generously offer to heal them, free of charge. If the Lone Wanderer declines her offer, she will tell them to be careful, as the Pitt slaves need everyone to be as healthy as possible. If they accept, she will do her best to heal them, but due to her lack of skill and the poor conditions in The Pitt, she may accidentally hurt them rather than heal them.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Nola spends her time in the grinding hole in the middle of Downtown, slicing at an old car and dodging shots from the slave master.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
When being healed by Nola, there is a risk of one of the Lone Wanderer's limbs being crippled because of the poor work conditions in the Pitt.

chr_02003e48.summary: Marco is a asian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Slaves. Found primarily around The Mill. Directly connected to quests: Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Marco is a mechanically-minded member of the Pitt slaves who is currently operating and maintaining the equipment in the Mill's rotary press control room. Secretly, however, he is also constructing improvised weaponry to assist in the eventual uprising against the Pitt raiders led by his friend Midea and former Pitt raider Wernher. He does this by upgrading the steel saws with scavenged car engine parts, turning them into formidable auto axes with which the slaves can fight the raiders. However, he will only supply these weapons to slaves that he knows will assist in the uprising when the time comes. Some of the other Pitt slaves in the Mill are working harder in order to conceal Marco's illicit activities from the bosses.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Marco spends all of his time in a room filled with computers. The computers cannot be used by the player, and activating the safety stop mechanism prompts an "access denied" response.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Unsafe Working Conditions: Marco gives the player character an auto axe if asked for one, once they have spoken to Midea in her quarters.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Brand is told about what Marco is doing, he will be killed for his role in making weapons.
• He can be found dead while the slaves are fighting the raiders.

chr_02003e2f.summary: Kai is a hispanic character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Slaves. Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The slightly depressed and illiterate Kai has taken on the role of cook, supplying the other Pitt slaves with slop, a meal that mostly consists of trog meat and irradiated water from the nearby river. She is particularly apathetic about the meal, and actually approves of those who decide not to eat it, being unsure of whether it or starvation would kill someone faster.

Beyond supplying the Lone Wanderer with slop, she can also inform them as to the whereabouts of Marco, who she knows to be in the Mill when he is not coming to her for meals. Regardless of the Lone Wanderer's actions, Kai will be killed during the uprising.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Kai dies automatically once the Free Labor quest is completed, even if she survives the battle between the Pitt slaves and Pitt raiders during the slave uprising. Just like Adan and the slave on the pillory, she is killed by the quest script and cannot be saved. If resurrected using the console, depending on the player's choices, she may return to her stall or be killed on sight by the raiders.

Other interactions:
• She will serve one portion of slop upon each interaction for free, with a nasty comment on it.
• Kai holds five bowls of slop at a time, her stock is replenished the next in-game day.
• Kai is the only source of slop in the game and will cease dishing it out after one has completed the quest Unsafe Working Conditions and talked to Midea about fighting in the Hole.

chr_02003e2e.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_02003e2e.summary: Brand is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around The Mill.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brand has taken the opportunity to supply the Pitt raiders with information about the other slaves, up to and including information about any secret plans the slaves are making. In exchange, he receives extra benefits and bonuses, and is allowed to rest more during the work detail. Because of this, he is not well liked by the other slaves, and has gained a reputation for being a snitch. As such, the slaves often warn each other and others not to trust him.

In interaction with Brand, the Lone Wanderer can choose to reveal the secrets of those involved in the uprising, including Wernher, Midea, Marco, and even themselves. In the case of Marco, Brand will be overjoyed to learn information with which he can cause Marco’s demise by revealing it to the Pitt raiders, as Marco is claimed to have repeatedly wronged him in the past.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Slave Snitch: By speaking to him, one may reveal several secrets to him, including telling him about the riot Wernher is organizing. He gives two stimpaks and 25 XP per piece of information. Telling Brand any "info" gives negative Karma.

Effects of player's actions:
• Telling him about Marco will result in Marco's death.
• Once the revolt starts, he may be killed by the other slaves, or survive by hiding.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Mill. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_02003e2d.summary: Adan is a african american character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Unlike most of the other workers in downtown, Adan is content with the life he has been forced to live by Ashur's army. Although he would much rather be free, he has decided that attaining freedom is currently an impossibility and thinking about it would only make him more miserable. He came to this conclusion after recovering several philosophy texts in the ruins, which he had Midea read to him. He also has a penchant for quoting from these texts, especially to those who do not understand his unique attitude.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Adan spends his days in front of the entrance to the Mill, sawing away at a destroyed bus with his steel saw. This is all he does until the quest Free Labor, in which his body can be found at the same location, being killed during the chaos caused by the uprising.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
Adan will speak with the player character about philosophy and how it relates to his life as a slave.

chr_02003435.summary: Pitt Raider is a asian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Interactions with player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Before entering the Hole, Pitt raiders and guards will show the Lone Wanderer little respect and often call them "scab" and "slave". Following the player character's success in the Hole, their demeanor will change and begin to respect them more and more.
• If one chooses to free the slaves by killing Lord Ashur and his followers during the main questline, then no more Pitt raiders will respawn afterward, making the special Pitt raider armors they wear limited in quantity.

Other interactions:
• If one's Intelligence is high enough, they may refer to the player character as "professor"; likewise, they comment on one's Strength if it is high enough. After completing the fights in The Hole, they may refer to the player character as "newbie".

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider:
The first time Pitt raiders of the generic variant are encountered is in the Capital Wasteland when answering Wernher's radio signal. In the Pitt itself, they are guarding every area except for the steelyard. Generic Pitt raiders are marginally stronger than standard raiders; they also have slightly superior armor and equipment.

The three Pitt raiders sent to pursue Wernher into the Capital Wasteland may be equipped with metal armor, making them somewhat tougher than average.

Guard:
Guards are found in the Pitt's Downtown and the Mill, watching the slaves. They are armed with 10mm SMGs and tire irons and wear one of the Pitt's raider armor variants.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across The Pitt encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Apparel & Goods.

chr_02003300.summary: Krenshaw is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Found primarily around Haven. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor, Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
After the betrayal and departure of Wernher, Krenshaw became Ashur’s second-in-command. He is in charge of maintaining The Pitt’s security and peace, with particular focus on defending against Trogs and preventing a rebellion by the slaves without culling too many of their population. He is also in charge of maintaining the floodlight generator rig that protects Haven from being overrun by Trogs. Duke is currently vying for his position.

When the Lone Wanderer gains their freedom by successfully winning a set of fights in the arena, Krenshaw congratulates them on their accomplishments and relays that Ashur wishes to see them, also providing them with "gifts" from him, those being their previously confiscated items.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Unsafe Working Conditions: Krenshaw is present during the speech Ishmael Ashur gives to the slaves prior to the player's participation in The Hole. After the fights, Krenshaw informs them that Ashur wishes to talk.
• Free Labor: Krenshaw can be heard arguing with Ashur when taking the elevator up to Haven, and leaves when Ashur promises to handle the situation. Krenshaw does not like that Ashur is holding an audience when the city is in danger, but reluctantly follows orders. Should one choose to steal Marie, Krenshaw will be the first raider outside to start firing at the player.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Haven. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Apparel & Goods.

chr_020032f8.summary: Grudd Bear is a african american character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around The Hole. Directly connected to quests: Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
During the Scourge, Grudd's younger brother Greg was taken in by the Brotherhood. However, he and John were left behind due to being "too wild and mean." They were then taken in by Ishmael Ashur for his raider army, and in his words, they became two of his "finest soldiers." By 2277, the Bear Brothers had become undefeated fighters in the Hole.

Grudd and John employ a particular effective method of attack, in which Grudd holds back and uses his Flamer to attack the target, while John attacks the target directly with his Deathclaw Gauntlet. Thanks to an addiction to RadAway, they are both nearly impervious to the arena’s radiation traps.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: Grudd is the brother of John Bear and Kodiak.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Unsafe Working Conditions: The Bear Brothers are the second round's only opponents. Grudd will attack with his flamer while his brother slashes through the Lone Wanderer's armor with a deathclaw gauntlet. Both brothers need to be killed to progress through the arena.

chr_020032e6.summary: Gruber is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around The Hole. Directly connected to quests: Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Gruber was once a Pitt slave, but he became one of the few to win his freedom through fighting in the arena. After winning his freedom, he continued to fight, ultimately advancing to the point where he is considered to be the best arena fighter in The Pitt. Prior to the Lone Wanderer’s arrival, he was undefeated in the arena. As a tested veteran of one-on-one combat, he is solely concentrated on furthering his career in the arena and keeping his rifle maintained.

When the Lone Wanderer is set up to fight him as their final test in the arena, Faydra predicts that they will not survive.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Unsafe Working Conditions: Gruber is the Lone Wanderer's final opponent in the Hole, and will open fire as soon as the round begins. One will need to kill him to finish the arena battles.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Hole. Notable equipment & inventory: Gamma Shield Armor, 5.56mm Round.

chr_020032e4.summary: Faydra is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Found primarily around The Mill. Directly connected to quests: Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Faydra guards the entrance to the arena, also known as the Hole. During her time in this position, she has scavenged several pieces of equipment from past fighters who died in the arena. As she has seen many past fighters fall, it takes someone of considerable combat capabilities to impress her. At least one Pitt slave regards Faydra as being the worst of the Pitt raiders, and says that the first thing they will do once the uprising takes place is burn her eyes out.

She coordinates the fights that take place in the arena and will provide instructions to the Lone Wanderer regarding participation in the fighting. She will make comments about each opponent that the Lone Wanderer progressively faces. She will also make additional comments about the Lone Wanderer's successes in the arena, beginning to gain a sense of respect for them.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She stands around in front of the Hole, waiting for an unlucky scab to get booted down and thrown into the fight.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Mill. Notable equipment & inventory: Chinese Assault Rifle, 5.56mm Round.

chr_02002bd7.summary: Prosper is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Into The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Before his capture by slavers, Prosper was a smuggler who transported illicit cargos of steel ingots from The Pitt to outlying areas. Despite his paranoia, nervousness, and carefulness, Prosper’s operation was compromised at some point prior to the Lone Wanderer meeting him. The majority of his crew were killed, while the others, including him, were sold to slavers traveling to Paradise Falls.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Into The Pitt: The Lone Wanderer can buy him and the other slaves in the slave pen from Ramsey or kill all of the slavers to get the key to open the pen. After either option, one can either threaten Prosper into giving them his slave outfit or get the slave outfit from the dead slave in the corner.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_02002940.summary: Slave Master is a asian character in The Pitt (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with The Pitt Raiders. Encountered in The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Tasked by Lord Ashur with watching the bridge that spans the Monongahela River leading into the Pitt, he watches both for any dangers coming in or any slaves trying to get out. Most days are uneventful, but every once in awhile, he gets a slave trying to escape and has a little fun taking pot shots at them with his rifle or watching them get blown up by land mines. He is also fond of "motivating" the slave workers by shooting in their direction.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If one sides with the Pitt slaves during Free Labor, the next time that the slave master is observed "motivating" a slave, he will be attacked by them with an auto axe.
• If the player character stands near him for too long (around 10-15 in-game minutes), he will deliver escalating threats including shooting his rifle close to them, before turning hostile and attacking.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across The Pitt encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level. Provides services: Apparel & Goods.

chr_02002211.summary: Ramsey is a caucasian character in The Pitt (Level 3, 80 HP). Found primarily around Wasteland. Directly connected to quests: Into The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ramsey and his group of slavers have been operating in the northern regions of the Capital Wasteland looking to enslave any lost wastelanders to sell to the raiders from The Pitt. They recently established a camp at the train tunnel in order to ferry slaves to and from The Pitt, and Ramsey is proud of their progress.

Ramsey is currently impatiently awaiting the arrival of one of the Pitt raiders, supposedly a man, in order to sell Prosper and two other slaves to him. He has been instructed by Eulogy Jones to only accept caps for the slaves rather than trade, and has also been instructed to inform the buyer that the slavers apologize for only having three slaves to sell and that they will have more the next time.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Into The Pitt: Ramsey carries the key to open the slave pen. There are three options for obtaining the slave pen key:
• # Pay for the slaves. (200 caps each, 600 caps total)
• # Steal the key from Ramsey.
• # Kill all of the slavers and loot the key to the slave pens off of Ramsey's corpse.

Other interactions:
• If the Lone Wanderer is hostile with Paradise Falls, Ramsey will recognize them and turn hostile.
• If the Lone Wanderer has killed all of the named slavers in Paradise Falls, Ramsey and his fellow slavers will warn them not to talk to them.

chr_0200109b.summary: Midea is a caucasian elderly character in The Pitt (Level 3, 35 HP). Encountered in The Pitt. Directly connected to quests: Free Labor, Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Midea was born in the Pitt shortly after the Scourge and has lived her entire life under the rule of Lord Ashur. Although she desires to free herself and her people from Ashur's rule by any means necessary, she has heard the frightening stories of what it was like in the city before he took over, and sometimes thinks that things are better with him in charge.

In order to have them secure a meeting with Ashur and steal the cure, Midea nominates the Lone Wanderer to both search the steelyard and fight in the Hole, viewing it as the only way that they will be able to get close to Ashur.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Into The Pitt: Wernher directs the Lone Wanderer to Midea as their contact for the mission, and Midea will offer them shelter during their stay in the Pitt.
• Unsafe Working Conditions: She nominates the Lone Wanderer to fight in order to speak with Ashur.
• Free Labor: She directs the player character to Wernher's hideout when they secure the cure.

Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer wears Ashur's power armor around her, she will comment in either a positive or negative light depending on how the quest Free Labor was finished.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sandra was raised as a woman of learning and is highly knowledgeable, particularly in medicine and chemistry. Sometime between 2255 and 2277, she heard rumors of the Pitt's emergence as an organized society and saw fit to travel to the raider-dominated city to meet its new lord, the fallen Brotherhood soldier Ishmael Ashur. Holding no qualms about the ruthlessness needed to reforge civilization, she openly supported Ashur's plans to unite the wasteland through force. For his part, Ashur immediately recognized Sandra's intellect and courage to seek him out despite their surroundings, inviting her to join his regime. He helped her set up a laboratory within his stronghold of Haven to put their combined knowledge to good use.

During these private moments, the two formed a close relationship that soon bloomed into romance.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Sandra never leaves the top floor of Haven where her laboratory and Marie's nursery are located.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Free Labor: The Lone Wanderer can ask Sandra about the true nature of the cure for TDC she's developing.
• Toys for Tots: If one sides with Ashur, the Lone Wanderer can agree to Sandra's request to collect teddy bears for baby Marie in exchange for caps.

Effects of player's actions:
• Taking Marie from her crib will make Sandra threaten the player character, but she may not immediately turn hostile. If one does return her to Sandra, either immediately or after killing Wernher during Free Labor, Sandra's interactions with the player character from then on will be colder and more abrasive due to no longer trusting them around her daughter.
• If one kills Sandra but does not take away Marie, the game will still act as if the Lone Wanderer has sided with the raiders.

chr_02000f20.summary: Ishmael Ashur, formally known as the Lord of The Pitt, is the leader of the raiders occupying the Pitt. A former soldier of the Brotherhood of Steel, he revitalized the city following its near-destruction by the Brotherhood.

sections.title: History
sections.text:
The Scourge:
Born on the West Coast, Ashur was picked for the Brotherhood of Steel expedition to D.C. under Star Paladin Owyn Lyons. With their innability to contact the Midwestern Brotherhood, the Brotherhood was forced to continue their mission and head towards Washington, D.C. During their travels, the expedition came across the ruins of the pre-War city of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Now known as "the Pitt," the city was lawless; gangs, raiders, slavers and many other kinds of horrors all freely wandered the streets, and anarchy ruled unchecked. The few innocent inhabitants had to scratch out a living in this terrorizing environment, most of who were either sick or dying from the combined effects of the intense radiation and pollution from pre-War industrial factories damaged by the bombs spewing into the atmosphere.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Ashur spends the majority of his time in his office at the top of Haven, but is occasionally seen giving speeches to the slaves of the Pitt every once in a while. He also runs the Pitt's radio station.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Haven. Notable equipment & inventory: Ashur's Power Armor, Shotgun Shell, Combat Shotgun, Frag Grenade, Recon Armor Helmet, Ashur's Key.

chr_02001082.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, combat, escort, travel, guard
chr_02001082.summary: Wernher is an escaped slave and former right-hand man of Ishmael Ashur from The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wernher was born around the time of the Scourge, which he approximates as occurring around thirty years prior to 2277, though it really could have only occurred after the Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel departed New California in 2254.

As Ashur's former second-in-command of the Pitt raiders, Wernher is one of the more intelligent of the city's denizens. He fell from grace after trying to oust Ashur. He was stripped of his rank and enslaved, working alongside the Pitt slaves he once ruled over. Unwilling to accept his fate, Wernher began organizing a slave revolt against Ashur, in collaboration with Midea, the de facto leader of the slaves. Wernher doesn't care about the folk laboring in the Pitt, seeing them primarily as a means to an end.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: If the Free Labor quest is completed by siding with the slaves, Wernher generally wanders Downtown and can be seen making conversation with the locals. However, he can also wander outside the city limits and seems to get stuck around the Bridge and train yard.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Into The Pitt: By the time the Lone Wanderer meets Wernher at a radio tower in the Capital Wasteland, he is engaged in combat with a trio of Pitt raiders who managed to track him down after his escape. They can either assist him in dispatching the group or watch as he takes care of them himself, which will change his initial reaction towards them, as he either thanks them for their assistance or becomes slightly frustrated that they neglected to help.
• Depending on the Lone Wanderer's choice of words during their first interaction, Wernher will refer to them as either "Hero," "Moneybags," or "Joker" for the duration of their time together, as they either say that they came to help, that they came for the promised reward, or joke about his difficulties in dealing with the raiders, the latter of which he is annoyed by.

chr_02000801.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

chr_0300d439.summary: Enclave Hellfire troopers are elite Enclave soldiers encountered in the Capital Wasteland and Adams Air Force Base around the year 2277.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Enclave Hellfire troopers are easily identifiable by their unique namesake power armor and signature flamethrower weapons. Often encountered starting at mid to high levels, Hellfire troopers are often paired with 2-3 standard Enclave troopers and occasionally an Enclave officer, whether on patrol, stationed at an Enclave outpost, or inserted into the field via randomized Vertibird drop-off points. They are tough, highly persistent combatants who will not let up for a second in a fight, relentlessly firing their weapon at anyone unlucky enough to come into contact.

chr_0300d437.summary: Enclave Hellfire troopers are elite Enclave soldiers encountered in the Capital Wasteland and Adams Air Force Base around the year 2277.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Enclave Hellfire troopers are easily identifiable by their unique namesake power armor and signature flamethrower weapons. Often encountered starting at mid to high levels, Hellfire troopers are often paired with 2-3 standard Enclave troopers and occasionally an Enclave officer, whether on patrol, stationed at an Enclave outpost, or inserted into the field via randomized Vertibird drop-off points. They are tough, highly persistent combatants who will not let up for a second in a fight, relentlessly firing their weapon at anyone unlucky enough to come into contact.

chr_0300cf36.role: Brotherhood of Steel, Brotherhood of Steel (Scribes) — Caucasian
chr_0300cf36.summary: Brotherhood of Steel Scribe is a caucasian character in Broken Steel (Level 7, 60 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel, Brotherhood of Steel (Scribes). Found primarily around Rockland Car Tunnel.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
There are three major scribe orders; each order is headed by a high scribe (proctor), designated by the head scribe.

• is responsible for weapons research and development. Guns, ammunition anything of an offensive nature. Once the Enclave exposes themselves to the Capital Wasteland by capturing Project Purity, the scribes come to realize just how technologically advanced the Enclave is compared to the Brotherhood as a whole. They are both excited at the prospect of analyzing new technology, particularly the Vertibirds, and frustrated at their lack of technological development. If interrupted, they will direct the Lone Wanderer to Scribe Jameson, or Elder Lyons when their situation develops. When the Brotherhood is ready to take the fight to the Enclave, they will express patriotic fervor for their victory.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Take it Back!: These scribes will be enthusiastic about the upcoming fighting for Project Purity.
• The American Dream: These scribes will direct the Lone Wanderer to Elder Lyons in the main laboratory.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Rockland Car Tunnel. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000854cf.

chr_0300bd81.summary: Dunbar is a deceased ghoul settler who joined Sanders' expedition to settle in Old Olney in 2277, during which most of the settlers were killed by deathclaws nesting in the underground tunnels.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Dunbar was known to be a joker, often amused by the problems faced by the "smoothskins," such as having to deal with living in areas polluted by radiation. A former resident of Underworld in the Museum of History, he personally found it ironic that their natural immunity meant ghouls were unbothered by radiation, yet their largest settlement in the Capital Wasteland had them holed up inside an old building and dwelling in darkness, separated from wasteland society.

Day after day, his only joy was to sit around and hold a silent crush for Tulip, the proprietor of Underworld's general goods store Underworld Outfitters. One day sometime in 2277, Dunbar was given a written note from Sanders, a vocal proponent of ghoul independence who had once rubbed shoulders with Roy Phillips, the public face of the revolution for ghoul rights.
