chr_0300bd7f.summary: Connelly is a ghoul character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Old Olney Underground.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A friend of Sanders, Connelly disagreed with the plans to head north and resettle away from humans. He wanted to link up with Roy Phillips at Warrington station, as he believed the northern wastes to be far too dangerous. Ultimately, he followed Sanders and the other ghouls, who together reached Old Olney, an empty ruin of a town. The ghouls settled in an underground camp, with Connelly erecting makeshift barricades to keep the local wildlife at bay.

These were designed to keep mole rats out and did not protect the camp from a deathclaw attack that occurred just as the Lone Wanderer approached. They likely wouldn't have helped regardless, as the attack came when the ghouls knocked down a wall to expand their living space, tunneling straight into a deathclaw nest.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Connelly dies in a scripted deathclaw attack, alongside Sanders and other ghouls, which triggers during Shock Value, when the player steps on the ramp leading to the ruined hospital.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Old Olney Underground. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0300bd7e.summary: Sanders is a ghoul character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Old Olney Underground.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A former follower of Roy Phillips, Sanders parted ways with the ambitious ghoul, believing his plans to settle into Tenpenny Tower were misplaced delusions of grandeur. Instead, he gathered a group of ghouls willing to try and establish a new settlement away from the bigotry of the wasteland, and headed north. Connelly accompanied Sanders, despite his sincere wish to join forces with Phillips and his revolution, rather than roam the northern wastes. The deathclaws attacked immediately, tearing the ghouls limb from limb, just as the Lone Wanderer approached their camp while searching for tech necessary to gain an advantage over the Enclave.

Only Kidd and Wint survived the attack, and only because they managed to outrun their fellow ghouls.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

Sanders is killed in a scripted deathclaw attack when the player approaches the slope leading into the demolished hospital during Shock Value.

chr_0300bd7d.summary: Badger is a ghoul character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 25 HP). Found primarily around Old Olney Underground.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Badger was once a member of Underworld, but after coming to a series of disagreements with the settlement’s leaders, he decided to split off and lead a group comprised of Sanders and several others to find a new home. They eventually settled the Old Olney underground, where Badger was responsible for foraging food and supplies. While playing a game of pool in his new home, Badger was surprised and killed by a group of Deathclaws that were also living in the underground.

chr_0300bcaa.summary: Megaton settlers are the unnamed wastelanders who have settled, but do not officially reside, in the city of Megaton, in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Megaton's unusual immigration laws seem to have created a condition where a substantial portion of the population of the town is in this situation. Essentially, new visitors to the town seem to be approved individually by the sheriff/mayor, Lucas Simms. Meeting this approval allows one to remain inside the town's protective walls, but does not constitute citizenship. Non-citizens of the town are not permitted to own housing, and instead must either rent lodging at Moriarty's Saloon, or for the less transient settlers, space in the common house is shared communally.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the player character's Karma is at the "very good" level, once per day while in town, a Megaton settler will come and give them some gift, such as bottle caps (sometimes even only 1 cap), food, a stimpak, or ammunition. The settler can usually be found around the entrance of Megaton and can vary in clothing, as well as change equipment throughout the game.
• If the player character decides to destroy Megaton with the bomb located in the town's center, any surviving settlers (known as Megaton refugees) that the player character encounters will immediately become hostile towards them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Megaton Clinic. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0300bb32.summary: Water caravan drivers are caravaneers for the Water Distribution Network at Rivet City.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: These weary drivers are a few of the wasteland scavengers who have signed up to lead water supply caravans for the Water Distribution Network. They have taken a break from their long trips across the wasteland, enjoying the free alcohol provided by Rivet City under the canopy at their water delivery station on the network. The alcohol is a way to incentivize them to return after their trips, as the attrition of the caravans and inexperience of their guards is hard not to notice.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quest:
Protecting the Water Way: The Lone Wanderer is tasked with speaking to Officers Davis and Lorin, who are accompanying a water caravan driver and his brahmin at Francis Scott Key Bridge. Upon reaching the site, the driver and the brahmin will immediately die. The driver's appearance is randomly chosen from standard wastelanders.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia). Notable equipment & inventory: Roving Trader Outfit. Provides services: Weapons, Armor, Alcohol, Books & Schematics.

chr_0300b823.summary: Brother Gerard is the first officer and gatekeeper for the Holy Light Monastery in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: When Mother Curie III had her encounter with the four water caravan guards from Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel, her religious "epiphany" led her to establish the Apostles of the Holy Light, an evangelical offshoot of the Church of the Children of Atom. Both she and Brother Gerard left Confessor Cromwell's flock in Megaton, seeing the belief in the "Great Division" as misguided, and the namesake C-23 Megaton nuclear weapon in Megaton as merely a "great symbol" of Atom instead. In less than two weeks after the activation of Project Purity, the two constructed a monastery for their new order in the ruins of a Springvale home, adding exterior walls in front and installing a tabernacle. From the podium, radiation devices were installed, activated on the pulpit, between which a bathtub rests.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Holy Water: Brother Gerard holds the monastery key, which opens a trapdoor leading into the Holy Light Monastery, and must be dealt with via diplomacy or force in order to enter.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Megaton is blown up after the events of Take it Back!, Gerard will appear in front of the Megaton ruins with Mother Curie III, both of whom will have been transformed into ghouls by the massive radiation spike. While Curie will now be a hostile feral ghoul reaver, Gerard will be a normal, non-hostile ghoul and will remain near the ruins to pray to Atom.
• If the Lone Wanderer has sabotaged Project Purity with President Eden's modified FEV, there will be a couple of new dialogue options available when speaking with Brother Gerard.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0300b39f.summary: Kidd is a ghoul character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Old Olney Underground. Directly connected to quests: Shock Value.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: One of Sanders' ghouls who tried to establish a new Underworld beneath Old Olney, Kidd and his partner, Wint, are the only survivors after a knocked-down wall unleashed a nest of deathclaws on the nascent community. They managed to survive by running faster than anyone else, and their primary concern is getting out of Old Olney as fast as possible. Kidd is shaken by the experience and focused on survival, and lets Wint deal with anyone wanting to talk to them while they're trying to get away.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Shock Value: Kidd and Wint are encountered upon entering the underground to find the Tesla coil. The two ghouls are fleeing the deathclaws attack. Kidd will not talk to the player, telling them to speak to Wint instead.

sections.text: Known locations: Old Olney Underground. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Wanderer Outfit, itm_0009b189.

chr_0300b39e.summary: Wint is a ghoul character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Old Olney Underground. Directly connected to quests: Shock Value.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Part of Sanders' group of ghoul settlers, trying to set up a place like the Underworld (only better), Wint and his partner, Kidd, are the only survivors. What seemed like a good idea at the time turned out to be a complete disaster when the ghouls found out just why Old Olney was abandoned: Deathclaws came at them full bore when they knocked down walls in the underground to expand their living area. Sanders had them settle right next to a deathclaw nest, and virtually all of Wint's friends paid the price. If he could, Wint would kill Sanders himself for the disaster, but the deathclaws got to the man first. He doesn't dwell on it, as he wants to get as far from Old Olney as possible, as he doesn't enjoy the prospect of becoming lunchmeat.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quest:
Shock Value: Upon entering the Old Olney underground to find a Tesla coil, Wint and Kidd can be encountered fleeing the fledgling ghoul community. Wint can provide some information on what happened, after which he and Kidd will leave using the ladder and disappear permanently.

sections.text: Known locations: Old Olney Underground. Notable equipment & inventory: Brahmin-Skin Outfit, itm_00078648.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2251, at Lost Hills in New California, the three year old Sarah lost her mother in infancy, and accompanied her father on the transcontinental expedition to Washington, D.C. in 2254, under the elders' council mandate to recover technology from eastern cities and bases.

Over the next twenty-two years, Sarah accumulated training, experience, and leadership skills. As she rose to become one of the finest fighters at the D.C. Bunker, her father (promoted to elder from star paladin, for the discovery of Liberty Prime) gradually switched the chapter's mission from recovery to super mutant containment. He lied to the elder council about following the original mission, and eventually disobeyed direct orders, leading to Lost Hills breaking ties with him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Companion:
Lyons is available as a temporary companion at Chevy Chase during Following in His Footsteps and while attacking the Memorial during Take it Back!. Her stats are normally on par with a normal Brotherhood of Steel paladin. However, while fighting the Enclave on the way to the memorial, her health is increased to 505, giving her extremely high durability on par with Star Paladin Cross. The increase is largely a convenience, as Lyons is marked as essential unless the player chooses to destroy the Citadel.

Furthermore, Sarah Lyons is coded as a non-player character companion, and therefore uses up ammunition for her weapons, unlike most non-player characters. She has more than 100 microfusion cells in her inventory, giving her a substantial amount of ammunition before she switches to her melee weapon.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Vertibird Interior. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_030091d5.summary: The following outlines the Brotherhood of Steel ranks seen throughout the Fallout series. For a comprehensive list of characters listed by game, see the characters article. For a general overview of the hierarchy, see this article.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Each rank in the Brotherhood of Steel is part of a hierarchy that follows the Chain That Binds. The ranks were devised by Roger Maxson as a way to help transition the former members of the United States Armed Forces into the Brotherhood. While all known Brotherhood of Steel chapters use these same core ranks, the specifics of each rank have differed over time and between chapters.

sections.title: Elders
sections.text:
High elder:
The high elder is the supreme leader of the entire Brotherhood of Steel and as such oversees the other elders. High elders may also honorarily be addressed as "generals".

Known high elders:
• Roger Maxson (2077 - 2135)
• Maxson II (2135 - 2155)
• John Maxson (2159 -?)
• VB Jeremy Maxson (ca. 2231 -?)

Elder:
The elders form the Brotherhood's ruling council. Individual elders are occasionally leaders of localized chapters of the Brotherhood. Under normal circumstances, the ability to become an elder is reserved for paladins, although there are exceptions, such as Elder Elijah, who was a scribe.

Elder cleric:
The highest ranked cleric, effectively an elder in their own right. This role is seemingly unique to the Knights of San Fernando, as it is the only currently known chapter where clerics act as the leadership caste.

sections.title: Paladins
sections.text:
Head paladin:
The commander of the paladins, responsible for overseeing their operations and training them. The head paladin may induct other members of the Brotherhood into the paladins at their discretion, depending on their aptitude.

• John Maxson was the head paladin of Lost Hills before he accepted the post of high elder in 2155. He was replaced by Rhombus.
• Nolan McNamara was the head paladin of the Mojave chapter until 2276. After the disastrous Operation: Sunburst, he became elder, with Edgar Hardin appointed head paladin.

Senior paladin:
Senior paladins are paladins that show promise to become head paladins. They are well respected among other paladins and knights and can greatly increase the morale of soldiers.

• Senior Paladin Talus, Lost Hills, 2161.
• Senior Paladin Hardin, during Elder Elijah's rule.

chr_0300836d.summary: Rivet City Security is a asian character in Broken Steel (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia). Notable equipment & inventory: Water Crate Key, Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform, Hangar Key.

chr_03007e35.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_03006f61.summary: The ghoul guards are ghouls hired by Griffon to guard the Museum Authority Building in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
These three ghouls are hired muscle for Griffon, a ghoul conman carrying out a scheme to resell the Brotherhood of Steel's Aqua Pura to raiders, slavers, the Brotherhood Outcasts, and other groups who are barred from receiving the Brotherhood's charity, as well as repackaging irradiated water in Aqua Pura bottles as miracle "Aqua Cura" and selling it to the ghoul residents of Underworld.

The guards were previously residents of Underworld who bought into Griffon's sales pitch but were later told the truth by Griffon: that Aqua Cura is just dirty water. Griffon subsequently swore them to secrecy by paying for their silence and continued service, bringing them into his scheme.

sections.title: Background & Story Role

chr_03006f60.summary: The ghoul guards are ghouls hired by Griffon to guard the Museum Authority Building in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
These three ghouls are hired muscle for Griffon, a ghoul conman carrying out a scheme to resell the Brotherhood of Steel's Aqua Pura to raiders, slavers, the Brotherhood Outcasts, and other groups who are barred from receiving the Brotherhood's charity, as well as repackaging irradiated water in Aqua Pura bottles as miracle "Aqua Cura" and selling it to the ghoul residents of Underworld.

The guards were previously residents of Underworld who bought into Griffon's sales pitch but were later told the truth by Griffon: that Aqua Cura is just dirty water. Griffon subsequently swore them to secrecy by paying for their silence and continued service, bringing them into his scheme.

chr_0300695a.summary: These bandits are members of Split Jack's gang. They are found at Wilhelm's Wharf roughly two weeks after the activation of Project Purity in 2277/2278.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Led by Split Jack, these bandits are plaguing the Water Distribution Network's water caravans. Their loyalty to Split Jack is tenuous at best, should he be deposed by the rules set down by himself they will not follow his replacement. Both blood thirsty and pragmatic, should the Lone Wanderer decide to challenge Split Jack for leadership of the gang, the remaining bandits won't follow their leadership. Instead they will agree to cut the Lone Wanderer in on the existing extortion plan should the Lone Wanderer do all the leg work and convince Officer Lepelletier that it's in their best interest to cooperate. If the Lone Wanderer doesn't visit them at least once a month they will think that the Lone Wanderer died and divvy up the loot among themselves.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Three of these characters will be attacking the bait caravan. While those are hostile, the others are initially friendly.
• Should the Lone Wanderer replace Split Jack by beating him in a duel, the bandits ask them to extort the "protection money" from Officer Lepelletier in his stead. When fighting Split Jack, the bandits will become hostile if the Lone Wanderer uses anything but the designated weapon.
• If the player assumes control of the gang, there are quest alternates for more cash: Speech, Karma, Strength, and Luck. The Karma option has two outcomes, one for Good Karma and one for Neutral and/or Evil Karma.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Notable equipment & inventory: itm_03003b37.

chr_030068c3.summary: The Enclave Sigma Leader is an Enclave military officer and Hellfire trooper serving at the mobile base crawler in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: He is the leader of Enclave Squad Sigma, a special Enclave unit assigned to protect Adams Air Force Base, and is encountered inside the crawler. He is the only Hellfire unit in the Sigma squad. The squad itself consists of 5-6 soldiers.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• The Lone Wanderer encounters the leader and his squad when inside the mobile base crawler.
• He can be mezzed and enslaved. Removing the slave collar after putting it on him will make him friendly towards the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Launch Platform Base. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_030068bf.summary: Stiggs is a repairman specializing in robotics, located at Adams Air Force Base in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A wastelander by birth, the Enclave found Stiggs in malnourished condition and brought him back to health from a severe bout of radiation poisoning. He was then put to work maintaining and creating the latest in flamethrower technologies for the Enclave, but he is troubled by these accomplishments.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Who Dares Wins: Stiggs approaches the Lone Wanderer on the lower level of the mobile platform and asks them if they are going to hurt him. If he is allowed to live, he can provide some information about the crawler. With the Robotics Expert perk, the Lone Wanderer can speculate what system the mainframe uses. Stiggs will compliment them as finally being someone who understands what he is talking about, and says they would be able to reprogram the robotic and turret systems inside the base so that they will target the Enclave.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Stiggs is left alive, he will escape the crawler and travel to the Adams storage facility with his sentry bot, Sparky, and his Mister Gutsy, Hoover. After the completion of Who Dares Wins, they will all disappear from the game.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Mobile Base Crawler. Notable equipment & inventory: RobCo Jumpsuit, Wrench, Eyeglasses, Pip-Boy Glove, itm_00078648.

chr_03006722.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_030064fe.role: Apostles of the Eternal Light — African American
chr_030064fe.summary: Rosa Meitner is a wandering wastelander who is found in the vicinity of Megaton about two weeks after the activation of Project Purity in 2277/2278.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rosa is a kindhearted traveler headed for Megaton. While passing through Springvale, she was gifted "holy water," and a pamphlet by Brother Gerard, and accepted them gratefully. When she arrived at Megaton, she approached Micky, the local water beggar, and offered him the holy water. However, unbeknownst to her, the water had been "blessed" by the Apostles of the Eternal Light with high levels of radiation, and the sickly beggar died after drinking it.

Witnessing the event was the Lone Wanderer, who had arrived at Megaton around the same time as her. Confused and grief-stricken, she begs the Lone Wanderer for aid, giving them the pamphlet and informing them of her encounter at the Holy Light Monastery. Afterwards, she wanders away from Megaton, inconsolable.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quest:
• Holy Water: Rosa and Micky's little incident is one of the ways to progress the quest. She will give the Lone Wanderer a holy water pamphlet, which will update the quest marker to point to the Holy Light Monastery on the Pip-Boy map.

Effects of player's actions:
• After speaking with the player character and begging them to stop the Holy Light cult, a deeply distraught Rosa will run off into the wasteland. She does follow a specific path, which leads to Rivet City's broken bow. If she manages to reach her destination, she will disappear.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Holy Water Pamphlet, Holy Water, Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_030057be.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox
chr_030057be.summary: Enclave Squad Sigma is an elite military unit of the Enclave's Department of the Army, stationed on board the mobile base crawler at Adams Air Force Base in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: As part of their military buildup aiming to conquer the Capital Wasteland, the Enclave under John Henry Eden instituted multi-faceted combat training for their soldiers, with the designation of "Sigma Squad" going to only the most hardened and experienced combat veterans. With multiple squads active at any time, each composed of a six-man team typically equipped with advanced power armor and under the command of a leader distinguished by their usage of specialized Hellfire power armor, Sigma is the Enclave's elite fighting force. Their prestige carries with it the responsibility of being dispatched to eliminate the most dangerous threats and defend the most high-value locations deemed "imperative" to the cause by Enclave high command.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: The squad members are initially stationed in their sleeping quarters above the entrance to the Enclave mobile platform but will proceed downstairs once the alarm is triggered to seek and destroy the Lone Wanderer. If one manages to hide from the soldiers, the squad will retire back to their quarters upstairs, except the leader, who wanders idly around the mobile base crawler area.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Who Dares Wins: Should the Lone Wanderer be spotted inside the Enclave mobile crawler, Enclave Squad Sigma will show up and attempt to neutralize them.

Effects of player's actions:
• If one triggers the alarm inside the mobile base crawler normally, Enclave Squad Sigma will spawn as normal Enclave soldiers (one Rank 1, three Rank 2s, one Tesla Soldier, and the Hellfire Trooper leader) despite supposedly being the Enclave's elite special forces.
• However, if the Launch Base Platform cell is entered without triggering the alarm (such as using the rear entrance near Stiggs), Enclave Squad Sigma will instead spawn in scaled appropriately to the player character's level.

chr_03005732.behavior: Aggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_03005732.summary: Paladins are a rank of the Brotherhood of Steel, reserved for the organization's elite members who have proven themselves as seasoned warriors and battlefield commanders.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Paladins are the protectors of the Brotherhood, considered to be their elite fighting force. Achieving the rank of paladin typically means the bearer is a highly trained combat veteran with extensive battlefield experience, marking them as a capable leader that completes the missions given to them and their subordinates dutifully. Due to the great responsibility that comes with their rank, paladins are often afforded the best equipment at the Brotherhood's disposal, such as power armor and advanced weaponry. They are trusted with maintaining the security of the Brotherhood's operations in their territory, being the first line of defense against enemies both inside and outside the organization.

sections.title: Ranks
sections.text:
Head paladin:
The head paladin is the overall commander of the paladins, responsible for implementing the elder's combat plans, enforcing Brotherhood laws and discipline on top of overseeing the overall training regime. They are a veteran soldier and are required to periodically convene with other caste heads and the elders.

Notable members:
• John Maxson, Lost Hills (promoted to elder by 2161)
• Head Paladin Rhombus, Lost Hills, 2161
• Head Paladin Lindquist (succeeded Kenneth Jones as elder)
• Head Paladin Edgar Hardin, Mojave, 2281

Star paladin:
Star paladins are only answerable to their elder and are given a wide authority to do what they see fit to accomplish their objectives.

The Midwest chapter renamed the position to paladin lord, but kept it identical in practice (being one step below the general/elder).

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Satellite Facility. Notable equipment & inventory: Brotherhood Power Armor.

chr_03005686.summary: Paladin Tristan is a caucasian character in Broken Steel (Level 10, 125 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel, Citadel Residents. Found primarily around Citadel - A Ring. Directly connected to quests: Death From Above, DC Ruins Exploration, Who Dares Wins.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Tristan was involved with the original expedition that found the Pentagon ruins with Elder Lyons. He has trained Sarah Lyons since she was young and he has a professional relationship with her. Tristan is loyal to Lyons and follows his direction and ideals of the Brotherhood's future closely. Tristan is wise and has a serious nature.

Tristan has climbed through the ranks of the Brotherhood of Steel and attained the status of a paladin. He acts as an operation specialist, planning many of the offensives in defeating the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland. Tristan is responsible for the daily operations of the Citadel and he helps assist Paladin Gunny with training new members. He is often found wandering the Citadel's main control room area, which is the old bay for Liberty Prime.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Death From Above: Tristan is coordinating an assault on the Enclave Satellite relay station to scrounge for intel on the Enclave's next move.
• Shock Value: Tristan sends the Lone Wanderer on a search for an odd component so the scribes can develop a special weapon.
• Who Dares Wins: Tristan orders one to access Adams Air Force Base via the Presidential metro. After infiltrating it, he gives them further orders on their assignment.
• Blood Brotherhood: Following the destruction of Adams Air Force Base, Tristan asks the player character to collect super mutant blood samples, so the scribes can research and develop a weapon that can destroy the super mutant population once and for all.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Citadel - A Ring. Notable equipment & inventory: Plasma Rifle.

chr_03005685.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox
chr_03005685.summary: Scribe Vallincourt is a scribe of the Brotherhood of Steel and one of Head Scribe Rothchild's assistants.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A member of the Order of the Shield, Vallincourt is as beautiful as she is intelligent. She assists Head Scribe Rothchild in weapons research and assorted gadgetry, as part of the Brotherhood's mission of preserving technology. In fact, she is what the Brotherhood considers a hardliner, a fervent believer in its original way. While she did not join the Brotherhood Outcasts when the schism happened, she remained skeptical about Elder Lyons' new direction.

Broken Steel:
After the activation of Project Purity and the breaking of the Enclave at the Jefferson Memorial, her attitude softens.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Related quests:
• Shock Value: If spoken to, Vallincourt will provide the deathclaw control scrambler and the location of an Enclave camp to test it at.

Other interactions:
• Talking to her before finishing Death From Above is impossible, as she will simply state that she is too busy to talk.
• Following Who Dares Wins, she points the player in the direction of Rothchild's scrap-gathering quest and explains the long-term plans for reverse-engineering Enclave technology.

sections.text: Known locations: Citadel - Laboratory. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000854cf.

chr_03004c77.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, sandbox
chr_03004c77.role: Apostles of the Eternal Light — Caucasian Elderly
chr_03004c77.summary: Mother Curie III, or Curie the Third, is a member of the Church of the Children of Atom and the founder and leader of the Apostles of the Eternal Light.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mother Curie is from Megaton.

Apostles of the Eternal Light:
In her vision, Atom called upon his flock to seek not Division, but instead "Enlightenment;" she believes that salvation in Eternal Light can only be attained through Atom's supreme and total Enlightenment—in other words, salvation is only possible by taking in radiation and becoming a ghoul, though few are able to surpass the level of Enlightenment and reach Eternal Light (taking in so much radiation that they achieve a visible glow). They see this transformation as a "rebirth" for the suffering so that they no longer fall to starvation, illness, or age, needing only "Atom's Glow" (radiation) to be happy.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Holy Water: The Lone Wanderer has the choice of persuading Curie to stop distributing the holy water to others, or stopping her by killing her and her followers.

Effects of player's actions:
• Mother Curie III appears as a hostile feral ghoul reaver if Megaton is blown up after starting Holy Water. According to Brother Gerard, who will also be transformed into a ghoul, this occurs because he and Mother Curie are preaching in Megaton when the bomb goes off.
• Although armed with a weapon, Mother Curie III is a peaceful character and does not become hostile if one kills Brother Gerard in order to enter the monastery, or by way of antagonizing speech options. If threatened, she states that she expected some form of religious persecution and that she refuses to respond to violence with violence.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Eternal Light Monastery. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_03004c76.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox
chr_03004c76.role: Apostles of the Eternal Light — Hispanic Elderly
chr_03004c76.summary: Brother Gerard is the first officer and gatekeeper for the Holy Light Monastery in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: When Mother Curie III had her encounter with the four water caravan guards from Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel, her religious "epiphany" led her to establish the Apostles of the Holy Light, an evangelical offshoot of the Church of the Children of Atom. Both she and Brother Gerard left Confessor Cromwell's flock in Megaton, seeing the belief in the "Great Division" as misguided, and the namesake C-23 Megaton nuclear weapon in Megaton as merely a "great symbol" of Atom instead. In less than two weeks after the activation of Project Purity, the two constructed a monastery for their new order in the ruins of a Springvale home, adding exterior walls in front and installing a tabernacle. From the podium, radiation devices were installed, activated on the pulpit, between which a bathtub rests.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Holy Water: Brother Gerard holds the monastery key, which opens a trapdoor leading into the Holy Light Monastery, and must be dealt with via diplomacy or force in order to enter.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Megaton is blown up after the events of Take it Back!, Gerard will appear in front of the Megaton ruins with Mother Curie III, both of whom will have been transformed into ghouls by the massive radiation spike. While Curie will now be a hostile feral ghoul reaver, Gerard will be a normal, non-hostile ghoul and will remain near the ruins to pray to Atom.
• If the Lone Wanderer has sabotaged Project Purity with President Eden's modified FEV, there will be a couple of new dialogue options available when speaking with Brother Gerard.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Wanderer Outfit, Monastery Key, Holy Water, Power Fist, Frag Grenade, Stimpak.

chr_03004c1a.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, follow, patrol, sandbox
chr_03004c1a.summary: Brotherhood Outcasts are members of the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel splinter faction collectively known as the Brotherhood Outcasts. They operate in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Brotherhood Outcasts are equal to their Capital Wasteland Brotherhood of Steel counterparts in terms of equipment and combat skill, making them some of the deadliest combatants in the Capital Wasteland, second only to the soldiers of the Enclave. Their armor is in marginally worse condition than that of their Brotherhood counterparts, but not to an extent that makes any practical difference.

Brotherhood Outcasts come in 3 different unofficial skill ranks, each equivalent to the initiate, knight, and paladin ranks of the main Brotherhood of Steel. They are neutral to the player character and other non-hostile wastelanders, albeit very rude and condescending. They will engage in combat against hostile wasteland creatures, raiders, and Enclave soldiers.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Outcasts can be found at their main base of operations, Fort Independence, which is manned by the main contingent of Brotherhood outcast soldiers. There is an Outcast detachment occupying an outpost in Bailey's Crossroads. Also, a moderate Outcast presence can be found in the vicinity of Fort Constantine and the SatCom Array NN-03d. Three Outcasts will always be found outside Fort Constantine patrolling a rising path just off the road leading to the facility (in addition to any Outcasts that may spawn periodically near the main gate). Two pairs of Outcast soldiers are always found near the SatCom Array; one pair patrols to its southwest near the remains of a metal shack, while another pair patrols northwest of the first, between the array and the fort.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_03003b64.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue
chr_03003b64.summary: Griffon is a ghoul conman hawking his "miracle" creation Aqua Cura to the residents of Underworld in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: An entrepreneur of dubious morals, after the Lone Wanderer reactivated Project Purity with the help of the Brotherhood of Steel in 2277, Griffon cooked up a scheme revolving around purchasing the bottled Aqua Pura and stashing it away to sell it later to those the Brotherhood refuses to barter with, such as raiders, slavers, the Brotherhood Outcasts, and others. Griffon's plan came about by circumstance: after hearing about the Brotherhood distributing Aqua Pura for free, Griffon tried to receive some from them, only to be turned away for being a ghoul. With no other option, Griffon offered to pay for the water -- which immediately earned the approval of Scribe Bigsley.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Amazing Aqua Cura!: Speaking to Griffon is one way to start the quest; others include being told about Griffon by Scribe Bigsley, or directly intruding in Griffon's operations at the Museum Authority Building. Through certain quest options, the player character is able to blackmail Griffon, allowing them to return once a week for their share of the cut or to be paid in full for their silence immediately.

Effects of player's actions:
• Griffon can be killed by an angry mob of Underworld residents if the player character chooses certain paths during The Amazing Aqua Cura!. If he somehow manages to defeat the mob, he will exit out the museum front door and permanently disappear from the game.
• After discovering the truth behind Aqua Cura, Scribe Bigsley can be informed about Griffon's scheme.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Museum of History Entrance. Notable equipment & inventory: Dirty Pre-War Businesswear, itm_03003b66.

chr_03003b3e.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: neutral. AI packages: guard, travel
chr_03003b3e.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Weapons, Armor, Alcohol, Books & Schematics)
chr_03003b3e.summary: Water caravan drivers are caravaneers for the Water Distribution Network at Rivet City.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: These weary drivers are a few of the wasteland scavengers who have signed up to lead water supply caravans for the Water Distribution Network. They have taken a break from their long trips across the wasteland, enjoying the free alcohol provided by Rivet City under the canopy at their water delivery station on the network. The alcohol is a way to incentivize them to return after their trips, as the attrition of the caravans and inexperience of their guards is hard not to notice.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quest:
Protecting the Water Way: The Lone Wanderer is tasked with speaking to Officers Davis and Lorin, who are accompanying a water caravan driver and his brahmin at Francis Scott Key Bridge. Upon reaching the site, the driver and the brahmin will immediately die. The driver's appearance is randomly chosen from standard wastelanders.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Notable equipment & inventory: Roving Trader Outfit. Provides services: Weapons, Armor, Alcohol, Books & Schematics.

chr_03003b3d.behavior: Very Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: guard, travel
chr_03003b3d.summary: These bandits are members of Split Jack's gang. They are found at Wilhelm's Wharf roughly two weeks after the activation of Project Purity in 2277/2278.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Led by Split Jack, these bandits are plaguing the Water Distribution Network's water caravans. Their loyalty to Split Jack is tenuous at best, should he be deposed by the rules set down by himself they will not follow his replacement. Both blood thirsty and pragmatic, should the Lone Wanderer decide to challenge Split Jack for leadership of the gang, the remaining bandits won't follow their leadership. Instead they will agree to cut the Lone Wanderer in on the existing extortion plan should the Lone Wanderer do all the leg work and convince Officer Lepelletier that it's in their best interest to cooperate. If the Lone Wanderer doesn't visit them at least once a month they will think that the Lone Wanderer died and divvy up the loot among themselves.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Three of these characters will be attacking the bait caravan. While those are hostile, the others are initially friendly.
• Should the Lone Wanderer replace Split Jack by beating him in a duel, the bandits ask them to extort the "protection money" from Officer Lepelletier in his stead. When fighting Split Jack, the bandits will become hostile if the Lone Wanderer uses anything but the designated weapon.
• If the player assumes control of the gang, there are quest alternates for more cash: Speech, Karma, Strength, and Luck. The Karma option has two outcomes, one for Good Karma and one for Neutral and/or Evil Karma.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Notable equipment & inventory: itm_03003b37.

chr_03003b3c.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, travel
chr_03003b3c.summary: Officer Lepelletier is a caucasian character in Broken Steel (Level 20, 170 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia). Directly connected to quests: Protecting the Water Way.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Serving as a member of the Rivet City security force, Lepelletier's dedication to duty earned her the right, or rather the misfortune, to be placed in charge of Rivet City's side of the Water Distribution Network following the Brotherhood's liberation of Project Purity. In exchange for money and technology, Rivet City and Lepelletier are cooperating with the Brotherhood to deliver water to the Capital Wasteland via armed caravans. Working out of a makeshift office just outside of Rivet City, Lepelletier deals with the caravan drivers, guards, and brahmin as they all work to deliver the water to the wasteland. However, almost as soon as the caravans started delivering water, they started getting ambushed. Lepelletier suspects something organized is going on.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Scribe Bigsley directs the Lone Wanderer to Lepelletier because the caravans have been plagued by an especially nasty band of bandits. One can also pass a Speech check to convince her to give them her plasma rifle.

Effects of player's actions:
• Lepelletier will turn hostile and attack the player character if they speak with her after joining the gang and extorting her for protection money. However, she will become neutral again after 24 in-game hours. Fighting Lepelletier will temporarily cause the rest of the Rivet City security force to turn hostile towards the player character as well.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia). Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Uniform.

chr_03003b3b.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, guard
chr_03003b3b.summary: Officer Davis is a african american character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Directly connected to quests: Protecting the Water Way.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Rivet City has contracted with the Brotherhood of Steel to help escort water caravans to their destination, in exchange for getting money and technology from the Brotherhood. Officer Davis is one of the security team hoping to be paid with technology.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Officers Davis and Lorin are in charge of protecting one of Project Purity's water caravans which will serve as bait for the bandits who plague the caravans.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Davis survives the bandit ambush, he will travel back to Rivet City to report to Officer Lepelletier. After Davis speaks with Lepelletier, he will disappear as soon as the player leaves the active map cell. Davis has no dialogue tree, and will simply thank the player for saving him if spoken to.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment

chr_03003b3a.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox
chr_03003b3a.summary: Split Jack is the leader of a mercenary gang in the Capital Wasteland, roughly two weeks after the activation of Project Purity in 2277/2278.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Once an average wasteland raider, Split Jack cleaned up his act and began combining his ruthless tendencies with a head for business. Now in charge of a group of bandits, he has devised a plan for theft and extortion involving the Water Distribution Network. His scheme involves attacking water caravans to steal Aqua Pura, then offering "protection services" to the network once Rivet City has had enough.

Split Jack is recruiting bandits to this end, He is mildly psychotic, though this is not always obvious,

He has established a simple power hierarchy among his crew, and the rules for his bandits are simple: the toughest lead. In practice, his underlings do what he says when he says to.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Split Jack is always at Wilhelm's Wharf, leading his crew.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Once Split Jack's name and location have been revealed, the Lone Wanderer can choose to kill Jack's whole band or replace him by challenging him to a death duel with pre-defined weapons. Additionally, if one has a high enough Speech, they can persuade him to stop hijacking water caravans. However, if this option is chosen, he will then order his men to kill whoever or whatever they please. This usually involves Grandma Sparkle first.

chr_03003b39.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, follow, sandbox
chr_03003b39.summary: These bandits are members of Split Jack's gang. They are found at Wilhelm's Wharf roughly two weeks after the activation of Project Purity in 2277/2278.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Led by Split Jack, these bandits are plaguing the Water Distribution Network's water caravans. Their loyalty to Split Jack is tenuous at best, should he be deposed by the rules set down by himself they will not follow his replacement. Both blood thirsty and pragmatic, should the Lone Wanderer decide to challenge Split Jack for leadership of the gang, the remaining bandits won't follow their leadership. Instead they will agree to cut the Lone Wanderer in on the existing extortion plan should the Lone Wanderer do all the leg work and convince Officer Lepelletier that it's in their best interest to cooperate. If the Lone Wanderer doesn't visit them at least once a month they will think that the Lone Wanderer died and divvy up the loot among themselves.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Three of these characters will be attacking the bait caravan. While those are hostile, the others are initially friendly.
• Should the Lone Wanderer replace Split Jack by beating him in a duel, the bandits ask them to extort the "protection money" from Officer Lepelletier in his stead. When fighting Split Jack, the bandits will become hostile if the Lone Wanderer uses anything but the designated weapon.
• If the player assumes control of the gang, there are quest alternates for more cash: Speech, Karma, Strength, and Luck. The Karma option has two outcomes, one for Good Karma and one for Neutral and/or Evil Karma.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC15a (Grayditch — Anchorage Memorial). Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_03003b38.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, guard
chr_03003b38.summary: Officer Lorin is a asian character in Broken Steel (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Directly connected to quests: Protecting the Water Way.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
There is usually a small contingent of caravan drivers, brahmin, and disgruntled Rivet City policemen buzzing around the bridge gangplank building. Officer Lorin is one of the most vocal in her displeasure at the almost-constant attacks, but her hand has been forced.

Following the success at Project Purity, Rivet City decided to help the Brotherhood of Steel distribute the clean water across the wasteland by protecting the water caravans. Lorin was sent out as part of these caravan guards.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Protecting the Water Way: Officers Lorin and Davis are in charge of protecting one of Project Purity's water caravans which will serve as bait for the bandits who plague the caravans.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Lorin survives the bandit ambush, she will travel back to Rivet City to report to Officer Lepelletier. After Lorin speaks with Lepelletier, she will disappear as soon as the player leaves the active map cell. Lorin has no dialogue tree, and will simply thank the player for saving her if spoken to.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform.

chr_03003851.summary: Brotherhood of Steel Scribe is a caucasian character in Broken Steel (Level 10, 115 HP). Found primarily around Jefferson Museum and Gift Shop.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
There are three major scribe orders; each order is headed by a high scribe (proctor), designated by the head scribe.

• is responsible for weapons research and development. Guns, ammunition anything of an offensive nature. Once the Enclave exposes themselves to the Capital Wasteland by capturing Project Purity, the scribes come to realize just how technologically advanced the Enclave is compared to the Brotherhood as a whole. They are both excited at the prospect of analyzing new technology, particularly the Vertibirds, and frustrated at their lack of technological development. If interrupted, they will direct the Lone Wanderer to Scribe Jameson, or Elder Lyons when their situation develops. When the Brotherhood is ready to take the fight to the Enclave, they will express patriotic fervor for their victory.

sections.text:

• Take it Back!: These scribes will be enthusiastic about the upcoming fighting for Project Purity.
• The American Dream: These scribes will direct the Lone Wanderer to Elder Lyons in the main laboratory.

chr_0300382d.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: angry. AI packages: travel
chr_0300382d.summary: Scribe Bigsley is a disgruntled Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel scribe stationed at the Jefferson Memorial after the Battle of Project Purity, operating as its administrator.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A competent yet combative individual, Scribe Bigsley's earliest known history is as a part of the Order of the Sword where he modified the output of several laser rifles. These proved unsafe after injuring several initiates, earning him a transfer to a different order. Now in the Order of the Shield, he was continually combative with his superiors, particularly Scribe Bowditch, whose theories of force field resonance Bigsley saw as "antiquated." He was then transferred to the Order of the Quill, where his particularly bad attitude would continue to hamper his career; his new superior Scribe Elizabeth Jameson refused to be drawn into his particular brand of arguments, and subsequently assigned him to field operations. He would later be assigned to Project Purity as the head of the water distribution network.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Holy Water: Scribe Bigsley tasks the player character with resolving the issue of Megaton's missing water shipment.
• Protecting the Water Way: Scribe Bigsley tasks the player character with resolving the issue of a organized bandit problem.
• The Amazing Aqua Cura!: Scribe Bigsley can be convinced to let the Lone Wanderer (either through Karma

Effects of the player's actions:
• Scribe Bigsley will greet the player alternately should they have sacrificed themselves, or have used their companions to active the Purifier at the end of the quest Take it Back!. This is the case even if the companions in question are arguably immune to the effects of radiation.

chr_03003730.summary: Rivet City Security is a hispanic character in Broken Steel (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security. Found primarily around Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform.

chr_030031ff.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_030031ff.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_03002e0a.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox, ambush
chr_03002e0a.summary: Paladin Jensen is a caucasian character in Broken Steel (Level 11, 130 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel. Found primarily around Fort Bannister.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A scout for Alpha Squad of the Brotherhood of Steel, Jensen is apt to make tactical blunders that put both himself and his teammates in jeopardy. He firmly denies that he's a liability. In fact, he models all his actions on his favorite superhero, Captain Cosmos.

After Broken Steel is loaded, Jensen is held prisoner inside a tent in the Talon Company camp at Fort Bannister. He was sent to scout out Fort Bannister in preparation for a Brotherhood of Steel assault against Talon Company in response to their attacks on Aqua Pura caravans but was found and captured.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• Paladin Jensen and the Brotherhood of Steel assault on Fort Bannister will not appear if the player character kills Commander Jabsco prior to completing the Take it Back! quest and beginning the Broken Steel content.
• After speaking with the Lone Wanderer, Jensen will charge out to attack the Talon Company forces defending Fort Bannister, where without the player character's assistance, he is almost certain to be mowed down by turrets and missile launcher-wielding Talon Company mercs. Soon afterward, a squad of several additional Brotherhood of Steel paladins (who can be found waiting for Jensen to the southwest of the main entrance hiding near some rocks) will appear and attack Fort Bannister.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Fort Bannister. Notable equipment & inventory: Brotherhood Power Armor.

chr_03002789.summary: Enclave Hellfire troopers are elite Enclave soldiers encountered in the Capital Wasteland and Adams Air Force Base around the year 2277.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Enclave Hellfire troopers are easily identifiable by their unique namesake power armor and signature flamethrower weapons. Often encountered starting at mid to high levels, Hellfire troopers are often paired with 2-3 standard Enclave troopers and occasionally an Enclave officer, whether on patrol, stationed at an Enclave outpost, or inserted into the field via randomized Vertibird drop-off points. They are tough, highly persistent combatants who will not let up for a second in a fight, relentlessly firing their weapon at anyone unlucky enough to come into contact.

chr_03002784.summary: Enclave Hellfire troopers are elite Enclave soldiers encountered in the Capital Wasteland and Adams Air Force Base around the year 2277.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Enclave Hellfire troopers are easily identifiable by their unique namesake power armor and signature flamethrower weapons. Often encountered starting at mid to high levels, Hellfire troopers are often paired with 2-3 standard Enclave troopers and occasionally an Enclave officer, whether on patrol, stationed at an Enclave outpost, or inserted into the field via randomized Vertibird drop-off points. They are tough, highly persistent combatants who will not let up for a second in a fight, relentlessly firing their weapon at anyone unlucky enough to come into contact.

chr_0300267d.summary: Megaton settlers are the unnamed wastelanders who have settled, but do not officially reside, in the city of Megaton, in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Megaton's unusual immigration laws seem to have created a condition where a substantial portion of the population of the town is in this situation. Essentially, new visitors to the town seem to be approved individually by the sheriff/mayor, Lucas Simms. Meeting this approval allows one to remain inside the town's protective walls, but does not constitute citizenship. Non-citizens of the town are not permitted to own housing, and instead must either rent lodging at Moriarty's Saloon, or for the less transient settlers, space in the common house is shared communally.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the player character's Karma is at the "very good" level, once per day while in town, a Megaton settler will come and give them some gift, such as bottle caps (sometimes even only 1 cap), food, a stimpak, or ammunition. The settler can usually be found around the entrance of Megaton and can vary in clothing, as well as change equipment throughout the game.
• If the player character decides to destroy Megaton with the bomb located in the town's center, any surviving settlers (known as Megaton refugees) that the player character encounters will immediately become hostile towards them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_030013ba.summary: Rivet City Security is a asian character in Broken Steel (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: DC Ruins Sector DC14d (L'Enfant Plaza — Anacostia). Notable equipment & inventory: Water Crate Key, Rivet City Security Helmet, Rivet City Security Uniform, Hangar Key.

chr_0300103d.summary: Talon Company mercs are members of the Talon Company, a mercenary company operating in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
* Only rank 1 mercs can be enslaved

Other interactions:
• Talon Company mercs are almost always hostile to the Lone Wanderer wherever they are encountered. In some areas, like Takoma Industrial and the Capitol Building, they will be found in combat with other groups such as super mutants, but will still be hostile to the player character.
• Talon Company mercs are involved in various random encounters across the Capital Wasteland, as well as in scripted encounters in certain locations, both in the base game and in Broken Steel.

Talon Company hit squads:
If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

If the player character has Good or Very Good Karma, then they may be attacked by hit squads consisting of two to three Talon Company mercs. Each merc will be carrying a note regarding the Lone Wanderer's bounty due to their good deeds.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Three Dog mentions that Talon Company mercs accept jobs that other mercenary companies would not do. Reilly of Reilly's Rangers notes her particular disgust towards the Talon Company, recalling a previous job they did which involved the killing of defenseless citizens (including women and children), commenting that they give all mercenaries a bad name. If the player character converses with her rudely, she will mention that they sound like an average Talon Company merc.

Fort Bannister acts as their main base of operations in the Capital Wasteland and is also where the Lone Wanderer will find the leader of Talon Company, Commander Jabsco.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Broken Steel add-on adds a fourth rank of Talon Company merc, with higher health and better armor, that appears at higher levels. Even at level 30, rank 4 Talon Company mercs are a relatively uncommon encounter. They are typically found in random encounters, rather than in fixed locations such as Fort Bannister. They are quite tough opponents, with good armor and very high health (more than twice that found on a rank 3) on par with that of a non-player character companion.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in 2251, at Lost Hills in New California, the three year old Sarah lost her mother in infancy, and accompanied her father on the transcontinental expedition to Washington, D.C. in 2254, under the elders' council mandate to recover technology from eastern cities and bases.

Over the next twenty-two years, Sarah accumulated training, experience, and leadership skills. As she rose to become one of the finest fighters at the D.C. Bunker, her father (promoted to elder from star paladin, for the discovery of Liberty Prime) gradually switched the chapter's mission from recovery to super mutant containment. He lied to the elder council about following the original mission, and eventually disobeyed direct orders, leading to Lost Hills breaking ties with him.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Companion:
Lyons is available as a temporary companion at Chevy Chase during Following in His Footsteps and while attacking the Memorial during Take it Back!. Her stats are normally on par with a normal Brotherhood of Steel paladin. However, while fighting the Enclave on the way to the memorial, her health is increased to 505, giving her extremely high durability on par with Star Paladin Cross. The increase is largely a convenience, as Lyons is marked as essential unless the player chooses to destroy the Citadel.

Furthermore, Sarah Lyons is coded as a non-player character companion, and therefore uses up ammunition for her weapons, unlike most non-player characters. She has more than 100 microfusion cells in her inventory, giving her a substantial amount of ammunition before she switches to her melee weapon.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Citadel - B Ring. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_04010bfc.summary: S. Marcella J., shortened to just Marcella, is a Christian missionary nomadically traveling the wasteland. In 2277, she can be found in Point Lookout trying to stop a dark plot.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Marcella was raised within the Abbey of the Road, a post-War Christian stronghold, where she was educated in the faith and eventually received her Rites of Mission. Since then, she has traveled throughout the wasteland to spread the word of the Bible and to do good. A secondary goal she follows is finding and recovering lost religious relics for later restoration and preservation. This gave her the knowledge to recognize dark relics like the Krivbeknih, which she discovered could be destroyed if it was brought to the Dunwich Building near Washington, D.C.

Early in her travels, she came to the Commonwealth, where she took shelter with a caravan during a windstorm. From the caravaneers, she heard worrying tales about the horrid state of the Pitt and wondered if she might eventually find her way there.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Dark Heart of Blackhall: After first meeting Obadiah Blackhall and getting his request to retrieve a lost heirloom, the Lone Wanderer is intercepted by Marcella, who hopes to stop them from helping fulfill a dark plot going on at Blackhall Manor.

Effects of player's actions:
After obtaining the Krivbeknih from the ritual site, if one returns to Marcella's tent at the outpost, they will find her murdered and the message "Die thief" written in blood close by, implied to be the work of smugglers encountered outside upon arrival.

Other interactions:
• Marcella can recite some passages from the Bible, specifically John 1:4-5, John 5:24, John 16:33, and 1 Corinthians 15:52.
• The Lone Wanderer can also tell Marcella about the Bible passage their mother Catherine liked, and she will recognize it and compliment them.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
• Has a 25% chance to appear

• Dependent on progressing The Dark Heart of Blackhall up to her death
