chr_0400f9f3.summary: Mister Burke is an associate of Allistair Tenpenny operating in Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Little to nothing is known about Burke's past before 2277 save for that he and Tenpenny first met sometime around when Allistair first began accepting tenants and building a security force for Tenpenny Tower. The elderly Tenpenny comments that over time, Burke did so well at catering to his needs, he hardly ever had to do anything himself.

It was originally an off-hand suggestion by Allistair, complaining about how the sight of Megaton ruined his view from his penthouse balcony (though he also suggested for the town to be vacated beforehand) that led to Burke coming to the shantytown and trying to learn more about its people and especially the bomb residing at its center. Colin Moriarty considers him a "class A weirdo" but has not presently done any further digging into the man, seeing him as just another paying customer at his bar.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Mister Burke can typically be found sitting in a chair in Moriarty's Saloon prior to starting The Power of the Atom. After one accepts the fusion pulse charge and arms the bomb in Megaton, he will return to Tenpenny Tower and wait for the Lone Wanderer to rendezvous with him on the balcony. If Megaton is successfully destroyed, he will then spend all of his time in or on the same floor as his suite. However, in any outcome where the bomb does not go off and he is not killed, Burke will simply be disabled the next time the player leaves his current location cell, disappearing from the game.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom: Talking to Mister Burke at Moriarty's Saloon will begin the destruction path of arming and detonating the Megaton bomb to destroy the town.

Effects of player's actions:
• If a female Lone Wanderer has the Black Widow perk, they unlock a unique interaction where Burke can be seduced. Afterward he will refer to the player character as his "lover" and will plan accordingly to go to Tenpenny Tower and convince Tenpenny to not blow up Megaton. Burke will actually disappear from the game altogether but will send a total of four love letters to Colin Moriarty to give to the Lone Wanderer as if he were at Tenpenny Tower, with the last one declaring they are breaking up.
• If one refuses Burke's offer or disarms the bomb without speaking to him, hitmen will show up at random encounters to attack them.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Little is known about Haley's past, even by himself. Apparently suffering from amnesia, his earliest clear memory is from around "a couple years" prior to 2277, waking up in the run-down shop he presently owns, but over time he learned not to be bothered by it. Instead, Haley saw fit to continue living in the store since most of it was already stocked; even his own name was borrowed from the pre-War signage. Once other Point Lookout locals started flocking to his shop, he settled into life as a trader, providing goods and offering services with his repair skills.

chr_0400e27b.summary: Moira Brown is the proprietor of the general store Craterside Supply in Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. She is an independent researcher studying post-nuclear survival methods for a guidebook to help others in the wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Past:
Moira is from the trading community of Canterbury Commons, where she grew up with an "uncommon curiosity about the world." and among the locals for her tinkering skills. Other residents of Megaton are generally annoyed with her eccentric behavior and "research," but cannot help but respect her effectiveness as a saleswoman.

Sometime between 2265 to 2267, a woman from Vault 101 came to Megaton and visited her shop; Moira took pity on the young woman's ignorance of wasteland life and offered to make some defensive modifications to her Vault jumpsuit. Though she eventually completed the armored jumpsuit, the client never returned for it, leading Moira to conclude she had died.

In her daily life, Moira takes every opportunity to learn as much as she can, largely by reading almost every book that comes through the town.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text:
Living most of her life in the relative safety of Megaton has left Moira oblivious as to how the wasteland functions. That said, she is a renowned optimist and always displays a chipper personality. Her drive to try to improve the lives of her fellow wastelanders inspired her to create the Wasteland Survival Guide. Though her research for the guide involves sending the Lone Wanderer into dangerous situations, Moira's naivete makes her fail to realize the full weight of her requests, which also leads to the ironic situation of keeping her new assistant away from the printing presses she uses, since she considers them to be more dangerous.

All that said, Moira is not completely detached from reality, as, in 2277, she recently hired a mercenary to serve as security for her shop.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: As the owner of Craterside Supply, she spends the day sweeping and trading as well as conducting odd experiments. She opens the store at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 8:00 p.m. Craterside Supply is also her home; Moira sleeps upstairs, and if the Lone Wanderer is caught trespassing after hours, she will become increasingly upset. The only time she will leave her shop is if Megaton is destroyed during The Power of the Atom. If Wasteland Survival Guide is completed before Megaton is destroyed, she will instead stay near the entrance to the ruins and only has the option to repair equipment, lacking an option to buy or sell items.

chr_0400e27a.summary: Elder Lyons is a caucasian elderly character in Point Lookout (Level 25, 145 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel, Citadel Residents. Encountered in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Beginnings:
Lyons was born in the early 23rd century, and was originally a star paladin stationed at the Brotherhood's Lost Hills bunker in Southern California. and the other was to reestablish contact with the "Eastern Brotherhood" and return them under Lost Hills' command (this detachment had fallen off the grid near Chicago and was believed to have gone rogue). Thus, the contingent led by Star Paladin Lyons (and including Lyons' three-year-old daughter Sarah and his friend and technological advisor Scribe Reginald Rothchild, as well as Star Paladin Cross, Paladin Henry Casdin, Initiate Ishmael Ashur, Paladin Tristan, Knight Colvin and Paladin Gunny) set out from Lost Hills and began the long journey east to the Washington, D.C. ruins.

Going east:
Contact with the "Eastern Brotherhood" evidently turned out to be unsuccessful.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text: His daughter, Sarah Lyons, is a member of the Brotherhood with the unique rank of sentinel. Reginald Rothchild is an old friend of Elder Lyons.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: As the leader of the Brotherhood of Steel, Lyons spends most of his day in the Citadel laboratory, A-ring or B-ring. He regularly converses with Scribe Rothchild, Bowditch, and Peabody on their various projects. In addition, he checks up on the progress on the Brotherhood's major project, rebuilding Liberty Prime, and supervises the armory as well as the smithy. When he is not working in the Citadel lab, he is usually eating in the A-ring's great hall, studying in his room in B-ring or sleeping.

chr_0400e23e.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox
chr_0400e23e.summary: Lucas Simms is the sheriff and de facto mayor of Megaton in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A native of Megaton, Lucas Simms grew up in the town and gained a deep understanding of what it takes to survive in the wasteland. Despite the harsh standard of living in the Capital Wastes, Lucas never surrendered his childhood cowboy fantasy, eventually acting on it to appoint himself the sheriff of Megaton in his adulthood; by 2277, few if any of the residents dispute his self-made position.

Along with his capacity as sheriff, Lucas also takes care of any public duty necessary for the people of his town - mayor, judge, etc. - and deals with most troublemakers by unceremoniously throwing them out of the town. More serious offenders, such as raiders trying to prey on the town, are shot dead on the spot, either by Simms, or by the town's militia and reprogrammed robots under his command.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Power of the Atom

Other interactions:
If Lucas, Moriarty, or both are killed, Manya Vargas, Leo Stahl, and Harden will have unique dialogue when next talked to.

chr_0400e235.summary: Amata Almodovar is a resident of Vault 101, the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar, and a major character. Along with Owyn Lyons and Sarah Lyons, she is one of only three characters in the game to have "Very Good" Karma.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The only daughter of the overseer, Amata is around the Lone Wanderer's age and the two grew up together ever since James arrived in the Vault with his child in tow. They bonded over many things, from Grognak the Barbarian to being raised by single fathers after their mothers passed away at a young age: Amata lost her mother at two, leaving her father, the overseer, to raise her on his own. The burden of leading the Vault and enforcing his isolationist policy slowly drove Amata and Alphonse apart, despite her deep love for her father and an innate sense of loyalty.

The bond between Amata and the Lone Wanderer developed into a deep friendship over the years, with the two becoming inseparable, best friends. Another was that he simply didn't like the Lone Wanderer, in part due to their father's stubborn, insubordinate personality.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Growing Up Fast: Amata organizes the Lone Wanderer's birthday party on July 13, 2268, gifting them an intact copy of the 14th issue of Grognak the Barbarian, and demonstrating some of the reactivity of the game.
• Future Imperfect: Amata takes the G.O.A.T. on August 3, 2274, together with the Lone Wanderer. Before entering the class room, she is harassed by the Tunnel Snakes, allowing the player to experiment with various approaches to resolving quests and introducing them to the Karma system.
• Escape!: Amata awakens the Lone Wanderer with news of James' escape from the vault. She offers a gun and outlines a plan for the Lone Wanderer's own escape. Toward the end of the quest, it turns out that she was captured and is interrogated by her father and Officer Mack.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Only if she was told to keep the pistol during "Escape!"

sections.text: During the Great War, a U.S. Navy jet aircraft crashed in Point Lookout, ejecting its pilot, who got stuck in a tree some distance from the crash site, and was killed by the locals after losing his rifle. After the crash, a local soldier from the Turtledove Detention Camp removed the blackbox recording but was attacked and killed by the hostile inhabitants of Point Lookout.

chr_0400a864.summary: Croatoa is a african american character in Point Lookout (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Point Lookout Tribals. Found primarily around Ark & Dove Cathedral. Directly connected to quests: Hearing Voices.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Croatoa has been a member of the tribe for some time, as he describes himself as "not so new" compared to the Lone Wanderer, who he welcomes upon their acceptance into the tribe. While other members of the tribe recently departed to attack Desmond Lockheart at the Calvert Mansion on Jackson's orders, Croatoa stayed behind, as he is more at home growing punga fruit than fighting. He has a passion for gardening, and a strong relationship with the punga, as he believes that people are able to reach a higher plane of existence through consumption of the plant's fruit.

He possesses a unique shovel that helps him to grow the punga, as it is covered in a fertilizer of some kind.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: He can be found wandering inside the outer walls of the Ark & Dove Cathedral, oftentimes tending to the punga.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
Croatoa will not become hostile like the unnamed tribals at the cathedral if the Lone Wanderer sides with Desmond during Thought Control, but will still attack if he sees them attacking any other tribals.

Other interactions:
With the Child at Heart perk or by passing a Speech check, the Lone Wanderer can get the fertilizer shovel from him.

chr_0400a862.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox
chr_0400a862.summary: Woodrose is one of the inhabitants of Point Lookout and the tribe mother of the local tribals in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A timid and thoughtful girl, Woodrose recently blossomed when she joined the local tribals. Tending to a variety of hydroponic punga plants, she cultivates new and more delicious strains, in accordance with Jackson's wishes. She is the tribe matriarch and has taken it upon herself to keep things running and make sure tribe members who have "transcended conscious thought" remember to eat and sleep, which is more work than most would think.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: She takes care of the tribals who cannot care for themselves after having part of their brain removed, helping them eat, sleep and with other essential tasks for living.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
When spoken to, Woodrose's dialogue comes off with a hostile tone toward the Lone Wanderer. This may be because they are not one of the tribals or she is simply stressed because of her tribal duties.

Like the rest of the tribe, she will become hostile if Professor Calvert is killed during A Meeting of the Minds.

chr_04009bfe.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: guard, patrol, sandbox
chr_04009bfe.summary: Jacob Humboldt is a african american elderly character in Point Lookout (Level 14, 95 HP). Found primarily around Plik's Safari. Directly connected to quests: Plik's Safari.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jacob is intrigued by the history of the United States and is an avid collector of Confederate memorabilia. He is said to be testing out his shotgun before going ghoul hunting in the swamps.

He is one of the members of Plik's hunting club and accompanies the Lone Wanderer during Plik's Safari.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Plik's Safari: Humboldt will fight along side the Lone Wanderer during the "safari."

Effects of player's actions:
• Jacob accompanies the Lone Wanderer during the Plik's Safari quest and helps fight off the feral ghouls. He may die during the safari unless he is reverse-pickpocketed with better weapons and armor, or is protected by the Lone Wanderer. If he survives the initial safari, he disappears from the game.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Plik's Safari. Notable equipment & inventory: Confederate Hat, Double-Barrel Shotgun, Shotgun Shell, Dirty Pre-War Businesswear.

chr_04009bf8.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: guard, patrol, sandbox
chr_04009bf8.summary: Rip Smithy is one of the inhabitants of Point Lookout. He is a member of Plik's hunting club, and accompanies the Lone Wanderer during Plik's Safari in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A merchant, hired-gun, and part-time smuggler, Rip Smithy recently made a boatload of caps selling a pair of child slaves named Sammy and Squirrel to Eulogy Jones over at Paradise Falls.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Plik's Safari: Unlike Jacob Humboldt, Smithy wears a practical suit of metal armor, and is equipped with a lever-action rifle for the safari. Despite these effective counter-measures, Smithy will likely meet his demise during Plik's Safari due to the large amount of feral ghouls. If he survives, he will boast and brag about how he saved the Lone Wanderer's life.

Effects of player's actions:
• If one puts on the ghoul mask before fighting in Plik's Safari, the ghouls will not attack the player character unless they are attacked. Also, Rip Smithy and Jacob Humboldt will not be attacked by the ghouls nor attack them.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Plik's Safari. Notable equipment & inventory: 10mm Round, Metal Armor, Lever-Action Rifle.

chr_04009b5a.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox
chr_04009b5a.summary: Plik is a ghoul researcher and self-proclaimed safari organizer operating from a coastal grotto in Point Lookout in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sometime prior to 2277, Plik observed the growing number of feral ghouls that were gathering in Point Lookout. He viewed them as an infestation of mindless creatures, disregarding the ethics of this given his own ghoulhood, and decided he wanted to slow their spread, if not completely stop it. His mission eventually led him to discover a grotto carved into the Maryland coastline by decades of erosion, which he then made his base of operations.

As he gathered more ferals within the underground cave system, studying them and making notes of their weaknesses in a personal journal, Plik saw an opportunity to both fulfill his goal of culling the feral population and make a tidy profit in the process.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Plik's Safari: The Lone Wanderer can pay Plik the 1,000 cap entry fee to join his safari hunting feral ghouls.

Effects of player's actions:
• Completing the quest Plik's Safari by eliminating all the feral ghouls Plik releases inside the coastal grotto has him reward the player character with the unique weapon The Dismemberer. He will also provide another ghoul hunt every 24 in-game hours and charge a reduced fee of 500 caps per hunt.
• Finding and reading Plik's personal journal in his quarters will grant the Ghoul Ecology perk (+5 damage dealt to feral ghouls).
• If killed, Plik will respawn inside the grotto after an in-game week.
• Although he can be enslaved with the Mesmetron, Plik will not have any associated voice lines during the exchange, only having the typical subtitled responses.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Coastal Grotto. Notable equipment & inventory: Merc Charmer Outfit, Bottle Cap, Spiked Knuckles.

chr_0400927d.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox
chr_0400927d.summary: Jimson is one of the inhabitants of Point Lookout and a member of the Point Lookout tribals in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Deeply superstitious and the most senior member of the tribals except for Jackson, he is responsible for spreading the message of communication to the followers not yet picking up on telepathic messages from the great leader. He is also the gatekeeper for the tribals at the Ark & Dove Cathedral and stands at the gate a majority of the time. After the Lone Wanderer has been accepted into the tribe, he will return inside the cathedral and talk to other tribals.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Walking with Spirits: Jimson instructs the Lone Wanderer to go to the sacred bog in order to gain entrance to the cathedral.

Effects of player's actions:
The Lone Wanderer will have to talk to Jimson to get into the cathedral for the Walking with Spirits quest. He will send them to the Mother Punga plant to pick seeds in order to join the tribe.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Ark & Dove Cathedral. Notable equipment & inventory: Tribal Garb.

chr_0400815a.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, dialogue, travel, patrol, combat
chr_0400815a.summary: Kenny is a hispanic child character in Point Lookout (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Miner's Rest. Directly connected to quests: Latchkey Kenny.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Fleeing the other swampfolk because he was not born with the right "look," Kenny is a lonely child looking for a friend to play with. He lives in the Herzog Mine. Kenny is exceptional at rigging traps.

Kenny was born to swampfolk and spent his early childhood hidden in his parent's basement because he "don't got the marks" which caused the other swampfolk to shoot at him like they would shoot at the others without the marks. During his time in the cellar, he learned how to make traps by taking apart and rebuilding anything he could find. He later ran away from home and took up residence in the old mine, where he is found in 2277. Kenny might have chosen the mine because rumors of it being haunted would keep locals away.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Kenny stays in his makeshift house and, on occasion, shoots junk off of a shelf with his BB gun for target practice.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
With a Speech check, using Child at Heart or by retrieving his Kenny-bear from the bottom of the mine's shaft, the Lone Wanderer can convince Kenny to let them stay with him in the mine, and use his containers. One can also play either tag or hide-and-seek with him when asked.

Other interactions:
• When asked about Old Man Herzog, Kenny will say he hung himself. When one travels deeper into the mine (Blackdamp Shaft), they can see a skeleton dangling by its neck from a rope.
• One can return Kenny-bear to Kenny, even if he has been convinced to let the Lone Wanderer stay. However, there is no reward other than his thanks.

chr_04006637.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sandbox
chr_04006637.summary: Jackson is a african american character in Point Lookout (Level 1, 75 HP). Affiliated with Point Lookout Tribals. Found primarily around Ark & Dove Cathedral. Directly connected to quests: Hearing Voices.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Jackson was not born with "the look." While a young man, however, he discovered a strange device in the wreckage of a ship. While examining it, he inadvertently activated a long-dormant power source connected to a holographic head. Jackson, deeply superstitious, interpreted this event as the manifestation of a powerful spirit. Jackson would return here with increasing frequency to "commune" with the spirit. This disembodied head, in reality, is a sentient person. During Jackson's séance encounters, he would be given instructions.

Thanks to the efforts of followers who slowly began appearing in Jackson's presence, along with the piecemeal guidance he passes along from his "visions" of the brain, the tribe has set up a surprisingly effective hydroponics system to grow large quantities of punga fruit.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Hearing Voices: Jackson has to be talked to in order to gain more information about the tribals and their ways.

Effects of player's actions:
• The only interaction with the player character is during the Hearing Voices quest where one has to talk to Jackson.
• Killing Jackson will result in no Karma loss.
• Killing him will also not affect the tribals' disposition towards the Lone Wanderer.
• Killing Jackson as he is talking to the hologram, before speaking to either him or the Calvert hologram, will open a different initial dialogue with the latter.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Ark & Dove Cathedral. Notable equipment & inventory: Tribal Garb.

chr_04006636.behavior: Unaggressive, cowardly; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox
chr_04006636.summary: Catherine can be found at the Riverboat Landing in the Capital Wasteland in the year 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Catherine is a denizen of the Capital Wasteland who lives near Rivet City. Her life was recently upended when her daughter Nadine left the region to find a fortune in the swamps of Point Lookout, against her mother's objections. Catherine doesn't believe that her daughter has the experience to survive in the wilderness, going so far as to recruit the Lone Wanderer to find her and bring her home safely. Though she fears for her daughter's safety, she implies that when she was Nadine's age, she was similarly foolhardy and adventurous.

As for Nadine's side of the dilemma, Catherine's daughter truly loves her mother, but only wishes to return when she has a sizable fortune to return with. Once Nadine takes control of the Duchess Gambit from the malicious Tobar, she reunites with her relieved mother in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Tailing the Tomboy: Catherine asks the Lone Wanderer to be on the lookout for her daughter Nadine when embarking on the journey to Point Lookout. As a reward, she will give the Lone Wanderer 300 caps and 10 refined punga fruit upon returning Nadine to her.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Arlington Library. Notable equipment & inventory: Wasteland Settler Outfit.

chr_04006635.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: happy. AI packages: dialogue, travel, sandbox
chr_04006635.summary: Nadine is an adventurer who left home to seek her fortune out in the wasteland and eventually found her way to Point Lookout in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Growing up with her mother Catherine in Rivet City, Nadine proved to be headstrong and naturally curious: trips to the banks of the Potomac River always involved her being the first to bag live mirelurk hatchlings, and she took to dyeing her hair bright orange. Catherine still worried that her daughter's wanderlust would flare up before she could gain the necessary experience to survive in the wasteland.

Sometime in July 2277, that pivotal moment came when the adult Nadine saw fit to leave home, feeling smothered by her mother's worries, and wanting to explore places beyond the Capital Wasteland. Even so, Nadine swore that once she had accrued her fortune, she would return home with it to share with her mother, though she was in no hurry.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Walking with Spirits: The Lone Wanderer learns from Nadine at the Ark & Dove Cathedral about the grotto where Jackson resides, starting Hearing Voices.
• Tailing the Tomboy

Effects of player's actions:
• When speaking with Nadine during Walking with Spirits, along with the location of the grotto, she also gives the option to remove the brain surgery scar inflicted during the Mother Punga hallucination.
• Choosing the dialogue option "Who cut open my head?" leads to Nadine starting an investigation into the matter. After this, she leaves the cathedral and reappears at the pier in Pilgrim's Landing, where she reveals Tobar's role as the guilty party and that she has taken over the Duchess Gambit as its new captain, making all subsequent boat trips free of charge.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: * After becoming captain of the Duchess Gambit

chr_04006634.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol, dialogue, sandbox
chr_04006634.role: Merchant / Service Provider (Alcohol, Food, Chems & Medicine, Supplies / Barter)
chr_04006634.summary: Tobar the Ferryman is a caucasian character in Point Lookout (Level 1, 70 HP). Found primarily around Arlington Library. Directly connected to quests: The Local Flavor.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Tobar is the captain of the steamboat Duchess Gambit, a ferry with which travelers can venture from the Capital Wasteland to Point Lookout, Maryland. In his youth, he was an adventurous and sprightly fellow whose curiosity took him up and down the coast from "the Commonwealth to the Broken Banks." Regardless of the veracity of his claims, he is a living reminder that the world will always have a place for the savvy and charming trickster. The Duchess was a small sightseeing vessel used for tourist excursions along the Chesapeake Bay before the War. Tobar's grandfather found her and, with the help of his caravan, restored the boat's boiler, allowing the vessel to be powered by steam heat from any fuel that will fit inside the burner.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Tobar stays at his boat waiting to take the Lone Wanderer back and forth as they please, and will trade merchandise with them in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Local Flavor: Tobar transports the player character to Point Lookout and will mention that there are untold treasures that lie within the swamps. When arriving in Point Lookout, he remarks about the smoke coming from Calvert Mansion and encourages the Lone Wanderer to check it out.
• Hearing Voices/Tailing the Tomboy: During Hearing Voices, it is revealed by Nadine that when people are rendered unconscious by the Mother Punga, someone sneaks into the sacred bog and removes a part of their brain. She later reveals the perpetrator to be Tobar, and locks him in the engine room of the Duchess Gambit. Tobar can then optionally be confronted, during which he taunts the Lone Wanderer about their "spirit walk," then attempts to justify his actions. Afterwards, he becomes hostile and must be killed.

chr_04005a39.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_04005a39.summary: Professor Calvert, also known as the Transcendent Master by Jackson's tribals, is the psychic, disembodied brain of a pre-War scientist residing in Point Lookout in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Professor Calvert was a member of the prestigious Calvert family before the Great War, and an accredited expert in the field of cognitive robotics. It was in this capacity that the professor became acquainted with other influential figures such as husband-wife business magnates Hugo and Cassidy Stolz, even inviting them to attend a dinner at his estate once. They were delighted to join him as he shared his latest projects with them; the professor's scientific pursuits enthralled Hugo and would later inspire some of his own projects in his bid to join the Vault-Tec board of directors. Despite their mutual respect, the couple found it rude that the professor would deliberately shun their acquaintance Desmond Lockheart from the dinner.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Hearing Voices: The Lone Wanderer speaks to Calvert in Jacksons' inner sanctum, and he instructs them to find a way to destroy Desmond's jamming device.
• Thought Control: Desmond gives the Cogwave jammer to the Lone Wanderer and instructs them to place it on the Wheel of Wonder. Before they can, Calvert telepathically orders the Lone Wanderer to throw the jammer in the trash compactor.
• A Meeting of the Minds: The choice arises whether to kill Calvert or Desmond. However, the Lone Wanderer must kill Calvert in the end regardless of their choice.

Effects of player's actions:
The Lone Wanderer must choose to kill either Desmond or Calvert at the end of the Meeting of the Minds quest; However, Calvert must be killed regardless of the outcome.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Point Lookout, Sea Cave. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_04003f6e.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, sandbox
chr_04003f6e.summary: Marguerite is a caucasian character in Point Lookout (Level 1, 75 HP). Found primarily around Moonshiner Shack. Directly connected to quests: A Spoonful of Whiskey.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A tough lady, Marguerite may not share the looks of the locals, but she is not troubled by them because she has been a Point Lookout resident since birth.

She is the descendant of a family of moonshiners from around the Point Lookout area, who sold their liquor during Prohibition. She is considered a local 'marsh folk' by the Swampfolk and remains unmolested unlike outsiders.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• A Spoonful of Whiskey: Marguerite will make her famous moonshine if the Lone Wanderer brings her the ingredients.

Effects of player's actions:
When first encountered, Marguerite pretends to be sick in an attempt to get the Lone Wanderer to gather materials to cure her "Orange Fever". If the Lone Wanderer's Medicine is high enough (over 70), she will drop the pretense and ask them to gather items to make moonshine.

If the Lone Wanderer has a high enough Repair skill (minimum 44), they can also volunteer to fix Marguerite's still for 100 caps (200 caps if a Speech check is passed).

After completing A Spoonful of Whiskey, Marguerite will make the Lone Wanderer her famous moonshine whenever they ask (once every 24 hrs), provided they give her the ingredients.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Moonshiner Shack. Notable equipment & inventory: Shotgun Shell, Sawed-Off Shotgun, Head Wrap, Wasteland Legend Outfit.

chr_04003f2c.summary: Dialogue Voice Placeholder is a caucasian character in Point Lookout (Level 1, 75 HP). Encountered in Point Lookout. Directly connected to quests: An Antique Land.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: DLC04FF01speakerNPC), Dialogue Voice Placeholder is defined as a Caucasian in Point Lookout. Appears in or relates to quests: An Antique Land.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 1, 75 HP. S.P.E.C.I.A.L. profile: STR 5, PER 5, END 5, CHA 152, INT 5, AGI 5, LCK 5. Behavioral traits: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Point Lookout encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_040035b4.behavior: Aggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, escort, travel, guard
chr_040035b4.summary: Desmond Lockheart is a former British intelligence agent from the pre-War era turned ghoul. In 2277, he resides in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Born in the era before the Great War over 250 years ago, Desmond claims to have belonged to the cutthroat world of international intelligence, operating under the flag of the United Kingdom leading up to the apocalypse. While nothing is known about the extent of his activities as a spy, he was at least well-connected to people in positions of power and authority, including husband-wife business magnates Hugo and Cassidy Stolz, who considered him a friend worth working with. In Lockheart's case, he elected to undergo a procedure involving controlled exposure to normally lethal doses of radiation, leading to his later ghoulification, one of the few known cases of ghouls existing before the bombs.

At some point, Desmond carried out an unspecified sabotage on the St.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Local Flavor: The Lone Wanderer helps Desmond defend Calvert Mansion during the tribal assault upon it.
• Walking with Spirits: Desmond insists the Lone Wanderer somehow get into the tribals stronghold and get them to divulge why they attacked the mansion.
• Hearing Voices: After returning with useless information, Desmond demands the Lone Wanderer find a way into the tribals' society.
• Thought Control: After getting in with the tribals, Desmond urges the Lone Wanderer to place a jammer on the Ferris wheel on the boardwalk in order to sever Calvert's leadership from the tribals.
• A Meeting of the Minds: Desmond is going to face Calvert once and for all.

Effects of player's actions:
• During A Meeting of the Minds, the Lone Wanderer must decide between killing Desmond or Calvert.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Calvert Mansion. Notable equipment & inventory: Desmond's Eyeglasses, Combat Shotgun, Shotgun Shell.

chr_04002f42.behavior: Unaggressive, brave; mood: surprised. AI packages: dialogue, travel, patrol
chr_04002f42.summary: S. Marcella J., shortened to just Marcella, is a Christian missionary nomadically traveling the wasteland. In 2277, she can be found in Point Lookout trying to stop a dark plot.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Marcella was raised within the Abbey of the Road, a post-War Christian stronghold, where she was educated in the faith and eventually received her Rites of Mission. Since then, she has traveled throughout the wasteland to spread the word of the Bible and to do good. A secondary goal she follows is finding and recovering lost religious relics for later restoration and preservation. This gave her the knowledge to recognize dark relics like the Krivbeknih, which she discovered could be destroyed if it was brought to the Dunwich Building near Washington, D.C.

Early in her travels, she came to the Commonwealth, where she took shelter with a caravan during a windstorm. From the caravaneers, she heard worrying tales about the horrid state of the Pitt and wondered if she might eventually find her way there.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Dark Heart of Blackhall: After first meeting Obadiah Blackhall and getting his request to retrieve a lost heirloom, the Lone Wanderer is intercepted by Marcella, who hopes to stop them from helping fulfill a dark plot going on at Blackhall Manor.

Effects of player's actions:
After obtaining the Krivbeknih from the ritual site, if one returns to Marcella's tent at the outpost, they will find her murdered and the message "Die thief" written in blood close by, implied to be the work of smugglers encountered outside upon arrival.

Other interactions:
• Marcella can recite some passages from the Bible, specifically John 1:4-5, John 5:24, John 16:33, and 1 Corinthians 15:52.
• The Lone Wanderer can also tell Marcella about the Bible passage their mother Catherine liked, and she will recognize it and compliment them.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
• Has a 25% chance to appear

• Dependent on progressing The Dark Heart of Blackhall up to her death

chr_04002f3e.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: sandbox, dialogue, travel, patrol
chr_04002f3e.summary: Obadiah Blackhall is a resident of the marshlands in Point Lookout and the sole inhabitant of Blackhall Manor in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Obadiah is the last known descendant of the Blackhalls, an influential family that had deep-rooted ties to the history of Point Lookout going back generations before the Great War; it was his ancestor Constance Blackhall who spearheaded the commercialization of the St. Mary's County location and turned Pilgrim's Landing into a tourist destination in the early 21st century.

Though he chooses to live alone and isolated in the marshes surrounding his family home, the elderly Obadiah has not abandoned the obsession with the occult that once gripped Constance. He desires to reclaim an important artifact, which he considers a "family heirloom," that was previously stolen but recently resurfaced in Point Lookout. With it, he aims to restore the influence the Blackhalls once had over the indigenous swampfolk.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Dark Heart of Blackhall: Blackhall wants the Lone Wanderer to bring back an old family heirloom that was stolen from him by the swampfolk.

Effects of player's actions:
• After completing his quest, if the Krivbeknih was returned to him, Obadiah can be found praying in his basement in front of a dead creeper. The player character is then given the option to engage in conversation after his initial disapproval, and he will request that they leave his home. From here, there are three unique choice options which he will only respond to once, then will never restart conversation upon leaving.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • If the player returned the book to Obadiah during the quest.

chr_0500b27d.behavior: Aggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: patrol
chr_0500b27d.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_05009a08.summary: Andrew Endicott was a 17th-century resident of Salem who was abducted by Zetan aliens.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Andrew detailed his experience in a holotape which was recorded by his alien abductors. He was reportedly abducted on May 17, 1697, directly from his home in Salem Village, and brought into the aliens' vessel.

As he was taken through the ship, he saw the stars, sun, and Earth through windows, leading him to assume he was somewhere in the "ether," close to where he believed Heaven would be; however, his experience made him conclude that he was actually in Hell, captured by what he viewed as devils. This led him to fear that the religious scriptures he followed had actually reversed Heaven and Hell.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Part of a medic squad attached to the 108th Infantry Battalion, Corporal Spurlock was no stranger to blood and guts on the battlefield, from blood sprays to missing limbs. Abducted together with the rest of her squad when they became separated from the main force during the Battle of Anchorage, she was kept in suspended animation and periodically thawed out for alien experiments. Unlike others, she fought hard to maintain her terror, as she was kept awake during vivisection. Shortly before the Lone Wanderer's arrival, she succumbed to shock and internal bleeding, joining her squadmates in death.

chr_05007e50.summary: Rivet City Security is a hispanic character in Mothership Zeta (Level 6, 60 HP). Affiliated with Rivet City Security, Rivet City Residents. Encountered in Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Rivet City security are the police and defense force of Rivet City, and they can be found patrolling the city's halls and social spaces. They are issued black-colored first generation combat armor, a riot helmet, and a 10mm submachine gun for the job. Following the Brotherhood of Steel's reclamation of Project Purity from the Enclave, and the project's subsequent activation, Rivet City security guards help protect water caravans for the Water Distribution Network.

If there are physical conflicts between the residents of Rivet City, the officers will intervene, and fine those who are caught stealing. However, their enforcement is lackluster. They seem to have a rather laid-back attitude towards their job, informing the player character that if "someone steals something from you, take it back.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• The Replicated Man: If the player has learned about the existence of Horace Pinkerton, Rivet City security can be asked about his whereabouts. They will respond by dismissing rumors that Pinkerton's ghost haunts the city's broken bow.
• You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head: These characters can inform the player on the potential whereabouts of Ted Strayer.

Effects of player's actions:
• Rivet City security guards will track if the player has committed minor (pickpocketing, theft, etc.) or major (assault, murder) crimes against Rivet City. They will initially be hostile when the player commits a crime, but if one returns 72 hours later they will no longer be hostile. However, they will warn the player not to commit further crimes, with differing dialogue depending on whether the player has committed major or minor crimes.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Mothership Zeta encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: Rivet City Security Uniform, Rivet City Security Helmet.

chr_05006c6c.summary: Private Beckett is a african american character in Mothership Zeta (Level 5, 240 HP). Found primarily around Cryo Lab.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Beckett was part of Elliott Tercorien's medic squad, under the command of Sergeant Daniels. Assigned to the 108th Infantry Battalion, the six medics were responsible for dealing with casualties from fighting the Chinese Army during the Battle of Anchorage.

His primary role was as a stretcher bearer, moving wounded troops to safe areas to provide medical aid or for evacuation to the rear lines. Beckett was abducted in the middle of the night, together with the rest of his team by the Zetans, and kept in suspended animation for the next two centuries until the arrival of the Lone Wanderer.

Unlike Tercorien, Beckett and the others were used for torturous medical experiments, which would leave them in horrific pain were they conscious.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Among the Stars: He can be revived from his stasis pod along with Sergeant Daniels. If the player revives him and Daniels without Elliott first preparing them, they will run into the operating room and fight each other to the death. Allowing Elliott to prepare them will result in two temporary allies: Although in pain, burning up inside, they will go toe to toe with the aliens during the assault on cryo storage.
• Both he and Daniels lose health naturally over time and will not heal themselves, even if somehow given stimpaks; this will eventually lead to their deaths. Additionally, Beckett and Daniels will die immediately upon the destruction of the cryo lab generator as part of a scripted event.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • He receives a Chinese assault rifle from Elliott if he is correctly revived.

chr_05006c6b.summary: Sergeant Daniels is a caucasian character in Mothership Zeta (Level 5, 240 HP). Found primarily around Cryo Lab.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Daniels was the NCO in charge of Elliott Tercorien's medic squad. Assigned to the 108th Infantry Battalion, the six medics handled casualties caused by the Chinese Army during the Battle of Anchorage.

Daniels was not a medic, instead erecting field tents and requesting medical evacuation via radio, after the medics completed field surgery or if the wounds were too severe to be safely treated on the battlefield. He was abducted in the middle of the night with the rest of his squad, stored onboard the mothership for the next two centuries.

Unlike Tercorien, the rest of his squad were used for torturous medical experiments, which would leave them in horrific pain were they conscious.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character

• Among the Stars: He can be revived from his stasis pod along with Beckett. If he is revived alone with Beckett without Elliott Tercorien first preparing them, they will run into the operating room and fight each other to the death. Otherwise, they become temporary allies while fighting through cryo storage.
• Both he and Beckett lose health naturally over time and will not heal themselves, even if somehow given stimpaks; this will eventually lead to their deaths. Additionally, Beckett and Daniels will die immediately upon the destruction of the cryo lab generator as part of a scripted event.

chr_05006871.summary: Wastelanders are humans and ghouls living in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are not affiliated with any other groups.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Wastelanders make a subsistence living off the land, trade with local settlements, and try not to be ravaged by the abundant (and usually hostile) wildlife, or bands of roaming raider gangs or slavers. Most are not aggressive, but will defend themselves if attacked.

Some of them do not want to open dialogue and tend to be rude, while others are pleasant and friendly towards the Lone Wanderer. Most are encountered in random encounters. These wastelanders are usually fleeing from anything from mole rats to a deathclaw, others may fight against these creatures, and some unlucky wastelanders are encountered already dead.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Alive
Wastelanders not involved in random encounters can be found in fixed locations:
• A wastelander being chased by a raider with a flamethrower will appear just outside the Calverton chapel.
• Three hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy the ghoul outpost.
• One can be found fighting a super mutant in the back of a blue truck just outside of Pennsylvania Avenue. If he or she survives, they will wander around the Brotherhood checkpoint.
• Two hostile ghoul wastelanders live inside the pylon shack, Sometimes, they can be dead when reached.
• Four hostile ghoul wastelanders occupy Shacktown.
• Two can be found in the wastelander tent and sniper vista, usually sitting near the fire.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* 25% chance of spawning headgear.
** 20% chance of spawning a frag grenade.

chr_05003302.behavior: Unaggressive, average; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel
chr_05003302.summary: Colonel Hartigan was an astronaut from the United States Air Force, abducted by aliens in the golden age of the Space Race. His corpse is found kept in stasis in Mothership Zetas engineering core as of 2277. His space capsule can be found in the research lab.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Colonel Hartigan was one of the pioneers of manned spaceflight, performing low-orbit flights under the auspices of the United States Air Force and the United States Space Administration in the 1960s. During the Clarabella 7 mission, his capsule failed to reach the rendezvous point and splashdown, with the government covering up the disappearance by claiming his craft crashed after becoming entangled in high-altitude weather balloons.

In reality, Hartigan was abducted by Zetans and brought onboard their mothership. He tried to initiate first contact, explaining his mission and trying to make peaceful overtures, suggesting that the Zetans and humans could learn from each other. His naivete was quickly removed with a shock baton, and he was later put in stasis.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:

• Among the Stars: Hartigan's spacesuit has to be salvaged in order to progress, as it allows the Lone Wanderer to complete a spacewalk and access other areas of the mothership.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Engineering Core. Notable equipment & inventory: Spacesuit.

chr_050032fc.summary: Toshiro Kago is a samurai from feudal-era Japan who was abducted and kept in cryonic stasis by the alien crew of Mothership Zeta up to 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Toshiro was abducted from Japan by the Zetans sometime during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, between the late 1560s to early 1600s, and was then cryogenically frozen by them aboard Mothership Zeta. He remained preserved until centuries later, when the Lone Wanderer and Somah thaw him out. He joins them in their counterattack against the Zetans, seeking to reclaim his lost weapon in the process.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Among the Stars: Toshiro can be spoken to about his missing sword and the Lone Wanderer can return it to him after retrieving it from the maintenance level.
• This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough...: During the final battle on the bridge, after the first wave of aliens are defeated, Toshiro will run in from a side door and assist Paulson and Somah in battling the next wave of attackers.

Effects of player's actions:
After the events of Mothership Zeta, he stays aboard Zeta and cannot be interacted with. He will disappear if one revisits the steamworks but will remain on the bridge if the player character travels to or from the Capital Wasteland. He can be found later in the living quarters.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text:
* Kago will use the sword if it is either recovered from the waste disposal area and given to him, or if one never enters the disposal area.
* Should the player decide to keep the sword, Kago will remain unarmed.

chr_050032fb.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: combat, travel, dialogue, sandbox, follow
chr_050032fb.summary: Paulson is an abducted rancher found frozen aboard Mothership Zeta, who becomes a part of the Lone Wanderer's ragtag crew fighting the aliens.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A rancher from the American frontier, from the period known as the "Wild West," Due to being kept in suspended animation for several hundred years, the plan could not come to fruition. He is the second-oldest human thawed by the Lone Wanderer following their abduction, behind Toshiro Kago.

While the concept of a spaceship is unfamiliar to him, he quickly picks up the term "aliens" from the Lone Wanderer at their first meeting, alternating with "little bastards" and "little buggers," though he could also call them green men or piles of horse shit.

His single-minded focus on killing every alien he comes across is due to the trauma of seeing and hearing his wife and son taken up by the mothership, crying and begging to save them, but being powerless to stop it.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Among the Stars: The player can bring Paulson along as a companion to the hangar, but he will refuse to enter either the robot assembly area or the cryo lab. Paulson will comment on the environment and nudge the player towards the objectives, as well as provide assistance when using the coils in the hangar to fry incoming aliens.
• The player can also ask him to accompany them in destroying the generator in the hangar area of the spaceship and to any of the optional areas connected to the engineering core.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Engineering Core. Notable equipment & inventory: .44 Round, Magnum, itm_05003306, itm_05003305, itm_05006e1e.

chr_0500096b.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: puzzled. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, travel, follow, guard
chr_0500096b.summary: Private Elliott Tercorien, serial number 3477809, is a pre-War U.S. Army soldier found abducted and held in a stasis chamber in Mothership Zetas engineering core. He is a major character.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Tercorien was a fully educated medical doctor before the Great War, who chose this career path as he believed he was better with blood and guts, rather than wires and gizmos. He had a cushy job at a civilian hospital in Washington, before giving up his job and enlisting in the U.S. Army. He received training in the nascent field of cryoscience, which showed promise as a potential tool for medical practitioners. he was attached to the 108th Infantry Battalion. Together with five other medics, he was responsible for patching up soldiers wounded in combat with the People's Liberation Army. The brutality of fighting produced an almost overwhelming stream of wounded, and though technically a private, Elliott was responsible for his entire team and their work.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
• Sgt. Daniels (active)
• Cpl. Rheems (K.I.A.)
• Cpl. Spurlock (K.I.A.)
• Pvt. Mears (K.I.A.)
• Pvt. Dawkins (M.I.A.)
• Pvt. Beckett (active)

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Among the Stars: The Lone Wanderer has the option of bringing Elliott Tercorien with them as a companion to the cryo lab to help out. While traveling through the laboratory, the player will come upon an experimentation lab with Sgt. Daniels and Pvt. Beckett being experimented upon. Tercorien will suffer a breakdown, attacking aliens with abandon and wiping them out, before asking the Wanderer to help them decide whether to put them out of their misery, gently euthanizing them both by cutting their oxygen supply, or revive them, so that Daniels and Beckett can help in the fight through the laboratory, at least until their bodies shut down - in other words, give them a soldiers' death.
• The dialogue option to ask him to accompany the Wanderer into the laboratory is only available once.

chr_0500096a.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: travel, dialogue, patrol, follow, sandbox
chr_0500096a.summary: Somah is a slaver from the Capital Wasteland who was abducted by the alien crew of Mothership Zeta in 2277 and confined in one of the ship's holding cells.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Prior to her abduction, Somah worked with the slavers of the wasteland, selling enslaved people to Paradise Falls. though she always had others perform the gunfighting side of the job. She further elaborates on her recruitment into the slave trade, saying it was because of her lifelong knack for tinkering with machines and being able to strip useful parts from them. Something else that helped her in her line of work was an ability to think fast and come up with plans on the fly in chaotic situations.

One of the few post-War abductees still left alive in the aliens' captivity by 2277, Somah was originally captured after picking up the radio signal broadcast by the downed recon craft Theta in the Capital Wasteland. She pursued this lead, hoping to potentially recover valuable scrap.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Not of This World: Somah helps the Lone Wanderer to escape the cell they were both placed in and navigate through the hostile alien ship on which they find themselves.
• Among the Stars: Somah can optionally be brought along as a companion while exploring the robot assembly sector.
• This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough...: If Somah survived the previous quest, she will help in the last battle by keeping the aliens at bay while the Lone Wanderer takes control of Zeta to battle the other mothership.

Effects of player's actions:
• Upon reaching the cryo-chambers, Somah will rejoin the party; she will now use a combat shotgun. She will also arm herself with any available weapons between escaping the cell and her splitting up, including those dropped by aliens.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: • Depending on whether the player character paid her to repair equipment beforehand.

chr_05000969.behavior: Unaggressive, foolhardy; mood: neutral. AI packages: dialogue, sandbox, travel, use item, follow
chr_05000969.summary: Sally is a caucasian child character in Mothership Zeta (Level 1, 525 HP). Encountered in Mothership Zeta. Directly connected to quests: Not of This World, This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough..., Among the Stars.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Sally and her sister were abducted shortly after the bombs dropped in 2077. Her parents were killed almost immediately after the war, leaving the two girls to themselves. After the abduction, the girls were separated, and Sally never learned that her sister died during one of the aliens' many experiments. She has blocked out most of the bad things that happened to her and is now a fixture in the lower levels of the ship, repeatedly escaping custody and exploring the ship's lower level. She has a degree of insight into the workings of the Mothership and the motives of the aliens that nobody else possesses.

The fact that Sally was abducted during the Great War makes her more than 200 years old. Sally also offers random alien items once every few hours, should the Lone Wanderer request them.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
Not of This World/Among the Stars/This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough...: Sally assists the Lone Wanderer throughout the Mothership Zeta quests by using her skills to open doors or to provide information as they move through the ship.

Effects of player's actions:
• After completion of the quests, Sally stays aboard the alien starship and scrounges for materials. The player character can return to the starship at any point and ask if she's found anything, and, if she has, she will give the items away. This interaction can be manipulated the same way random encounters can be manipulated. The player character can also simply wait 24 hours and ask her again, and she will give away more items.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Mothership Zeta encounter zones. Notable equipment & inventory: itm_000340fb.

chr_0004c67d.summary: Failed FEV subjects are mutants that were once humans. They can be found in Vault 87.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They are hideously mutated Vault 87 FEV test subjects. In the Vault 87 terminal entries, a vast majority of the deaths logged in the computers were caused by FEV experimentation.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
Failed FEV subjects appear to have undergone much of the same physical changes that other super mutants went through after FEV exposure, such as greenish skin and increased muscle mass and bone density. However, their internal structures seem to have grown at a random, rapid pace throughout their body, resulting in the muscles and bones bursting the skin, killing them in a horrific and painful fashion. The failed FEV subjects' upper torsos are much larger and far more visibly mutated than their legs, with enormous tumor-like growths blooming from the neck and shoulders. They all wear tattered Vault 87 jumpsuits.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Failed FEV subject:
Found in the Vault 87 test labs, they are all dead and their holding cells have a small amount of radiation. According to the Vault 87 laboratory computer, they are among many of the FEV test subjects that have died due to their brains being unable to support even the most simple actions of the human body and behavior after being injected with FEV.

chr_00073e25.role: Wasteland Scavengers, Scavenger Dogs — Yao Guai
chr_00073e25.summary: Scavenger's Yao Guai is a yao guai creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 7, 220 HP). Affiliated with Wasteland Scavengers, Scavenger Dogs. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
They can be encountered across the entire Capital Wasteland in and around craggy, hilly places, or in caverns. There are two spots where one is guaranteed to come across concentrated populations of yao guai, including the yao guai tunnels and the yao guai cave. Yao guai are generally found in pairs or sometimes wandering alone, frequently at night. Some wasteland scavengers travel with a yao guai companion. They will not attack on sight and can be approached safely, although they will defend themselves and their ally if threatened.

Gameplay attributes:
Yao guai attack by using running pounces followed by slashes and bites after closing the distance to their target. Like all creatures with pounce attacks, the yao guai cannot pounce with a crippled hind leg. However, even with a crippled limb, it will resume charging after a split second.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Yao guai:
The standard yao guai with all characteristics listed above. Prime locations are in the cliffside cavern and the yao guai tunnels, but they can also be found across most of the wasteland.

Scavenger's yao guai:
These yao guai seem domesticated. They travel alongside scavenger-merchants, defending them against any threat that may arise.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Can be found in cliffside cavern.
• Can be found in yao guai tunnels.
• Can be found in the yao guai cave.

chr_00073e1d.summary: Scavenger's Dog is a dog creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 1, 20 HP). Affiliated with Scavenger Dogs, Wasteland Scavengers. Encountered in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Though 200 years have passed since the Great War, dogs have stayed generally unaltered by radiation. Dogs are a favored pet for traveling merchants as they provide both companionship and protection. As a result of the radiation, most dogs have lost their fur and have slightly mottled skin, but some have retained their fur coats and appear somewhat normal.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
Dogs are quadrupedal canines that can run at incredible speeds, allowing them to chase down prey. While running, they use their long tails to keep their balance. They are carnivorous and have sharp, pointy teeth designed to rip into flesh.

Gameplay attributes:
Dogs are usually encountered in packs of four to six. To low level characters, this could mean trouble since a pack can easily overwhelm and surround them. To higher level characters, they are little more than a nuisance, yet can still be difficult to put down as a result of their erratic and agile running patterns. Vicious dogs (and their variants) are always hostile unless the Lone Wanderer possesses the Animal Friend perk.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Raider guard dog:
Raider guard dogs fight alongside their masters, the raiders. Since they are trained as guard dogs, they are very attentive and can spot threats easier than many other creatures. Raider guard dogs will tend to run at targets they find hostile, alerting the raiders of their presence. They are still affected by the Animal Friend perk, but will not attack raiders.

Scavenger's dog:
These dogs are found around scavenger's encampments and will be friendly to others as long as they do not act aggressively to them or their master. These dogs have slightly less Hit Points and attack damage than vicious dogs.

There is a Karma loss for killing a scavenger's dog, as well as the scavenger themselves and/or the scavenger's brahmin if they have one.

chr_00072b8b.summary:
Glowing ones or luminous necrotic post-humans are ghouls who have absorbed so much radiation that they emit a strong green glow. Glowing ones have become living conduits of radioactivity and emit radiation involuntarily, so they can still be dangerous to normal humans, even after dying.

Feral glowing ones are generally stronger than normal feral ghouls. They are radioactive to the point of being able to voluntarily release it from their bodies in a brilliant burst.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
In New California:
Although most glowing ones encountered across the wastes have become feral, those encountered in New California are generally civil (if not sane).

Until Necropolis was overrun by the super mutants in 2162, glowing ones lived quietly in the remains of Vault 12, separate from the normal ghouls on the surface. Just above ground, several were kept in evenly-spaced cages lining the Hall of the Dead, apparently as a source of lighting. All glowing ones at Necropolis were kept within the church or the Vault. Those who dwelt within Vault 12 were all capable of articulate speech, and expressed themselves in strange, poetic declarations. The six imprisoned at the church were only known to mumble and drool.

Nearby, a separate population of peaceful ghouls were forced to take refuge in a sewer by the ghoul warlord Set.

sections.title: Biology
sections.text: The distinctive luminescence that is the trademark of the glowing one can be best attributed to an unusually high amount of radioactive material that builds up in the bloodstream and muscle tissue of a typical ghoul. Sometimes, upon the transformation into a feral ghoul, the neurological systems of the body cease filtering these particles from the blood and tissue, instead of causing them to build a distinctive bio-luminescence that is a characteristic of the glowing ones. In daylight, they simply appear to be incredibly pale feral ghouls, but in the darkness, they glow with a vivid yellow-green hue, their opaque skeletons clearly visible as in an x-ray. Approaching a deceased glowing one can cause minor radiation exposure.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00072b8a.summary: Feral ghouls (also known as mindless zombies, ghoul crazies, feral necrotic post-humans, or simply ferals) are ghouls that have lost their upper faculties and ability to reason, regressing into basic instinct and behaving more like vicious wild animals attacking any non-ghouls they encounter regardless of former ties like friends or family.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Biology:
The degeneration into a feral state (referred to as ferocious post-necrotic dystrophy) is not fully understood. It is known that it is a result of a degeneration of the brain (which is not affected by the regenerative mutation of the spinal cord) and emerges following the atrophy of higher brain functions, accompanied by an increased level of aggression and appetite. When the loss of capacity for thought is complete, a ghoul is considered feral. The factors that may cause a ghoul to enter this state are unclear, but anti-social or isolated ghouls may be more susceptible to it. Exposure to intense radiation may also be a factor; feral ghouls have no body heat and emit lethal levels of radiation, indicating that feral ghouls are for all intents and purposes dead, their functions sustained only by their high irradiation.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Feral ghoul:
TV series article: Feral ghoul (TV series)
Feral ghouls (also known as mindless ghouls, ghoul crazies or zombies) are the basic feral ghoul variant, wearing only a pair of tattered shorts and noticeably weaker than standard human opponents, they are easily dispatched with one or two headshots from any decent weapon or a solid hit from a decent melee or unarmed weapon. Despite their shrill noise and remarkable speed, they are only truly a threat when they have the advantage of numbers, or when the player character is at a low level. Some feral ghouls come in different colors as well as different types. The colors are different depending on how the human looked before turning into a feral ghoul.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00072b87.summary: Feral ghouls are creatures found in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are ghouls who have lost their sanity and ability to reason due to radiation, making them aggressive to anyone who is not another ghoul. Feral ghouls are partially held by many humans to be responsible for the discrimination shown towards all ghouls, whether or not they have retained their mental faculties.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Gameplay attributes:
Feral ghouls often give a loud, low-pitched screech or growl before attacking enemies. This can be helpful in dark places or areas with objects blocking the Lone Wanderer's view, especially in the metro system and the Dunwich Building. As with normal ghouls, ferals are entirely resistant to radiation. This makes a glowing one especially dangerous when encountered with regular ferals, as they constantly emit radiation that will heal the ghouls within the surrounding area.

Feral ghouls attack with no strategy. They rush foes in one massive onslaught. At first, they attack with a running over-the-head strike. When close to an enemy, they will swipe at them horizontally or diagonally.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Feral ghoul:
The basic feral ghoul variant in Fallout 3 wears only a pair of tattered shorts (or ripped pants) and is noticeably weaker than standard human opponents. They are easily defeated with one or two headshots or a solid hit with a decent weapon in close-quarters combat. Despite their noisy shrieks and remarkable speed, they are not much of a threat unless they outnumber their enemies.

Some feral ghouls come in different colors as well as different types. Some are a "healthy" pink color while others are a grimy gray color. Their skin colors are different depending on what ethnicity they were prior to ghoulification.

Feral ghouls can drop rare pass cards in blue and red colors, with a 1.25% chance of dropping a given color of pass card.
