chr_0001d76f.role: Megaton Residents — Robot — Mister Handy / Gutsy
chr_0001d76f.summary: Deputy Steel is a robot — mister handy / gutsy creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 9, 350 HP). Affiliated with Megaton Residents. Found primarily around The Armory.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Previously purchased from Tinker Joe, Deputy Steel is a General Atomics Mister Gutsy, reprogrammed to assist Sheriff Simms with upholding security in the armory. It got its deputy title from Simms, who is living out his Wild West childhood fantasies. Every once in a while, Deputy Steel gets some polishing from Harden Simms.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• If the Lone Wanderer has a Science skill of 75 or more, they can deactivate both Deputy Steel and Deputy Weld using the computer terminal in the armory. If a Stealth Boy is used before entering, the Lone Wanderer might sneak over to the terminal undetected to deactivate Deputy Steel and loot the place without any conflict.

Effects of player's actions:
• If Deputy Weld, Megaton's Protectron guard, is destroyed after Broken Steel is installed, Deputy Steel will assume Deputy Weld's post.
• In the Game of the Year edition this is not the case, instead Deputy Steel will remain in the armory. However, Deputy Steel will still show up if the Lone Wanderer attacks Deputy Weld, as will Sheriff Simms.
• If the Lone Wanderer enters the armory in Megaton, Deputy Steel will become hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Armory. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_00017a03.role: Robots, Tenpenny Tower Residents — Robot — Protectron
chr_00017a03.summary: Shakes is a protectron robot that functions as a bartender in the Federalist Lounge at Tenpenny Tower in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Shakes is the Federalist Lounge's robotic bartender, and he dutifully serves drinks twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week. In fact, being a bartender is all Shakes has ever known; he was commissioned by Allistair Tenpenny for that very purpose. Shakes doesn't have much to say, but he can offer discounts on drinks if you know which buttons to press.

Shakes serves only alcohol and stimpaks.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer convinces Tenpenny to allow the ghouls to live at the tower, Shakes will survive after the ghouls "purge" the tower of its human residents. Apparently, Roy Phillips does not find killing Shakes necessary, as he is not human.
• Initially, Shakes serves drinks at some of the highest prices across the Capital Wasteland. However, if the Lone Wanderer hacks into his programming terminal, his prices can be lowered significantly. The terminal is beside him on the bar and if hacked into Shakes be set to either sell at a "Holiday Discount (10%)" or a hefty "V.I.P. Discount (50%)" (but not both). If the Lone Wanderer is caught doing this, Shakes and all the bar patrons will become hostile. After hacking his terminal and setting up the V.I.P.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Tenpenny Tower Lobby. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0001d6e2.summary: Metro Protectron is a robot — protectron creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 75 HP). Affiliated with Metro Security Robots. Found primarily around Dupont Circle Station.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Many Protectrons were commissioned by the U.S. Army before the Great War of 2077. They are painted a dark olive drab with a white star on their chest. These mechanized soldiers still wander the wastes, attacking everything from radroaches to Brotherhood Outcasts. The Pitt adds a new variety of Protectron called the "factory Protectron", which lacks a glass dome but possesses a single ocular lens and a cage around the combat inhibitor. The top of where the dome would be appears to be made to look like a construction hard-hat and the body has a yellow coloration. Broken Steel adds "Enclave Protectrons," which appear to be much newer, with red glass domes and a polished steel-gray finish. A special red-painted Protectron also appears at the House of Wares in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Protectrons have a glass dome on top of their heads that acts as an ocular lens that allows the Protectron to scan its surroundings and act accordingly. This glass dome also houses a laser emitter that shoots a high-powered laser beam. The same type of laser is mounted in both of the Protectron's "hands/claws". Although Protectrons are rather slow and ponderous, their upper body can swivel up to about 90 degrees to either side before having to step into a different position, which means that they can easily keep track of their target.

All Protectrons come with a combat inhibitor mounted on their back that allows them to selectively target opponents, depending on pre-programmed guidelines. The combat inhibitor is generally left exposed, making it easy to disable when approaching a Protectron from behind.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Protectron:
Both operational and destroyed protectrons can be found throughout the wasteland.

Metro Protectron:
Metro Protectrons are found in many metro stations. When approached, they will ask the Lone Wanderer for a metro ticket. If they possess one, then it will be automatically taken from the player character's inventory and the Protectron will remain friendly, continuing to walk around the metro station attacking any enemies. Otherwise, the Protectron will turn hostile. On the Red and Blue metros in D.C., the associated red and blue pass cards serve this purpose. Metro Protectrons have the same stats as the standard Protectrons, despite their mundane functions.

Nuka-Cola security:
This model of Protectron is only found active on the Nuka-Cola plant's factory floor.

chr_0001cf87.summary: Raider Guard Dog is a dog creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 3, 60 HP). Affiliated with Wasteland Dogs. Found primarily around Wasteland, Springvale Elementary School, DC Ruins Sector DC21a (Red Racer Factory — Bailey's Crossroads).

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Though 200 years have passed since the Great War, dogs have stayed generally unaltered by radiation. Dogs are a favored pet for traveling merchants as they provide both companionship and protection. As a result of the radiation, most dogs have lost their fur and have slightly mottled skin, but some have retained their fur coats and appear somewhat normal.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
Dogs are quadrupedal canines that can run at incredible speeds, allowing them to chase down prey. While running, they use their long tails to keep their balance. They are carnivorous and have sharp, pointy teeth designed to rip into flesh.

Gameplay attributes:
Dogs are usually encountered in packs of four to six. To low level characters, this could mean trouble since a pack can easily overwhelm and surround them. To higher level characters, they are little more than a nuisance, yet can still be difficult to put down as a result of their erratic and agile running patterns. Vicious dogs (and their variants) are always hostile unless the Lone Wanderer possesses the Animal Friend perk.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Raider guard dog:
Raider guard dogs fight alongside their masters, the raiders. Since they are trained as guard dogs, they are very attentive and can spot threats easier than many other creatures. Raider guard dogs will tend to run at targets they find hostile, alerting the raiders of their presence. They are still affected by the Animal Friend perk, but will not attack raiders.

Scavenger's dog:
These dogs are found around scavenger's encampments and will be friendly to others as long as they do not act aggressively to them or their master. These dogs have slightly less Hit Points and attack damage than vicious dogs.

There is a Karma loss for killing a scavenger's dog, as well as the scavenger themselves and/or the scavenger's brahmin if they have one.

chr_0001cf81.summary: Giant Worker Ant is a giant ant creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 2, 30 HP). Affiliated with Giant Ants. Found primarily around Wasteland, Shalebridge.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Giant ants are large mutated arthropod insects of the Formicidae family, genus Camponotus, most likely black carpenter ants. Some scientists theorize this mutation comes from the effects of extended exposure to radiation. Giant ants have retained a strong swarm instinct and will attack prey in packs or double-down to protect the nest if their queen is threatened in any way.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
They make a loud, chattering noise with their mandibles and are better adjusted to daylight than their California counterparts. There are five variants of these ants, including workers, soldiers, queens, invaders, and the mutated forager ants. Ant nectar can occasionally be looted from their corpses and refuse piles (found in their lairs).

Gameplay attributes:
Ants usually attack head-on in droves of up to five. They do not try to flank enemies but will surround them if they get close enough. Their mandibles can be devastating to a low-level player, but they are not much of a threat to those who are high-level or well-equipped. If their antennae are crippled, ants will frenzy and attack everything around them, including their own kind. The Entomologist perk will increase damage against giant ants and other insects by 50%.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Giant ant:
This ant variant can only be found dead throughout the Capital Wasteland.

Giant soldier ant:
These are the colony's main defense against intruders. They are plentiful and will often overwhelm an enemy, either letting it run off or killing it on the spot, usually the latter.

Giant worker ant:
As their name suggests, these ants do most of the work around the colony. They are relatively frail but are found in large groups.

Giant ant queen:
The mother of their respective ant brood, this variant is roughly four to five times larger than an average giant ant. When threatened, her wings will buzz about and she will hiss at the enemy. She will then proceed to spit acidic saliva at the enemy in an attempt to ward it off.

quotes: Sentry bots possess an authoritative array of speech programming, though it mainly expresses its current programming out loud, much like the protectron. However, sentry bots have a deeper voice, instilling fear in all.
chr_0001cf6e.summary: Sentry Bot is a sentry bot creature or robotic unit in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Level 12, 500 HP). Affiliated with Brotherhood of Steel. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC15a (Citadel Outer Perimeter). Directly connected to quests: Take it Back!.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Sentry bots have two arms equipped with powerful weapons: a minigun or Gatling laser on their right, and a missile launcher on their left. All models have wheeled tripod legs.

They are programmed with an authoritative and professional military personality, in contrast to the "gung-ho" patriotic personality of the Mister Gutsy.

Gameplay attributes:
Sentry bots are the highest-level robots in Fallout 3; they are extremely durable, possessing as much health as a deathclaw but lacking a weak point that could be targeted for additional damage. In fact, their heads are more durable than their torsos, though targeting the head yields a greater chance of a Critical Hit. Like other robots, sentry bots are equipped with a combat inhibitor and will frenzy if it is disabled. Although they are fast, they have a slow turning speed.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Sentry bot:
Sentry bots come in many different guises, distinguishable by their paint, which shows their affiliation: Enclave, Brotherhood Outcasts, United States Armed Forces, etc.

Enclave sentry bot:
Significantly darker in appearance, wearing matte black paint and dark red sensors, the Enclave model hosts improved systems. They appear at Raven Rock, as well as alongside certain Enclave squads found in the wasteland. In Broken Steel, they are encountered guarding sections of the Adams Air Force Base.

Strike team sentry bot:
The most expensive option for recruitment in Operation: Anchorage is a winterized minigun variant sentry bot, costing 4 recruitment markers. In addition to the minigun variant, there is a Gatling laser equipped winterized sentry bot which was cut from Operation: Anchorage.

U.S.

sections.title: Notable sentry bots
sections.text: • FO3BS Sparky, found in the mobile base crawler.

chr_0100cf2d.summary: The Chimera is a modified mining rig with a mounted laser cannon, acting as a Chinese battle tank.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Chimeras fought American vertibirds and power armor soldiers during the liberation of Alaska. It was included in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation created by VSS at the behest of General Chase.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Originally, it was a mining rig. The Chinese had refitted the vehicle with long range weapons and reinforced armor.

Gameplay attributes:
The player character may encounter Chimera tanks twice throughout the campaign, a pair off in the distance during The Guns of Anchorage and at the fuel depot during Paving the Way. Only one Chimera is ever actually fought, serving as a miniboss at the fuel depot. Walking into a Chimera while crouching will knock the player character down, causing damage.

Chimera tanks are described as being superior to any American tank available. They are equipped with a unique laser weapon similar to Liberty Prime's eye laser. Chimeras take slightly increased damage when shot in the screws and noticeably increased damage when shot in the cannon or radar antenna.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0100ad4e.summary: Mark I Turret is a security turret creature or robotic unit in Operation: Anchorage (Level 2, 40 HP). Encountered in Operation: Anchorage.

sections.title: Automated turret
sections.text:
Specifications:
Automated turrets come in two distinct variants, differentiated by both the mounting style and ammo type used. The ceiling mounted type is an automatic firearm shooting conventional bullets, whereas floor mounted turrets are energy weapons, firing laser beams similar to those of the laser rifle, but capable of much faster rate of fire. Both varieties have unlimited ammunition. As a rule of thumb, odd numbered turret models are conventional firearms, and even numbered turrets are energy-based.

Gameplay attributes:
Automated turrets are often found in military installations or areas of historical value. Although not too damaging at lower levels, they can be quite deadly if they surprise the Lone Wanderer, or if they are in groups.

sections.title: Alien turret (Mothership Zeta)
sections.text:
Specifications:
Alien turrets are always ceiling-mounted and can be harder to see, due to their much smaller size. They shoot blue energy shots similar to the disintegrator and have an identical barrel design to that of the disintegrator. They fire in rapid salvos of five shots; the individual pulses can be highly damaging and can take a chunk out of the Lone Wanderer's health if they get caught out in the open for too long.

Gameplay attributes:
It is possible to remotely detonate them using nearby switches aboard the Mothership. They explode in a blast of green plasma, similar to a plasma grenade. Like normal turrets, they are unable to shoot directly below them and can be shut down using the Robotics Expert perk if the player character is able to reach them by jumping while crouched.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Mark I:
These can be found in buildings and on bridges and ceilings. A couple are found at Fort Independence. These turrets are often used by organizations such as the Brotherhood Outcasts, but can be found widely across the wasteland. Even raiders use them as sentries. They can be frenzied just like any other turret when the player character cripples the lens.

Mark I (Operation: Anchorage):
These turrets are found throughout Operation: Anchorage, defending various strongholds in round bunkers, just outside the facilities.

Mark II:
These turrets can be found both inside and outside buildings, as well as on bridges. All floor-mounted models have laser weaponry and can be frenzied when their targeting chip is destroyed. Some can be found outside the Citadel.

chr_0100a4e0.summary: Spider drones are robots employed by the Chinese Army in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation in the Fallout 3 add-on Operation: Anchorage.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Before the war, these robots served as mobile landmines for the Chinese army. Their method of attack is to approach enemy targets and simply self-destruct; the explosion acting as a fragmentation mine would. They are only encountered briefly during the quest "Paving the Way."

According to a Chinese terminal entry, the model encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation is designated "spider drone Mk VI prototype" and are air dropped via bombers.

Gameplay attributes:
A Chinese terminal entry advises their own soldiers to be careful around the drones, even though they are configured to only attack Americans. To this effect, one will occasionally see a Chinese soldier fighting one of these on the way to the Chimera armor depot.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: DLC02SpiderMine), Spider Drone is defined as a Robotic Drone in Operation: Anchorage.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 1, 20 HP. Behavioral traits: Aggressive, confidence: foolhardy.

chr_01008cf5.role: U.S. Strike Team, U.S. Army (Anchorage Simulation) — Sentry Bot
chr_01008cf5.summary: Strike team units are commandable allies encountered in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation who replicate the pre-War United States Army soldiers that fought in the Battle of Anchorage in the Sino-American War.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The initial invasion of Alaska by Chinese military forces in 2066 overwhelmed American defenders, and it was not until the deployment of the T-45 power armor the following year that the Chinese advance was halted. As the Chinese military lost the initiative, the situation rapidly deteriorated into trench warfare as neither side was capable of breaking the stalemate and forcing peace terms on the enemy.

Following the liberation of Anchorage, General Constantine Chase commissioned Virtual Strategic Solutions to create a digital simulation based on the final events of the battle for training purposes. The simulation included recreations of the American defenders, with Chase as their battlefield commander.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
During the Operation: Anchorage quest Paving the Way, the player character receives a field promotion from General Chase and gains the ability to command an interactive strike team. The team is initially selected via Patterson's terminal in the U.S. Army field headquarters command tent, by spending recruitment markers given by Lieutenant Morgan; Morgan gives a total of five markers, and up to three units can be selected.

On the terminal, different compositions of the strike team can be selected with respect to the three unit slots and five markers available. Once selected, the team composition is final and cannot be changed again via the terminal. However, units can be dismissed by simply speaking to them, and they can also die during combat.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Strike team infantryman:
A rifleman clad in winterized combat armor with matching helmet who is armed with an R91 assault rifle. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team grenadier:
This soldier wears winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and is armed with a 10mm SMG and five frag grenades. Costs 1 recruitment marker.

Inventory

Strike team missile unit:
Strike team missile units are protected by winterized combat armor with a matching helmet and carry a N99 10mm pistol as well as a missile launcher. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

Inventory

Strike team sniper:
Like the other human team members, snipers wear winterized combat armor with a matching helmet. Their armament consists of a trench knife and a sniper rifle. Costs 2 recruitment markers.

These turrets are often used by organizations such as the Brotherhood Outcasts, but can be found widely across the wasteland. Even raiders use them as sentries. They can be frenzied just like any other turret when the player character cripples the lens.

Mark I (Operation: Anchorage):
These turrets are found throughout Operation: Anchorage, defending various strongholds in round bunkers, just outside the facilities.

Mark II:
These turrets can be found both inside and outside buildings, as well as on bridges. All floor-mounted models have laser weaponry and can be frenzied when their targeting chip is destroyed. Some can be found outside the Citadel.

chr_01003387.summary: The Chimera is a modified mining rig with a mounted laser cannon, acting as a Chinese battle tank.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Chimeras fought American vertibirds and power armor soldiers during the liberation of Alaska. It was included in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation created by VSS at the behest of General Chase.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Originally, it was a mining rig. The Chinese had refitted the vehicle with long range weapons and reinforced armor.

Gameplay attributes:
The player character may encounter Chimera tanks twice throughout the campaign, a pair off in the distance during The Guns of Anchorage and at the fuel depot during Paving the Way. Only one Chimera is ever actually fought, serving as a miniboss at the fuel depot. Walking into a Chimera while crouching will knock the player character down, causing damage.

Chimera tanks are described as being superior to any American tank available. They are equipped with a unique laser weapon similar to Liberty Prime's eye laser. Chimeras take slightly increased damage when shot in the screws and noticeably increased damage when shot in the cannon or radar antenna.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Operation: Anchorage encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0200aa38.summary: Trogs are a species of degenerated mutants native to the surrounding area of the Pitt, appearing as enemies and the Fallout 76 update Expeditions: The Pitt.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A trog is the common name for humans that have reached the final stage of infection with the troglodyte degeneration contagion (TDC). Due to the contagion being endemic to the town, approximately 20% of the populace of the Pitt are highly likely to transform into these feral monstrosities, roaming the ruined streets and wrecked buildings while hiding in darkness and attacking any non-trog entities on sight. Studies by Sandra Kundanika have shown that children born in TDC-active areas virtually have a 100% degeneration rate and become feral within weeks of birth.

Trog fledglings are younger, smaller, and weaker than fully grown trogs, but remain stronger than a normal human. When alone, they are easily dispatched, but a larger group can overwhelm prey.

sections.title: Background & Story Role

chr_0300b81e.summary: Mother Curie III, or Curie the Third, is a member of the Church of the Children of Atom and the founder and leader of the Apostles of the Eternal Light.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Mother Curie is from Megaton.

Apostles of the Eternal Light:
In her vision, Atom called upon his flock to seek not Division, but instead "Enlightenment;" she believes that salvation in Eternal Light can only be attained through Atom's supreme and total Enlightenment—in other words, salvation is only possible by taking in radiation and becoming a ghoul, though few are able to surpass the level of Enlightenment and reach Eternal Light (taking in so much radiation that they achieve a visible glow). They see this transformation as a "rebirth" for the suffering so that they no longer fall to starvation, illness, or age, needing only "Atom's Glow" (radiation) to be happy.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• Holy Water: The Lone Wanderer has the choice of persuading Curie to stop distributing the holy water to others, or stopping her by killing her and her followers.

Effects of player's actions:
• Mother Curie III appears as a hostile feral ghoul reaver if Megaton is blown up after starting Holy Water. According to Brother Gerard, who will also be transformed into a ghoul, this occurs because he and Mother Curie are preaching in Megaton when the bomb goes off.
• Although armed with a weapon, Mother Curie III is a peaceful character and does not become hostile if one kills Brother Gerard in order to enter the monastery, or by way of antagonizing speech options. If threatened, she states that she expected some form of religious persecution and that she refuses to respond to violence with violence.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Wasteland. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0300ad89.summary: Albino Radscorpion is a radscorpion creature or robotic unit in Broken Steel (Level 13, 1500 HP). Encountered in Broken Steel.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
Radscorpions are not only armed with two powerful claws but also have a venomous sting that can kill victims if not treated quickly. Since they are indigenous to desert environments, they do not mind brightly-lit environments and will attack anyone in broad daylight as well as at night. Radscorpions can be seen burrowing into the ground from time to time, much like their pre-War counterparts. These burrows are likely where they sleep and take refuge from the harsh conditions of the external environment, such as intense heat and sandstorms.

Gameplay attributes:
Radscorpions will usually attack head-on and then attempt to flank their prey. Unlike other creatures, radscorpions lack a "weak point" that can be targeted for extra damage (such as a "head" for a headshot), which makes V.A.T.S.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Radscorpion:
The most common variety of radscorpion. These venomous predators seem to possess varying speeds, some taking their time and others bolting at top speed. Their size ranges from that of a large dog to small livestock.

Giant radscorpion:
A much larger radscorpion with a much more potent venom. These terrifying creatures can reach incredible sizes, ranging from livestock to a Corvega. The giant radscorpion is commonly encountered in the west and far south of the Capital Wasteland. It is not uncommon to see one turn from the target and back off, only to be joined by another and charge in again. In fact, they seem to operate in pairs most often, only preferring to attack alone when their partner is dead.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Broken Steel encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

Stiggs purchased the robot from a wandering trader named Tinker Joe. He can be identified from other Mister Gutsy robots by his distinctive silver and black paint job and dark red eye sensors. He is one of two robots owned by Stiggs, the other being Sparky.

chr_03008ccf.role: Enclave Combat Robots, Robots, Automated Turrets — Security Turret
chr_03008ccf.summary: Mark VIII Turret is a security turret creature or robotic unit in Broken Steel (Level 9, 300 HP). Affiliated with Enclave Combat Robots, Robots, Automated Turrets. Encountered in Broken Steel.

sections.title: Automated turret
sections.text:
Specifications:
Automated turrets come in two distinct variants, differentiated by both the mounting style and ammo type used. The ceiling mounted type is an automatic firearm shooting conventional bullets, whereas floor mounted turrets are energy weapons, firing laser beams similar to those of the laser rifle, but capable of much faster rate of fire. Both varieties have unlimited ammunition. As a rule of thumb, odd numbered turret models are conventional firearms, and even numbered turrets are energy-based.

Gameplay attributes:
Automated turrets are often found in military installations or areas of historical value. Although not too damaging at lower levels, they can be quite deadly if they surprise the Lone Wanderer, or if they are in groups.

sections.title: Alien turret (Mothership Zeta)
sections.text:
Specifications:
Alien turrets are always ceiling-mounted and can be harder to see, due to their much smaller size. They shoot blue energy shots similar to the disintegrator and have an identical barrel design to that of the disintegrator. They fire in rapid salvos of five shots; the individual pulses can be highly damaging and can take a chunk out of the Lone Wanderer's health if they get caught out in the open for too long.

Gameplay attributes:
It is possible to remotely detonate them using nearby switches aboard the Mothership. They explode in a blast of green plasma, similar to a plasma grenade. Like normal turrets, they are unable to shoot directly below them and can be shut down using the Robotics Expert perk if the player character is able to reach them by jumping while crouched.

sections.title: Variants

They can be frenzied just like any other turret when the player character cripples the lens.

Mark I (Operation: Anchorage):
These turrets are found throughout Operation: Anchorage, defending various strongholds in round bunkers, just outside the facilities.

Mark II:
These turrets can be found both inside and outside buildings, as well as on bridges. All floor-mounted models have laser weaponry and can be frenzied when their targeting chip is destroyed. Some can be found outside the Citadel.

chr_03007e36.role: Apostles of the Eternal Light — Feral Ghoul
chr_03007e36.summary: Sun of Atom is a feral ghoul creature or robotic unit in Broken Steel (Level 9, 240 HP). Affiliated with Apostles of the Eternal Light. Found primarily around Eternal Light Monastery. Directly connected to quests: Holy Water.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Once a man, this feral glowing one is the son of Mother Curie III, leader of the Apostles of the Eternal Light. While meditating in Springvale, Mother Curie was approached by four members of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel on their water delivery run to Megaton. When they found her there, she told them where she was from, and they gave her some crates of Aqua Pura and told her to share the water with her people. In her religious stupor, she took this to be a vision from Atom himself, interpreting the Brotherhood members as "armored angels" of Atom who gave her the water to be "blessed" with radiation to spread the cult's message of "enlightenment" to everyone. In their eyes, this is a humanitarian mission, bringing salvation and "warmth" to the suffering people of the wasteland.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• If the Lone Wanderer attacks anyone in the monastery or engages in certain dialogue options with Mother Curie III, Sun of Atom will turn hostile.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Eternal Light Monastery. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_03006520.role: Apostles of the Eternal Light — Feral Ghoul
chr_03006520.summary: Atom's Champion is a non-hostile feral ghoul reaver found in the Holy Light Monastery. Atom's Champion is one of two non-hostile feral ghouls in the monastery, the other being Sun of Atom.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This feral ghoul reaver is being used by the Apostles of the Eternal Light as an example of one who has given himself over to the Eternal Light and achieved salvation and Enlightenment. Atom's Champion is considered by Mother Curie III to be an exemplary disciple of her sect of the Church of the Children of Atom cult, who has taken in enough Atom's Glow to be transformed rather than die from radiation poisoning. However, the fact that he does not rip everyone in the monastery apart is not because of divine grace, but only due to remnants of functioning brain matter. Atom's Champion does not have any blood relation to Curie III, unlike Sun of Atom, who was created from Curie's own son.

quotes: Sentry bots possess an authoritative array of speech programming, though it mainly expresses its current programming out loud, much like the protectron. However, sentry bots have a deeper voice, instilling fear in all.
chr_030064d6.summary: Presidential Metro Sentinal Unit is a sentry bot creature or robotic unit in Broken Steel (Level 12, 500 HP). Affiliated with Robots. Found primarily around Presidential Metro.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Sentry bots have two arms equipped with powerful weapons: a minigun or Gatling laser on their right, and a missile launcher on their left. All models have wheeled tripod legs.

They are programmed with an authoritative and professional military personality, in contrast to the "gung-ho" patriotic personality of the Mister Gutsy.

Gameplay attributes:
Sentry bots are the highest-level robots in Fallout 3; they are extremely durable, possessing as much health as a deathclaw but lacking a weak point that could be targeted for additional damage. In fact, their heads are more durable than their torsos, though targeting the head yields a greater chance of a Critical Hit. Like other robots, sentry bots are equipped with a combat inhibitor and will frenzy if it is disabled. Although they are fast, they have a slow turning speed.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Sentry bot:
Sentry bots come in many different guises, distinguishable by their paint, which shows their affiliation: Enclave, Brotherhood Outcasts, United States Armed Forces, etc.

Enclave sentry bot:
Significantly darker in appearance, wearing matte black paint and dark red sensors, the Enclave model hosts improved systems. They appear at Raven Rock, as well as alongside certain Enclave squads found in the wasteland. In Broken Steel, they are encountered guarding sections of the Adams Air Force Base.

Strike team sentry bot:
The most expensive option for recruitment in Operation: Anchorage is a winterized minigun variant sentry bot, costing 4 recruitment markers. In addition to the minigun variant, there is a Gatling laser equipped winterized sentry bot which was cut from Operation: Anchorage.

U.S.

chr_0300626e.summary: Vault 87 super mutants are hostile creatures encountered in Fallout 3 and its add-ons Broken Steel and Mothership Zeta. Distinct from the creations of the Master encountered in New California, these mutants were created from FEV experiments by Vault 87 scientists shortly after the Great War. By 2277, they have escaped the Vault and pose a serious threat to the inhabitants of the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
These super mutants were created in the Evolutionary Experimentation Program, an experiment assigned to Vault 87. This modified strain of FEV was used to create these mutants and resulted in a new strain of super mutant which, in addition to becoming sterile, grow larger and stronger as they age. Their routine behavior included raiding to kidnap people for conversion with the EEP mutagen.

Their inability to reproduce (possibly bolstered by the FEV batch and/or human procreation instincts) led to an obsession with preserving their species. They attempt to capture live humans as often as possible, to infect them with FEV, or "green stuff," at Vault 87.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
The inferior FEV strain used at Vault 87 retains the recursive growth patterns characteristic to FEV but has a different effect, which may be also linked to how the infection was performed in the labs. Test subjects were exposed a single time to FEV in isolated chambers, where the virus was deployed as airborne particulate. When exposed, phenotypical changes occur within three days and include increased muscle mass, changes in skeletal structure and atrophy of all visible sexual characteristics, creating a uniform body shape devoid of genitalia or another sexual dimorphism. At ten days, skin pigmentation becomes a mixture of yellow and green, while its thickness and resistance to radiation and other environmental hazards rapidly increases.

However, a key problem with this batch is that the mutation often does not stop.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Super mutant:
These are the youngest and weakest of the Capital Wasteland super mutants. They are usually encountered in groups of two or three, led by the strongest one. Regular super mutants have almost twice as much health as most standard human non-player characters, but this is somewhat offset by their lack of body armor, thus they are a fairly easy opponent for mid-level player characters. Some of their prime locations are the GNR building plaza, the Mall, the Capitol Building, the Statesman Hotel, the National Archives and Falls Church. Four can also be found aboard Mothership Zeta in stasis chambers in the cryo lab. Freeing them will prompt their hostility to both the player character and the aliens.

chr_03003b33.summary: Brahmin is a brahmin creature or robotic unit in Broken Steel (Level 1, 40 HP). Affiliated with Brahmin. Found primarily around DC Ruins Sector DC09b (The Mall — Northwest). Directly connected to quests: Protecting the Water Way.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Most brahmin have been domesticated throughout the years since the Great War. However, some can still be seen wandering through the wasteland. Brahmin are used primarily for meat and milk. Their hides are also valuable, because they are tanned to make leather. Traders often use domesticated brahmin as pack animals. The Brotherhood of Steel uses them to distribute clean water to the wasteland inhabitants after Project Purity has launched.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
It would seem that over time, radiation has transformed brahmin into conjoined organisms which are a single creature. As a result of the constant exposure to radiation, these formerly normal cows have sprouted a second, independent head. Brahmin also have eight stomachs. When talking to Rose, it is revealed that male brahmin also have four testicles. Their skin has turned a toasty, dusty rust color from the fallout exposure and their horns have in turn become a dirty brown. Their udders have also grown abnormally large, almost dragging on the ground. Brahmin milk is used by Moira Brown as part of a homemade radiation poisoning remedy, along with magnets and "a few happy thoughts."

Gameplay attributes:
Brahmin are low-level creatures and are little more than a nuisance at the beginning of the game if a hostile one is even found.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Brahmin:
Brahmin are the only bovine in the game, mostly seen in makeshift settlements like the Republic of Dave, Megaton and Arefu. They are also found just outside the Regulator HQ and even as pack brahmin, carrying goods. They will seldom be encountered as enemies. If hostile brahmin are found, they can easily be killed.

Mad brahmin:
Mad brahmin are brahmin which have gone insane. Unlike regular brahmin, they will be hostile to the Lone Wanderer without the Animal Friend perk. However, having the same health as a normal brahmin, they are fairly easy to kill. Mad brahmin can only be found as part of a random encounter in a herd of two to five.

chr_03001fcc.summary: Liberty Prime, later upgraded and renamed to Liberty Prime Mark II, is a giant combat robot originally constructed by the Strategic Arms Division of the United States Army as a superweapon to achieve victory against China in the Sino-American War. It was intended to be deployed in combat as the spearhead of the liberation of Anchorage, Alaska from PLA occupation, but never saw deployment due to its lack of a suitable power source.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Pre-war origins:
In response to the occupation of Anchorage, Alaska by the Chinese People's Liberation Army during the Sino-American War, the United States Army contracted RobCo Industries, General Atomics International and Mass Fusion Confident that the project would soon yield result, General Chase publicly confirmed in June 2072 that the U.S. Army was working with General Atomics and RobCo to create a superweapon meant to establish dominance of the United States on the Alaskan front. Propaganda posters also purported the existence of a Chinese super robot, dubbed Warmachine, and called for the United States to build its own.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: DLC03LibertyPrime), Liberty Prime is defined as a Robot — Liberty Prime in Broken Steel. Marked as essential (cannot be killed during normal gameplay until plot flags allow). Faction memberships: Brotherhood of Steel, Enclave. Appears in or relates to quests: Death From Above. Linked story events: Destruction of Liberty Prime, Liberty Prime March & Project Purity Activation.

chr_0300103e.summary: Feral ghouls (also known as mindless zombies, ghoul crazies, feral necrotic post-humans, or simply ferals) are ghouls that have lost their upper faculties and ability to reason, regressing into basic instinct and behaving more like vicious wild animals attacking any non-ghouls they encounter regardless of former ties like friends or family.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Biology:
The degeneration into a feral state (referred to as ferocious post-necrotic dystrophy) is not fully understood. It is known that it is a result of a degeneration of the brain (which is not affected by the regenerative mutation of the spinal cord) and emerges following the atrophy of higher brain functions, accompanied by an increased level of aggression and appetite. When the loss of capacity for thought is complete, a ghoul is considered feral. The factors that may cause a ghoul to enter this state are unclear, but anti-social or isolated ghouls may be more susceptible to it. Exposure to intense radiation may also be a factor; feral ghouls have no body heat and emit lethal levels of radiation, indicating that feral ghouls are for all intents and purposes dead, their functions sustained only by their high irradiation.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Feral ghoul:
TV series article: Feral ghoul (TV series)
Feral ghouls (also known as mindless ghouls, ghoul crazies or zombies) are the basic feral ghoul variant, wearing only a pair of tattered shorts and noticeably weaker than standard human opponents, they are easily dispatched with one or two headshots from any decent weapon or a solid hit from a decent melee or unarmed weapon. Despite their shrill noise and remarkable speed, they are only truly a threat when they have the advantage of numbers, or when the player character is at a low level. Some feral ghouls come in different colors as well as different types. The colors are different depending on how the human looked before turning into a feral ghoul.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Broken Steel encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_040116f6.summary: Feral ghouls are creatures found in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. They are ghouls who have lost their sanity and ability to reason due to radiation, making them aggressive to anyone who is not another ghoul. Feral ghouls are partially held by many humans to be responsible for the discrimination shown towards all ghouls, whether or not they have retained their mental faculties.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Gameplay attributes:
Feral ghouls often give a loud, low-pitched screech or growl before attacking enemies. This can be helpful in dark places or areas with objects blocking the Lone Wanderer's view, especially in the metro system and the Dunwich Building. As with normal ghouls, ferals are entirely resistant to radiation. This makes a glowing one especially dangerous when encountered with regular ferals, as they constantly emit radiation that will heal the ghouls within the surrounding area.

Feral ghouls attack with no strategy. They rush foes in one massive onslaught. At first, they attack with a running over-the-head strike. When close to an enemy, they will swipe at them horizontally or diagonally.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Feral ghoul:
The basic feral ghoul variant in Fallout 3 wears only a pair of tattered shorts (or ripped pants) and is noticeably weaker than standard human opponents. They are easily defeated with one or two headshots or a solid hit with a decent weapon in close-quarters combat. Despite their noisy shrieks and remarkable speed, they are not much of a threat unless they outnumber their enemies.

Some feral ghouls come in different colors as well as different types. Some are a "healthy" pink color while others are a grimy gray color. Their skin colors are different depending on what ethnicity they were prior to ghoulification.

Feral ghouls can drop rare pass cards in blue and red colors, with a 1.25% chance of dropping a given color of pass card.

chr_04010add.summary: Vicious Dog is a dog creature or robotic unit in Point Lookout (Level 3, 60 HP). Affiliated with Wasteland Dogs. Found primarily around Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Though 200 years have passed since the Great War, dogs have stayed generally unaltered by radiation. Dogs are a favored pet for traveling merchants as they provide both companionship and protection. As a result of the radiation, most dogs have lost their fur and have slightly mottled skin, but some have retained their fur coats and appear somewhat normal.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
Dogs are quadrupedal canines that can run at incredible speeds, allowing them to chase down prey. While running, they use their long tails to keep their balance. They are carnivorous and have sharp, pointy teeth designed to rip into flesh.

Gameplay attributes:
Dogs are usually encountered in packs of four to six. To low level characters, this could mean trouble since a pack can easily overwhelm and surround them. To higher level characters, they are little more than a nuisance, yet can still be difficult to put down as a result of their erratic and agile running patterns. Vicious dogs (and their variants) are always hostile unless the Lone Wanderer possesses the Animal Friend perk.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Raider guard dog:
Raider guard dogs fight alongside their masters, the raiders. Since they are trained as guard dogs, they are very attentive and can spot threats easier than many other creatures. Raider guard dogs will tend to run at targets they find hostile, alerting the raiders of their presence. They are still affected by the Animal Friend perk, but will not attack raiders.

Scavenger's dog:
These dogs are found around scavenger's encampments and will be friendly to others as long as they do not act aggressively to them or their master. These dogs have slightly less Hit Points and attack damage than vicious dogs.

There is a Karma loss for killing a scavenger's dog, as well as the scavenger themselves and/or the scavenger's brahmin if they have one.

chr_0401034d.summary: Mole Rat is a mole rat creature or robotic unit in Point Lookout (Level 3, 40 HP). Affiliated with Mole Rats. Encountered in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mole rats are mutated rodents that are much larger than their ancestral species prior to the Great War. They have survived as a species by burrowing underground where the soil protected them from direct nuclear explosions. However, they were still greatly mutated by the subsequent radioactive fallout, increasing their size and aggression. A number of people in the wastes have been known to train and keep them as pets.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Biology:
Mole rats exhibit no signs of increased intelligence when compared to those alive pre-War. Their incisors show increased enamel and dentin growth, making them razor-sharp. In addition to increased aggressiveness, they are also highly resistant to pain. They are generally found in packs of three to four, but are occasionally encountered in pairs or even by themselves. They are often witnessed standing on their hind legs and sniffing the air, allowing them to smell any approaching predators. They occasionally scratch at the ground, attempting to dig a burrow.

Gameplay attributes:
Mole rats are very aggressive but may retreat if severely outmatched. They fight for their food by biting at their prey with their large incisors.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Found throughout the Capital Wasteland.
• FO3PL Found in Point Lookout.

chr_0401034b.summary: A bloatfly is a mutated pest resembling an oversized biting horse or common housefly, often found in Appalachia, the Capital Wasteland, the Commonwealth and the Mojave Wasteland.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
An example of the mutations caused by the Great War, the bloatfly is an evolution of either the Musca domestica (common housefly) or Tabanus genera of biting horse fly.

Biology:
The standard bloatfly has a green and brown carapace and is significantly larger and more tenacious than its predecessors. Its size inhibits previous flight characteristics and agility, making it impossible to feed like pre-War horse flies did. Instead, it uses its engorged stinger and pupae gestating within its abdomen to incapacitate prey. Bloatflies can resort to scavenging in situations where prey or other sources of sustenance are scarce. It adapted to its enlarged size with a unique gland that enables it to balance and maintain speed despite its size.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: Bloatflies attack at long range by peppering their prey with spine-bedecked larva launched from its abdomen. They tend to attack in groups, and may pose an additional threat based on their ability to attack from a distance.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Active across Point Lookout encounter zones. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_04011163.summary: Point Lookout tribals are characters that inhabit Point Lookout's Ark & Dove Cathedral in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Point Lookout tribals wander the cathedral, cultivating punga and meditating. However, these normally peaceful cultists can be very brutal when told to be so. They assault the Calvert Mansion because the Transcendent One instructed them to. They are proficient with improvised melee weapons but are also capable with firearms.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Gameplay attributes:
Tribals are surprisingly tough opponents; even the weakest of them are on par with a Brotherhood of Steel paladin in terms of durability and combat skill, and the highest-level tribals exceed even super mutant brutes and super mutant masters. Their tribal garb serves as mediocre, but still functional armor. In contrast, named tribals, including their leader Jackson, are standard human non-player characters, and are relatively easily killed.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Interactions overview:
Note: Tribals will only have a finger on their corpse when they are assaulting the Calvert Mansion and after attaching the cogwave jammer to the Ferris wheel during Thought Control.

Quests:
• The Local Flavor: Tribals will attempt to burn the Calvert Mansion to the ground.
• Thought Control: If the Lone Wanderer decides to put the cogwave jammer on the Ferris wheel, the Point Lookout tribals will attack them while on the boardwalk.

Effects of player's actions:
If the player character sided with Desmond during Thought Control, Point Lookout tribals will be permanently hostile toward them.

chr_0400fcad.summary: Mirelurks are giant mutated crustaceans living in the Potomac River watershed in 2277. They can be commonly found together with the reptilian mirelurk kings. Fallout 3 initially featured four types of mirelurks, with two more added in the Point Lookout add-on.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Gameplay attributes:
All mirelurks, except for kings, are protected by a thick shell that is difficult to penetrate, even with powerful ballistic weapons such as the Gauss rifle. The face, however, is unarmored but presents a small target. Furthermore, when charging, a mirelurk will lower its head to protect this area. However, the face will inevitably be exposed once the creature commences close combat. Extremities are also more vulnerable than the rest of the body, though not as much as the face. Low-level characters will find mirelurks to be among their deadliest enemies.

Mirelurks are extremely territorial, and they will attack any trespasser on sight and run it down relentlessly. They also take advantage of their strength in numbers, often breaking away to solicit support if there are additional mirelurks in the area.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Mirelurk:
The most common type of mirelurk has a whitish-gray shell, is about a head shorter than a normal human, and walks slightly slower. Mirelurks fight with their claws and lack ranged attacks. At close range they can charge forward in a brief burst of speed for a headbutt, which also makes it impossible to target their face. However, their face is most vulnerable in the seconds after a headbutt, when their 'head' is raised.

‡ Due to their hard shells, shots on the torso only do half of the normal damage.

Mirelurk hunter:
A much larger, greenish-brown colored version of mirelurk. In addition to their two main arms, hunters also have two pairs of small, segmented appendages growing out of their chest which they may attack with, but do so rarely.

sections.title: Related quests
sections.text:
• The Wasteland Survival Guide
• Oasis
• Agatha's Song
• The Nuka-Cola Challenge

chr_0400ecf9.summary: Ruzka is a unique yao guai, living in the far northwest corner of Point Lookout. Ruzka is, in fact, the only yao guai found in the add-on, in a small alcove at the end of a small inlet channel, nearby the jet crash site and the sacred bog.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Ruzka the Wonder Bear was the former star attraction of Point Lookout, known for her ball dancing abilities. After the Great War, Ruzka would completely lose her domestic behaviors over the next two hundred years, turning into a feral yao guai. She resides in the remote northwestern corner of Point Lookout. Amusing herself with the big red ball dating back to her circus days and preying on the unwary swampfolk, Ruzka is incredibly dangerous to anyone who happens upon her lair.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Other interactions:
• Ruzka is hostile and will attack on sight unless the Lone Wanderer has the Animal Friend perk. She is 20% larger than a regular yao guai.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Point Lookout. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0400e1a1.summary: Robobrain Sentry is a robot — robobrain creature or robotic unit in Point Lookout (Level 1, 20 HP). Affiliated with Robots. Found primarily around Underground Lab.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Gameplay attributes:
Robobrains are a fairly common sight in the Capital Wasteland. They can be found in many abandoned buildings, in use by groups such as the Enclave and the Brotherhood Outcasts, or even simply wandering the wastes.

There are three variants of the Robobrain. The first, and most common, is the military variant used by the U.S. Army, recognizable by its green paint scheme with a prominent white serial number stenciled on the front. They are more commonly used by various factions. Less common is the gray-colored civilian model, seen wandering the wasteland at random. The Point Lookout add-on introduces the final variant, the Robobrain sentry, which is identical in appearance to the civilian model but has significantly more health.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Robobrain:
The standard Robobrain variant. Usually found roaming the wasteland or in some pre-War buildings, they are often hostile to the player. A few non-hostile Robobrains are also found in Vault 112.

U.S. Army Robobrain:
This variant of Robobrain is often found in former U.S. Army buildings, such as Fort Constantine and the National Guard depot, but are also encountered wandering the wasteland.

Enclave Robobrain:
A variant of Robobrain used by Enclave forces. Usually roaming the wasteland with an Enclave patrol or in specific Enclave-inhabited areas.

Robobrain sentry (Point Lookout):
A unique variant of Robobrain found in the St. Aubin Medical Facility, where they guard and maintain Professor Calvert and defend his facility from intruders.

sections.title: Notable Robobrains
sections.text: • Masterbrain, located in the Vault-Tec headquarters administration.

chr_0400c1e7.summary: Geri is a dog residing in the Calvert Mansion in Point Lookout, acting as a companion of the ghoul Desmond Lockheart. He appears.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
For years, Desmond has had Geri and his other dog Freki, eventually training them to be his attack dogs. Geri was the abused ward of a group of raiders before being saved by Desmond, who later tracked down the raiders and fed them alive to mole rats. Geri and Freki's loyalty and obedience have earned them both the rare honor of being among the few that Desmond trusts and cares about in the post-nuclear world.

At one point, the dogs chased off Nadine after she wandered too close to the mansion grounds, causing her to stay away when the Point Lookout tribals' latest assault commenced shortly before the Lone Wanderer's arrival on the Duchess Gambit.

sections.title: Daily schedule
sections.text: Along with Freki, Geri patrols the foyer and stairs of the mansion.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Effects of player's actions:
• The Local Flavor: The dogs appear assisting in fighting against the tribals invading the mansion.
• Thought Control: After meeting with Desmond following the destruction of Calvert Mansion, he states that Freki and Geri were caught in the blast and killed.

chr_0400a56c.summary:
Mirelurk is a commonly used term referring to a range of mutated aquatic species endemic to the Eastern Seaboard, particularly the Capital Wasteland, the Commonwealth and Appalachia.

A similar term, lakelurk, is used to refer to species in the Colorado watershed in the Mojave Wasteland.

First introduced in Fallout 3, they have appeared in every Fallout game since, based on crustaceans or similar species, though not fish.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mirelurks have the dubious distinction of being one of the first radioactive mutants to emerge into the world, as a result of widespread radioactive pollution of the environment by United States megacorporations, such as Poseidon Energy and General Atomics. Environmental organizations such as the Nahant Oceanological Society, dedicated to saving the oceans, attempted a variety of last-ditch efforts to raise awareness of this problem and encourage radical action to curtail environmental destruction at the hands of reckless corporations. However, their efforts were in vain. Ignored by authorities, to the point where they refused to even take their phone calls (as was the case with the Boston Port Authority), they attempted to garner attention by reporting the situation to the Galaxy News Network.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
The social structure of mirelurk species resembles a caste system, with intelligent mirelurk kings and the giant mirelurk queens at the top.

Mirelurk:
One of the most common variants of the mirelurk, Scylla serrata horrendus (a name used by both the Enclave and the Lone Wanderer) is the result of mixing between horseshoe and blue crabs.

Their most noticeable feature is the large, chitinous shell that provides excellent resistance to firearms, melee weapons, and even ray guns. Soft body parts, such as their faces and sections of their abdomen, are much less resistant.

Crab mirelurks instinctively know how to protect themselves with their shell. When faced with prey that can attack them at long range, a crab mirelurk will lower its head to cover its body with the chitinous shell, greatly increasing its ability to survive.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: Cellar, Blackdamp Shaft. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0400732e.summary: Protectron is a robot — protectron creature or robotic unit in Point Lookout (Level 3, 75 HP). Affiliated with Robots. Found primarily around Chinese Intelligence Bunker. Directly connected to quests: The Velvet Curtain.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Many Protectrons were commissioned by the U.S. Army before the Great War of 2077. They are painted a dark olive drab with a white star on their chest. These mechanized soldiers still wander the wastes, attacking everything from radroaches to Brotherhood Outcasts. The Pitt adds a new variety of Protectron called the "factory Protectron", which lacks a glass dome but possesses a single ocular lens and a cage around the combat inhibitor. The top of where the dome would be appears to be made to look like a construction hard-hat and the body has a yellow coloration. Broken Steel adds "Enclave Protectrons," which appear to be much newer, with red glass domes and a polished steel-gray finish. A special red-painted Protectron also appears at the House of Wares in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Protectrons have a glass dome on top of their heads that acts as an ocular lens that allows the Protectron to scan its surroundings and act accordingly. This glass dome also houses a laser emitter that shoots a high-powered laser beam. The same type of laser is mounted in both of the Protectron's "hands/claws". Although Protectrons are rather slow and ponderous, their upper body can swivel up to about 90 degrees to either side before having to step into a different position, which means that they can easily keep track of their target.

All Protectrons come with a combat inhibitor mounted on their back that allows them to selectively target opponents, depending on pre-programmed guidelines. The combat inhibitor is generally left exposed, making it easy to disable when approaching a Protectron from behind.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Protectron:
Both operational and destroyed protectrons can be found throughout the wasteland.

Metro Protectron:
Metro Protectrons are found in many metro stations. When approached, they will ask the Lone Wanderer for a metro ticket. If they possess one, then it will be automatically taken from the player character's inventory and the Protectron will remain friendly, continuing to walk around the metro station attacking any enemies. Otherwise, the Protectron will turn hostile. On the Red and Blue metros in D.C., the associated red and blue pass cards serve this purpose. Metro Protectrons have the same stats as the standard Protectrons, despite their mundane functions.

Nuka-Cola security:
This model of Protectron is only found active on the Nuka-Cola plant's factory floor.

chr_04006646.summary: Freki is a dog residing in the Calvert Mansion in Point Lookout, acting as a companion of the ghoul Desmond Lockheart. He appears.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
For years, Desmond has had Freki and his other dog Geri, eventually training them to become his attack dogs. While Geri was the abused ward of a group of raiders before being saved by Desmond, Freki's past is unclear. Regardless, Freki and Geri's loyalty and obedience have earned them both the rare honor of being among the few that Desmond trusts and cares about in the post-nuclear world.

At one point, the dogs chased off Nadine after she wandered too close to the mansion grounds, causing her to stay away when the Point Lookout tribals' latest assault commenced shortly before the Lone Wanderer's arrival on the Duchess Gambit.

• Thought Control: After meeting with Desmond following the destruction of the mansion, he states that Freki and Geri were caught in the blast and killed.

chr_0500d2e3.summary: Alien is a alien (zeta) creature or robotic unit in Mothership Zeta (Level 3, 25 HP). Encountered in Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Origins:
The aliens aboard mothership Zeta have been abducting humans and other creatures for cryonic preservation and experimentation, as well as collecting man-made objects for study. Many of these abducted humans end up dead on lab tables with missing limbs or turned into abominations; others remained cryonically preserved in their cryo lab or kept imprisoned in cells for future use.

The aliens' abductions have occurred for centuries, since at least the late 1560s to early 1600s, as their captives are known to have included Toshiro Kago, a samurai from feudal Japan of that time; as well as Andrew Endicott, a resident of Salem, Massachusetts in 1697.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The aliens, known as Zetans, are relatively small, humanoid beings with wrinkled green-yellowish skin. Their bodies, elongated with a long torso, are lean. Their legs are shorter and jointed differently than a normal human and their limbs are also proportionally different than a normal humanoid. They also display no body hair of any kind. Their humerus and femurs are the same lengths as their forearms and tibias, and they have a small hunch on the top of their back at shoulder level. Their long, thick neck and large head lean slightly forward.

All Zetans have no noticeable outer ears or noses, instead only having small orifices for ears and nostrils. Their heads are large and have mouths with no teeth and a light green tongue. They have large opaque black eyes with no discernible iris or pupil.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Alien:
Aliens wearing the white skin tight crinkled space suits and black boots are the ones most commonly seen aboard Mothership Zeta. They act as the common enemy and will always be hostile. They are found in large numbers, with very few drones with them. Aliens may have inertia suppression fields, depending on the player character's level, despite being described as "frail/weak" they may take numerous bullets to kill even without their shields.

Aliens have three outfits, all without gloves, and differing only cosmetically:
• The first outfit is a crinkled white skintight space suit with black boots and two black stripes near the wrists.

chr_0500c2f9.summary:
Being aware of the enemy

Abominations are creatures encountered on board Mothership Zeta in 2277.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The results of the alien crew's genetic experiments on human abductees, abominations are humans who have been irreversibly transformed by combining their DNA with that of the Zetans themselves. The reasons behind their creation are left unspecified. Abominations are first seen in the experimentation lab, in five small chambers with white force field doors. Two abominations are also seen dead on lab tables, with an alien worker standing near one body.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Abominations are tall, lanky humanoid with black eyes and dozens of thin orange veins visible on its body beneath its light green skin. An abomination's physique is a noticeable mix between human and Zetan anatomy, such as their hands bearing five jointed digits instead of three suction-cupped tentacles, and an enlarged cranium sitting atop a long, muscular neck. Mentally, they are comparable to feral ghouls, unable to communicate other than in gurgling growls and screams, and completely primal and animalistic, pointing and screaming at the same time, and then attacking anyone without mercy or hesitation, human or alien. When killed, their bodies contain various items such as alien power modules or alien epoxy. They can also be looted for miscellaneous items like packs of cigarettes, pre-War money, harmonicas or pre-War books.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Abomination:
Abominations can be found in the biological research section of Mothership Zeta. At the highest level, they have the same heath as deathclaws and can easily take away chunks of the player character's heath.

quotes: "'*Calm alien speech*" — Alien captain
"'*Alien speech*" — Alien worker
chr_0500c0c8.summary: Alien Worker is a alien (zeta) creature or robotic unit in Mothership Zeta (Level 1, 30 HP). Found primarily around Experimentation Lab.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Origins:
The aliens aboard mothership Zeta have been abducting humans and other creatures for cryonic preservation and experimentation, as well as collecting man-made objects for study. Many of these abducted humans end up dead on lab tables with missing limbs or turned into abominations; others remained cryonically preserved in their cryo lab or kept imprisoned in cells for future use.

The aliens' abductions have occurred for centuries, since at least the late 1560s to early 1600s, as their captives are known to have included Toshiro Kago, a samurai from feudal Japan of that time; as well as Andrew Endicott, a resident of Salem, Massachusetts in 1697.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The aliens, known as Zetans, are relatively small, humanoid beings with wrinkled green-yellowish skin. Their bodies, elongated with a long torso, are lean. Their legs are shorter and jointed differently than a normal human and their limbs are also proportionally different than a normal humanoid. They also display no body hair of any kind. Their humerus and femurs are the same lengths as their forearms and tibias, and they have a small hunch on the top of their back at shoulder level. Their long, thick neck and large head lean slightly forward.

All Zetans have no noticeable outer ears or noses, instead only having small orifices for ears and nostrils. Their heads are large and have mouths with no teeth and a light green tongue. They have large opaque black eyes with no discernible iris or pupil.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Alien:
Aliens wearing the white skin tight crinkled space suits and black boots are the ones most commonly seen aboard Mothership Zeta. They act as the common enemy and will always be hostile. They are found in large numbers, with very few drones with them. Aliens may have inertia suppression fields, depending on the player character's level, despite being described as "frail/weak" they may take numerous bullets to kill even without their shields.

Aliens have three outfits, all without gloves, and differing only cosmetically:
• The first outfit is a crinkled white skintight space suit with black boots and two black stripes near the wrists.

chr_0500ad56.summary: Experimental weapons drones are alien robots encountered in the weapons lab on board of Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Specifications:
Experimental weapons drones are similar in appearance to guardian drones, with exception of the weapons they carry. Aside from their basic drone cannon, each experimental weapons drone also carries a drone cannon Ex-B.

Gameplay attributes:
Experimental weapons drones are initially friendly; they will not attack the player unless attacked first.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: DLC05LvlRobotRangedPodExLab), Experimental Weapons Drone is defined as a Alien Drone (Zeta) in Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 1, 50 HP. Behavioral traits: Aggressive, confidence: foolhardy.

chr_0500aa22.summary: The alien captain is the captain of Mothership Zeta in 2277. He serves as the main antagonist of the add-on.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The alien captain is the leader of the aliens on Mothership Zeta, equipped with the Captain's Sidearm and a shiny blackish-gray, skin-tight space suit with three glowing cyan dots on the left side of his chest. As the ship's captain, he has access to the defensive and offensive systems of Mothership Zeta - the shields and death ray, respectively.

sections.title: Interactions with the player character
sections.text:
Quests:
• This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough...: In the bridge, he is seen sitting calmly in a chair. There, the alien captain must be killed in a battle to seize control of the ship.

Other interactions:
The captain's first appearance is in the observation deck, where he appears as a large orange holographic alien head and will "speak" to the player character, but as with all the other aliens, it is impossible to understand. However, Somah will assume the captain is threatening the human escapees, suggesting that it could even have involved threatening to fire the death ray at the Earth. Upon entering the death ray control room it is shown that the deathray is simply pointed at an empty spot of space instead of Earth.

sections.title: Locations & Equipment
sections.text: Known locations: The Bridge. Carries standard equipment for their faction and level.

chr_0500a9b4.role: Robots, Alien Combat Robots — Alien Drone (Zeta)
chr_0500a9b4.summary: Support Drone is a alien drone (zeta) creature or robotic unit in Mothership Zeta (Level 30, 350 HP). Affiliated with Robots, Alien Combat Robots. Encountered in Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Support drones are tan-colored robots with one glowing yellow eye with a red circle in the middle, as well as two long tan mechanical arms with claw hands with which can perform a swing attack at their enemy. Their torso includes a small black rectangular panel with two dials on it, under which are five small rectangular buttons, with the second button pressed in.

They float in midair, although their single hover platform has no thrusters or any other visible way for them to do so. The hover platform is shaped like an triangle with a wide base, with a glowing red circle in the center.

Gameplay attributes:
Support drones are the simplest model of alien drones and will attack on sight.

sections.title: Background & Story Role
sections.text: In game files (EditorID: DLC05CrRobot6Melee), Support Drone is defined as a Alien Drone (Zeta) in Mothership Zeta. Faction memberships: Robots, Alien Combat Robots.

sections.title: Combat Profile & Behavior
sections.text: Combat baseline: Level 30, 350 HP. Behavioral traits: Very Aggressive, confidence: foolhardy.

"'*Alien speech*" — Alien worker

itm_0007401c.summary: Ledoux's hockey mask is a unique piece of headgear in Fallout 3, worn by Goalie Ledoux, leader of the gang Sudden-Death Overtime.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The unique hockey mask sports a Damage Resistance of 4 and awards the wearer 25 additional AP (equal to the Action Boy/Action Girl perk). It can be repaired with hockey masks.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: As an optional objective of The Nuka-Cola Challenge, Sudden Death Overtime and its leader can be found at the Red Racer factory after obtaining the Nuka-Cola Clear formula from the Nuka-Cola plant. There is no Karma penalty for killing Ledoux and his group. You can also obtain the mask by reverse-pickpocketing better headgear into Ledoux's inventory, then pickpocketing the mask when he puts on the better headgear.

itm_00073fec.summary: Three Dog's head wrap and Three Dog's glasses are unique pieces of clothing worn by Three Dog, DJ of Galaxy News Radio.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
It is slightly darker than the regular headwraps. This headwrap is one of the only two pieces of headwear that provide a Luck bonus, the other is the lucky shades. The headwrap's effects stack with other items that increase Luck, like the lucky shades or the Ranger battle armor.

Any head wrap can be used to repair Three Dog's head wrap, and any eyewear can be used to repair his glasses.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: If one chooses to kill Three Dog, the items can be obtained off his corpse (beware, this has serious consequences). They can also be acquired via reverse-pickpocketing.

itm_00070877.summary: Linden's Outcast Power Armor is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 40.0, value 740 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This set of T-45d power armor was once worn by Branchtender Linden, a former member of the Brotherhood Outcasts. After joining with the reclusive Treeminders to pay the debt he feels owed to them for saving his life, Linden forewent wearing the armor but still retained possession of it.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Linden's armor is a moderately resilient suit of power armor, with the bonus of giving an increase of 5 in the Big Guns skill, an exception to the normal T-45d power armor modifiers.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The armor is located in Oasis, given by Linden after completing the quest Oasis by using Laurel's liniment on Harold's heart. Afterward, one can talk to Linden to receive their reward.

itm_0006c587.summary: Armored Vault 101 Jumpsuit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 12.0, value 180 caps). Linked to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The armored vault jumpsuit is a variant of the Vault-Tec vault suit, modified to better protect its owner in combat. It is a normal vault jumpsuit with several plates, most likely from leather armor, attached to provide additional protection.

The jumpsuit provides bonuses ideal for low level characters as +5 to Energy Weapons and Small Guns are fairly beneficial at the start of the game, where small guns like the 10mm pistol and energy weapons like the laser pistol are quickly obtainable.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The suit can be found in Craterside Supply, Moira's store in Megaton. Moira bestows this gift on the Lone Wanderer for complying with a request to recall how life in Vault 101 was. Moira explains that she made this suit for a girl from the vault around "10 or 12 years ago," but the girl never returned to pick it up, leading Moira to speculate that she may have died.
• It can also be stolen or bought from her for around 180 caps if one chooses to not help her with the Wasteland Survival Guide.
