sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: OutfitUniquePrewarSpring2). Weight: 2.0, Value: 10 caps. Effects: Agility +1.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage

itm_000cb60e.summary: Sleepwear is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 10 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The sexy sleepwear gives a +1 bonus to Charisma.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Sleepwear:
Sleepwear is a piece of Fallout 3 cut clothing. It is identical to sexy sleepwear and can only be retrieved through the console.

Unique variants:
• All-nighter nightwear (Broken Steel)
• Naughty nightwear
• A non-equippable version in Tranquility Lane is known as lacy underwear.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Inside a Pulowski Preservation shelter in Arlington Cemetery.
• Two in Madame Jealle's in L'Enfant.
• On the shelves of Potomac Attire at the Rivet City market.
• On a shelf in the penthouse suite in Tenpenny Tower if the Love machine theme is bought. It does not appear in the Megaton version, however.
• Worn by Dukov, Fantasia, and Cherry in Dukov's Place.
• Worn by Snowflake, the hairdresser in Underworld.
• Worn by the northern shack raider's partner in Evergreen Mills.
• Susan Lancaster wears it when asleep.
• FO3BS Two in a female wastelander camp between the VAPL-58 power station and Kaelyn's Bed & Breakfast (The Waters of Life completed).
• FO3BS One in the Old Olney S. Wilson Building, garden gnome and teddy bear scene.
• FO3TP Lying on a bed in the abandoned apartments of the Uptown area of The Pitt.

itm_000cb60d.summary: Pre-War Casualwear is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 3.0, value 12 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: When equipped, none grant any Damage Resistance or Damage Threshold, but all outfit variants grant a temporary +1 Agility and all hats grants a temporary +1 Perception. Casualwear and relaxedwear can be repaired with other instances of each other, while parkstroller and spring outfits can be repaired of other instances of each other. With the Jury Rigging perk, all outfits can be repaired with instances of all others as well as both light armor and other pieces in the "clothing" and "headgear" categories.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
(Dirty) pre-War casualwear:
The male version consists of a brown sweater-vest and a pair of brown pants while the female version consists of a blue dress and heels.

(Dirty) pre-War relaxedwear:
The male version consists of a green sweater-vest and khaki slacks while the female version consists of a yellowish/brown dress, black belt, and black heels.

(Dirty) pre-War spring outfit:
The male version consists of a red plaid shirt and brown pants while the female version consists of a pink dress with red heels.

(Dirty) pre-War parkstroller outfit:
The male version consists of a gray short-sleeved button-up shirt and blue jeans while the female version consists of a greenish-yellow dress and heels.

sections.title: Headwear
sections.text:
Pre-War hat:
A worn brown leather hat.
• It can be found in most homes of any given non-player character.
• Can also be found in the inventory of any random merchant that sells apparel.
• Many of the Omerta thugs wear them, including Big Sal.
• In Goodsprings there are two - one in Doc Mitchell's house, one can be bought from Chet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.
• In one of the motel rooms of El Rey Motel.

Pre-War baseball cap:
A red baseball cap with a brim in the front.
• Can be found on the corpse south of Goodsprings laying on the cliff visited during Barton the Fink
• Can appear being worn by Powder Gangers

Pre-War bonnet:
A pre-War woman's bonnet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.

itm_000cb60b.summary: Merc Cruiser Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 12.0, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: They come in several variants with different appearances but identical stats. Each variant can be repaired using any of the other merc outfits, with one exception.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Merc adventurer outfit:
Merc adventurer outfits can be looted from several non-player characters such as Nathan and Billy Creel, both in Megaton, Dave in the Republic of Dave, Brock and Shrapnel, both in Rivet City, Bittercup in Big Town and Justin (The Family) in Meresti Metro station. It is sold by Moira in Megaton and Bannon at Potomac Attire. It can also be found in some footlockers and storage.

The appearance of the male variant is a large black vest with a red long-sleeved undershirt and black pants. The female variant is the same though it is short-sleeved and exposes the midriff. The collar of the male variant has three teeth on a string, worn like a necklace. On the female variant, there is an 8-ball patch stitched on the left sleeve. It also has spurs on the boots.

itm_000cb603.summary: The Chinese jumpsuit and the Chinese commando hat are pieces of clothing in Fallout 3. The Communist commander outfit can be considered a high definition recreation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The basic People's Liberation Army uniform is a single piece jumpsuit, whose design is based on the Mao suit. It has four large front pockets, arranged symmetrically, the Chinese flag over the upper right pocket and is typically worn together with a large leather belt, shoulder belt, and a commando hat.

The accompanying commando hat is an ushanka style hat with the ear and neck flaps tied up, displaying the insignia of Communist China in the centre of the front face. Jumpsuits seen in America carry the insignia of the Chinese Iron Army on the right sleeve and have two red stars on the collar lapels.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The jumpsuit is a decorative piece of armor, with half the DR provided by the starting Vault 101 security armor and low item hit points.

Unique variants:
Jumpsuits
• FO3OA Winterized Chinese jumpsuit (non-playable)
• FO3OA General Jingwei's uniform (non-playable)
Hat

• FO3OA General Jingwei's uniform (non-playable)

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Chinese jumpsuit:

Dirty Chinese jumpsuit:
• Rivet City: The dirty Chinese jumpsuit can be purchased at Potomac Attire.
• Taft Tunnel under the Jefferson Memorial: Found at abandoned infiltrator listening posts.
• Mama Dolce's: Looted from Chinese remnants.
• Dead pilot random encounter: One of these can also be found on a dead Chinese commando. A radio signal from a Chinese radio beacon guides to the commando's corpse.

Chinese commando hat:
• Taft Tunnel under Jefferson Memorial: Near the Very Hard locked terminal that Doctor Li hacks.

itm_000cb5ff.summary: Highway Scar Armor is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 15.0, value 180 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Worn by raiders, raider armor consists of scraps of clothing fabricated both before and after the Great War, armored with scavenged pieces of metal. Each variant of raider armor in Fallout 3 can be repaired using any of the other raider armors. The helmets can only be repaired with other copies of the same model; they cannot be used to repair each other.

Raider badlands armor:
A bandolier is draped across the front of the apparently leather overshirt (vaguely resembling a tank top), and on the left knee, there appears to be some sort of colander being used as a knee pad. The outfit also includes shorts made from either leather or some variety of canvas-like material. A screwdriver is secured near one boot, in similar fashion to a boot knife.

itm_000cb5f0.summary: Shellshocked Combat Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 5.0, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Combat armor is among the best forms of protection in the post-War Capital Wasteland. It has the fifth-highest DR for non-power armors, only lower than Ranger battle armor, Lag-Bolt's combat armor (only available with Broken Steel), metal armor, and Metal Master armor. It is fairly useful for early to mid-level characters, as it can probably be acquired before the Ranger armor, and doesn't have the penalty to Agility that metal armor has.

Unlike the reinforced variants common on the West Coast, all the combat armor available in the Capital Wasteland is short-sleeved, having only the shoulder pads and chest plates covering the torso. Plates covering the groin, knee, shin and foot are also featured.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Cut versions:
• Sim regen armor
• Shellshocked combat armor (Identical to standard combat armor - Form ID:, helmet: ).

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: Unique apparel are highlighted with a darker background

itm_000b1056.summary: Pre-War businesswear is a type of clothing found in Fallout 3. They come in two variants, which have identical stats and can be used to repair each other.

Grimy pre-War businesswear consists of a dark gray suit with a red tie, while the female outfit consists of a dark gray jacket and matching skirt that reaches to the knees.

Dirty pre-War businesswear:
Dirty pre-War businesswear is a light tan pinstriped suit and black tie for men, and a light tan jacket and skirt to the knees for women.

Power-suit armor:
Power-suit armor is cut content from Fallout 3, appearing only in the game's files. In addition to a DR similar to light armor (+20), it also adds one point to both Agility and Charisma, with a Speech bonus of only +3, which is 2 less than regular businesswear, with a value doubled to 12 caps.

itm_000a3045.summary: Merc Grunt Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 12.0, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: They come in several variants with different appearances but identical stats. Each variant can be repaired using any of the other merc outfits, with one exception.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Merc adventurer outfit:
Merc adventurer outfits can be looted from several non-player characters such as Nathan and Billy Creel, both in Megaton, Dave in the Republic of Dave, Brock and Shrapnel, both in Rivet City, Bittercup in Big Town and Justin (The Family) in Meresti Metro station. It is sold by Moira in Megaton and Bannon at Potomac Attire. It can also be found in some footlockers and storage.

The appearance of the male variant is a large black vest with a red long-sleeved undershirt and black pants. The female variant is the same though it is short-sleeved and exposes the midriff. The collar of the male variant has three teeth on a string, worn like a necklace. On the female variant, there is an 8-ball patch stitched on the left sleeve. It also has spurs on the boots.

itm_00083c5c.summary: Vance's longcoat outfit is a piece of clothing in Fallout 3, a unique variant of the regulator duster worn by Vance in Meresti Metro station.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: This outfit can be repaired with leather armor and provides bonuses of 1 to Charisma and Perception as well as a bonus of 10 to Small Guns.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Vance's longcoat outfit can be obtained by killing or reverse-pickpocketing Vance. Killing Vance will make all other members of The Family hostile. Killing any of them will also make the residents of Arefu hostile, but only if Blood Ties was completed peacefully beforehand.

itm_00074336.summary: Head Wrap is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 0 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The headwrap has a weight and value of 0 as well as a Damage Resistance of 1. They can only be repaired with other head wraps. Unlike most clothing, they cannot be repaired by merchants because they have no value. However, this is negligible, since its condition does not affect its damage resistance (because it is already at the minimum).

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Gray:
Brock, Laszlo Radford and Wild Bill (The Pitt add-on) sport the gray variant. This is also worn by the wastelander in the random encounter 'More Than Just Scrap'. This wastelander respawns every 73 in-game hours, and can be killed repeatedly for their gray head wrap, with no negative consequences.

Dark gray:
The dark gray head wrap is worn by Alejandra Torres, Belle Bonny and Mei Wong. It is also found on a shelf near the pitching machine inside Herzog Mine in Point Lookout.

White:
Billy Creel, Bill Seward, Stockholm and Marguerite carry the white version.

Yellow/red plaid:
The yellow/red variation is included in the game files of Fallout 3, but is not used in the base game. Midea in the add-on The Pitt wears it. It can not be repaired by merchants; but only by other head wraps.

itm_0005bb70.summary: Dirty Pre-War Parkstroller Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 3.0, value 5 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: When equipped, none grant any Damage Resistance or Damage Threshold, but all outfit variants grant a temporary +1 Agility and all hats grants a temporary +1 Perception. Casualwear and relaxedwear can be repaired with other instances of each other, while parkstroller and spring outfits can be repaired of other instances of each other. With the Jury Rigging perk, all outfits can be repaired with instances of all others as well as both light armor and other pieces in the "clothing" and "headgear" categories.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
(Dirty) pre-War casualwear:
The male version consists of a brown sweater-vest and a pair of brown pants while the female version consists of a blue dress and heels.

(Dirty) pre-War relaxedwear:
The male version consists of a green sweater-vest and khaki slacks while the female version consists of a yellowish/brown dress, black belt, and black heels.

(Dirty) pre-War spring outfit:
The male version consists of a red plaid shirt and brown pants while the female version consists of a pink dress with red heels.

(Dirty) pre-War parkstroller outfit:
The male version consists of a gray short-sleeved button-up shirt and blue jeans while the female version consists of a greenish-yellow dress and heels.

sections.title: Headwear
sections.text:
Pre-War hat:
A worn brown leather hat.
• It can be found in most homes of any given non-player character.
• Can also be found in the inventory of any random merchant that sells apparel.
• Many of the Omerta thugs wear them, including Big Sal.
• In Goodsprings there are two - one in Doc Mitchell's house, one can be bought from Chet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.
• In one of the motel rooms of El Rey Motel.

Pre-War baseball cap:
A red baseball cap with a brim in the front.
• Can be found on the corpse south of Goodsprings laying on the cliff visited during Barton the Fink
• Can appear being worn by Powder Gangers

Pre-War bonnet:
A pre-War woman's bonnet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.

itm_000b0278.summary: The Talon combat armor and matching Talon combat helmet are pieces of armor in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Talon combat armor is the combat armor issued to all of the mercenaries who work for Talon Company. The matching Talon combat helmet is a unique helmet that can only be found on Commander Jabsco, the group's local commander in the Capital Wasteland, who resides in Fort Bannister.

This armor and helmet are black colored variations of the traditional combat armor. The suit bears the Talon Company logo in white on the left breast.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The armor can be obtained by killing a member of the Talon Company mercenaries, commonly found at Fort Bannister.
• The helmet can only be obtained from Commander Jabsco in Fort Bannister.
• Many dead Talon Company mercenaries inside the Takoma Industrial factory can be looted for their armor.
• FO3MZ Engineering core - One set of armor in a room with a bed.

itm_000abbe2.summary:
Kid's outfits are diverse pieces of clothing in Fallout 3, worn by the various children in the Capital Wasteland.

Wearing kid's outfits will change the player character's body into that of a child, lacking defining adult features though remaining the same scale.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
The outfits can be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing the wearers with better armor. The Pip-Boy 3000 icons for these outfits are that of a Vault 101 jumpsuit.

Athlete of the Wastes outfit:
The Athlete of the Wastes outfit features a white buttoned shirt with a pink and white two-tone jacket worn over it, accompanied with worn gray shoes and either belted denim pants or a belted denim skirt and dark gray undershirt depending on the character's gender. It is worn by Maggie, Flower, Biwwy, Squirrel, Joseph and James Hargrave. It is also worn by Sally, who appears in Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Hats
sections.text:
Only the kid's baseball cap and the kid's Murray the Mole hat are obtainable via reverse-pickpocketing. The kid's police hat and ragamuffin tophat are only obtainable via console commands.

Kid's ballcap with glasses:
Kid's ballcap with glasses can only be found in the game files. It features a two-tone white and red baseball cap with black-framed eyeglasses.

Ragamuffin tophat:
While many children wear the ragamuffin outfit, only Eclair and Kenny possess the matching ragamuffin tophat. It features a plain black tophat adorned with maroon-rimmed goggles.

Wasteland scout hat:
The wasteland scout hat can only be found in the game files. It features a beige campaign hat decorated with a police badge in the male design, and a green garrison cap decorated with a yellow diamond in the female design.

itm_000ab491.summary: The police hat is a piece of headwear found in the Fallout 3 add-ons Broken Steel, Point Lookout and Mothership Zeta, and in Fallout: New Vegas.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Police hat:
Standard issue for various police departments, the police hat is blue with a silver badge on the frontside.

Responders police hat:
Created by the Responders in Appalachia after the Great War, this version of the police hat has a distinctive red trim and was issued alongside a Responders police uniform to members to distinguish from pre-War police.

Kid's police hat:
A smaller version of the hat, commonly worn by children.

sections.title: Overview & Properties

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage

itm_000a6f78.summary: T-51b powered armor is a later form of power armor and represented the peak of armored infantry technology before the Great War. In Fallout 3, the T-51b power armor is a unique model of armor and can only be found in Fort Constantine.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The T-51b power armor provides 50 Damage Resistance and increases Radiation Resistance by 25. Wearing the helmet will provide an additional 10 DR, 8 RR, and provide a +1 bonus to Charisma. The armor set cannot be repaired with other armor and must be taken to a vendor for repairs. This armor is tied with the Enclave Hellfire armor as having the best DR in the game.

sections.title: Variant
sections.text: • Winterized T-51b power armor FO3OA

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
The T-51b armor is in Fort Constantine, sealed in a room that requires three keys from different locations.

The first key needed is Ted Strayer's special key. Ted Strayer is located in Rivet City. There are four ways to get the key from him: paying him in caps, passing a hard Speech check and convincing him, pickpocketing the key from him, or threatening him (requires 6+ Strength or the Toughness perk).

The second key can be obtained from Dukov, located at Dukov's Place, which is a hotel building. There are numerous ways to obtain Dukov's key. Buying the key from him is one simple way. Another easy way to obtain his key is to convince him with the Black Widow perk if the Lone Wanderer is female. Alternatively, Fantasia, one of Dukov's girls, can be convinced with the Lady Killer perk if the player character is male.

itm_0005c682.summary: Pre-War businesswear is a type of clothing found in Fallout 3. They come in two variants, which have identical stats and can be used to repair each other.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Grimy pre-War businesswear:
Grimy pre-War businesswear consists of a dark gray suit with a red tie, while the female outfit consists of a dark gray jacket and matching skirt that reaches to the knees.

Dirty pre-War businesswear:
Dirty pre-War businesswear is a light tan pinstriped suit and black tie for men, and a light tan jacket and skirt to the knees for women.

Power-suit armor:
Power-suit armor is cut content from Fallout 3, appearing only in the game's files. In addition to a DR similar to light armor (+20), it also adds one point to both Agility and Charisma, with a Speech bonus of only +3, which is 2 less than regular businesswear, with a value doubled to 12 caps.

itm_0005b6eb.summary: The security uniform and matching security helmet are pieces of armor in Fallout 3. It comes in two versions with different visual appearances but identical stats.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Rivet City security force uniform and the matching Rivet City security helmet are the standard protection for members of Rivet City security force. Whereas the Tenpenny security uniform is worn by the guards of Tenpenny Tower, the Tenpenny security helmet can be found in the game files but is not actually used in the game.

The two security uniforms have the lowest Damage Resistance out of all combat armor variants, offering slightly less protection than even the Talon combat armor. Actually, they provide no better protection than ordinary leather armor and weigh more, thus reducing both movement speed and sneak characteristics. Nonetheless, they provide better protection than most clothing worn in the wasteland, including merc outfits and raider armor, and convey a bonus of +5 to Small Guns.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The uniforms can be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing or killing a guard and looting their corpse. Dusty of Big Town, who wears one of the helmets, is the only character to wear a part of a Rivet City uniform without living in Rivet City.
• A Rivet City security guard may be found in one of the holding cells in Mothership Zeta.

itm_0005b6e8.summary: Raider Blastmaster Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 3.0, value 20 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Worn by raiders, raider armor consists of scraps of clothing fabricated both before and after the Great War, armored with scavenged pieces of metal. Each variant of raider armor in Fallout 3 can be repaired using any of the other raider armors. The helmets can only be repaired with other copies of the same model; they cannot be used to repair each other.

Raider badlands armor:
A bandolier is draped across the front of the apparently leather overshirt (vaguely resembling a tank top), and on the left knee, there appears to be some sort of colander being used as a knee pad. The outfit also includes shorts made from either leather or some variety of canvas-like material. A screwdriver is secured near one boot, in similar fashion to a boot knife.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider armor:
Nine raider armor models are added in the add-on The Pitt and are randomly worn by the raiders in The Pitt, except for the Leather Rebel, Bombshell Armor, and Metal Master Armor, which are Mill Worker quest rewards.
• Bombshell armor FO3TP
• Leather Rebel FO3TP
• Metal Master armor FO3TP
• Raider iconoclast armor FO3TP
• Raider commando armor FO3TP
• Raider throwdown armor FO3TP
• Raider ordinance armor FO3TP
• Raider paingiver armor FO3TP
• Gamma shield armor FO3TP

• Hand-me-down raider armor (visually identical with raider sadist armor).
• Highway scar armor (visually identical with raider blastmaster armor).
• Sharp-dressed raider's armor, gives +10 speech and 1 CH (visually identical with raider painspike armor).

itm_00028ff9.summary:
Pre-War outfits are a type of clothing found in Fallout 3.

Casualwear and relaxedwear (as well as their dirty variants) can be repaired with each other. Similarly, parkstroller and spring outfits (as well as their dirty variants) can be used to fix each other.

All of these outfits are for sale from the clothing shop in Tenpenny Tower and Rivet City.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
(Dirty) pre-War casualwear:
Used before the Great War, this can still be found in 2277 on characters in many locations. For males, it is a white long-sleeved shirt with a brown sweater-vest and dark pants. For females, it is a light blue short-sleeved dress with black high-heels.

Locations:
• Clean version worn by Anthony Ling, Pat Neusbaum, Janet Rockwell, Old Lady Dithers and Mabel Henderson.
• Two dirty variants in Lady Frumperton's Fashions.
• Dirty variant worn by Bill Wilson, Old Man Harris, Bannon, Vera Weatherly, Father Clifford, Michael Hawthorne, Irving Cheng, Carol and two Tenpenny residents.

(Dirty) pre-War parkstroller outfit:
Found in a suitcase on the boat underneath Arefu, or in a house in Minefield. For men, it consists of a white short-sleeved shirt and blue jeans.

sections.title: Headwear
sections.text:
Pre-War baseball cap:
A red baseball cap, the kind worn on those hot summer days before the Great War.

Pre-War baseball caps can be found in various locations and shops in the Capital Wasteland. Talking with Stanley at the Lone Wanderer's 10th birthday party and asking if he has any more gifts will result in a free cap. One can then be found in the Lone Wanderer's dresser at the start of Escape!. This headwear can be looted from Overseer Mack's body (if one kills Mack, and if they killed Overseer Almodovar previously) in Trouble on the Homefront.

The pre-War baseball cap is undersized when worn by children. It is anchored inside the head mesh and will clip through a child-character-model's face and forehead.

Pre-War bonnet:
A pre-War woman's bonnet. The bonnet appears the same regardless of the gender of the wearer.

itm_00028ff8.summary: Kid's Party Hat is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 5 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The party hat is a plain red paper party hat with yellow polka dots and blue streamers poking out of the top. Despite being made of paper, it still provides 1 DR.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Kid's party hat - Slightly smaller version only worn by children in Fallout 3. Otherwise, it is completely indistinguishable from the regular variant.
• Stanley's party hat - Unique variant only worn by Stanley Armstrong during the quest Growing Up Fast. Provides zero damage resistance. It appears slightly slanted when worn.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Vault 101 - In the diner during the quest Growing Up Fast.
• Sewer waystation - On a ghoul named Gallo.
• FO3BS Water caravan ambush near Arefu, on a table next to the Wastelander holotape.
• Little Lamplight - Ask Sticky about his hat upon meeting him and he will give it to the Lone Wanderer.
• FO3MZ Mothership Zetas cargo hold - Four party hats on a shelf with other pre-War clothing.

itm_00023030.summary: The Ranger battle armor and matching Ranger battle helmet are pieces of armor worn by members of the mercenary group Reilly's Rangers.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Ranger battle armor is a variant of combat armor. The matching Ranger battle helmet is used only by the group's engineer Donovan. Each suit has the same serial number (41-90MPW) painted on the back, along with a US Army star.

Ranger battle armor is the strongest non-powered armor available in the game, and for player characters who value Agility over Strength, the Ranger armor is preferable to power armor. Some forms of power armor also carry an explicit -1 or -2 penalty to Agility, which lowers Sneak. Furthermore, unlike power armor, combat armor requires no special training to use.

The +5 Action Points boost, +1 Luck, and +10 Small Guns make this armor particularly useful for lower-level Small Guns player characters. It remains useful for anyone up to level 30, due to Damage Resistance level, modest weight, and ease of repair.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: The armor can be acquired during the quest Reilly's Rangers by looting the Rangers' corpses in the Statesman Hotel or as a reward from Reilly upon completion of the quest. The armor can also be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing the Rangers at the Ranger compound. The helmet can only be obtained from Donovan, either by looting it from his corpse or reverse pickpocketing.

itm_0009b188.summary: Biker Goggles is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Biker goggles are made up of two clear glass lenses and are kept over the eyes with a leather strap.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Biker goggles are often found on raiders and wastelanders. They can also be bought readily from merchants that specialize in selling general goods (such as Moira Brown) and clothing (such as Crow). When available for sale from merchants, they are typically sold in perfect condition.
• Worn by Stockholm and Caleb Smith.
• Can be looted from William Brandice's corpse in Marigold station.
• On a table near the door connecting the two Taft Tunnel sections, Jefferson Memorial rotunda side.
• FO3PL Two can be found on a shelf near the pitching machine inside Herzog Mine in Point Lookout.
• FO3PL Three in Herzog Mine, one near a toolbox close to the Miner's Rest entrance. Another one center of the map, next to a skeleton and one more near a toppled over cart in the south.

itm_0009b186.summary: Motorcycle helmets are pieces of headwear that appear in Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas and Van Buren.

sections.title: Variants

Motorcycle helmet:
Motorcycle helmets are helmets commonly worn by various wastelanders.

itm_0008c83c.summary: Merc Veteran Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 12.0, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: They come in several variants with different appearances but identical stats. Each variant can be repaired using any of the other merc outfits, with one exception.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Merc adventurer outfit:
Merc adventurer outfits can be looted from several non-player characters such as Nathan and Billy Creel, both in Megaton, Dave in the Republic of Dave, Brock and Shrapnel, both in Rivet City, Bittercup in Big Town and Justin (The Family) in Meresti Metro station. It is sold by Moira in Megaton and Bannon at Potomac Attire. It can also be found in some footlockers and storage.

The appearance of the male variant is a large black vest with a red long-sleeved undershirt and black pants. The female variant is the same though it is short-sleeved and exposes the midriff. The collar of the male variant has three teeth on a string, worn like a necklace. On the female variant, there is an 8-ball patch stitched on the left sleeve. It also has spurs on the boots.

itm_0008a6dd.summary: Button's Wig is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 20 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
It resembles a powdered wig from the 17-18th centuries.

At the expense of -1 to Perception, it grants bonuses of 1 to Intelligence, 5 to Barter and 10 to Speech skills. It also provides a Damage Resistance of 1. It can only be repaired by merchants.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The wig is found on top of Button Gwinnett's cabinet in the National Archives, near the end of the Stealing Independence quest.

itm_0007c17d.summary: Shady Hat is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 40 caps). Linked to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The shady hat can be obtained as a reward for doing the mirelurk observation quest as part of Moira Brown's "The Wasteland Survival Guide" missions. Place Moira's observer unit inside a nest deep in the Anchorage Memorial. To get it, the Lone Wanderer must place an observer unit in a mirelurk egg nest without killing any of the mirelurks in the area.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: MS03StealthHat). Weight: 1.0, Value: 40 caps. Effects: Perception +1, Sneak +5.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage
sections.text: Used in quests: Wasteland Survival Guide. Obtained through exploration, containers, or quest progression in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

itm_0007c17c.summary: Modified Utility Jumpsuit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 30 caps). Linked to quests: Trouble on the Homefront.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This unique jumpsuit is similar to the normal Vault 101 utility jumpsuit, with the differences being that it provides different stat bonuses, it is dirty like Dad's wasteland outfit and it has green instead of red sneakers when worn by a female character. It can be repaired with vault jumpsuits, Dad's wasteland outfit and other copies of itself.

It provides +1 to Luck, +10 to Radiation Resistance and +5 to Repair.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The modified utility jumpsuit may be rewarded by completing Trouble on the Homefront, either by siding with Alphonse Almodovar (requiring him to be still alive) or by siding with Amata and the rebels, and then peacefully talking down Alphonse. All other resolutions, including flushing Vault 101's water chip, will not reward the jumpsuit.

itm_00078647.summary: Enclave Officer Hat is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Wearing this uniform does not turn Enclave characters non-hostile or affect the attitude of other factions; Fallout 3 does not include faction disguise mechanics and the player character's factions are not altered when equipping the uniform.

The hat is the only hat to provide a bonus to Energy Weapons. It also bears a different insignia in its inventory icon, having a bird with its wings spread, rather than its actual insignia of the Enclave "E" in a ring of stars.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: OutfitEnclaveOfficer01Hat). Weight: 1.0, Value: 6 caps. Effects: Energy Weapons +5.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage
sections.text: Found at locations: Launch Platform Base. Carried or sold by: Enclave Officer, Security Officer.

itm_00078646.summary: The Chinese jumpsuit and the Chinese commando hat are pieces of clothing in Fallout 3. The Communist commander outfit can be considered a high definition recreation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The basic People's Liberation Army uniform is a single piece jumpsuit, whose design is based on the Mao suit. It has four large front pockets, arranged symmetrically, the Chinese flag over the upper right pocket and is typically worn together with a large leather belt, shoulder belt, and a commando hat.

The accompanying commando hat is an ushanka style hat with the ear and neck flaps tied up, displaying the insignia of Communist China in the centre of the front face. Jumpsuits seen in America carry the insignia of the Chinese Iron Army on the right sleeve and have two red stars on the collar lapels.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The jumpsuit is a decorative piece of armor, with half the DR provided by the starting Vault 101 security armor and low item hit points.

Unique variants:
Jumpsuits
• FO3OA Winterized Chinese jumpsuit (non-playable)
• FO3OA General Jingwei's uniform (non-playable)
Hat
• FO3TP Hat of the People
• FO3OA General Jingwei's uniform (non-playable)

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Chinese jumpsuit:
• Tranquility Lane: The Chinese jumpsuit is worn by the commandos when the failsafe terminal is activated. It can not be looted from their bodies, as they are rendered unconscious and not killed, and all inventory from the simulation is deleted upon exit.

Dirty Chinese jumpsuit:
• Rivet City: The dirty Chinese jumpsuit can be purchased at Potomac Attire.
• Taft Tunnel under the Jefferson Memorial: Found at abandoned infiltrator listening posts.
• Mama Dolce's: Looted from Chinese remnants.
• Dead pilot random encounter: One of these can also be found on a dead Chinese commando. A radio signal from a Chinese radio beacon guides to the commando's corpse.

Chinese commando hat:
• Taft Tunnel under Jefferson Memorial: Near the Very Hard locked terminal that Doctor Li hacks.

itm_00078644.summary:
Raider armor is a name that refers to various types of armor worn by raiders.

Some raiders, like the Khans, wear typical leather armor and other regular types of armor. This article covers types of armor that are worn only (or mostly) by raiders.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Raider badlands armor:
A bandolier is draped across the front of the top of a pair of tan overalls and on the left knee there appears to be some sort of colander being used as a knee pad. The outfit also includes shorts made from either leather or some variety of canvas-like material. A screwdriver is secured near one boot, akin to a boot knife.

Raider blastmaster armor:
It appears to employ a tire of some kind as the shoulder pad and has a pair of roman sandals as footwear. Around the waist appears to be a mattress or quilt for a bed, and the back of it is a bit burned. On the right forearm there is the Arclight Helmet nailed into the leathery sleeve, and the shins are possibly the remainder of baseball shin guards.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: ArmorRaider02Helmet). Weight: 3.0, Value: 20 caps.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage
sections.text: Found at locations: Cryo Lab, Empty House, Shalebridge Hill.

itm_0007836e.summary: The MP-47/A prototype medic power armor is a unique suit of power armor in Fallout 3. It is a U.S. Army variant of the T-45d power armor equipped with an auto-injector system that administers Med-X when the wearer is injured.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The armor automatically administers Med-X when the player's health falls below 33% or when any limb's health drops below 25%. The player must have Med-X in their inventory for the system to function; the script consumes one dose per activation. There is a 2.5 in-game hour cooldown between injections and voice lines.

The suit-administered Med-X provides a distinct "Suit Med-X" effect: +25 Damage Resistance and temporary suppression of crippled limb penalties (e.g., limping) and addictions. Regular Med-X can still be used manually, and the effects stack for up to +50 Damage Resistance. Limb injuries and addictions must still be permanently treated with stimpaks or a doctor (or the My First Laboratory for addictions).

sections.title: Location
sections.text: • Old Olney, Olney sewers: The armor is found on a dead Brotherhood of Steel initiate, stuck in a culvert with a wastelander and mercenary, also dead. Enter through either of the entrances to the sewer, and make the way to the narrow hallway. The door leading to the room is located on the outward side of the hallway, the entrance is usually guarded by a deathclaw.

itm_00075203.summary: Brotherhood Power Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 8.0, value 110 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Power armor can only be worn if the player character has gained the Power Armor Training perk, either by talking to Paladin Gunny in the Citadel, by starting the Take it Back! quest, or by completing the Anchorage Reclamation simulation. T-45d power armor can be repaired using components from the T-51b power armor, but the reverse is not possible. All non-unique variants of T-45d power armor have identical properties and effects, and only differ in their appearance and use in certain quests.

itm_0006b465.summary: Tesla Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 9.0, value 120 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
A heavily modified suit of standard Mark II armor, with the primary difference being the Tesla device rigged to the suit with five attraction coils mounted on rounded shoulders. While it retains the original's segmented armor coverage, the Tesla device aids with the operation of energy weapons and protects against both laser and plasma based weapons.

This armor has a more dilapidated appearance compared to Mark II armor, featuring visible rust, scratches, and wear. Tesla armor technology is not an original invention of the Enclave, and different models have previously been recovered by high-ranking Brotherhood of Steel soldiers, such as Henry Casdin.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The armor makes the operation of energy weapons by the wearer easier, boosting the Energy Weapons skill of the operator. Tesla armor has Tesla coils on the shoulder pads and some lights running down the legs. It is overall bulkier than other power armors.

Although this is powerful armor, the only way to get it (and spare suits for repairs) is by fighting Enclave soldiers or finding at least one in the Mothership Zeta add-on. The Enclave soldiers' armor is usually acquired in a rather poor condition. Despite this drawback, the armor is still one of the best to be found by the end of the game.

Tesla armor can be given to Protector Casdin at Fort Independence for 5.56mm rounds, frag grenades, RadAway or stimpaks as part of the unmarked quest The Outcast Collection Agent.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Worn by Enclave soldiers.
• FO3MZ On display in the weapons lab.
• FO3MZ In the Cryo lab, in the west room, on a shelf next to a plasma pistol

itm_0005c9a1.summary: Tortiseshell Glasses is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 8 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: A pair of brownish-orange flecked Protecto brand glasses that are rarer than other variants. They provide a Damage Resistance of 1 and no other effects. They can be repaired with any other type of glasses.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Mister Burke, Martha Wilson and Old Man Harris wear a pair.
• On the table next to Snowflake, the ghoul barber on the second floor of the Underworld.
• A pair is on one of the mounted brahmin heads in Dukov's Place. Two more pairs are on the pool table on the bedroom, on a stand.
• One inside the Citadel laboratory mess hall on the left-most table on the back wall.
• Two inside Tenpenny Tower at New Urban Apparel, behind a mannequin. Must be stolen.
• One on a table in Lady Frumperton's Fashions.
• One can be obtained with the purchase of the love machine theme for the Megaton house or Tenpenny Tower suite.
• A pair can be found in Mister Burke's house in Megaton.
• Inside the Taft Tunnel after the Lone Wanderer's second encounter with the Enclave and feral ghouls, about halfway through the tunnel.

itm_0005c99f.summary: Sunglasses is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 8 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Sunglasses are tinted glasses that keep glare from the sun out of the wearer's eyes. They provide a Damage Resistance of 1 and no other effects. They can be repaired with other glasses.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Lucky shades
• FO3BS Lag-Bolt's shades

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Sam Warrick and Snowflake both wear a pair of sunglasses.
• Inside the Roosevelt Academy Arts and Athletics Hall, in a bathroom in the southwest, on a hand dryer.
• They can be found on the table with the clock, wrench, and coffee mug inside the irradiated metro, in a west hallway.
• A pair can be found in My Megaton house or the Tenpenny Tower suite, if one purchases the Love machine theme.
• FO3TP Two pairs can be found in the Pitt on mannequins. The first is in Uptown in one of the Pitt raider shacks. The second is in the underground section right after switching off the floodlights in the following room; and cannot be reached after completing The Pitt and returning, as there is a "stair gate" blocking entrance into the room.

itm_0003e54a.summary: Regulator Duster is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 10.0, value 70 caps). Linked to quests: Lawbringer.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The duster outfit seems to consist of a black undershirt and a pair of gray canvas pants underneath a long, brown leather overcoat with the sleeves rolled up above the elbow, a pair of leather gloves on the character's hands, and a pair of motorcycle boots for footwear.

It can be repaired with other Regulator dusters and provides a Damage Resistance of 10 as well as a bonus of 1 to Charisma and a bonus of 5 to Small Guns.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Sheriff's duster
• Vance's longcoat outfit

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One is given at 100% condition by Sonora Cruz if the Lone Wanderer joins the Regulators. To join the Regulators, one must have the Lawbringer perk. Taking the perk will add the location of Regulator HQ to the Pip-Boy world map.
• If the player character has Evil Karma and does not have the Lawbringer perk, Regulators will occasionally show up to attack the Wanderer for a bounty, at which point a Regulator duster can be obtained by killing them and looting their corpses.
• If the player character has the Lawbringer perk and reverse-pickpockets the unnamed Regulators inside the Regulator HQ, they will have a new duster in 72 hours.
• If the player character takes the Lawbringer perk, there will be a dead Regulator on a stairway as soon as one enters Arlington Cemetery, as well as a note for Junders Plunkett, who is in the area.

itm_0002d11b.summary: Mayor MacCready's outfit and MacCready's helmet are pieces of clothing in Fallout 3, worn by Mayor MacCready from Little Lamplight.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The outfit is primarily an olive-green field jacket worn with matching cargo pants fitted with metal kneepads. A helmet with goggles is also worn alongside a long white scarf, used as a hood.

They can only be obtained by using console commands as MacCready cannot be pickpocketed nor damaged.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: HelmetMayorMacCready). Weight: 1.0, Value: 60 caps.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage
sections.text: Carried or sold by: Mayor MacCready. Obtained through exploration, containers, or quest progression in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland).

itm_00050e44.summary: Party Hat is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 5 caps). Linked to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The party hat is a plain red paper party hat with yellow polka dots and blue streamers poking out of the top. Despite being made of paper, it still provides 1 DR.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Kid's party hat - Slightly smaller version only worn by children in Fallout 3. Otherwise, it is completely indistinguishable from the regular variant.
• Stanley's party hat - Unique variant only worn by Stanley Armstrong during the quest Growing Up Fast. Provides zero damage resistance. It appears slightly slanted when worn.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Vault 101 - In the diner during the quest Growing Up Fast.
• Sewer waystation - On a ghoul named Gallo.
• FO3BS Water caravan ambush near Arefu, on a table next to the Wastelander holotape.
• Little Lamplight - Ask Sticky about his hat upon meeting him and he will give it to the Lone Wanderer.
• FO3MZ Mothership Zetas cargo hold - Four party hats on a shelf with other pre-War clothing.

itm_0004e6a0.summary: Eyebot Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 5.0, value 20 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: It is a rare metal helmet made from the shell of an Enclave Eyebot, with flames painted on the top.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• During The Waters of Life quest after entering the Taft Tunnel, look for a small hallway with lockers, a footlocker, and a desk. The helmet can be found sitting on top of the desk.
• On a raider northeast of the Chryslus Building near an Enclave outpost (south of the raid shack). (After The Waters of Life).
• On another raider in the far eastern area of the map, south of MDPL-16 power station and northeast of Relay tower KX-B8-11. There are several Enclave bodies and crates scattered around; approaching them will cause a group of raiders to spawn atop a cliff to the northwest. One of them will possess the helmet. (After Take it Back!).

itm_0004445b.summary: Lincoln's Hat is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 40 caps). Linked to quests: Head of State, Lincoln Artifacts.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: A 19th century black felt, stovepipe hat famously worn by the 16th President of the United States of America, Abraham Lincoln. At some point prior to the nuclear apocalypse, it was put on display in the Museum of History in Washington, D.C., where after 200 years of neglect, the hat has become worn and tattered and largely discolored with dirt and grime.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The hat is located in the Museum of History. From the lower halls, enter the offices. Continue forward and head up the stairs. At the end of the stairway, turn right, head down the hallway and enter the first room on the right. It will be filled with rubble; the hat is slightly to the left, by a large desk. The hat is lying on the floor about 6–10 feet from the room entrance on the left. If one can't find the room it is the northwestern room on the local map. One can either fall down to the room from above when going upstairs or get there directly from the offices.

sections.title: Related quests
sections.text: • Lincoln's Profit Margins - The hat is included in the list of items related to Lincoln that can be sold to Leroy Walker, Hannibal Hamlin or Abraham Washington. If the hat is sold to Hannibal, he says he will enshrine it, but since the hat is added to his inventory, he will wear it instead. He dismisses the hat as being “silly looking”, and as such, does not offer a high price for it.

itm_0004443f.summary: The advanced power armor Mk II, named in-game as Enclave power armor, is a set of power armor in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Nicknamed Black Devil power armor by the Brotherhood of Steel, the advanced power armor Mark II is a high-end model of power armor developed after the Great War and started before the destruction of the Enclave Oil Rig in 2241. This suit is used as the standard power armor of the Enclave Department of the Army in the Capital Wasteland in 2277. It is composed entirely of lightweight composites rather than the usual combination of metal and composite plates found on the earlier advanced power armor. Unlike the original advanced power armor, the Mark II features a large profile, and more effective, segmented armor plates to achieve a superior degree of protection, with the hump replaced with pauldrons that evoke old world power armor designs, such as the T-45.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The set consists of two pieces, the body armor, and helmet. Like all power armor, power armor training is required to equip it. It provides +1 Strength and -1 Agility. There is also a 5% increase to Radiation Resistance.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Worn by Enclave soldiers.
• FO3BS Three are found in the Rockland car tunnel, two of which on the floor, one on a nearby Enclave soldier's corpse.

itm_0002f563.summary: The slave collar, prisoner collar, or the total pacification collar as referred to by its creator the Big MT company, was a pre-War control device used to enforce discipline through a variety of measures, from non-lethal electric shots to lethal decapitation with explosives.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Available in several models before the Great War, slave collars follow a simple but deadly design, that of a small explosive charge encased in five pounds of durable steel (actual collar weight varies by game). A microphone/speaker and a radio wave receiver and transmitter may also be present though models vary. When remotely triggered, the receiver signals the detonation of the charge, obliterating everything above the neck of the wearer without damaging the surrounding area. The collar's transmitter constantly broadcasts its position and environmental input to the controller, meaning wearers can be constantly monitored and eavesdropped upon.

In addition, the collars are designed to detonate when tampered with.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Slave collar:
The standard run-of-the-mill slave collar was used to subjugate slaves to the will of their master.

Explosive collar:
Explosive collars are used by the Mojave Brotherhood of Steel to make sure detained prisoners comply.

Destroyed collar:
A slave collar that has already been detonated. In Freeside, on the corpse simply named "Man." He is equipped with a destroyed slave collar that can be taken off of him. It is implied that he tried to remove the collar himself but ended up triggering the explosive. It is identical to normal collars.

Dead Money collar:
A slave collar from Big MT that Elijah tinkered with to make his captives obey orders to crack open the Sierra Madre Casino & Resort.

Deactivated bomb collar:
A slave collar from Little Yangtze that Elijah tinkered with in order to understand its internal workings.

itm_0003d1fe.summary: The slave collar, prisoner collar, or the total pacification collar as referred to by its creator the Big MT company, was a pre-War control device used to enforce discipline through a variety of measures, from non-lethal electric shots to lethal decapitation with explosives.

sections.text:

In addition, the collars are designed to detonate when tampered with.

itm_00034121.summary: Armored Vault 101 Jumpsuit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 12.0, value 180 caps). Linked to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The armored vault jumpsuit is a variant of the Vault-Tec vault suit, modified to better protect its owner in combat. It is a normal vault jumpsuit with several plates, most likely from leather armor, attached to provide additional protection.

The jumpsuit provides bonuses ideal for low level characters as +5 to Energy Weapons and Small Guns are fairly beneficial at the start of the game, where small guns like the 10mm pistol and energy weapons like the laser pistol are quickly obtainable.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The suit can be found in Craterside Supply, Moira's store in Megaton. Moira bestows this gift on the Lone Wanderer for complying with a request to recall how life in Vault 101 was. Moira explains that she made this suit for a girl from the vault around "10 or 12 years ago," but the girl never returned to pick it up, leading Moira to speculate that she may have died.
• It can also be stolen or bought from her for around 180 caps if one chooses to not help her with the Wasteland Survival Guide.

itm_00034120.summary: The Mechanist's costume and the matching The Mechanist's helmet are pieces of Fallout 3 armor worn by the eponymous self-proclaimed superhero, the Mechanist, who is hiding out in the robot repair center south of Canterbury Commons in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Mechanist's armor is inspired by robots, with greaves and armor heavily resembling a robot's body, and the helmet having two antennae sticking out. It gives a decent DR of 20 and gives a +1 bonus to Endurance, although it's fairly heavy at 15 lbs and gives a penalty of -1 Charisma.

The body plate and waist fitting bear similarities to that of a sentry bot, the shoulder covering pauldrons and upper arm-guards appear to be refurbished from robobrain parts, and the elbow guards appear to be furnished from Protectron shoulder joint casings.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The armor can be obtained either by killing the Mechanist or persuading him to give up his career.

sections.title: Related quests
sections.text: Should the player character be asked by Uncle Roe to solve the town's "superhero" problem, the Mechanist's costume can be handed over to the AntAgonizer to end the town's problems. Alternatively, wearing the costume in the AntAgonizer's presence will turn her hostile.

itm_0003411f.summary: The AntAgonizer's costume and the matching The AntAgonizer's helmet are worn by the AntAgonizer, who is one of the two superheroes fighting in Canterbury Commons in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The AntAgonizer's armor is ant themed, with shoulder pads, greaves and armguards resembling a giant ant's carapace, and the helmet having insectoid eyes and matching antennae. It gives a decent DR of 20 and a +1 bonus to Agility, although it is fairly heavy at 15 lbs. and gives a penalty of -1 in Charisma.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: They can be obtained from the AntAgonizer either through negotiation or by killing her. If Uncle Roe has asked for a solution to the town's "superhero" problem, the AntAgonizer's costume can be handed over to the Mechanist to end the town's problems. Alternatively, wearing the costume in the Mechanist's presence will turn him hostile. When the costume is given to the Mechanist, he will hand over the unique laser pistol, Protectron's Gaze.

sections.title: Related quests
sections.text: • This costume is used in the quest The Superhuman Gambit in Canterbury Commons.

itm_0003411c.summary: Vault 101 security armor and Vault 101 security helmet are a suit of armor worn by the vault security officers.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: It consists of a riot helmet with a hinged, acrylic visor and a padded, puncture-resistant vest. Although this armor has a relatively low Damage Resistance rating, it will be the first set of armor the Lone Wanderer will be able to possess and will provide basic protection against early-game foes. The Vault 101 security armor also has little or no movement penalties, allowing characters to move quicker than with other, bulkier variants.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Worn by Vault 101 security officers.
• If Susie Mack is encountered in the wasteland, she will be wearing the Vault 101 security armor without the helmet.
• In Vault 101's atrium/upper level, two sets are found in the security station, in the weapon lockers.

itm_0003411b.summary: Red Racer Jumpsuit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 2.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: These suits provide a bonus of +5 to Repair. The Red Racer and handyman jumpsuits can be repaired with Red Racer jumpsuits. The RobCo jumpsuit can be repaired with other copies of itself.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Army mechanic jumpsuit:
Added with the add-on Operation: Anchorage, the green army mechanic jumpsuit is used by American grease-monkeys (U.S. Army mechanics) in the Anchorage Reclamation simulation while repairing power armor and vehicles.

It is available to the player only through the use of console commands or glitches.

Unlike most armor and weapons in Operation: Anchorage, the jumpsuit does not have an extremely high HP count, and will degrade normally.

The Red Racer jumpsuit is a basic yellow jumpsuit with a red Red Racer logo on its back.

Jenny Stahl and Lucky Harith both wear this clothing. It is also used by some vendors. It cannot be found at the Red Racer factory, but can be purchased from Bannon and Seagrave Holmes in Rivet City.

itm_00034119.summary: The security uniform and matching security helmet are pieces of armor in Fallout 3. It comes in two versions with different visual appearances but identical stats.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Rivet City security force uniform and the matching Rivet City security helmet are the standard protection for members of Rivet City security force. Whereas the Tenpenny security uniform is worn by the guards of Tenpenny Tower, the Tenpenny security helmet can be found in the game files but is not actually used in the game.

The two security uniforms have the lowest Damage Resistance out of all combat armor variants, offering slightly less protection than even the Talon combat armor. Actually, they provide no better protection than ordinary leather armor and weigh more, thus reducing both movement speed and sneak characteristics. Nonetheless, they provide better protection than most clothing worn in the wasteland, including merc outfits and raider armor, and convey a bonus of +5 to Small Guns.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The uniforms can be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing or killing a guard and looting their corpse. Dusty of Big Town, who wears one of the helmets, is the only character to wear a part of a Rivet City uniform without living in Rivet City.
• A Rivet City security guard may be found in one of the holding cells in Mothership Zeta.

itm_00034105.summary: The Ranger battle armor and matching Ranger battle helmet are pieces of armor worn by members of the mercenary group Reilly's Rangers.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Ranger battle armor is a variant of combat armor. The matching Ranger battle helmet is used only by the group's engineer Donovan. Each suit has the same serial number (41-90MPW) painted on the back, along with a US Army star.

Ranger battle armor is the strongest non-powered armor available in the game, and for player characters who value Agility over Strength, the Ranger armor is preferable to power armor. Some forms of power armor also carry an explicit -1 or -2 penalty to Agility, which lowers Sneak. Furthermore, unlike power armor, combat armor requires no special training to use.

The +5 Action Points boost, +1 Luck, and +10 Small Guns make this armor particularly useful for lower-level Small Guns player characters. It remains useful for anyone up to level 30, due to Damage Resistance level, modest weight, and ease of repair.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: The armor can be acquired during the quest Reilly's Rangers by looting the Rangers' corpses in the Statesman Hotel or as a reward from Reilly upon completion of the quest. The armor can also be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing the Rangers at the Ranger compound. The helmet can only be obtained from Donovan, either by looting it from his corpse or reverse pickpocketing.

itm_000340fe.summary: Wasteland Doctor Fatigues is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 2.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Crudely made, they provide only the most basic of protection and are easy to come by, as they can be bought from traders, can be found on many corpses or inside several homes throughout the Capital Wasteland, it can also be found on most Megaton settlers.

Wasteland outfits can be repaired with brahmin-skin outfits, wasteland settler outfits, wasteland wanderer outfits, wasteland surgeon outfits, wasteland doctor fatigues, and roving trader outfits. The matching headwear can only be repaired with other copies of their respective model.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Brahmin-skin outfit:
A dirty off-white in color (gray for the coveralls), the brahmin-skin outfit consists of a crudely-stitched pair of overalls and a patched shirt. They appear to have received only the most rudimentary treatment in tanning and tailoring.

Wasteland legend outfit:
The wasteland legend outfit is identical to the merc veteran outfit. It will spawn randomly in lockers and footlockers or be sold by merchants. It can also be found on various enemies throughout the Capital Wasteland.

Wasteland settler outfit:
The wasteland settler outfit consists of a green, rag-like shirt and a pair of gray-brown pants.

Wasteland wanderer outfit:
The wasteland wanderer outfit is a tan jacket with a hood and off-white pants tucked into riding boots.

itm_000340fd.summary: Eyeglasses is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 8 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Eyeglasses are black rounded-square framed glasses that provide a Damage Resistance of 1 and no skill bonuses. They can be repaired with any other type of glasses.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Jonas, Murphy, Stiggs and Dr. Zimmer all wear eyeglasses.
• Inside a Pulowski Preservation shelter in L'Enfant West.
• One inside Lady Frumperton's Fashions in Dupont Circle.
• One inside Arlington Library in a bathroom on a hand dryer.
• One inside Dukov's Place on the mounted brahmin heads.
• In My Megaton house or Tenpenny Tower suite when purchasing the Love machine theme.
• Inside Vault 101 on Jonas Palmer's corpse.
• Two at New Urban Apparel, behind a mannequin. Must be stolen.
• FO3BS In the northwest corner of the Old Olney S. Wilson Building, with a teddy bear and a garden gnome.
• FO3BS In Old Olney underground, on a table with reading glasses, center of the map.
• FO3BS On a desk next to an eye chart inside the air control tower of Adams Air Force Base.

itm_000340fc.summary: The Pint-Sized Slasher mask is a piece of headwear in Fallout 3 and its add-on Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The mask is the signature costume of the Pint-Sized Slasher, a pre-War serial killer who some believed to be more than a myth.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: It is a colorful clown's mask with a spotted hat on top, specially made to be wearable by children, while also striking fear into the hearts of victims.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Tranquility Lane:
Found in the Tranquility Lane simulation, this version of the mask has a Damage Resistance of 6 (and can only be repaired by merchants).

It is only accessible as an item during the quest Tranquility Lane, as it is automatically removed when exiting the simulation.

Point Lookout:
The non-simulation version of the mask in Point Lookout has a Damage Resistance of 1 and can be repaired with other copies of itself. In addition, it decreases Perception by 1 while increasing Melee Weapons by 5.

itm_000340f2.summary: Vault 101 Child's Jumpsuit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 5 caps). Linked to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: It is a children's version of the Vault 101 jumpsuit and the standard attire for all children in Vault 101. The Lone Wanderer is equipped with this suit during their childhood in the vault.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: The jumpsuit is equipped on the player during Growing Up Fast. Afterwards, it is removed from the inventory and is only obtainable with console commands.

itm_000340ef.summary: Vault jumpsuits or Vault suits (terms used interchangeably) are the iconic gear of Vault dwellers and by and large the symbol of Vault-Tec Corporation, being worn by mascots Vault Boy and Vault Girl.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Designed specifically for use within Vaults, jumpsuits are an inexpensive, easily produced solution to the age-old problem of clothing large numbers of people while maintaining a modicum of comfort and utility. Within the Vaults, they are also meant to reduce tension by providing every dweller with the same type of clothes, regardless of their standing. Marketed as a fashionable, comfortable design, before the war, they were an instantly recognizable symbol of both Vaults and the corporation behind them, featuring an iconic blue-and-yellow color scheme. Barb Howard implies that this color scheme was inspired by Cooper Howard's blue-and-gold sheriff's outfit from his western films.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: VaultSuit112). Weight: 1.0, Value: 6 caps. Effects: Speech +2, Melee Weapons +2.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage
sections.text: Found at locations: Vault 112. Carried or sold by: Stanislaus Braun. Used in quests: Scientific Pursuits.

itm_000340e6.summary: Sexy Sleepwear is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 1.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The sexy sleepwear gives a +1 bonus to Charisma.

sections.title: Variants

Sleepwear:
Sleepwear is a piece of Fallout 3 cut clothing. It is identical to sexy sleepwear and can only be retrieved through the console.

Unique variants:
• All-nighter nightwear (Broken Steel)

itm_000340d3.summary: The Chinese jumpsuit and the Chinese commando hat are pieces of clothing in Fallout 3. The Communist commander outfit can be considered a high definition recreation.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The basic People's Liberation Army uniform is a single piece jumpsuit, whose design is based on the Mao suit. It has four large front pockets, arranged symmetrically, the Chinese flag over the upper right pocket and is typically worn together with a large leather belt, shoulder belt, and a commando hat.

The accompanying commando hat is an ushanka style hat with the ear and neck flaps tied up, displaying the insignia of Communist China in the centre of the front face. Jumpsuits seen in America carry the insignia of the Chinese Iron Army on the right sleeve and have two red stars on the collar lapels.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The jumpsuit is a decorative piece of armor, with half the DR provided by the starting Vault 101 security armor and low item hit points.

Unique variants:
Jumpsuits
• FO3OA Winterized Chinese jumpsuit (non-playable)
• FO3OA General Jingwei's uniform (non-playable)
Hat
• FO3TP Hat of the People
• FO3OA General Jingwei's uniform (non-playable)

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Chinese jumpsuit:
• Tranquility Lane: The Chinese jumpsuit is worn by the commandos when the failsafe terminal is activated. It can not be looted from their bodies, as they are rendered unconscious and not killed, and all inventory from the simulation is deleted upon exit.

Dirty Chinese jumpsuit:
• Rivet City: The dirty Chinese jumpsuit can be purchased at Potomac Attire.
• Taft Tunnel under the Jefferson Memorial: Found at abandoned infiltrator listening posts.
• Mama Dolce's: Looted from Chinese remnants.
• Dead pilot random encounter: One of these can also be found on a dead Chinese commando. A radio signal from a Chinese radio beacon guides to the commando's corpse.

Chinese commando hat:
• Taft Tunnel under Jefferson Memorial: Near the Very Hard locked terminal that Doctor Li hacks.

itm_000340d1.summary: Dirty Pre-War Spring Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 3.0, value 5 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: When equipped, none grant any Damage Resistance or Damage Threshold, but all outfit variants grant a temporary +1 Agility and all hats grants a temporary +1 Perception. Casualwear and relaxedwear can be repaired with other instances of each other, while parkstroller and spring outfits can be repaired of other instances of each other. With the Jury Rigging perk, all outfits can be repaired with instances of all others as well as both light armor and other pieces in the "clothing" and "headgear" categories.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
(Dirty) pre-War casualwear:
The male version consists of a brown sweater-vest and a pair of brown pants while the female version consists of a blue dress and heels.

(Dirty) pre-War relaxedwear:
The male version consists of a green sweater-vest and khaki slacks while the female version consists of a yellowish/brown dress, black belt, and black heels.

(Dirty) pre-War spring outfit:
The male version consists of a red plaid shirt and brown pants while the female version consists of a pink dress with red heels.

(Dirty) pre-War parkstroller outfit:
The male version consists of a gray short-sleeved button-up shirt and blue jeans while the female version consists of a greenish-yellow dress and heels.

sections.title: Headwear
sections.text:
Pre-War hat:
A worn brown leather hat.
• It can be found in most homes of any given non-player character.
• Can also be found in the inventory of any random merchant that sells apparel.
• Many of the Omerta thugs wear them, including Big Sal.
• In Goodsprings there are two - one in Doc Mitchell's house, one can be bought from Chet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.
• In one of the motel rooms of El Rey Motel.

Pre-War baseball cap:
A red baseball cap with a brim in the front.
• Can be found on the corpse south of Goodsprings laying on the cliff visited during Barton the Fink
• Can appear being worn by Powder Gangers

Pre-War bonnet:
A pre-War woman's bonnet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.

itm_000340d0.summary:
Pre-War outfits are a type of clothing found in Fallout 3.

Casualwear and relaxedwear (as well as their dirty variants) can be repaired with each other. Similarly, parkstroller and spring outfits (as well as their dirty variants) can be used to fix each other.

All of these outfits are for sale from the clothing shop in Tenpenny Tower and Rivet City.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
(Dirty) pre-War casualwear:
Used before the Great War, this can still be found in 2277 on characters in many locations. For males, it is a white long-sleeved shirt with a brown sweater-vest and dark pants. For females, it is a light blue short-sleeved dress with black high-heels.

Locations:
• Clean version worn by Anthony Ling, Pat Neusbaum, Janet Rockwell, Old Lady Dithers and Mabel Henderson.
• Two dirty variants in Lady Frumperton's Fashions.
• Dirty variant worn by Bill Wilson, Old Man Harris, Bannon, Vera Weatherly, Father Clifford, Michael Hawthorne, Irving Cheng, Carol and two Tenpenny residents.

(Dirty) pre-War parkstroller outfit:
Found in a suitcase on the boat underneath Arefu, or in a house in Minefield. For men, it consists of a white short-sleeved shirt and blue jeans.

sections.title: Headwear
sections.text:
Pre-War baseball cap:
A red baseball cap, the kind worn on those hot summer days before the Great War.

Pre-War baseball caps can be found in various locations and shops in the Capital Wasteland. Talking with Stanley at the Lone Wanderer's 10th birthday party and asking if he has any more gifts will result in a free cap. One can then be found in the Lone Wanderer's dresser at the start of Escape!. This headwear can be looted from Overseer Mack's body (if one kills Mack, and if they killed Overseer Almodovar previously) in Trouble on the Homefront.

The pre-War baseball cap is undersized when worn by children. It is anchored inside the head mesh and will clip through a child-character-model's face and forehead.

Pre-War bonnet:
A pre-War woman's bonnet. The bonnet appears the same regardless of the gender of the wearer.
