itm_000340c1.summary: The kid's baseball cap is a headgear item used by kids who participate in baseball games.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The baseball cap is made of a soft fabric dyed red. The Pip-Boy 3000A categorizes the kid's baseball cap as an apparel item. There is an adult version of the cap.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Vault 101 (vanishes after Growing Up Fast).
• Reverse-pickpocket off of: Derek Pacion in Canterbury Commons. Biwwy and a generic Little Lamplight resident in Little Lamplight. Junior Smith in Andale.

itm_00033598.summary: Hockey masks are pieces of headwear in Fallout 3. Covering the face, they are off-white with red and blue stripes on it and have a worn appearance.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The benefits to the wearer of the hockey mask is that their Unarmed skill is raised by 5 points when equipped.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Hockey masks can be found throughout the Capital Wasteland, but can most often be found on raiders.
• Worn by the members of Sudden-Death Overtime.

itm_00033080.summary: Metal Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 5.0, value 70 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: A craft metal armor created from a variety of scrap pieces put on a black leather armor. The metal helmet is similar in shape to a motorcycle helmet, though with a dirty silver color instead of white, as well as no neck wrap or goggles for males, and for females, the helmet is made of rusted metal and is open faced, similar in shape to combat helmets (although it still muffles the user's voice while worn). The shoulder plates have metal spikes welded onto them.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Gamma shield armor FO3TP - The gamma shield armor isn't unique, but does have a few benefits over regular metal armor. The gamma shield armor adds to Radiation Resistance, but also weighs 15 more pounds.
• Samurai armor FO3MZ - The samurai armor, worn by Toshiro Kago, has a lower DR than metal armor, but increases Melee Weapons and total damage done by those weapons by 10.

• Apocalypse gladiator armor - Apocalypse gladiator armor and apocalypse gladiator helmet are an armor set cut from Fallout 3. They are identical with metal armor and metal helmet in terms of looks and stats except for an increased durability (75 instead of 50 item HP for the helmet and 1200 instead of 500 for the armor).

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Can be found on Leroy Walker at either Lincoln Memorial or Paradise Falls.
• Can sometimes (rarely) be bought from Moira at Craterside Supply in Megaton.
• Can occasionally be bought from Karl at Meresti Metro station.
• Can be found on Commander Jabsco at Fort Bannister.
• Can be found on Jotun and Ymir at Paradise Falls.
• Can be found in National Archives sub-basement behind a Very Hard locked gate.
• Can be found in a locked footlocker (average) at the entrance to the deathclaw sanctuary.
• Worn by the bandits who attack the Aqua Pura caravans in Broken Steel.
• Should one choose to join them, Split Jack will give the Lone Wanderer a suit and helmet.
• One helmet can always be found at the top of the Washington Monument, near the mattress.
• Can be bought from Flak 'n' Shrapnel in Rivet City.

itm_0003307e.summary: Raider Blastmaster Armor is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 16.0, value 180 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Worn by raiders, raider armor consists of scraps of clothing fabricated both before and after the Great War, armored with scavenged pieces of metal. Each variant of raider armor in Fallout 3 can be repaired using any of the other raider armors. The helmets can only be repaired with other copies of the same model; they cannot be used to repair each other.

Raider badlands armor:
A bandolier is draped across the front of the apparently leather overshirt (vaguely resembling a tank top), and on the left knee, there appears to be some sort of colander being used as a knee pad. The outfit also includes shorts made from either leather or some variety of canvas-like material. A screwdriver is secured near one boot, in similar fashion to a boot knife.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider armor:
Nine raider armor models are added in the add-on The Pitt and are randomly worn by the raiders in The Pitt, except for the Leather Rebel, Bombshell Armor, and Metal Master Armor, which are Mill Worker quest rewards.
• Bombshell armor FO3TP
• Leather Rebel FO3TP
• Metal Master armor FO3TP
• Raider iconoclast armor FO3TP
• Raider commando armor FO3TP
• Raider throwdown armor FO3TP
• Raider ordinance armor FO3TP
• Raider paingiver armor FO3TP
• Gamma shield armor FO3TP

• Hand-me-down raider armor (visually identical with raider sadist armor).
• Highway scar armor (visually identical with raider blastmaster armor).
• Sharp-dressed raider's armor, gives +10 speech and 1 CH (visually identical with raider painspike armor).

itm_0003307a.summary: Advanced Radiation Suit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 8.0, value 100 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: This suit has higher radiation resistance than any other armor or clothing in Fallout 3. It covers the entire body. As such, it is impossible to wear a helmet or glasses with this armor, except for the biker goggles.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Radiation suit
• Environment suit

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• It can be found deep within Vault 87, in the test labs. In the room with the lab technician's terminal (on a desk to the right), one of the options will be to unlock the storage room. Choose that option, then turn around and go back out the door that led into the room and turn left. That door is the storage room and contains an advanced radiation suit. Alternatively, the door can be unlocked with a Lockpick skill of 50.
• From level 7 onwards, another may be found in the Franklin Metro utility, in a box named radiation suit case, at the bottom of a flooded tunnel.
• Another two are in Mothership Zeta, in the operating room in the cryo lab, on a table.

itm_00033078.summary: The radiation suit is a suit that protects its wearer from the harmful effects of radiation to a certain extent. It is not a good idea to wear this in combat, however, as it has extremely low durability. This suit covers the entire body, and, as such, it cannot be worn with any helmet or glasses, with the exception of the biker goggles.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Advanced radiation suit
• Environment suit

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The radiation suit can be bought from Moira Brown in Craterside Supply.
• Can also sometimes be found at other fine retailers (such as Chief Gustavo in Tenpenny Tower or Flak & Shrapnel's in Rivet City).
• Can be found on a dead scientist, face-down in the back of a pool of radiation in the northern wastelands, near Oasis.
• Two suits can be found in the Wheaton Armory.
• One can be found on a dead scientist at the Greener Pastures disposal site.
• One can be found at the topside entrance of Vault 87 (the entrance is more irradiated than any other location in the game).
• Two can be found at the hidden irradiated pool, on the bodies of Isabella Proud and her colleague Jason.
• Two can be found in the office of Jalbert Brothers waste disposal.
• Two can be found in the armory of the National Guard depot.

itm_0003064d.summary: Recon armor and its matching recon armor helmet is a specialized suit of armor issued to East Coast Brotherhood of Steel initiates.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Intended to serve as the under-armor of the T-45d power armor, the recon armor is a vacuum-sealed asbestos jumpsuit covering the entire body. Attached to it is the interface and mounts for the T-45d power armor. Its purpose is twofold - it allows the user to actually operate the armor and protect soft tissue from heat and moving parts inside the suit. Unlike the under-armor for the T-51b power armor models, this one is also designed to offer limited protection from small-arm weapons.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Recon armor is ideal for stealth-based characters. Its Damage Resistance and Sneak bonus make it a good choice for early-game characters.

Recon armor can be used to repair Chinese stealth armor. Repairing this armor is difficult, as recon armor is relatively scarce. Most of the time the players will need to rely on an NPC for repairs.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Composite recon armor:
Composite recon armor is identical to recon armor in terms of stats and looks except for an increased durability. Composite recon helmet is a recon armor helmet with increased durability and an additional bonus of +1 to Perception. Only the helmet can be acquired by conventional means in Broken Steel, but both armor and helmet can be obtained by using console commands without the add-on.

Outcast recon armor:
The Outcast recon armor is, like the name suggests, a Brotherhood Outcasts version of the recon armor. It has the Outcasts' coloration, the armor is more valuable and the helmet gives +1 Perception. The armor and helmet are only available to the player using console commands.

Lyons' Pride recon armor:
It is the same as normal recon armor, except with a Lyons' Pride symbol.

itm_0002b385.summary: Roving Trader Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 2.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The suit can be repaired with other copies of itself, as well as various wasteland outfits. The hat can only be repaired using copies of itself. Both items can be worn to increase one's Barter skill by 5.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Roving trader outfit:
• Characters that wear the roving trader outfit include Ben Canning, wasteland merchants, Gallo, Smiling Jack, Quinn, Lucky Harith and Crazy Wolfgang.
• Can be found on scavengers (or their corpses) that wander around the Capital Wasteland.
• Can also be found on scavengers in random encounters, such as in front of the Super-Duper Mart, Broadcast tower KB5, or at Meresti trainyard.
• Two can be found on dead scavengers in the deathclaw sanctuary; one of them also has a roving trader hat.
• Dogmeat's old master, a scavenger, has one. The player character will find their corpse when they come across Dogmeat fighting four raiders in the Scrapyard.
• Can be bought from merchants.

Roving trader hat:
• Can be reverse pick-pocketed from Lucky Harith and Crow.
• Can be found on Evan King in Arefu.

itm_00025b83.summary: The Pip-Boy 3000 is a pre-War electronic Personal Information Processor (PIP) serving as a database for the wearer's personal information and inventory. It appears and.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Manufactured by RobCo Industries, copies of the Pip-Boy 3000 model were distributed to the residents of Vault-Tec Vaults both in the American Southwest and on the East Coast prior to the Great War, in supplies large enough that generations over a span of 200 years were still able to receive one.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: In both Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas, the Pip-Boy is worn on the character's left forearm. The default Pip-Boy access buttons are the key on PC, the circle button on PS3, and B on Xbox 360. This multifunction device has been programmed by Pip-Boy developers to display the wearer's stats, area maps, inventory, and item properties. It also includes a Geiger counter and a radio. Its screen doubles as a flashlight for fixing visibility issues in dark or obscured areas (enabled by holding down the access button). A user can set their color preference for the display. The four colors available are amber, blue, green, and white. The color chosen will also affect VATS and the UI. The display color must be changed through the pause menu rather than the Pip-Boy itself. By default it is set to green in Fallout 3 and amber in Fallout: New Vegas.

sections.title: Functions (Fallout 3)
sections.text:
STATS tab:
• Status - Displays the user's condition, radiation levels, and any effects that are currently active.
• CND - Condition: Status of limbs, number of stimpaks, and enables directional application of stimpaks to crippled areas or to the body as a whole.
• RAD - Radiation: Precise reading of user's radiation level using internal Geiger counter and options to administer Rad-X and RadAway as necessary.
• EFF - Effects: Displays effects of currently equipped clothing, radiation level, chemicals the user has ingested, the well-rested function, any addictions the user may have, as well as any crippled limbs.
• S.P.E.C.I.A.L. - Displays the user's SPECIAL information as well as indicating positive(+) or negative effects on these levels.

itm_000239cc.summary: The security uniform and matching security helmet are pieces of armor in Fallout 3. It comes in two versions with different visual appearances but identical stats.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Rivet City security force uniform and the matching Rivet City security helmet are the standard protection for members of Rivet City security force. Whereas the Tenpenny security uniform is worn by the guards of Tenpenny Tower, the Tenpenny security helmet can be found in the game files but is not actually used in the game.

The two security uniforms have the lowest Damage Resistance out of all combat armor variants, offering slightly less protection than even the Talon combat armor. Actually, they provide no better protection than ordinary leather armor and weigh more, thus reducing both movement speed and sneak characteristics. Nonetheless, they provide better protection than most clothing worn in the wasteland, including merc outfits and raider armor, and convey a bonus of +5 to Small Guns.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The uniforms can be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing or killing a guard and looting their corpse. Dusty of Big Town, who wears one of the helmets, is the only character to wear a part of a Rivet City uniform without living in Rivet City.
• A Rivet City security guard may be found in one of the holding cells in Mothership Zeta.

itm_000239cb.summary: The security uniform and matching security helmet are pieces of armor in Fallout 3. It comes in two versions with different visual appearances but identical stats.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Rivet City security force uniform and the matching Rivet City security helmet are the standard protection for members of Rivet City security force. Whereas the Tenpenny security uniform is worn by the guards of Tenpenny Tower, the Tenpenny security helmet can be found in the game files but is not actually used in the game.

The two security uniforms have the lowest Damage Resistance out of all combat armor variants, offering slightly less protection than even the Talon combat armor. Actually, they provide no better protection than ordinary leather armor and weigh more, thus reducing both movement speed and sneak characteristics. Nonetheless, they provide better protection than most clothing worn in the wasteland, including merc outfits and raider armor, and convey a bonus of +5 to Small Guns.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The uniforms can be obtained by reverse-pickpocketing or killing a guard and looting their corpse. Dusty of Big Town, who wears one of the helmets, is the only character to wear a part of a Rivet City uniform without living in Rivet City.
• A Rivet City security guard may be found in one of the holding cells in Mothership Zeta.

itm_0002042f.summary: Raider Painspike Armor is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 16.0, value 180 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Worn by raiders, raider armor consists of scraps of clothing fabricated both before and after the Great War, armored with scavenged pieces of metal. Each variant of raider armor in Fallout 3 can be repaired using any of the other raider armors. The helmets can only be repaired with other copies of the same model; they cannot be used to repair each other.

Raider badlands armor:
A bandolier is draped across the front of the apparently leather overshirt (vaguely resembling a tank top), and on the left knee, there appears to be some sort of colander being used as a knee pad. The outfit also includes shorts made from either leather or some variety of canvas-like material. A screwdriver is secured near one boot, in similar fashion to a boot knife.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Pitt raider armor:
Nine raider armor models are added in the add-on The Pitt and are randomly worn by the raiders in The Pitt, except for the Leather Rebel, Bombshell Armor, and Metal Master Armor, which are Mill Worker quest rewards.
• Bombshell armor FO3TP
• Leather Rebel FO3TP
• Metal Master armor FO3TP
• Raider iconoclast armor FO3TP
• Raider commando armor FO3TP
• Raider throwdown armor FO3TP
• Raider ordinance armor FO3TP
• Raider paingiver armor FO3TP
• Gamma shield armor FO3TP

• Hand-me-down raider armor (visually identical with raider sadist armor).
• Highway scar armor (visually identical with raider blastmaster armor).
• Sharp-dressed raider's armor, gives +10 speech and 1 CH (visually identical with raider painspike armor).

itm_0002042e.summary: Tunnel Snake Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 4.0, value 8 caps). Linked to quests: Escape!.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: It is a leather jacket with a snake emblem on the back, worn on top of a Vault 101 jumpsuit. It is worn by the Tunnel Snakes gang in Vault 101 and provides a Damage Resistance of 4 and a bonus of 5 to Melee Weapons. To repair it, the Lone Wanderer needs another Tunnel Snake outfit.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• During Escape!:
• One can help Butch DeLoria save his mother from radroaches during the quest (in any of the available ways). Once the roaches are dead, Butch will reward the player character with his outfit.
• Instead of helping him, one can just kill Butch (or allow him to be killed by radroaches) and then loot his jacket.
• After completing Trouble on the Homefront:
• One can obtain this outfit by killing Butch in Rivet City.
• If the player character has sabotaged Vault 101, they can loot the Tunnel Snake outfit from Freddie Gomez's body in a random encounter.
• The Lone Wanderer can reverse pickpocket better armor on him without having to sabotage the vault, by taking better armor with them inside, such as raider armor.
• Three more can be obtained in Vault 106.

itm_00020426.summary: Combat Helmet is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 5.0, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Combat armor is among the best forms of protection in the post-War Capital Wasteland. It has the fifth-highest DR for non-power armors, only lower than Ranger battle armor, Lag-Bolt's combat armor (only available with Broken Steel), metal armor, and Metal Master armor. It is fairly useful for early to mid-level characters, as it can probably be acquired before the Ranger armor, and doesn't have the penalty to Agility that metal armor has.

Unlike the reinforced variants common on the West Coast, all the combat armor available in the Capital Wasteland is short-sleeved, having only the shoulder pads and chest plates covering the torso. Plates covering the groin, knee, shin and foot are also featured.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Cut versions:
• Sim regen armor
• Shellshocked combat armor (Identical to standard combat armor - Form ID:, helmet: ).

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: Unique apparel are highlighted with a darker background

itm_0001ea6d.summary: Pre-War Casualwear is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 3.0, value 8 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: When equipped, none grant any Damage Resistance or Damage Threshold, but all outfit variants grant a temporary +1 Agility and all hats grants a temporary +1 Perception. Casualwear and relaxedwear can be repaired with other instances of each other, while parkstroller and spring outfits can be repaired of other instances of each other. With the Jury Rigging perk, all outfits can be repaired with instances of all others as well as both light armor and other pieces in the "clothing" and "headgear" categories.

sections.title: Outfits
sections.text:
(Dirty) pre-War casualwear:
The male version consists of a brown sweater-vest and a pair of brown pants while the female version consists of a blue dress and heels.

(Dirty) pre-War relaxedwear:
The male version consists of a green sweater-vest and khaki slacks while the female version consists of a yellowish/brown dress, black belt, and black heels.

(Dirty) pre-War spring outfit:
The male version consists of a red plaid shirt and brown pants while the female version consists of a pink dress with red heels.

(Dirty) pre-War parkstroller outfit:
The male version consists of a gray short-sleeved button-up shirt and blue jeans while the female version consists of a greenish-yellow dress and heels.

sections.title: Headwear
sections.text:
Pre-War hat:
A worn brown leather hat.
• It can be found in most homes of any given non-player character.
• Can also be found in the inventory of any random merchant that sells apparel.
• Many of the Omerta thugs wear them, including Big Sal.
• In Goodsprings there are two - one in Doc Mitchell's house, one can be bought from Chet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.
• In one of the motel rooms of El Rey Motel.

Pre-War baseball cap:
A red baseball cap with a brim in the front.
• Can be found on the corpse south of Goodsprings laying on the cliff visited during Barton the Fink
• Can appear being worn by Powder Gangers

Pre-War bonnet:
A pre-War woman's bonnet.
• Many can be found at Vault 19 in the dressers of the rooms in the blue and red sectors of the vault.

itm_0001dc1c.summary: Ghoul Mask is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 3.0, value 50 caps). Linked to quests: Tenpenny Tower.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A mask which completely covers the face and appears to consist of multiple patches of feral ghoul skin sewn together. It provides a Damage Resistance of 3.

The hidden unique effect of the mask is that while equipped, feral ghouls cannot turn hostile against the player character and their companions unless provoked. Although it is stated in-game that feral ghouls will attack despite the mask if you stay too close to them for too long, this is not true. You can stand next to them indefinitely, follow them around or even try to talk to them.

Despite the mask being considered headwear, it is counted as a piece of eyewear and not as "full" headwear, like the hockey mask and its unique variant. As such, certain headwear can be worn with it. In addition, any worn helmet will not degrade while wearing this mask.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The headwear is obtained by siding with Roy Phillips when completing the Tenpenny Tower quest, either by helping Roy directly or killing all the human residents of Tenpenny Tower independently and then talking to him in the metro tunnels.

itm_0001cbdd.summary: Vault 101 security armor and Vault 101 security helmet are a suit of armor worn by the vault security officers.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: It consists of a riot helmet with a hinged, acrylic visor and a padded, puncture-resistant vest. Although this armor has a relatively low Damage Resistance rating, it will be the first set of armor the Lone Wanderer will be able to possess and will provide basic protection against early-game foes. The Vault 101 security armor also has little or no movement penalties, allowing characters to move quicker than with other, bulkier variants.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Worn by Vault 101 security officers.
• If Susie Mack is encountered in the wasteland, she will be wearing the Vault 101 security armor without the helmet.
• In Vault 101's atrium/upper level, two sets are found in the security station, in the weapon lockers.

itm_0001cbdb.summary: Wasteland Settler Outfit is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 2.0, value 6 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Crudely made, they provide only the most basic of protection and are easy to come by, as they can be bought from traders, can be found on many corpses or inside several homes throughout the Capital Wasteland, it can also be found on most Megaton settlers.

Wasteland outfits can be repaired with brahmin-skin outfits, wasteland settler outfits, wasteland wanderer outfits, wasteland surgeon outfits, wasteland doctor fatigues, and roving trader outfits. The matching headwear can only be repaired with other copies of their respective model.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Brahmin-skin outfit:
A dirty off-white in color (gray for the coveralls), the brahmin-skin outfit consists of a crudely-stitched pair of overalls and a patched shirt. They appear to have received only the most rudimentary treatment in tanning and tailoring.

Wasteland legend outfit:
The wasteland legend outfit is identical to the merc veteran outfit. It will spawn randomly in lockers and footlockers or be sold by merchants. It can also be found on various enemies throughout the Capital Wasteland.

Wasteland settler outfit:
The wasteland settler outfit consists of a green, rag-like shirt and a pair of gray-brown pants.

Wasteland wanderer outfit:
The wasteland wanderer outfit is a tan jacket with a hood and off-white pants tucked into riding boots.

itm_00015038.summary: The Pip-Boy 3000 is a pre-War electronic Personal Information Processor (PIP) serving as a database for the wearer's personal information and inventory. It appears and.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Manufactured by RobCo Industries, copies of the Pip-Boy 3000 model were distributed to the residents of Vault-Tec Vaults both in the American Southwest and on the East Coast prior to the Great War, in supplies large enough that generations over a span of 200 years were still able to receive one.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: In both Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas, the Pip-Boy is worn on the character's left forearm. The default Pip-Boy access buttons are the key on PC, the circle button on PS3, and B on Xbox 360. This multifunction device has been programmed by Pip-Boy developers to display the wearer's stats, area maps, inventory, and item properties. It also includes a Geiger counter and a radio. Its screen doubles as a flashlight for fixing visibility issues in dark or obscured areas (enabled by holding down the access button). A user can set their color preference for the display. The four colors available are amber, blue, green, and white. The color chosen will also affect VATS and the UI. The display color must be changed through the pause menu rather than the Pip-Boy itself. By default it is set to green in Fallout 3 and amber in Fallout: New Vegas.

sections.title: Functions (Fallout 3)
sections.text:
STATS tab:
• Status - Displays the user's condition, radiation levels, and any effects that are currently active.
• CND - Condition: Status of limbs, number of stimpaks, and enables directional application of stimpaks to crippled areas or to the body as a whole.
• RAD - Radiation: Precise reading of user's radiation level using internal Geiger counter and options to administer Rad-X and RadAway as necessary.
• EFF - Effects: Displays effects of currently equipped clothing, radiation level, chemicals the user has ingested, the well-rested function, any addictions the user may have, as well as any crippled limbs.
• S.P.E.C.I.A.L. - Displays the user's SPECIAL information as well as indicating positive(+) or negative effects on these levels.

itm_00014e13.summary: Power Armor is a armor / apparel in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (DR 40.0, value 740 caps). Linked to quests: Take it Back!.

itm_0000431e.summary: Vault jumpsuits or Vault suits (terms used interchangeably) are the iconic gear of Vault dwellers and by and large the symbol of Vault-Tec Corporation, being worn by mascots Vault Boy and Vault Girl.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Designed specifically for use within Vaults, jumpsuits are an inexpensive, easily produced solution to the age-old problem of clothing large numbers of people while maintaining a modicum of comfort and utility. Within the Vaults, they are also meant to reduce tension by providing every dweller with the same type of clothes, regardless of their standing. Marketed as a fashionable, comfortable design, before the war, they were an instantly recognizable symbol of both Vaults and the corporation behind them, featuring an iconic blue-and-yellow color scheme. Barb Howard implies that this color scheme was inspired by Cooper Howard's blue-and-gold sheriff's outfit from his western films.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Armor / Apparel from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: VaultSuit101). Weight: 1.0, Value: 8 caps. Effects: Speech +2, Melee Weapons +2.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage

itm_000c5634.summary: Wasteland Survival Guide is a skill book in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 1 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This is one of the rewards for the Wasteland Survival Guide quest. It has no purpose other than to serve as game flavor. In addition to the one given to the Lone Wanderer at the end of the quest, additional copies can be found in the possession of wastelanders in a random encounter which occurs after the quest has been completed. It is much larger than an ordinary book.

The description for the book is composed of four sections, which changes depending on the quality of the book, and the tone in which it was written. The book is composed of three chapters—Survive, Thrive, and Revive—which correspond to the three sets of three missions Moira gives the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Book description
sections.text:
Most sections are only decided by how many chapters are complete, not which ones, so each chapter has been organized based on this number.

In sections where the tone of the Lone Wanderer's responses makes a difference, text is displayed in the order Standard-Snide-Sly-Tough-Smart.

Example complete description:
By putting together the appropriate sections from below, completing every bonus objective and using standard responses would yield the following description for the book:
Lead Author and Subject Matter Expert:
Assistant Author: Moira Brown

This indispensable guidebook contains everything that a survivor in the wasteland could need to know.

Every page contains a gem of brilliant insight into how to survive in the wastes, thrive among its denizens, and revive your survivor community.

sections.title: First Section: Credit
sections.text:
This is the section where Moira Brown credits herself and the Lone Wanderer for completing the book. Depending on how many total chapters are complete, Moira will credit the Lone Wanderer with more or less of the work.

All chapters complete:
Lead Author and Subject Matter Expert:
Assistant Author: Moira Brown

2 chapters complete:
Author: Moira Brown
Expert Researcher:

1 chapter complete:
Author: Moira Brown
Researcher:

No chapters complete:

itm_000ab2ef.summary: You're SPECIAL! is a book published and written for children by Vault-Tec. This book identifies the seven key attributes that are viewed as the most desirable in a Vault resident. The attributes are as follows in order: Strength, Perception, Endurance, Charisma, Intelligence, Agility, and Luck (S.P.E.C.I.A.L.). Each of the attributes is given a brief description.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: This book is the first opportunity the player character has for building their personality and skills. Each of the attributes is initially assigned five points. There are an additional five points for distributing across each attribute. This gives a total of forty points (5 x 7 = 35 points + 5 points = 40 points) that can be distributed among each attribute. The maximum number of points allotted to an attribute is ten points, with the minimum being one, meaning that only 33 of the 40 points can be truly distributed to one's discretion.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• FO3 Vault 101, in the Lone Wanderer's playroom, during Baby Steps.
• FO4 Sole Survivor's house, in Shaun's room.

itm_0005a795.summary: Wasteland Survival Guide is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 1 caps). Linked to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This is one of the rewards for the Wasteland Survival Guide quest. It has no purpose other than to serve as game flavor. In addition to the one given to the Lone Wanderer at the end of the quest, additional copies can be found in the possession of wastelanders in a random encounter which occurs after the quest has been completed. It is much larger than an ordinary book.

The description for the book is composed of four sections, which changes depending on the quality of the book, and the tone in which it was written. The book is composed of three chapters—Survive, Thrive, and Revive—which correspond to the three sets of three missions Moira gives the Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Book description
sections.text:
Most sections are only decided by how many chapters are complete, not which ones, so each chapter has been organized based on this number.

In sections where the tone of the Lone Wanderer's responses makes a difference, text is displayed in the order Standard-Snide-Sly-Tough-Smart.

Example complete description:
By putting together the appropriate sections from below, completing every bonus objective and using standard responses would yield the following description for the book:
Lead Author and Subject Matter Expert:
Assistant Author: Moira Brown

This indispensable guidebook contains everything that a survivor in the wasteland could need to know.

Every page contains a gem of brilliant insight into how to survive in the wastes, thrive among its denizens, and revive your survivor community.

sections.title: First Section: Credit
sections.text:
This is the section where Moira Brown credits herself and the Lone Wanderer for completing the book. Depending on how many total chapters are complete, Moira will credit the Lone Wanderer with more or less of the work.

All chapters complete:
Lead Author and Subject Matter Expert:
Assistant Author: Moira Brown

2 chapters complete:
Author: Moira Brown
Expert Researcher:

1 chapter complete:
Author: Moira Brown
Researcher:

No chapters complete:
Author: Moira Brown
Research Assistant:

itm_000c8503.summary: Android Component is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 0 caps). Linked to quests: The Replicated Man.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: These internal components are used inside "androids" (synths) developed by the Institute. According to Dr. Zimmer, they are unique to advanced androids like A3-21 (i.e. generation 3 synths) and would not be removable unless the android it was taken from had already been killed. However, this is untrue: according to Victoria Watts from the Railroad, an android component was successfully removed from A3-21 without causing his death. Furthermore, androids have more than one of these components, as A3-21 still possesses one which can be removed on death even though Victoria Watts had already extracted one from him.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The android component is a fully weightless and valueless item used for The Replicated Man. Appearance-wise, the component looks like a 10A power fuse, identical to the fuse used to restore power to the Jefferson Memorial during The Waters of Life.

sections.title: Related quest
sections.text: • The Replicated Man: The player character will acquire an android component from Victoria Watts and is given the option of using it to convince Dr. Zimmer that the missing android he is looking for is dead. Android components will be considered as quest items until The Replicated Man is completed or failed.

itm_000033ff.summary: The Soil Stradivarius (pronounced "swal") was one of the most prized and unique instruments ever made by the Italian craftsman Antonio Stradivari.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The Soil Stradivarius is a violin that was built by Antonio Stradivari in 1714; its name, like other Stradivarius violins, was given to it later over time. Prior to the Great War, the Soil was owned by Hilda Egglebrecht, a talented violinist. She kept the instrument in a specially-made case which would maintain the exact conditions needed to keep the instrument in perfect shape. After she was invited to enter Vault 92, a vault purportedly dedicated to preserving musical talent, Hilda took the Stradivarius with her inside. After the failure of Vault 92's experiment, the Soil Stradivarius has since remained within the depths of the deteriorating vault for the following two centuries.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The violin can be found in Vault 92's sound testing block in a recording studio, which is the southernmost room there. It is on a wooden table. To enter, activate the studio computer on the other side of that hallway.

sections.title: Related quest
sections.text: • Agatha's Song: Agatha, an elderly violinist and descendant of Hilda Egglebrecht, tasks the Lone Wanderer with recovering the Soil Stradivarius for her. The violin can then be given to her, or alternatively sold to Abraham Washington in Rivet City or Ahzrukhal in Underworld (and then can be optionally recovered and given to Agatha).

itm_000bb000.summary: Schematics - Shishkebab are the schematics needed to make a Shishkebab, a Melee Weapons skill weapon in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: As with all non-explosive custom weapons, possessing multiple copies of the schematics increases the initial condition of the weapon – one copy gives a condition equal to 75% of a character's Repair skill, two gets 100%, and three gets 125%.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One set of schematics can be obtained from Vance at the end of the Blood Ties questline. You can also kill Vance to obtain his Shishkebab (it is fully functional but very degraded).
• Lucky Harith, the weapon specialized caravan merchant, sells a set of schematics.
• One on a table in an unmarked Brotherhood Outcast shack west of SatCom Array NN-03d.

sections.title: Components
sections.text:
Once you have the schematics, you will need a workbench and one each of the following items:

Component locations:
• The Benson house in Minefield has all the parts
• All of the parts needed can be easily found around the town of Minefield; you'll find a motorcycle gas tank and motorcycle handbrake just outside Gillian house`s front door and you can find a pilot light at the Gibson house just to the right when you enter the house, inside the oven in the kitchen, and there are broken lawn mowers all over Minefield with lawn mower blades inside.
• All parts (motorcycle gas tank, motorcycle handbrake and a lawn mower blade) with the exception of the pilot light can be found right outside the CO Headquarters shack at Fort Constantine. A pilot light can be found inside the CO Headquarters.

itm_000bafff.summary: The schematics - Rock-It Launcher are the schematics needed to make the Big Guns weapon "Rock-It Launcher" in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Possessing multiple copies of schematics increases the initial repair condition of the weapon: One copy gives a condition percent equal to 75% of the player's repair skill, two gets 100%, and three gets 125%. While four copies of the schematic exist in the game, having the fourth copy does not improve your weapon's initial condition.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Can be bought off Moira Brown in Megaton for a price of 799–1200 bottle caps, depending on Barter skill level and whether the player has the Dream Crusher perk.
• In the armory of Rivet City, located in the ship's bridge tower, behind a Very Hard locked door. On the shelf to the left when you walk in.
• Can also be bought, stolen via pickpocketing or by killing the traveling merchant Crazy Wolfgang.
• Another copy of the schematics can be found in the "Framed Quote" within the Vault 101 clinic.

sections.title: Components
sections.text:
Once the player character has the schematics, they will need a workbench and one of each of the following items:
• Vacuum cleaner
• Leaf blower
• Firehose nozzle
• Conductor

Component locations:
• All items (including schematics) can be bought at Craterside Supply in Megaton.
• A few of the components can be stolen in Lucky's (Lucky's also has all of the components needed to make a shishkebab, dart gun and Nuka-grenade). Another such location is the room that Horace Pinkerton has taken refuge in at the Rivet City bow, which contains practically everything needed to make all of the crafted weapons.

itm_0005b6d0.summary:
A wrench or spanner is a tool used to provide grip and mechanical leverage in applying torque to turn objects, usually rotary fasteners, such as nuts and bolts.

In Fallout 2 and Fallout Tactics, it is used as a weapon, while in Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas it remains as a simple miscellaneous item, used to make weapon repair kits. In Fallout 4 and Fallout 76, wrenches are junk items, while pipe wrenches are used as weapons.

sections.title: Models
sections.text:
Regular wrench:
A typical wrench used by mechanics.

Adjustable wrench:
A wrench with a movable jaw that adapts the tool to different sized objects.
• For the unique version found in Fallout 3, see: Donovan's wrench.
• For the cut content version found in Fallout 3 Mothership Zeta add-on, see: Spanner.

Combination wrench:
A wrench with two different ends, an open end and a socket end, to maximise utility. Useful both as a tool and for scrap.

Pipe wrench:
A wrench with two serrated jaws designed for assembling or disassembling cylindrical objects like pipes. It has been converted into a weapon after the Great War.
• For the unique version found in Fallout 76, see: Mechanic's Best Friend

Rusty old monkey wrench:
A typical wrench used by mechanics for hurting people.

Heavy wrench:
A typical wrench used by mechanics for hurting people.

itm_0008c216.summary: The Gettysburg Address is a historical speech by Abraham Lincoln which appears as a static world object and a cut miscellaneous item in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The Gettysburg Address, as it came to be known, was a speech given by President Abraham Lincoln in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania on November 19, 1863, after a major battle was fought there. In the speech, Lincoln invoked the principles of human equality espoused by the Declaration of Independence and redefined the American Civil War as a struggle not merely for the Union, but as a "new birth of freedom" that would bring true equality to all of its citizens.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
• A static world object version of the Gettysburg Address is displayed at the Capitol Preservation Society in Rivet City.
• The text of the Gettysburg Address can be seen, in its entirety, inscribed on the south wall of the Lincoln Memorial.
• If Head of State is completed in favor of the Abolitionists, and they reclaim the Lincoln Memorial, then Hannibal Hamlin will stand in front of Lincoln's statue in the memorial every day from 1 to 2 p.m. and recite the full Gettysburg Address. Hannibal's delivery of the speech can be heard above.

itm_0008c215.summary: The Emancipation Proclamation is a historical document mentioned in Fallout 3. It also exists in physical assets which are cut content in the game.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Emancipation Proclamation was a wartime executive order issued by President Abraham Lincoln in 1862, during the American Civil War. The proclamation declared the freedom of all slaves in states of the Confederate States of America. This marked the "beginning of the end" for institutionalized slavery in the United States; it reframed the Civil War as not just being about preserving the Union, but also upholding core principles of equality in abolishing slavery, with Lincoln alluding to these goals in his subsequent Gettysburg Address.

After the war, abolitionists were concerned that since the proclamation was a war measure, it had not permanently ended slavery. This would subsequently come to pass with the adoption of the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: Daniel Littlehorn from Littlehorn & Associates, located at the scrapyard, rewards the Lone Wanderer with 10 to 15 caps and -10 Karma for each ear. This is the bad Karma alternative to the Lawbringer perk, in which fingers are collected instead of ears.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Ears can be found on good characters (such as Abraham Washington or Agatha) when the Contract Killer perk has been chosen.
• If other characters (including partners, guards, and the Mysterious Stranger), creatures, or environmental aspects (such as: an exploding cars) do more then 50% of the target's total HP in damage, an ear will not appear on the body.
• An easy way to earn ears is to go to Rivet City, as the security guards there respawn every three days.
• The most abundant supply of ears that can be found are off of Regulators which are encountered randomly through having negative Karma.
• Slaver-hunting hitmen are also a good supplier of ears, should one also choose to be a slaver.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
An ophthalmoscope is a medical instrument used to examine the eyes. However, the object in the game resembles an otoscope, which is used to examine the ears.

The ophthalmoscope can be recognized as the medical instrument James uses to observe the Lone Wanderer's eyes before the G.O.A.T. exam. However, no light appears to be emitted from the ophthalmoscope, which is necessary to effectively examine the eyes.

This item can be used as Rock-It Launcher ammunition.

• In the utility tunnels near the White House plaza, in the first room on the right.

itm_0003d34d.summary: The G.E.C.K. (Garden of Eden Creation Kit) is a terraforming device created by Future-Tec, a division of Vault-Tec Corporation, to ease the process of harnessing the post-nuclear wasteland for Vault dwellers.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Developed by Stanislaus Braun, the kit contains the basic amenities needed to establish a post-nuclear settlement. Although advertised as a miracle solution for a land ravaged by nuclear warfare, the G.E.C.K. was based on a variety of assumptions about the post-nuclear world, as its creators had no real way to determine what challenges the survivors of the nuclear war would face.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Packed into a large, silvered briefcase with the kit's abbreviation, the G.E.C.K. was intended to be standard equipment for all Vaults, as a fully self-contained terraforming module capable of creating and sustaining life in a post-War environment. Vault-Tec proudly declared that, "even in the event of total global annihilation, a properly functioning G.E.C.K. will create an earthly paradise."

In reality, it was a more modest tool. The kit included seed and soil supplements, a cold fusion power generator, matter-energy replicators, atmospheric chemical stabilizers and water purifiers.

Reading material and information was included with the kit, including selections from the Library of Congress, a complete set of encyclopedias, and other information that would benefit those trying to survive.

itm_0003bd33.summary: Modified FEV Virus is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 0 caps). Linked to quests: Death From Above, The American Dream.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The sealed vial contains a modified strain of the Forced Evolutionary Virus developed by Enclave president John Henry Eden around 2277, based on the earlier FEV Curling-13 strain used by the Chemical Corps in 2241. Eden intended for it to be placed into the water purification system making up the core of Project Purity beneath the Jefferson Memorial, acting on his altered version of pre-War classified plans made by the former US government that allegedly never came to fruition.

According to President Eden, the virus is designed to only target the physiology of super mutants, ghouls, and all other "unclean" citizens, namely anyone who had been born in the wasteland and exposed to its environmental radiation and other mutational effects from birth.

sections.title: Effects
sections.text:
While in the base game of Fallout 3, the effects of using the modified FEV are only implied during the ending slide, during the events of the add-on Broken Steel, set two weeks after the activation of Project Purity, they are shown in full. if the player character decided to contaminate the purifier with the modified FEV, what President Eden said of its capabilities is confirmed as accurate and the FEV proves to be completely lethal to the wasteland at large.

The medical facility of every city in the Capital Wasteland (excluding Tenpenny Tower and Paradise Falls) is filled with new patients dying from FEV infection.

itm_0002d3a5.summary: The food sanitizer, officially the Tastee Cleen Sanitizer, is a miscellaneous item in Fallout 3. It was produced by Abraxodyne Chemical.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The food sanitizer has a passive effect on the user's food items as long as it is in their inventory. While in the inventory, the food sanitizer will increase the HP value restored by most consumables by 20%.

Equation: Initial HP x 1.2 (or 120%) = final amount of HP

Example: Nuka-Cola 10 HP x 1.2 = 12 HP

The food sanitizer has no effect on other types of consumables, and will not reduce any adverse effects, such as the food's radiation rating. Furthermore, it has no effect on alcoholic beverages, purified water, bubblegum, gum drops, Nuka-Cola Quantum, Mississippi Quantum pie, the alien food found on Mothership Zeta, and the slop dished out in the Pitt. It does work on fresh fruits and vegetables, Punga fruit from the Point Lookout add-on and the three new water varieties from the Broken Steel add-on.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: It is awarded after finding the medicine in the Super-Duper Mart as part of the Wasteland Survival Guide quest, along with the sanitizer instructions. According to the sanitizer instructions, it will cleanse most food and drink in the user's inventory of harmful bacteria, allowing greater nutritional gain. The food sanitizer is not a quest item, and as such will be temporarily removed from the inventory in certain situations.

itm_0002920f.summary: Metro Ticket is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 1 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Metro tickets are requested at any metro station in the Capital Wasteland that still has active Protectrons. Having a ticket can prevent making one of these robots hostile.

These Protectrons are inactive by default, but can be activated by hacking a nearby terminal as they then come out of their capsule and search the area for hostiles and passengers. When a Protectron is activated, it will approach a target and scan for a ticket. If it finds one on them, it will take the ticket and let the person move along.

sections.text:
• Found commonly in metro stations.
• Some feral ghouls in the metro tunnels carry tickets.
• One in a desk at Carol's Place.
• One in a desk in the County sewer mainline.
• One in a desk at Dupont Circle station, near a protectron pod.
• In two desks inside the Farragut West station, another one on a console near a protectron pod.
• One on a desk near a protectron pod inside Anacostia Crossing Station.
• One on a desk near a protectron pod inside Metro Central.
• One on a desk near a protectron pod inside Foggy Bottom station.
• FO3BS 46 tickets can be found scattered throughout Olney Powerworks. In the building, there are 36 metro tickets assembled in a traditional triangular card stack on a desk.
• FO3BS Old Olney S. Wilson Building, 10 held by an intact garden gnome and a teddy bear, using them as playing cards.

itm_00028ee9.summary: The Lincoln Memorial poster is a quest item in Fallout 3. which can serve as the reference needed by Caleb Smith as part of the quest Head of State. It is a poster of the Lincoln Memorial.

sections.text:
The poster is located in the Museum of History's Museum Offices, on the topmost floor, over a desk and on the wall just to the left of the top of the staircase to that level (Lincoln's voice is on the next desk). The poster will not spawn until after starting Head of State.

To easily find this, go to the cell at the rear of the Museum Offices and go up the staircase leading to the highest floor. Directly at the top of that staircase, the poster will be on the wall next to a desk and a filing cabinet that has fallen over, and can identified by its yellowed border.

sections.title: Related quest
sections.text:
• Head of State
• Lincoln's Profit Margins

sections.text: Forceps are a type of pre-War handheld medical equipment used for grasping and holding items during surgery. Forceps are frequently accompanying similar equipment on compartment trays. itm_000250a6.summary: Tweezers is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 3 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The tweezers are a type of pre-War handheld medical equipment used for grasping and extracting during surgery. They have two pincers and a small handle for handling by one hand, and can be used a ammunition for the Rock-It Launcher.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:

• My First Infirmary, when the Lone Wanderer purchases it from Moira for their house in Megaton or Lydia Montenegro for their suite in Tenpenny Tower.

itm_000250a5.summary: Scalpel is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 5 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The scalpel is a pre-War hand-held medical equipment used for cutting flesh and tissue during surgery. This item is portable, can be placed on any flat surface, and is made of stainless steel. A scalpel has a sharp cutting edge and a handle for use with one hand.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: It is useful only as Rock-It Launcher ammunition.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Scalpels can be found randomly in most first aid boxes across the Capital Wasteland. They can also be found in most medical facilities lying on tables and trays, such as James' office and the Megaton clinic. There are also two in Red's clinic in Big Town.

itm_000250a4.summary: Scissors is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 3 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
They are a piece of pre-War hand-held medical equipment used during surgery. Scissors are a portable item, can be placed on any flat surface, and are made of tungsten carbide.

Identified as a Metzenbaum style of scissor, it has shanks for holding and controlling the item and the blade tips are blunted. These items are associated with other hand-held medical equipment on compartment trays and are often accompanying them.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: They are only useful as Rock-It Launcher ammunition.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
These items can be found in clinics across the Capital Wasteland.
• Three in the Anchorage Memorial facility.
• Three in the Underworld concourse.
• Two in Vault 101's clinic.
• Four in Tenpenny Tower's lobbies.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A bonesaw is a type of pre-War handheld medical tool used primarily for amputations. The item is portable, has a metal saw for cutting into flesh and bone, and a wooden handle. This item is associated with other handheld medical equipment on a compartment tray and often accompanies them. The Pip-Boy categorizes the bonesaw as a junk item. It is therefore useful only as Rock-It Launcher ammunition as it cannot be used as a weapon.

Bonesaws are found on the "My First Infirmary" house improvement for the Lone Wanderer's house or suite.

sections.title: Locations

• Big Town in Red's clinic.
• Megaton clinic
• Springvale school restroom on ground floor.
• Vault 87 clinic.
• Vault 101 clinic
• Vault 112 clinic.
• Temple of the Union storeroom.
• Anchorage Memorial clinic.

itm_0001edc5.summary: Brotherhood of Steel Holotag is a misc / quest item in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (value 1 caps). Linked to quests: DC Ruins Exploration.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• The inhabitants of the Citadel wear the item and they can be looted from their corpses. In doing so, this can garner dozens of holotags, particularly with the Broken Steel add-on. Scribe Jameson, along with the rest of the faction in the Citadel A ring, will not turn hostile if their comrades are killed in different sections (e.g. courtyard, lab, B ring) if they do not witness it.
• In the Citadel A ring there is one in the den on the small desk just before the room with the beds.
• Taft Tunnel, on the Citadel end, has a living Brotherhood paladin with one that can be looted when they are killed.
• Citadel exterior, the unnamed Brotherhood members high on the catwalks using the sniper nests (due south of the Citadel gates) may be killed as well (the unnamed member outside near the sentry bot only gets knocked unconscious).

sections.title: Related quest
sections.text: • Collecting Holotags: In Fallout 3, holotags recovered from fallen Brotherhood members can be turned in to Scribe Jameson at the Citadel (A-Ring archives) in exchange for 100 caps and 25 XP each, but only before embarking on the Take it Back! quest. With Broken Steel, this can be continued beyond that quest. Jameson also talks about offering technology from time to time in return but never gives any.

itm_00003a7f.summary: The Declaration of Independence is an item found in the ruins of D.C's National Archives. It can be recovered by the Lone Wanderer for the Rivet City historian Abraham Washington.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
The Declaration of Independence is a pronouncement adopted by the Second Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, announcing that the thirteen American colonies were now sovereign states, no longer under British rule. The ruler of Great Britain when the Declaration was enacted was King George III.

The document was authored principally by Thomas Jefferson, and included sections such as the introduction, indictment, and preamble. In terms of signatories, 56 delegates signed the document, with John Hancock signing first and Button Gwinnett signing second. The phrase, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness" is from the document. Benjamin Franklin served as the oldest signatory and Edward Rutledge was the youngest.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: In the National Archives' Strongroom, in a safe in the back of the room where one encounters Button Gwinnett.

itm_0000000f.summary:
Bottle caps, also referred to as caps for short, are the standard currency in Fallout, Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas, Fallout 4, Fallout 76, Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel and Fallout Shelter.

Fallout 2 is an exception, with bottle caps being an archaic currency supplanted by the NCR minted dollar, while Fallout Tactics uses Brotherhood scrip and ring pulls.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Durable, portable, and instantly recognizable, bottle caps (predominantly those used in the production of the soft drink Nuka-Cola) rapidly became one of the most common currencies accepted by traders in post-War North America; this was actually speculated by a think tank researcher in the 21st century who had accurately predicted the role they would play in a post-holocaust economy. On the West Coast, the earliest known adoption of bottle caps as currency took place in New California. Within ten years of the founding of the Hub in 2093, caps became the standard currency of the wasteland. The widespread use by Hub merchants leading to the nickname Hub bucks, Hubbucks, bucks, Hub script, or just script.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
Nuka-Cola bottle cap:
Standard Nuka-Cola bottle caps featuring 21 crimps and ridges, used as the basic form of currency throughout many of the American wastes. Their value differs throughout the games.

Counterfeit Nuka-Cola bottle cap:
Physically they appear identical to standard Nuka-Cola bottle caps and are presumably intended to be used for trading in place of actual bottle caps. They are produced by unknown persons, have no trade value, and cannot be used for any monetary purpose.

Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle cap:
This nonstandard variant, taken off Sunset Sarsaparilla bottles, is used in the Mojave Wasteland alongside Nuka-Cola caps.

Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap:
A rare variant of the Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle cap, featuring a blue star on the underside of the cap.

itm_000cb602.summary: Occam's Razor is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 10, value 65 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

• Trench knife FO3OA - The trench knife's stats are identical to the regular combat knife. The only difference is a unique "knuckle-duster" skin.
• Sim version combat knife FO3OA - A sim-only version of the combat knife which differs only in health (essentially non-degrading).
• Sim version trench knife FO3OA - A sim-only version of the trench knife which differs only in health (essentially non-degrading).

sections.title: Locations

itm_000cb601.summary: Fisto! is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 25, value 100 caps). Linked to quests: Not of This World.

itm_000cb548.summary: Victory Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 40, uses .308 Caliber Round, value 450 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
While identical in damage to the sniper rifle, the Victory rifle has triple the item HP and knocks down targets with Critical hits. However, it pays for this ability with a reduced Critical Multiplier of 3.

Durability:
The Victory rifle can fire a total of about 250 shots, the equivalent of 50 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Sniper rifle - Common variant.
• Reservist's rifle - Also identical to the sniper rifle in damage, the Reservist's rifle uses less AP to fire in V.A.T.S, but only holds 3 rounds in a magazine. It also fires slightly faster and has slightly less recoil when using the scope.
• FO3OA Sim version - A sniper rifle with very high durability can be obtained through a glitch in the Operation: Anchorage add-on. See Operation: Anchorage glitches for details.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The Victory rifle is inside a locked (Very Hard) locker in the sniper shack overlooking Rockbreaker's Last Gas from a hill to the west. Getting it will require a Lockpick skill of 100. There is no key or trigger that will open the locker; however, Dogmeat can be told to find a weapon in the house and retrieves it from the locker. Star Paladin Cross, Jericho, Butch, Clover, Sydney, and Sticky will also pick it up to kill the caged radroaches.

itm_000cb547.summary: Vengeance is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 11, uses Electron Charge Pack, value 2400 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Vengeance has one of the highest DPS ratings of all automatic weapons in Fallout 3, and can handily slaughter most opponents. Like all Gatling lasers, it runs on electron charge packs.

Durability:
Vengeance can fire a total of about 3030 beams, the equivalent of 13 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Gatling laser - The standard variant.
• Precision Gatling laser FO3BS - While not as powerful as Vengeance, the precision Gatling laser has a very high critical multiplier of 0.2.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
Vengeance can be found in the deathclaw sanctuary, which is located in a mountain west of Paradise Falls near the Potomac and southwest from Fort Constantine right next to Broadcast tower KB5. The sanctuary outside has a small number of deathclaws, and around ten reside in the sanctuary itself. There is also usually an Enclave outpost close to the entrance.

Vengeance is found in the southeast of the sanctuary and is located next to or sometimes in what is literally a pool of blood, surrounded by a group of green mushrooms and mutilated human remains under a rock formation. The opening to the rock formation is facing away from one's approach direction, so listen for dripping sounds, as water drips from the roof in the rock formation.

itm_000cafa9.summary: Plunkett's Valid Points is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 12, value 30 caps). Linked to quests: Not of This World.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Plunkett's Valid Points was Junders Plunkett's weapon of choice, a lightweight set of spiked knuckles. Plunkett had murdered many using his fists alone. When his raider brethren were hunted down by Regulators he sought refuge in Arlington House, where he awaits someone worthy to hunt him down and take up the knuckles, hoping the bounty hunter will seek out a just cause with it.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Plunkett's Valid Points are a unique version of the spiked knuckles. It inflicts 3 more damage per hit than the regular set of spiked knuckles, and has double the chances of a Critical Hit. The spiked knuckles only have the standard chance at criticals.

Durability:
Plunkett's Valid Points can successfully strike about 333 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Brass knuckles - The common variant found in Fallout 3.
• FO3TP Steel knuckles - Slightly stronger than the regular brass knuckles, the steel knuckles only use 14 AP per V.A.T.S. swing.
• Spiked knuckles - A variant of knuckles with spikes affixed.
• Love Tap - A variant of the regular Knuckles that was cut from the base game.

itm_000c80be.summary: Stabhappy is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 10, value 65 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics

With its low AP requirement of 17, a player with high Agility can deliver a good deal of damage with only a single round of V.A.T.S. By combining Luck, Finesse and the Ninja perk in various ways, Stabhappy will critical strike 100% of the time. The weapon also damages limbs at a slightly increased rate.

Durability:
Stabhappy can successfully strike about 1200 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Combat knife - The standard variant.
• Occam's Razor - A slightly stronger version of the regular combat knife, though it is less effective than Stabhappy. It is wielded by Talon Commander Jabsco.
• Trench knife FO3OA - The trench knife's stats are identical to the regular combat knife. The only difference is a unique "knuckle-duster" skin.
• Sim version combat knife FO3OA - A sim-only version of the combat knife which differs only in health (essentially non-degrading).
• Sim version trench knife FO3OA - A sim-only version of the trench knife which differs only in health (essentially non-degrading).

itm_000c80ba.summary: Firelance is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 80, uses Alien Power Cell, value 750 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
In addition to its 100% critical chance and high damage, the Firelance sets its target on fire upon strike, causing 2 points of damage every second for 5 seconds. Both the Pyromaniac and Xenotech Expert perks affect this weapon and it uses the rare alien power cells as ammunition.

Durability:
Firelance can fire 63 shots, the equivalent of 7 reloads, from full condition, before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Alien blaster - The common variant found in the Capital Wasteland.
• Captain's Sidearm FO3MZ - A unique, cleaner, shinier alien blaster used by the alien captain.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: The Firelance can only be obtained in the Unidentified Flying Debris random encounter. See Fallout 3 random encounter locations (Type A) for locations where this event may take place. The encounter occurs only once per character playthrough.

itm_000c80b9.summary: Love Tap is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 8, value 20 caps). Linked to quests: Not of This World.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Love Tap boasted slightly higher Damage than their common counterparts, a Critical Multiplier of 2 as opposed to 1 for the regular brass knuckles, and they were to deal more Critical Damage than common brass knuckles. In addition, they'd require 3 fewer Action Points per attack in V.A.T.S. However, Love Tap was hindered by only having 100 item HP, half as much as regular brass knuckles.

Love Tap could successfully strike about 250 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants

• Brass knuckles
• Steel knuckles FO3TP

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: This weapon cannot be found anywhere in the game. It is obtainable only via console commands. To get Love Tap, use the console command:

itm_000c80b8.summary: Clover's Cleaver is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 15, value 100 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

itm_000c800e.summary: Xuanlong Assault Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 12, uses 5.56mm Round, value 400 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Xuanlong assault rifle is a general-purpose automatic firearm. Chambered for the same 5.56mm round as other assault rifles, it is the overall most powerful weapon in this class. The Xuanlong has the same AP cost, spread and critical multiplier as all other assault rifles. It also has the same low durability as regular Chinese assault rifles, being the second most fragile assault rifle in the game.

Although repairing this weapon can be difficult at lower levels, at higher levels, one can find spare Chinese assault rifles more often. The Xuanlong has the highest base damage of any automatic conventional firearm, as well as the highest non-critical damage per second of all weapons affected by Small Guns. It also features a modified 36-round magazine, 12 rounds higher than all other assault rifles.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Chinese assault rifle - the common variant.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: It is found on Prime's body in the diner near the Jury Street Metro station. Prime will not spawn until the Jiggs' Loot quest is completed.

itm_000c6e5b.summary: Jack is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 30, value 200 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Jack is a unique variant of the uncommon melee weapon, the Ripper. It is equal in power per single hit to its cousin, but has a higher potential damage rate, due to its slight but noticeable boost to the critical hit rate. It also does an extra 50% damage against limbs.

The higher critical chance increases the power of this weapon enormously because it hits over 30 times per second. The listed weapon damage is divided over the individual hits, but the critical bonus damage is not. This means every hit has a normal chance to critical and do the full critical bonus damage. If one performs a sneak attack critical with the Better Criticals perk while holding this weapon, they have the chance to do a brutal 60+ damage hit 30 times a second.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Ripper - The common variant in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: After The Waters of Life quest, Jack will appear in the deathclaw sanctuary, on the body of the second dead Enclave officer in the southern area of the cave. The body is surrounded by other dead bodies, including that of a giant ant on occasion. If all deathclaws have previously been killed, then the officer will spawn with a very low amount of health - approximately 2 bars.

itm_000c553f.summary: Protectron's Gaze is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 24, uses Energy Cell, value 320 caps). Linked to quests: The Superhuman Gambit.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Protectron's Gaze acts as a miniature laser shotgun that fires a fairly tight spread of five laser beams while expending only one energy cell. It has a slightly slower rate of fire and a significantly smaller magazine (20 as opposed to 30) than the standard laser pistol.

Durability:
Protectron's Gaze can fire a total of 520 shots, or 26 full cells, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Laser pistol - The common variant in Fallout 3.
• Colonel Autumn's laser pistol - A unique variant carried by Colonel Autumn prior to the release of the add-on, Broken Steel.
• Colonel Autumn's laser pistol (Broken Steel) - A unique variant carried by Colonel Autumn with the add-on Broken Steel installed.
• Smuggler's End - A unique variant owned by Elder Lyons.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: It is awarded after handing the AntAgonizer's armor to the Mechanist. The Mechanist states that the weapon is crafted from the parts of his loyal robot assistant that was killed by the AntAgonizer, the event that inspired him to become a superhero. The weapon cannot be obtained by killing him.

itm_000c553e.summary: Ant's Sting is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 4, value 30 caps). Linked to quests: The Superhuman Gambit.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Ant's Sting poisons those injured by it, dealing an additional 4 damage every second for 10 seconds. Because poison damage stacks, rapidly hitting an opponent outside of V.A.T.S. can raise Ant's Sting's DPS to very high levels. After attacking 12 times within 4 seconds, its actual DPS rises to 90. However, most enemies will already be defeated before Ant's Sting can pass this turning point. This effect makes this one of the most powerful melee weapons in the game.

Durability:
Ant's Sting can successfully strike about 1250 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Knife - the common variant found throughout the Capital Wasteland.
• Slasher knife - appears in Tranquility Lane and can only be obtained outside of the simulation through console commands.
• FO3PL Ritual knife - even more powerful than the Ant's Sting, the ritual knife only uses 12 AP for each V.A.T.S. attack.
• FO3PL Toy knife - using even less AP than the ritual knife, 10 compared to 12, the toy knife uses the lowest amount of AP for any weapon in Fallout 3. However, it does very little damage, much less than the regular knife.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Received when you complete the mission The Superhuman Gambit. Side with the AntAgonizer and give her the Mechanist's costume for the weapon.

itm_000c310f.summary: Board of Education is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 12, value 60 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
It is composed of a plank of wood with nails hammered through it like all other nail boards found throughout the Capital Wasteland. Although not a highly damaging weapon, it has a faster attack than the standard nail board, meaning it does more damage per second. Unlike common nail boards, the Board of Education actually has a chance to score a Critical Hit.

Durability:
The Board of Education can successfully strike about 250 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Found in the clifftop shacks inside the abandoned shack east of the bridge, under the bed.

itm_000c0327.summary: BB Gun is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 4, uses BB, value 36 caps). Linked to quests: Growing Up Fast.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This gun is one of the weakest weapons in the game, with a base damage of only 4.

Durability:
The BB gun can fire a total of about 417 BBs, the equivalent of 5 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• The version received on the Lone Wanderer's 10th birthday is different than the standard BB gun. It has higher item health (1,000), a much faster rate of fire, no chance for a Critical Hit, and does not degrade with use. It is also a quest item, meaning that it cannot be dropped. There is no way to obtain this version of the weapon outside of Growing Up Fast, except through the use of console commands.
• Black Bart's Bane - A unique BB gun that was cut from the final game.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Found in the Lone Wanderer's room during the quest Escape!
• Bailey's Crossroads Metro - On the lower level of the metro, there is a gun with 75 BBs at the makeshift range.
• Big Town - In the possession of Kimba.
• Dukov's Place - A gun (but no ammunition) can be found on the second floor in the southern corridor.
• Evergreen Mills - A gun may be bought from Smiling Jack.
• Megaton - Sometimes sold by Moira Brown.
• Tenpenny Tower - One can be bought from Chief Gustavo, the security chief.
• VAPL-58 power station - On the roof along with 13-22 BBs.
• Northwest from the scrapyard, there is a power station. The first power pylon south of it (near a skeleton in a chair) has a gun and around 10 BBs, as well as a Nuka-Cola Quantum.
• Available for purchase at most gun stores.

itm_000bff62.summary: The Shocker is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 20, value 150 caps). Linked to quests: Not of This World.

sections.title: Background
