sections.text: Part of a civilian pilot program by the Shocker Glove R&D Team, the Shocker glove delivers enhanced damage against robots but came with multiple safety warnings. The glove’s instability means the consumer was warned to be cautious, including not looking directly at it during operation, however the player won't have any ill-effect if they do look directly at the glove.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
While identical to the standard power fist in term of raw damage against organic foes, the Shocker deals an additional 25 damage to robots. However, it also degrades faster than the standard power fist.

Durability:
The Shocker can successfully strike about 400 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Power fist - The common variant in Fallout 3.
• Fisto! - A more powerful version of the power fist, it deals the most raw damage of any unarmed weapon.
• Sim version power fist FO3OA - A sim-only version of the power fist which differs only in health (essentially non-degrading).

itm_00066c77.summary: The Break is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 6, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Although not a highly damaging weapon, The Break has a rapid attack, allowing many blows to be landed quickly.

Durability:
The Break can successfully strike about 667 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The Break is found on a pool table in the center of Paradise Falls next to the roasting brahmin near the entrance to Eulogy's pad.

itm_00066c76.summary: Ol' Painless is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 30, uses .32 Caliber Round, value 250 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Ol' Painless does slightly more damage per shot and has a higher rate of fire than the regular hunting rifle. It can be repaired with hunting rifles, making it easy to maintain due to its commonality. Ol' Painless is one of the few weapons with 0 spread, meaning with a 100 Small Guns skill, non-V.A.T.S. shots go exactly where they are aimed.

Durability:
Ol' Painless can fire a total of about 556 rounds, the equivalent of 112 reloads, from full condition before breaking, roughly 111 shots less than the regular hunting rifle.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Hunting rifle - The standard variant.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Republic of Dave Capitol Building - found inside a locked safe in Dave's office, which Dave's special key is required to open. The key can be acquired as a reward for the unmarked quest Election Day, or through dialogue options and Speech checks during the quest You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head. The safe is marked as owned, meaning residents of the Republic of Dave will consider taking the rifle theft, costing Karma, even if the key was given to the player character.

itm_0001a334.summary: 10mm Pistol is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 9, uses 10mm Round, value 30 caps). Linked to quests: Companion Recruitment: Butch DeLoria.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The pistol uses 10mm ammunition, commonly found in Washington, D.C. and the surrounding Capital Wasteland. It is similar to the Colt 6520, which is more common on the West Coast. It is also the first actual gun available in the game and can be found in many other places around the game world.

This weapon can be used to repair the silenced 10mm pistol and Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol.

Durability:
The 10mm pistol can fire a total of about 556 rounds, the equivalent of 47 reloads, from full condition before breaking, an amount roughly half of what the Chinese pistol can fire.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Silenced 10mm pistol - While not unique, the silenced 10mm pistol is a suppressed version of this weapon. Although weaker, it does not give away its user's position when fired while sneaking.
• Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol - Carried by Enclave Colonel Augustus Autumn, the colonel's 10mm pistol is nearly twice as powerful as the regular version.
• Butch's 10mm pistol - A unique pistol used by Butch DeLoria when acting as a companion.
• - A unique pistol found on Sonora Cruz. It deals 100 damage, but Sonora always flees from enemies and never uses her pistol.
• FO3OA - A sim-only version of the weapon which has been re-skinned to appear newer and less worn. It also differs in health, with a whopping 999,150 hit points, essentially preventing the gun from ever degrading. This weapon is not normally accessible outside of the simulation.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• This is the first real gun available in-game, as Amata offers one to the Lone Wanderer at the beginning of the quest Escape!, who can then choose to accept it or tell her to keep it. The pistol is also in perfect condition and will be useful to low-level player characters. It belongs to her father, who she stole it from.
• It is found in large quantities throughout the Capital Wasteland, as low and medium level raiders and wastelanders often use the weapon.
• It can be found in many random safes throughout the wasteland, mostly Easy locked ones.
• Amata will carry one into the wastes if the player chooses to drive everyone out of Vault 101, after the quest Trouble on the Homefront.
• Officers Wilkins, Richards, O'Brian, Taylor, and Gomez all carry the 10mm pistol.

itm_0001a333.summary: Gatling Laser is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 9, uses Electron Charge Pack, value 611 caps). Linked to quests: The American Dream.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Gatling laser is the most advanced weapon type for the Big Guns skill. It is similar to the minigun, however, the Gatling laser is actually not a Gatling weapon, as the barrels do not rotate when it fires - instead, the barrels fire in a rotating order. However, although the animation for this firing makes it appear very random and haphazard, the barrels do not have to 'wind-up' like the minigun, making the Gatling laser much easier and quicker to use. Gatling laser and its variants are some of the few weapons in-game capable of shooting down vertibirds.

One can easily take out any threat at a safe distance with a Gatling laser. At long range, it is actually an incredibly accurate weapon, though it performs poorly in V.A.T.S.

At point-blank range, it actually aims a bit lower than the cross-hair.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Vengeance - A unique variant that is more powerful but less durable.
• Precision Gatling laser FO3BS - While not as powerful as Vengeance, the precision Gatling laser has a very high critical multiplier of 0.2.
• Fawkes' Gatling laser - A unique, non-player version of the Gatling laser used by Fawkes after the end of The American Dream quest.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Gatling lasers are most commonly found on Enclave, Brotherhood Outcasts and Brotherhood of Steel soldiers. These soldiers can be found in areas like the Washington Monument, Fort Independence, inside Arlington Library, Pennsylvania Avenue and outside of the Citadel.
• Defender Rockfowl will often carry one.
• Inside Raven Rock, there is a Gatling laser in an Enclave crate behind a blue energy shield as the player character is leaving Raven Rock after one has spoken with President Eden. One will notice it on the right as they near the sentry bots which fight off three Enclave soldiers, just before the final door (leading to the Capital Wasteland). Deactivate the shield with the computer and the Gatling laser can be found in one of the five crates. There is a random chance to obtain a second Gatling laser in this location.

itm_000b2943.summary: Rolling Pin is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 3, value 10 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A plain wooden rolling pin ordinarily used in baking to flatten dough. It is one of the weakest melee weapons in the game.

Durability:
The rolling pin can successfully strike about 667 times from full condition before breaking. Due to its much higher base damage of 20, the simulation version can only successfully strike about 100 times before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: A special version exists in the simulation Tranquility Lane, with significantly higher damage. It is found on the kitchen table in the Rockwell residence. If accessed outside the simulation via console command, it cannot be unequipped without using, nor removed from one's inventory without resetting the quest flag by using.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• In the Taft Tunnel not too far from the last door with the Brotherhood of Steel guard, on a table near a plush chair.
• In Mama Dolce's food distribution, top floor on a desk near Mama Dolce's loading yard door.

itm_000b2644.summary: Miss Launcher is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 20, uses Missile, value 400 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Miss Launcher is a unique version of the standard missile launcher model. It is more comparable to a grenade launcher than a missile launcher, as it has an arcing flight. Standard missiles fired from this weapon do not fly; instead, the missile-tube itself has been converted to propel them pneumatically. In doing so, both the missile's explosive warhead and unused solid rocket fuel are free to detonate together, increasing the missile's explosive damage potential by 30%. A side-effect is this also reduces the chances of giving away your position if fired from hiding, as compared with a regular missile launcher.

The damage bonus comes at the cost of range; the Miss Launcher's drastically underpowered propulsion system renders it incapable of hitting targets farther than 30 feet away, half the range possible with thrown grenades.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Missile launcher - The standard version found in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
The Miss Launcher is located in a weapons storage room inside Fort Independence, near the center of the map on the bottom floor of the lower levels. The lock will always have to be picked (75 Lockpick) on the front door, unless Defender Rockfowl, Defender Morgan, or Protector Casdin are pickpocketed for the key. However, it is possible to avoid having to fight the inhabitants if the player character completes the unmarked quest, Outcast Collection Agent, up to the point when Casdin will trust the player character. This will make the Outcasts inside the Fort friendly.

Once inside, go down to the lower level. There are two entrances into the basement. The first way is through an entrance outside that leads directly to the lower level. It, like the main entrance, is a hard locked door.

itm_000abbe4.summary: Colonel Autumn's laser pistol is a specially modified laser pistol found on Colonel Autumn.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Like many other unique weapon variants, it is visually identical to its common counterpart, in this case, the AEP7 laser pistol. If Broken Steel is installed, it is replaced by a different variant. Otherwise, it is fully automatic, uses energy cells, uses very few action points, and has a 30-round capacity, but can only be repaired manually.

Durability:
Colonel Autumn's laser pistol can fire a total of about 1250 shots, the equivalent of 42 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Laser pistol - The common variant in Fallout 3.
• FO3BS Colonel Autumn's laser pistol (Broken Steel) - A unique variant carried by Colonel Autumn with the add-on Broken Steel installed.
• Protectron's Gaze - A unique variant given by the Mechanist.
• Smuggler's End - A unique variant carried by Elder Lyons.
• Cross' laser pistol - A unique, non-playable version used by Star Paladin Cross, with identical stats to the regular version.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: It is found on Colonel Autumn in the Jefferson Memorial rotunda, during the main quest Take it Back!

itm_000a874b.summary: The Tenderizer is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 30, value 230 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Tenderizer is a more powerful variant of the standard sledgehammer.

Durability:
The Tenderizer can successfully strike about 500 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variant
sections.text: • Sledgehammer - The common variant.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: It is located inside the Anchorage Memorial, in the utility room with the broken door. To find the door, enter the Memorial Service Entrance on the east side of the memorial. At the junction, turn left to find the second door on the right. The door can be fixed by finding the door component, but a Lockpick or Science skill of 50 is required to be able to open the safe in which the door component is stored in the top level of the building. One can look behind the Nuka-Cola dispenser to obtain the passcode for the computer in the same room, which will then unlock the safe. A Repair skill of 35 or higher is required to fix the door with the help of the component. Without the component, a Repair skill of 95 is required.

itm_000a01dd.summary: Nail Board is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 8, value 30 caps). Linked to quests: Protecting the Water Way.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Composed of a wooden board with nails driven through one end. They are mostly carried by base level super mutants. Although not a highly damaging weapon, it deals rapid attacks, permitting numerous blows to be dealt quickly.

Durability:
The nail board can successfully strike about 150 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Board of Education - Better in all regards, damage, item HP, etc.
• Jericho's nail board - A unique, non-playable version used by Jericho with identical stats to the regular version.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Nail boards are commonly carried by super mutants and raiders.
• Some weapons shops, such as Flak 'N Shrapnel's, occasionally sell nail boards.
• One at Hallowed Moors Cemetery.
• One on a table in the Taft Tunnel, next to a ruined couch.
• FO3BS One at an Enclave camp due east of Wheaton Armory (after The Waters of Life).

itm_00060c2c.summary: The Zhu-Rong v418 Chinese pistol is a small gun in Fallout 3. It is a unique and incendiary version of the Chinese pistol.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Zhu-Rong v418 fires slower than a regular Chinese pistol, and does the same four points of base damage per shot, but has an incendiary effect that adds to its exceptionally low damage over the course of 5 seconds. It has the second-longest range of all incendiary weapons, and enemies killed with this pistol will often explode into dozens of flaming chunks. Its damage-per-second is actually lower than a regular Chinese pistol (without considering reloading times).

Durability:
The Zhu-Rong v418 can fire a total of about 1667 rounds, the equivalent of 167 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The Zhu-Rong v418 can be found in L.O.B. Enterprises, behind a Very Hard locked door (requires a Lockpick skill of 100), in the CEO's office in the secure-case on his desk in the east wing of the building. The key to the case is inside his desk. It is also possible to reach the case by moving along the edge of the destroyed top floor until reaching the other side of the locked door.

itm_00092966.summary: Reservist's Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 40, uses .308 Caliber Round, value 500 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Reservist's rifle has +50% more durability (item HP) than the regular sniper rifle, preserving the damage and critical rate more effectively. It also has a slightly higher rate of fire in exchange for lower magazine capacity.

It has 3 rounds instead of 5 in each magazine and costs 6 AP less to shoot in V.A.T.S., compared to other sniper rifles (32AP vs 38AP). The Reservist's rifle can be repaired with common sniper rifles.

As with generic sniper rifles, it has a very high critical multiplier of x5, which can be used to almost guarantee critical hits: Combining 10 Luck, Finesse (+5%), and Survival Guru (+3%), grants a 90% critical chance with the rifle at full repair.

If using V.A.T.S., which grants +15% critical chance bonus, all shots that hit will be critical hits.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Sniper rifle - The common variant found throughout the Fallout 3 game world.
• Victory rifle - While identical in strength to the sniper rifle, the Victory rifle has an additional 200 item HP, and knocks down targets with critical hits. However, it pays for this ability with a reduced critical chance of 3.
• Sim version FO3OA - A sniper rifle with ridiculously high durability which can be obtained through a glitch with the Operation: Anchorage add-on. See Operation: Anchorage glitches for details.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: This variation of the sniper rifle is used by the Drifter in Dickerson Tabernacle Chapel.

itm_00078442.summary: Highwayman's Friend is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 10, value 75 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Highwayman's Friend deals slightly more damage than the normal tire iron, along with benefiting from its fast attack speed. However, it is two pounds heavier than the standard variant.

Durability:
The Highwayman's Friend can successfully strike about 1,000 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Tire iron - The standard variant.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Sitting on a shelf in Dominic and Machete's house in Canterbury Commons. There is no Karma loss for taking it.

itm_00078441.summary: Vampire's Edge is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 15, value 100 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Vampire's Edge does slightly more damage than the regular version; it also weighs only 1 pound compared to the 3 pounds of the Chinese officer's sword. Due to the very low weight, fast attack speed, high critical chance, and good durability, the Vampire's Edge is among the best melee weapons in the game, despite its lower base damage value compared to other unique melee weapons.

Durability:
Vampire's Edge can successfully strike about 1000 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Chinese officer's sword - The common, non-unique version.
• FO3OA Jingwei's shocksword - An electrified version of the Chinese officer's sword, the shocksword is much stronger and deals electrical damage over time.
• FO3MZ Samurai's sword - An ancient weapon from Japan that deals an extra helping of damage on critical hits and is much more durable than the standard sword.
• Clover's Cleaver - A Chinese officer's sword that was cut from the base game. It was intended to be used by Clover and was to be the Evil follower's unique weapon, much like Fawkes' super sledge and Butch's Toothpick were for the other Karma levels.
• FO3MZ Katana - A variant of the samurai's sword that deals much less critical damage, but knocks foes down with critical hits.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
The Vampire's Edge belongs to Vance, and can be found in a 'sword cabinet' (labeled as such in-game) in his room at Meresti Metro station, an important location during the Blood Ties quest. Apart from its unique label, the sword cabinet's appearance is that of a normal wooden cabinet.

The cabinet is a 'Hard' level lock to unlock via lockpicking. Vance carries the key to the cabinet and may be pickpocketed, but he is a difficult target to pickpocket unnoticed, even with a Stealth Boy active. The key can, of course, also be looted from his corpse.

itm_00078440.summary: Butch's Toothpick is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 10, value 50 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Butch's Toothpick is a unique switchblade. It is owned by Butch DeLoria, a resident of Vault 101. Owing to its doubled base damage, higher crit damage and crit multiplier, it is significantly more powerful than an ordinary switchblade. It can be repaired with regular switchblades.

Durability:
Butch's Toothpick can successfully strike about 300 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Switchblade - The common variant in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: • Butch will be carrying this unique switchblade during the Trouble on the Homefront quest.

itm_0007843f.summary: Fawkes' Super Sledge is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 32, value 300 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
It weighs two pounds less, does 7 more damage, and is 33% more durable than an ordinary super sledge, having 250 more item HP, for a total of 1000 item HP.

Durability:
Fawkes' super sledge can successfully strike about 625 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
Fawkes does not have this weapon by default, but it will be immediately added to Fawkes' inventory and equipped by him as soon as his cell door is opened and he is freed (independent of main quest progression). The Lone Wanderer can then acquire it from Fawkes by speaking to him and asking him to trade any time on the way to the G.E.C.K. chamber. If taken from him, he will default to using his non-playable sledgehammer for melee.

If he was rescued during Finding the Garden of Eden and survived the quest, Fawkes will later reappear outside Raven Rock at the end of The American Dream with a Gatling laser. However, at this point, Fawkes will no longer have any items that he had in Vault 87, including his super sledge or default sledgehammer.

itm_0007843d.summary: O'Grady's Peacemaker is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 6, value 100 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
It can be repaired with other police batons. There was to be a guard called O'Grady who would carry this weapon, but he was cut from the final version. Compared to the normal police baton, it has higher damage, item HP, and value, but costs more AP to use in V.A.T.S.

Durability:
O'Grady's Peacemaker can strike a total of about 1333 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: This weapon cannot be found anywhere in the game and can only be obtained via console command.

itm_0006b53a.summary: The Kneecapper is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 75, uses 12-Gauge Shotgun Shell, value 350 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Kneecapper deals much more damage and is significantly more accurate than the regular sawed-off. The Kneecapper deals damage through raw power alone, since it does not deal any critical hit damage.

Durability:
The Kneecapper can fire a total of about 111 shots, the equivalent of 56 reloads, from full condition before breaking. This is 56 fewer shots than the common sawed off shotgun.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Sawed-off shotgun - the standard variant.
• FO3PL Double-barrel shotgun - a variant found around Point Lookout.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: • It can be obtained from Ronald Laren who lives in Girdershade.

itm_0006b539.summary: A3-21's Plasma Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 50, uses Microfusion Cell, value 2200 caps). Linked to quests: The Replicated Man.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A3-21's plasma rifle is an upgraded plasma rifle. It deals 50 damage at max Energy Weapons and condition and has a critical % multiplier of 2.5. The rifle is also durable, with an item HP of 1,200. Each attack from A3-21's plasma rifle in V.A.T.S. uses 25 Points and the rifle has a small weapons spread at 0.2.

Durability:
A3-21's plasma rifle can fire a total of 600 bolts, or about 50 full reloads from full condition, before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Plasma rifle - The common variant in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: A3-21's plasma rifle is carried by Harkness, and can be received by the player character through two of the endings of The Replicated Man quest.

itm_0006b538.summary: Eugene is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 7, uses 5mm Round, value 1500 caps). Linked to quests: Reilly's Rangers.

sections.title: Overview & Properties
sections.text: Item classification: Weapon from Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (EditorID: WeapUniqueMS18Minigun). Weight: 18.0, Value: 1500 caps.

sections.title: Where to Find & Usage
sections.text: Carried or sold by: Brick. Used in quests: Reilly's Rangers.

itm_0006b536.summary: Smuggler's End is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 18, uses Energy Cell, value 450 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Smuggler's End shoots twice as fast outside of V.A.T.S. and does 6 more damage per shot than the laser pistol. This weapon has a weight of 2, compared to the standard version's 3, and also has an additional 150 HP.

Durability:
The Smuggler's End can fire a total of 694 bolts, the equivalent of 24 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Laser pistol - The common variant in Fallout 3.
• Colonel Autumn's laser pistol - A unique variant carried by Colonel Autumn prior to the release of the add-on Broken Steel.
• Colonel Autumn's laser pistol (Broken Steel) - A unique variant carried by Colonel Autumn with the add-on Broken Steel installed.
• Protectron's Gaze - A unique variant given by the Mechanist.
• Cross' laser pistol - A unique, non-playable version used by Star Paladin Cross, with identical stats to the regular version.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
The Citadel, B ring: It is found in perfect condition in Elder Lyons' personal safe. The safe is locked with a Very Hard lock or opened via Elder Lyons' terminal, requiring Very Hard hacking, located on the desk to the left as one enters his room.
• Dogmeat can be used to obtain the pistol without hacking the terminal or unlocking the safe, as his search for a weapon function ignores locks on containers.

itm_0006b535.summary: Black Bart's Bane is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 8, uses BB, value 60 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This weapon's damage, critical damage, and item HP are all double that of a normal BB gun, and its value has been raised accordingly from 36 to 60 caps. In all other aspects, it is identical to a normal BB gun.

Durability:
Black Bart's Bane can fire a total of about 417 shots, the equivalent of 5 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: This weapon can not be found anywhere in the game. It is obtainable only via console command on PC or inventory edit on Xbox 360. To get Black Bart's Bane, use the console command:

itm_0006b534.summary: The Terrible Shotgun is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 80, uses 12-Gauge Shotgun Shell, value 250 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Compared to the standard combat shotgun, the Terrible Shotgun has the second-highest damage of all weapons in the Small Guns category and a far larger spread than normal shotguns. Full damage is only done if all pellets hit, making it most effective in close-quarters.

Critical hit damage with this weapon is applied to each individual pellet fired (outside of V.A.T.S.). If all nine pellets sneak attack critical at the same time, the weapon's total critical damage is 360. Paired with the Better Criticals perk, it can go up to 540. The base damage of the weapon doubled by the sneak attack bonus results in a total damage amount (with all pellets hitting) of between 880 and 1240, capable of killing even high-level enemies in one shot in close-quarters.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Combat shotgun - the standard variant found throughout the Capital Wasteland.
• Charon's shotgun - a non-player character only version carried by Charon.
• FO3OA Sim version - A simulation-only version used exclusively during the Anchorage Reclamation simulation with far more durability but otherwise identical stats.
• FO3BS Grenade launcher - a test weapon created for a G.E.C.K. tutorial. It uses shotgun shells but instead fires frag grenades as projectiles.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The weapon is located at Evergreen Mills, carried by Smiling Jack, the non-hostile raider merchant. He can be killed with no Karma loss, or it can be pickpocketed from him.

itm_0006b533.summary: Wanda is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 12, uses 5.56mm Round, value 500 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Compared to the standard R91 assault rifle, Wanda does greater damage and critical damage, has a higher magazine capacity (30 vs 24), and has higher health. No disadvantages and several advantages compared to the standard makes it a great alternative for a Small Guns-focused character.

This weapon exists in the game files, and can only be obtained through console commands.

Durability:
Wanda can fire a total of about 1,250 shots, the equivalent of 42 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Wanda is located inside the mailbox marked "weapons" within TestQAItems.

itm_0006b532.summary: Law Dog is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 9, uses .32 Caliber Round, value 210 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This weapon is identical to the common.32 pistol, except that it has slightly increased damage and nearly doubled value.

Durability:
Law Dog can fire a total of about 556 shots, the equivalent of 112 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Since the weapon is cut, the Law Dog does not appear in anywhere in the game; it can only be obtained by using the console command.

itm_0006b531.summary: Col. Autumn's 10mm Pistol is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 13, uses 10mm Round, value 325 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A 10mm pistol employed by Colonel Augustus Autumn as his personal sidearm. He uses it during the capture of Project Purity to shoot and kill Janice Kaplinski, and can also potentially use it to kill the Lone Wanderer while interrogating them at Raven Rock. By the time of the Battle of Project Purity, he replaces the 10mm pistol with a unique laser pistol.

It does more damage and critical damage compared to the standard 10mm pistol. It also has a higher value and item HP and is always found at 100% condition.

Durability:
Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol can fire a total of about 577 rounds, the equivalent of 49 reloads, from full condition before breaking, roughly 23 more rounds than the normal 10mm. It fires around 20 magazines (or 245 rounds) more than the silenced version.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
The weapon is carried by Autumn when he appears inside the Jefferson Memorial during The Waters of Life and at Raven Rock during The American Dream.

It is possible to obtain it from his inventory during the former quest, after he collapses to the floor when James releases the radiation in the control room. This can be accomplished by directly face the Colonel's body, with the cursor on it in first-person view, then switch to third-person view and rotate the camera by 180 degrees. Doing so will show the "search" prompt for Autumn's corpse, allowing for obtaining both the weapon, its ammo, and his unique outfit.

itm_0006e7cc.summary: Sydney's 10mm "Ultra" SMG is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 9, uses 10mm Round, value 430 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Sydney's 10mm "Ultra" SMG does 2 extra points of damage per shot and holds 20 more rounds of ammunition in the magazine when compared against the base 10mm SMG, which also allows it to do substantially more damage per second when reloading times are considered.

Durability:
Sydney's 10mm "Ultra" SMG can fire a total of about 926 rounds, the equivalent of 19 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• 10mm SMG - The standard version found throughout the Fallout 3 game world.
• Sim version FO3OA - A sim-only version of the weapon which differs only in health, with a whopping 999,250 hit points, essentially preventing the gun from ever degrading. The weapon is not accessible outside of the simulation without the use of the Gary 23 exploit or console commands.

• 10mm Alloy Steel Submachinegun - Another version of the weapon was cut from the Operation: Anchorage DLC. Called the 10mm Alloy Steel Submachinegun, it is otherwise identical to the standard 10mm SMG.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Sydney the relic hunter carries this weapon. It can be obtained from her corpse or finishing the quest and afterwards, giving her "A note from Little Moonbeam's father".

itm_00061793.summary: Wazer Wifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 28, uses Microfusion Cell, value 900 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
While identical in appearance to the laser rifle, it does 6 more damage and also comes equipped with a larger magazine, with 30 shots instead of the standard 24. It also has 80% more item HP than the standard laser rifle, with 800 more hit points.

Durability:
The Wazer Wifle can fire a total of about 1552 shots, the equivalent of 52 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Laser rifle - Standard version laser rifle.
• Metal Blaster FO3TP - This unique variant of the AER9 fires nine beams at once, using one microfusion cell similar to the Protectron's Gaze laser pistol. This feature, coupled with its remarkably high damage-per-shot makes it a devastating short to close-range weapon, though its effectiveness greatly diminishes at a range with the "shotgun effect". It can be obtained by bringing fifty steel ingots to Everett in The Pitt.
• Tri-beam laser rifle FO3BS- The tri-beam laser rifle is a variant of the AER9 that fires three high-powered beams per shot - similar to the Metal Blaster - though it does require three microfusion cells every time the trigger is pulled. This weapon is not unique, dropped from super mutant overlords and is not repairable with anything but other tri-beam laser rifles.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Biwwy offers to sell his unique laser rifle in Little Lamplight for 500 caps because he has been kicked off the scavenger team and no longer goes out on patrols - he no longer needs a gun, but figures that the Lone Wanderer might. With sufficient Barter skill, the price can be haggled down to 250 caps. If one has the Child at Heart perk, the Wazer Wifle can be obtained for free with no option to pay anything for it. If one has a high enough Barter skill, the gun must be purchased for 250 caps, that is if one is unable to pay the higher price.

itm_000303a2.summary: Blackhawk is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 55, uses .44 Magnum Round, value 500 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The weapon previously belonged to Agatha's husband, who modified it and often practiced his shooting with it. After he passed away, he left the weapon to his wife. If the Lone Wanderer assists Agatha in recovering the Soil Stradivarius and also acquires a sheet music book for her, she passes the weapon on to them.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Like the standard scoped.44 Magnum, Blackhawk is a powerful, accurate sidearm. It has no recoil when looking down the scope and firing.

Durability:
Blackhawk can fire a total of about 218 rounds, the equivalent of 37 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Scoped.44 Magnum - The standard variant.
• Callahan's Magnum FO3BS - Named after famous gunfighter and security guard Harold Callahan, Callahan's Magnum is the more effective version of Blackhawk, dealing more damage with less wear and tear.
• Paulson's revolver FO3MZ - Drawn by cowboy Paulson in the hostile confines of Mothership Zeta, it lacks the scope and fires a slew of pellets instead of a single bullet.
• Wernher's scoped.44 Magnum FO3TP - An unobtainable version of the scoped.44 Magnum carried by Wernher. It has significantly higher item HP but is otherwise identical to the standard variant.

itm_0003c07a.summary: Lincoln's Repeater is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 50, uses .44 Magnum Round, value 500 caps). Linked to quests: Head of State, Lincoln Artifacts.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: A 19th-century Henry repeating rifle that was once owned by Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States of America, at some point prior to the Great War, the rifle was loaned to the Museum of History in Washington, D.C. where it remained displayed for the next 200 years after the nuclear apocalypse.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A high-powered lever-action rifle chambered for.44 Magnum rounds, thus making it unique as the only rifle to use that ammo type in the game. Lincoln's repeater is also the strongest single-shot, precision rifle in the game despite only having a x2 critical multiplier and a very slow rate of fire. While it lacks a scope, it also has 0 spread (perfect accuracy), meaning one's accuracy at long range can be maintained by ignoring the bugged scope auto-aim. It also has a magazine capacity of 15 rounds and is very effective at long range in V.A.T.S.

Lincoln's repeater is only repairable with hunting rifles, despite being a lever-action rifle itself.

Durability:
Lincoln's repeater can fire a total of about 400 rounds, the equivalent of 33 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• FO3PL Lever-action rifle - a non-unique variant physically identical to Lincoln's repeater save for the textures.
• FO3PL Backwater rifle - a unique variant of the lever-action rifle.

itm_0003713d.summary: Combat Shotgun is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 20, uses 12-Gauge Shotgun Shell, value 90 caps). Linked to quests: Companion Recruitment: Charon.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: This model of shotgun was deployed as a close assault fire team's primary weapon (supplemented with explosives, an N99 pistol and a power fist) during the Anchorage Reclamation, and many working units have been scavenged by raiders, slavers and Talon Company mercs in the Capital Wasteland.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The combat shotgun combines a large drum magazine with high close-range damage. The only drawback is the weapon's poor reliability, as the combat shotgun deteriorates quickly. The combat shotgun is not fully-automatic.

Durability:
The combat shotgun can fire a total of about 145 rounds, the equivalent of 13 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• The Terrible Shotgun - a unique variant of the combat shotgun carried by the raider merchant Smiling Jack. It has a higher damage output, but twice the weapon spread and is 3 pounds heavier.
• Charon's shotgun - a non-player character only version carried by Charon.
• FO3OA Sim version - A simulation-only version used exclusively during the Anchorage Reclamation simulation with far more durability but otherwise identical stats.
• FO3BS Grenade launcher - a test weapon created for a G.E.C.K. tutorial. It uses shotgun shells but instead fires frag grenades as projectiles.

itm_0003422b.summary: Experimental MIRV is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 10, uses Mini Nuke, value 2500 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The experimental MIRV is a unique Fat Man that can be found in the bomb shelter area of the National Guard depot. This weapon deals the most damage of any weapon in the entire game, as it acts like a shotgun version of the Fat Man, delivering eight mini nukes at once. The MIRV actually does the same damage as a Fat Man per mini nuke, as 12 880/8 equals 1 610. It will not fire if the Lone Wanderer doesn't have at least 8 mini nukes in their inventory to load it with. If they have fewer than 8 mini nukes, the weapon will reload but never discharge the payload.

Durability:
The Experimental MIRV can fire a total of 63 shots, the equivalent of 504 mini-nukes, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Fat Man - The common variant in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: The player must complete the unmarked quest Keller Family Refuge before they can gain access to the secure section of the depot housing the weapon, though it's also possible to gain entrance to the armory by using a glitch. See the bugs section on National Guard depot for more details.

itm_0002d3b7.summary: Repellent Stick is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 1, value 120 caps). Linked to quests: Wasteland Survival Guide.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The repellent stick is a simple wooden stick with "mole rat repellent" (a combination of jet and psycho) on it. The stick is exceptionally effective against mole rats, as one hit causes an allergic reaction on mole rats, causing their bodies to smoke and their heads to explode after five seconds, while a second hit will cause the explosion to happen instantly. Do not be fooled by what Moira says when the Lone Wanderer first gets the stick, as it's an experiment gone wrong.

If used on any creature other than a mole rat, it will still cause the "smoking" effect, though it won't cause them to explode.

Durability:
Due to its very low base damage, the repellent stick can successfully strike about 2000 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: This item is obtained from Moira Brown at Craterside Supply in Megaton during the quest Wasteland Survival Guide.

itm_0002b3cb.summary: Chinese Officer's Sword is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 10, value 75 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A People's Liberation Army officer's dress sword, these weapons are remnants from the United States' war with China, an event that triggered the Great War.

With its high durability and fast attack speed, the Chinese officer's sword is an excellent weapon outside of V.A.T.S., whereas swings in V.A.T.S. use 28 AP.

Durability:
The Chinese officer's sword can successfully strike about 1000 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Vampire's Edge - The weakest of the Chinese officer's sword's unique variants, Vampire's Edge weighs only one pound, and is the only variant to use the regular sword's skin.
• Clover's Chinese officer's sword - A unique, non-playable version used by Clover with identical stats to the regular version.
• FO3OA Jingwei's shocksword - An electrified version of the Chinese officer's sword, the shocksword is much stronger and deals electrical damage over time.
• FO3OA Sim version - A version of the weapon which appears only within the Anchorage simulation. Unlike other sim-specific weapons, this version has a higher base and critical damage than its normal counterpart and also causes disintegration for non-player characters killed by a critical hit similar to Jingwei's shocksword.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Megaton, in Jericho's house, stabbed into a teddy bear.
• Republic of Dave, in the Museum of Dave, most likely a relic from Dave's traveling days.
• There's one in Abraham Washington's museum in Rivet City, behind a rubble pile near some lockers.
• On a dead Chinese commando, located at the origin point of the Chinese radio beacon, as a result of a random encounter.
• The Chinese captain at Mama Dolce's is another holder of this sword.
• Can be found on several insane inhabitants of Vault 106 who all use melee weapons.
• Raiders all throughout the game may carry them, and they will appear more often when the player character is at a higher level.
• Crimson at Paradise Falls carries one.
• There's one in the weapons lab in the Mothership Zeta add-on.

itm_00029769.summary: Rolling Pin is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 20, value 10 caps). Linked to quests: Tranquility Lane.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A plain wooden rolling pin ordinarily used in baking to flatten dough. It is one of the weakest melee weapons in the game.

Durability:
The rolling pin can successfully strike about 667 times from full condition before breaking. Due to its much higher base damage of 20, the simulation version can only successfully strike about 100 times before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: A special version exists in the simulation Tranquility Lane, with significantly higher damage. It is found on the kitchen table in the Rockwell residence. If accessed outside the simulation via console command, it cannot be unequipped without using, nor removed from one's inventory without resetting the quest flag by using.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• In the Taft Tunnel not too far from the last door with the Brotherhood of Steel guard, on a table near a plush chair.
• In Mama Dolce's food distribution, top floor on a desk near Mama Dolce's loading yard door.

itm_000289c3.summary: Switchblade is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 5, value 35 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The switchblade is a small and lightweight melee weapon. It is affected by the melee damage bonus from Strength.

Durability:
The switchblade can successfully strike about 400 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Butch's Toothpick - Carried by Butch DeLoria outside of Vault 101, Butch's Toothpick does more damage than the regular switchblade, and has a higher chance to inflict a critical hit.
• Butch's switchblade - A unique, non-playable switchblade carried by Butch.
• FO3TP Concealed switchblade - A miscellaneous item that can be given to the player by Wernher during Into The Pitt if they ask him if they can sneak a weapon past the gate guards, then ask for a knife. It is replaced by a normal switchblade once Into The Pitt is completed.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Switchblades can be found on random raiders or Talon Company mercs across the Wastelands.
• Cherry carries one.
• Springvale school, on the upper level: stabbed into the desk with the diary terminal.
• In a suitcase at the foot of Billy Creel's bed in Megaton.
• Vault 101, if you kill or pickpocket Butch while escaping the Vault.
• Canterbury Commons: two can be found in Dominic and Machete's Garage.
• Old Olney: in a mail dropbox.
• Warrington trainyard: Bessie Lynn has one. Either kill her or pickpocket it.
• Chevy Chase: across from GNR, there is a school with dead super mutants from Following in His Footsteps. Search the desks, and you will most often find a switchblade, along with some beer.
• Can be found in random metal boxes across the Capital Wasteland.

itm_0002869c.summary: The slasher knife is a unique knife found in Fallout 3. It is the signature weapon of the Pint-Sized Slasher.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The knife does a lot more damage than a normal knife - more than twice that of any other knife in the game. This results in it almost always dismembering the target. It can be repaired with other knives, including unique variants. The weapon also sports a unique, clean, pre-war texture compared to other knives that sport a more rusty appearance.

Durability:
The slasher knife can successfully strike about 400 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Knife - the common variant found throughout the Capital Wasteland.
• Ant's Sting - obtained by siding with the AntAgonizer in The Superhuman Gambit, Ant's Sting is slightly stronger than the regular knife, and deals poison damage over time.
• FO3PL Ritual knife - even more powerful than the Ant's Sting, the ritual knife only uses 12 AP for each V.A.T.S. attack.
• FO3PL Toy knife - using even less AP than the ritual knife, 10 compared to 12, the toy knife uses the lowest amount of AP for any weapon in the base game of Fallout 3. However, it does very little damage, much less than the regular knife.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
The knife is obtained along with the Pint-Sized Slasher mask during the Tranquility Lane quest if the player character decides to help Betty kill all the residents of Tranquility Lane. It is then located in the doghouse beside the abandoned house and is automatically equipped upon receiving it.

At the end of the quest or upon exiting the simulation, the knife is automatically removed from your inventory. The glitch which allows one to take items out of the Anchorage Reclamation simulation does not work here due to the fact that it is a "quest item" and cannot be removed from the player character.

itm_0001ffec.summary: Assault Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 8, uses 5.56mm Round, value 300 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The R91 is a general-purpose automatic firearm, effective from short to medium range. However, the high spread and low damage per shot greatly reduce its effectiveness against targets at a longer range or hard targets like giant radscorpions. Nevertheless, it remains a lightweight, hard-hitting weapon for low to mid-level Small Guns users. Condition degrades at a moderate rate. Poor-condition assault rifles are sold by many vendors across the wasteland and are often found in raider camps, buildings, and Metro tunnels.

Durability:
The assault rifle can fire a total of 1250 rounds, the equivalent of 53 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Infiltrator FO3TP - A scoped, silenced, and stockless version of the R-91 assault rifle. It is comparable to the silenced 10mm pistol in that it sacrifices firepower to reduce noise.
• Perforator FO3TP - A unique version of the Infiltrator, it has the slowest rate of fire of any assault weapon.
• Sim version FO3OA - A sim-only version of the weapon that differs only in health (essentially non-degrading). It features a cleaner, less-battered texture with fresh wood and darker metal areas than its wasteland counterpart. Available via the assault package in the deployment terminal.

• Wanda - A unique R-91 assault rifle that was cut from the final game.
• Alloy steel assault rifle FO3OA- A variant named "alloy steel assault rifle" can be found in the data files for Operation: Anchorage.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Rivet City - One or two assault rifles can be bought from Flak 'N Shrapnel's shop.
• Tenpenny Tower - They can sometimes be bought from Chief Gustavo. Also, every guard in the tower carries one. The player character will be given one for free during the Tenpenny Tower quest.
• Springvale school - An assault rifle in poor condition can be found early, inside the mining tunnels next to some dead wastelanders, 5.56 ammunition, and a Chinese Army: Special Ops Training Manual.
• One on the shelf in Farragut West station, behind an Average locked door in the north.
• There are some locations in which up to seven assault rifles in very poor condition can be found. They can be put to good use as repair parts, especially if the player has a Repair skill of 100.
• The National Guard depot's armory and training wing.

itm_00004354.summary: Spiked Knuckles is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 9, value 25 caps). Linked to quests: Not of This World.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Brass knuckles with spikes.

Durability:
The spiked knuckles can successfully strike about 667 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Brass knuckles - The more common variant found in Fallout 3.
• FO3TP Steel knuckles - Slightly stronger than the regular brass knuckles, the steel knuckles only use 14 AP per V.A.T.S. swing.
• Love Tap - A variant of the regular knuckles that was cut from the base game.
• Plunkett's Valid Points - A unique variant of spiked knuckles found on Plunkett, they have the lowest AP cost in the base game.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Spiked knuckles are found throughout the Capital Wasteland. They are commonly found on low level raiders, as well as in lockers and other similar containers.

itm_00004353.summary: Sniper Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 40, uses .308 Caliber Round, value 300 caps). Linked to quests: You Gotta Shoot 'Em in the Head.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The sniper rifle is the top-tier long-range weapon. It deals high damage and is equipped with a scope. It is a fragile gun with a scarce ammo type.

The sniper rifle has a very noticeable sway to it when manually aimed. The sway can be reduced with either a higher skill level in Small Guns or by entering sneak mode. At 100 points in Small Guns, the scope has no sway at all. A crippled arm will result in severe sway while using the scope, regardless of the Small Guns skill level.

Sniper rifles can cause the same result as the Bloody Mess perk even if the player character has not chosen that perk. They are utilized best from high vantage point locations.

The manual aim is usually more accurate (especially at greater distances), but V.A.T.S. should not be overlooked. A headshot in V.A.T.S.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Victory rifle - While identical in strength to the sniper rifle, the Victory rifle has an additional 200 item HP, and knocks down targets with critical hits. However, it pays for this ability with a reduced critical chance of 3.
• Reservist's rifle - Also identical to the sniper rifle in strength, the Reservist's rifle uses less AP to fire, but only holds 3 rounds in a magazine. It also fires slightly faster and has slightly less recoil when using the scope.
• FO3OA Sim version - Unobtainable through normal gameplay.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Behind Arlington Library, in Talon Company recon camp; respawns with merc.
• In the Bethesda ruins, there is a raider with a sniper rifle west of the Offices West building very close to the spawn point. Every 72 in-game hours the raiders respawn. There is also a raider on the catwalk between the Offices East and Offices West buildings who carries a sniper rifle and has some ammunition nearby. He doesn't respawn.
• A Talon Company merc in the Capitol Building, in the upper floors of the Hall of Columns, uses one.
• Knight Captain Dusk in the Citadel has one.
• In the damp cave at Oasis, on a skeleton in the east.
• Deathclaw sanctuary - Two can be found on the bodies of raiders.
• In the entrance of Fort Bannister, south of the Jalbert Brothers waste disposal. It is lying on a table at the southeast high bunker.

itm_00004352.summary: Super Sledge is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 25, value 180 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
It has a slow swing speed, but makes up for this with high damage. With a well maintained super sledge, enough melee skill, and Critical Hits (Sneak or otherwise), most enemies can be killed (including super mutant masters and Enclave soldiers) with a single hit.

Durability:
The super sledge can successfully strike about 600 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Fawkes' super sledge - A significantly better super sledge, it does more damage, weighs less, and has better durability. It can only be taken from Fawkes during Finding the Garden of Eden.
• Super mutant overlord super sledge FO3BS - Carried only by the rare melee-equipped super mutant overlord, this version has an object effect which inflicts an extra 25 damage per hit when used by non-player characters against the player. This damage ignores Damage Resistance and is independent of the condition of the weapon. This version is otherwise identical to the standard version of the weapon.

• Discharge hammer FO3BS - A cut version which inflicts additional electrical damage against robots.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Super sledges may be found on melee oriented super mutants at higher levels.
• Can be found on members of the Outcasts and Brotherhood of Steel paladins.
• Three in Paradise Falls: Both Ymir and Jotun carry a super sledge, and one can be stolen from Lock and Load.
• One in the National Archives, secure wing east, next the a mercenary.
• FO3BS There is one in the lower armory of the mobile base crawler and two in the upper armory.
• One can be found on top of a bookcase at the Raider wreckage fortifications. Its condition is low but is a useful find.
• One can be found inside SatCom Array NN-03d, near the top exit ladder.
• FO3PL Another may also be found on a smuggler on top of the Point Lookout Lighthouse.

itm_00004351.summary: Sledgehammer is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 20, value 130 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A sledgehammer is used in heavier working conditions, such as industrial areas or for breaking ground.

This is a powerful melee weapon for low to mid-level player characters, however, it has a relatively high weight. It has great reach, but a slow swinging speed. It can be found at some metro stations, and industrial sites such as the Pitt.

Durability:
The sledgehammer can successfully strike about 500 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• The Tenderizer - A unique variant that is more powerful.
• Fawkes' sledgehammer - A unique, non-playable version used by Fawkes with a marginally higher attack speed.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Two in Hank's Electrical Supply.
• One in the Jefferson Memorial rotunda.
• One in the Jefferson Memorial sub-basement.
• One can be stolen from Lucas Simms' house in Megaton.
• One can be stolen from a shelf in Herbert "Daring" Dashwood's suite at Tenpenny Tower.
• Carried by super mutant brutes.
• Caleb Smith carries one.
• FO3BS Four in Scribe Bigsley's office at the Jefferson Memorial.
• FO3BS Three in the mobile base crawler at Adams Air Force Base.
• FO3BS Two in Olney Powerworks.
• FO3BS One in the Rockland car tunnel.
• FO3PL One in the blackdamp shaft section of Herzog Mine, near the pit upon entering.

itm_00004350.summary: Silenced 10mm Pistol is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 8, uses 10mm Round, value 250 caps). Linked to quests: The Waters of Life.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A 10mm pistol equipped with a suppressor, which allows for silent kills if the target is killed with the first shot. This stealth feature comes at the cost of durability and damage, but a sneak attack always results in a critical hit, so the lower damage can be compensated for, especially with the Better Criticals perk.

Firing the silenced 10mm pistol will not increase the chance to be detected unless the player character has a very low Sneak skill. It is therefore useful for killing weaker enemies like radroaches, mole rats, and sometimes even raiders, without drawing attention from other enemies. A high enough Small Guns skill makes it a useful close-quarters weapon in office building type settings, such as the Bethesda ruins and the Museum of History.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• 10mm pistol - The base variant, it deals more damage than the silenced 10mm pistol.
• Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol - Carried by Colonel Autumn, the colonel's 10mm pistol is nearly twice as powerful as the regular version.
• FO3OA Sim version - A sim-only version of the weapon which has been re-skinned to appear newer and less worn. It also differs in health, with a significant 999,150 hit points, essentially preventing the gun from ever degrading. This weapon is not normally accessible outside of the simulation.

• No ammo silenced 10mm pistol - This strange pistol is only obtainable with the Operation: Anchorage add-on. This variant degrades but has a bottomless magazine.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Germantown Police HQ - in the armory on the ground floor of the station.
• Megaton - can be purchased from Moira Brown in Craterside Supply on rare occasions.
• Megaton - can be obtained by killing Mr. Burke before or after he kills Lucas Simms.
• Paradise Falls - on the counter of Lock and Load. Must be stolen, no Karma loss.
• Rivet City - can be purchased from Flak 'N Shrapnel's in the Rivet City Marketplace.
• Tenpenny Tower - can be purchased from Michael Masters, if the ghouls were allowed to live there.
• Vault 108 - in the entrance near some mole rats.
• In Marigold station, down on the tracks, leaning in a cubby hole of a locker, along with a box of 10mm rounds.
• The hotel occupied by the Brotherhood of Steel, next to Pennsylvania Avenue northwest.

itm_0000434f.summary: 10mm Pistol is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 9, uses 10mm Round, value 225 caps). Linked to quests: The Waters of Life, Trouble on the Homefront, Escape!.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The pistol uses 10mm ammunition, commonly found in Washington, D.C. and the surrounding Capital Wasteland. It is similar to the Colt 6520, which is more common on the West Coast. It is also the first actual gun available in the game and can be found in many other places around the game world.

This weapon can be used to repair the silenced 10mm pistol and Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol.

Durability:
The 10mm pistol can fire a total of about 556 rounds, the equivalent of 47 reloads, from full condition before breaking, an amount roughly half of what the Chinese pistol can fire.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Silenced 10mm pistol - While not unique, the silenced 10mm pistol is a suppressed version of this weapon. Although weaker, it does not give away its user's position when fired while sneaking.
• Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol - Carried by Enclave Colonel Augustus Autumn, the colonel's 10mm pistol is nearly twice as powerful as the regular version.
• Butch's 10mm pistol - A unique pistol used by Butch DeLoria when acting as a companion.
• - A unique pistol found on Sonora Cruz. It deals 100 damage, but Sonora always flees from enemies and never uses her pistol.
• FO3OA - A sim-only version of the weapon which has been re-skinned to appear newer and less worn. It also differs in health, with a whopping 999,150 hit points, essentially preventing the gun from ever degrading. This weapon is not normally accessible outside of the simulation.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• This is the first real gun available in-game, as Amata offers one to the Lone Wanderer at the beginning of the quest Escape!, who can then choose to accept it or tell her to keep it. The pistol is also in perfect condition and will be useful to low-level player characters. It belongs to her father, who she stole it from.
• It is found in large quantities throughout the Capital Wasteland, as low and medium level raiders and wastelanders often use the weapon.
• It can be found in many random safes throughout the wasteland, mostly Easy locked ones.
• Amata will carry one into the wastes if the player chooses to drive everyone out of Vault 101, after the quest Trouble on the Homefront.
• Officers Wilkins, Richards, O'Brian, Taylor, and Gomez all carry the 10mm pistol.

itm_0000434e.summary: Shishkebab is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 35, value 200 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Shishkebab is a makeshift "flaming sword" that requires the appropriate schematics to build. The motorcycle gas tank provides a reservoir of fuel, the handbrake becomes part of the handguard and likely the ignition trigger for the pilot light, the lawn mower blade becomes the blade of the sword, and the pilot light ignites the fuel-coated blade when the sword is drawn.

The Shishkebab, in addition to its Melee damage, will also set the target on fire, dealing 2 damage per second for 5 seconds. The Pyromaniac perk will also increase the Shishkebab's melee damage and boost fire damage from 2 to 3 damage per second for 5 seconds. Any humanoid companion can use a Shishkebab. Like all custom weapons, it can be upgraded with v2 or v3 schematics.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Vance wields a Shishkebab which will be in poor condition if looted from him after killing him.

itm_0000434d.summary: Scoped .44 Magnum is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 35, uses .44 Magnum Round, value 300 caps). Linked to quests: The Waters of Life, Reilly's Rangers.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The scoped.44 Magnum is a very high-powered pistol. It has a very long effective range, which is further extended by the scope but also has a low rate of fire for a double-action revolver. There is no recoil when looking through the scope and firing.

Durability:
A fully-repaired Magnum can fire approximately 229 rounds, or 39 reloads, from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Blackhawk - While it is much stronger than the regular.44, it is also the fastest to degrade of the unique versions.
• Callahan's Magnum FO3BS - Named after famous gunfighter and security guard Harold Callahan, Callahan's Magnum is the more effective version of Blackhawk, dealing more damage with slightly more wear and tear on the gun.
• Paulson's revolver FO3MZ - Drawn by space cowboy Paulson in the hostile confines of Mothership Zeta, it fires a slew of pellets instead of a single bullet. It is also unique for not having a scope, while other variants of.44 Magnum revolvers do.
• Wernher's scoped.44 Magnum FO3TP - An unobtainable version of the scoped.44 Magnum carried by Wernher. It has significantly higher health but is otherwise identical to the standard variant.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• In the truck to the left of the tent where you find the 5th Keller family transcript.
• Inside Vance's office wall safe during the Blood Ties quest. Must be stolen.
• On one of the skeletal remains in the Marigold station, along with a box of.44 Magnum cartridges.
• On a table a few feet away from the very hard locked door in the broken bow portion of Rivet City, near Horace Pinkerton's lab.
• Inside Reilly's Rangers headquarters.
• Mister Crowley of Underworld, Eulogy Jones of Paradise Falls, Willy Wilson of Andale, Billy Creel in Megaton, and Crow, the traveling merchant, all wield this gun.
• In a sunken boat near the Jefferson Memorial.
• Under a flight of stairs in the Hubris Comics printing room.
• Near a rotting brahmin corpse in the Shalebridge Hill ant tunnels.

itm_0000434c.summary: Sawed-Off Shotgun is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 50, uses 12-Gauge Shotgun Shell, value 150 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The sawed-off shotgun is a double-barrel shotgun that has had its stock and part of its barrels sawed-off, granting it increased mobility in return for drastically reduced range. It has two triggers, one for each barrel. The sawed-off shotgun appears to have been fitted with a pistol grip, in favor of the shortened stock-grip assembly. Rust is visible on the metallic parts of the shotgun, and a makeshift strap made out of thin sheet metal keeps the barrels and forearm together. It is affected by the Gunslinger perk. The sawed-off shotgun is unable to deal critical damage.

This weapon has one of the largest spread of all weapons in Fallout 3. In order to get high damage, one essentially has to treat the gun like a melee weapon and fire it at point-blank range so that the whole shot impacts the target.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• The Kneecapper - Carried by Ronald Laren, the Kneecapper is far more powerful than the normal sawed-off shotgun or even a combat shotgun. It is also lighter and more accurate than the regular version, but fires slightly slower and is less durable.
• FO3PL Double-barrel shotgun - A weapon similar in appearance to the sawed-off shotgun found around Point Lookout. However, neither weapon can be used to repair each other.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Can be found on random characters around the Capital Wasteland, mainly raiders.
• Arlington Library - In the children's wing, through the door in the media archives, on a bookshelf.
• One in the raider camp to the southeast of Hallowed Moors Cemetery, on a small table.
• One can be found together with some shotgun shells on a table at the riverside raider shacks.
• Two on the shelf in the utility tunnels.
• One in a trailer at Seward Square, just east of the Anacostia Crossing Station entrance.
• One in Dukov's Place, in a small room behind the counter.
• One on the shelf in Mister Burke's house.
• One on the shelf at Flak 'N Shrapnel's. Must be stolen.
• Inside SatCom Array NN-03d, on on a small table behind some sandbags.
• One behind the counter of the Statesman Hotel restaurant.

itm_00004349.summary: Ripper is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 30, value 100 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Ripper is a compact chainsaw-like weapon consisting of a powered knife with a bladed chain. Unlike other melee weapons in the Capital Wasteland, the Ripper is unique in that the player character can hold down the attack button and an enemy at melee range will continuously receive damage. In V.A.T.S., it can cause an instant kill.

In the add-on The Pitt, a weapon with identical functionality called an auto axe is added, which can be repaired with the Ripper.

Durability:
The Ripper can successfully strike approximately 400 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • Jack - identical to the Ripper in raw damage, but more durable and has the ability to score critical hits. It also does an additional 50% damage to limbs.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• There are four Rippers in Andale, in the Smith's basement and in the Wilson's garden shed. Note that taking them counts as stealing.
• Marigold station, behind the locked door with the turning light, in an east niche.
• Outcast leader Protector Henry Casdin at Fort Independence carries one.
• Enclave soldiers occasionally carry them.
• Some Brotherhood of Steel members around the Citadel have them.
• The AntAgonizer uses one.
• Occasionally Moira Brown has one for sale at Craterside Supply.
• Flak 'N Shrapnel's in Rivet City sometimes has one for sale.
• Tulip in Underworld sells one of them from time to time.
• Many members of the Brotherhood Outcasts use them when fighting robots outside Fort Constantine.
• Some Enclave troops in Raven Rock use them after Colonel Autumn orders them to attack the player character.

itm_00004348.summary: Railway Rifle is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 30, uses Railway Spikes, value 200 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The gun fires railway spikes as crude flechettes, making a distinctive "toot-toot" noise after each shot like a train whistle. Though only moderately damaging, it is very effective at dealing limb damage (due to a 3x limb damage multiplier), able to cripple limbs with just one shot. On the killing shot, a spike may tear off the struck limb or head, and possibly pin it to a fixed object, for example, a wall or the floor. Its accuracy is not poor for a semi-auto rifle, but will often miss at longer range, making it more effective at short to medium ranges. It is most effective in V.A.T.S. where its limb-destroying effects can be put to precision use. It is also remarkably effective at disarming enemies, as it will often launch their weapons a substantial distance on a V.A.T.S. hit.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• Laszlo Radford uses the railway rifle. He is a random encounter who may be found at certain locations throughout the wasteland, but only appears after the Lone Wanderer has obtained at least one schematic for the railway rifle.
• All of the components can be found in Fort Independence. Simply walk into the building and go straight and open the door. On the back left shelf, all the way to the left is a crutch. After that, back up and go right. There will be a staircase, then a door afterward, open the door and proceed downward. Go into the cubicle on the far end of the room on the right. There will be shelves containing three fission batteries and a steam gauge assembly. Then, move into the other room on the same floor. Turn right, and there will be a table with two pressure cookers.

itm_00004347.summary: Power Fist is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 20, value 100 caps). Linked to quests: Not of This World.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Similar in construction to the "Big Frigger" power fist, this pneumatic-type power fist is a large metal glove with a piston and ram built-in above the wearer's fist. The piston shoots the ram forward with every punch, allowing the fist to deal more damage than most unarmed weapons. Unlike the Big Frigger brand, this pneumatic-based power fist doesn't use energy cells to operate.

Durability:
The power fist can successfully strike about 500 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Fisto! - A more powerful version of the power fist, it deals the most damage of an unarmed weapon.
• The Shocker - While equal in strength to the normal power fist against organic foes, the Shocker deals an additional 25 damage to robots.
• Sim version FO3OA - A sim-only version of the weapon which differs only in health (essentially non-degrading).

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
The power fist can be found randomly throughout the Capital Wasteland and can be purchased from some merchants, but its location is fixed in the following locations:
• Tepid sewers, in a personal footlocker that can be opened by Rocksalt's key, inside a closet off of the room where a group of raiders is found fighting mole rats.
• Paradise Falls, slaver barracks, in a mop bucket in the southeast corner of the room. This power fist is in perfect condition.
• Rock Creek Caverns, behind the mirelurk king.
• Two are on a small dock to the southeast of the Citadel, in the personal footlockers, which are locked with Very Hard locks. The key to the footlockers can be found next to an ammunition box in the nearby sunken boat.
• Purchasable from Chief Gustavo in Tenpenny Tower.

itm_00004346.summary: Pool Cue is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 3, value 15 caps). Available across Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) locations and merchants.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
This weapon may serve well in the earliest parts of the game as the player's first foes are weak. But this weapon becomes useless, to say the least, in other parts of the game. Due to its low damage, it can be easily replaced when compared to other 2-handed melee weapons.

Durability:
The pool cue can successfully strike about 333 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: The Break - The Break is the build-a-better-pool-cue, with the ability to get a critical hit, as well as more damage and item HP.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• A pair of pool cues can be found on almost all pool tables throughout the wasteland.
• In the Grayditch abandoned home, on a bookcase.
• One in Alexandria Arms, on a pool table.
• One on a pool table in the Arlington Library.
• Two southwest of the Arlington sewer, on a pool table and one nearby.
• One on a pool table in Dukov's Place.
• Three in the Evergreen Mills bazaar, on a pool table.
• Fort Constantine, personnel offices, on a pool table.
• L'Enfant plaza, on a pool table near the hazmat disposal site L5.
• Two in La Maison Beauregard, on a pool table.
• One in the The Muddy Rudder, on a pool table.
• Two in the Museum station, on a pool table.
• Paradise Falls, outside. On a pool table.
• Two in the Rivet City market, on a pool table.
• Three in the Statesman Hotel's restaurant, on a pool table.
• Two in the Federalist Lounge.

itm_00004345.summary: Police Baton is a weapon in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland) (Damage 4, value 70 caps). Linked to quests: Escape!.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Consisting of a straight, extending club, mostly used by security guards and police, they serve many purposes, such as riot control and criminal arrests. They still have their use today.

Although not very powerful, it has an extremely fast swing speed. Opponents who armed with melee weapons themselves will often block, stunning the baton's wielder for a few seconds.

Durability:
The police baton can successfully strike about 1250 times from full condition before breaking.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text: • O'Grady's Peacemaker - It was supposed to be used by a Vault 101 security guard named O'Grady who is in the game, but the weapon was cut from the final version of the game.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
