Rivet City Clinic Computer System
For doctor's eyes only. Unauthorized use will result in fine, confinement, or possible banishment by order of the City Council.

Regional Health Hazards:
Apart from the standard dangers, Rivet City provides a few uncommon problems for long-time residents:

• Lockjaw: Muscle spasms, especially of the jaw, from getting cuts on the rusty ship hull. Treat with penicillin, when available.

• Red-lung: Respiratory problems from regularly inhaling rust particles - particularly a problem for hangar deck residents and shut-ins. Treat with steam therapy and time outside to flush system.

• Fish poisoning: Less of a problem nowadays, but occasionally someone finds a fish in the river and is dumb enough to try to eat the thing.

sections.title: Abraham Washington's terminal
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the cornered desk in Abraham Washington's room. It has an Average lock.
Abraham Washington - Private Notes
Current Expeditions and Status

Declaration Expedition:
Recovery of the Declaration of Independence seems to be a loss. That damn woman I hired, Sydney, she said she could do it. Haven't seen her in months. I bet she's dead or ran off with the advance I gave her. That's the last time I trust someone. Told Harkness to keep an eye out for her just in case she ever comes back to the city. That's what I get for sending a woman to do a man's job!

Lincoln Artifacts Expedition:
Came to find out through the grapevine that there are a bunch of Lincoln's artifacts still in the Museum of History. I think I may branch out from just collecting documents if I could get my hands on those gems.

sections.title: The Family's terminal
sections.text:
There are two of these terminals around where The Family eats and holds their meetings.
Use of this system is only by permission of Vance.

The First Law:
The First Law "Feast not on the flesh: consume only the blood. This is our strength."

We do not eat the flesh of those we kill for food. We will only drink of their blood and leave the body intact. The consumption of flesh is filthy and unclean. This action is what causes the humans to treat us like animals. We are not animals, we are The Family.

The Second Law:
The Second Law "Bear not the child: welcome only the exile. This is our fate."

Because we carry the stain of our past in our bodies, we can never let it pass to our offspring who would in turn carry out our foul actions beginning the cycle anew.

sections.title: Vance's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found in Vance's living quarters.

Vampires Defined:
Vampires are beings based on folklore that prey on humans for the purpose of obtaining their blood. In these fictitious stories the blood serves as both a food source and a center of power for the vampire. It is a common motif in these tales that a victim could become a vampire if bitten by one. Other noted attributes of the vampire are its ability to change into the form of a bat or wolf, to become gaseous at will, the ability to hypnotize the opposite gender and increased life span.

Daytime Fear:
It is interesting to note that the vampire is traditionally regarded in literature as having an aversion to sunlight.

sections.title: Doctor Lesko's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found in the recently built shack by the Wilks' house.

Where did I go wrong?:
Batch A27 is a complete failure. I must return to my original formulas and begin the process all over again. Perhaps the pressure of working in these conditions without proper laboratory equipment is to blame, perhaps I simply didn't splice the correct genetic instructions or perhaps I am fatigued. Whatever the case may be, A27 is proving to be a disaster. I must introduce a new formula soon or I may not be alive to see my hypothesis come to fruition.

Sample location discovered!:
This terminal entry is found during the Those! quest.
I've found the perfect specimen for my experiments inside Marigold station! I've set up shop underground for now while I prepare the experiment.

sections.title: W. Brandice's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found inside the Brandice's house across the street from the Wilks' house. It is in the bedroom up the staircase.

6-17-2277:
I can't believe I went through all that trouble to leave Navarro and make my way across the country just to get stuck in this shithole. I'll be damned if I'm going to die here.
Now that we're cut off from Lesko and Wilks, I think we're on our own. The damn ants keep trying to find a way to get inside the house. Even as I'm typing this, I can hear them scraping the walls looking for a way through. I don't know how much longer we can last.

4-02-2277:
I'm going to have to find a better way to protect Sheila and Will from those ants. Ever since Lesko came to town, I'm certain they're getting more and more aggressive. Wasteland ants are bad enough, but at least you could run away from them.

sections.title: Liberty Prime Operation
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on two cut I-beams on two protruding pipes in front of Liberty Prime in the laboratory.
Citadel System Link 39L

Welcome, Scribe Rothchild

Project Summary:
Classified Eyes Only

Military Contract 38917: Codename "Liberty Prime"

Project Goal: No less than the creation of the most powerful combat robot the battlefield has ever seen, with the express goal of liberating occupied Anchorage, Alaska from its Chinese aggressors.

Summary: The United States Army has succeeded in contracting both RobCo and General Atomics International to work on their first joint project.

The robot they create, Liberty Prime, will be the very embodiment of American military might -- a walking, talking, nuke-tossing hero who will remind the world what it means to be a super power.

sections.title: Citadel lab terminal
sections.text:
Note: There are six of terminals located throughout the laboratory. Five are wall terminals and one a desk terminal.
One is located on the wall next to the Smithy, one, the desk terminal, is located on the counter in the armory, one is located on the wall to the west of the armory, one is located on the wall to the east of the Armory, one is located on the west wall of the laboratory, one is located next to the Bathroom.
Welcome, Brother

AVF Problem:
Recent experiments with Accelerated Vector Fusion (AVF) have not gone according to plan. All Scribes assigned to the Lab should check with Scribe Rothchild on a daily basis, and obtain any modified technical parameters as needed.

Warning!: Leaky Hydraulics:
It is come to our attention that several Scribes have slipped on hydraulic fluid near the eastern end of the robot lift.

sections.title: Terminal
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the counter in the armory.
Weapon Information Research Database

Choose Weapon

N99 10mm Pistol:
The 10mm N99 sidearm was standard issue military gear following the phase out of the N80 in 2051. The N99 was known for its ability to survive in the harshest of conditions and in many tests, the weapon was able to reliably be restored to working condition after an extended period of time exposed to hard elements and without maintenance.

The N99 proved to stand up to its claims and as a result, is one of the most common weapons found in use in the Wasteland. While many civilian weapons were ruined beyond use in the exterior conditions following the war, the N99 is commonly able to be easily restored to working order by anyone with the most basic knowledge of firearm mechanics.

sections.title: Overseer's terminal
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the section of the wall directly behind the overseer's desk in the overseer's office. It has a Very Easy-difficulty lock, and can be unlocked with the Overseer's terminal password.
Welcome, Overseer.

Tunnel Snakes:
If Butch and his leather-clad delinquents accost Amata one more time, they'll have more to deal with than their acerbic teacher.

Their "services" have come in handy upon occasion, I must admit, but they're starting to become unruly. If dogs become feral, they must be put down. I'll have to remind Butch of that upon our next meeting.

Beatrice:
Just what Vault 101 needs -- an absent-minded, sexually repressed sycophant. Beatrice has served Vault 101 admirably for years, but her mind is growing feeble.

sections.title: Vault 101 medical data system
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the desk in the vault's clinic office. It is inaccessible during Escape!
Remember: Medical files are confidential!

Freddie Gomez:
Freddie's VDS is getting worse. Most days, he can't even get out of bed. When he does manage to function, Freddie hides his insecurities and low self esteem behind a bully's mask.

Vault-Tec medical protocols dictate the prescription of anti-anxiety medication when Vault Depressive Syndrome is involved, but do I really want to string the kid out on Chlorpromazine for the rest of his life?

Stanley:
Stanley continues to suffer from severe and chronic head pain. I've been feeding him aspirin like it's candy, but I'm reticent to give him anything stronger.

sections.title: Confessor Cromwell's terminal
sections.text:
Terminal is located in the Children of Atom building.
Welcome, Confessor. May you walk in the Glow...

Atom's Nucleus:
People often innocently ask me "Confessor, why do you worship a bomb?" Like curious children, they come to me with questions about the most visible and perhaps controversial aspect of our faith. The innocent among us hear my sermons before the great symbol, they see us bathe in the waters, and they wonder if it is danger we seek -- a suicide pact, perhaps. And while you may be tempted to answer their curiosity with anger, my gentle Children of Atom, you must never do so.

The core of Atom's philosophy teaches us peace. That we must educate the curious and work towards alleviating their ignorance, that we must teach them to accept the glory of the Division of the past and to seek the glory of the Division that is to come.

sections.text:
Terminal is found in the reactor room.
Engineer Section Use Only

Trouble Ticket TT007:
Maintenance Code: RL00 Green
Issue: Lighting on B Level
Engineer: Carl Maynard

Fix Notes:
If I told Zack once, I've told him a thousand times... stop using the higher amperage ballasts in the lighting grid on B Level. They will overheat within days and blow out because the power taps up there weren't installed to spec. Had to replace 37 ballasts with Type K09A ballasts and use a power tap converter on each one. Billing my missed dinner with that sexy red-headed violinist up in Women's Dorm 7 to Zack's Work Credit account!

Engineer: Carl Maynard

Trading Post 92 Employees Only

Intra-Vault Mail 000476:
To: Richard Rubin, Overseer Vault 92
From: Gordie Sumner

This is the FIFTH time I've requested that you allow me to release our supply of headphones and personal audio listening gear to the residents. It seems unfair that residents are required to listen to their music selections in the studio rooms. I have an ample supply of the type of equipment that would allow most residents to relax in their beds and enjoy their musical recordings. Please let me know your reasons behind this matter.

To: All Vault Residents
From: Gordie Sumner

I am pleased to announce that we now have strawberry pudding available in the Vault Store for 10 work credits.

Personal Entry 000897332:
Reading this entry adds the Overseer Rubin personal entry 00897332 note to the player's Pip-Boy.
As per instructions, the broadcast equipment for the White Noise has been rerouted from the sound booths and tied directly into the entire Vault's loudspeaker system. I'll now be able to execute Vault-Tec Confidential Plan WNMSCE (White Noise Mind Suggestion Combat Experimentation). I have three of Professor Malleus's team doing what I need to get done and hope to show some concrete results soon. I had the engineers make it so the WN can be either triggered from the control center or at the local security consoles. The password to these consoles is "UIY2249".

sections.title: Doctor Lesko's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found in the recently built shack by the Wilks' house.

Where did I go wrong?:
Batch A27 is a complete failure. I must return to my original formulas and begin the process all over again. Perhaps the pressure of working in these conditions without proper laboratory equipment is to blame, perhaps I simply didn't splice the correct genetic instructions or perhaps I am fatigued. Whatever the case may be, A27 is proving to be a disaster. I must introduce a new formula soon or I may not be alive to see my hypothesis come to fruition.

Sample location discovered!:
This terminal entry is found during the Those! quest.
I've found the perfect specimen for my experiments inside Marigold station! I've set up shop underground for now while I prepare the experiment.

sections.title: W. Brandice's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found inside the Brandice's house across the street from the Wilks' house. It is in the bedroom up the staircase.

6-17-2277:
I can't believe I went through all that trouble to leave Navarro and make my way across the country just to get stuck in this shithole. I'll be damned if I'm going to die here.
Now that we're cut off from Lesko and Wilks, I think we're on our own. The damn ants keep trying to find a way to get inside the house. Even as I'm typing this, I can hear them scraping the walls looking for a way through. I don't know how much longer we can last.

4-02-2277:
I'm going to have to find a better way to protect Sheila and Will from those ants. Ever since Lesko came to town, I'm certain they're getting more and more aggressive. Wasteland ants are bad enough, but at least you could run away from them.

sections.title: Broken terminal
sections.text:
Terminal is located in Doc Church's clinic.
ERROR 0xF141A013
"No Data Storage Detected."
"Check Tape Drive Connection."

sections.title: Confessor Cromwell's terminal
sections.text:
Terminal is located in the Children of Atom building.
Welcome, Confessor. May you walk in the Glow...

Atom's Nucleus:
People often innocently ask me "Confessor, why do you worship a bomb?" Like curious children, they come to me with questions about the most visible and perhaps controversial aspect of our faith. The innocent among us hear my sermons before the great symbol, they see us bathe in the waters, and they wonder if it is danger we seek -- a suicide pact, perhaps. And while you may be tempted to answer their curiosity with anger, my gentle Children of Atom, you must never do so.

The core of Atom's philosophy teaches us peace. That we must educate the curious and work towards alleviating their ignorance, that we must teach them to accept the glory of the Division of the past and to seek the glory of the Division that is to come.

sections.title: Moira's terminal
sections.text:
Terminal is located in the Craterside Supply.
Doc-u-tron Desktop
model 986

Welcome, MOIRA. What would you like to do today?

Store Inventory:
> Data corrupted! Use hardcopy backups.

Track Current Experiments:
It is a lovely day for science! What shall we test today, MOIRA?

Do brahmin heads learn independently?:
> More study of brahmin language required.

Can explosives be used to expand town?:
> Lucas Simms requests all testing cease.

Can Mole-Rats be domesticated?:
> Yes, if defanged, declawed, & lobotomized.

How to prevent raider attacks?:
> Raiders refuse to sit for interviews.

What do Super-Mutants eat?:
> Research assistants.

What happened to China?:
> Reports uncertain. China may be fictional.

Can centaurs talk?:
> Abundance of tongues suggests so.

What is the purpose of being?:
> To perform science.

obj_00053d44.summary: The Rivet City terminal entries are entries found on various terminals in Rivet City in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Security's terminal
sections.text:
Note: These two wall terminals are located throughout the bridge tower. They have a Very Easy lock.
Welcome to the Rivet City computer system.
What would you like to do today?

Security Log:
Security Log:

Two more reports of Mirelurk noise from the bow section. There isn't a damn thing that can be done about it. As soon as we clean out one nest, another moves in. I just wish everyone would stop bitching about it.

Railing on the flight deck is still broken. Problem has been referred to the council.

Brock got in a fight with that Sister character. If it happens again, I'm going to have to kick Sister off the ship.

Caught James Hargrave stealing food at Gary's Galley. Tammy paid the fine, although she blistered my ears the whole time.

Openings:
Note: This entry is only available if any generic Rivet City security member is killed.

sections.title: Rivet City Clinic patient data system
sections.text:
Note: This wall terminal is located in the Rivet City Clinic. It has an Average lock.
Rivet City Clinic Computer System
For doctor's eyes only. Unauthorized use will result in fine, confinement, or possible banishment by order of the City Council.

Regional Health Hazards:
Apart from the standard dangers, Rivet City provides a few uncommon problems for long-time residents:

• Lockjaw: Muscle spasms, especially of the jaw, from getting cuts on the rusty ship hull. Treat with penicillin, when available.

• Red-lung: Respiratory problems from regularly inhaling rust particles - particularly a problem for hangar deck residents and shut-ins. Treat with steam therapy and time outside to flush system.

• Fish poisoning: Less of a problem nowadays, but occasionally someone finds a fish in the river and is dumb enough to try to eat the thing.

sections.title: Abraham Washington's terminal
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the cornered desk in Abraham Washington's room. It has an Average lock.
Abraham Washington - Private Notes
Current Expeditions and Status

Declaration Expedition:
Recovery of the Declaration of Independence seems to be a loss. That damn woman I hired, Sydney, she said she could do it. Haven't seen her in months. I bet she's dead or ran off with the advance I gave her. That's the last time I trust someone. Told Harkness to keep an eye out for her just in case she ever comes back to the city. That's what I get for sending a woman to do a man's job!

Lincoln Artifacts Expedition:
Came to find out through the grapevine that there are a bunch of Lincoln's artifacts still in the Museum of History. I think I may branch out from just collecting documents if I could get my hands on those gems.

obj_0004e15d.summary: The Ranger compound terminal entries are a series of entries found on terminals in and outside of the Ranger compound in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Ranger Compound outer terminal
sections.text:
Reilly's Rangers Eyes Only
If you're reading this, you better get your ass out of here!

Unlock Security Door:
> Door Release Engaged

Notice from Canterbury Search Party:
Bad news. Rangers haven't seen Cheryl and got troubles of their own. Muties been snatching people left and right. Reilly's men are going to keep an eye out round here. They suggested we head to the western ruins, across the river and search there, so I guess that's what we'll do. Damn it, sis, why didn't you just wait for us?

sections.title: Reilly's terminal
sections.text:
Reilly's Rangers Eyes Only
Hope you asked Reilly first, you dumbass!

Brick:
Name: Brick
Position: Heavy Weapons
Age: 24
Term of Contract: Ongoing
Merits/Demerits: 5/1
Pay: 50 caps/mission
Status: Active

Brick is an outstanding asset to the Rangers. I find her zeal for destruction to be an asset rather than a liability. She is reliable and calm under fire, although can be a bit impatient during mission planning phases or debriefings. She seems fiercely loyal to the Rangers, and would be a great go-to person in the event of a falling out in the ranks.

Butcher:
Name: Butcher
Position: Medic
Age: 31
Term of Contract: Ongoing
Merits/Demerits: 3/0
Pay: 70 caps/mission
Status: Active

Butcher is an important part of our team.

Welcome, Overseer.

Tunnel Snakes:
If Butch and his leather-clad delinquents accost Amata one more time, they'll have more to deal with than their acerbic teacher.

Their "services" have come in handy upon occasion, I must admit, but they're starting to become unruly. If dogs become feral, they must be put down. I'll have to remind Butch of that upon our next meeting.

Beatrice:
Just what Vault 101 needs -- an absent-minded, sexually repressed sycophant. Beatrice has served Vault 101 admirably for years, but her mind is growing feeble.

Freddie Gomez:
Freddie's VDS is getting worse. Most days, he can't even get out of bed. When he does manage to function, Freddie hides his insecurities and low self esteem behind a bully's mask.

Vault-Tec medical protocols dictate the prescription of anti-anxiety medication when Vault Depressive Syndrome is involved, but do I really want to string the kid out on Chlorpromazine for the rest of his life?

Stanley:
Stanley continues to suffer from severe and chronic head pain. I've been feeding him aspirin like it's candy, but I'm reticent to give him anything stronger.

sections.title: Confessor Cromwell's terminal
sections.text:
Terminal is located in the Children of Atom building.
Welcome, Confessor. May you walk in the Glow...

Atom's Nucleus:
People often innocently ask me "Confessor, why do you worship a bomb?" Like curious children, they come to me with questions about the most visible and perhaps controversial aspect of our faith. The innocent among us hear my sermons before the great symbol, they see us bathe in the waters, and they wonder if it is danger we seek -- a suicide pact, perhaps. And while you may be tempted to answer their curiosity with anger, my gentle Children of Atom, you must never do so.

The core of Atom's philosophy teaches us peace. That we must educate the curious and work towards alleviating their ignorance, that we must teach them to accept the glory of the Division of the past and to seek the glory of the Division that is to come.

Private - Please Do Not Access Without Permission

Where Did I Go Wrong?:
Batch A27 is a complete failure. I must return to my original formulas and begin the process all over again. Perhaps the pressure of working in these conditions without proper laboratory equipment is to blame, perhaps I simply didn't splice the correct genetic instructions or perhaps I am fatigued. Whatever the case may be, A27 is proving to be a disaster. I must introduce a new formula soon or I may not be alive to see my hypothesis come to fruition.

obj_00024d66.summary: The Rivet City terminal entries are entries found on various terminals in Rivet City in Fallout 3.

sections.title: Security's terminal
sections.text:
Note: These two wall terminals are located throughout the bridge tower. They have a Very Easy lock.
Welcome to the Rivet City computer system.
What would you like to do today?

Security Log:
Security Log:

Two more reports of Mirelurk noise from the bow section. There isn't a damn thing that can be done about it. As soon as we clean out one nest, another moves in. I just wish everyone would stop bitching about it.

Railing on the flight deck is still broken. Problem has been referred to the council.

Brock got in a fight with that Sister character. If it happens again, I'm going to have to kick Sister off the ship.

Caught James Hargrave stealing food at Gary's Galley. Tammy paid the fine, although she blistered my ears the whole time.

Openings:
Note: This entry is only available if any generic Rivet City security member is killed.

sections.title: Rivet City Clinic patient data system
sections.text:
Note: This wall terminal is located in the Rivet City Clinic. It has an Average lock.
Rivet City Clinic Computer System
For doctor's eyes only. Unauthorized use will result in fine, confinement, or possible banishment by order of the City Council.

Regional Health Hazards:
Apart from the standard dangers, Rivet City provides a few uncommon problems for long-time residents:

• Lockjaw: Muscle spasms, especially of the jaw, from getting cuts on the rusty ship hull. Treat with penicillin, when available.

• Red-lung: Respiratory problems from regularly inhaling rust particles - particularly a problem for hangar deck residents and shut-ins. Treat with steam therapy and time outside to flush system.

• Fish poisoning: Less of a problem nowadays, but occasionally someone finds a fish in the river and is dumb enough to try to eat the thing.

sections.title: Abraham Washington's terminal
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the cornered desk in Abraham Washington's room. It has an Average lock.
Abraham Washington - Private Notes
Current Expeditions and Status

Declaration Expedition:
Recovery of the Declaration of Independence seems to be a loss. That damn woman I hired, Sydney, she said she could do it. Haven't seen her in months. I bet she's dead or ran off with the advance I gave her. That's the last time I trust someone. Told Harkness to keep an eye out for her just in case she ever comes back to the city. That's what I get for sending a woman to do a man's job!

Lincoln Artifacts Expedition:
Came to find out through the grapevine that there are a bunch of Lincoln's artifacts still in the Museum of History. I think I may branch out from just collecting documents if I could get my hands on those gems.

obj_00018471.summary:
The Citadel terminal entries are a series of entries found on terminals in the Citadel in Fallout 3.

=Citadel laboratory terminals=

sections.title: Liberty Prime Operation
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on two cut I-beams on two protruding pipes in front of Liberty Prime in the laboratory.
Citadel System Link 39L

Welcome, Scribe Rothchild

Project Summary:
Classified Eyes Only

Military Contract 38917: Codename "Liberty Prime"

Project Goal: No less than the creation of the most powerful combat robot the battlefield has ever seen, with the express goal of liberating occupied Anchorage, Alaska from its Chinese aggressors.

Summary: The United States Army has succeeded in contracting both RobCo and General Atomics International to work on their first joint project.

The robot they create, Liberty Prime, will be the very embodiment of American military might -- a walking, talking, nuke-tossing hero who will remind the world what it means to be a super power.

sections.title: Citadel lab terminal
sections.text:
Note: There are six of terminals located throughout the laboratory. Five are wall terminals and one a desk terminal.
One is located on the wall next to the Smithy, one, the desk terminal, is located on the counter in the armory, one is located on the wall to the west of the armory, one is located on the wall to the east of the Armory, one is located on the west wall of the laboratory, one is located next to the Bathroom.
Welcome, Brother

AVF Problem:
Recent experiments with Accelerated Vector Fusion (AVF) have not gone according to plan. All Scribes assigned to the Lab should check with Scribe Rothchild on a daily basis, and obtain any modified technical parameters as needed.

Warning!: Leaky Hydraulics:
It is come to our attention that several Scribes have slipped on hydraulic fluid near the eastern end of the robot lift.

sections.title: Terminal
sections.text:
Note: This terminal is located on the counter in the armory.
Weapon Information Research Database

Choose Weapon

N99 10mm Pistol:
The 10mm N99 sidearm was standard issue military gear following the phase out of the N80 in 2051. The N99 was known for its ability to survive in the harshest of conditions and in many tests, the weapon was able to reliably be restored to working condition after an extended period of time exposed to hard elements and without maintenance.

The N99 proved to stand up to its claims and as a result, is one of the most common weapons found in use in the Wasteland. While many civilian weapons were ruined beyond use in the exterior conditions following the war, the N99 is commonly able to be easily restored to working order by anyone with the most basic knowledge of firearm mechanics.

obj_000031c7.summary: The Meresti Metro station terminal entries are a series of entries found on various terminals at the Meresti Metro station in Fallout 3.

sections.title: The Family's terminal
sections.text:
There are two of these terminals around where The Family eats and holds their meetings.
Use of this system is only by permission of Vance.

The First Law:
The First Law "Feast not on the flesh: consume only the blood. This is our strength."

We do not eat the flesh of those we kill for food. We will only drink of their blood and leave the body intact. The consumption of flesh is filthy and unclean. This action is what causes the humans to treat us like animals. We are not animals, we are The Family.

The Second Law:
The Second Law "Bear not the child: welcome only the exile. This is our fate."

Because we carry the stain of our past in our bodies, we can never let it pass to our offspring who would in turn carry out our foul actions beginning the cycle anew.

sections.title: Vance's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found in Vance's living quarters.

Vampires Defined:
Vampires are beings based on folklore that prey on humans for the purpose of obtaining their blood. In these fictitious stories the blood serves as both a food source and a center of power for the vampire. It is a common motif in these tales that a victim could become a vampire if bitten by one. Other noted attributes of the vampire are its ability to change into the form of a bat or wolf, to become gaseous at will, the ability to hypnotize the opposite gender and increased life span.

Daytime Fear:
It is interesting to note that the vampire is traditionally regarded in literature as having an aversion to sunlight.

Washington DC Metro Transit Authority Meresti Trainyard Remote Access Security Terminal

> Door Released

Activate Internal Security:

Weapon Information Research Database

Choose Weapon

N99 10mm Pistol:
The 10mm N99 sidearm was standard issue military gear following the phase out of the N80 in 2051. The N99 was known for its ability to survive in the harshest of conditions and in many tests, the weapon was able to reliably be restored to working condition after an extended period of time exposed to hard elements and without maintenance.

The N99 proved to stand up to its claims and as a result, is one of the most common weapons found in use in the Wasteland. While many civilian weapons were ruined beyond use in the exterior conditions following the war, the N99 is commonly able to be easily restored to working order by anyone with the most basic knowledge of firearm mechanics.

Welcome, Scribe Rothchild

Project Summary:
Classified Eyes Only

sections.title: The Family's terminal
sections.text:
There are two of these terminals around where The Family eats and holds their meetings.
Use of this system is only by permission of Vance.

The First Law:
The First Law "Feast not on the flesh: consume only the blood. This is our strength."

We do not eat the flesh of those we kill for food. We will only drink of their blood and leave the body intact. The consumption of flesh is filthy and unclean. This action is what causes the humans to treat us like animals. We are not animals, we are The Family.

The Second Law:
The Second Law "Bear not the child: welcome only the exile. This is our fate."

Because we carry the stain of our past in our bodies, we can never let it pass to our offspring who would in turn carry out our foul actions beginning the cycle anew.

sections.title: Vance's terminal
sections.text:
This terminal can be found in Vance's living quarters.

Vampires Defined:
Vampires are beings based on folklore that prey on humans for the purpose of obtaining their blood. In these fictitious stories the blood serves as both a food source and a center of power for the vampire. It is a common motif in these tales that a victim could become a vampire if bitten by one. Other noted attributes of the vampire are its ability to change into the form of a bat or wolf, to become gaseous at will, the ability to hypnotize the opposite gender and increased life span.

Daytime Fear:
It is interesting to note that the vampire is traditionally regarded in literature as having an aversion to sunlight.

sections.title: Confessor Cromwell's terminal
sections.text:
Terminal is located in the Children of Atom building.
Welcome, Confessor. May you walk in the Glow...

Atom's Nucleus:
People often innocently ask me "Confessor, why do you worship a bomb?" Like curious children, they come to me with questions about the most visible and perhaps controversial aspect of our faith. The innocent among us hear my sermons before the great symbol, they see us bathe in the waters, and they wonder if it is danger we seek -- a suicide pact, perhaps. And while you may be tempted to answer their curiosity with anger, my gentle Children of Atom, you must never do so.

The core of Atom's philosophy teaches us peace. That we must educate the curious and work towards alleviating their ignorance, that we must teach them to accept the glory of the Division of the past and to seek the glory of the Division that is to come.

sections.title: General information
sections.text:
Random encounters in Fallout 3 take the form of unique situations, friendly and/or hostile encounters, or small tasks for the player to perform which are randomly drawn from a broad list of possibilities, and occur in various predetermined encounter areas across the Capital Wasteland. They should not be confused with scripted events that only occur in certain pre-defined locations. Once a random encounter has been activated in a particular area, no other random event will occur in that area. The game can be saved before entering a triggering area, allowing the player to reload the prior save if an activated encounter occurs that is less than desirable.

Unique vs. repeatable:
Encounters can be unique or repeatable. Unique encounters can only occur once per play-through whereas repeatable ones can occur at multiple locations.

sections.title: List of encounters
sections.text:
The encounters are grouped by living characters or creatures they contain. There are no duplicate listings; if you are looking for an encounter that involves multiple parties, make sure to check all potentially relevant sections.

There are encounters not described below which involve the Talon Company, the Enclave, raiders, and super mutants which are scripted events occurring at specific locations. These encounters are not random. See individual location pages for encounters outside of what is listed below.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Random encounter map:
• Yellow dots denote 'Type A' encounter locations.
• Red dots denote 'Type B' encounters locations (the red lines are way-point connections).
• Green dots denote fixed Outcast patrol spawn points (these locations, though not random, duplicate the characters from the Outcast Patrol random encounter with unique characters).

Trigger approaches:
Approaches that will trigger the encounters are listed below.

obj_000c9cea.summary: Footlocker is an interactive container / safe in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Lock difficulty: Hard (75). Located in Northwest Seneca Station.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They can be found almost anywhere. They are silver in color and mostly hold bottle caps, ammunition, and sometimes armor, clothing, and Stealth Boys. Unless found in a settlement or building, they are usually not locked. The lock difficulties on footlockers can range anywhere from very easy to very hard. Just like any other lock, it is possible to break the lock while attempting a force lock, thus keeping the player from the contents unless using the Infiltrator perk. They can also be found in safehouses. Most of them can be safe to store things in it.

sections.title: Personal footlocker
sections.text: Personal footlockers can be found in the same places as regular footlockers. Most of the time (but not always) footlockers are named "personal" because it contains special loot, or belongs to a special non-player character.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One can be found (locked) in Fort Bannister in the lower part of where Commander Jabsco is. It is hidden behind a makeshift wall. There is also one in the bottom of the largest crater at the nearby Bannister crater.
• One can be found north of VAPL-58 power station in a makeshift pylon shack along with a mini nuke and a Keller family transcript.
• Two can be found east of the Citadel on a dock. These are locked with a Very Hard lock and can either be picked open or unlocked with the key in the nearby sunken boat.
• Many are located in the Citadel, in the barracks.
• One can be found in the second house to the right in Springvale. It contains random loot, or most often it will be found [EMPTY].

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: Small items such as bottles of Nuka-Cola can be placed on the rear shelf for display. Ovens are a good source for pilot lights if the player is looking for miscellaneous components. They can also contain foods such as iguana-on-a-stick, squirrel on a stick, and other regular food items. On top of them, there are also occasionally pressure cookers, metal cooking pots, pans, and other food items.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Ovens can be found almost anywhere in the wasteland of Fallout 3, mainly where there are houses or people.
• Five in Our Lady of Hope Hospital's 2nd level.
• Four in Museum of History's lower halls.
• Three in the Statesman Hotel's restaurant.
• Two clean ones in Raven Rock level 3.

obj_000b25b3.summary: Footlocker is an interactive container / safe in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Lock difficulty: Hard (75). Located in Commanding Officer's Quarters.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They can be found almost anywhere. They are silver in color and mostly hold bottle caps, ammunition, and sometimes armor, clothing, and Stealth Boys. Unless found in a settlement or building, they are usually not locked. The lock difficulties on footlockers can range anywhere from very easy to very hard. Just like any other lock, it is possible to break the lock while attempting a force lock, thus keeping the player from the contents unless using the Infiltrator perk. They can also be found in safehouses. Most of them can be safe to store things in it.

sections.title: Personal footlocker
sections.text: Personal footlockers can be found in the same places as regular footlockers. Most of the time (but not always) footlockers are named "personal" because it contains special loot, or belongs to a special non-player character.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One can be found (locked) in Fort Bannister in the lower part of where Commander Jabsco is. It is hidden behind a makeshift wall. There is also one in the bottom of the largest crater at the nearby Bannister crater.
• One can be found north of VAPL-58 power station in a makeshift pylon shack along with a mini nuke and a Keller family transcript.
• Two can be found east of the Citadel on a dock. These are locked with a Very Hard lock and can either be picked open or unlocked with the key in the nearby sunken boat.
• Many are located in the Citadel, in the barracks.
• One can be found in the second house to the right in Springvale. It contains random loot, or most often it will be found [EMPTY].

obj_00077784.summary: The dresser is a furniture item used by people for displaying and storing items. The dressers have three or more drawers for storing items, a flat surface for displaying items, and four legs for supporting the dressers above the ground. The dressers were used in the Vault-Tec Vaults.

sections.title: Models
sections.text:
Vault dresser:
The dressers are made of metal with wooden facings for the drawers and a shallow shelf. The dressers have three drawers, a shallow shelf, and a ribbed display stand. Four legs support the dressers. The dressers are used in the Vaults to store vault jumpsuits.

Cabinet dresser:
Many are scattered throughout the wasteland and often contain various clothing items, mainly pre-War outfits.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Vault dressers:
• Two can be found in the Lone Wanderer's apartment.
• The DeLoria's apartment has one dresser.

Cabinet dressers:
• Various houses in Megaton.
• Inside the houses of the Minefield.
• Rivet City, in various rooms or the market.
• Eulogy's pad in Paradise Falls.
• In the suites of Tenpenny Tower.
• In the remains of destroyed houses. (ex: Faded Pomp Estates)

obj_0006f222.summary: Filing cabinets are used as containers to store various items such as bottle caps, pre-War money, ammunition, and other junk items. Before the Great War, they were used for containing important files, archives, information, notes, and many other things.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: They can be found in nearly every building throughout the wasteland, most commonly in office-type buildings.

sections.text: Random junk is usually found inside of these containers, or even nothing at all. On infrequent occasions, one might find caps, ammunition, or pre-War money.

obj_0002faa5.summary: Cash Register is an interactive container / safe in Fallout 3 (Capital Wasteland). Lock difficulty: Hard (75). Located in Upper Deck, Tenpenny Tower Lobby, Rivet City Market.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
Cash registers were ubiquitous in shops prior to the Great War, used to store money and record transactions.

Registers in active shops generally contain bottle caps, while those in abandoned buildings usually contain pre-War money, and sometimes one or two bobby pins.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
Registers can be found throughout the Capital Wasteland in both active and abandoned stores.
• Seven can be found in the National Archives.
• Six can be found in Rivet City.
• Five can be found at the Super-Duper Mart, with most of them containing pre-War money.
• Three can be found in Underworld.
• Three can be found in Tenpenny Tower.

obj_0003aefb.summary: The desk is a container in Fallout 3. It is a furniture item used by a person for supporting and storing items.

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
A desk has a flat surface for working on and for supporting other items, two columns of file drawers for storing items, and two legs for supporting the desk above the ground. Desks are commonly associated with chairs and are often found accompanying them.

The student desk is a furniture set that incorporates a desk and a chair. The desk is a variant of the table. Desks are communally used in the Vault-Tec vaults. Items can be placed into and taken from desks.

sections.title: Desk models
sections.text:
• Wooden office desk - This desk model has a wooden surface, two columns of three files drawers each made of metal, and two legs on either side of the desk for support. For additional support, a metal brace is placed below and connecting the drawers. These desks are used in the vaults.
• There is a metal corner desk in Megaton house if the Lone Wanderer chose to disarm the atomic bomb during The Power of the Atom quest.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text: Desks can be found innumerably in the wasteland and serve as both containers and world objects.

obj_00094ec1.text:
Finesse is a perk. This perk grants an extra 5% chance to land a critical hit upon an opponent regardless of the player's Luck attribute. This bonus is affected by a weapon's critical multiplier.

Although an extra 5% critical chance is undoubtedly helpful to any character, combining Finesse with other critical-enhancing effects ensures you get the most bang for your buck.
• Taking the Better Criticals perk increases critical damage by 50%.
• Using a weapon with a critical multiplier, such as the hunting rifle, greatly increases your chances of a critical without using an extra perk.

sections.title: Effects
sections.text:
This perk grants an extra 5% chance to land a critical hit upon an opponent regardless of the player's Luck attribute. This bonus is affected by a weapon's critical multiplier.

Although an extra 5% critical chance is undoubtedly helpful to any character, combining Finesse with other critical-enhancing effects ensures you get the most bang for your buck.
• Taking the Better Criticals perk increases critical damage by 50%.
• Using a weapon with a critical multiplier, such as the hunting rifle, greatly increases your chances of a critical without using an extra perk. A character with 5 Luck, Finesse, and a hunting rifle has a 20% critical chance outside of V.A.T.S.

Characters with very low Luck arguably do not benefit as much from Finesse, as they are not typically reliant on critical chance to be effective.

obj_00094ebc.text:
Cannibal is a perk. The perk has one rank and requires the Lone Wanderer to be level 12 or above. It allows them to feed on the corpses of both humans and non-feral ghouls.

Each corpse feasted on restores 25 HP, adds three rads and reduces Karma by one point. If the act is witnessed by friendly non-player characters, they will turn hostile, as cannibalism is considered a crime against nature. However, companions do not turn hostile.

obj_00044cac.text:
Lawbringer is a perk. The Lone Wanderer will get a note from the Regulators telling them that they "require their aid in bringing the scum and pestilence that inhabit our home to justice" and ask the player character to report to Sonora Cruz at Regulator HQ for details. Sonora Cruz, the leader of the Regulators, will pay the Lone Wanderer for each "evil" person brought to justice (killed) and requests their fingers as proof.

Sonora will pay 5 caps per finger unless one has 750 or more Karma, at which point she will pay 10 caps per finger.

sections.title: Description
sections.text:
The Lone Wanderer will get a note from the Regulators telling them that they "require their aid in bringing the scum and pestilence that inhabit our home to justice" and ask the player character to report to Sonora Cruz at Regulator HQ for details. Sonora Cruz, the leader of the Regulators, will pay the Lone Wanderer for each "evil" person brought to justice (killed) and requests their fingers as proof.

Sonora will pay 5 caps per finger unless one has 750 or more Karma, at which point she will pay 10 caps per finger. The price per finger is determined by one's Karma before the turn-in. Each finger turned in will net the Lone Wanderer 10 Karma.

obj_00044ca8.text: Contract Killer is a perk. The player character will get a note from Littlehorn & Associates telling them to go to the scrapyard. Daniel Littlehorn, the CEO, resides at the scrapyard office. He offers a contract for the ears of "good" people. He will pay 10 caps per ear, unless the Lone Wanderer has -750 or less Karma, at which point he will pay 15 caps per ear. This is determined by the Lone Wanderer's Karma before the turn in, not after. Each ear will give the Lone Wanderer -10 Karma, regardless of their current Karma.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: The player character will get a note from Littlehorn & Associates telling them to go to the scrapyard. Daniel Littlehorn, the CEO, resides at the scrapyard office. He offers a contract for the ears of "good" people. He will pay 10 caps per ear, unless the Lone Wanderer has -750 or less Karma, at which point he will pay 15 caps per ear. This is determined by the Lone Wanderer's Karma before the turn in, not after. Each ear will give the Lone Wanderer -10 Karma, regardless of their current Karma. The player will make the most caps when near but above -750 karma by dropping ears until they only have enough to reach -750, turning them in, then picking the remaining ears back up and turning them in.

sections.title: Bounties
sections.text: With this perk, the player character can remove an ear from every good human or non-feral ghoul character they kill. The ear can then be sold to Daniel Littlehorn at the scrapyard for 15 caps and -10 Karma.

sections.title: Elevator control
sections.text: Welcome to VSS, a Limited Liability Company

sections.title: VSS research terminal
sections.text:
Virtual Strategic Solutions, Inc.

SIM-U-TEC Chamber 003

9/06/77:
Entry 0540

Sim back up and running after another few days of changes. Chase is running everyone ragged, making tweaks here and there. The sim is, without any shadow of a doubt, divorced from reality. I've never seen the classified military reports, but some of the stuff Chase has added to the sim? There's no way it happened like that.
Version 7-36-099 was scrapped after Chase decided his face didn't look just right. I realize progress reports aren't the place for this, but there are concerns that the man is losing it. No one confronts him because everyone is scared. After West-Tek dropped off the grid, there were lots of rumors about the military commandeering private contractors, and no one wants to give Chase a reason to do that here.

sections.title: Research terminal
sections.text:
• PITT BIORESEARCH STATION *
• KRAG-JENSEN PROTOCOLS LOADED *

Baby Monitor:
> Baby Status: Healthy and Well

Trog Studies:
Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion
Research by Dr. Sandra Kundanika

An epidemic of the environs around the Pitt, which I have named Troglitic Degeneration Contagion (or simply "TDC") appears to be the result of intensely concentrated radiation, but the unique toxins and pollutants in the Pitt cause it to be far more pervasive.

Anyone living in TDC-active areas experience skin lesions after a few weeks of exposure, which can clear up after a month or more away from infected areas. For many healthy adults, this is the full extent of the effect. TDC also seems to interact with brain chemistry in a manner that produces a number of psychological effects, even if the subject remains physically healthy.

obj_020071c0.summary: Footlocker is an interactive container / safe in The Pitt. Located in The Mill. Associated with quests: Free Labor, Unsafe Working Conditions.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They can be found almost anywhere. They are silver in color and mostly hold bottle caps, ammunition, and sometimes armor, clothing, and Stealth Boys. Unless found in a settlement or building, they are usually not locked. The lock difficulties on footlockers can range anywhere from very easy to very hard. Just like any other lock, it is possible to break the lock while attempting a force lock, thus keeping the player from the contents unless using the Infiltrator perk. They can also be found in safehouses. Most of them can be safe to store things in it.

sections.title: Personal footlocker
sections.text: Personal footlockers can be found in the same places as regular footlockers. Most of the time (but not always) footlockers are named "personal" because it contains special loot, or belongs to a special non-player character.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One can be found (locked) in Fort Bannister in the lower part of where Commander Jabsco is. It is hidden behind a makeshift wall. There is also one in the bottom of the largest crater at the nearby Bannister crater.
• One can be found north of VAPL-58 power station in a makeshift pylon shack along with a mini nuke and a Keller family transcript.
• Two can be found east of the Citadel on a dock. These are locked with a Very Hard lock and can either be picked open or unlocked with the key in the nearby sunken boat.
• Many are located in the Citadel, in the barracks.
• One can be found in the second house to the right in Springvale. It contains random loot, or most often it will be found [EMPTY].

They can also be found in safehouses. Most of them can be safe to store things in it.

sections.title: Personal footlocker
sections.text: Personal footlockers can be found in the same places as regular footlockers. Most of the time (but not always) footlockers are named "personal" because it contains special loot, or belongs to a special non-player character.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One can be found (locked) in Fort Bannister in the lower part of where Commander Jabsco is. It is hidden behind a makeshift wall. There is also one in the bottom of the largest crater at the nearby Bannister crater.
• One can be found north of VAPL-58 power station in a makeshift pylon shack along with a mini nuke and a Keller family transcript.
• Two can be found east of the Citadel on a dock. These are locked with a Very Hard lock and can either be picked open or unlocked with the key in the nearby sunken boat.
• Many are located in the Citadel, in the barracks.
• One can be found in the second house to the right in Springvale. It contains random loot, or most often it will be found [EMPTY].

obj_03005705.summary: Tesla Coil is an interactive activator / device in Broken Steel. Located in Olney Powerworks. Associated with quests: Shock Value.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Before the Great War, a power plant owned by PPE was constructed in the vicinity of Old Olney, and the staff there conducted research and development on a Tesla coil. The plant was located near the S. Wilson office building and a children's hospital; when the bombs fell, these structures sank underground and formed a connected passageway to the power plant.

Around two weeks after the Enclave's defeat at the Jefferson Memorial and the reactivation of Project Purity by Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel in 2277, the Brotherhood dispatched the Lone Wanderer to investigate the Olney Powerworks facility and salvage the Tesla coil for use as a defensive measure at the Citadel. Parts of it were also later incorporated into a new model of Tesla cannon that was supplied to the Lone Wanderer ahead of the Battle of Adams Air Force Base.

sections.title: Location
sections.text:
The Tesla coil can be found in Olney Powerworks, inside the central reactor. It is protected by an electrical field which can be turned off by the three surrounding switches. Alternatively, there is a room next to the coil with a remote access terminal inside requiring Science 75 to hack. That terminal releases a failsafe that turns off the electrical field.

Taking the Tesla coil before turning off the electrical field will cause the player character to lose a significant amount of Health.

Log Entry MA-0089:
Museum Authority Log Entry MA-0089

Remmings over at the Museum of Technology is complaining again about the Planetarium system malfunctioning. I've replaced the playback unit on that thing 3 times now. Seems like the system keeps crashing and trying to restart itself, then crashes again... keeps repeating the cycle until it's completely rebooted. I suggest that we acquire a new type of system in next year's budget. The cost of replacing it now and fitting a new system is cheaper than the amount we've spent shoving in replacement parts.

obj_030081de.summary: Enclave Crate is an interactive container / safe in Broken Steel. Lock difficulty: Very Hard (100).

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text: The Enclave crates can be broken up into these types, though in some areas there may be semi-unique crates with other names pertaining to their specific contents.

sections.title: Variants
sections.text:
• Enclave crate - Contains various things, food, ammunition, sometimes clothing, whatever odds and ends the deployment scavenges from wastelanders.
• Enclave medical crate - Called first aid box in-game. It contains the same things an ordinary medkit would contain, but can also contain random food and has a slightly higher chance of containing purified water.
• Enclave ammo crate - Contains random ammunition, more often than not it contains microfusion cells and energy cells.
• Enclave weapons crate - Weapons crates may contain plasma pistols, plasma rifles, plasma grenades, pulse grenades, as well as laser rifles and laser pistols.
• Enclave grenade box - These are simply called "grenade box" in-game, usually contains a couple plasma grenades and pulse grenades.

sections.title: Others containers
sections.text:
• Enclave locker - Usually only titled "locker," they use the same world model as lockers in vaults. Enclave lockers may contain metal armor among other random items of apparel. Three of these can be found at Rockbreakers Last Gas.
• Enclave footlocker - Similar to an Enclave crate except it usually contains caps.
• Enclave power armor crate - Simply called "armor crate." One such crate can be found in Colonel Colonel Autumn's personal bedroom behind a photonic resonance field. These usually contain a single piece of advanced power armor.
• Enclave grenade box - Simply called "grenade box" in-game and usually contains a couple of plasma grenades and pulse grenades.

If attempting The Nuka-Cola Challenge, it takes 300 Nuka-Colas to get the necessary 30 Nuka-Cola Quantums.

obj_030011c1.text: Rad Tolerance is a perk in the Fallout 3 add-on Broken Steel. With this perk, you suffer no effects from Minor Radiation Poisoning (-1 END). This perk has no effect on greater radiation levels. For example, Advanced Radiation Poisoning (-2 END, -1 AGI) will still affect your character and so on. Unless your Endurance score is already at 10, using Intense Training to increase your Endurance would be more effective than taking this perk.
obj_030011c1.summary: Rad Tolerance is a perk in the Fallout 3 add-on Broken Steel. With this perk, you suffer no effects from Minor Radiation Poisoning (-1 END). This perk has no effect on greater radiation levels. For example, Advanced Radiation Poisoning (-2 END, -1 AGI) will still affect your character and so on. sections.title: Effects
sections.text: With this perk, you suffer no effects from Minor Radiation Poisoning (-1 END). This perk has no effect on greater radiation levels. For example, Advanced Radiation Poisoning (-2 END, -1 AGI) will still affect your character and so on. Unless your Endurance score is already at 10, using Intense Training to increase your Endurance would be more effective than taking this perk. Moreover, by this level the player will no doubt have multiple, plentiful ways of curing radiation sickness, and the Endurance loss has almost no effect on performance anyway (HP will not be reduced by the temporary condition, only poison resistance, itself a seldom-used statistic), so this perk is of dubious use, if any.

sections.text:
Camp Turtledove
Clearance Level Alpha
C.O. Private Operations Terminal

ALERT: Suspected Spy (Ch.):
Federal Agencies have added a new person of interest to our watch list.

Doctor Jiang is a Chinese National defector. Naturalization agents in Norfolk processed his defection after jumping over from a merchant ship he was stowed away on. Jiang was apparently in communication with a US Naval Intelligence contact for some months prior. He's reportedly brokered an immunity deal in exchange for his help recovering intelligence from the downed submarine off our coast.

Jiang is staying in room 1D at the Homestead Motel off the boardwalk. We're explicitly forbidden from issuing a search warrant against this location, but are authorized to monitor his activities in public.

sections.title: Marcella's terminal
sections.text:
Note: This desk terminal is located on the desk in Marcella's tent.
Private Field Journal
S. Marcella J, Abbey of the Road
Point Lookout Expedition
"I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life." John 8:12

Obadiah Blackhall:
Met local by name of Obadiah Blackhall. He lives in an old manor by himself. Class A manipulator. He solicited me to recover a book, which he claimed to be a family heirloom. The man gives me a bad feeling. I want to investigate this book and his connection to the swampfolk of the region, but he was reluctant when pressed for more information.

UPDATE: Confirmed Blackhall connection with regional beliefs. Appears that a recent ancestor to Obadiah, named Constance Blackhall, acquired obscure text known as Krivbeknih.

obj_0400f759.summary: Footlocker is an interactive container / safe in Point Lookout. Located in Point Lookout.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: They can be found almost anywhere. They are silver in color and mostly hold bottle caps, ammunition, and sometimes armor, clothing, and Stealth Boys. Unless found in a settlement or building, they are usually not locked. The lock difficulties on footlockers can range anywhere from very easy to very hard. Just like any other lock, it is possible to break the lock while attempting a force lock, thus keeping the player from the contents unless using the Infiltrator perk. They can also be found in safehouses. Most of them can be safe to store things in it.

sections.title: Personal footlocker
sections.text: Personal footlockers can be found in the same places as regular footlockers. Most of the time (but not always) footlockers are named "personal" because it contains special loot, or belongs to a special non-player character.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• One can be found (locked) in Fort Bannister in the lower part of where Commander Jabsco is. It is hidden behind a makeshift wall. There is also one in the bottom of the largest crater at the nearby Bannister crater.
• One can be found north of VAPL-58 power station in a makeshift pylon shack along with a mini nuke and a Keller family transcript.
• Two can be found east of the Citadel on a dock. These are locked with a Very Hard lock and can either be picked open or unlocked with the key in the nearby sunken boat.
• Many are located in the Citadel, in the barracks.
• One can be found in the second house to the right in Springvale. It contains random loot, or most often it will be found [EMPTY].

obj_0500ab72.summary: Reid Underwood's terminal is found in the lower west section of the cargo hold of Mothership Zeta in the Fallout 3 add-on Mothership Zeta.

sections.title: Transcripts
sections.text:
Log Entry 4-11-2063:
They think we're stupid; that we have no idea what they're up to. But we know. Barbed wire topped fences and security cameras be damned! We'll get the truth to come out if it's the last thing we do! The conspiracy has to end, and we will be the ones who drag it from the shadows and cast it into the spotlight for all to see. They deny everything. They deny the place even exists! But here we are, faced with armed guards who patrol the dunes and robotic sentries calculating our every move. They're careful, but not careful enough. I've found a loophole, a way in, and I mean to exploit it soon.

Log Entry 4-15-2063:
We've done it! We have it in our hands! The smoking gun...

obj_05009921.summary: Teleportation Matrix is an interactive door / passage in Mothership Zeta. Located in Engineering Core, Cryo Lab, Observation Deck. Associated with quests: This Galaxy Ain't Big Enough..., Mothership Zeta: Steerage Rats.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text:
The teleportation matrix is an alien device used for transportation, found onboard Mothership Zeta. Each teleportation matrix connects to another one and allows instant travel between the two. When used, it creates orange particles around the user.

Although each teleportation matrix can only be used for traveling to one other matrix, it appears that multiple matrices may connect to the same target and that the connection is not necessarily a two-way one. As an example, the matrix on the bridge can be reached from a matrix in the living quarters but it cannot be used to travel back. The same matrix on the bridge can also be reached from another one in the engineering core.

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
• 14 matrices, only found throughout Mothership Zeta.
• Seven in the weapons lab.
• One in the maintenance level.
• Six in the robot assembly.

obj_0500abb0.text: Xenotech Expert is a perk in the Fallout 3 add-on Mothership Zeta. It increases the damage done with alien weapons by 20%.
obj_0500abb0.summary: Xenotech Expert is a perk in the Fallout 3 add-on Mothership Zeta. It increases the damage done with alien weapons by 20%.

sections.title: Effects
sections.text: It increases the damage done with alien weapons by 20%.

sections.title: Obtaining
sections.text:
To get this perk, the player character must find a "shooting range" in the weapons lab (a room with an alien atomizer and an alien disintegrator next to a switch). The ranges are approximately in the center of the map north-to-south, and on the eastern side. Activating the switch closest to the door summons brahmin, while activating the far switch teleports enemies abducted by the aliens to a second range.

In order to get the perk, ten enemies must be killed with alien weapons consecutively. There are five types of enemies at the shooting range:
- Raiders
- Yao guai or deathclaw
- Sentry bots
- Robobrains
- Giant or albino radscorpions

Additionally, the player does not have to kill any enemies. Rather, spawning them through the button and letting them kill each other is enough for the perk to be obtained.

sections.title: Affected weapons
sections.text: This is a list of weapons that are affected by Xenotech Expert. All alien weapons are affected except the Electro-Suppressor and the unique Captain's Sidearm.

qst_0006136d.summary: Power Armor Training at the Brotherhood of Steel Citadel: obtain personal authorization from Elder Owyn Lyons and complete field instruction under Paladin Gunny in the Courtyard.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Complete the scientists' evacuation to the Citadel during the main quest "The Waters of Life" (MQ05). Primary locations: Citadel - Laboratory, Citadel - B Ring, Citadel - A Ring, Arlington Public Library Lobby, Chevy Chase East, DC Ruins Sector DC15a (Citadel Outer Perimeter).

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Permanent "Power Armor Training" perk; Ability to equip all Brotherhood, Outcast, and Enclave Power Armor as well as the unique T-51b set. Key participants: Star Paladin Cross, Sentinel Lyons, Elder Lyons, Scribe Rothchild, Paladin Bael, Knight Captain Gallows.

qst_0002a274.summary: Hidden at the far northern edge of the map lies the lush green grove of Oasis, where the Treeminders cult worships a living mutant tree named Harold (familiar from Fallout 1 and 2!).

sections.title: Detailed walkthrough
sections.text:
The ritual:
When the player character approaches Oasis, Tree Father Birch will ask that they follow him, saying that "He" has summoned them. If agreed to, Birch will unlock the gate to the village and lead the player character to an outdoor hut. Birch explains that he is the leader of the Treeminders, and that "He" has summoned the player character to the village. Although vague about who or what "He" is and wishing the player character to find out on their own, a Speech check may be passed to discover what "He" is. The Treeminders ask that the player character drink a sap in a ritual to purge them of all evil that might be inside, so that "He" may go unharmed.

After the ritual, the Lone Wanderer is placed in the Grove, where they meet Harold.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Travel to Oasis (far north-center of the Capital Wasteland) and undergo the purification ritual with Tree Father Birch. Primary locations: Sunken Chambers.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Barkskin perk (+5% Damage Resistance); Unique Poplar's Hood / Mask / Charm; Miss Launcher or Linden's Outcast Power Armor (depending on your choice!). Key participants: Branchtender Maple, Tree Father Birch, Leaf Mother Laurel, Bloomseer Poplar, Branchtender Cypress, Branchtender Linden.

qst_0009b5bb.summary: Buying pre-war historical relics in Rivet City: Capitol Preservation Society curator Abraham Washington is willing to pay handsomely for the original Bill of Rights, the Magna Carta, and artifacts from Abraham Lincoln's era.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Speak with Abraham Washington in his museum on Rivet City's mid deck (before, during, or after the Stealing Independence quest). Primary locations: Midship Deck.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: 75–100 caps for the Bill of Rights and 75–100 caps for the Magna Carta; 40 to 200 caps for each Abraham Lincoln artifact sold (with high Barter/Speech); Donated exhibits added to the Rivet City museum's glass display cases. Key participants: Abraham Washington.

qst_000943ee.summary: Recruit the intelligent super mutant Fawkes after escaping Enclave headquarters at Raven Rock: the strongest and toughest companion in Fallout 3, armed with an unlimited Gatling Laser and completely immune to radiation.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Free Fawkes from Isolation Room 5 in Vault 87 during "Finding the Garden of Eden" (MQ08), then meet him outside the Raven Rock exit at the end of "The American Dream" (MQ09) with Good Karma. Primary locations: Test Labs.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Powerhouse companion Fawkes with an unlimited Gatling Laser and Super Sledge; Option to send Fawkes into the irradiated Project Purity chamber during the "Take it Back!" finale (with Broken Steel installed). Key participants: Fawkes.

qst_000943ed.summary: Recruit the loyal hound Dogmeat at the Scrapyard: the Capital Wasteland's most faithful four-legged companion follows the Lone Wanderer regardless of Karma and can scavenge for supplies alongside a humanoid follower.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Travel to the Scrapyard, located south of Minefield and northeast of the Car Dealership. Primary locations: Wasteland.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Permanent companion Dogmeat (occupies a separate animal slot and travels alongside any second companion!); Scavenges for weapons, ammo, chems, and food on voice command. Key participants: Dogmeat.

qst_000943ec.summary: Purchase bodyguard Clover from slaver boss Eulogy Jones in Paradise Falls: the fanatically loyal slave follows only a character with Evil Karma.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Gain entry to Paradise Falls and speak with Eulogy Jones in his mansion pad while having Evil Karma. Primary locations: Eulogy's Pad.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Permanent companion Clover (specializes in Melee Weapons and Small Guns). Key participants: Clover, Eulogy Jones.

qst_000943eb.summary: Purchase the pre-War military Mister Gutsy robot Sergeant RL-3 from traveling merchant Tinker Joe: a formidable hovering companion armed with a plasma weapon and flamer for characters with Neutral Karma.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Meet robot vendor Tinker Joe outside the RobCo Facility (north of Tenpenny Tower) while having Neutral Karma and 1,000 caps. Primary locations: Wasteland.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Combat robot companion Sergeant RL-3 (equipped with a built-in plasma rifle and flamer); High durability (scales up to 9,500 HP with Broken Steel). Key participants: Sergeant RL-3, Tinker Joe.

qst_0009426d.summary: Reunite with childhood acquaintance and Tunnel Snakes leader Butch DeLoria at the Rivet City bar: after resolving the crisis in Vault 101, Butch heads out to the surface and is willing to travel with a Neutral-Karma Lone Wanderer.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Complete the side quest "Trouble on the Homefront" (MS16) with Butch alive, then find him in The Muddy Rudder bar in Rivet City while maintaining Neutral Karma. Primary locations: Vault 101 Lower Level.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Free companion Butch DeLoria; Free haircuts for your character out in the field at any time. Key participants: Butch.

qst_000872e6.summary: Overarching storyline quest for the first half of Fallout 3's main campaign: tracking down your missing father, James, through leads in Megaton, Galaxy News Radio, the Rivet City lab, and Smith Casey's Garage.

sections.title: Detailed walkthrough
sections.text:
NOTE: Where it says optional, it means the player character can skip the parts before it, like going straight to Smith Casey's garage will finish the quest and the player character will not have to go to Rivet City.

Megaton and '300 Pieces of Silver':
Objective: Investigate the nearby town of Megaton for information about James.

In Megaton, everyone will point the player character to the saloon owner, Colin Moriarty who will offer to tell you where your dad is if you give him 100 caps. If one does not accept the offer, he will ask for 300 the next time one talks to him. You can also use Speech to convince Moriarty that your father told you about him or choose certain dialogue options to get him to give the Lone Wanderer a discount, provided they agree to kill Silver and bring back the caps she stole.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Starts automatically upon exiting Vault 101 into the Capital Wasteland at the end of "Escape!".

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Story transitions to "Following in His Footsteps", "Galaxy News Radio", and "Scientific Pursuits"; Discovery of key Capital Wasteland locations (Megaton, Rivet City, Vault 112).

qst_0006f1e8.summary: Bounty hunting on behalf of the Capital Wasteland's lawmen: upon taking the Lawbringer perk at Level 14, the Lone Wanderer joins the Regulators and turns in severed fingers from slain evildoers to Sonora Cruz.

sections.title: Description
sections.text:
The Lone Wanderer will get a note from the Regulators telling them that they "require their aid in bringing the scum and pestilence that inhabit our home to justice" and ask the player character to report to Sonora Cruz at Regulator HQ for details. Sonora Cruz, the leader of the Regulators, will pay the Lone Wanderer for each "evil" person brought to justice (killed) and requests their fingers as proof.

Sonora will pay 5 caps per finger unless one has 750 or more Karma, at which point she will pay 10 caps per finger. The price per finger is determined by one's Karma before the turn-in. Each finger turned in will net the Lone Wanderer 10 Karma.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Select the Lawbringer perk upon reaching Level 14 or higher. Primary locations: Regulator Headquarters, Arlington House, Scrapyard Office, Arlington Cemetery North.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Unique Regulator Duster (+1 Charisma, +5 Small Guns); 10 caps and +5 good Karma per evil character's finger (plus 1,000 caps for the special bounty on J.D. Crockett!). Key participants: Sonora Cruz, Daniel Littlehorn, Junders Plunkett.

qst_0006f1e7.summary: Secret assassination contracts for Littlehorn & Associates: upon taking the Contract Killer perk at Level 14, the hero collects ears from slain good-natured people and sells them to the mysterious Daniel Littlehorn at the Scrapyard.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: The player character will get a note from Littlehorn & Associates telling them to go to the scrapyard. Daniel Littlehorn, the CEO, resides at the scrapyard office. He offers a contract for the ears of "good" people. He will pay 10 caps per ear, unless the Lone Wanderer has -750 or less Karma, at which point he will pay 15 caps per ear. This is determined by the Lone Wanderer's Karma before the turn in, not after. Each ear will give the Lone Wanderer -10 Karma, regardless of their current Karma. The player will make the most caps when near but above -750 karma by dropping ears until they only have enough to reach -750, turning them in, then picking the remaining ears back up and turning them in.

sections.title: Bounties
sections.text: With this perk, the player character can remove an ear from every good human or non-feral ghoul character they kill. The ear can then be sold to Daniel Littlehorn at the scrapyard for 15 caps and -10 Karma.

qst_00062736.summary: Recruit Brotherhood of Steel veteran Star Paladin Cross at the Citadel: the cyborg bodyguard who once escorted your father James and you as an infant to Vault 101 joins a Good-Karma Lone Wanderer free of charge.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Reach the Citadel during the main quest "The Waters of Life" (MQ05) and speak with Star Paladin Cross in the Laboratory or the A Ring while having Good Karma. Primary locations: Citadel - Laboratory.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
sections.text: Rewards: Free elite companion Star Paladin Cross in full Brotherhood Power Armor; Skilled in Energy Weapons and Melee Weapons (armed with a Super Sledge and Laser Pistol). Key participants: Star Paladin Cross.

qst_0005ecfd.summary: A major scavenger hunt for ten authentic relics of the 16th US President, Abraham Lincoln, inside the Museum of History: each artifact found can be given to Hannibal Hamlin's freed slaves, sold to collector Abraham Washington, or handed over to slaver Leroy Walker to be destroyed.

sections.title: Detailed walkthrough
sections.text:
The artifacts of Abraham Lincoln found in the Museum of History can be sold to various people in the Capital Wasteland. Besides selling them to "normal" traders for their item value, certain characters will pay increased prices because of the artifacts' historical value or symbolic meaning.

These characters are Hannibal Hamlin, leader of the ex-slaves at Temple of the Union; Leroy Walker, leader of the slavers who occupy Lincoln Memorial; or Abraham Washington, a historian and curator of Rivet City's Capitol Preservation Society.

sections.title: Item locations
sections.text:
All nine artifacts can be found in the Museum of History. The letters refer to locations on the map to the right.

Lower halls:
• Lincoln's diary is found when the Lone Wanderer first goes up the steps in the large display room on the way to the Museum of History offices, lying on the first display to the right. The diary might not be on the display so be sure to examine around the general area.

Offices, first floor:
• Lincoln's hat is found in a room on the 1st floor of the Museum of History offices. The room is the first door to the right from the entry stairwell and has a collapsed ceiling (one can also drop down into it from the second floor). The hat is on the floor among the rubble (to the right of the desk on the left when entering the room). It may be hard to spot with the shadows, make sure the Pip-Boy light is on.

sections.title: Value
sections.text:
A successful Speech check almost always doubles the price paid for the artifacts. In Abraham's case, a high Barter will double the offer.

There is no way to get back any items sold to Abraham Washington or Leroy Walker, except for the Lincoln Memorial poster. One can, however, steal back the items one sells to Hannibal.

Highest payouts are underlined and bolded.

qst_0002fa33.summary: Recruit retired raider Jericho in Megaton: the grizzled Capital Wasteland veteran will only come out of retirement to travel with an Evil-Karma character for a 1,000-cap signing bonus.

sections.title: Story Role & Setup
sections.text: Speak with Jericho on the streets of Megaton, inside his house, or at Moriarty's Saloon while having Evil Karma and 1,000 caps. Primary locations: Jericho's House.

sections.title: Participants, Choices & Rewards
